intro.heading: What you are actually buying when you pay for a one-to-one hour
paragraphs: A 1-to-1 IB tutor in the UAE costs more per hour than any other format on the market, and the reason is arithmetic rather than branding. In a group of six, an hour of teaching is shared six ways. In a school class of twenty-two, the same hour is shared twenty-two ways and the teacher is also running the room. Pay for one-to-one and the hour goes on one student's gaps: the question they cannot start, the graph they read backwards, the paragraph that loses four marks every single time. That is the product. Everything else here is about what the hour should cost, what moves the price, and how to tell afterwards whether the money did any work.

Rates published across the Emirates run from about AED 33 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for a tutor marketed on reputation. Bestimate's 2026 rate table for Dubai puts a visiting in-home tutor at AED 180 to AED 350 and a subject specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 or more. Those are other people's published prices, read in October 2026, and they describe the market you are shopping in rather than a price list of ours. IB Gram quotes against the plan a family actually needs, after a free trial lesson, which is why this page gives you the market's numbers instead of a headline rate.

Three things move a quoted figure more than anything else. Level comes first: a Higher Level Chemistry tutor is scarcer than a Standard Level one, and scarcity sets price. Subject comes second — English A and Business Management have deep tutor pools in the UAE, while Higher Level Physics, Computer Science and Arabic A have thin ones. Timing comes third. A 5pm Gulf Standard Time slot on a weekday is the most contested hour in the country, because the school run across Dubai, Sharjah and Abu Dhabi empties into it. A family who can take 8pm has more tutors to pick from and more room to ask for a longer block at the same rate.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one IB tuition as live online lessons in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service run only in India, and nobody is dispatched to a UAE address. For a family in Al Ain or Ras Al Khaimah that distinction is the difference between a specialist and whoever happens to be nearby: the pool stops being thirty minutes wide and becomes the whole roster. It also takes travel out of the bill, and travel is what the two-hour minimum and the higher hourly figure on a visiting booking are really covering.

One last thing before the numbers. A tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student has already produced. No sentence of an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay may come from the tutor's keyboard. One site competing for this search sells finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; under IB academic-honesty rules that purchase puts a whole Diploma at risk, and no saving on a tutoring bill is worth it. Paying for teaching is spending on a skill the student keeps. Paying for someone else's words is a malpractice file waiting to be opened.

1-to-1-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Which programme your child sits changes how many one-to-one hours are worth buying and when. A Primary Years pupil needs short, frequent sessions; an MYP student needs the habits that survive the jump to the Diploma; a Diploma student buys hours against six subjects, three internal deadlines and one exam window.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external exams, so one-to-one hours here are diagnostic rather than remedial. The usual reasons a UAE family books are an English-language gap after arriving mid-year, number fluency that has not kept up, or a child who will not write at length. Thirty or forty-minute sessions work better than sixty at this age, and the honest answer is often six to eight sessions rather than a standing weekly slot.
programmes.countryNote: PYP pupils in the Emirates also carry Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the programme, and in Dubai those lessons are built on a 40-minute teaching unit. A new arrival with no Arabic is usually behind on script before anything else, and that is the cheapest gap to close early. Waiting until Year 6 turns thirty inexpensive hours into a hundred expensive ones later.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against criteria A to D in every subject, which is where most families first meet the gap between knowing the content and answering to a command term. One-to-one time in Years 9 and 10 is the best-value money in the whole five years, because it is cheap preventive work: the student learns to read a criterion strand and write to it. The Personal Project in Year 11 needs process coaching, not content teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Plenty of UAE schools run the MYP to Year 11 and then offer the Diploma, while others switch pupils to Cambridge IGCSE for two years. Those two routes need different preparation, and families often only discover which one their school uses in Year 9. Ask the coordinator before you buy a term of hours, because MYP-to-Diploma and IGCSE-to-Diploma have genuinely different gaps to close over one summer.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where one-to-one spending concentrates and where it is most easily wasted. Six subjects, three of them Higher Level, each with an internal assessment, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. A family who books two Higher Level subjects at one hour a week for two years is committing to roughly 140 hours. Deciding which two subjects, and which eight weeks of the year, is worth more than negotiating AED 20 off the rate.
programmes.countryNote: IB programmes account for about 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, so the local Diploma cohort is a minority inside a very large school market — 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25. In practice that means a Higher Level Physics or Computer Science set at a UAE school can be five or six students, and a tutor who has taught that exact combination may live nowhere near you. Online delivery is what makes the match possible at all.

1-to-1-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Tutor supply is not even across subjects, and supply is what sets the price of an hour. The list below flags where UAE pools are deep, where they are thin, and what the hour is usually spent on — so you can see why two quotes for the same programme arrive hundreds of dirhams apart.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most-requested Diploma subject in the Emirates and the one with the widest spread of quoted rates. Higher Level AA carries proof, calculus depth and a Paper 3 that rewards stamina, and the tutor pool for it is thinner than for Standard Level. Hours here are best spent on unseen problems under the clock, not on re-teaching topics the student can already recite.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A different course, not an easier one. AI leans on modelling, statistics and the graphic display calculator, and students who switched from AA mid-course often arrive with gaps in exactly the statistics content AI examines most. Check the entry requirements of any UAE engineering or computing degree before paying for a route change; some expect AA.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: One of the thinnest tutor pools in the country at Higher Level, which is why Physics quotes sit at the top of the specialist band. Marks go on definitions, graph gradients with units, and the long-answer questions where a correct method earns nothing because it was never written down. The online whiteboard handles derivations better than a kitchen table does.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics drive most requests, and Higher Level Chemistry is the subject UAE families most often struggle to cover locally. The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 and is worth buying feedback hours on at the planning stage, well before a write-up exists. A tutor can question a method; a tutor cannot supply one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A deep pool of tutors and therefore the most competitive pricing of the three sciences. The marks are lost in command-term precision — describe, explain, outline, evaluate — and in data-based questions where students answer the biology instead of the graph. Sessions that end in a marked past-paper answer beat sessions that end in notes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the internal assessment commentaries are the usual reason for booking. Students lose marks by drawing a correct diagram and then not referring to it, and by writing commentary that summarises an article rather than applying a concept to it. Feedback hours before each commentary deadline are worth more than weekly content teaching.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: One of the easiest subjects to find a UAE-based tutor for, so the rate should sit in the middle of the market rather than the top. Most of the available marks sit in evaluation and in use of the case study, and that is a writing skill which responds quickly to one-to-one marking against the published criteria.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Deep tutor supply, wide quality spread. The Individual Oral and the Paper 1 guided analysis are where hours convert fastest, because both are structural problems rather than knowledge problems. A second language English speaker in a UAE school often needs comparison practice rather than more vocabulary.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Frequently requested by families who arrived in the Emirates partway through secondary school. The marks are in text type conventions and register, which can be taught in short, frequent sessions. This is one of the few subjects where a 40-minute slot twice a week outperforms a single hour.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: A thin pool for Arabic A in particular, and a subject nearly every competitor leaves off its list entirely. Dubai schools must teach Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum, so a student can be carrying school Arabic and Diploma Arabic at once. Sessions work on script fluency, written structure and the vocabulary load that a late starter never built.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Scarce at Higher Level across the Emirates, and often taught in very small school sets. Hours go on the paper-based algorithm questions students cannot practise on a screen, plus structured feedback on the solution-development process without a line of the student's code being written for them.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Growing quickly in UAE schools and under-served by local tutors. The marks are in research-study recall tied precisely to the command term, and in an internal assessment that rests on an experimental method. Short weekly sessions with written feedback usually beat an intensive block here.

1-to-1-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: What a one-to-one hour costs, and what you can realistically book, changes with where you live — mostly because distance prices a visiting tutor and does nothing at all to an online one. Below is what families in each part of the country actually run into when they start pricing hours.

regions.name: Dubai — Marina, JLT and Jumeirah
regions.note: The deepest tutor supply and the most contested slots in the country. Visiting tutors quote the lower end of the in-home band here because travel is short, but 4pm to 6pm is booked solid. Families who take an 8pm online slot get a wider choice of specialists at the same rate.

regions.name: Dubai — Arabian Ranches, Mudon and the Dubailand villa communities
regions.note: A visiting tutor adds twenty to forty minutes of driving each way, and that is what pushes a quoted in-home rate towards the top of the AED 180 to 500 band and forces a two-hour minimum. Online removes both the travel charge and the minimum.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi island and Al Reem
regions.note: Good school supply, thinner tutor supply than Dubai, especially at Higher Level sciences. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of pupils at their own school, so the obvious local option is often not a lawful one. Online widens the pool past the island.

regions.name: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas
regions.note: Long school runs and late finishes mean a 4pm start rarely survives contact with traffic. A 6.30pm or 8pm online slot is both easier to keep and cheaper than paying a tutor for the half-hour they spent on the Sheikh Zayed bridge.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Fewer IB cohorts than the coast, inspected by ADEK rather than KHDA, and a genuinely small specialist pool. Families here have historically paid a travel premium or driven to Abu Dhabi. One-to-one online makes the rate the same as a Marina family's.

regions.name: Sharjah — Al Nahda, Muwailih and Al Khan
regions.note: Many pupils cross into Dubai for school, which eats the early evening. Sharjah's own authority approves fees, curricula and assessment methods for schools in the emirate, so option lists differ from Dubai's. Late online slots suit the commute better than any visiting arrangement.

regions.name: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Private schools here sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate regulator. Visiting IB specialists are scarce and quote accordingly; several families report being offered a group class as the only local option. Online pricing ignores the distance entirely.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah
regions.note: The two emirates no competitor page in this market even mentions. A Higher Level specialist driving from Dubai would add two hours of travel to a one-hour lesson, which is why that booking is rarely offered and never cheap. Live video is the only format where the subject, not the postcode, decides the match.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB schools
schoolClusters.note: Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, with IB programmes accounting for about 7% of enrolment. Seven more schools open for 2026-27, three of them IB, adding 16,846 places. A bigger market has not made Higher Level specialists easier to find — it has spread a small IB cohort across more campuses.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain IB schools
schoolClusters.note: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools are supervised by ADEK, which oversees private-school licensing and accreditation in the emirate. Diploma sets outside the island can be small, and ADEK's ethics rules stop a school's own staff from tutoring their pupils for a fee — the two reasons an Abu Dhabi family ends up looking beyond the school gate.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: A standing slot in Gulf Standard Time, one tutor and one student, with marking between sessions. This is the cheapest effective unit for a subject that is merely behind rather than in trouble, and the easiest to audit: a student who cannot show you a marked answer after four weeks is not being taught, they are being supervised.

sections.heading: What a one-to-one IB tutor costs in the UAE, by format
paragraphs: A one-to-one IB hour in the UAE is advertised anywhere between AED 33 and AED 650. The band is that wide because five different products are being sold under one word. A university student revising alongside a Year 10 pupil and a trained Diploma teacher marking Paper 3 answers are not the same purchase, and the market prices them accordingly.

The table below collects what providers in this market actually publish, read in October 2026. Each figure belongs to the company that published it, not to IB Gram. We do not run a public rate card, because the sensible number depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks are left; a family gets a quote after the free trial lesson, when there is something real to quote against.

Two patterns in the table matter more than the headline numbers. First, the in-home band overlaps the specialist band almost exactly — so paying for a visit often buys travel rather than expertise. Second, small-group pricing looks like a discount per student until you divide the hour by the headcount, which the next section does. Three of the better-ranked pages in this search publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family is invoiced in.

Monthly packages are quoted in this market too: around AED 799 for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. A package is only cheaper per hour if the sessions are actually used, so ask what happens to an unused session and whether it expires. Ask also whether a quoted figure includes VAT, because a rate that turns out to be exclusive moves a monthly budget by a real amount.

sections.heading: Why the same hour is quoted at AED 150 and at AED 600
paragraphs: Parents comparing three quotes for identical work usually assume one provider is overcharging. More often the three quotes are pricing different risks. A tutor who teaches Higher Level Physics has fewer competitors than one who teaches Standard Level Biology, and a tutor who will mark a timed Paper 2 before Thursday is selling their evening as well as the lesson.

The drivers below are the ones that move a UAE quote materially. Level and subject scarcity between them explain most of the spread. Slot time explains a surprising amount of the rest: the 4pm to 6pm Gulf Standard Time window is the only one most families ask for, so it is the only one with no spare supply. Session length cuts the other way, because a 90-minute block costs a tutor less in switching time than two 45-minute ones.

Use the final column as a script. A provider who cannot say which level a tutor has taught, which board, how work gets marked, or what happens to a cancelled hour is quoting a number rather than a service. Ask for the private tuition work permit position too — it is free to hold, so there is no cost excuse for not having one.

Two practical levers are left once you know the drivers. Take a later slot, and the same tutor often has availability at a lower point in their own week. Buy 90 minutes rather than two separate hours, and the per-hour figure usually falls, because the tutor loses less time to setting up and winding down. Insist on being quoted in dirhams: a rate advertised in dollars shifts with the exchange rate on the day you pay it.

sections.heading: The attention arithmetic: one-to-one, a pair, a group of four, a class of twenty-two
paragraphs: Small-group tuition looks like the obvious saving. Four students at AED 120 each pays a tutor AED 480 for the hour, which is why centres offer it, and each family pays less than half a one-to-one rate. The question nobody in this search answers is what each student receives for that money.

Divide the hour by the headcount and the picture changes. In a pair, an even split gives each student thirty minutes of directed attention. In a group of four, fifteen. In a tuition-centre class of eight, under eight minutes. In a school class of twenty-two, under three — and that teacher is also managing behaviour, collecting work and answering the loudest hand. The split is never even in practice, which helps the confident student and nobody else.

That arithmetic does not make groups worthless. A group is a perfectly good way to work through a past paper everybody has already attempted, or to cover a topic nobody in the room has met. What a group cannot do is diagnose. A student who has been getting 4s for two years has a specific, personal reason for it — a misread command term, a missing algebra step, an essay structure that collapses in the third paragraph — and finding it takes a tutor watching one student work. That is the hour you are buying at the one-to-one rate.

The pair deserves a word of its own, because it is the arrangement families ask for most. Two siblings in one hour works when both sit the same paper at the same level in the same session; it works badly when one is in Year 11 and the other in DP2, which is the commonest version. Thirty minutes each, aimed at two different problems, is usually worse value than one child getting a full hour and the other getting one the following week.

sections.heading: One-to-one at a UAE address versus one-to-one over live video
paragraphs: Most families searching for a one-to-one IB tutor picture someone in the room, and that market genuinely exists in the Emirates: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts a visiting tutor at AED 180 to AED 350, and in-home listings reach AED 500. Those bookings usually carry a two-hour minimum, because no tutor drives to Mudon or Khalifa City for sixty minutes. Monthly in-home packages in this market sit around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one IB tuition as live online lessons, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service offered only in India. That is a limit worth stating plainly rather than burying, and the comparison below is why we think it is the better buy for a UAE family rather than merely the cheaper one.

The decisive column is the tutor pool. A visiting arrangement limits you to specialists within a drive of your community, which for Higher Level Chemistry in Al Ain or Computer Science in Ras Al Khaimah may mean nobody at all. Live video makes the subject, not the postcode, the thing that decides the match. It also removes the twenty minutes at the start of a visit when a tutor is still parking, and makes the screen a shared whiteboard that keeps a record of every worked solution.

What a family needs at their end is modest: a laptop or tablet, a headset, and a connection steady enough for video, which in most UAE homes means sitting near the router rather than buying anything. A second device as a document camera helps in maths and the sciences, because a phone propped over a page lets the tutor watch the working appear rather than see only the answer. None of that adds to the hourly rate.

sections.heading: What a 60-minute one-to-one hour should actually contain
paragraphs: An hour of one-to-one teaching has a shape, and a parent who knows the shape can tell within a fortnight whether the money is working. The commonest failure in this market is not an unqualified tutor; it is an hour spent on homework supervision. The student is busy, the room is quiet, nothing is diagnosed, and four months later the grade has not moved.

The breakdown below is the structure our tutors work to for a Diploma or Cambridge IGCSE student. The two blocks that matter most are the diagnostic at the start and the timed practice near the end. Diagnosis is what you cannot buy in a group; timed practice under exam conditions is what converts knowledge into marks, and it is the first thing to disappear when a tutor is being paid to be agreeable.

Each right-hand column is something you can check without sitting in on the lesson. Ask to see a marked answer with a criterion or mark-scheme reference against it. Ask what was set for next week and whether it was looked at. If a student cannot name one thing they were doing wrong and can now do differently, the hour was supervision, and supervision is available at a quarter of the price.

If the shape is missing, ask for it before changing tutor. Plenty of capable teachers drift into homework help because that is what the student brings to the screen and nobody has said otherwise. Say that you want timed questions and a marked answer every week, and give it a fortnight. A tutor who adjusts was under-briefed; a tutor who cannot has been selling you an hour of company at a specialist rate.

sections.heading: Paying for coursework hours without crossing the academic-honesty line
paragraphs: The internal assessments are the best-value hours a Diploma family can buy and the most dangerous ones to buy carelessly. Best value, because a 20-mark exploration or a 24-mark scientific investigation is roughly a fifth of the subject grade and is produced over months rather than in two hours in a hall. Dangerous, because the work must be the student's own and because this search contains sites selling finished internal assessments for AED 3,750.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the criteria, question the method, point at a strand that is not being met, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not provide sentences, restructure the argument on the student's behalf, supply a research question, or edit the text to completion. The student's coordinator will be asked to confirm the work is authentic; buying words puts the whole Diploma at risk, and no grade is worth that trade.

Figures below are the published limits and mark allocations most UAE families ask about. Confirm the current numbers against your child's own subject guide or coordinator before planning around them, because the IB revises guides on a subject cycle and no syllabus document is reproduced on this site. Where hours are genuinely worth buying is early: at the planning stage, when a weak research question can still be replaced, rather than three days before submission when nothing lawful can save it.

sections.heading: When one-to-one hours are worth most: the calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: Hours bought at the wrong time of year are the biggest avoidable waste in a UAE tutoring budget. Demand concentrates into the eight weeks before a session, which is when rates sit at the top of the market and the specialists are already booked. The same hours, bought three months earlier, cost less and do more, because there is still time to change something.

Cambridge and Pearson publish their dates, and those are the ones quoted below. Cambridge runs a June and a November series with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones. Using the wrong zone's timetable is a real risk: Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after doing so. Ask your school's exams officer which zone your centre sits in before planning anything around a timetable you downloaded.

No IB session or results date is published on this page. The IB's own site could not be verified from this project, and a wrong date on a page like this would plan a family's year around fiction. Treat the May session as the one UAE schools sit, and confirm the exact window, the upload deadlines and the results date with your child's IB coordinator.

One scheduling point that costs families money every year: entries are made by the school, months before the papers. Cambridge's final entries for the March 2027 series fall on 27 November 2026, which is before most parents have thought about the exam at all. If a level or a tier needs changing, that decision belongs in the weeks before the entry deadline, and it is worth an hour of a specialist's time to get right.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what that changes about hiring a tutor
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools in the UAE, and which one holds your child's school file changes what you can read before you spend. Dubai sits with KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises private-school licensing and accreditation. Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge both regulate private education and approve fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

None of those bodies endorses a tutoring service, and IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them. What they give you is free diagnostic information: an inspection report names the subjects where attainment or progress is weak, which is a far better guide to where an hour should go than a general sense that maths is hard. A school rated well overall can still have one department that has lost two teachers in a year.

The permit question is separate and worth getting right. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so no figure is quoted here. Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor without one has no price-based excuse.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: the cost nobody budgets for
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns a school-leaving certificate into something a UAE institution or employer will accept, and it catches families late. It is a paperwork process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate's attestation channel, not a teaching problem — and not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or speeds up. What a tutor can do is tell you which grades the file will need while there is still time to earn them.

The British-track requirements are published. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One page ranking for these searches tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects. The published figure is five.

For the IB Diploma there is no points threshold quoted here, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site. Anyone publishing an IB equivalency score without that source is guessing with your child's year. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel directly, start the file in the final year rather than after results day, and do not treat tutoring as a requirement of the process — it is not, and nobody should sell it to you as one.

Families arriving from an American-curriculum school have a different checklist. The published requirement there is a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. Those are test bookings with their own deadlines, so they belong on the same calendar as the exam entries rather than being discovered in the final term.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the hours outside the Diploma budget
paragraphs: Families costing a Diploma usually budget for six subjects and forget three. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a particular curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and in Dubai those subjects are mandatory in every private school whatever the licensed international curriculum. They carry reports, they carry marks, and they take time out of the same evening as Higher Level Chemistry.

KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements are specific. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education need KHDA's own sign-off to teach them.

There is one hard constraint on tutoring here. For the mandatory UAE subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. A tutor therefore works with the school's own material and the stream the child is placed in — not an imported workbook and not a parallel syllabus. That is an honest limit, and it is the opposite of what most of this market implies by listing Arabic as a subject chip and saying nothing else about it.

sections.heading: What a one-to-one tutor cannot fix, at any hourly rate
paragraphs: A page about value owes you the other half of the argument. One-to-one tuition is a strong purchase for a diagnosable problem in one or two subjects. It is a weak purchase for everything else, and families who buy it for everything else are the ones who conclude that tutoring does not work.

Four hours a week across four subjects, bought in February of the exam year, will not raise six grades. A student who has not read the set texts is short of weeks, not hours. A student who misses sleep because the timetable already runs to 10pm does not need another appointment in it. A student who has chosen three Higher Levels against their own strengths has a subject-choice problem that a tutor can advise on and cannot solve. And nobody can promise a grade: the paper is marked by the board, and a provider promising a specific score is selling something they do not control.

The honest version is cheaper than the alternative. Pick the one subject where the gap is clearest, buy six to eight hours, insist on marked work and timed practice, and review it against the next assessment the school sets. If the marks move, extend. If they do not, change the tutor or the diagnosis rather than adding a second subject. That is how a UAE family spends AED 2,000 a month well, and it is the same method whether the rate is AED 180 or AED 450.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and two slots that work
process.description: The three facts that decide whether a specialist exists for you: subject, level, and the two windows in Gulf Standard Time your week can actually hold. Naming an 8pm fallback alongside a 5pm preference widens the pool considerably, because the early-evening slot is the one every family in the Emirates asks for first.

process.title: We cost the plan before anything is booked
process.description: You get a figure for the plan — how many hours, over how many weeks, with marking included or not — rather than a headline rate with extras discovered later. Where we think fewer hours would do, we say so. A quote that assumes a two-year commitment for a problem that needs eight weeks is not a quote, it is a subscription.

process.title: A free trial lesson, then a written diagnosis
process.description: One free trial lesson per subject, booked through the site, with no payment taken beforehand. The tutor's job in that hour is to find the specific error, not to be impressive. Afterwards you get it in writing: what is actually going wrong, which component the marks are leaking from, and how many hours it should reasonably take.

process.title: Weekly one-to-one hours with marking attached
process.description: A standing slot, the same tutor, work set between sessions and marked before the next one. Timed questions under exam conditions are part of every cycle from the first month, not something saved for the final six weeks when there is no longer time to act on what they reveal.

process.title: A review after every six to eight hours
process.description: We look at the school's most recent assessment beside the marked work from the sessions and decide one of three things: carry on, change the focus, or stop. Open-ended tutoring that nobody reviews is how a reasonable monthly figure turns into a year of spending with nothing to show for it.

whyPoints.title: One student per session, with nothing shared
whyPoints.description: Every session we arrange is one tutor and one student. No group rate, no silent second student on the call, no hour split two ways while both families pay. The ratio is the product, and it is the only reason a one-to-one rate can be justified over a group seat.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure here carries its source
whyPoints.description: The rates on this page are other providers' published prices, named and dated October 2026, because a market number without a source is a marketing number. Three of the better-ranked pages in this search publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars rather than the currency you are invoiced in.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool wider than any commute
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, the Higher Level Physics specialist does not also have to live within a drive of Al Ain or Ras Al Khaimah. Scarce subjects stop carrying a local scarcity premium, and a small school cohort stops limiting what your child can be taught properly.

whyPoints.title: Feedback on the student's own work, and nothing beyond it
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, mark and give criterion-level feedback. They do not supply sentences for an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. This market contains sites selling finished coursework; the IB treats that as malpractice, and the student carries the consequence.

whyPoints.title: A trial before an invoice, and a review after
whyPoints.description: One free trial lesson per subject with no payment taken beforehand, a written diagnosis after it, and a review every six to eight hours against the school's own assessments. You should be able to see what the hours bought, in marked work, before deciding to buy more.

faqs.question: Why is the same one-to-one IB hour quoted at AED 150 by one provider and AED 650 by another?
faqs.answer: Because five different products share one word. Published UAE figures run from AED 33 to AED 52 at the budget online end up to AED 650 for a tutor marketed on reputation, with trained subject teachers between AED 150 and AED 300 and specialists from AED 200 to AED 450 or more, all read October 2026. The spread is mostly level and subject scarcity: Higher Level Physics, Computer Science and Arabic A have thin UAE pools. Slot time and whether marking is included between sessions explain much of the rest.

faqs.question: How much of a teacher's attention does my child lose in a class of twenty-two?
faqs.answer: Divide the hour by the headcount and an even split gives under three minutes each, and that teacher is also managing the room, collecting work and answering the loudest hand. The real split is never even, which helps confident students. This is arithmetic for comparison rather than a measured figure, but it is the reason a school class teaches a course well and still cannot find out why one student keeps losing the same four marks. Diagnosis is the thing one-to-one time buys.

faqs.question: Is small-group tuition at a third of the price the better buy?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. A group of four at AED 90 to AED 160 per student is good value for working through a past paper everyone has already attempted, or covering a topic nobody in the room has met. It is poor value for diagnosis, because fifteen even-split minutes is not long enough to watch one student work and find the specific error. The usual sensible answer is a short block of one-to-one hours to identify the problem, then group or school teaching to consolidate it.

faqs.question: What should I expect to see inside a 60-minute one-to-one lesson?
faqs.answer: Marked work handed back in the first five minutes, ten minutes of diagnostic questioning where your child talks more than the tutor, about twenty minutes of teaching aimed at the error found, then fifteen minutes of timed questions with no help offered, marked against the published criteria before the hour ends. The last two minutes set a specific task. If the hour was spent supervising homework, you bought supervision, which this market sells at a quarter of the price.

faqs.question: We asked for someone to teach our child at a Dubai address. Why is this delivered over live video?
faqs.answer: Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India; every UAE session is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The market for visiting tutors in the Emirates is real — Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts them at AED 180 to AED 350, with in-home listings reaching AED 500 and a two-hour minimum common. What that premium buys is travel. Online keeps the specialist and removes the drive, which matters most for subjects with thin local supply.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level cost more per hour than Standard Level, and is that justified?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically 20 to 40 per cent more in this market, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. Fewer tutors have taught the Higher Level content and the additional paper, so fewer people can mark a Higher Level answer properly. The question worth asking is not whether the premium exists but whether this particular tutor has taught Higher Level cohorts, in which board, and for how long. A provider who cannot answer that is charging a Higher Level rate for Standard Level experience.

faqs.question: How do we judge what an hour bought rather than what it cost?
faqs.answer: Three pieces of evidence, all of which should exist without you asking. A dated, timed attempt at exam-style questions. A mark against it that quotes the criterion letter or mark-scheme point, not just a score. And a specific task set for next week that follows from the error found this week. Then compare the school's next assessment with the one before it. If the marks have not moved after six to eight hours, change the tutor or the diagnosis rather than adding a second subject.

faqs.question: Which parts of a science internal assessment are worth paying one-to-one time for?
faqs.answer: The planning stage, by a wide margin. The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 and a weak research question limits the mark no matter how well the write-up is done, so feedback hours are worth most while the question can still be replaced. Later hours go on data treatment and evaluation, where students lose marks for uncertainty handling and for conclusions the data does not support. Confirm the current criteria with your child's subject teacher, since the IB revises guides on a subject cycle.

faqs.question: Is it allowed to pay a tutor to read an Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: Reading and giving feedback is allowed and normal; supplying content is not. A tutor may teach argument structure and referencing, ask why a paragraph does not answer the research question, and point at where the criteria are not met. A tutor may not provide sentences, restructure the argument for the student or edit the text to completion. The essay has a 4,000-word limit and the words must be the student's own. Your child's coordinator will be asked to confirm authenticity, so the boundary protects the student, not the tutor.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in the UAE pay for a permit, and is that cost inside our rate?
faqs.answer: No, and so it should not be. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and the application runs through the MoHRE app, website and e-services. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it costs nothing, there is no price-based excuse for not holding one.

faqs.question: Does hiring a one-to-one tutor need anything from KHDA, ADEK or SPEA?
faqs.answer: No. Those bodies regulate schools, not your private arrangement with a tutor. KHDA oversees private-education quality in Dubai, ADEK supervises private-school licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and Sharjah's authority approves fees, curricula and assessment methods in that emirate. A tuition business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit, which is a different thing from an individual's work permit. IB Gram holds no regulator endorsement and claims none.

faqs.question: Will the Ministry of Education equivalency file add costs we have not planned for?
faqs.answer: The process itself is paperwork run through the Ministry and your emirate's attestation channel, and no tutoring company performs it or can speed it up. Where it can cost you is in grades: the British track needs five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five, plus one Advanced Level at E or two AS subjects. Knowing that in Year 10 is free. Discovering it after results day is expensive.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies need one-to-one hours of their own?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and families routinely leave them out of the budget. They are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, they carry reports and they take time from the same evening as Higher Level subjects. One limit matters: for these subjects, using different or additional content without the Ministry's prior permission is prohibited, so a tutor works from the school's own material and the stream your child is placed in rather than an imported workbook or a parallel syllabus.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the number of hours we pay for in a month?
faqs.answer: Usually it changes the timing rather than the total. School days shorten, so an afternoon slot can start earlier, and many families move sessions to after Iftar, which suits tutors working to Gulf Standard Time. Eid weeks are typically skipped and made up later rather than billed. The practical advice is to decide the Ramadan pattern in advance and to protect whichever weeks sit closest to a mock or an internal deadline, because those are the hours that are hardest to replace afterwards.

faqs.question: If the connection drops in the middle of a paid hour, what happens to it?
faqs.answer: The tutor reconnects, and if the session cannot be completed the remaining time is rescheduled rather than treated as taught. Practical steps reduce the problem: use a wired connection or sit near the router, keep a phone as a backup camera, and have the tutor share the whiteboard file afterwards so nothing from the lesson is lost. One honest advantage over a visiting arrangement is that a dropped slot can usually be replaced later the same week, where a cancelled visit is often charged in full because the drive was committed.

faqs.question: If nobody in the UAE teaches my child's subject combination, what are we offered?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than quietly booking a generalist. Higher Level Physics, Computer Science and Arabic A have genuinely thin UAE pools, and small school sets make them scarcer. The options are a specialist based outside the Emirates teaching in your evening slot, a short block with a near-specialist to cover the parts they can teach properly, or a wait for the right match with a date attached. The one option we do not offer is a tutor who has not taught that level pretending otherwise.

faqs.question: How many weeks should we give one-to-one tuition before judging it?
faqs.answer: Six to eight hours of teaching, or roughly two months of a weekly slot, measured against the school's next real assessment rather than the tutor's impression. By then there should be marked timed work with criterion references, and your child should be able to name a specific error they can now avoid. If the marks have not moved and nobody can tell you why, the diagnosis was wrong. Changing tutor at that point is cheaper than extending a plan nobody is reviewing.

faqs.question: Is the first one-to-one lesson free, and what conditions come with it?
faqs.answer: One free trial lesson per subject, booked through the site, with no payment taken before it happens. The tutor's task in that hour is diagnostic, so bring your child's most recent marked assessment, the subject and level, the board where it applies, and any internal deadline that is close. Afterwards you receive a written view of what is going wrong and how many hours it should take. If the match is wrong, you owe nothing and we will try a different tutor.

1-to-1-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Price the plan, not the hour
1-to-1-ib-tutor.closingBody: The hourly rate is the least useful number in this decision. What decides whether a one-to-one IB tutor in the UAE is worth the money is which subject you choose, which eight weeks of the year you buy, whether marked timed work exists afterwards, and whether anybody reviews it. Tell us the subject, the level and two slots that work in Gulf Standard Time, and we will cost the plan before you commit to anything. The first lesson is free, lessons run online one-to-one, and you should be able to see in marked work what the hours bought before you buy more of them.

intro.heading: The IGCSE year is a calendar problem before it is a teaching problem
paragraphs: Almost every UAE family who starts looking for a 1-to-1 IGCSE tutor is reacting to a mark: a mock paper that came back lower than expected, a report that moved a grade down, a teacher comment about the pace of the Extended course. The mark is real. What the mark does not tell you is how much of it is still movable, and that depends almost entirely on the date. A grade 5 in a mock sat in October of Year 11 and a grade 5 in a mock sat in April are the same number describing two different situations, and they need two different plans.

This page is built around the calendar for that reason. Not the school calendar alone, and not the board calendar alone, but the order in which decisions close. The subject list closes first, usually in Year 9 or early Year 10. The tier closes next, when the school commits to a Core or Extended entry. The final entry itself closes months before the papers. Coursework and practical components close on the school's internal deadlines, which are earlier again. Forecast grades close after that. By the time the student walks into the hall, the only remaining variable is how they use two hours of paper time.

A tutor who starts by asking what topics your child finds hard is asking a reasonable question in the wrong order. The first question is the date, because the date decides the method. Far out from the series, an hour is best spent rebuilding a topic from the bottom: notation, definitions, the arithmetic that keeps going wrong, the habits that make revision possible later. Close in, the same hour is spent on papers: question selection, timing, the exact wording a mark scheme rewards, and the three or four marks a student gives away on every single paper for reasons that have nothing to do with understanding.

The second thing this page does is count. UAE families lose more teaching weeks than they expect, and they lose them in predictable places: the winter break, the spring break, National Day, Eid, two mock fortnights, and whatever study-leave arrangement the school runs. A family starting one-to-one IGCSE tuition in January for a June series does not have twenty-one weeks of teaching. They have about sixteen usable hours at one session a week, which is a different budget and a different plan from the one they imagined on the phone.

What follows is the whole arithmetic: the usable weeks by start month, the published Cambridge and Pearson dates that set the outer bounds, the components that keep their own clocks, what the UAE market charges for an hour and who publishes those figures, and the two windows after results day that shut inside a fortnight. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video to families anywhere in the Emirates, and the honest reason is in the comparison table further down rather than in an adjective here.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: IGCSE is not one qualification in the UAE. It is two awarding bodies, two tiering systems, three sitting windows a year, and a set of components that do not all run on the exam timetable. Knowing which combination your child is entered for is the start of every plan.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with a further March series used by some centres, and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Subjects are identified by a four-digit syllabus code - 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology - and the code, not the subject name, defines the papers sat. Most Cambridge subjects are tiered: a Core entry covers a narrower syllabus and carries a lower grade ceiling than an Extended entry.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A UAE centre and a cousin's school in another country can therefore sit the same paper on different days. Ask the exams officer which zone your centre sits in before any revision plan is built around published dates.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Subject codes look different - 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology - and several subjects are untiered, so one paper set serves the whole ability range. Some Pearson routes allow units to be sat across more than one series, which spreads the assessment load for a student who has arrived late or who is rebuilding after a weak year.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and revises them, so a UAE family should work from the live official timetable rather than from a date copied onto a tutoring page. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, a gap worth planning for.

programmes.name: Core and Extended tiering
programmes.ageRange: Decided in Year 10 or early Year 11
programmes.description: On tiered Cambridge subjects the school enters each student for Core or Extended. Core covers less content and the grade range awarded stops short of the top grades; Extended covers the full syllabus and the full range. The decision is made from classroom evidence, it is written onto the entry, and once the final entry deadline has passed it is not a decision a parent can reopen. A student capped at Core who needs a higher grade for an A Level or IB Diploma place has a timing problem, not a revision problem.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE this matters more than it does in a single-system country, because students move between schools and between curricula mid-course. A child arriving from an Indian-curriculum or American school in Year 10 is often placed on Core as a precaution while the school gathers evidence. If the target course upstream asks for a grade above the Core ceiling, the evidence for an amendment has to be built and submitted before the entry closes, which is months before the paper.

programmes.name: What the IGCSE grades are being used for
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16+ - the year after the series
programmes.description: IGCSE grades do three separate jobs in the UAE, and they have different thresholds. They decide sixth-form or IB Diploma entry at the student's own school or a new one. They form part of the Ministry of Education equivalency file for a British-track certificate. And they are read by universities alongside whatever comes next. A plan that optimises for one of those three and ignores the others is how families find out in Year 13 that a subject was missing from the count.
programmes.countryNote: For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. One ranking UAE tutoring site states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before you build a subject plan around it.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subjects below are listed with the codes that appear on a statement of entry, because that is the string a tutor needs. Two subjects can share a name and assess different content across a different number of papers. The description says where the marks usually go missing rather than what the syllabus contains.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended (Cambridge); untiered Mathematics A (Pearson)
subjects.description: Two papers on most routes, no coursework, so the whole grade is decided inside the exam hall. Marks go missing in three recurring places: algebraic manipulation under time pressure, multi-step problems where method marks are available but not claimed, and the last two questions, which are often attempted with ten minutes left rather than planned for.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics (Cambridge 0606, Pearson 4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths entry by students heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level. Calculus, trigonometric identities and series arrive earlier and faster than in 0580. Students who coast through 0580 often meet their first genuine difficulty here, and the gap shows up in mocks rather than in classwork.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity, electromagnetic induction and anything involving a graph gradient produce the heaviest losses. The practical component carries its own paper and its own habits: tables drawn before readings, units in the column heading, anomalies identified rather than quietly dropped. Those conventions are teachable over video using the student's own recorded data.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and organic reaction pathways account for most of the lost marks, and they compound: a student who is unsure about moles loses marks in titration, in yields and in electrolysis. Extended papers ask for explanation rather than recall, so answers that name a phenomenon without a mechanism score about half.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap rather than the difficulty. Marks go on command terms: describe, explain, suggest and compare each want a different answer shape, and a student who writes everything they know about a topic scores the two marks available for the one thing asked. Data questions on unfamiliar experiments are the other reliable gap.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, double or single award
subjects.description: Common in UAE schools where a student takes a broad option block. The syllabus is narrower than the three separate sciences, which helps, but the papers move between biology, chemistry and physics inside one hour, which does not. One-to-one time is usually best spent on the weakest of the three strands rather than spread evenly.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.levels: Single tier, coursework route available on some specifications
subjects.description: Reading questions reward precise selection of evidence rather than long quotation, and directed writing is marked on audience and register as much as on content. Where a coursework portfolio route is used, the school's internal deadlines land well before the exam series, so the coursework work has to be done while content teaching is still in progress.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.levels: Single tier, with a speaking component
subjects.description: The speaking test is scheduled by the school inside the board's window and is often sat before the written papers. Students lose marks by answering the prompt in two sentences and waiting, and by treating the conversation as a vocabulary test. Timed practice on unseen prompts is the single most useful use of a one-to-one hour here.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks that most students leave on the table: axes labelled, curves labelled, the shift drawn and then explained in words. The data-response paper rewards students who use the figures given rather than general knowledge. Evaluation marks at the end of extended answers are the most commonly missed marks in the whole paper.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study papers punish pre-prepared answers. Marks come from applying a concept to the specific business described, and a student who defines the concept accurately but never mentions the company scores poorly. Calculation questions on break-even and cash flow are often the easiest available marks and the ones left unattempted.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.levels: Single tier, with pre-release material on some specifications
subjects.description: A thin market for specialist tutors in the UAE, which is exactly why format matters. Theory papers want precise terminology; the programming component wants working code and a trace table. Pseudocode conventions used by the board differ from the language taught in class, and that mismatch costs marks on every paper.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language and Arabic as a Foreign Language (Cambridge 0508, 0544)
subjects.description: Taken by UAE students both as an IGCSE option and alongside the mandatory Arabic the school must timetable. The two codes are not interchangeable and a student placed in the wrong one meets either unfamiliar grammar or an unrewarding ceiling. Written accuracy and reading speed are where the one-to-one hour pays.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The emirate your child studies in changes which authority holds the school's file, which school calendar the family lives by, and how far the nearest specialist in a thin subject actually is. Lessons are delivered online over live video, so what follows is about calendars and regulators rather than about driving distance.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK-curriculum schools the largest share. Mock fortnights in January and March are near-universal, and they are the fixed points a revision plan should bend around.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, so an online IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi should be someone with no relationship to the school's own timetable.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. School-run distances are longer here and the evening window is later, which matters when a family is trying to fit two subjects into one week in exam term. A student sitting the Cambridge March series in Al Ain follows their own centre's zone timetable, not the one a Dubai school publishes.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai schools, which pushes a realistic session start past 5pm on weekdays and makes the weekend the only place a two-hour coursework block fits.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Specialist coverage for subjects such as 0478 Computer Science or 0606 Additional Mathematics is thin in the northern emirates, and online delivery is the difference between a subject specialist and whoever is nearest.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Families here often drive to Dubai or Sharjah for tuition, which costs more weekday hours than the lesson itself. A live video session recovers that time for revision.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. The east-coast school year follows the same term pattern but the pool of IGCSE subject specialists within reach is smaller than in any other emirate. Sessions scheduled to Gulf Standard Time and delivered online remove the problem rather than working around it.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. Students commonly attend school in Sharjah or Ajman, so the family's timetable is set by a journey rather than by the school bell. Booking the weekly one-to-one hour on a non-commuting evening is usually worth more than booking the subject the student asked for.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. Students we support attend schools across this group, and each runs its own mock and coursework calendar.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: ADEK holds the licensing and accreditation file for these schools. Their internal deadlines for coursework and their mock windows differ from Dubai's by a fortnight or more, which is enough to change where a January to June plan puts its heaviest weeks.

schoolClusters.city: The northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Schools here sit under SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. Subject coverage in the local tutoring market is the thinnest in the country, particularly for Extended-tier sciences.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: One-to-one IGCSE tuition is the same format in every case - one student, one teacher, live video - but the shape of the booking should follow the distance to the series. These are the four shapes families actually use, and the dates at which each one makes sense.

modes.title: The year-round subject hour
modes.description: One session a week in one subject, booked from Year 10 or early Year 11 and run alongside school teaching. The hour follows the school's scheme of work rather than racing ahead of it, closing gaps in the week they appear instead of excavating them in April. This is the cheapest version of the whole arrangement per mark gained, and the version fewest families start with.
bullets: Written work set between sessions and marked before the next one
The school's own assessment calendar used as the planning spine
Topic order driven by paper weighting, not by the textbook
Reviewed at each mock against the marked script

modes.title: The twelve-week paper block
modes.description: Booked when the first paper is roughly a term away, usually after a January or March mock. Content teaching gives way to paper work: full papers under time, question selection, mark-scheme language, and a running error log that the student keeps. The aim is recovering marks on questions the student already partly understands, which is where late gains actually live.
bullets: A marked past paper brought to every session
One timing rule practised at a time rather than all of them at once
The error log reviewed first, before any new content
Zone-correct timetable used for the final fortnight sequencing

modes.title: The coursework and practical clinic
modes.description: Short, intensive blocks aimed at the components that run on their own deadlines: a First Language English portfolio, a Geography enquiry, a Computer Science programming task, a science practical paper. The tutor teaches the technique, explains how marks are allocated, and gives IGCSE coursework feedback on a draft the student then revises. The student writes every word that is submitted.
bullets: Feedback given against the published assessment criteria
The student's own data, question and argument throughout
School internal deadlines treated as the hard dates, not the board's
No part of a submitted piece drafted, rewritten or edited to completion by the tutor

modes.title: The results and retake sprint
modes.description: A short block starting on results day. The statement of results is read subject by subject, the remark question is decided inside the board's window, and if an IGCSE November retake is the right answer the plan for it is built that week. Between a November sitting and the result reaching the student there can be a two-month gap, so the next step is planned before the wait starts.
bullets: Subject-by-subject reading of the marks, not just the grades
Remark and enquiry decisions taken inside the published window
Retake entry made by the centre well ahead of the series
The gap between sitting and result used for the next qualification

sections.heading: What a 1-to-1 IGCSE tutor can still change, counted in weeks
paragraphs: An hour of one-to-one teaching is not worth the same in September as it is in April, and the difference has nothing to do with effort. It is about which decisions are still open. In September of Year 10 the subject list can change, the tier is unsettled, and a weak topic can be rebuilt from the bottom with time to consolidate it. Six weeks before Paper 1 the entry has gone in, the tier is fixed on it, the coursework has been submitted, and the only remaining variable is how many marks the student fails to collect on questions they can already partly answer.

This is why the date comes before the subject on a first call. The date decides the method. Far out, the hour buys content and habits: notation, definitions, command terms, the arithmetic slip that recurs in every topic. Close in, the hour buys paper discipline: which question to start with, how long to spend, what the mark scheme rewards in words, and which two or three marks are given away on every paper for reasons unrelated to understanding. Those are different lessons in a different order, and running them the wrong way round wastes the money.

Read the table below from your own distance to the first paper rather than from the top row. The column that matters most is the third one. Families rarely regret starting early. They regret discovering in April that the tier was locked in November and that the grade ceiling went with it, or that a coursework mark banked in February cannot be revisited no matter how many hours are bought in May.

sections.heading: The first hour is a diagnosis, not a lesson
paragraphs: A first session that opens with teaching is a session spent guessing. There are ten facts that decide what every subsequent hour should contain, and a UAE parent usually knows two of them. None are difficult to obtain. Most sit on the statement of entry, the school's option sheet or the exams officer's email, and the ones that do not can be answered in a sentence by the head of year. Collecting them takes one hour once, and it is the hour that makes the next twenty worth buying.

The most commonly missing item is the syllabus code. Parents know the subject name; the board assesses the code. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics A are different papers with different conventions, and 0580 Core and 0580 Extended are different courses with different ceilings. A tutor who has been teaching the wrong one for a term has been teaching well and uselessly. The second most commonly missing item is the series, which sets every other date on the plan, including the week revision has to peak.

The tenth row of the table is the one families find strangest and is often the most useful. What the target grade is actually for changes the plan completely. A grade needed to meet an A Level entry requirement is a different job from a grade needed to fill out the Ministry of Education equivalency count, which is a different job again from a grade a student wants for their own reasons. One of those three can sometimes be met by a different subject entirely, at less cost and in less time.

sections.heading: Counting the hours you actually have between now and the paper
paragraphs: Families plan in calendar weeks and buy in sessions, and the two numbers are never the same. Between January and a June series there are roughly twenty-one calendar weeks. The UAE term year removes a spring break, a mock fortnight, Eid, and in most schools a study-leave arrangement that ends normal timetabling before the first paper. One session a week through that period is about sixteen usable hours in one subject. Sixteen hours is enough to rebuild two or three whole topics and fix paper technique. It is not enough to re-teach a two-year course, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling a feeling.

The table below is the arithmetic done in advance for the common start months, against a June series. It is a planning model built from the standard UAE term pattern rather than a measurement of any one school, so check the losses column against your own school calendar: International schools in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and the northern emirates do not break at identical times, and the mock fortnight is the item that varies most.

Two conclusions fall out of it and both are unpopular. The first is that starting one subject in November usually produces more marks than starting two in March for the same total spend, because the hours arrive while content teaching can still be absorbed. The second is that a six-week block is a real intervention with a real job - paper technique, question selection, the highest-frequency errors - and it should be bought and judged as that, rather than as a last-minute attempt at a syllabus.

sections.heading: Why the IGCSE entry deadline sits months before the paper
paragraphs: The single most expensive misunderstanding in an IGCSE year is that the exam date is the deadline. It is the last date. The decisions that shape the result are taken by the school months earlier, when the final entry is submitted with the board, the tier on it and the subject list fixed. The Cambridge IGCSE final entry deadline for the March 2027 series is 27 November 2026, for an exam period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027. That is ten weeks of distance between the paperwork and the paper, and everything on the paperwork is settled in the autumn.

The forecast-grade date is the one that surprises parents most. For the same March 2027 series, Cambridge asks for forecast grades by 27 February 2027 - inside the exam period itself. The school produces those from mock evidence and classwork, which is one practical reason a mock is worth taking seriously even though it awards nothing. Results reach the centre through Cambridge's own system on 13 May 2027, with certificates following in late June, so a family needing a result for an onward application works from the statement first.

Pearson Edexcel runs its own clocks. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 - roughly nine weeks after the papers. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so every date here should be confirmed against the live official timetable on the board's own site before a plan is built on it.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the UAE term year: where the hour moves to
paragraphs: In several recent years Ramadan has fallen squarely inside the revision term for a June series, and in the UAE that is a timetable change rather than a mood change. School days shorten. Afternoons are quieter and evenings are later. Families who try to hold a 4pm session through Ramadan usually lose two or three of them before admitting the obvious, and those are expensive weeks to lose when the first paper is eight weeks away.

The workable answer is to move the hour rather than cancel it, and to decide that in advance rather than week by week. A post-Iftar slot works well for older students and is easy to hold for a month when it is booked as a block. Where that is not possible, a shorter midday session during the shortened school week, with written work set for later, keeps continuity without asking a fasting fifteen-year-old to do algebra at 5pm. A Ramadan revision plan that is agreed in January survives; one improvised in March does not.

The rest of the UAE calendar needs the same treatment. National Day, the winter and spring breaks, Eid and the school's own study-leave arrangement remove weeks that a January plan has already silently spent. Online delivery helps here in a specific and unglamorous way: a session can follow a family to Al Ain, to a grandparent's house abroad, or into a travel week, because nobody has to be driven anywhere for it to happen.
bullets: Agree the Ramadan slot in January, as a block, not week by week
Treat the mock fortnight as teaching time lost, and plan around it
Keep one session in each break week if the series is under twelve weeks away
Set written work for travel weeks rather than cancelling the sequence

sections.heading: Nine subjects, one weekly hour: how the hour gets allocated
paragraphs: A typical UAE IGCSE student sits eight or nine subjects. Almost no family buys one-to-one tuition in eight or nine, and the ones who try usually buy half an hour of nothing in each. Allocation is the real decision, and it should be made from marked scripts rather than from the subject the student dislikes most. A student who dislikes Chemistry and is on target in it does not need the hour; the subject sitting one grade below the threshold an onward course requires does.

The distance to the paper changes the answer. With twelve weeks or more, two subjects can share a fortnight-by-fortnight rotation as long as written work is set in the off week, and both can move. Under eight weeks, splitting the hour between two subjects usually produces two thin attempts instead of one real one. At that point the honest advice is to pick the subject where the grade matters most and say so, rather than selling two subjects' worth of hours.

One row in the table below causes arguments and should not. Where a coursework or practical mark is already banked and low, no amount of hours can revisit it, and the achievable total has to be recalculated against the written papers that remain. Telling a family that in February is uncomfortable. Telling them in June, after they have paid for four months of hours aimed at a ceiling that had already dropped, is worse.
