process.title: Tell us the school, the board and the paper
process.description: The useful first message names the school, the programme, the subject, the level and, for IGCSE, the syllabus code. If you have the ADEK inspection rating for the school or a marked mock script, send those too. Those details decide which tutor fits; a request for maths help does not.

process.title: We match on syllabus, not on postcode
process.description: We look for a tutor who has taught and marked the exact components your child sits, then check availability against your household timetable in Gulf Standard Time. Because lessons are online, the match is not limited to people who could drive to Khalifa City or Al Reef on a weekday evening.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the parent welcome to sit in
process.description: The trial is a working session rather than a sales call. The tutor usually sets a short past-paper task, marks it live and explains where the marks went. Parents are welcome to listen. If the fit is wrong, say so and we match again rather than asking you to persevere.

process.title: Four weeks of diagnostics before any promises
process.description: The first month establishes a baseline from marked work: which components lose marks, whether the problem is content, pace or technique, and what a realistic target looks like. You get a written note after each session. No tutor on this platform predicts a grade, because nobody honestly can.

process.title: If no specialist is free, we say so
process.description: Some combinations are genuinely scarce, Higher Level Computer Science at a particular hour, Arabic A literature at a specific level, a Paper 3 specialist in the three weeks before a session. When nothing fits, we tell you that and when it might change, rather than placing a near-match and letting you find out later.

whyPoints.title: We read the ADEK report before we match
whyPoints.description: The regulator publishes subject and phase judgements for every private school in the emirate. Using them means a tutor starts with evidence about where a school's teaching is strongest and weakest, instead of starting with a parent's understandable but imprecise sense that something is wrong.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Mathematics 0580 and 4MA1 are not the same course to teach, and Analysis and Approaches is not Applications and Interpretation with harder numbers. We match on the code, the tier and the paper, which is why we ask for details that feel excessive in a first message.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in local time around the school bus, activity schedules and, during Ramadan, a post-Iftar slot. Where a family travels between the emirate and abroad through the year, the same tutor keeps the slot rather than the booking lapsing and restarting with someone new.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on academic honesty
whyPoints.description: Tutors coach internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essays against the published criteria. They do not write them, supply data or choose topics. We state that to the student at the first session, because an unclear line is how a well-meaning family ends up in a malpractice case.

whyPoints.title: Market pricing published with its sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page come from named competitor pages and published rate tables, not from us. That lets a family judge any quote, including ours, against what the market actually charges. Our figure is quoted before a trial lesson and never presented as a market average.

whyPoints.title: Independent, with no school or board connection
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no formal connection with any Abu Dhabi school, with ADEK or with any awarding body, which is also why nothing on this page should be read as an official statement of a school's performance or a regulator's requirements.

faqs.question: What does an ADEK inspection rating tell me about whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: More than the overall band suggests. Read past the cover page to the judgements by phase and by subject. If attainment in upper-secondary mathematics is rated below the rest of the school, and your child takes a Higher Level mathematics course, that is a concrete reason to add support in that subject and only that subject. If the school is strong in the subject but your child is not, the problem is individual and the diagnostic question changes. Either way the report tells you where the school's teaching is reliable, which is exactly the information a parent otherwise has to guess at.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in the UAE run from about AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor online to AED 650 for a named specialist. EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. Those are market figures from those providers, not our price list. Our own rate depends on subject, level and tutor, and is quoted before the free trial lesson so you can compare it against the bands above.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor or an online tutor the better choice for a Khalifa City family?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is scarce for you. If a genuine specialist in your child's subject and level lives a short drive away and has the slot you need, hiring locally is a reasonable choice. In practice the constraint is the radius: a Chemistry Higher Level specialist who has marked Paper 2 may not live near Khalifa City, so families end up with a near-match on subject. Online keeps the one-to-one teaching and drops the geography, so the match is made on the component your child actually sits. Lessons with us are online only in the UAE.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit from the authorities?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and every official source we could check states that the permit itself is issued free of charge. Employed residents generally need their employer's agreement before tutoring privately, and the permit covers an individual tutoring privately rather than running a centre, which is a separate licence. We do not publish penalty amounts, because the ministry has not specified them publicly and the figures circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi schools do your tutors work with students from?
faqs.answer: Students come to us from across the emirate: the island cluster around Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, Saadiyat and Yas, and the newer mainland communities towards Al Shamkha. Because teaching is online, the relevant question is not which schools we are near but which boards and components a tutor has taught. We ask for the school name so a tutor knows the scheme of work and assessment calendar in use. We have no connection with any school named on this page, and naming one implies nothing about the school.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Chemistry internal assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach what each criterion rewards, review a draft against the published descriptors, point out that the evaluation section names no concrete limitation, question whether the conclusion follows from the data, and show an exemplar at a known mark band. A tutor cannot choose the research question, supply data, write or rewrite text, or hand over a structure to fill in. Your daughter's supervisor signs an authenticity declaration and the work goes through text-matching software, so the boundary protects her diploma rather than restricting the help she can have.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB sciences internal assessment worth and what are its criteria?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria: A research design, B data analysis, C conclusion and D evaluation, each worth 6 marks, and it is capped at 3,000 words. It counts for 20 per cent of the final grade at both Higher and Standard Level in Biology, Chemistry and Physics. Criterion D is where able students lose most, because evaluating a method means naming specific limitations and realistic improvements rather than writing that more repeats would help. Knowing the mark split changes how a student allocates the weeks they have.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic and Islamic Studies while doing the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Private schools in Abu Dhabi teach Arabic to all students under Ministry of Education rules applied through ADEK, as a first language for Arabic speakers and as an additional language for others, with the year groups set by the regulator. Islamic Education applies to Muslim students, and Abu Dhabi schools also deliver the moral, social and cultural studies strand. These are assessed by the school and recorded on the school report rather than on the IB transcript. Confirm the exact requirements for your child's year group with the school registrar, because the regulator revises them periodically.

faqs.question: What is Ministry of Education equivalency and when should an Abu Dhabi student apply?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is the ministry's assessment of an international qualification against the UAE secondary certificate, and UAE universities, government employers and some scholarship routes ask for it. The application needs the attested certificate and transcript, identity documents and evidence of years of schooling completed. Start earlier than the paperwork suggests: the ministry sets which subjects must appear on the certificate, and that list is revised, so confirm it with your Diploma coordinator in Year 11 or DP1 rather than after results. MoE equivalency for IB students is administrative, not difficult, unless a required subject was dropped two years earlier.

faqs.question: When do registration deadlines and results dates fall for the May and November IB sessions?
faqs.answer: Schools register May-session candidates with the IB around mid-November of the preceding year, and November-session candidates around mid-May of the same year. Written papers run late April to late May for the May session and October to mid-November for the November one. Results have landed in early July and in the first days of January respectively in recent sessions, each followed by a short window for a remark. Cambridge and Edexcel June series results arrive in mid-August. Your Diploma coordinator or exams officer confirms the exact dates for your child's cohort.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we would rather agree that before the month begins than improvise during it. The regulator announces shortened school days for Ramadan, and Ramadan 1448 is expected to start in the second week of February 2027, subject to moon sighting. That lands on top of mock season and the heaviest coursework deadlines, so families who plan nothing lose about four weeks of revision. A post-Iftar slot, often shorter than the usual session, holds better than an afternoon one. Tell us your preferred pattern in January and we will set it with the tutor.

faqs.question: My son sits IGCSEs in June and we are only starting in February. Is that too late?
faqs.answer: It is late enough to change what you should buy, not too late to be worth buying. With roughly fourteen weeks left, broad syllabus coverage is the wrong purchase. The productive version starts from the marked mock script, identifies the two or three topics costing the most marks, and spends the time on those plus paper technique: timing, command terms and showing working so method marks survive a slip. Spring break is the strongest revision window in the Abu Dhabi calendar. What nobody can honestly offer at this stage is a predicted outcome.

faqs.question: Should my child take Maths AA or Maths AI for a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra and proof route and is the one expected by most engineering, physics, computer science and economics programmes, in the UAE and abroad. Applications and Interpretation is statistics and modelling led, calculator throughout, and suits business, social science, design and life science routes. The decision should be made against the written entry requirements of the specific programmes your child is considering, not against which course looks easier. Our Maths AA and AI tutors routinely see students who chose by reputation in DP1 and regretted it in DP2.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for the subject and the time we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you when it might change. Some combinations are genuinely scarce: Higher Level Computer Science in a narrow evening window, Arabic A literature at a particular level, or a Paper 3 specialist in the three weeks before a session when everyone wants one. The alternative is placing a near-match and letting a family discover the gap in April, which costs them more than waiting. Where it helps, we suggest a different slot, a fortnightly pattern or a short diagnostic block with a specialist rather than a weekly commitment.

faqs.question: How do sessions fit around an Abu Dhabi school bus and the homework that follows?
faqs.answer: By being scheduled after the bus, not before homework. Khalifa City and Al Raha routes commonly drop between 15:30 and 16:15, so a 17:00 start holds across a term while a 16:00 start collapses the first time traffic is heavy. Al Shamkha and Al Reef routes push that later again. We set one fixed weekly slot, keep sessions to sixty or ninety minutes, and set a task that connects to the school's own homework rather than adding a parallel workload. Weekend mornings work well where weekday evenings are crowded with activities.

faqs.question: Do your tutors cover both Cambridge and Edexcel for IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction matters more than parents expect. Cambridge 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology set an Extended candidate a multiple-choice paper at 30 per cent, a theory paper at 50 per cent and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper at 20 per cent. Edexcel 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 structure their papers differently and assess practical skills within the written papers. Extended Essay support in Abu Dhabi and Diploma work aside, the single most useful thing you can send us for IGCSE is the syllabus code from the school.

abu-dhabi.closingHeading: Start with the report, then the paper, then the tutor
abu-dhabi.closingBody: If you do one thing after reading this page, open your school's ADEK inspection report and find the judgement for your child's subject and phase. Then ask the teacher three questions: what the baseline predicts, what the current working grade is, and which component the gap sits in. With those answers, matching a tutor takes a short conversation rather than a trial-and-error term. Send us the school, the board, the level and the syllabus code, and we will tell you plainly whether we have a specialist free for that component and that hour, or whether you would be better served waiting a few weeks for one.

abu-dhabi/1-to-1-ib-tutor.heroSubtitle: A 1-to-1 IB tutor in Abu Dhabi is worth paying for because of the ratio, not because of the label. In a class of eighteen a student speaks for a minute or two; in an hour alone they are answering, being interrupted, being corrected and rewriting continuously. This page sets out what that difference produces week by week, how an hour is actually spent, and what one-to-one cannot do. Sessions run live over video at Gulf Standard Time, starting with a free trial lesson.

abu-dhabi/1-to-1-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below works with one student at a time and marks that student's written work between sessions. They name the subject group and level they teach, because the ratio only pays off if the person on the other end of it knows the component your child is losing marks on.

intro.heading: The ratio is the product; everything else is packaging
paragraphs: Parents buy one-to-one tutoring for a reason they rarely articulate, and it is not that the tutor knows more than the school teacher. Often they know less. What they have is undivided attention, and attention is the mechanism by which a misconception gets found and corrected. In a Diploma class of eighteen a student can sit through a term with a wrong model of how a reaction works, nodding in the right places, because nothing in the format requires them to say it out loud. An hour alone makes that impossible to sustain past the first ten minutes.

That is the whole argument, and it is worth examining rather than accepting. The things a ratio of one buys are specific and countable. The student talks, which means their reasoning is audible and therefore correctable. The tutor interrupts, which means an error is caught at the moment it is made rather than after a week of practising it. Written work gets marked individually and returned with the specific missing step named. And the pace is set by what the student does not yet understand rather than by a scheme of work covering a cohort.

The things it does not buy are equally specific, and this market almost never mentions them. One-to-one provides no peer pace, which matters for students who work because others are working. It is poor value for breadth: covering a whole syllabus at a ratio of one is an expensive way to do what a class does adequately. And it can create dependence if the sessions do the thinking rather than demanding it, which is the commonest way a year of hours produces very little.

Abu Dhabi gives the argument a sharper edge than most markets. Diploma cohorts here are small per school, spread between the island schools, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor and the newer mainland communities. A student in a Higher Level class of three has the attention already, which changes what tutoring is for: not more explanation, but someone outside the school who can mark their work against the markbands and tell them something their teacher has not. Conversely a student in a large Middle Years class in a mainland school may genuinely never have had a question answered at the moment they asked it.

What follows is organised around the ratio. It sets out how an hour is spent minute by minute, why diagnosis is only really possible at one to one, how the formats compare on measurable things rather than on claims, what to do about the cases where one-to-one is the wrong purchase, how to pace a tutor across two Diploma years without buying hours you do not need, and what makes a pairing work or fail. IB Gram delivers all of this one-to-one over live video; we do not run home visits in Abu Dhabi, because home visiting is a service offered only in India.
bullets: The ratio buys audible reasoning, immediate correction and individual marking
It does not buy peer pace, and it is poor value for covering breadth
In a Higher Level class of three, attention is not the missing ingredient
A session that does the thinking for a student produces dependence, not progress
Ask how an hour is structured before asking how much it costs

abu-dhabi/1-to-1-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: What a ratio of one is for changes with the programme, because what the student needs from an adult changes. Here is what one-to-one is actually good at in each stage of the IB, and where it is usually wasted.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: One-to-one is at its most efficient here and also easiest to overbuy. Reading aloud with immediate correction, and number facts rehearsed to automaticity, are things a ratio of one does far better than any class. Twenty focused minutes beat an hour, and for most children at this stage three short sessions a week outperform one long one at the same total cost.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the subject families most often want at this stage is Arabic, which is mandated alongside the licensed curriculum. One-to-one is genuinely strong for early language work because it generates speaking time that a mandated class period, organised separately for Arabs and non-Arabs, cannot provide per child.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The ratio earns its cost when it is aimed at one criterion rather than a subject. A student at Criterion A seven and Criterion C three needs a specific skill rehearsed on marked examples, which is exactly what one-to-one does and what a class cannot. Used to re-explain content the class already covered, it is expensive repetition.
programmes.countryNote: Mainland Abu Dhabi schools often run larger Middle Years classes than the island IB schools, and that is where students most commonly arrive having never had an answer corrected at the moment they gave it. The first sign is a student who can describe a method confidently and cannot execute it under a question.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The highest-value and highest-risk use of one-to-one. High value because markband judgement on the student's own written answers is almost impossible to deliver in a class, and that is where Diploma grades move. High risk because a weekly session that works through whatever is due tomorrow is homework supervision at a specialist rate.
programmes.countryNote: Small Diploma cohorts across this emirate mean two things at once. The student may already have substantial teacher attention, so the tutoring has to add something the school is not providing. And local supply of a genuine Higher Level specialist in any one subject is thin, which is the practical reason the ratio is easier to achieve remotely than locally.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: internal assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: The clearest case for a ratio of one, because the work is individual by definition and the feedback has to be about this student's argument rather than about arguments in general. The session format is almost entirely questioning: the tutor reads, asks, and the student revises. Nothing the tutor writes goes into the submission.
programmes.countryNote: School internal deadlines cluster in the same weeks across several Abu Dhabi schools, so the sessions have to be booked against your own school's dates rather than spread evenly. One provider in the wider UAE results sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750, which is the purchase that ends a candidacy rather than rescuing it.

abu-dhabi/1-to-1-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often book one-to-one for, with a note on what the ratio specifically fixes in each. The point is that different subjects need the attention for different reasons.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The ratio matters because method has to be watched being produced. A tutor looking over a student's working line by line catches the step that gets skipped, which no amount of worked examples on a board will reveal. Higher Level proof work is almost impossible to correct any other way.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Here the attention goes on interpretation rather than computation. The student has to say what a statistical result means in context, out loud, and be pushed when the sentence is vague. That exchange is the whole intervention and it cannot happen in a class of eighteen.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Misconceptions in electricity and mechanics survive classroom teaching remarkably well, because students can follow a worked solution without holding the underlying model. The ratio surfaces it within minutes: asked to predict, they predict wrongly, and the correction can begin from the right place.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation chains and equilibrium reasoning need the student to narrate their steps. The internally assessed investigation needs individual questioning about their own data, which is the work the ratio exists for. Expect more questions than explanations in a good session.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mostly a writing intervention rather than a content one. A six-mark answer needs six distinct points and most students produce two restated three times. One-to-one correction on the student's own answers, repeated across a handful of sessions, changes that faster than any other format.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams have to be drawn by the student while someone watches, because the error is always in what gets labelled or which curve moves. Evaluation needs a judgement pushed out of them rather than modelled at them. Both are high-return and quick at a ratio of one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is individual by definition, and rehearsing it with timing and interruption is only possible one to one. Paper one analysis improves when a tutor reads the student's thesis and asks what question it answers, which is a conversation rather than a lesson.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The band separator is application to the organisation in the stem, and the fix is having generic sentences struck out in front of the student while they explain what they meant. That is uncomfortable and effective, and it is a ratio-of-one activity.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Speaking time per student is the limiting factor in any language class, and one-to-one multiplies it. For Abu Dhabi students carrying Arabic alongside the Diploma, the gap is usually written structure against the criteria rather than fluency, and that needs individual marked writing.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Almost unteachable in a group and quite teachable one to one, because the work is pressing a student on their own claims until the argument holds. A good session here contains very little exposition and a great deal of questioning, and the output is the student's own revision.

abu-dhabi/1-to-1-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: The ratio is the same everywhere; what differs by community is whether it is achievable locally at all. Here is what the practical choice looks like across the emirate.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Local one-to-one options exist for common subjects, so the real question here is subject depth rather than availability. For a Higher Level science the local pool thins fast and the ratio is easier to get remotely with a specialist.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A small catchment with more IB students than local tutors, which means the person available is frequently a generalist. Buying the ratio from a generalist is paying a specialist price for attention without expertise.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: Students are often home only after 16:00 because of long bus runs, so a local tutor has to be free late and willing to travel both ways. That filters the pool on logistics rather than on subject, which is the wrong filter.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: The widest genuine local choice in the emirate for common subjects, and the one area where a local one-to-one arrangement is usually competitive. Still thin for a specific Higher Level component.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Growing cohorts, small Diploma classes. Students here frequently already have teacher attention, so the tutoring has to add markband judgement from outside the school rather than more explanation.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Larger mainland classes and long inbound journeys. This is where students most often arrive never having had a wrong answer corrected at the moment they gave it, which is the clearest case for the ratio.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Under ADEK like the capital, but the local specialist pool for a Higher Level subject is close to empty. The realistic choice is between remote one-to-one arrangements, which at least compete on subject depth.

regions.name: Al Dhafra and the Western Region
regions.note: Very limited Diploma provision locally. For most Higher Level subjects there is no local one-to-one option at any price, so remote delivery is the market rather than a substitute for it.

schoolClusters.city: Island IB schools: Saadiyat, Al Reem and Yas
schoolClusters.note: Small Diploma cohorts and relatively high teacher attention already. Students we support in this cluster are usually buying external markband judgement and coursework questioning rather than more explanation, which changes what a session should contain and makes short, sharply aimed arrangements better value than standing weekly slots.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland corridor: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: Larger classes in several schools and longer transport, so students arrive with less individual correction behind them and more to gain from the ratio alone. Sibling bookings are common here, and back-to-back individual slots work better than a shared hour because the two children rarely need the same skill.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one aimed at a component
modes.description: A fixed slot across a term, pointed at one paper or one criterion. The rule that makes it work is that the session does not follow the week's homework. Homework supervision at a specialist rate is the commonest way a year of one-to-one produces little, and protecting the session from tomorrow's deadline is what prevents it.

modes.title: Coursework questioning against school deadlines
modes.description: Short sequences of sessions timed to your school's internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge draft dates. The format is deliberately lopsided: the tutor reads and asks, the student talks and then revises. Nothing written by a tutor enters the submission, and the dated trail of revisions stays with the student.

modes.description: Two or three sessions whose only purpose is to find out what the problem is. A timed paper marked and categorised, one session of targeted questioning to test the hypothesis, and a written view on whether a longer arrangement is worth buying. Sometimes the answer is no, and that is a useful thing to pay for.

sections.heading: What a ratio of one actually changes
paragraphs: Four things change when the ratio goes from eighteen to one, and all four are mechanisms rather than feelings. The student's reasoning becomes audible, because they have to produce it rather than recognise it. Errors get caught at the moment of production, before a week of practice entrenches them. Written work is marked individually against the markbands, with the specific missing step named. And the pace follows what this student does not understand rather than a scheme of work built for a cohort.

The first of those is the one that does the real work, and it is worth being concrete about why. A student can follow a worked solution on a board with no model of why any step is taken. Nothing in a class requires them to reveal that. Asked to predict an outcome in front of a tutor, they predict wrongly within minutes, and the correction can start from where the misconception actually is instead of from where the syllabus says they should be. This is why a good first session contains far more questions than explanations and can feel, to a parent listening from the next room, like very little teaching.

The second is about timing rather than content. In a class, a mistake in Tuesday's work is corrected when the books come back, by which point it has been repeated in homework. One to one, it is corrected in the sentence after it is made. Over a term that difference compounds, because each error is caught once rather than practised and then unlearned.

None of this depends on the tutor being more knowledgeable than the school teacher, and it is worth saying so, because providers in this market tend to imply the opposite. What it depends on is the format and on the tutor knowing the component well enough to ask the right question. Attention without expertise produces a pleasant hour. Expertise without the ratio is what school already provides.
bullets: Audible reasoning, immediate correction, individual marking, student-set pace
A good first session is mostly questions and can look like little teaching
An error caught at production is cheaper than one caught a week later
Attention without subject expertise produces a pleasant and useless hour

sections.heading: Where the hour actually goes
paragraphs: Most providers describe a session in general terms and leave the structure to the tutor. That is fine when the tutor is good and expensive when they are not, so the shape below is published rather than implied. It is the standard structure for a sixty-minute Diploma or Middle Years session, and the proportions matter more than the exact minutes.

The thing to notice is how little of it is exposition. Roughly ten minutes of the hour is the tutor talking at length; the rest is the student working, answering, being interrupted, or writing under timed conditions while the tutor watches. A session where the tutor talks for forty minutes is a lecture delivered at a one-to-one price, and it is the most common failure mode in this market because it feels productive to everyone present.

The second thing to notice is that the hour ends with something written down. Either a timed section completed under exam conditions, or the next entry in the error log, or a specific piece of written work set for before the next session. A session that ends with a general agreement to practise more produces nothing durable, and over a term that is how twenty hours disappear without a trace.

For a ninety-minute session, which suits the late Khalifa City and Al Raha school runs, the structure stretches rather than changes: the retrieval opening stays short, the timed writing block roughly doubles, and the marking review at the start goes deeper. For a Primary session, twenty to thirty minutes with the same shape works better than an hour at any age below about ten.

sections.heading: Diagnosis is only really possible at a ratio of one
paragraphs: A school report tells you a position. A marked script tells you a category of error. Neither tells you the misconception underneath it, and the misconception is what determines whether a term of work will succeed. Finding it requires asking a student to reason out loud and following where it goes wrong, which is a one-to-one activity by nature.

A worked example makes this concrete. A Diploma Physics student loses marks consistently on circuit questions. The marked script categorises those as method losses, which suggests drilling. At a ratio of one, five minutes of questioning reveals that the student believes current is used up as it passes through components. No amount of practice on potential dividers fixes that; it has to be rebuilt. A class cannot find it because the student's written work looks like carelessness, and drilling would have spent the term reinforcing the wrong model.

This is also why the first session with us produces a marked baseline rather than teaching. Every lost mark is tagged as recall, method, command term or timing, and the counts come to you in writing. That table decides whether you are buying technique work, which responds in weeks, or content rebuilding, which needs a term. It is the difference between a plan and an appointment, and it is the one thing you should insist on before agreeing hours.

There is a limit worth stating. A diagnosis explains the work in front of you; it does not predict a grade. Boundaries move, papers vary, and a student who has rebuilt a model can still have a difficult morning. What the diagnosis removes is the guesswork about whether the hours are aimed at the right thing, which is a narrower claim than this market usually makes and one that can be checked.

sections.heading: One-to-one, small group and class compared on countable things
paragraphs: Comparisons in this market are usually about quality, which cannot be measured, so the table below compares formats on things that can be counted. The figures are illustrative arithmetic from class sizes rather than research findings: they are what the ratio implies, not a study, and they are stated that way deliberately.

The arithmetic is unflattering to the class format in one specific respect and generous to it in another. Student talk time and individually marked written work scale almost directly with the inverse of the ratio, which is why one-to-one dominates on both. But cost per hour of content covered goes the other way: a class teaches a whole syllabus at a cost per student that one-to-one cannot approach. Those are not in conflict. They describe two different jobs.

The practical conclusion for a family is therefore boring and correct. Use the school for breadth, because it is good at it and already paid for. Use a small group if peer pace is what your child is missing, which is a real thing for some students and worth more than any explanation. Use one-to-one for the specific component where individual correction is the only mechanism that works, and keep that engagement short and aimed.

One Abu Dhabi caveat. In a Higher Level class of three or four, which is common in this emirate, the class is already close to a small group and the attention argument weakens considerably. The reason to buy one-to-one for such a student is different: an external reader who will mark their work against the markbands and tell them something their teacher, who sees it every day, has stopped noticing.

sections.heading: When one-to-one is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: Three situations come up regularly where a ratio of one is the wrong answer, and a provider willing to say so is worth more than one who is not. Recognising your own case here saves more money than any negotiation.

The first is breadth. A student who has fallen behind across a whole Higher Level syllabus needs many hours of content, and buying those at a specialist one-to-one rate is the most expensive way to get them. The better pattern is the school's own provision plus a longer, cheaper weekly arrangement, with one-to-one reserved for the components that stay stuck. A provider who sells you twenty specialist hours to cover a syllabus is selling the wrong product well.

The second is motivation that depends on other people. Some students work because the person next to them is working, and for them a small group outperforms one-to-one at a lower price. This is not a character flaw and it is reasonably easy to spot: if homework happens at school and not at home, the social setting is doing the work. A free trial lesson will usually reveal it within twenty minutes.

The third is dependence, and it is the most insidious because it looks like success. If sessions consist of the student bringing problems and the tutor solving them, the student's grade can stay flat for a year while every session feels productive. The structural defence is the one in the session table above: most of the hour is the student working, with a timed block where no help is given. If you listen to a session and hear the tutor talking for forty minutes, that is the failure happening.

sections.heading: Pacing a tutor across two Diploma years
paragraphs: Families who start one-to-one at the beginning of Diploma year one and keep a weekly slot until the papers often spend a great deal for a modest result, because the hours are uniform while the need is not. The need is lumpy: it spikes around the transition into the Diploma, around coursework deadlines, and in the final run-up, and it is close to zero in the middle of some terms.

A more efficient pattern follows the calendar. A diagnostic early in Diploma year one, while there is time for a content problem to be fixed cheaply. A short block if that diagnostic finds something. A coursework block timed to the school's internal assessment and Extended Essay draft deadlines, which cluster across Abu Dhabi schools. A second diagnostic after the year-one examinations. Then a measured block before the external papers, opening and closing with comparable timed papers.

That pattern typically costs less than a continuous weekly slot and targets better, because each engagement starts from fresh evidence rather than from momentum. It also leaves the student doing their own work in the gaps, which is the behaviour that actually produces a Diploma grade and the behaviour a continuous arrangement can quietly replace.

On dates, one caution. Cambridge and Pearson publish their IGCSE and International GCSE series dates and those can be cited: Cambridge's March 2027 series closed final entries on 27 November 2026 for an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. For the IB, no session or results date appears on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date here would be unverified; your school's Diploma coordinator is the authority, and that is who should set the dates your plan is built around.

sections.heading: What makes a pairing work, and what to do when it does not
paragraphs: At a ratio of one the relationship is a larger part of the product than it is in any other format, and this is the part of the market that handles failure worst. A pairing that is wrong is usually obvious within two or three sessions, and the common outcome is that a family either persists out of politeness or stops paying for tutoring altogether, when the correct action is to change the tutor.

Three things predict a working pairing. The challenge level has to be right: a tutor who makes everything easy produces comfort, and one who makes everything hard produces silence. The student has to be talking for most of the session, which you can check by listening from the next room for ten minutes. And the tutor has to be willing to say that something is wrong, because a tutor who only praises cannot correct.

Three things predict failure. The session following the week's homework rather than a plan. The tutor talking for most of the hour. And nothing written down at the end, so there is no record and no work set. Any of those three present after three sessions is reason to raise it, and they are all visible without any subject knowledge.

Our arrangement is that the tutor changes and the engagement does not. If a pairing is not working, say so after two or three sessions, and a different tutor picks up the same error log and the same baseline paper without renegotiating anything. That is only possible because the record exists independently of the person, which is one of the less obvious reasons for insisting on the record in the first place.

sections.heading: Who may teach your child privately, and the Abu Dhabi rule
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published and figures circulating online could not be verified, so no amount appears here. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold the permit and to show it; it is a document, the question is routine, and the answer is checkable.

Abu Dhabi carries an additional rule that bears on one-to-one specifically, because the convenient choice here is often the wrong one. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported rather than read from the current policy document, so verify the wording against ADEK's own publication. The principle holds regardless: the person who sets and marks your child's school assessments should not also be paid to prepare them for it.

One last boundary, since one-to-one is where coursework support happens. A tutor may explain criteria, model technique on different material, ask questions about a draft and mark the student's own practice against the markbands. No tutor text goes into a submission, at any price. A provider in the wider UAE results sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750; the IB's academic-honesty rules make that a matter for the candidate, which means the consequence falls on your child rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: What does a ratio of one actually buy that a good school class does not?
faqs.answer: Four things, all mechanisms rather than impressions. The student's reasoning becomes audible, because they have to produce it rather than recognise it. Errors are corrected at the moment they are made instead of after a week of practice. Written work is marked individually against the markbands with the specific missing step named. And the pace follows what this student does not understand rather than a scheme of work for a cohort. None of it requires the tutor to know more than the school teacher; it requires the format plus enough subject knowledge to ask the right question.

faqs.question: How much of a one-to-one hour should the tutor be talking?
faqs.answer: Roughly ten minutes of sixty. The rest should be the student answering, working under correction, or writing under timed conditions while the tutor watches. A session where the tutor explains for forty minutes is a lecture delivered at a one-to-one price, and it is the commonest failure in this market because it feels productive to everyone in the room. You can check it without any subject knowledge by listening from the next room for ten minutes and noticing who is speaking.

faqs.question: My child is in a Higher Level class of three. Do they still need one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but for a different reason than most families assume. In a class of three the attention is already there, so buying more explanation adds little. What such a student usually lacks is an external reader: someone outside the school who will mark their written answers against the markbands and notice what a teacher who sees the work daily has stopped noticing. That is a narrower and cheaper engagement than a weekly slot, often a diagnostic plus a coursework block rather than a standing arrangement across the year.

faqs.question: How quickly would a misconception show up in a session?
faqs.answer: Usually within the first ten or fifteen minutes, if the tutor asks the student to predict rather than to recall. A worked example: a Physics student losing marks on circuit questions looks careless on paper, and the marked script categorises it as a method problem. Asked to predict what happens to current through a series of components, they reveal a belief that current is used up along the way. Drilling potential dividers would have spent the term reinforcing that. A class cannot find it because nothing in the format requires the belief to be stated.

faqs.question: Is a small group ever better than a 1-to-1 arrangement?
faqs.answer: Yes, for students whose work depends on other people working. If homework reliably happens at school and reliably does not happen at home, the social setting is doing real work and a group of four to six will often outperform one-to-one at a lower price. It is not a character flaw and it is usually visible within twenty minutes of a free trial lesson. The honest trade-off is talk time: a group gives each student roughly a sixth of the hour, so a specific component gap gets less attention than it needs.

faqs.question: How do we stop sessions turning into homework supervision?
faqs.answer: Agree in advance what the session is for and defend it. The pattern that destroys a year of one-to-one is the student arriving with tomorrow's deadline and the tutor helping with it, every week, at a specialist rate. It feels useful and produces a flat grade. The structural defences are a named target component, written work set by the tutor rather than by the school, and a timed block in every session where no help is given. If you look at a term of session notes and see only school assignments, that is what has happened.

faqs.question: What does dependence on a tutor look like, and how do we avoid it?
faqs.answer: It looks like success, which is why it is dangerous. Sessions where the student brings problems and the tutor solves them feel productive to everyone and leave the student unable to produce the same work alone. The grade stays flat across a good year. The defence is structural rather than motivational: most of the hour is the student working, there is a block every session where no help is available, and the written work set is done between sessions and marked rather than done in the session. Ask any provider how they guard against this.

faqs.question: How many one-to-one hours does a Diploma subject really need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families buy, if they are aimed correctly and spaced by need rather than by habit. A continuous weekly slot across two Diploma years spends uniformly on a need that is lumpy: it spikes at the transition into the Diploma, around coursework deadlines, and before the papers. A pattern of a diagnostic each year, short blocks where the diagnostic finds something, and a measured block before the papers usually costs less and targets better, because each engagement starts from fresh evidence rather than from momentum.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two of my children in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Back-to-back individual slots usually work well; a genuinely shared hour rarely does unless the children are in the same subject and year. Two children on different criteria or different papers have almost nothing to work on together, so a shared session halves the attention without halving the need. Back-to-back slots keep each child's error log and baseline separate while saving on scheduling, and in the central Abu Dhabi districts that is the most common sibling arrangement families settle on.

faqs.question: What do we do if the tutor is good but the pairing is wrong?
faqs.answer: Say so by the third session. A wrong pairing at a ratio of one is usually obvious early, and the common mistake is persisting out of politeness until the family gives up on tutoring altogether. With us a different tutor picks up the same baseline paper and the same error log without renegotiating the arrangement, which is possible because the record belongs to the engagement rather than to the person. Ask any provider what happens in this situation before you start, not after.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a permit for one-to-one sessions, even online?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask to see it. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Could we just pay our child's own subject teacher for private sessions?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, no. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This has been press-reported rather than read from the current policy text, so verify the wording against ADEK's own publication. The principle is sound anywhere: the person who sets and marks your child's school assessments should not also be paid privately to prepare them for it.

faqs.question: How should a session be structured for a younger child?
faqs.answer: Shorter and more often. Below roughly age ten, twenty to thirty minutes with the same shape as an hour works considerably better than sixty minutes, and three short sessions a week usually outperform one long one at the same total cost. The retrieval opening matters more at this age than anywhere, because the point is building automaticity in reading fluency and number facts. A provider selling hour-long sessions to a seven-year-old is selling a format rather than responding to how attention works.

faqs.question: Can a 1-to-1 tutor cover a whole syllabus we have fallen behind on?
faqs.answer: They can, and it is the most expensive way to do it. Covering breadth at a specialist one-to-one rate buys at a premium what a class does adequately and has already been paid for. The better pattern is the school's own provision plus a longer, cheaper weekly arrangement for content, with one-to-one reserved for the components that stay stuck after that. A provider who sells twenty specialist hours to cover a syllabus is selling the wrong product competently, and saying so costs us the sale.

faqs.question: Why do you not publish a single hourly price on this page?
faqs.answer: Because the number depends on subject, level and whether marking is inside it, and quoting before reading a marked script is guesswork. What we will publish is the market: AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist, AED 180 to 500 in-home with travel inside the rate, each from provider pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table read in October 2026. Those are the market rather than our price list. Ours follows the free trial and the baseline paper.

abu-dhabi/1-to-1-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Listen to ten minutes of a session and judge for yourself
abu-dhabi/1-to-1-ib-tutor.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the test: listen to ten minutes of a one-to-one session and notice who is doing the talking. If it is the tutor, the ratio is being wasted and you are paying a premium for a lecture. If it is your child, answering, being interrupted and writing under correction, the mechanism is working. Take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would actually teach, ask for a categorised baseline paper before agreeing any hours, and insist that written work is set, marked and returned. Sessions run live over video at Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The case for one student in the room is arithmetic, not sentiment
paragraphs: Most pages selling individual tuition make an emotional argument about attention. The stronger argument is numerical, and a parent can check it. In a class of twenty-four, a student speaks for perhaps two minutes an hour and has one written attempt marked a week, usually five or six days after writing it. In a session with a 1-to-1 IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi, the same student writes for forty minutes, has every attempt marked inside the hour, and hears the criterion each mark was awarded against. Those three ratios, not warmth or rapport, are what move a grade.

The reason they matter at IGCSE specifically is that most lost marks are not failures of understanding. They are habits that nobody has had time to interrupt: working omitted on a 'show that' question so method marks go unclaimed, a command word read as a synonym for an easier one, an answer to the question the student expected instead of the one printed, a graph scaled so the plotted points occupy a third of the grid. In a class these persist for a year because the feedback arrives too late and too generally to break them. In a one-to-one session they are interrupted at the moment they happen, which is the only point at which a habit is cheap to change.

This page is built around that claim and tests it honestly. It does the ratio arithmetic properly, including cost per corrected attempt, where group teaching sometimes wins. It sets out what the first diagnostic hour should establish. It covers the command-word vocabulary that decides how marks are allocated across every subject, which is the highest-yield thing an individual session can teach and the thing a class has no time for. Then it goes subject by subject through what one hour can genuinely repair, and what needs a block.

After that come the decisions families actually face: one session a week or two, one tutor across two subjects or a specialist for each, and the published AED rates for individual, small-group and class teaching in this market so any quote can be placed. The page ends with the cases where individual tuition is the wrong purchase, because they are real and nobody in this market writes them down.

Two facts to state up front. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video to families across the emirate and does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, where ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools; visiting tutors are a service available only in India. And IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform holding no approval from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, with no premises in the UAE. Every AED figure below was published by somebody else and is attributed.

abu-dhabi/1-to-1-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi cohorts are mobile, and a large share of individual tuition demand here comes from students who arrived into IGCSE from a different system. The route a child took into Year 10 changes what the first sessions have to do, because the gaps are structural rather than random.

programmes.name: Continuing from a British-curriculum Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The straightforward route: Key Stage 3 in the same school, then two examined years. Gaps here are specific and traceable, usually to a topic taught in a term the student missed or to a set change that skipped a strand. Individual tuition is efficient in this case because the diagnosis is narrow, and three sessions on one strand often closes something that has been dragging a grade for two years.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi this route runs through the island's long-established schools and the Khalifa City corridor, where maths setting often begins in Year 8. A setting decision made at twelve can still be shaping a tier decision at fifteen, which is worth raising in writing with the subject lead rather than accepting as settled.

programmes.name: Transferring in from a CBSE or Indian-curriculum school
programmes.description: Usually a strong procedural foundation, particularly in mathematics, meeting an unfamiliar assessment style. The content gap is often smaller than the family fears and the technique gap larger: IGCSE papers reward method written out, structured multi-part reasoning and command-word discipline rather than a correct final answer. A student can be mathematically ahead of the class and still lose marks on every paper for a term.
programmes.countryNote: This transfer is common across the Mussafah, Baniyas and Mohammed Bin Zayed City corridors, where several boards sit side by side. The first individual session should be spent on a marked IGCSE paper rather than on content, because the gap is almost always in how the answer is presented, and that is a fast repair once named.

programmes.name: Transferring in from an American-curriculum school
programmes.description: Here the assessment culture differs more than the content. Continuous assessment and coursework-weighted grading give way to terminal examinations where a single paper carries most of the subject. Students are often unpractised at long timed papers and at the extended-response question, where a position has to be held and supported across a paragraph rather than answered in a sentence.
programmes.countryNote: Yas Island, Al Reem Island and Saadiyat have significant American-curriculum provision, so this transfer appears most in those communities. The useful early work is timed practice at full paper length, which parents often resist because it looks like testing rather than teaching. It is the fastest route to the marks.

programmes.name: Transferring in from IB Middle Years
programmes.description: MYP builds inquiry, criterion-referenced self-assessment and extended project work, all of which transfer well. What does not transfer is the examination technique: MYP criteria reward process and reflection, while IGCSE papers reward precise answers to printed questions under time. Students from this route often write too much and too reflectively, which costs marks on short-answer items.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run MYP into either Diploma or IGCSE, and a mid-stream move between them is common when a family changes school. Individual sessions should start by marking one of the student's MYP-style answers against an IGCSE mark scheme, which makes the difference visible in about ten minutes.

abu-dhabi/1-to-1-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families most often book individual sessions for, described by what an hour alone with a tutor does that a class hour cannot. The distinction matters, because a subject where the gap is content needs a block and a subject where the gap is technique can move in a single session.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 0980, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The clearest case for individual work, because errors are visible at the line they occur. A class marks the final answer; a tutor watching the working intervenes at the step where the sign flipped or the substitution went in wrongly. Method marks on multi-step questions are the single largest recoverable pool in the subject.

subjects.name: Physics (0625, 0972, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Individual time is best spent on the practical paper's written demands and on the two topics that reliably confuse: electricity and moments. A class teaches the content once; a student who misunderstood the current-voltage relationship in week three carries it to the exam unless somebody notices, which takes one conversation and a diagram.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 0971, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles work compounds, so an individual session earns its fee by rebuilding the first line of every calculation until it is automatic. A class cannot wait for one student to reach that point. Organic chemistry rewards pattern recognition, which is taught by having the student classify unfamiliar examples out loud and being corrected immediately.

subjects.name: Biology (0610, 0970, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: A volume subject where the individual gain is in extended-response discipline. Students know more than their marks suggest and write around the question instead of into it. One hour spent marking three six-mark answers against the criteria, aloud, usually changes how the next twenty are written.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500, 0990)
subjects.description: Moves faster in individual sessions than any other subject, because writing is personal and class feedback is necessarily generic. Audience and register for the directed-writing task, and ruthless compression without copied phrasing for the summary, are both learnable in a handful of sessions once somebody edits with the student rather than for them.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Individual time pays in the note-making and summary exercises, where candidates lose accuracy marks by writing far more than the task allows. The speaking component differs between the two specification variants, so the first session should confirm which one the school entered before any rehearsal is planned around it.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Frequently taught in small school groups with little individual attention available, which is why it generates disproportionate tuition demand. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive abruptly, and the test of readiness is whether a student can begin an unfamiliar multi-step question without being prompted at each stage.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Diagram and evaluation subjects where the individual hour is spent drawing rather than discussing. A labelled axis, a shifted curve and a stated new equilibrium carry marks that are lost whenever a student explains in prose what the diagram should have shown. Evaluation needs a position held and defended, which is coached one answer at a time.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Trace tables are abandoned halfway by most students and completed by few, and the difference is almost entirely practice under supervision. Validation against verification, pseudocode conventions and the problem-solving paper's structure all reward short repeated individual drills rather than long revision.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Source and case-study subjects where marks hinge on using evidence rather than recalling it. An individual session is where a student learns to quote a figure from a resource, attribute a source and answer the actual command word, three habits that classroom feedback rarely has the minutes to correct per student.

sections.heading: The ratio arithmetic, including where group teaching wins
paragraphs: Three numbers decide what a teaching hour is worth to one student: how many minutes that student spends producing work, how many of their attempts get marked, and how long they wait for the marking. All three degrade with group size, and they degrade faster than the price falls, which is the honest case for individual tuition. It is also, read the other way, the honest case against it in some situations, because cost per corrected attempt is not always lowest at a ratio of one.

Work the numbers through for a sixty-minute hour. In a class of twenty-four, teacher talk and administration take a large share, the student writes for perhaps fifteen minutes, speaks for one or two, and has one piece marked a week with the feedback arriving several days later. In a group of six the writing time is similar but the marking is quicker and some of the feedback is addressed to this student. Individually, the student writes for around forty minutes, every attempt is marked inside the session, and the wait is seconds. A tutor also hears the student's reasoning, which is where misconceptions actually live.

Where group teaching wins is on cost per corrected attempt for a student who is broadly on track. If the problem is that a child does too little practice rather than that they practise wrongly, a group class that enforces structure for a lower fee per student is reasonable value. Individual tuition earns its premium when the practice is happening and the marks still are not, because that gap is almost always a specific, diagnosable habit, and a habit needs to be interrupted while it is being performed.

sections.heading: What the first individual hour should establish
paragraphs: A first session that goes well does not teach much. It establishes which of four different problems the student has, because they look identical on a report card and need completely different work. The four are: content not known, content known but method not written, command word misread, and paper not completed. A fifth, less common but worth excluding early, is that the student is entered on a different specification from the one they have been revising.

The diagnostic itself is simple and depends on having a marked script in front of both of them. Where did the marks go? If the student can talk fluently through a question they scored two out of six on, the content is there and the writing is not. If they cannot start it, the content is missing. If they wrote a correct answer with no working on a 'show that' question, they have lost method marks to a habit. If the last two questions are blank, this is pacing, and it will not respond to more content teaching. The distinctions take about fifteen minutes to make and change everything that follows.

What should come out of the first hour is a written statement of the problem in one sentence, narrow enough to be wrong: not 'needs to improve in chemistry' but 'loses three to five marks per paper on mole calculations because relative formula mass is computed from memory rather than written down'. A parent who receives a sentence like that can judge progress. A parent who receives general reassurance cannot, and will still be unable to in March.

sections.heading: Command words: the instruction vocabulary that decides the mark allocation
paragraphs: Examination papers are written in a controlled vocabulary, and each word in it carries an implied mark structure. A student who treats describe, explain, compare and evaluate as rough synonyms for 'write about' will lose marks on every paper of their life regardless of how well they know the subject. This is the highest-yield thing an individual session can teach, and it is almost never taught in a class, because it needs a student's own answer in front of them to correct.

The pattern is consistent across subjects. Describe wants observable features with no causation. Explain wants a mechanism, usually a because. Compare wants both sides in the same sentence, not two separate paragraphs. Suggest invites a reasoned possibility and tolerates more than one right answer. Calculate wants the working shown and the unit stated. Evaluate wants a judgement reached, not a list of advantages followed by a list of disadvantages. The marks follow those structures, so an answer with the right content in the wrong shape scores badly.

The drill that fixes this is short and dull, which is why it survives individual tuition and not group teaching. Take four questions the student has already answered, cover the answers, and have them state what each command word is asking for before writing anything. Then have them rewrite one answer to the required shape and mark it aloud against the published criteria, criterion by criterion. Ten minutes a session for a month is usually enough, and the gain shows up across every subject at once because the vocabulary is shared.

sections.heading: What a single hour actually repairs, subject by subject
paragraphs: Families buy tuition in hours and think in terms, which makes it hard to judge value. The useful distinction is between a procedure, which one session plus a week of practice can fix, and a fluency or knowledge gap, which needs a block of four to eight. Being told which of the two you are buying is a reasonable expectation and a good test of whether the tutor has diagnosed anything.

Procedures are specific and testable. The formula line before a calculation. Choosing a graph scale so the points fill the grid. Completing a trace table to the last row. Planning a directed-writing answer by naming audience, form and purpose in two minutes. Phrasing an observation in testable terms. Each of these is a habit with a definable right version, and a student who has done it correctly five times under supervision will usually keep doing it.

Blocks are different work. Algebraic fluency, mole calculations, organic chemistry pattern recognition, extended-response discipline, vocabulary in an additional language: these are built by repetition over weeks, and the measure of progress is a falling error rate on repeated attempts rather than a feeling of improvement. The table below splits the subjects accordingly, so a parent can ask for the right size of commitment rather than the default of a weekly slot until the exams.

The practical use of that split is in the booking conversation. Ask the tutor, after the diagnostic session, which of the two they think they are selling and how they will know when it is done. A procedure answer should come with a number: five correct supervised repetitions, then checked again a fortnight later. A block answer should come with a measure and a review point: four sessions on this question type, then a timed attempt scored against the same paper. A tutor who cannot describe the end of the work in either form is describing an open-ended arrangement, and open-ended arrangements are where most of the money in this market goes without anybody being able to say what it bought.

sections.heading: One session a week, two, or a short block before the series
paragraphs: Cadence gets decided by the calendar and the family's budget, usually in that order, and it is worth deciding on the problem instead. The question to answer first is whether the gap is knowledge, fluency or technique, because each responds to a different rhythm. Knowledge gaps need a longer single slot where content can be taught and then tested in the same sitting. Fluency needs frequent short contacts, because the interval between practice sessions is when a wrong method gets rehearsed. Technique needs a short block and then stopping.

The second consideration is what the student does between sessions, which matters more than the number of sessions. A session is where errors are diagnosed; the week is where they are corrected. A student who does the set work and a student who does not will diverge within a month regardless of how many hours were purchased, which is why the set work should be small, specific and checked at the start of the next session rather than optional.

The third is knowing when to stop, which almost nothing in this market is designed to tell you. A plan should get narrower across a term: fewer components, fewer hours, a more specific target. If a tutor is still working across the whole syllabus in week ten, the plan is touring rather than repairing. The honest end state for most subjects is that tuition stops before the exams because the component stopped losing marks, and the remaining preparation is the student's own timed practice.

sections.heading: One tutor across two subjects, or a specialist for each
paragraphs: This decision is usually made on budget and should be made on where the marks are. At Core and lower Extended level, one tutor can reasonably cover maths and a science, because much of the science difficulty at that level is mathematical and a strong mathematician handles it. At the top of the Extended tier the picture changes, because the mark-winning detail becomes specification-specific: which practical paper is sat, how an observation must be phrased, how a graph is expected to be drawn, which formulae are given and which are assumed.

There is also a hidden cost to combining. Two subjects means two sets of marked scripts to read, two components to track and two mark schemes to work from, inside the same weekly hour. In practice one subject gets the attention and the other gets the last fifteen minutes, which is worse than not booking it. If the budget allows only one slot, the better arrangement is usually to put the specialist on the subject with the weaker marks and use the school's own clinic provision for the other, which is free and under-used.

Where combining genuinely works is when the two subjects share a single failing habit. A student losing method marks in maths is usually losing them in physics too, and a student who cannot hold a position across a paragraph will underperform in both economics and history. In that case one tutor working on the shared habit across both subjects is more efficient than two specialists each addressing it separately, and the plan should say so explicitly rather than treating the pairing as a convenience.

sections.heading: What the Abu Dhabi market charges for individual, small-group and class teaching
paragraphs: Published UAE figures make the ratio premium visible. Budget online tutoring, often by university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with one platform quoting from the low AED 30s. Qualified subject tutors online sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300; one UAE agency publishes IGCSE from AED 150. IGCSE, IB and A Level specialists are quoted between about AED 200 and AED 450, with a UK-based agency publishing AED 270 and a rate aggregator giving AED 200 to AED 450 or more. In-home individual sessions, which carry travel inside the rate, are quoted between roughly AED 180 and AED 500. Named premium tutors reach AED 650.

Group rates are quoted per student and are lower, which is the whole appeal, but the comparison families should run is cost per corrected attempt rather than cost per hour. A group hour at a third of the price that produces a quarter of the marked attempts for your child is not a saving. Monthly shapes published in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions, and roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Rate aggregators estimate weekly one-hour tuition at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

All of those figures were published by other organisations in 2026 and are reproduced so you have a reference band. None is IB Gram's price list; the rate here is agreed after the free trial lesson rather than published in advance. For context on household cost, Dubai's regulator confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in that emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under a wider economic incentives package, so for many families the tuition line is the part of the education budget that is actually moving.
