sections.heading: When individual tuition is the wrong thing to buy
paragraphs: Four situations come up repeatedly where a family is about to buy individual sessions and should not, and saying so costs us a booking and keeps the page honest. The first is a tier ceiling. If a child is entered for the Core tier in a tiered subject, the top grades are not available to them no matter how good the teaching is, because the Core papers do not contain the questions those grades are awarded for. The work to do is a conversation with the subject lead about the entry, not a tutor.

The second is an administrative problem wearing academic clothes. A missed entry deadline, a wrong specification on the entry, an unregistered private candidacy: none of these is fixed by teaching, and all of them are urgent in a way tuition is not. Cambridge's own published key dates make the point: for the March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. Deadlines sit months ahead of papers, and a family discovering this in January is dealing with an administrative fact.

The third is a student doing no work between sessions. The lesson diagnoses; the week repairs. A student who attends willingly and practises nothing will show a flat error rate across two months of excellent teaching, and the right response is to find out why rather than to buy more hours. The fourth is a motivation or wellbeing problem presenting as a subject problem. A fifteen-year-old who has stopped trying in four subjects at once is not short of a maths tutor, and the school's pastoral team is the better first call. Individual tuition is powerful and narrow. It repairs diagnosed, specific, academic gaps, and it is poor value against anything else.
bullets: A tier ceiling is an entry decision, not a teaching problem
Entry deadlines sit months before the papers; check them before booking hours
No practice between sessions means a flat error rate whatever the teaching is like
A whole-timetable collapse is a pastoral conversation before it is a tutoring one

sections.heading: Coursework, drafts and what a tutor working alone with a student must not do
paragraphs: Individual tuition creates the conditions in which academic honesty gets quietly breached, because nobody else is in the room. A tutor working alone with a student on a coursework folder is one bad decision away from supplying sentences, and a student under deadline pressure will often invite exactly that. The boundary therefore has to be explicit at the start rather than negotiated at eleven at night in April.

The rule the boards apply is that assessed work must be the candidate's own. A tutor may teach the skills, explain the assessment criteria, discuss a plan, ask questions about a draft and give written feedback on what the student has produced. Supplying text, reshaping a paragraph until the sentences are no longer the student's, or correcting a draft to completion is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on the tutor. That asymmetry is worth stating to a teenager directly: the person who loses the qualification is them.

There is a materials rule alongside it. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and examiner reports are the boards' copyright and are published on their own sites for anyone to read. A tutor should point a family to the official page rather than distribute copied folders, and a tutor who offers unreleased material should end the engagement. The useful version of document literacy is knowing which document answers which question: the specification for what is examined, the mark scheme for how marks are awarded, the examiner report for what went wrong in the last series. Our position is plain: a tutor here teaches, questions, marks against criteria and gives feedback on the student's own draft, and nobody will produce assessed work on a candidate's behalf.
bullets: Set the boundary at the first session, not during a deadline week
Feedback on the student's own draft is allowed; supplying text is not
The malpractice consequence falls on the candidate, not the tutor
Read specifications and mark schemes on the board's own site

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the marked script
process.description: The specification code from the statement of entry, the tier where the subject is tiered, and the most recent marked paper. With those three the first session diagnoses instead of interviewing, and the match is made on who has prepared candidates for those papers rather than on who has a free Tuesday.

process.title: A free trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Thirty minutes at no charge with the matched tutor and no card details taken, one per family. Watch for two things: how many minutes your child spends writing rather than listening, and whether the tutor names a criterion when marking an answer. Those two observations tell you more than any discussion of teaching philosophy.

process.title: Get the problem in one sentence
process.description: The first full session should end with a written statement narrow enough to be wrong, naming the component, the habit and the marks at stake. Not a comment about needing more detail, but something like losing three to five marks a paper on mole calculations because formula mass is computed from memory.

process.title: Four sessions, then a marked repeat
process.description: Work the named component for four sessions ending in a timed, scored attempt at the same question type that was diagnosed in week one. You then hold a before and an after. If nothing has moved and the tutor cannot say why, we match again rather than sell a fifth session on optimism.

process.title: Narrow the scope, then stop
process.description: From week five the target gets narrower, and hours move off a component once it stops losing marks. The honest end state for most subjects is that individual tuition finishes before the exams, with the remaining preparation being the student's own timed practice. A plan that grows to fill the term is not a plan.

whyPoints.title: The hour is spent on this student's errors
whyPoints.description: Work starts from the script the school already marked, so the session addresses the questions this child got wrong rather than a scheme of work written for a class. That is the entire value of the ratio, and it is measurable: four or more corrected attempts in a session against roughly one a week in a classroom.

whyPoints.title: Marked against published criteria, out loud
whyPoints.description: Answers are marked to the board's own criteria with the criterion named, so the student hears what each mark is awarded for instead of whether the answer was good. This is the habit that survives into the exam hall, and it is the clearest separation between specification teaching and general subject help.

whyPoints.title: Command-word work that pays across every subject
whyPoints.description: Ten minutes a session on describe, explain, compare, calculate, suggest and evaluate changes how answers are shaped in every paper the student sits. It needs the student's own answer in front of them to correct, which is exactly what a class hour cannot provide and an individual hour can.

whyPoints.title: Scoped tightly, with an endpoint
whyPoints.description: Each engagement names a component and a measure, and the scope narrows across the term rather than expanding. Hours come off a component once it stops losing marks. A tutor still working across the whole syllabus in week ten is charging for attendance, and we would rather say so than keep the slot.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the specification, not on travel time
whyPoints.description: An Additional Mathematics 0606 or Pearson 4CH1 specialist is found among tutors who have prepared candidates for those papers anywhere in the Gulf timezone. For families in Baniyas, Mussafah and Al Maqtaa, where local individual supply for Extended science is thin, that changes what is available rather than merely what is convenient.

whyPoints.title: The cases against individual tuition are on the page
whyPoints.description: Tier ceilings, missed entry deadlines, no practice between sessions and whole-timetable collapse are all situations where buying hours is poor value, and they are written out above. A comparison that never argues against its own product is a brochure, and a parent reading this market deserves better than another brochure.

faqs.question: What does one-to-one teaching actually give my child that a class of twenty-four cannot?
faqs.answer: Three measurable things. Producing time: roughly forty minutes of writing in a sixty-minute session against ten to fifteen in a class. Corrected attempts: four or more a session against about one a week. And feedback latency: seconds instead of days, which is what makes a habit cheap to break, because the error is interrupted while it is being performed. The fourth, less countable, is that a tutor hears the student's reasoning aloud, and misconceptions live in the reasoning rather than in the written answer.

faqs.question: Is a small group of four cheaper per mark gained than individual sessions?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on what is wrong. If the problem is that your child does too little practice rather than practises wrongly, a group that enforces structure at a lower fee per student is reasonable value. If the practice is happening and the marks are not moving, the gap is a specific diagnosable habit, and a habit needs interrupting at the moment it occurs, which a group cannot do for one student. Compare cost per corrected attempt rather than cost per hour; a third of the price for a quarter of the marking is not a saving.

faqs.question: How long should a single IGCSE session be, sixty minutes or ninety?
faqs.answer: Ninety when there is a real content gap, because the useful sequence is diagnose, teach, then have the student complete a timed attempt in the same sitting, and sixty minutes often ends before the attempt. That leaves the week's practice unsupervised at the point it matters most. Sixty works well for fluency and technique work, and two forty-five-minute sessions a week work better still for things like algebraic manipulation or trace tables, because they halve the interval in which a wrong method can be rehearsed into a habit.

faqs.question: What should the tutor tell me after the very first session?
faqs.answer: One sentence naming the problem narrowly enough that it could be proved wrong. Not that your child needs to show more detail, but something closer to: loses three to five marks a paper on mole calculations because relative formula mass is worked out from memory instead of written down. A statement like that lets you judge progress in four weeks. General reassurance after session one will still be general reassurance in March, and by then you will have paid for twenty hours without a way to assess any of them.

faqs.question: Why do command words matter so much more than parents expect?
faqs.answer: Because the mark structure follows them. Describe awards marks for observable features with no causation; explain requires a mechanism; compare wants both sides weighed in one sentence; calculate wants method and a unit; evaluate wants a judgement reached rather than a list. A student who treats these as synonyms writes correct content in the wrong shape and scores badly across every paper they sit. It is the highest-yield thing an individual session teaches, and it needs the student's own answer in front of them, which is why classes rarely manage it.

faqs.question: My child understands the subject but the marks are poor. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three things, and a marked script tells you which. Method not written, so method marks on multi-step questions go unclaimed even when the final answer is right. Command word misread, so the answer addresses a different question from the one printed. Or pacing, where the last questions are blank rather than wrong. All three are technique rather than knowledge, all three respond quickly to individual work, and none of them improves with more content teaching, which is the usual and expensive first response.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both maths and physics for my child at Extended level?
faqs.answer: At Core and lower Extended, often yes, because much of the physics difficulty is mathematical. At the top of Extended it is usually better to split, since the mark-winning detail becomes specification-specific: which practical paper is sat, how observations must be phrased, how graphs are expected to be drawn. There is also a practical trap. Two subjects in one weekly hour normally becomes one subject plus the last fifteen minutes. If budget allows one slot, put the specialist on the weaker subject and use the school's clinic for the other.

faqs.question: How many individual sessions before I can tell whether this tutor is right?
faqs.answer: Four, if they are structured for it. Session one diagnoses from a marked script and produces a one-sentence problem statement. Sessions two and three teach and practise the named component. Session four sets a timed attempt at the same question type and scores it. You then hold a before and an after on comparable work, which is the only honest basis for a decision. Four weeks of warm reports with no repeat attempt anywhere in them is not evidence, however pleasant the sessions have been.

faqs.question: Do individual tutors in Abu Dhabi need a licence to teach my child privately?
faqs.answer: They need a permit. Private tutoring in the UAE runs through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring privately without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask to see it before the first paid session; it costs nothing to hold.

faqs.question: Is it allowed for a teacher at my child's own school to take them for paid sessions?
faqs.answer: Not their own students. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, as reported in the press, prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on a summary, including this one. The practical point stands either way: a tutor offering to teach your child privately while teaching them in school is offering something they should not.

faqs.question: How much practice should my child do between individual sessions?
faqs.answer: Small, specific and checked. One question set of fifteen to thirty minutes, on the exact question type worked on in the session, handed back at the start of the next lesson. The session diagnoses and the week repairs, which means a student doing nothing between sessions will show a flat error rate across two months of good teaching. If the set work is not happening, the right response is to find out why rather than to buy more hours, because more hours will produce the same flat line at twice the cost.

faqs.question: When should individual tuition stop?
faqs.answer: When the component stops losing marks, which is usually before the exams rather than at them. A plan should narrow across a term: fewer components, fewer hours, a more specific target. If a tutor is still working across the whole syllabus in week ten, the engagement has become attendance. The healthy end state is that the student runs their own timed practice in the final weeks, with the tutor available for a short block if a mock reveals something new. Open-ended weekly tuition to the last day is common and rarely necessary.

faqs.question: Is individual tuition worth it if my child is entered for the Core tier?
faqs.answer: It can be, for a specific purpose, but check the entry first. The Core papers do not contain the questions the top grades are awarded for, so the ceiling is set by the tier rather than by the teaching. Where individual work pays on Core is completeness: most Core candidates lose grades by leaving questions unattempted, and the proportion of a paper attempted is the fastest thing to move. If the family's target sits above the Core ceiling, the conversation to have is with the subject lead about the tier, in writing.

faqs.question: What happens in an individual session if my child will not talk?
faqs.answer: A good tutor stops talking too, and puts a question in front of them instead. Silence in a one-to-one session is usually a response to being asked to perform conversationally, and it resolves when the task is written rather than spoken. If it does not resolve across two sessions, the match is wrong and should be changed rather than persisted with; some teenagers will work for one adult and not another for reasons neither can articulate. Use the free trial to see which you have before paying for a term.

faqs.question: How do I stop a weekly session from drifting into general homework help?
faqs.answer: Write the scope down and ask for it in the session note each week. Homework help is reactive and open-ended by nature, which is why most tuition drifts into it: there is always something due tomorrow. The discipline is to name one component, work it until a timed repeat attempt improves, then name the next one. Agree with the tutor that homework can take the last ten minutes if it must, and that the first forty belong to the named component regardless of what is due.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a coursework folder without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary needs stating at the first session rather than during a deadline week. A tutor may teach the skills, explain the assessment criteria, discuss a plan, ask questions about a draft and give written feedback on what the student has produced. Supplying text or reshaping a paragraph until the sentences are no longer the student's is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the tutor. Say that to your child directly: the person who loses the qualification is them, not the adult who helped.

abu-dhabi/1-to-1-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Bring a marked script and take the trial
abu-dhabi/1-to-1-igcse-tutor.closingBody: A 1-to-1 IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi is worth paying for when there is a diagnosed, specific gap and someone to interrupt it while it happens. So start with evidence rather than a booking: find the most recent marked paper, note the specification code and the tier, and look at where the marks actually went. Then take the free trial lesson, one per family and no card details taken, and watch how long your child spends writing. Expect a one-sentence problem statement at the end of the first full session, and a timed repeat attempt by the fourth. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the emirate.

intro.heading: Why a strong school still leaves a Higher Level gap
paragraphs: Al Bandar is the waterfront end of Al Raha Beach: apartments and townhouses around a marina, a short walk or a two-minute drive from a British school that continues into the Diploma Programme, and a few minutes further from a full IB continuum school in Al Raha Gardens. By any measure these are good schools, and the families here know it. That is exactly why the tutoring question in this community looks different from the question in a district with a long commute and a thin school choice.

Nobody in Al Bandar is hiring a tutor because the teaching is poor. They are hiring one because a class of eighteen Higher Level chemists moves at a pace set by the middle of the room, and because certain components get almost no airtime anywhere. Paper 3 of Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is an extended investigation; most schools set one, perhaps two, across two years, because there is simply no room in the scheme of work for more. A student can therefore arrive at the examination having practised a component worth a substantial share of the grade exactly twice.

The same pattern repeats across the assessment. Internal assessment criteria are published in letters with mark allocations attached, and very few students have ever had those descriptors read to them in plain English. They write a competent report, score in the middle of every criterion, and nobody can tell them which sentence would have moved them up a band. The Extended Essay allocates its largest single block of marks to critical thinking, and the most common failure is an essay that summarises its sources beautifully and never argues with them.

The decisions are the third gap. Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation is a choice made in Year 11, frequently on the basis of which looks easier, and it has consequences for degree eligibility that only surface during applications. Three Higher Levels where one is a genuine stretch is a reasonable plan with a predictable cost: the stretch subject will need hours, and it is better to budget for them in September than to discover them in February, when the coursework calendar has already closed in around the student and there is no spare week left to spend.

Lessons here run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For a community that wants a component specialist rather than general subject support, that is the whole argument. The number of people who can teach Paper 3 technique properly and happen to be free to drive to a marina apartment at six in the evening is very small; the number who can do it on a screen is not.

abu-dhabi/al-bandar.programmesIntro: Al Bandar enquiries concentrate at the top of the school: Diploma Higher Level work, the coursework components, and the IGCSE year immediately before them. The notes below describe the component pressure in each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Levels, three Standard Levels, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. The internal assessment is the same component with the same criteria at both levels, which surprises families: a Standard Level student needs the same supervision hours for a report as a Higher Level one, even though the taught content is lighter.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session, which compresses everything into the autumn and early spring of Year 13: coursework drafts, the Extended Essay submission, predicted grades and university deadlines. An Al Bandar student should be finishing the Extended Essay before mock season rather than alongside it. Confirm every IB date with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org rather than with any date found on a tutoring site.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The year that sets up the Higher Level decision. A high Extended grade is necessary but not sufficient for a comfortable Higher Level science, because the Diploma rewards handling uncertainty, criticising a method and arguing from data rather than reproducing content accurately.
programmes.countryNote: Entry deadlines sit months before the papers. Cambridge sets final entries for the March 2027 series at 27 November 2026, with examinations from 3 February to 4 March 2027, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones, warning that candidates using the wrong zone version carry that risk. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, reported as descriptors. The useful thing about the MYP for a student heading into the Diploma is that it trains criterion reading early, provided somebody explains the descriptors. Where that does not happen, the student arrives at the internal assessment with the same blind spot five years later.
programmes.countryNote: Al Bandar sits between a British school running IGCSE and a full continuum school running the MYP, so neighbours' children frequently follow different routes to the same Diploma. For a parent comparing them, the honest position is that neither route is a disadvantage; what matters is whether the student has been taught to read a descriptor and write to it.

abu-dhabi/al-bandar.subjectsIntro: The list below is weighted towards the Higher Level subjects and components Al Bandar families actually ask about, with the specific place marks are lost in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers and further calculus, and a Paper 3 that asks for sustained investigation in a single extended context. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Marks go on justification: the assumption stated, the step shown, the conclusion tied back to the question.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator use is assumed throughout, and the statistical routines decide whole questions: regression, chi-squared, hypothesis testing. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams. Students who treat it as the easier option find the modelling questions unforgiving.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the heaviest Higher Level load, and the reactivity patterns reward memory combined with reasoning rather than either alone. The internal assessment's evaluation criterion is where most Al Bandar students leave marks on the table.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circuits are where the quantitative work hardens. Uncertainty propagation is examined in Paper 2 and again in the investigation, and a student who can state a relationship but not carry an uncertainty through it loses marks twice for the same gap.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Precision of language decides extended answers: the right terms in the right order, not a correct process described in everyday words. The investigation requires a statistical test chosen and justified, which catches students who took biology to avoid mathematics.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy under time pressure carries more marks than written fluency. Axes mislabelled, a shift drawn where a movement along was needed, or an unmarked new equilibrium cost marks no explanation recovers. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that reward arithmetic discipline.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1, the guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, is the component with the least classroom time and the widest mark spread. The Individual Oral is a separate skill: a structured ten-minute argument linking a global issue to two works, delivered under time.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Command terms do the grading. Distinguish, evaluate and examine want different structures, and a strong general answer written against the wrong command term caps in a middling band. The internal assessment needs a real organisation and a genuine decision to analyse.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision
subjects.description: Thirty-four marks across five criteria, with critical thinking carrying twelve of them. Most of the damage is done at the research question: a title too broad produces an essay that describes rather than argues, and no amount of later editing repairs that.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Treated as unassessed by students until the prescribed titles arrive, then rushed. The essay rewards a genuine argument about how knowledge is produced, with real examples, rather than a survey of positions. It is graded alongside the Extended Essay towards the diploma points.

regions.name: Al Zeina

abu-dhabi/al-bandar.modesIntro: The formats below are component-shaped rather than subject-shaped, because that is what families in this precinct ask for.

modes.title: Single-component technique block
modes.description: A defined set of sessions on one component: Paper 3 investigation technique, the evaluation criterion of a science investigation, or Paper 1 unseen analysis. Finite, because the skill is finite. Most students need four to six sessions on a component they have never been taught explicitly, and then practice rather than more teaching.

modes.title: Higher Level weekly subject support
modes.description: The standard arrangement for a stretch Higher Level: one hour a week through the term with the same specialist, practice drawn only from Higher Level material, and marking against the published scheme. The point of keeping it weekly is that Higher Level content accumulates faster than a student can catch up on in a block.

modes.title: Extended Essay and TOK supervision
modes.description: Sequenced across Year 12 and the start of Year 13: scope the research question, learn what each criterion asks, draft alone, then two review rounds. The reflections are planned from the start rather than written at the end, because criterion E is designed to detect exactly that.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, component by component
paragraphs: Families choosing Higher Levels generally understand that the content is heavier. What catches them out is that the difference is not uniform across components, so a student can be comfortable with the extra material and still be badly exposed on one paper.

In the sciences, Higher Level questions reach further into the syllabus but sit in the same paper structure, which means practice has to come from Higher Level papers only. A student drilling Standard Level questions because they are easier to find is practising the wrong difficulty, and will meet the real thing cold. In mathematics the difference is structural: Higher Level adds a third paper that behaves nothing like the other two.

The internal assessment is the component that surprises people most, because it does not change. Same component, same criteria, same marks at both levels. A Standard Level chemistry student therefore needs the same supervision hours for an investigation as a Higher Level one, which means a student with three Standard Level sciences has three full reports to write and no reduced requirement anywhere.

The admissions consequence runs the other way. Higher Level grades carry the weight in university offers, and the related degree usually names the subject at Higher Level as a prerequisite. That makes an hour spent on a stretch Higher Level worth more, in admissions terms, than the same hour on a comfortable Standard Level - which is a useful way for an Al Bandar family to decide where a limited budget goes.

sections.heading: The criteria by letter, and what each descriptor is actually asking for
paragraphs: No competing page found in this market names a single assessment criterion. That is a strange omission, because the criteria are published, they carry specific mark allocations, and a student who has had them explained in plain language writes a measurably better piece. Most students have never had that conversation; they have been given a checklist and a word limit.

Take the science investigation. Four criteria, each carrying six marks, and the one students lose most reliably is evaluation. The descriptor wants specific weaknesses, their effect on the result, and realistic improvements. What students write is a paragraph about human error and needing more time, which could be appended to any experiment ever conducted and therefore scores almost nothing. Six marks are available there and they are among the easiest on the whole report to earn once the student knows what is wanted.

The Extended Essay is the clearest case of all. Thirty-four marks across five criteria, and twelve of them - more than a third - sit on critical thinking. An essay that summarises its sources accurately and does not interrogate them is a middling essay by construction, however well written. Criterion E, engagement, carries six marks and is assessed through the reflections, which is precisely why reflections written in the final week read as thin: the criterion was designed to detect that.

The table lists the components and letters Al Bandar students ask about most. Criteria and mark allocations change between syllabus versions, so treat this as orientation and confirm the exact wording and marks against your child's current subject guide, which their teacher or Diploma coordinator can provide.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
paragraphs: This decision is made in Year 11, often on the basis of a rumour about which is easier, and it determines which degrees a student can apply to two years later. It deserves half an hour of proper thought and almost never gets it.

The two courses are different subjects wearing the same name. Analysis and Approaches is algebra, functions, calculus and proof, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator, and at Higher Level it adds proof by induction, complex numbers and further calculus. Applications and Interpretation is statistics, modelling and data, with technology assumed throughout, and at Higher Level it adds matrices, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams. Neither is soft. Students who choose Applications expecting an easy route find the modelling questions unforgiving, and students who choose Analysis without comfort for abstraction find Paper 1 brutal.

The admissions position is the part to get right. Engineering, physics and mathematics degrees normally expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and Applications is rarely sufficient on its own for those routes. Economics, business, psychology and the social sciences generally accept either, sometimes with a preference. For medicine and the life sciences, acceptance varies by institution. The only safe method is to read the published entry requirements for the specific courses on the shortlist, including the universities in the Emirates, rather than relying on a general rule from a tutoring page, this one included.

If the decision has already been made and looks wrong, it is not always fatal. A switch between routes is possible early in Year 12 at most schools, and after that the realistic plan is to work the chosen route hard and build the application around what it does support. Where a student has Applications and wants engineering, the conversation to have is with admissions offices now rather than with a tutor in Year 13.

sections.heading: Paper 3 and the other components nobody has time to drill
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has a component that the scheme of work cannot give proper time to, and it is almost always the one that rewards practice most. Naming them is the single most useful thing a page like this can do for an Al Bandar parent, because these are the components where a small number of targeted hours changes a grade.

In Higher Level mathematics it is Paper 3. It is a sustained investigation inside one extended context, with questions that build on each other, and a student who has only ever answered discrete questions finds the structure unfamiliar even when every individual step is within reach. Schools typically set one or two across two years. Four or five properly reviewed attempts changes performance on it substantially, and that is a finite piece of work rather than a term of teaching.

In the sciences it is the evaluation criterion of the investigation and the data-based questions that ask for criticism of a method rather than recall. In English A it is Paper 1, the guided analysis of an unseen text, which has the widest mark spread of any component and the least classroom time because set texts have to be taught. In economics it is the fifteen-mark evaluation question written under time pressure. In Theory of Knowledge it is everything, because students treat the course as unassessed until the prescribed titles appear.

The common feature is that none of these is a content gap. A student losing marks on Paper 3 usually knows the mathematics; a student losing marks on an unseen text usually reads well. What is missing is the shape of the answer, and that is taught in a handful of sessions and then practised. It is also why a tutor who asks which component rather than which subject is a better buy than one who asks how many hours you want.
bullets: Higher Level maths Paper 3: sustained investigation, practised once or twice in two years
Sciences: the evaluation criterion and the method-criticism questions
English A Paper 1: widest mark spread, least classroom time
Economics: the fifteen-mark evaluation written against the clock

sections.heading: What a Higher Level specialist costs, and why the pool is small
paragraphs: A fair question from a community that can afford to choose: why does a Higher Level specialist cost more than a general subject tutor, and is the difference real? The answer is supply. The number of teachers who have taught Higher Level chemistry through several examination cycles, marked to the published scheme and supervised a dozen investigations is small in any city. The number who have done the same for Paper 3 of Analysis and Approaches is smaller still.

The published market bands reflect it. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and 300 an hour. An IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist sits between AED 200 and 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Unitors advertising IB tuition from AED 200. A premium named tutor can reach AED 650, which BartyED publishes. Budget tutors, usually university students, start nearer AED 45 to 65 an hour on EdFlik's own published figures. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work.

The difference buys something specific rather than prestige. A specialist can tell you, from a marked script, which of three causes is costing the marks and roughly how long each takes to fix. A generalist teaches the topic again. For a component problem - Paper 3 shape, the evaluation criterion, unseen analysis - the generalist's hour often does nothing at all, which makes it the more expensive option despite the lower rate.

One caution about how specialists are described. Nobody should be presented to you as a current examiner unless that status can be evidenced, and examiner status should never be used to imply access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or paper content. Ask what the person has taught, for how many cycles, and to what level, which are checkable questions. IB Gram quotes after a consultation and a trial lesson rather than publishing a rate card, because the span between a primary reading session and Paper 3 supervision is too wide for one number.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay and TOK, counted backwards from Year 13
paragraphs: These two components are graded together towards the diploma points, and both are lost in the same way: by being left until the term when everything else is also due. An Al Bandar family can avoid that entirely with a timeline, and the timeline is not complicated.

The Extended Essay should have a research question settled before the summer between Year 12 and Year 13, and a complete first draft written during that summer. That is the single highest-value piece of planning in the Diploma, because the autumn of Year 13 carries internal assessment drafts, predicted grades and university applications at once, and anything still unwritten by then competes with all of it. A question settled early is also a question that can be narrowed when the research shows it is too broad, which is the most common structural failure.

Theory of Knowledge needs less time but earlier attention. Students treat it as unassessed because it has no content to revise, then meet the prescribed titles and discover that the essay wants a genuine argument about how knowledge is produced, supported by real examples they have not been collecting. Keeping a running note of examples from their own subjects through Year 12 costs nothing and makes the essay straightforward.

Specific IB dates are not published on this page. Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session, which is safe to say, but no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB's own site. Get the submission dates from your school's Diploma coordinator, who works to internal deadlines earlier than the IB's in any case, and build the plan on those. A tutoring provider quoting IB dates without naming its source is guessing.
bullets: Research question settled before the summer between Year 12 and Year 13
Complete first draft written in that summer, not in the autumn term
Collect TOK examples from real subject work through Year 12
Work to the school's internal deadlines, which precede the IB's own

sections.heading: Choosing three Higher Levels in Year 11
paragraphs: This is the decision that creates most of the work described on the rest of this page, and it is taken in a Year 11 spring term when the student has no experience of Diploma assessment to judge by. Al Bandar families tend to approach it well informed about the schools and badly informed about the subjects, because the information available is about results rather than about what each course asks for.

Three principles hold up. The first is that a Higher Level choice should be driven by the degree intention where one exists, because the related subject at Higher Level is usually the named prerequisite and a missing one is very hard to work around later. The second is that two comfortable Higher Levels and one genuine stretch is a workable plan, while three stretches is not: the coursework load alone makes it unsustainable, since each subject brings its own internal assessment regardless of level. The third is that the Standard Levels are not a rest. They carry the same internal assessment requirement as their Higher Level versions, so a student with three Standard sciences has three full reports to write.

The signals worth reading from Year 11 are specific rather than general. For Higher Level mathematics, comfort with abstraction and with being wrong for twenty minutes matters more than the Extended grade. For the sciences, how a student handled the practical write-ups and whether they can criticise a method predicts the investigation better than content marks. For English A at Higher Level, performance on unseen material predicts Paper 1, which is where the mark spread sits.

Where the mix turns out wrong, the window to change it is narrow - usually the first weeks of Year 12 - and after that the realistic plan is to resource the stretch subject deliberately. That is a better outcome than drifting: a family that accepts in September that one Higher Level will need a weekly hour all year spends less, and gets more, than one that discovers the same thing from a February report.
bullets: Let the degree intention drive the Higher Level choice where one exists
Two comfortable Higher Levels and one stretch works; three stretches does not
Standard Levels carry the same internal assessment load as Higher Levels
Read Year 11 signals: handling of practicals, comfort with abstraction, unseen work

sections.heading: The honesty boundary on the investigation and the essay
paragraphs: A community that can afford to buy a great deal of help needs the line drawn clearly, because at least one site competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Submitting purchased work is malpractice under IB rules. The sanction falls on the student, not on the seller, and it can reach the diploma itself.

What a tutor may legitimately do is more than most families realise. Teach the subject content the assessment rests on. Read each criterion descriptor aloud and explain in plain language what it is asking for, which is most of the value in the first two sessions. Interrogate a research question until it is narrow enough to answer in the word count. Read a draft the student has written and identify where the argument does not follow, where the data analysis does not support the conclusion, and where the reflection is thin. Teach referencing conventions properly.

What a tutor may not do is supply text. No paragraph, no rewritten conclusion, no processed dataset dropped into a results section, no bibliography typed out for copying. The subtler breach is heavy line-editing: a sentence in the submitted document composed by the tutor is a sentence the student did not write, and the supervisor's authenticity declaration then says something untrue. Similarity checking applies to the final submission.

The sequence that works is also the sequence that teaches. Scope the question in one session. Learn the criteria in a second, before any writing. Draft alone. Bring the draft and leave with a list of specific problems. Solve them alone. Repeat once. That is about four to six hours of paid supervision across a term, it produces a better piece than ten hours of someone improving a draft, and the student leaves able to do the next one without help.
bullets: Allowed: content teaching, criterion explanation, scoping, feedback on the student's own draft
Not allowed: any tutor-composed text in the submitted document
Heavy line-editing is the same breach wearing a respectable name
Four to six supervision hours across a term, properly sequenced, is usually enough

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: Paper 3, the evaluation criterion, the unseen text on Paper 1, the fifteen-mark evaluation question. A component brief gets you a specialist in four to six sessions of finite work. A subject brief gets you a term of general teaching, which for a component problem often changes nothing at all.

process.title: Send a marked script or a returned draft
process.description: The diagnosis comes from evidence. A marked Paper 2, a returned investigation draft with the teacher's criterion comments, or a mock script tells a specialist which of several causes is operating. That five-minute read replaces an hour of guessing and usually shortens the plan rather than lengthening it.

process.title: Confirm the level and the route
process.description: Higher or Standard, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and which syllabus version the school is teaching. Practice material has to match: Standard Level questions train the wrong difficulty for a Higher Level student, and criteria differ between syllabus versions.

process.title: Trial lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: One hour with the person who would teach the block, not a coordinator. It ends with a written view: which cause is operating, how many sessions it should take, and what the student needs to do between them. If the match is wrong we rematch rather than persuade.

process.title: Finish the block, then stop
process.description: A component block ends when the student can self-mark against the published scheme, which is usually four to six sessions. Continuing past that point buys attendance rather than marks. Where a second component needs work, it gets its own block and sometimes its own specialist.

whyPoints.title: Component specialists, not subject generalists
whyPoints.description: The requests from this precinct are specific - Paper 3, criterion evaluation, unseen analysis - and they are matched to someone who has taught that component through several examination cycles. Online delivery is what makes that pool reachable from a marina apartment at six in the evening.

whyPoints.title: Criteria explained before any writing
whyPoints.description: Criterion letters and their mark allocations are read and worked to in plain language in the first sessions. No competing page found in this market names a single criterion, and students who have never had the descriptors explained write competent work that scores in the middle of every band.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level practice from Higher Level material
whyPoints.description: Standard Level questions are easier to find and train the wrong difficulty. Practice is drawn from Higher Level papers only, marked against the published scheme, so the mark the student sees means what it will mean in May.

whyPoints.title: Route decisions checked against degrees
whyPoints.description: The Analysis or Applications choice is tested against the published entry requirements for the specific courses on the shortlist, not against a general rule. Where a route does not support an intention, the useful conversation is with admissions offices rather than with a tutor.

whyPoints.title: Finite blocks that end
whyPoints.description: A component block finishes when the student can self-mark against the scheme. Continuing beyond that sells attendance. For a household that can afford open-ended tutoring, knowing when to stop is a genuine part of the service.

whyPoints.title: No claims that cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No regulator accreditation, no self-asserted ratings, no examiner status asserted without evidence, and no suggestion that examiner status gives access to marking decisions, boundaries or paper content. Ask what someone has taught and for how long, which is checkable.

faqs.question: Our school is strong. Why would an Al Bandar student need a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Because a class of eighteen Higher Level students moves at the pace of the middle of the room, and because some components get almost no airtime anywhere. Paper 3 of Higher Level mathematics is an extended investigation, and most schemes of work can only fit one or two across two years. Criterion descriptors are published with marks attached and are rarely read to students in plain language. Neither of those is a teaching failure; they are consequences of a timetable, and they are what a specialist block addresses.

faqs.question: What exactly is Paper 3 in Higher Level mathematics?
faqs.answer: A sustained investigation set inside one extended context, with questions that build on each other rather than standing alone. Students who have only answered discrete questions find the structure unfamiliar even when every individual step is within reach, which is why performance on it often understates the student. Four or five properly reviewed attempts changes that substantially. Since schools typically set one or two in two years, it is the clearest example of a finite piece of work that a short block of sessions can genuinely fix.

faqs.question: Which criterion do students lose most marks on in a science investigation?
faqs.answer: Evaluation, by a clear margin. Six marks are available and the descriptor asks for specific weaknesses, their effect on the result, and realistic improvements. What most students write is a paragraph about human error and needing more time, which could be attached to any experiment ever performed and therefore earns almost nothing. It is among the easiest blocks of marks on the report to earn once a student knows what is wanted. Confirm the current criteria and marks against your child's subject guide, since these change between syllabus versions.

faqs.question: How is the Extended Essay actually marked?
faqs.answer: Across five criteria totalling thirty-four marks, with critical thinking carrying twelve of them - more than a third of the essay. That single allocation explains the most common failure: an essay that summarises its sources accurately and never interrogates them is a middling essay by construction, however elegantly written. Criterion E, engagement, carries six marks and is assessed through the reflections, which is exactly why reflections written in the last week read as thin. Confirm the current criteria with your child's supervisor or coordinator.

faqs.question: Did we choose the wrong maths route if our child wants engineering?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is worth checking now rather than in Year 13. Engineering, physics and mathematics degrees normally expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and Applications and Interpretation is rarely sufficient on its own for those routes. A switch is often possible early in Year 12 and rarely afterwards. If the route is fixed, the productive conversation is with the admissions offices of the specific universities on your shortlist, including those in the Emirates, rather than with any tutoring provider's general advice.

faqs.question: Is the internal assessment easier at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: No, and this surprises most families. It is the same component with the same criteria and the same marks at both levels. A Standard Level chemistry student needs the same supervision hours for an investigation as a Higher Level one, even though the taught content is lighter. A student with three Standard Level sciences therefore has three full reports to write with no reduced requirement anywhere, which is worth factoring into the Year 12 workload rather than discovering in the spring.

faqs.question: Can we practise with Standard Level papers if Higher Level ones run out?
faqs.answer: Better not. Standard Level questions are easier to find and they train the wrong difficulty, so a Higher Level student who drills them meets the real thing cold. The more productive approach when Higher Level material is thin is to re-sit papers already attempted, under time, and mark them against the published scheme again - repeat attempts on a hard paper teach more than first attempts on an easy one. Papers are referenced and linked from the official source rather than supplied as downloads.

faqs.question: Why does a Higher Level specialist cost more than a general tutor?
faqs.answer: Supply. The number of teachers who have taught Higher Level chemistry through several examination cycles, marked against the published scheme and supervised a dozen investigations is small in any city. Published market bands reflect it: qualified subject tutors online sit around AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. For a component problem the cheaper generalist hour frequently achieves nothing, which makes it the more expensive option despite the lower rate.

faqs.question: Which English component causes the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Paper 1, the guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text. It has the widest mark spread of any component in the subject and the least classroom time, because the set texts have to be taught and there is only so much timetable. Students who read well still lose marks because the shape of the answer is unfamiliar: what to notice first, how to structure an argument about an unseen passage under time, how much to quote. That is a handful of sessions of technique followed by practice, not a term of teaching.

faqs.question: When should our Year 12 start the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: The research question should be settled before the summer between Year 12 and Year 13, and a complete first draft written during that summer. The autumn of Year 13 carries internal assessment drafts, predicted grades and university applications at once, so anything unwritten by then competes with all of it. An early question is also one that can still be narrowed when the research shows it is too broad, which is the most common structural failure. Work to your school's internal deadlines, which precede the IB's own.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a component block usually take?
faqs.answer: Four to six for a component a student has never been taught explicitly, then practice rather than more teaching. The block ends when the student can self-mark their own attempt against the published scheme and arrive at roughly the mark a teacher would give. Continuing past that point buys attendance instead of marks. Where a second component also needs work it gets its own block, and sometimes its own specialist, rather than being folded into an open-ended weekly arrangement.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to apartments in Al Raha Beach?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. In this precinct the trade is particularly clear: the school run is short, so the household does not need a tutor to solve a logistics problem. What it needs is a specialist in one component, and the number of people who can teach Paper 3 technique properly and also happen to be free to drive to a marina apartment at six on a Tuesday is very small. Online delivery removes that constraint entirely.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be described as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Only if the status can be evidenced, and even then it should never be used to imply access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content. Examiner claims are common in this market and frequently unverifiable. The checkable questions are more useful: what has this person taught, at what level, for how many examination cycles, and have they marked to the published scheme. Those answers tell you what you actually need to know about whether they can read your child's script usefully.

faqs.question: Will you proofread our child's essay before submission?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense most people mean. A tutor can read a draft the student wrote and identify where the argument fails, where the evidence does not support the claim, where a criterion is unmet and where the referencing is wrong. What cannot happen is editing to completion: a sentence in the submitted document composed by the tutor is a sentence the student did not write, and the supervisor's authenticity declaration then says something untrue. The student leaves with a list of problems and solves them alone.

faqs.question: What do you actually send after a session?
faqs.answer: The annotated work from the lesson and a short written note saying what was covered, what was marked against the scheme and what to do before next time. For a component block the note also records how close the student's self-marking came to the tutor's, because closing that gap is the measure that matters. What you will not get is a weekly percentage or progress score, since a number invented by the person being paid is not evidence of anything.

abu-dhabi/al-bandar.closingHeading: Name the component and the rest is straightforward
abu-dhabi/al-bandar.closingBody: For an Al Bandar family the shortest route to a useful arrangement is to stop asking for a subject and start naming the component. Send a marked script or a returned draft, say whether it is Higher or Standard and which maths route, and the plan is a finite block with a specialist: four to six sessions, criteria explained in plain language, Higher Level practice marked against the published scheme, and an end point defined as the student being able to self-mark. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, every market figure here names its source, and criterion details should be confirmed against the current subject guide.

intro.heading: An established island district, and the questions its households actually ask
paragraphs: Al Bateen is one of Abu Dhabi's older residential districts, running down the island's western shore past the marina, the dhow yard and the executive airport. It has not been rebuilt in the way the eastern waterfront has, and the household mix reflects that. Multi-generation Emirati family compounds sit near embassy residences and near expatriate households that have been in the emirate for a decade or more. Very few families here are in their first year in the UAE.

That changes the enquiry. In the newer mainland communities, the first tutoring question is usually about a curriculum transition that happened eighteen months ago. In Al Bateen it is more often about a decision three or four years ahead: which Arabic route a bilingual child should take, whether Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation keeps a medical or engineering degree open, and what the Ministry of Education will require when the certificate is used inside the UAE.

Bilingual households carry a particular load that nobody outside them sees. A child who speaks Arabic at home and sits an international programme in English may be entered for Arabic as a first language, which is an academically demanding literature course, not a conversation class. Being fluent at home does not make a student ready for literary analysis in Standard Arabic, and the gap between spoken fluency and written register is where marks go. The reverse happens too: a strong Arabic reader placed in a second-language class, bored for two years, and quietly losing access to a bilingual diploma that was available all along.

The second recurring theme is the certificate itself. Families who intend their child to study at a UAE university, or to use an international qualification for employment inside the country, need the equivalency rules rather than general reassurance. Those rules are published and specific: the British track counts five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus an Advanced Level or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. Getting that wrong in Year 10 is expensive to fix in Year 13, and the subject grid is usually signed off long before anyone reads the requirement.

Everything below is organised around those decisions. There are tables on the Arabic routes, on what each curriculum must show for equivalency, on the Maths route choice, on the word limits that cap every written component, on what the market charges in AED, and on whether the person teaching your child is legally permitted to do so. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; the delivery model is one-to-one tuition over live video, and the honest advantage in an established district like this one is access to specialists in narrow subjects rather than to whoever lives nearby.

abu-dhabi/al-bateen.programmesIntro: Three programme routes account for almost all Al Bateen enquiries. The useful distinction between them is not difficulty but how early a decision locks in, because the island's established families tend to plan several years out.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three taken at Higher Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS forming the core. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, with up to three additional points available from TOK and the Extended Essay together. The group structure is the part that matters for planning: a student cannot simply drop a language or a science to make room.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Bateen bilingual student the Diploma offers a genuine advantage, because Arabic can be taken as a Language A alongside English A under the bilingual diploma route. That decision affects the whole six-subject grid and should be taken in MYP 5 or Year 11, not in the first month of DP1 when the timetable has already been built.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led framework organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than subject periods, ending in the Grade 5 or 6 Exhibition. There are no external exams. Reporting is descriptive, which parents moving from a graded system often find hard to read, and the specific skills a child is behind on can be hidden inside positive general comments.
programmes.countryNote: The practical PYP question in Al Bateen households is bilingual literacy: a child reading well in English and barely at all in Standard Arabic. The time to address that is in the primary years, when short regular Arabic reading sessions still feel normal, rather than in MYP 4 when the written register expected jumps sharply.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written examinations at the end of a two-year course, with tiered entry in many Cambridge subjects. The number of subjects taken varies by school, which matters because UAE equivalency counts five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 and excludes Arabic and Islamic education from that count.
programmes.countryNote: One competitor page ranking for this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The published requirement is five accredited subjects, with Arabic and Islamic education outside the count. An Al Bateen family planning a subject grid should work from the Ministry's own wording and verify it directly rather than from a tutoring page.

abu-dhabi/al-bateen.subjectsIntro: This selection reflects what Al Bateen families request most, weighted towards languages, humanities and the two Mathematics routes. Each note says what the component actually assesses, because the subject name alone does not tell you which tutor to ask for.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A literature course taught and assessed in Standard Arabic, with unseen textual analysis, comparative essay work and an individual oral. Spoken fluency at home is not the same preparation as the written register this demands. Marks are lost on structure and on literary terminology rather than on comprehension.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: A second-language course with listening, reading, writing and an individual oral based on stimulus material. The commonest misplacement in bilingual households is a heritage speaker entered at the wrong level, either bored at SL or exposed at Arabic A. A diagnostic piece of writing settles it faster than a conversation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-and-calculus route. Higher Level adds Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper worth a fifth of the grade, where the question supplies no method. This is the route most engineering and mathematics degrees name in their prerequisites, which is why the choice is made on destination rather than on comfort.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led work. Perfectly rigorous at Higher Level, and accepted for many degrees, but some mathematics and physics courses name Analysis and Approaches specifically. Marks here are lost in interpretation: a correct model followed by a sentence that misdescribes what a parameter means.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work in Paper 1, essay work in Papers 2 and 3, plus an Internal Assessment capped at 2,200 words. Students lose marks by narrating rather than arguing, and by neglecting the evaluation of origin, purpose and content in source questions. The regional options are a genuine advantage for students in this part of the world.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three Internal Assessment commentaries, each capped at 800 words, built on recent news articles. Diagram precision carries the written papers: an unlabelled axis or a missing new equilibrium caps an otherwise strong evaluation. Higher Level adds quantitative components that reward disciplined working.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as the Ansoff matrix and break-even analysis are easy to learn and easy to apply shallowly. Marks come from applying them to the specific case, with figures, rather than from naming them. The Higher Level research project requires real organisational evidence, which takes planning well before the deadline.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms separate the top grades. The Internal Assessment is where marks are most recoverable, because a tightly framed research question and an honest uncertainty analysis score well without needing an elaborate experiment. Mole calculation slips remain the commonest silent loss.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: For bilingual Al Bateen students whose stronger academic language is Arabic, English B can be the right entry rather than English A. The course assesses conceptual understanding of text type and audience as much as accuracy, and students coached only on grammar underperform on the writing tasks.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: A mandatory subject in UAE private schools, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arab students. Tutoring has to work from the school's approved material, because using different or additional content without Ministry permission is not allowed.

abu-dhabi/al-bateen.regionsIntro: Al Bateen sits at the quiet end of the island, and the neighbourhoods around it determine both the school options and the length of the daily run. These notes are about those practicalities rather than about the view.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Immediately north-east of Al Bateen and effectively continuous with it, a dense mix of apartment towers and older villas. Many Al Bateen families use its clinics, shops and tuition centres, and secondary students often share the same schools, so the two districts generate near-identical subject requests.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Inland from Al Bateen across Khaleej Al Arabi Street, home to The British School Al Khubairat and a long-established villa population. It is the shortest significant school run from Al Bateen and one of the few that stays under twenty minutes in afternoon traffic.

regions.name: The Corniche
regions.note: The island's northern waterfront strip, largely apartment living, reached from Al Bateen in ten to fifteen minutes. Students there sit the same papers but typically have shorter commutes, so their lesson slots start earlier in the afternoon than Al Bateen's island-crossing families.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Reached by bridge from the island's north side and home to Cranleigh Abu Dhabi. For Al Bateen families this is a cross-island run of around half an hour, which makes a second journey for in-home tuition impractical on a school day.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: The British International School Abu Dhabi and Repton Abu Dhabi sit here. From Al Bateen the run crosses the whole island, so families making it usually settle on evening lesson slots from 18:00 Gulf Standard Time onwards.

regions.name: Al Nahyan
regions.note: A central island district between Al Bateen and the eastern waterfront, with a dense mix of schools and a long-established Arabic-speaking population. Requests for Arabic as a first language come heavily from this corridor and from Al Bateen itself.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Off-island to the east, where several British and American schools sit. A handful of Al Bateen families commute out there for a specific programme, which is the longest regular run from this district and the clearest argument for keeping tuition off the road.

schoolClusters.note: This cluster is within a short drive of most Al Bateen addresses and includes both IB Diploma and American programme provision. Because several of these schools serve long-tenure and bilingual households, requests for Arabic at first-language level are proportionally higher here than elsewhere in the emirate.

sections.heading: Who lives in Al Bateen, and why the enquiry is different here
paragraphs: The direct answer: Al Bateen households are predominantly long-tenure, frequently bilingual, and planning several years ahead. Their tutoring requests cluster around language-stream placement, subject-choice decisions with university consequences, and UAE equivalency, rather than around catching up after a recent curriculum change.

The district's composition explains it. This is an older part of the island that was not cleared and rebuilt, so the population turns over slowly. Multi-generation Emirati households sit alongside diplomatic residences and expatriate families who have been here long enough to have a child finishing the Diploma and another in primary. The parents have usually been through one UAE school system already and know what they are asking about, which is not the case in a community that fills up with new arrivals every August.

A useful consequence is that enquiries arrive with better information. An Al Bateen parent is more likely to know the Higher Levels their child is taking, the internal deadline for the Extended Essay, and whether the school enters Cambridge or Pearson papers. That shortens matching considerably, and it changes what a first session should do: less diagnosis of the obvious, more work on the specific component.

The less helpful consequence is that the decisions are heavier. A language-stream misplacement found in DP2 cannot be fixed. A Mathematics route that does not satisfy a degree prerequisite is discovered at application, not at selection. The sections below are weighted towards those irreversible choices because that is where an hour of attention is worth most in this district.

sections.heading: The Arabic routes a bilingual Al Bateen student can be placed in
paragraphs: Arabic is not one subject. Inside a single Al Bateen school year group there may be students taking Arabic as a first language, Arabic as an additional language, Arabic A within the Diploma, Arabic B and Arabic ab initio. These are different courses with different assessments, and a tutor matched to the wrong one wastes the term.

The regulatory layer sits underneath all of it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students.

The commonest misplacement in bilingual households is a heritage speaker entered too high. A child who speaks Arabic at home all day may still have had no formal instruction in literary analysis, grammatical terminology or the written register, because none of those appear in domestic conversation. The reverse error also happens: a genuinely strong Arabic reader parked in a second-language class, bored, and losing the chance at a bilingual diploma.

A short written diagnostic settles this in one session. Ask for a piece of analytical writing in Standard Arabic on an unseen text, not a spoken interview. The result tells you the stream, and it also tells the tutor whether the work needed is vocabulary and script or structure and terminology, which are completely different teaching jobs.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what an Al Bateen school leaver has to be able to show
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a foreign school certificate for use inside the country. It matters at the point of applying to a UAE university or to some employers, and the requirements are published rather than negotiable. Four of the ten competitor query clusters researched for this project mention equivalency nowhere at all.

For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. They must also pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is the detail families most often get wrong when planning a subject grid.

For the American track the requirements are different in kind. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. Those are test thresholds rather than subject counts.

For the IB there is no points figure published that this project has been able to verify on the Ministry's own site, and no such figure is stated here. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject IGCSE requirement, which does not match the five-subject rule in the published source. Treat the table below as a map of what to check, confirm it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, and note that IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees any part of the equivalency process.

sections.heading: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the single decision Al Bateen families ask about most, and it is usually framed as a question about difficulty when it is really a question about destination. Both routes exist at Standard and Higher Level. Both are respectable. They are not interchangeable for every degree, and the constraint comes from the universities rather than from the IB.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and calculus-heavy route. Proof, functions, trigonometry and calculus carry it, and Higher Level adds Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper worth a fifth of the grade in which no method is supplied. Students who have learned procedures without understanding why they work are exposed by that paper more than by any other component in the Diploma.

Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling, statistics and the use of technology, with its own Higher Level content on graph theory and matrices. It is not an easier course; it is a different one. Where it causes problems is at application, because some mathematics, physics and engineering degrees name Analysis and Approaches in their published prerequisites and will not accept the alternative.

The honest method is dull and effective. Write down the three or four degree subjects your child might apply for, read the published entry requirements for each one on the university's own admissions pages, and choose the route that keeps all of them open. Do that in Year 11 or MYP 5. Do not do it on the basis of which teacher the student prefers, and do not take a tutoring page's word for a prerequisite, including this one.
