sections.heading: Building a weekly pattern that survives to March
paragraphs: A pattern that holds has three properties and most arrangements have one. It sits inside the real afternoon rather than an optimistic one. It has a length matched to the work it carries. And it has an agreed rule for what happens when a week goes wrong, because weeks do go wrong and the absence of a rule is what turns one missed session into an abandoned arrangement.

The rule we recommend is simple: a missed session is rescheduled within the same week or converted into set work that is checked at the next session. It is never simply cancelled, because the first cancellation that costs nothing is the one that makes the second easy. Families who agree this at the start lose two or three sessions a term. Families who do not lose closer to eight.

Build the week around the heaviest subject rather than distributing effort evenly. One subject taken seriously, with a long weekend block and a short weekday review, moves measurably. Four subjects at a weekly half hour each do not, and they consume more total time while producing less. This is particularly true in the Diploma, where a single Higher Level grade usually matters more to a university offer than small improvements across three Standard Level subjects.

Then leave the pattern alone for a term. The commonest unforced error is restructuring after three weeks because a mock went badly, which destroys the only continuity the student had. Twelve weeks is the shortest period over which a change in approach can be fairly judged, and the measurement should be an external one: the next marked paper, not an impression.

sections.heading: Ramadan, term breaks and the shape of the UAE academic year
paragraphs: The UAE academic year has a shape that a tutoring plan either respects or fights. Term one runs from late August or early September to mid-December and is the longest teaching block, which makes it the right place for content work and habit building. Term two is short, interrupted and contains the mock season, which makes it the technique term. Term three is examination-focused and, for examination year groups, largely over before it ends.

Ramadan changes the day rather than the year. Private schools across the emirate run shortened hours, children are home considerably earlier, and an early afternoon slot becomes available that exists at no other point in the calendar. Some students work better in that earlier window; older ones often prefer a post-Iftar session, which tends to be calmer than a rushed term-time evening. Either arrangement is better than the common outcome, which is a month of quietly lapsed sessions followed by a late restart.

The long summer break is the only period in which a genuine foundation rebuild is possible, because nothing competes with it. A student entering the final Diploma year or Year 11 with a real content gap should close it in July and August, not in October while new material is arriving. Families in this district often travel for part of the summer, and a live video arrangement follows them, which is one of the practical advantages of the format.

Two smaller points. Eid breaks move each year and are worth checking against any block you have booked. And the week after a term break is almost always a weak week academically, so it is a poor place to schedule a measurement or an important coursework deadline if there is any choice in the matter.

Shortened Ramadan days open an early slot available at no other time

sections.heading: A tutor in the villa against a specialist on a shared screen
paragraphs: Al Rawdah is villa housing, and families here naturally ask about a tutor coming to the house. It is worth answering the question properly. In this market, in-home one-to-one visits run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and comparable listings, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a comparably qualified tutor working online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The visible premium is the travel. The invisible cost is that the available pool shrinks to whoever is willing to drive across the island at the specific hour your afternoon allows, and that filter selects for availability rather than for subject expertise.

IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Abu Dhabi families run one-to-one over live video, and in a district whose binding constraint is the clock, that removes the one variable nobody can control. A tutor stuck on Airport Road is a cancelled session; a tutor on a screen is not.

The format also suits the work this page is about. Marked scripts, mark schemes, timed papers, criteria beside a draft and a calendar of deadlines are all documents, and documents are easier to share and annotate on screen than to pass across a table. What exists afterwards is the annotated file, which the next session can start from.

The honest limitation is attention supervision for younger students. A child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task is harder to hold on video, particularly below thirteen, and for those students we recommend shorter and more frequent sessions with a parent within earshot rather than pretending the format solves everything.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework, and when to buy it
paragraphs: Every programme in this district carries work produced away from the examination hall: a Diploma internal assessment in each subject, the Extended Essay at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600, the MYP Personal Project. That work must be the student's own, and a breach is recorded against the student rather than against anyone helping them, which is why the boundary matters to your family more than it does to us.

A tutor interrogates the research question until it can be answered inside the limit. A tutor says that a planned method will not generate data capable of supporting a conclusion, before the data exists. A tutor reads a draft against the published criteria and names the criterion that is unevidenced, teaches the missing skill and returns the work. A tutor asks a student to justify a paragraph aloud.

A tutor does not supply text, rewrite a section into something the student could not have produced, edit a draft to completion, or hand over a topic, structure or data set ready-made. Nothing is bought in from anywhere. One operation in this market sells completed Diploma internal assessments outright; that is an integrity breach packaged as a service, and the student carries the consequence.

The scheduling point, which is what this page is really about, is that honest coursework help has to be bought early. At the proposal and method stage everything useful is also entirely safe. Three days before submission, the only remaining options are cosmetic or improper. So put the coursework blocks on the calendar in September using the school's own deadline list, not the board's, and the question of crossing a line never arises.
bullets: Questions, methods and criteria coaching, placed early in the process
Feedback against published criteria, on the student's own text only
No supplied text, no rewriting to completion, no ready-made topics or data
Book coursework blocks in September against the school's deadline list

sections.heading: Starting in Al Rawdah, and what we say about availability
paragraphs: The first conversation covers three things and takes about fifteen minutes. Which school and therefore which board and calendar. What time the child is genuinely home, which sets the slot. And the last piece of work a teacher marked, which tells a specialist whether the problem is content, technique or pacing. Families who send the script before the call get considerably more out of it.

Then a diagnostic session rather than an introduction. The tutor works through the script with your child, establishes what is actually happening, and writes down what a term of work would contain and in which slot. You keep that plan whether or not you continue. Occasionally the honest conclusion is that your child needs a protected study hour and a deadline list rather than a tutor, and we say so when that is what the evidence shows.

On availability we are direct. The slot a district like this wants, four to five o'clock on a weekday, is the busiest window in the UAE time zone, and a specific subject at a specific hour may not be available. Rarer Diploma languages and some Higher Level combinations are thin generally. When there is no honest match we say so and offer the nearest real alternative rather than putting a generalist in front of a Higher Level paper.

One market note worth having as a parent. Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Operating without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount you are quoted as unverified. Asking the question costs nothing.
bullets: School, real arrival time and the last marked script, in that order

process.title: Time the afternoon before choosing anything
process.description: School finish, collection, drive and thirty minutes to eat. That sum produces an earliest honest start, which for most Al Rawdah households is four o'clock and for a Saadiyat or Khalifa City school nearer five. Every other decision follows from that number, and skipping it is why arrangements fail in November.

process.title: Ask the school for its own deadline list
process.description: Not the board's dates: the school's internal coursework deadlines, mock windows and report dates for the year. Those are the dates that actually bind a student, they are usually earlier than the board's, and almost no family requests them in September when they would be most useful.

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: Where marks left the page distinguishes a content gap from a technique problem from a pacing problem. Those three need different plans and different session lengths, so the script determines the shape of what we recommend rather than simply confirming that help is needed.

process.title: Match the length to the work
process.description: Ninety minutes at the weekend for a full timed paper or an essay written and dissected; forty-five minutes midweek for marking, drilling and setting. For primary students, twenty-five minutes three times a week. Buying one standard hour for everything is the commonest quiet waste in this market.

process.title: Agree the rule for a bad week
process.description: A missed session is rescheduled inside the same week or converted into set work checked at the next session, never simply cancelled. Families who agree this at the start lose two or three sessions a term. Families who do not lose closer to eight, and usually abandon the arrangement by February.

whyPoints.title: We solve the scheduling problem first
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring arrangements in this district fail on the clock rather than on teaching quality. We time the afternoon by school direction, publish an earliest honest start, and match session length to the work it has to carry, because an arrangement that collapses in November helped nobody.

whyPoints.title: Dates published with the board named
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's March 2027 entries closed 27 November 2026 for examinations from 3 February. Pearson's November 2026 window ran to 19 November. We name the board, link the live official timetable, and publish no IB dates at all because the IB's own site is the only acceptable source for those.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed, never implied
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure here names who published it and the month it was read: EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, BartyED and Bestimate's 2026 table. Three of the six competitor pages examined publish no price at all. These are market bands, not an IB Gram price list.

whyPoints.title: No journey added to your afternoon
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, which removes the one variable nobody controls in this district. A tutor held up on Airport Road is a cancelled session. It also means the annotated script and the shared document still exist next week, which a kitchen-table conversation does not.

whyPoints.title: Continuity protected deliberately
whyPoints.description: The same tutor and the same slot, held through term breaks, moved on purpose for Ramadan rather than left to lapse, and judged after twelve weeks on a marked paper instead of restructured after three on an impression. Continuity is most of what makes a weekly hour worth buying.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the busiest hour
whyPoints.description: Four to five o'clock on a weekday is the most contested window in this time zone, and a specific subject at a specific hour sometimes does not exist. We say so, offer the nearest real alternative, and never substitute a generalist for a Higher Level specialist to fill a slot.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a tutoring session can realistically start in Al Rawdah?
faqs.answer: Four o'clock for a child schooled in Al Mushrif, Al Karamah or Al Nahyan, and nearer five for one travelling to Saadiyat or Khalifa City. The sum is school finish between half past one and half past two, plus collection, plus the drive at the least cooperative hour on Airport Road, plus thirty minutes to eat and decompress. Sessions agreed for seven o'clock because they sounded convenient in August are competing with homework and sleep, and they are the ones being cancelled by November.

faqs.question: Is a forty-five minute session long enough to be worth booking?
faqs.answer: For some work, yes, and for other work no. Forty-five minutes comfortably covers a marked question set reviewed against the scheme, a mechanism drill, a technique correction or a coursework draft section. It cannot accommodate a full essay written and then dissected, because the writing alone consumes it. The pairing that works best for a Year 11 or Diploma student is a ninety-minute weekend block for heavy work plus a forty-five-minute weekday slot for consolidation, which costs the same as two hours and achieves more.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge examination entries actually close?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due on 27 November 2026 for examinations running from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Families who plan from the examination date alone miss the entry window by a wide margin. Ask your school's examinations officer for the entry deadline for your child's series as soon as the subject choices are settled.

faqs.question: Why does my child's school issue a particular Cambridge timetable version?
faqs.answer: Because every Cambridge examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable. Cambridge states that using the correct version for your zone is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after consulting the wrong one. The practical rule is to use the timetable the school issues and to confirm the zone with the examinations officer rather than assuming it, and never to plan from a timetable found through a search engine.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school for in September?
faqs.answer: Its own internal deadline list: coursework submission dates, mock windows and report dates for the year. Those dates bind your child more tightly than the board's do, they are usually earlier, and almost nobody requests them when they would be most useful. Add the examination board and full syllabus code for every examined subject, and the Cambridge zone where it applies. That single page of information shapes a whole year of planning and costs one email to obtain.

faqs.question: Should we schedule tutoring around Ramadan or pause it?
faqs.answer: Move it rather than pause it. Schools across the emirate run shortened days, which puts children home much earlier and opens an early afternoon slot that exists at no other point in the year. Older students often prefer a post-Iftar session, which tends to be calmer than a rushed term-time evening. The common outcome, a month of quietly lapsed sessions followed by a late restart, costs three or four weeks of momentum at exactly the point in the year when mocks are approaching.

faqs.question: My child's mock went badly. Should we change the plan immediately?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Restructuring after a bad mock destroys the only continuity the student has, and three weeks is far too short a period to judge an approach fairly. Twelve weeks is the shortest honest measurement window, and the measurement should be external: the next marked paper rather than an impression of how sessions feel. What a bad mock should trigger is a careful read of the script with the tutor, because the distribution of lost marks usually explains it and often points at technique rather than content.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to villas in Al Rawdah?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and Abu Dhabi lessons run one-to-one over live video. Independent in-home tutors do work in this district at market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, against AED 150 to AED 300 online. In a district where the clock is the binding constraint, a tutor delayed on Airport Road is a cancelled session, which online delivery removes entirely.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we buy tutoring for at once?
faqs.answer: Usually one, taken seriously. One subject with a ninety-minute weekend block and a short weekday review moves measurably. Four subjects at a weekly half hour each consume more total time and produce less, because nothing gets enough continuity to change. In the Diploma this matters more than families expect, since a single Higher Level grade typically carries more weight in a university offer than small gains spread across three Standard Level subjects.

faqs.question: What happens when we miss a session because of travel or illness?
faqs.answer: The arrangement needs a rule agreed in advance, because weeks go wrong and the absence of a rule is what turns one missed session into an abandoned plan. Ours is that a missed session is rescheduled within the same week where possible, or converted into set work that is inspected at the start of the next session. Families who agree this at the outset lose two or three sessions a term. Families who treat cancellation as costless tend to lose closer to eight.

faqs.question: Is the summer break worth using for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is the only period in which a genuine foundation rebuild is possible, because nothing competes with it. A student entering Year 11 or the final Diploma year with a real content gap should close it in July and August rather than in October while new material is arriving. Many families in this district travel for part of the summer, and a live video arrangement follows them, which means the plan survives a six-week absence instead of being abandoned and restarted in September.

faqs.question: How long before an examination is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: It is rarely too late, but the target changes with the time available. Six weeks is not enough for content rebuilding and is ample for technique: tariff discipline, command terms, pacing across a full paper and self-marking against the scheme. Those are the fastest-moving variables in any grade. Coursework is different, because a draft near its deadline leaves only cosmetic room, which is exactly when families start asking for help nobody should provide.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an internal assessment that is due next week?
faqs.answer: Only within a boundary that leaves limited room that late. A tutor can read what exists against the published criteria and name the criterion that is unevidenced, then teach the missing skill. What cannot happen is text being supplied, a section rewritten into something the student could not have produced, a draft edited to completion, or a topic or data set handed over ready-made. A malpractice finding is recorded against the student, which is why the sensible move is to book coursework blocks in September instead.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free in the only slot our week allows?
faqs.answer: We tell you plainly rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. The four to five o'clock weekday window is the most contested in this time zone, and a specific subject at a specific hour sometimes does not exist, particularly for the rarer Diploma languages and some Higher Level combinations. The alternatives we offer are a different day, a shorter weekday session paired with a weekend block, or a tutor in another time zone, and if none of those works we say so.

faqs.question: Which term of the year should we do what in?
faqs.answer: Term one, from late August to mid-December, is the longest teaching block and the right place for content work and habit building. Term two is short, interrupted and contains the mock season, which makes it the technique term: tariffs, command terms and pacing. Term three is execution, and for examination year groups it is largely over before it formally ends. Planning content work for term two is the commonest sequencing error, and it is the hardest one to recover from.

abu-dhabi/al-rawdah.closingHeading: Time the afternoon, then choose the tutor
abu-dhabi/al-rawdah.closingBody: The useful first step in Al Rawdah costs nothing and takes ten minutes. Work out when your child is genuinely through the door, add thirty minutes, and write down the earliest hour that is honestly available on each day of the week. Then ask the school for its own internal deadline list for the year. Those two documents decide which tutor can help you, what session length to buy and when the heavy work has to happen, and they prevent the one failure that is almost universal here: a reasonable arrangement agreed at an impossible time. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so nothing in the plan depends on anyone crossing Airport Road at four o'clock.

abu-dhabi/al-reef.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IB Diploma, the MYP and both Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE routes that Al Reef children sit at schools along the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor. Each profile names the board, the level and the papers that person teaches, so you can match on syllabus rather than on a star rating.

intro.heading: Two kinds of Al Reef household, one shared timetable problem
paragraphs: Al Reef is really two communities sharing a postcode. The villas sit in four precincts built to different styles, mostly occupied by families who moved out of the island for space and a garden. Al Reef Downtown is a ring of apartment blocks above a retail plaza, where households are smaller, often younger, and frequently on a first UAE posting. The two groups ask different questions about tutoring, and a page that treats them as one audience is useless to both.

What they share is geography. Al Reef sits beside the airport interchange, which means almost no child attends school inside the community. The school run goes north-west towards Khalifa City and Al Raha, or further on to Al Reem Island, Saadiyat and Yas. In light traffic that is twenty minutes. At 07:15 and again at 15:00 it is not. By the time a car is back in the precinct, a tutor arriving from the island would be arriving at 17:30 at the earliest, and leaving at 18:30 with another thirty minutes of road ahead.

That arithmetic is why one-to-one online tuition suits Al Reef particularly well. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we run only in India. What an Al Reef family gets instead is a subject specialist chosen for the paper their child is weakest on, available at 16:30 or at 20:00, with no travel charge folded into the hourly rate and no cancelled lesson because the Sheikh Khalifa bridge was closed.

The academic pressure points differ by precinct more than you would expect. Villa households tend to have two or three children at the same school, which turns tutoring into a scheduling exercise across Year 7, Year 10 and DP1. Downtown households more often have one child, a recent curriculum change behind them, and a specific gap to close before the next report. A family that has just moved from a CBSE or American school into a Cambridge IGCSE Year 10 is not short of ability; the child has simply never written an answer to a six-mark command term before. Precinct also changes the evening: households on the far side of the community reach the Khalifa City link later, and that pushes a workable lesson slot back by a quarter of an hour.

The rest of this page is written for those situations. It explains which schools Al Reef children actually attend and what each one teaches, what ADEK's inspection bands mean when you read a school report, what the Abu Dhabi tutoring market charges in AED and who charges it, how the Cambridge entry calendar runs months ahead of the exam, how the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons sit alongside an international timetable, and exactly what a tutor is permitted to do when an Internal Assessment is due.

abu-dhabi/al-reef.programmesIntro: Al Reef children are spread across three programme families, and the programme matters more than the school name when you are choosing a tutor. A Year 10 Cambridge student and an MYP Year 5 student may live four doors apart and need completely different support.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run 1-7 per subject with up to three bonus points from TOK and the EE. The workload is not evenly spread: DP1 ends with Internal Assessment drafts in several subjects at once, and DP2 begins with mock exams while the EE is still being redrafted.
programmes.countryNote: Al Reef DP candidates mostly travel to Raha International School, The British International School Abu Dhabi on Al Reem Island, or Cranleigh Abu Dhabi on Saadiyat. Those are three different DP cultures with different internal deadline calendars, so a tutor working with an Al Reef family needs the school's own IA schedule rather than a generic one.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0-8, with no public exam until the optional MYP eAssessment. Reports carry criterion letters rather than percentages, which parents new to the IB often misread as a soft grade. Criterion D in sciences and Criterion C in individuals and societies are where most marks quietly disappear.
programmes.countryNote: MYP families in Al Reef are usually planning the jump into DP1 at the same school. The useful tutoring window is MYP 4 and 5, when a student can still build the mathematical fluency that Analysis and Approaches Higher Level assumes from day one. Starting that work in DP1 is late, not impossible.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by terminal papers, with Core and Extended tiers in many Cambridge subjects. Syllabus codes are the practical detail: Cambridge Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Maths 0580, while Pearson International GCSE Maths A is 4MA1 and Physics is 4PH1. The papers are not interchangeable, and neither are the mark schemes.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Al Reef run Cambridge in some subjects and Pearson in others, which is legitimate and common. Before booking, check the code printed on your child's last mock paper. A tutor who teaches 0580 well is not automatically fluent in 4MA1's calculator-paper style.

abu-dhabi/al-reef.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Reef families request most often, with what each one actually assesses and the point at which marks are usually lost. The list is deliberately specific; a request for help with maths is not the same as a request for help with the Paper 3 problem-solving extension.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the whole course. Higher Level adds Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper worth 20% of the grade, where students who can execute routine techniques still stall because the question gives no method. Proof, complex numbers and the calculus of parametric curves are the usual HL casualties.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-led work. Marks are lost on interpretation rather than calculation: a correct regression line followed by a sentence that misstates what the gradient represents scores the mark for the line and nothing for the comment. The Higher Level content on graph theory and matrices is often taught late.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism is the reliable trouble spot at every level. Students can recite the formulae and still misdraw a circuit when two resistors are in parallel inside a larger series loop. At IB Higher Level, fields and induction demand sign conventions that nobody enforces in class.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics separate grades. The Internal Assessment is where IB Chemistry marks are most recoverable, because a clear research question and honest uncertainty analysis score heavily and cost nothing but planning time. Mole calculations under exam pressure remain the commonest silent error.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where students are penalised for imprecise language rather than ignorance. Answers that say a substance moves without naming the gradient, the membrane or the protein lose marks the student believes they earned. Statistical treatment of data in the IA is routinely thin.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the whole game. An axis labelled with a quantity instead of a price, or a shift drawn without a new equilibrium marked, caps an otherwise strong evaluation. Higher Level adds quantitative elements and the policy questions where command terms such as discuss and evaluate carry explicit mark weight.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two unseen texts in Paper 1, comparative essay work in Paper 2, plus the Individual Oral built on a global issue. Students often prepare content and neglect structure, then run out of time in Paper 1. Higher Level candidates also sit the HL essay, a 1,200-1,500 word piece on a studied text.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The Extended tier reaches grade 9 and includes functions, vectors and more demanding trigonometry; Core caps lower. Choosing the tier is a real decision with university consequences, and it is usually made in Year 10 on the basis of one set of mocks. Non-calculator arithmetic is the hidden weakness.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: A mandatory subject in UAE private schools, taught separately for Arab and non-Arab students under the published requirements. Many Al Reef children arrive mid-phase with no Arabic and are placed by year group rather than by level, which is where the frustration starts. Steady short sessions beat intensive blocks here.

abu-dhabi/al-reef.regionsIntro: Al Reef sits at a junction, and the surrounding communities matter because that is where the schools are. These notes describe each neighbour in terms of what it does to an Al Reef family's week rather than as a property listing.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The closest cluster of schools to Al Reef and the destination for most of the community's primary-age children. Al Yasmina Academy and GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi both draw heavily from the villas, and the morning queue onto the Khalifa City access road is the reason 16:30 is the earliest realistic lesson slot.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Home to Raha International School, the IB continuum school most Al Reef DP families name first. The internal deadline calendar there drives when Internal Assessment support is needed, which is typically a cluster of drafts in the final term of DP1 rather than a steady year-long trickle.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Apartment towers along the Khor Al Raha channel, closer to the island than Al Reef and often the first address families take before moving out to a villa. Students here sit the same papers and share tutors, but their afternoons start earlier because the school run is shorter.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: The British International School Abu Dhabi and Repton Abu Dhabi are both on Al Reem, which makes it the longest regular commute an Al Reef family takes. A 15:00 finish there can mean a 16:15 arrival home, so evening sessions from 18:00 are common for secondary students.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: West Yas Academy serves a mix of Al Reef and Yas households on an American programme. The island's event calendar genuinely affects scheduling: race and concert weekends change traffic on the Yas bridges, and a video lesson is unaffected by either.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Cranleigh Abu Dhabi sits here and takes a small but steady number of Al Reef children. It is the furthest practical school run from the community, and families making it rarely add a second trip for a tutor in the same day.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: A large mainland district south of Al Reef with a different school mix, including Indian-curriculum provision. Families who move between the two communities often change board as well as school, and that transition is the most common reason for a first tutoring enquiry.

schoolClusters.city: The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: This is where the majority of Al Reef children are enrolled. The corridor carries British, American and IB programmes within a few kilometres of each other, so siblings in one household are regularly on different boards. Confirm the programme and the syllabus code before matching a tutor.

schoolClusters.city: The island schools Al Reef families commute to
schoolClusters.note: A smaller group travels onto the island or the outer islands for a specific programme, usually the IB Diploma or a British sixth form. These runs are long enough that a second journey for tuition is rarely practical, which is the main reason online sessions are requested here.

abu-dhabi/al-reef.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Al Reef request. The difference between them is not quality but cadence, and choosing wrongly is the commonest reason a family stops after three sessions.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term-long
modes.description: One or two sixty-minute sessions a week in a single subject, running alongside the school's own scheme of work. This is the format that suits a Year 10 student who is coping but drifting, and the one that makes Internal Assessment work manageable because drafts arrive in sequence rather than in a pile.

modes.title: Exam-block intensive
modes.description: A fixed run of ninety-minute sessions in the eight to ten weeks before a terminal paper, built backwards from the exam date. Content coverage is deliberately narrow: the two or three topics the student is losing marks on, worked through past-paper questions under timed conditions rather than taught from scratch.

modes.description: Common in the Al Reef villas, where two or three children need different subjects at different levels. Sessions are stacked back to back in one evening so the household gives up one night rather than four, with separate tutors for each child and separate notes to the parent.

sections.heading: What a search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Al Reef is usually asking
paragraphs: The literal answer: families in Al Reef can book one-to-one IB and IGCSE tuition delivered over live video, with sessions from 16:30 Gulf Standard Time, matched to the syllabus code their child's school teaches. There is no tutor driving into the precinct, and the hourly rate carries no travel component because there is no travel.

Behind that search sit three different needs. The first is diagnostic: a report has come home with a grade the parent did not expect and nobody has explained which paper caused it. The second is logistical: the family knows what help is needed and cannot fit it into a week that already contains a forty-minute school run twice a day. The third is transitional: the child has changed curriculum, country or both in the last eighteen months and the gap is structural rather than a matter of effort.

Al Reef generates a high share of the third kind. The community is a common first or second address for families arriving in Abu Dhabi, partly because of its position near the airport and partly because the villas are priced below the island. A child who has moved from an American middle school into Cambridge IGCSE Year 10 has to learn a new assessment language in a few months, and that is a teachable problem with a clear end point.

What the search is rarely asking for is a general study-skills course. By the time a parent in Al Reef types this query, they usually know the subject. The question is whether anyone can cover 0625 Paper 4 properly, this term, at a time that exists in their week.
bullets: Diagnostic requests start with a report card nobody has decoded

sections.heading: The Al Reef school run, precinct by precinct, and when a lesson can start
paragraphs: Nothing shapes tutoring in Al Reef as much as the drive. The community has no private school inside it, so every family is on the airport road or the Khalifa City link twice a day. The precinct a family lives in changes the exit they use, and that changes the arrival time home by fifteen to twenty minutes in afternoon traffic.

The table below sets out the realistic picture. It is built from one-way journeys in normal weekday afternoon conditions, not from a map's shortest estimate. The final column is the point at which a student can sit down having eaten something, which is the only lesson start time worth planning around. A session booked for the moment the car pulls in is a session the student spends half of recovering.

Two patterns come out of it. Families using Khalifa City schools can genuinely run a 16:30 lesson, which keeps the evening intact and suits primary and lower-secondary students who fade after 19:00. Families commuting to Al Reem or Saadiyat are better served from 18:00, and DP students in that group often prefer 20:00, after dinner, when they would otherwise be working alone anyway.

The third pattern is the one families discover too late. A tutor travelling from the island to Al Reef adds an hour of road to a sixty-minute lesson, and that hour is paid for either in money or in a later start. Removing the journey is the single largest scheduling gain available to a household in this community.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection bands, and reading an Abu Dhabi school report properly
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are not regulated by KHDA. That is Dubai. In this emirate the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools, and it publishes its own inspection outcomes. Al Reef parents who have moved from Dubai routinely look for a KHDA rating for a Khalifa City school and find nothing, because the rating sits with ADEK instead.

Inspection reports in the UAE use a six-band scale, and the bands are not grades in the way a parent instinctively reads them. Acceptable is a pass against the framework, not a warning. Good is the point at which most families stop worrying. The gap between Good and Very Good is usually about consistency across year groups rather than about the strongest teaching in the school, which is why a Very Good school can still have a weak department and a Good school can have an outstanding one.

That distinction is the practical one for tutoring. An inspection band describes a whole school. Your child sits in one classroom with one teacher for 0620 Chemistry. The band tells you how the school is run; it tells you nothing about whether the Chemistry set is three weeks behind the scheme of work because of a staffing change in October. Ask the subject question directly at parents' evening.

Ratings change, and they should be read on ADEK's own school listing rather than taken from an aggregator or from a page like this one. Treat the table below as a translation of the vocabulary, not as a verdict on any named school.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around the Abu Dhabi airport corridor, in AED
paragraphs: Most pages in this market publish no price at all. The figures below are market rates in the UAE gathered from providers' own published pricing and from a published 2026 Dubai tutoring rate survey by Bestimate. They are not IB Gram's price list. They are here so that an Al Reef family can tell whether a quote they have been given is normal, high or suspiciously low.

Read the table as a set of bands rather than a single number, because three things move a rate: the level, the format and whether travel is priced in. A university student tutoring online sits at the bottom. A named examiner-level specialist sits at the top. In-home visits carry the travel inside the hourly rate, which is why the in-home band starts higher than the online one for identical teaching.

Monthly packages are common and worth comparing on sessions rather than on headline price. Published examples in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. The same survey put weekly one-hour tuition at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

One caution specific to this community. Al Reef sits far enough from the island that some in-home providers quote a higher rate or a minimum two-hour booking to make the journey worthwhile. If you are comparing an in-home quote against an online one, compare the cost of a term, including travel loading and the sessions lost to road closures, rather than the cost of an hour.

sections.heading: Online lessons versus a tutor driving to Al Reef: the honest comparison
paragraphs: Parents searching for a home tutor in Al Reef are asking a reasonable question, and it deserves a straight answer before any sales argument. In-home tutoring exists in Abu Dhabi, it works for some families, and it has real advantages: a young child concentrates better with an adult physically present, and a parent can hear the lesson from the next room.

It also has costs that are easy to miss. The tutor pool shrinks to people willing to drive to the airport corridor, which is a smaller group than the pool of people who teach 0625 Paper 4 well. Travel time is paid for one way or another. A 17:00 session becomes a 17:40 session when the road is heavy, and a cancelled journey is a cancelled lesson rather than a rescheduled one.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE, and does not run a centre in the emirate. Tuition for Al Reef families is one-to-one online tuition over live video, with a shared screen for working through papers and a written note to the parent afterwards. The case for it in this community is specific rather than general: you get the Chemistry Higher Level specialist instead of whoever is free and willing to drive forty minutes.

sections.heading: The Cambridge calendar counted backwards from the exam
paragraphs: The single most useful thing an Al Reef family can know in October is that the deadline which decides next year's exams has usually already passed by the time anyone starts revising. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.

Take the Cambridge March 2027 series as the worked example, because its published key dates show the gap clearly. The exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027. Final entries are due on 27 November 2026, more than two months before the first paper. Forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027. Results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. A family that decides in January to add a subject has missed the entry window.

There is a zone trap worth knowing about as well. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the published guidance is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in rather than downloading the first timetable a search returns.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official PDF rather than a restated date. For IB sessions, Abu Dhabi DP candidates sit the May session, but confirm every exam and results date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, because no IB date is restated on this page.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside a British or IB timetable
paragraphs: Every family in Al Reef with a child in a UAE private school is running two curricula at once, whether or not they think of it that way. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. The international programme is the one in the prospectus; the mandatory UAE subjects sit alongside it.

The requirements are published and precise. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and the advice is that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. For these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited, which is why a tutor working on Arabic or Islamic Education sticks to the school's own material rather than importing a programme from elsewhere.

Practically, this is the subject Al Reef's newer arrivals struggle with most, because children are placed by year group rather than by Arabic level. A Year 8 student with no Arabic sits in a Year 8 class. Short, frequent sessions on vocabulary and script, aligned to the school's units, close that gap faster than a weekend intensive.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, Extended Essay or Personal Project
paragraphs: This is the boundary that matters most, and it is the one some providers in this market cross openly. Assessed coursework belongs to the student. A tutor teaches the skills, explains the criteria, asks the questions a supervisor would ask, and gives feedback on work the student has already done. A tutor does not supply text that ends up in a submission.

In practice the line is easier to hold than it sounds. Teaching a student how Criterion B is awarded in a sciences Internal Assessment is teaching. Reading a student's method section and saying that the uncertainty treatment will not score because no instrument precision is stated is feedback. Suggesting a research question is a grey area best handled by teaching the student how to narrow their own. Handing over a paragraph is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor.

The same applies to materials. Official syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards that publish them. The right approach is to work from the official source, cite it, and link to it, rather than distribute copies. IB Gram does not host or supply board documents as downloads.

Al Reef DP families often meet this question in the final term of DP1, when several Internal Assessments land together and the temptation to outsource rises with the pressure. The honest fix is earlier scheduling, not more help: IA work spread over three months is a manageable project, and the same work compressed into three weeks is the situation in which academic honesty gets tested.

sections.heading: If no specialist is free: coverage, match time and the fallback
paragraphs: No platform covers every subject at every level at every hour, and claiming otherwise is the fastest way to waste a family's week. Coverage in Abu Dhabi is deep in mainstream subjects and thinner in the niches, and an Al Reef family deserves to know which group their request falls into before they commit to a trial.

Mainstream requests are usually matched within a couple of working days: IGCSE Maths, the sciences, English, IB Mathematics at both routes, Economics, Business Management. These have several available tutors and a choice of time slots, including the 16:30 slot that suits Khalifa City commuters.

The thinner areas are predictable. Higher Level Further Mathematics, Arabic as a first language at Higher Level, Music, Film, and some second-language combinations have fewer specialists and longer match times. Where no UAE-based tutor covers a subject, lessons may be delivered by a specialist in another time zone, usually from India, over the same live video format. That is disclosed before booking rather than discovered afterwards, and the time slot is agreed to suit Gulf Standard Time.

Demand is also seasonal in a way that affects Al Reef directly. The final term of DP1 produces a surge of Internal Assessment requests across the Al Raha corridor at once, because several schools set their internal deadlines in the same fortnight. Booking an IA coaching block in February rather than April is the difference between a choice of tutors and a waiting list.

The honest fallback position, when nothing fits, is to say so. A family told in two days that a Film Higher Level specialist is not available can go elsewhere with their term intact. A family strung along for three weeks cannot. Where a match is partial, the sensible compromise is to start on the component that can be taught now and keep the rest under review.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus code, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that saves a week names the board and the code: 0580 or 4MA1, 0625 or 4PH1, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. An Al Reef family can read all of this off the front of their child's last mock paper, and it halves the matching time.

process.title: Send the last marked paper or report
process.description: A marked paper tells a tutor more in five minutes than a phone call does in thirty. It shows which command terms the student is losing marks on and whether the problem is content, timing or exam technique. Report-card comments are useful mainly for what the subject teacher chose to mention.

process.title: Pick a slot that survives the school run
process.description: Choose the time your child can actually sit down, fed and settled, rather than the time the car arrives home. For Khalifa City commuters that is usually 16:30; for Al Reem and Saadiyat runs it is 18:00 or later. A realistic slot is the difference between a term of lessons and three.

process.title: Use the first session as a diagnostic
process.description: The opening session should end with a short written statement of what is wrong and what the plan is: the topics, the papers, the order and the number of weeks. If it ends with general encouragement instead, ask for the specifics before booking further sessions.

process.title: Review at four sessions, not at the end of term
process.description: Four sessions is enough to see whether the match works and whether the student is doing the work between lessons. Changing tutor at that point costs nothing. Discovering a mismatch in May, with a terminal paper three weeks away, costs the grade.

whyPoints.title: The tutor is chosen for the paper, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, the pool is not limited to people prepared to drive to the airport corridor. An Al Reef student weak on Physics Paper 4 gets someone who teaches that paper, which is a different and better selection criterion than proximity.

whyPoints.title: Nothing is lost to the road
whyPoints.description: A sixty-minute online session is sixty minutes of teaching. No travel loading sits inside the rate, no lesson is cancelled because a bridge is closed, and a session can be moved by an hour on the day without anyone's journey being wasted.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: Schools serving Al Reef run Cambridge and Pearson side by side, sometimes within one child's timetable. Matching on the code rather than the subject avoids the common failure where a competent tutor teaches the wrong paper style for a term.

whyPoints.title: The regulator and the rules are explained, not borrowed
whyPoints.description: This page names ADEK, MoHRE and the published mandatory-subject requirements because Abu Dhabi families need to understand them. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of them, and says so rather than implying otherwise.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: Where a subject has no available UAE-based specialist, that is stated, along with whether a tutor in another time zone would be teaching the sessions. A family can then decide with the facts rather than find out in week three.

faqs.question: Can we get a home tutor who comes to our villa in Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for Al Reef families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Independent tutors and agencies in Abu Dhabi do travel to the airport corridor, and published market rates for in-home one-to-one work run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel priced in. The practical trade-off is the tutor pool: in-home limits you to people willing to make a forty-minute drive each way, while an online session lets you choose the specialist who actually teaches your child's paper.

faqs.question: Which schools do most Al Reef children attend?
faqs.answer: No private school sits inside Al Reef, so families commute. The largest group goes to Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor, which includes Al Yasmina Academy, GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi and Raha International School. A smaller group travels onto Al Reem Island for The British International School Abu Dhabi or Repton Abu Dhabi, or to Saadiyat for Cranleigh Abu Dhabi. Those schools run British, American and IB programmes, so two children on the same Al Reef street can be sitting entirely different assessments. Check the programme before choosing a tutor.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson realistically start in Al Reef?
faqs.answer: It depends on the commute, not on the precinct. Families using Khalifa City schools are usually home in time for a 16:30 Gulf Standard Time start. Al Raha runs push that to 17:00. A commute to Al Reem Island or Saadiyat Island means 18:00 is more realistic, and Diploma Programme students on that run frequently choose 20:00, after dinner, when they would otherwise be working alone. The time to book is the time your child can sit down settled and fed, which is rarely the moment the car pulls in.

faqs.question: Who regulates the schools my child might attend from Al Reef?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, and publishes inspection outcomes for them. Dubai schools are overseen by KHDA, Sharjah's by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Al Reef parents arriving from Dubai often search for a KHDA rating for an Abu Dhabi school and find none, because the rating belongs to ADEK. Check current ratings on ADEK's own school listing.

faqs.question: Does an Outstanding inspection rating mean my child does not need a tutor?
faqs.answer: An inspection band describes how a whole school is run across all phases and subjects. Your child sits in one classroom, with one teacher, for one syllabus. A school rated Very Good can have a department that lost two staff in October and is three weeks behind the scheme of work, and a school rated Good can have an exceptional science team. Use the band to judge the institution and ask the subject question directly: what is in place this year for a student targeting a 7 or a grade 9 in this specific course?

faqs.question: My child moved from an American school into Cambridge IGCSE. How long does that gap take to close?
faqs.answer: Usually a term of focused work, not a year. The ability is rarely the issue. What is missing is the assessment language: command terms, the mark allocation behind a six-mark question, and the habit of answering what was asked rather than writing everything known about the topic. That is teachable and measurable. Expect the first four sessions to be spent on past-paper technique in one subject, then the same approach transfers to the others with much less input. Al Reef sees a high share of these transitions because the community takes many new arrivals.

faqs.question: We have three children in Al Reef Villas at different levels. Can that be scheduled sensibly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and stacking is usually better than spreading. Booking consecutive slots on one evening means the household gives up one night a week rather than three or four. Each child has their own tutor, chosen for their own subject and level, with separate notes to the parent afterwards. The coordination is only on timing. This pattern suits villa households in particular, where siblings often attend the same school on different programmes and need completely different support.

faqs.question: Is private tutoring in Abu Dhabi legally regulated?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher tutor them privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: This is reported to be prohibited, and it is not a grey area worth testing. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's published policy before relying on it. A tutor from outside the school avoids the issue entirely and often gives more candid feedback.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge entries close for an Al Reef student?
faqs.answer: Far earlier than most families expect. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due on 27 November 2026 while the exam period itself runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027. Forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Entries are submitted by the school as the centre, not by parents, so the conversation to have in October is about which subjects and tiers are being entered. Adding a subject in January is generally too late.

faqs.question: Do we need to worry about Cambridge timetable zones?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a genuine risk rather than administrative trivia. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge's own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in and work from the timetable it issues, rather than downloading whichever PDF a search returns first. Revision plans built on the wrong zone's dates can be days out.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit around an IB or British timetable?
faqs.answer: They run alongside it. UAE private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and these subjects are mandatory regardless of the licensed international programme. Published requirements specify separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Tutoring for these subjects must work from the school's own approved material.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Internal Assessment without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor explains how each criterion is awarded and what the mark allocation rewards, asks the questions a supervisor would ask, and gives feedback on a draft the student has already produced. A tutor does not supply text, data or analysis that ends up in a submission. The practical protection is timing: an Internal Assessment spread across three months is a manageable project, while the same work compressed into three weeks is where academic honesty gets tested. Official mark schemes and papers are cited and linked, never redistributed.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for a niche Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, usually within a few working days. Mainstream requests such as IGCSE Maths, the sciences and English match within one or two working days. Narrower ones take longer: Higher Level Further Mathematics, Arabic as a first language at upper secondary, Music, Film and some second-language combinations have small specialist pools. Where no UAE-based tutor covers the subject, a specialist in another time zone may teach the sessions over the same live video format, and that is disclosed before booking. Where nothing fits, the honest answer is a decline, so your term is not wasted.

faqs.question: Is online tuition genuinely effective for a child who prefers face-to-face teaching?
faqs.answer: For most secondary students, yes, provided the format is one-to-one rather than a recorded class or a large group. Shared screens suit the work these courses demand: annotating a past paper, building a graph, stepping through a mark scheme line by line. Younger children, roughly up to Year 5, often do concentrate better with an adult physically present, and that is a fair reason to look at in-home provision for that age. For a DP or IGCSE student losing marks on a specific paper, the quality of the subject match matters far more than the room.

abu-dhabi/al-reef.closingHeading: Start with the syllabus code and the time your child can actually sit down
abu-dhabi/al-reef.closingBody: If you are in Al Reef and weighing up tutoring, two pieces of information move things fastest: the syllabus code printed on your child's last mock paper, and the time of day they are settled enough to work. With those, a specialist can be matched in a couple of working days for mainstream subjects, and you will be told plainly if your request falls into one of the thinner areas. Lessons run one-to-one over live video from 16:30 Gulf Standard Time onwards, so the school run along the airport road stops dictating what is possible in the evening.
