sections.heading: Set placement, set changes and what a parent can actually ask for
paragraphs: Large schools set by ability in the examined subjects, and the set a student sits in shapes what they are taught, how fast, and sometimes which tier they are entered for. Parents are often reluctant to raise it, partly because it feels like complaining and partly because they do not know what a reasonable request looks like.

A reasonable request is specific and evidenced. Not that your child is in the wrong set, but that their last two assessment scores sit at the top of their current set, that a diagnostic shows they handle Extended-style questions competently, and that you would like to understand what the school needs to see before a move is considered. That is a conversation a head of department can act on. A general expression of disappointment is not.

It is also worth asking what a set change actually involves, because the answer is not always encouraging. Mid-year moves can mean missing topics covered at a different pace, and a student who moves up in February may need bridging work on material the higher set covered in October. That is manageable with support and unmanageable without it, and a school will usually tell you honestly which it would be.

Finally, accept that the school may be right. Teachers who have entered candidates for the same syllabus for a decade have a calibrated sense of who copes with Paper 4. If the school declines and explains why, the useful next step is to work on the specific weakness they name rather than to escalate. Parents who do that are generally listened to the following year.
bullets: Bring two recent scores and a diagnostic, not a general concern
Ask what the school needs to see before a move is considered
Check what topics a mid-year move would skip, and bridge them
If the school declines with reasons, work on the named weakness

sections.heading: Arriving from an Indian or Pakistani board into IGCSE
paragraphs: A substantial number of students in this district move from a national board into an international one, often at the end of class nine or ten. The families expect the content to be the difficulty and it almost never is. Indian and Pakistani board students generally arrive with more content than the IGCSE requires, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, and they can calculate competently under pressure.

What changes is the assessment. IGCSE papers reward answer construction against command terms and mark tariffs rather than complete worked solutions, and they ask for application to unfamiliar contexts rather than reproduction of a taught method. A student trained to produce a full, formal solution will write at length and score partially, and the first set of results looks alarming to a family who knows the child is strong.

The second change is written explanation. Science papers at IGCSE require a mechanism explained in prose, with specific vocabulary, in a few lines. Students from recall-heavy systems describe what happens rather than explaining why, and that single habit costs marks on every paper until it is corrected. It is a technique fix, usually four to six weeks of deliberate practice, not a content rebuild.

The third is English register in the written subjects, which is sometimes a genuine language issue and more often a conventions issue. Knowing what an IGCSE directed-writing task actually wants is learnable quickly. Treating it as a general English deficiency leads families to buy years of language tuition when they needed six weeks of task-specific work.
bullets: Content is usually not the problem; assessment style is
Answers must match command terms and tariffs, not be full formal solutions
Science prose explanation is the habit that costs marks every paper
Written English is often conventions rather than language ability

sections.heading: The Al Wahda afternoon, and the hour that is genuinely free
paragraphs: This district has one real advantage over the villa communities and the islands: many children are schooled within a few minutes of home. A ten-minute bus ride or a walk from Al Nahyan means a student can be through the door by three, which creates a usable study window that a Khalifa City or Jubail Island family simply does not have.

The disadvantage is space. Al Wahda is apartment living, often with siblings sharing a room and a living room that is the only quiet surface in the home. A student who needs ninety uninterrupted minutes with a laptop and headphones is competing with a household, and that competition is the real constraint rather than the clock. Families who agree the hour with everyone in the apartment, rather than just with the student, lose far fewer sessions.

Where the commute does bite is for Diploma students travelling to Al Mushrif, Al Bateen or Khalifa City, since Diploma provision in the immediate area is limited. Those students are home later and tired, and their heavy work belongs at the weekend with a short weekday review rather than a full evening hour that will be cancelled by the third week.

Ramadan changes the shape usefully. Schools across the emirate run shortened days, which puts children home considerably earlier and opens an early afternoon slot that does not exist for the rest of the year. Older students often prefer a post-Iftar session. Either way, the month is worth planning for in advance rather than letting arrangements lapse through it.
bullets: Short local school runs leave a genuine early-afternoon window
Apartment space, not time, is usually the binding constraint
Diploma commuters should put heavy work at the weekend
Shortened Ramadan days open a slot that exists at no other time

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in central Abu Dhabi, and who published the number
paragraphs: This market is unusually opaque about price. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this project publish no figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which no family here transacts in. The bands below are market rates in dirhams as of October 2026, each attributed to whoever published it, and none of them is an IB Gram price list.

A budget online tutor, generally a university student or a non-specialist, runs AED 45 to 150 an hour; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at entry tiers. A qualified subject tutor working online is AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits are AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table and comparable listings. Genuine IB, IGCSE or A Level specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and premium named tutors reaching AED 650. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for roughly eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

For a family in this district the useful framing is not the hourly rate but what the hour is for. An hour of content re-delivery duplicates what a competent large school already provides, and at AED 200 that is an expensive duplicate. An hour spent marking your child's own script against the official scheme, or diagnosing a tier decision, buys something the school cannot provide at any price. The same money produces very different value depending on which of those you ask for.

Group arrangements are common here and genuinely cheaper per student, and they work for shared revision of a common syllabus. They do not work for individual error patterns, which are by definition different for each student in the group. Families who understand that distinction tend to use a group for revision and an individual hour for diagnosis, which is a sensible split.
bullets: Qualified subject tutor, online, market rate: AED 150 to 300 an hour
In-home visits carry travel inside the rate at AED 180 to 500
Market packages seen: AED 799 monthly online, AED 1,599 to 1,799 in-home

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework in a crowded cohort
paragraphs: In a large cohort the teacher supervising thirty internal assessments reads perhaps one draft of each. That shortage is precisely why families in this district are offered, and sometimes buy, help that crosses a line. The offers are easy to find in this market: one operation sells completed Diploma internal assessments outright. The consequence of using them falls on the student as a malpractice finding, which can cost a diploma.

So what a legitimate tutor does with coursework is worth stating explicitly. Interrogate the research question until it can be answered inside the word limit. Check that a planned method will generate data capable of supporting a conclusion, before any data exists. Read a draft against the published criteria and name the criterion that is currently unevidenced. Teach the skill the draft is missing, then hand it back. Ask the student to justify a paragraph aloud, which exposes borrowed reasoning quickly.

What a legitimate tutor never does is supply text to be pasted, rewrite a section into something the student could not have produced, edit a draft to completion, or hand over a topic, structure or data set ready-made. Nothing is bought in from anywhere. These are not cautious positions; they are the difference between support and malpractice.

We also do not supply or reproduce subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. They are the boards' copyright and your child's school holds them legitimately. A tutor who offers a library of board documents as a selling point is signalling something about how they treat rules in general.
bullets: In a large set, a coursework draft gets roughly one read
Questions, methods and criteria coaching, as early as possible
No supplied text, no rewriting to completion, no ready-made topics or data
Board materials are referenced and linked, never redistributed

sections.heading: Getting started in Al Wahda
paragraphs: Three things before a first session, and none of them is a conversation about ambition. The board and full syllabus code for every examined subject, in writing from the school. The most recent marked script in the subject that worries you. And the honest answer about what time your child is actually at a desk, which in an apartment household means a time the whole family can keep rather than a theoretical one.

Then a diagnostic session rather than an introduction. The tutor works through the script with your child, marks it against the official scheme, and names what is actually happening: content gaps, tariff discipline, command-term misreading, pacing, or a tier that does not fit. You get that written assessment whether or not you continue, and it is also the document to take into a conversation with the school about a set or tier change.

After that the plan is narrow on purpose. One subject properly beats four subjects thinly, especially in a district where families are often funding tuition out of a tight household budget. If the diagnosis says the issue is technique rather than content, the plan is six weeks of drilling and then a re-measurement on a real paper, not an open-ended weekly arrangement.

Two honest limits. Coverage for the rarer Diploma languages and some Higher Level combinations is thin in this time zone, and we say so rather than substituting a generalist. And whoever you engage, from any provider, it is worth asking whether they hold the private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligibility covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, treat any amount quoted to you as unverified.

process.title: Get the board and the code in writing
process.description: Ask the school for the examination board and full syllabus code of every examined subject, plus the Cambridge zone where it applies. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations with the same subject name, and practising the wrong one is the most expensive avoidable error in this market.

process.title: Send the most recent marked script
process.description: Not a report and not a description. The script shows where marks left the page: evenly across the paper means content, collapse in the final third means pacing, losses on the analysis half of questions the child understood means command terms. Those three need completely different plans.

process.title: Take a diagnostic session
process.description: The tutor marks the script with your child against the official scheme, names the pattern, and writes it down. If a tier or set question is live, the diagnostic draws on questions from both tiers so the written output is usable evidence rather than an opinion. You keep it either way.

process.title: Fix one subject and one hour
process.description: A single subject, a single weekly slot the whole household can keep, and a defined target: six weeks of technique drilling, or a specific content list, with a re-measurement date. Narrow plans survive. Plans across four subjects collapse in the fourth week and cost more to abandon.

process.title: Re-measure on a real paper
process.description: A full paper under genuine timing, marked against the scheme, compared with the first one. If the marks have not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does. Sessions that feel productive are not evidence, and in a district where budgets are tight that distinction matters.

whyPoints.title: We do the thing a large set cannot
whyPoints.description: Individual script marking, error patterns tracked across weeks, and a tier diagnosis based on your own child rather than on their position in a cohort of twenty-eight. Re-teaching the syllabus duplicates what an Al Wahda school already does competently, and duplicating it at AED 200 an hour is poor value.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes named, not implied
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610, 0500, 0510; Pearson 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1, 4EA1. A tutor who does not ask which code your child sits is about to practise the wrong papers, and exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole competitor area cluster we examined.

whyPoints.title: The tier ceiling stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge Core caps at grade C. That is not a difficulty setting, it is a permanent limit on the session, and it closes sixth-form and university doors quietly. We would rather tell a family that early in Year 10 than help them revise harder towards a ceiling nobody mentioned.

whyPoints.title: Prices published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every dirham band on this page names who published it and the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages examined publish no price at all. Knowing the market bands is what allows a household on a budget to recognise a reasonable quote and refuse an unreasonable one.

whyPoints.title: Narrow plans rather than packages
whyPoints.description: One subject, one hour, a defined target and a re-measurement date. The alternative, an open arrangement across several subjects, is what families in this district most often regret, and it is also the easiest thing for a provider to sell. We would rather finish and be recommended.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed credentials
whyPoints.description: We explain what the Department of Education and Knowledge does and point to the Ministry for equivalency. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no UAE office, and claims none of those things anywhere.

faqs.question: My child understands the work in class but gets poor examination marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Because class performance and examination performance measure different things. In class the work is untimed, supported and often discussed. An examination is a timed solo performance scored for discrete creditable points, and the specific skills it needs, matching answer length to the mark tariff, reading command terms correctly and pacing across a full paper, are rarely corrected individually in a set of twenty-eight. Send the marked script. The distribution of lost marks across the paper usually identifies the cause in minutes, and it is almost never a knowledge problem.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge Core tier mean for my child's final grade?
faqs.answer: It caps it. A Core candidate in Mathematics 0580 sits papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded higher than grade C, however well they perform; Extended candidates sit papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. The tier is therefore a ceiling rather than a difficulty setting, and it quietly closes sixth-form and university routes that ask for a B. In a large cohort the decision is often made on relative class performance early in Year 10, so that is the moment to bring individual evidence rather than Year 11.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel papers?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, in writing, for the examination board and the full syllabus code of every examined subject, and for the centre's Cambridge zone where that applies. Cambridge uses numeric codes such as 0580 for Mathematics and 0625 for Physics; Pearson uses 4MA1 and 4PH1 for the same subjects. The papers, the tiering and in places the content emphasis differ, so revising the wrong board's past papers for a term is close to wasted effort. Keep that list and give it to any tutor you engage.

faqs.question: How many points should a six-mark answer contain?
faqs.answer: Six distinct creditable points. This is the single commonest reason capable students underperform: they write a dense, articulate paragraph containing three ideas and score three, then cannot understand the mark. The habit to build is mechanical. Read the tariff before reading the question, decide how many points you intend to make, allow roughly a minute per mark plus reading time, and count the points before moving on. It needs no subject knowledge, which is why it is the cheapest grade improvement available.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child move up a set at an Al Wahda school?
faqs.answer: A tutor can produce the evidence; the decision stays with the school. What works is specific and documented: two recent assessment scores at the top of the current set, plus a diagnostic drawn from both tiers showing the student handles higher-tier questions competently, plus a question about what the school needs to see before a move is considered. Also ask what topics a mid-year move would skip, because that bridging work is the difference between a successful change and a difficult one.

faqs.question: My child came from a CBSE school. Why are the marks worse here?
faqs.answer: Usually because the assessment changed rather than because the standard rose. Students arriving from Indian and Pakistani boards typically have more content than IGCSE requires and can calculate well under pressure. What they have not practised is answer construction against command terms and tariffs, application to unfamiliar contexts, and prose explanation of a mechanism in a few precise lines. Those are technique habits, and four to six weeks of deliberate practice usually changes the marks visibly. Buying a content rebuild instead wastes both time and money.

faqs.question: Is a group class or an individual tutor better value in this district?
faqs.answer: They do different jobs. A group is genuinely cheaper per student and works well for shared revision of a common syllabus, because the content is the same for everyone in the room. It cannot address individual error patterns, which are by definition different for each student, and those patterns are what cost capable students their grades. A sensible split for a household on a budget is a group for revision plus a small number of individual sessions for diagnosis and script marking.

faqs.question: Do your tutors visit apartments in Al Wahda?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and all Abu Dhabi lessons run one-to-one over live video. Independent in-home tutors do work in this district, and their published rates carry the travel, which is why market in-home figures run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 online. In apartment housing there is also a space cost: a visiting tutor occupies the only quiet shared surface in the home.

faqs.question: What is the fastest grade improvement available before an examination series?
faqs.answer: Technique, not content. In order: matching answer length to the mark tariff, separating command terms so that describe, explain and evaluate trigger different responses, and pacing across a full paper under genuine timing. In the sciences, the alternative-to-practical paper rewards experimental conventions that are rarely drilled and are learnable in a few hours. Content rebuilding is slower and only worth funding where a marked script actually proves the gap, which is why we ask for the script first.

faqs.question: How much do private tutors charge per hour in central Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates as of October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to 150 for a budget or university-student tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the figure, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or A Level specialist. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for about eight online sessions. Those figures come from published competitor pricing and Bestimate's 2026 rate table, and they are the market rather than our own price list.

faqs.question: Does Arabic count towards the Ministry of Education equivalency subjects?
faqs.answer: No. On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Candidates also need one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor page in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own site before building a university plan on it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor read my child's internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, against the published criteria, and in a large cohort that is valuable because the school teacher reads roughly one draft of thirty. The tutor names the criterion that is currently unevidenced, teaches the missing skill and returns the work. What does not happen is text being supplied, a section rewritten into something the student could not have produced, a draft edited to completion, or a topic or data set handed over ready-made. The malpractice consequence falls on your child, which is why that line holds.

faqs.question: Can we get past papers and mark schemes from you?
faqs.answer: No. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and redistributing them is not something we do. Your child's school can supply them legitimately, and the boards publish specimen material on their own sites. A tutor working with your child references and links official material rather than handing over copies. Any provider advertising a library of board documents is telling you something about its general attitude to rules.

faqs.question: What time should a session start for a child schooled in Al Nahyan?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most districts in the emirate can manage. A ten-minute bus ride or a walk means a student can be at a desk by half past three, which is a genuine advantage over the islands and the outer communities. The real constraint in apartment housing is space rather than time: a student needs ninety minutes with headphones and a closed door, which has to be agreed with the whole household. Diploma students commuting to Al Mushrif or Khalifa City should put heavy work at the weekend instead.

faqs.question: What happens during Ramadan and the shortened school days?
faqs.answer: Schools across the emirate reduce hours, children are home considerably earlier, and an early-afternoon slot becomes available that exists at no other point in the year. Older students frequently prefer a post-Iftar session, which tends to be calmer than a rushed term-time evening. The mistake is letting arrangements lapse for the month and restarting late, which costs three or four weeks of momentum. We set the Ramadan pattern before the month begins rather than during it.

abu-dhabi/al-wahda.closingHeading: Bring the code and the script
abu-dhabi/al-wahda.closingBody: Two documents decide what an Al Wahda family should buy. The first is the examination board and full syllabus code for every examined subject, in writing from the school, because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations wearing the same subject name. The second is the most recent marked script, because where the marks left the page distinguishes a content gap from a tariff problem from a pacing problem, and those three need entirely different plans. Send both and the first session becomes a diagnosis rather than an introduction. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, in the hour your household can genuinely keep.

intro.heading: Why the gap exists, and why it is not a judgement on the school
paragraphs: Al Zahiyah sits on the north-eastern side of Abu Dhabi island, the dense older district behind the eastern waterfront, with apartment blocks stacked close together and a mixed population drawn from across the world. Households here are frequently more budget-conscious than those on the western island, more likely to be in rented apartments, and more likely to have a single child receiving support rather than three. The household is also likelier to be weighing a tuition centre class against a private tutor on price alone.

The tutoring question that arrives from this district is usually diagnostic and financial at the same time. A report has come home with a grade that surprised the family, nobody has explained which component caused it, and the parent wants to know both what is actually wrong and what the least expensive way of fixing it is. Both are fair questions and both have specific answers, and the second one is easier to answer once the first has been settled properly.

Start with why the gap exists. In a class of twenty-four to twenty-eight students, an hour of teaching contains a fixed amount of individual attention, and the arithmetic is unforgiving: two or three minutes per student if the teacher distributes it evenly, which no teacher can do while also teaching. That is not a criticism of the school or the teacher. It is the structure of classroom teaching everywhere, and it is the thing one-to-one work exists to supplement. Understanding that changes the conversation from blame to logistics.

The second structural limit is reporting. A report card compresses a term into a grade, an effort mark and a few sentences written for thirty families. It cannot say that your child understands the chemistry and loses six marks a paper to unit omissions, or that they know the content and run out of time on the final long question. It is not a dishonest document and it is not a useless one; it is simply the wrong instrument for the question the family has. Those are the facts a plan needs, and they are not on the report. They are obtainable by asking the right person a specific question, and this page explains which question and which person.

What follows is built for a family that wants evidence before spending. There are tables comparing individual feedback across class, group and one-to-one settings, on what a report does and does not tell you, on symptoms and their underlying causes subject by subject, on how to measure progress without relying on a feeling, and on the cheapest effective path through the published market rates. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, since home visits are a service we run only in India.

abu-dhabi/al-zahiyah.programmesIntro: Three routes cover almost all Al Zahiyah enquiries. The notes below focus on where each one produces a diagnosable problem, because that is what a first session should be identifying.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written papers after two years, tiered in many subjects, with codes that decide the match: Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, and Pearson 4MA1 and 4PH1. Most subjects now carry no coursework, so the entire grade is produced in a few hours of examination.
programmes.countryNote: That concentration is why exam technique matters so much at this level and why it is the cheapest thing to fix. An Al Zahiyah student who knows the content and loses marks to timing and command terms can usually recover a grade in a handful of sessions, which is a very different proposition from a two-year programme.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked from 0 to 8, with no terminal examination unless the school enters eAssessment. Reports show criterion letters, which is more informative than a percentage if you know how to read them and less informative if you do not.
programmes.countryNote: The criterion letters are an advantage for a family wanting evidence. Ask the school which criterion the marks were lost on, across subjects. A student consistently weak on one criterion in three different subjects has one problem, not three, and that is the single most useful thing a report of this kind can reveal.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed work carries a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade, which means a substantial part of the result is produced outside class and outside exam conditions.
programmes.countryNote: For a budget-conscious household this is where attention is best spent, because internally assessed marks are earned under no time pressure with the criteria published in advance. A short block of criterion coaching on one component can move more marks than a term of general support in the same subject.

abu-dhabi/al-zahiyah.subjectsIntro: Each note pairs a subject with the symptom that most often brings an Al Zahiyah family to a tutor, because the symptom usually points at a cause that is cheaper to fix than the family expects.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The commonest symptom is a student who can do the work slowly and cannot finish the paper. That is almost always arithmetic and algebraic fluency rather than understanding, and short frequent drilling fixes it. The second symptom is a non-calculator paper exposing a gap nobody noticed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The symptom at Higher Level is strong performance on Papers 1 and 2 with a collapse on Paper 3, which supplies no method. That is a reasoning gap rather than a content gap and it takes sustained practice on unfamiliar extended problems with the solution withheld.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The symptom is full marks on the calculation and nothing on the comment. Students produce a correct regression or model and then describe it inaccurately in words, which costs the interpretation marks. Written answers marked line by line fix this faster than more statistics teaching.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: The symptom is a student who understands the physics and cannot rearrange the equation. Beneath most apparent physics weakness in Years 10 and 11 is algebra, and treating it as physics wastes a term. Electricity is the exception that is genuinely a physics problem, particularly mixed circuits.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The symptom is strong descriptive answers and lost calculation marks. Mole work is a procedural skill that decays without practice, and a fortnight of short drills recovers it. At Diploma level the recoverable marks are in the investigation, where the criteria are published in advance.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The symptom is a student who clearly knows the material and scores in the middle band. The cause is almost always imprecise language: movement described without naming the gradient, the membrane or the protein. Marked written answers, weekly, are the whole remedy.

subjects.name: English
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0500 and 0510 · IB English A and B
subjects.description: The symptom is running out of time on the final question. That is a planning and mark-allocation problem rather than a writing problem, and it is fixed by reading the marks available before writing. Students entered for First Language English who would fit Second Language English are a separate and common issue.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: The symptom is well-learned definitions and middling marks. Application carries the grade: the concept has to be applied to the specific business in the extract, with its figures. Students who revise terminology and not application reliably sit in the middle bands regardless of effort.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The symptom is lost diagram marks that the student believes they earned. An unlabelled axis or a shift drawn without a new equilibrium caps the answer however good the evaluation. Diagram drilling is quick, cheap and among the highest-yield work available in this subject.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools and taught separately from the first-language stream. The symptom in a mixed district like this one is a student placed by year group rather than by level, sitting in a class pitched well above them. Short frequent sessions on script and core vocabulary are the realistic route.

abu-dhabi/al-zahiyah.regionsIntro: Al Zahiyah's neighbours matter here mainly for where the schools are and what the comparison options cost. Each note is written from an Al Zahiyah apartment rather than from a map.

regions.name: Al Maryah Island
regions.note: Immediately north across a short bridge, a financial district with no school of its own. Al Zahiyah and Al Maryah households often use the same schools and the same bus routes, though Al Maryah families tend to be scheduling around working hours rather than around cost.

regions.name: Al Nahyan
regions.note: South-west in the centre of the island, with a dense school mix and a long-established Arabic-speaking population. Al Zahiyah students frequently attend schools in that corridor, and the afternoon run between the two is short enough for a 16:30 start.

regions.name: Al Wahda
regions.note: West around the Al Wahda interchange, one of the slowest points on the island at pick-up. Al Zahiyah families whose school run passes through it should plan a 17:00 start on weekdays rather than 16:30.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Across the island to the west, with the heaviest concentration of tuition centres in the city. It is the natural comparison point for a budget-conscious Al Zahiyah family, and the drive there and back is itself a second school run in the same afternoon.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: South-east across the channel, home to The British International School Abu Dhabi and Repton Abu Dhabi. From Al Zahiyah the run is fifteen to twenty-five minutes, which makes it one of the more manageable Diploma commutes on the island.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: North over the bridge, home to Cranleigh Abu Dhabi. Fewer Al Zahiyah families commute there, and those who do commit the whole afternoon, so evening slots from 18:00 are the practical option.

regions.name: Al Mina and the port area
regions.note: Directly north-west of Al Zahiyah, largely commercial. It matters mainly as traffic: port and market movements add to the same roads the school buses use, which is part of why the window before 16:30 is unreliable here.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of a class hour, and what it leaves undone
paragraphs: The direct answer: in a class of twenty-four to twenty-eight students an hour of teaching contains roughly two or three minutes of potential individual feedback per student, and no teacher can distribute it evenly while also teaching the lesson. A one-to-one hour contains sixty minutes of it. That difference is the entire reason private tuition exists, and it has nothing to do with the quality of the school.

The arithmetic matters because it tells you what classroom teaching is good at and what it cannot do. It is good at delivering content systematically to a group, at modelling method, and at setting and reviewing common assessments. It cannot diagnose one student's recurring error pattern, because diagnosing that requires reading their work closely and asking them to explain their reasoning aloud.

That is why the symptoms described throughout this page persist for terms. A student who omits units loses marks on every paper and is told to be careful. A student who misreads command terms writes more and scores less and is told to focus. Neither instruction names the actual behaviour, because naming it requires watching one student work through several questions, which is a one-to-one activity.

The practical consequence for a budget-conscious Al Zahiyah family is encouraging rather than expensive. The work that only one-to-one can do is often short. Finding and fixing a recurring error pattern is a handful of sessions, not a year. The content teaching, which is the expensive part, is the part the school is already doing well.

sections.heading: What a report card does not tell you, and what to ask instead
paragraphs: A report card is a summary written for thirty families at once, under time pressure, in a format the school has standardised. It is not dishonest and it is not useless. It is simply the wrong instrument for the question a parent actually has, which is what specifically is costing marks and what should be done about it.

The items a report cannot carry are predictable. It cannot say which component the marks were lost on. It cannot say whether the problem is content, timing or command terms. It cannot say whether the student is three weeks behind the scheme of work because of a staffing change in October. And it cannot say whether the grade reflects a mock paper sat with half the syllabus still untaught.

All of that is obtainable by asking, and subject teachers answer specific questions readily. The difference between asking how my child is getting on and asking which criterion they lost marks on in the last assessment is the difference between a sentence of reassurance and a usable fact. The second question is also easier for a teacher to answer, which is why it usually gets a better reply.

The table lists the questions worth asking and who to direct each one to. Take them to a parents' evening or send them by email. In an MYP school the equivalent question is which criterion, across subjects, and that single question sometimes reveals that three apparent subject problems are one skill problem.

sections.heading: What a first diagnostic session should produce
paragraphs: Before spending anything on a programme, a family should know what is wrong in specific terms. That is what a first session is for, and it is reasonable to judge a tutor entirely on what that session produces. The output should be written, specific, and short enough to read in a minute.

A good diagnostic ends with four things. A named list of what the student is losing marks on, in order of how many marks it costs. A statement of whether each item is content, fluency, timing or technique, because those have different remedies. An estimate of how many sessions each item needs. And the order in which they should be addressed, since algebra precedes physics and fluency precedes speed.

The input that makes this possible is a marked paper. A complete past paper, sat to time, unmarked or marked by the school, tells a tutor more in ten minutes than an hour of conversation. Bringing one to a first session is the single most efficient thing an Al Zahiyah family can do, and it costs nothing but the time to sit the paper at the weekend.

If a first session ends with general encouragement and a suggestion to book a term, that is useful information too. Ask for the written list before agreeing to anything further. A tutor who can produce it will do so readily, and one who cannot has not diagnosed anything yet. The list is also what makes a quote arguable: a problem described as a fortnight of drilling should not be priced as two terms.

sections.heading: Group class, small group or one-to-one: the honest trade-off
paragraphs: Al Zahiyah families compare these options more carefully than most, and the comparison deserves a straight answer rather than an argument for the most expensive choice. Each format does something the others do not, and the right one depends entirely on what the diagnostic found.

A tuition centre group class is the cheapest supervised option and is genuinely useful for revising content the whole group is weak on. Its limit is that it cannot diagnose an individual, cannot work on one student's Internal Assessment, and cannot adapt mid-session to one student's misunderstanding without stalling the others. For a student whose problem is a knowledge gap shared with their class, it is good value.

A small online group of two to four students at the same board, level and tier is the best-value format for timed paper practice, because the errors are often common and a mark-scheme walkthrough benefits everyone in the room. It stops being suitable the moment the work becomes individual, which includes any coursework component and any individual diagnosis.

One-to-one is the only format that does diagnosis, error-pattern work and criterion coaching, and for those jobs it is not a premium version of the others but the only option. The cost-effective approach in this district is to use it for exactly those jobs, in short blocks, and to leave content revision to the cheaper formats or to the school. Mixing the two deliberately, rather than choosing one format for everything, is what produces the lowest total spend.

sections.heading: Symptoms and their actual causes, subject by subject
paragraphs: Most families describe a problem by its symptom, which is reasonable because the symptom is what they can see. The value of a diagnostic is that the symptom and the cause are often in different subjects, and treating the symptom can mean paying for a term of teaching that was never going to help.

The clearest example is physics in Years 10 and 11. A student who understands forces and cannot rearrange an equation looks like a physics problem and is an algebra problem. Four weeks of algebra fluency resolves it; a term of physics teaching does not, because every lesson stalls at the same point and the student concludes they are bad at the subject.

The pattern repeats with different pairings. Lost marks in biology usually come from imprecise language rather than from gaps in knowledge. Middling business studies grades come from revising definitions rather than practising application. Lost economics marks come from diagram conventions, which take two sessions to fix and are worth marks on every paper for two years.

The table pairs each symptom with its usual cause and an honest estimate of the time involved. Use it to interrogate a quote. If a provider proposes a two-term programme for a problem this table describes as a fortnight of drilling, ask them to explain what the remaining months contain.

One caution about the table: it describes the usual cause, not the only one. A student losing marks on written answers may have a genuine content gap underneath, and the diagnostic exists precisely to tell the two apart before anybody spends money on the wrong remedy.

sections.heading: Measuring progress without relying on a feeling
paragraphs: The commonest way tutoring money is wasted is not fraud. It is a family paying for a year of sessions that everyone feels positive about, with no measurement, discovering at results time that nothing moved. Avoiding that costs nothing except the discipline of deciding in advance what will be measured.

The measure has to be the same thing twice. A raw mark on a comparable paper at the start and again after a block is evidence. A different paper of unknown difficulty is not. A tutor's report that the student is more confident is not evidence either, though it may be true and is worth having alongside the number.

Error pattern is the second measure, and in some ways the better one. If a student omitted units on nine marks' worth of questions in January and on one mark's worth in March, that is progress even if the overall score barely moved, because the remaining marks are elsewhere. Keeping a written list of recurring errors makes this visible without any extra work.

Set the review points in advance: four sessions in, to judge whether the match works, and at the end of each block, to judge whether the problem closed. Four sessions is early enough that changing tutor costs nothing. Discovering a mismatch in the final term, with a paper three weeks away, costs the grade.

None of this requires a spreadsheet. A single sheet of paper with the start mark, the end mark and three named errors on it does the whole job, and it is the thing to ask a tutor to maintain from the first session.

sections.heading: The cheapest effective path, with the published rates
paragraphs: The figures below are market rates in the UAE, drawn from providers' own published pricing and from a published 2026 Dubai tutoring rate survey by Bestimate. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list. For a household where cost is a genuine constraint, the useful question is not the lowest rate but the lowest total spend that fixes the diagnosed problem.

Published hourly figures run from roughly AED 45 to 65 at the budget online end and AED 33 to 52 from one platform's entry tier, AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB from an agency that publishes rates, AED 270 from a UK-based agency, a survey band of AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist exam-year work, and AED 650 at the premium named end. In-home visits in the emirate are published between roughly AED 180 and AED 500, with travel inside the hour.

Monthly bundles are where the travel premium shows up most plainly. A package of eight online sessions is advertised at around AED 799; four two-hour in-home sessions, which is fewer hours, is quoted at AED 1,599 to 1,799. On a weekly one-hour pattern the same survey puts budget support at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-market at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist exam-year work at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more.

The cheapest effective path usually looks like this. Spend one session on a diagnostic with a marked paper in hand. Buy a short block at a mid-market rate for the one thing that costs the most marks. Use a group format or the school for content revision. Re-test. Then decide whether a second block is justified. That sequence frequently costs less than two months of undifferentiated weekly support and moves more marks.

sections.heading: An in-home tutor in an Al Zahiyah apartment, compared with online
paragraphs: Al Zahiyah is central and well connected, so a tutor based on the island can reach most addresses here quickly, and families asking about in-home tuition are not being unrealistic about the geography. Two things about this district nonetheless point the other way.

The first is cost. Published in-home rates in the emirate start above the published online rates, between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, against roughly AED 45 to 300 online depending on tier. For a household choosing the lowest effective total spend, that difference pays for the extra sessions that actually close a gap.

The second is space. Apartments in this district are generally compact, often with one working surface shared with the rest of the household's evening. A video session in a bedroom with a laptop is frequently quieter and less disruptive than a visitor in the living room, and it does not require the family to clear a room for an hour.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE, and does not operate a centre in the emirate. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for marking papers. In-home provision still has a real advantage for younger children who need an adult physically present to stay on task, which is worth saying on a page recommending something else. For a Year 11 candidate losing marks on one component, the subject match matters far more than the room.

sections.heading: Trials, conditions and the claims worth refusing
paragraphs: Where a trial session is offered free, the conditions attached belong on the same screen as the word: how long the session is, whether it is a full lesson or an introduction, whether a card is required, and what happens automatically afterwards. A trial with undisclosed conditions is a sales step rather than a trial, and it is reasonable to ask for the terms in writing before booking.

Several claims in this market should simply be refused. Any promise of a specific grade, any assurance that marks will rise by a stated amount, or a refund tied to a result: no provider can promise an examination outcome and anyone offering to is selling something other than teaching. Any claim of approval, accreditation or licensing from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, unless a document number can be shown. IB Gram holds none of those.

Statistics without their basis are the third category. A satisfaction percentage, an average score or a success rate presented without the number of students, the date and the method behind it is not evidence. Published review ratings should be checked for consistency as well: researched competitors in this market display different rating figures on the same page.

The fourth is the offer to supply completed work. Assessed coursework must be the student's own, and the consequence of a malpractice finding falls on the student and can mean a diploma is not awarded. A tutor explains the criteria, questions the method and gives feedback on existing drafts. Nothing beyond that enters a submission, and board papers and mark schemes come through the school rather than from a provider's library.
bullets: Trial conditions stated on the same screen as the offer, in writing
No grade promise, no promise of a grade rise, no outcome-linked refund
No regulator or board approval claimed without a document number
No statistic without the number of students, the date and the method
No supplied text, data or analysis for any assessed submission

process.title: Sit one full paper at the weekend
process.description: Before contacting anyone, have your child write one complete past paper to time, in one sitting, with nothing open. It costs a Saturday morning and it is the single most informative input a tutor can be given. A conversation about how a student feels about a subject tells almost nobody anything useful.

process.title: Ask the subject teacher the specific question
process.description: Email the subject teacher and ask which questions the marks were lost on and whether the cause is content, timing or command terms. Specific questions get specific answers, and in an MYP school the equivalent question is which criterion, across subjects. Three apparent subject problems are often one skill problem.

process.title: Buy a diagnostic before buying a programme
process.description: Pay for one session and judge it on what it produces: a written list of losses in priority order, each classified by type, with an estimated session count and an order to tackle them. If the session ends in general encouragement instead, ask for the list before committing to anything more.

process.title: Match the format to the finding, not to the budget alone
process.description: A content gap shared with the class is cheapest addressed in a group. Timed paper practice suits a small group at the same board and tier. An individual error pattern or an Internal Assessment criterion needs one-to-one, in a short block. Using the cheapest format for the wrong job is more expensive than using the right one.

process.title: Set the review points before the first session
process.description: Four sessions in, to judge the match, and at the end of each block, with a re-test on the original material. Four sessions is early enough that changing tutor is free. The alternative is a year everybody feels positive about and a results day nobody expected.

whyPoints.title: The diagnosis comes before the quote
whyPoints.description: A written list of what is losing marks, in priority order and classified by type, is produced before any programme is proposed. A family can then judge a quote against a named problem rather than against a general offer of support.

whyPoints.title: The cheapest format that works is recommended
whyPoints.description: Where a group class or the school's own support would address the finding, this page says so. One-to-one is used for the jobs only one-to-one can do, which is diagnosis, error patterns and criterion coaching, and those are usually short blocks.

whyPoints.title: Progress measured on comparable material
whyPoints.description: Blocks begin and end with the same or equivalent material, sat to time, so the change in raw mark is evidence rather than impression. The recurring error list is kept in writing, which makes improvement visible even when the headline score moves slowly.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it and is presented as the market rather than as our price. That is what makes it possible for a budget-conscious household to tell a fair quote from an inflated one.

whyPoints.title: No promises that cannot be kept
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantee, no outcome-linked refund, no claimed approval from any regulator or examination board, and no statistic without its basis. IB Gram holds no accreditation from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

faqs.question: Why does my child need a tutor if the school in Al Zahiyah is good?
faqs.answer: Because of arithmetic rather than quality. In a class of twenty-four to twenty-eight, an hour of teaching contains two or three minutes of potential individual feedback per student, and no teacher can distribute that evenly while also teaching. Classroom teaching is good at delivering content systematically and poor at diagnosing one student's recurring error pattern, because that requires reading their work closely and hearing them reason aloud. The gap is structural, it exists in every school system, and the work that fills it is often shorter than families expect.

faqs.question: What should I ask the subject teacher instead of how my child is doing?
faqs.answer: Ask which questions the marks were lost on and why, and whether the cause is a content gap, a timing problem or command terms. Ask what each component is worth in the final grade. Ask whether the class is on schedule against the scheme of work. Specific questions get specific answers and are easier for a teacher to answer than a general one. In an MYP school, ask which criterion the marks were lost on, across subjects, because one weak criterion in three subjects is one problem rather than three.

faqs.question: What should a paid diagnostic session actually produce?
faqs.answer: Four things, in writing. A named list of what the student is losing marks on, ordered by how many marks each costs. A classification of each item as content, fluency, timing or technique, since those have different remedies. An estimated session count for each. And the order to tackle them, because algebra precedes physics and fluency precedes speed. Bring a complete past paper sat to time, which tells a tutor more in ten minutes than an hour of conversation. If the session ends in general encouragement, ask for the list before booking more.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class in Abu Dhabi good value?
faqs.answer: For the right job, yes. A group class is the cheapest supervised option and is genuinely useful for revising content the whole group is weak on, since the teaching is identical for everyone who needs it. Its limits are real: it cannot diagnose an individual, cannot work on one student's Internal Assessment, and cannot adapt mid-session without stalling the others. Ask the class size before comparing any rate, because six students and twelve students are different products at the same headline price.

faqs.question: When is a small online group better than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For timed paper practice where two to four students share the same board, level and tier. The errors are often common across students, so a mark-scheme walkthrough benefits everyone present, and the cost per student is lower than one-to-one. It stops being suitable the moment the work becomes individual, which includes any coursework component and any genuine diagnosis. Groups are arranged where a matching set of students exists at the same point in the same specification, rather than promised in advance of one existing.

faqs.question: My child understands physics but keeps losing marks. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Nine times out of ten it is algebra rather than physics. A student who understands forces and cannot rearrange an equation at speed looks like a physics problem and is a mathematics problem, and every physics lesson stalls at the same point until the fluency is fixed. Roughly four weeks of algebraic rearrangement drilling resolves it. A term of physics content teaching does not, and it leaves the student concluding they are bad at the subject. Electricity, particularly mixed series and parallel circuits, is the genuine exception.

faqs.question: Why does my child score in the middle band in biology despite knowing the content?
faqs.answer: Almost always imprecise language. Mark schemes in biology reward naming the mechanism: the gradient, the membrane, the transport protein, the specific enzyme. An answer that describes something moving without naming what makes it move loses marks the student believes they earned, and the student reads the lost marks as unfair rather than as a phrasing habit. The remedy is marked written answers, weekly, against the official scheme, with the reason written next to each lost mark. Four to six weeks is usually enough.

faqs.question: How quickly can diagram marks in economics be fixed?
faqs.answer: Usually in two or three sessions, which makes it among the highest-yield work available in the subject. The marks are lost on convention rather than on understanding: an axis labelled with a quantity where a price belongs, a curve shifted without a new equilibrium marked, a diagram drawn after the written answer rather than before it. Once the conventions are automatic, they earn marks on every paper for the rest of the course. It is worth asking for this specifically rather than booking general economics support.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether a tutoring block in Al Zahiyah is working?
faqs.answer: On the same material twice. A raw mark on a comparable paper at the start of a block and again at the end is evidence; a different paper of unknown difficulty is not. Track the recurring error list as well, because a student who omitted units on nine marks' worth in January and one mark's worth in March has improved even if the total barely moved. Set review points in advance: four sessions in to judge the match, and the end of each block to judge the outcome.

faqs.question: What is the least expensive route that actually moves a grade?
faqs.answer: One paid diagnostic session with a marked paper in hand. Then a short three to six session one-to-one block on whichever problem costs the most marks. Then content revision through a group class or the school's own support, which is free to the family. Then a re-test, and only then a decision about a second block. That sequence frequently costs less than two months of undifferentiated weekly support and moves more marks, because every dirham is spent on a named problem.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to apartments in Al Zahiyah?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Two things about this district point the same way. Published in-home rates in the emirate run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, against roughly AED 45 to 300 online depending on tier. And apartments here are compact, so a video session at a desk with headphones is often less disruptive than clearing the living room for a visitor.

faqs.question: What should a free trial session include before we book?
faqs.answer: The conditions, stated in writing on the same screen as the offer: how long the session is, whether it is a full lesson or an introduction, whether a card is required, and what happens automatically afterwards. A trial with undisclosed conditions is a sales step rather than a trial. It is reasonable to ask what the session will produce as well, because a trial that ends with a written list of what is losing marks is worth far more than one that ends with a positive impression.

faqs.question: Which tutoring claims should I refuse outright?
faqs.answer: Any promise of a specific grade, any assurance that marks will rise by a stated amount, or a refund tied to a result, because no provider can promise an examination outcome. Any claim of approval, accreditation or licensing from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson without a document number; IB Gram holds none of those. Any statistic presented without the number of students, the date and the method behind it. And any offer to supply completed coursework, which exposes the student to a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: How do I know whether a published rating is trustworthy?
faqs.answer: Check it for internal consistency first. Researched competitors in this market display different rating figures in different places on the same page, and one shows a rating from a small number of reviews alongside a claim about a far larger student body. A rating that is not backed by countable, attributable, dated reviews is a decoration. More useful signals are whether the provider will state the tutor's board and syllabus code, whether reschedule terms are in writing, and what a first session produces.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment if we are on a tight budget?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it may be the best value available, because internally assessed marks are earned under no time pressure with the criteria published in advance. A short block explaining how each criterion is awarded, questioning the method, and giving feedback on a draft the student has already written can move more marks than a term of general subject support. The boundary matters: no text, data or analysis is supplied for the submission, because a malpractice finding falls on the student and can mean a diploma is not awarded.

abu-dhabi/al-zahiyah.closingHeading: Diagnose first, then buy the smallest thing that fixes it
abu-dhabi/al-zahiyah.closingBody: The useful order for an Al Zahiyah family is unglamorous and cheap. Have your child sit one full past paper to time at the weekend. Email the subject teacher the specific question about which marks were lost and why. Pay for one diagnostic session and insist it ends in a written list. Then buy the shortest block that addresses whatever costs the most marks, leave content revision to the school or a group class, and re-test before spending anything further. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, with the marked paper shared on screen and kept by the student.

abu-dhabi/baniyas.tutorsIntro: Requests from Baniyas skew towards two things: written Standard Arabic for students carrying the first-language course inside an English-medium school, and maths and science at IGCSE where a grade is at risk rather than where a top grade is being chased. Both are taught one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Who studies in Baniyas, and what the household is weighing up
paragraphs: Baniyas is not a new community and does not behave like one. It sits east of Abu Dhabi city, past Mussafah, split across Baniyas East and West and the Shabiya sectors, with Bawabat Al Sharq as its centre of gravity. Housing is lower-rise and more affordable than the island or the newer villa districts, and a high proportion of households have been here for a decade or more rather than arriving on a three-year posting. That changes the tutoring conversation in three concrete ways.

The first is budget discipline. A family planning across ten years of schooling, often for three or four children, treats AED 300 an hour as a decision rather than a rounding error. They want to know what each provider model actually charges, what the difference buys, and whether a smaller number of well-targeted hours would do the same job. Nobody in this district is impressed by a page that refuses to publish a price, which several of the best-ranked tutoring sites for these searches still do.

The second is the Arabic stream. In many Baniyas households Arabic is the language of the home, and the children sit Arabic as a first language inside an English-medium international school. That course is examined on grammar, classical and modern texts and formal written register, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction. Fluent spoken dialect does not carry a student through it, and the gap between the two is the single most common reason a report card in this district looks inconsistent.

The third is distance. There is no cluster of private international schools inside Baniyas itself, so children travel - towards Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City, or further to Khalifa City and the island. A tutor driving out here is pricing a round trip into the hour, which the published market bands show plainly: travel adds roughly AED 30 to 150 an hour across every source, and one advertised in-home monthly package sits at double the online equivalent. The same journey also shortens the evening at both ends, because a bus that leaves the Mussafah corridor in the afternoon arrives later than any published timetable implies, and the household's real start time for anything academic is pushed past six on most weekdays of the term.

What is on offer here is one-to-one tuition over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For a Baniyas household the gain is not novelty but access: the pool of people who can teach written Standard Arabic to a Diploma standard, or Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4, is not limited to those willing to drive to this side of the city on a weekday evening.
bullets: A long-settled district, so tutoring is a budget decision rather than an impulse
Arabic as a first language is frequently the subject that needs most attention
No private international school cluster inside the district; children travel to school
Travel adds roughly AED 30-150 an hour across every published rate source
Every lesson is one-to-one over live video, so the hour buys teaching only

abu-dhabi/baniyas.programmesIntro: Three stages cover almost every enquiry from Baniyas, and the pressure points differ sharply between them. The notes below describe what each one demands of a student in this district rather than summarising a syllabus.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The qualification most Baniyas students take, and the one where tutoring decisions are usually about protecting a grade rather than chasing an A star. Cambridge tiers maths and the sciences into Core and Extended; Pearson structures its papers differently. The tier entry caps what is possible, so the decision deserves evidence and a deadline in the diary.
programmes.countryNote: The schools this district uses do not all enter the same board, and some mix them across subjects. For a parent the first practical step is to find the syllabus code on the entry - 0580 or 0607 for Cambridge maths, 4MA1 for Pearson - because the paper structures differ even where the mathematics is identical. For UAE equivalency, five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3 are counted, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Baniyas students who take it have usually travelled to a school in another district to do so, which makes their evenings shorter than their classmates'. Internal assessments carry around a fifth to a quarter of most subject grades and are produced almost entirely at home.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session. For a Baniyas student that puts maximum pressure on the autumn of Year 13, when internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay and predicted grades for university applications all arrive together. Confirm every IB date with the school's Diploma coordinator or ibo.org; secondary listings of IB session dates are not reliable enough to plan a year on.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Reported against four criteria per subject, each out of eight. Parents used to percentages find the reporting hard to act on, and students often sit in the middle band for two years without anyone explaining which descriptor they are failing to meet. The fix is usually technique on open-ended tasks rather than more content.
programmes.countryNote: A Baniyas student transferring between an MYP school and a GCSE school meets the same content described in a different language. The quickest win is to take one marked task, read the descriptors in plain English, and rewrite the piece to hit the next band. That is a two-session job and it changes how the student reads every subsequent brief.

abu-dhabi/baniyas.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Baniyas households book most, with the component that costs the marks named rather than a general description of the course.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.levels: The mandatory stream, MYP and DP Language A
subjects.description: Grammar, classical and modern texts and formal written register, assessed in Standard Arabic. The usual gap in this district is between confident spoken dialect and examined written Standard Arabic. Marks go on inflection, formal structure and text analysis rather than on comprehension.

subjects.name: Islamic education
subjects.levels: The mandatory stream, Arab and non-Arab routes
subjects.description: Taught in Standard Arabic for Arab students and in the school's curriculum language for others, against centrally prescribed content. Tutoring supports reading comprehension, terminology and structured written answers; the material itself cannot be substituted for something easier.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended sits on Papers 2 and 4, Core on Papers 1 and 3, so practice does not transfer between tiers. Marks go on transformations, vectors, and the long structured questions where a student does the hard step then answers a different question from the one asked.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and the moments and momentum questions carry most of the marks lost. The alternative-to-practical paper tests experimental reasoning in writing and rewards a student who has practised criticising a method rather than reciting one.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables separate the middle grades from the top ones. Students who memorise the ion tests as a list rather than as chemistry lose them under exam pressure, which is a teaching problem with a short fix.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: A long syllabus with very specific examinable detail: named enzymes, named vessels, named stages. Students doing well in class and poorly in mocks are usually revising topics instead of practising the command words the paper actually uses.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Rewards accurate controlled writing and careful reading rather than flair. For students whose home language is Arabic this is often the right entry, but it carries consequences for later university language conditions that are worth checking before Year 10.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistical route through Diploma maths, and not the easy option. Regression, chi-squared and hypothesis testing on the graphical display calculator decide whole questions, and Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Graded by command term as much as by content: distinguish, evaluate and examine want different answer structures. The internal assessment needs a real organisation and a decision genuinely worth analysing, which is where most of the early work goes.

abu-dhabi/baniyas.modesIntro: Three formats suit this district, and the choice is usually driven by budget and by how many children need help at once rather than by preference.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on a single subject
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, a fixed hour each week. For a household watching the total, concentrating on the one subject where a grade is genuinely at risk is more effective than spreading four half-hours across four subjects. The tutor sees the student across months and can tell the difference between a bad week and a real gap.

sections.heading: What each kind of tutoring provider charges, and who will tell you
paragraphs: Start with the uncomfortable fact about this market. Of the strongest pages ranking for these searches, three publish no price at all, and one asks the price in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. Two quote US dollars. A household in Baniyas comparing options therefore has to assemble the picture from scraps, which is precisely why the table below exists.

The models are genuinely different products. A local freelance tutor is cheapest per hour at the low end and carries the most risk, because nobody except you is checking qualifications or the MoHRE permit. A tuition centre spreads cost across a group and has premises, which in Dubai means it needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An international marketplace is a self-service directory with pricing in dollars. An agency does the matching and charges for it.

Where a figure in the table is attributed to a provider, that provider published it. Unitors advertises IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase shows AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from the low thirties. Bestimate's 2026 rate table gives in-home ranges of AED 180 to 350 and specialist ranges of AED 200 to 450 and above. Those are market rates, dated, and they are not IB Gram's quote.

The last row of the table is the honest version of what is on offer here. No published rate card, because a Higher Level chemistry hour and a Year 7 maths hour are not the same purchase. No travel, because UAE delivery is online one-to-one over live video. A trial lesson with the matched tutor before any term is committed to, so the comparison you make is against teaching rather than against a brochure.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context for a Baniyas household
paragraphs: An hourly rate on its own tells a family very little. What helps is seeing the figure next to the other numbers in the same household budget, which is the comparison no competing page in this market makes. Fees are the dominant line, and in the Emirates fee levels and increases are not set by a school in isolation; the emirate authority approves them. For Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the published federal description is explicit that the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

Against that, tutoring is a smaller and more controllable line. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages have included around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits at home. Those last two numbers are the clearest published statement of what driving costs.

The sensible planning move for a household here is to treat tutoring as a block with a purpose rather than a standing subscription. A term of one subject before a mock, a coursework supervision block with a known end date, a diagnostic to decide whether anything more is needed. That shape costs less and works better than a general weekly arrangement that nobody reviews.

One point of context worth knowing from the other emirate. Dubai's regulator confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi runs its own arrangements through the Department of Education and Knowledge, so do not read Dubai's decision as applying here; ask your own school what has been approved.
