sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic education and social studies: the stream nobody plans for
paragraphs: In Baniyas this is often the most consequential part of the page. Private schools in the Emirates are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must still comply with the Ministry's general regulations. Whatever international curriculum a school is licensed to deliver, those subjects sit on the timetable, are taught, are assessed and appear on the report.

The most detailed published guidance on how these classes are organised comes from Dubai's regulator, which requires that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic education and social studies, schools organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It sets Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for social studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arab students in Islamic education and in moral, social and cultural studies. Abu Dhabi schools work to the Department of Education and Knowledge's own requirements, so confirm your school's arrangement with the school.

Two further details from that guidance are practically useful. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. And the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry, is strictly prohibited - which means a tutor cannot swap the school's prescribed material for something more convenient.

What tutoring can do within those limits is narrow and genuinely effective. For Arabic as a first language: grammar, formal written register and text analysis, taught in Standard Arabic, against the texts the school has set. For Islamic education and social studies: reading comprehension, subject terminology and the structure of a written answer. No competitor page found in this market has a section on any of this; Arabic appears on their pages as a chip on a subject list.

sections.heading: Is the person you are paying legally permitted to tutor in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a fair question and it has a clear answer, which only one competing page in this market addresses at all. Private tuition in the Emirates requires a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents assume: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so a figure quoted on a website as the fine should be treated as unverified - a number circulating widely could not be confirmed against any official source.

One restriction matters for Abu Dhabi households in particular. Professional-ethics rules reported for private and charter school staff in the emirate bar teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct has been reported to carry the same bar. That is press-reported rather than quoted from a current policy document, so verify it against the Department of Education and Knowledge's own publication if the point matters to you. Either way, your child's own class teacher is the wrong person to hire.

IB Gram holds no regulator permit, runs no premises in the Emirates, and does not describe itself as approved or accredited by any authority, because it is not. What it does is match families with tutors for online one-to-one lessons. The permit question is one to put directly to any individual taking payment, and the table sets out who needs what.

sections.heading: Group lessons, small groups and one-to-one
paragraphs: Group tuition is a genuine option and this page is not going to pretend otherwise. A group of three or four students at the same stage and the same board, taught by one teacher, costs each family substantially less per hour and works well for content coverage: a syllabus topic explained once, questions worked through together, homework set for everyone. For a Baniyas household with two children and a fixed budget, that arithmetic deserves a hearing.

The limits are equally real. A group moves at one pace, which is the pace of nobody in it. A student whose problem is a specific misconception goes unheard, because the lesson cannot stop for twenty minutes to unpick one person's algebra. Coursework supervision cannot be grouped at all in any meaningful way: an internal assessment is individual work with an individual research question, and a group session on it risks producing suspiciously similar submissions, which is an academic-honesty problem rather than an efficiency gain.

The pattern that tends to work is mixed and sequenced. Use group or class teaching for breadth, then buy a small number of one-to-one hours precisely where the marked evidence says marks are being lost. Four well-targeted individual hours in February often beat twenty general ones spread from September, and they cost less in total. The reason to start with a marked paper rather than a subject name is exactly this: it tells you how few hours you actually need.

What IB Gram runs in the Emirates is one-to-one over live video. That choice follows from what families ask for - a specific paper, a specific component, a specific misconception - rather than from a view that groups are bad. Where the need is genuinely breadth across a whole syllabus, a school's own revision programme or a centre class may be the better value, and saying so is more useful than pretending otherwise.
bullets: Groups are cheaper per hour and effective for covering content breadth
A group cannot stop to unpick one student's specific misconception

sections.heading: What an inspection rating tells a Baniyas parent, and what it does not
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. Parents in this district use those ratings heavily when choosing a school, and they are worth using - but they answer a different question from the one a tutoring decision asks.

An inspection judges a school: leadership, teaching quality across departments, outcomes, inclusion, governance. It is an aggregate. A school rated well overall can have one department that is thin in a particular year because two teachers left in August, and a school rated less well can have an outstanding physics teacher. Neither fact appears in the headline band, and both are the sort of thing that determines whether your Year 11 needs help in chemistry.

The practical use of a report for tutoring purposes is in its detail rather than its grade. Inspection reports comment on specific subjects and phases, on attainment in Arabic and Islamic education, and on the progress of particular groups. Reading the paragraph about your child's phase in their subject is far more informative than reading the overall band, and it is free to do.

What no rating does is tell you which of your child's six subjects is going wrong. That question is answered by marked work: a mock paper, a returned internal assessment draft, a criterion-marked task. Bring the marked thing, not the inspection report, to a conversation about tutoring. And treat any provider that claims a regulator has approved it with suspicion, because the Department licenses schools, not tutoring platforms, and nobody should imply otherwise.
bullets: Inspection outcomes judge a whole school, not a single department in a single year
The subject and phase paragraphs are more useful than the headline band

sections.heading: IGCSE then A Level, or the Diploma? A Baniyas student's decision
paragraphs: Because this district's children travel to school, families here often have a real choice of post-16 route rather than whatever the local school happens to offer. The schools within reach include British sixth forms and IB Diploma programmes, and the two are different bets rather than one being better.

The Diploma is six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, graded on a points scale. It suits a student who is broadly strong, organised, and either undecided about a degree subject or aiming at a system that likes breadth. It is unforgiving of a student who is excellent at three things and weak at a fourth, because the fourth still has to be passed and the coursework load is relentless.

The A Level route narrows to three or four subjects and goes deeper. It suits a student with a clear direction, particularly into engineering, medicine or economics, and it allows a weakness to be dropped rather than managed. The trade-off is that the choice is made earlier and reverses badly, and that a student who later changes direction may find a prerequisite missing.

For UAE equivalency the British route has published requirements: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB points threshold is published on this page, because no official source was read for one - ask the Ministry or check moe.gov.ae rather than trusting a figure on a tutoring site, including this one.
bullets: Diploma: breadth, six subjects, heavy coursework, points scale, no weak link permitted
A Level: depth in three or four, a weakness can be dropped, the choice reverses badly
Equivalency for the British route: five subjects at E or grade 3, plus A Level or AS passes
No IB equivalency figure is published here; verify that one with the authorities

sections.heading: What a tutor will and will not do with assessed work
paragraphs: This boundary is worth spelling out for every family, and particularly where a provider in the same search results sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules, the penalty lands on the student rather than on the seller, and it can cost a diploma. No amount of discretion makes that a sensible purchase.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. Teach the subject content the assessment rests on. Explain each criterion and what its descriptors actually require, which most students have never had done for them in plain language. Challenge a research question that is too broad to answer in the word count. Read a draft the student has written and say where the argument does not follow, where the evidence is thin and where the structure buries the point. Teach referencing properly.

What a tutor may not do is supply text. Not a paragraph, not a rewritten conclusion, not a worked data analysis pasted into a results section, not a bibliography typed out to be copied. The subtler version of the same breach is heavy line-editing: if a sentence in the submitted document was composed by the tutor, the work is no longer the student's own, and the supervisor's authenticity declaration becomes false.

The sequence that works is unglamorous and reliable. Agree the question. Draft alone. Bring it in and leave with a list of problems. Solve them alone. Repeat. Students who work that way produce better pieces than students handed an improved draft, because they have actually learned to write the thing, which is what the next assessment will ask of them again.
bullets: Allowed: content teaching, criterion explanation, scoping, feedback on the student's draft
Not allowed: any supplied text that reaches the submitted document
Heavy line-editing crosses the same line as authoring
The student signs the authenticity declaration and carries the consequence

process.title: Say what the budget and the goal are
process.description: A household deciding between four hours and forty should say so at the start. It changes the recommendation: a diagnostic block and a plan the family runs itself is a legitimate outcome, and it is better advice than a term of general support that nobody reviews. We would rather sell four useful hours than twenty vague ones.

process.title: Send the marked work
process.description: A mock paper, a criterion-marked task or a returned coursework draft tells a specialist which component is losing marks. That is a five-minute diagnosis from evidence rather than an hour of guessing from description, and in this district it usually reduces the number of hours needed rather than increasing it.

process.title: Confirm the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 are different purchases, and a Core entry caps the grade whatever the teaching. The school's entry confirmation settles it. For Cambridge candidates, ask the examinations officer which of the six administrative timetable zones the school sits in before planning around any published timetable.

process.title: Ask us, and the tutor, about the permit
process.description: You are entitled to ask any individual taking payment for private tuition whether they hold the MoHRE permit, and we expect you to. It is free of charge, valid two years, and issued in a stated two working days, so there is no good reason for a tutor not to have one or to be evasive about it.

process.title: Trial lesson, then a term or a block
process.description: One hour with the matched tutor, not a sales call. It ends with a written view on whether the problem is content, technique or pacing and how many sessions it should take. From there you choose a term, a finite block, or nothing, and a wrong match is rematched rather than defended.

whyPoints.title: Prices on the page, with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider or table it came from and the year. In a market where three of the strongest ranking pages publish no price and one refuses to answer its own pricing question, an attributed number is the minimum a Baniyas household should accept before paying anybody.

whyPoints.title: The Arabic stream treated as a subject
whyPoints.description: Arabic as a first language and Islamic education are taught here by teachers working in Standard Arabic, against the material the school has set. Across the competitor pages researched for this market, not one has a section on the mandatory UAE subjects at all.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered in full
whyPoints.description: The resolution number, the issuing ministry, the categories eligible, the validity, the stated processing time and the fact that no fine schedule is published. You can take that list to any tutor, including one you find elsewhere, and ask the questions yourself.

whyPoints.title: Honest about group teaching
whyPoints.description: Groups are cheaper and genuinely better for covering breadth. Where that is what a family needs, saying so is more useful than selling one-to-one hours. What one-to-one does better is fix a specific misconception, which is what marked work usually reveals.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the hour
whyPoints.description: UAE lessons are online one-to-one over live video, so the rate covers teaching rather than a round trip east of the city. The published in-home bands and packages show what that difference is worth in AED, and for this district it is the bulk of the saving.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No regulator accreditation, no premises in the Emirates, no star ratings, no percentage of students who improved. Where a figure cannot be sourced it is left out, including the IB equivalency threshold that at least one ranking competitor publishes without a basis.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors who will come to a house in Baniyas?
faqs.answer: No. Every lesson for a UAE family is one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India. The practical reason is cost and reach. Published market data shows travel adding roughly AED 30 to 150 to an hourly rate, and one advertised in-home monthly package sits at around double its online equivalent. A district east of the city also narrows the list of tutors willing to drive out on a weekday evening, which is exactly the wrong constraint when you need a specific subject specialist.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to get help for a Baniyas student?
faqs.answer: Usually a short diagnostic block rather than a long term. Three or four sessions built around a timed paper marked against the official scheme will identify which component is losing marks, and many families then run the practice themselves with a written plan. Where more is needed, concentrating on the single subject where a grade is genuinely at risk beats spreading half-hours across four subjects. Budget-tier online tutors start around AED 45 to 65 an hour by EdFlik's published rates, with qualified subject tutors from about AED 150.

faqs.question: Which private schools do children from this district usually attend?
faqs.answer: There is no cluster of private international schools inside Baniyas itself, so children travel. The nearest significant concentration of places sits around Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City, including Cambridge-curriculum campuses with fees below the island averages. Families wanting a British sixth form or a full IB continuum generally travel further, to Khalifa City, the Al Raha corridor or across the bridges. Check any school against the Department of Education and Knowledge's own listing, since it licenses and inspects private schools in the emirate.

faqs.question: Can you help with Arabic as a first language for a child in an English-medium school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most common request from this district. The course assesses grammar, classical and modern texts and formal written register, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction, so a child fluent in spoken dialect at home can still be well behind in examined written Arabic. Tutoring concentrates on written register, grammar and text analysis using the texts the school has actually set. Published guidance prohibits substituting different or additional content without Ministry permission, so the material stays the school's.

faqs.question: Are Arab and non-Arab students taught Islamic education together?
faqs.answer: The published guidance for Dubai schools is explicit that they are not: schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic education and social studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Abu Dhabi schools work to the Department of Education and Knowledge's own requirements, so confirm your school's arrangement with the school. Tutoring follows whichever route your child is on, in the matching language of instruction.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is allowed to work in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time with applications through its smart app, website or e-services system. Teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen are all eligible. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts have been published officially.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre class better value than one-to-one lessons?
faqs.answer: For covering a syllabus, often yes. A group of three or four at the same stage and the same board shares the cost, and content explained once serves everyone. For fixing a specific misconception it is poor value, because the class cannot stop for twenty minutes on one student's algebra. Coursework should never be done in a group at all, since an internal assessment is individual work and similar submissions create an academic-honesty problem. A mixed approach, with a small number of targeted individual hours, usually costs less overall.

faqs.question: How much does one-to-one IGCSE tutoring cost around Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates give the range. Unitors advertises IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour; qualified subject tutors online sit roughly AED 150 to 300; specialists in IB, IGCSE or A Level run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Budget university-student tutors start nearer AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik's own figures. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for exam-year specialists. IB Gram quotes after a trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does a Core entry in Cambridge IGCSE maths limit my child's options?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the limit is administrative rather than a judgement. On most Cambridge syllabuses a Core entry caps the grade available at C or 5, and Core and Extended sit on different papers, so practice does not transfer. A student who may want a Diploma place or a British sixth form needs the Extended entry. Decide it in Year 10 on the evidence of a timed Paper 2 and Paper 4 marked against the official scheme. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge sets final entries at 27 November 2026.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher tutor them privately for extra money?
faqs.answer: It is reported that professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi bar teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. Treat that as press-reported rather than as a quotation from a current policy document, and check the Department of Education and Knowledge's own publication if the point matters. Either way the arrangement is a poor idea, because the person assessing and reporting on your child should not also be paid by you.

faqs.question: What does an inspection rating actually tell me about a school?
faqs.answer: It judges the whole school across leadership, teaching, outcomes, inclusion and governance, and it is an aggregate. A well-rated school can have a thin department in a particular year; a lower-rated one can have an excellent physics teacher. The useful part for a parent is the detail: the paragraphs on your child's phase and subject, and the comments on attainment in Arabic and Islamic education. Those are far more informative than the headline band, and reading them costs nothing.

faqs.question: Should a Baniyas student take the IB Diploma or A Levels after Year 11?
faqs.answer: They are different bets. The Diploma is six subjects with three at Higher Level plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, which suits a broadly strong and organised student with no obvious weak subject. A Level narrows to three or four and goes deeper, which suits a clear direction into engineering, medicine or economics and allows a weakness to be dropped. Since children from this district travel to school anyway, the choice is real, and it should be made on the student rather than on the commute.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write part of my child's internal assessment if we ask?
faqs.answer: No, and the request should be refused by anyone reputable. A tutor may teach the subject, explain each criterion, challenge a research question that is too broad, give feedback on a draft the student produced and teach referencing. Supplying text that reaches the submitted document is malpractice under IB rules, and so is heavy line-editing that leaves tutor-composed sentences in the final version. The student signs an authenticity declaration, similarity checks apply, and the penalty falls on the student rather than on whoever sold the words.

faqs.question: How many children in one household can you teach in the same week?
faqs.answer: As many as need it, with one qualification: each child gets their own tutor matched to their own subject and stage unless two siblings genuinely share a subject and a board, which does happen a year apart in IGCSE maths. Because nobody is driving, lessons can be stacked into consecutive hours on one or two evenings rather than scattered across five. In an apartment, the practical limit is usually the number of quiet rooms and the strength of the connection rather than tutor availability.

faqs.question: What happens if we book a term and it is not working by week four?
faqs.answer: Say so and we rematch, without a further charge for the lesson where the mismatch became clear. A tutoring arrangement that is not working by week four rarely recovers, and the usual cause is a mismatch of style or specialism rather than effort. What we will not do is offer an outcome-linked refund, because grades depend on the student's work as well as the teaching, and anyone promising money back against a grade is making a promise they cannot control.

abu-dhabi/baniyas.closingHeading: Four useful hours beat forty vague ones
abu-dhabi/baniyas.closingBody: If you are comparing IB and IGCSE tutors in Baniyas, start with two things: the marked paper that shows where the marks are going, and the honest budget. Those two facts usually produce a smaller recommendation than families expect - a diagnostic block, one subject, a defined number of hours - and a plan you can run yourself afterwards. Lessons are one-to-one over live video with no travel priced into the rate, every AED figure on this page names its source, and you are entitled to ask any tutor you pay, here or elsewhere, to show you their MoHRE permit.

intro.heading: What a parent can actually verify before paying
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in Abu Dhabi says it is good. Almost none of them will show you anything. That is the real problem behind the search for the best IB home tutor: the word best has no test attached to it, so families end up choosing on availability, on a recommendation from one parent at the school gate, or on whoever answered the phone first. Three months later the grade has not moved and there is nothing to review, because nothing was ever written down.

So this page is organised around evidence rather than adjectives. There are exactly four things a parent can check before money changes hands, and three things you can check every month afterwards. Before: where the tutor is resident and whether they hold the private tuition permit that UAE residents need; which IB components they have actually taught and supervised; what a session produces in writing; and what the diagnosis is after one free lesson. Afterwards: the annotated scripts, the shrinking error log, and the dated record of which coursework draft was discussed on which day.

The home-tutoring question deserves a straight answer rather than a deflection, because it is a reasonable thing to want. In-home one-to-one tuition in the UAE market is published at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with travel priced into the rate; a Dubai rate survey puts the usual band at AED 180 to AED 350. Abu Dhabi geography changes the maths more than the figures suggest. A tutor who finishes a lesson in Al Bateen at 5pm and needs to be in Khalifa City at 6pm is committing roughly two hours to deliver one, and the second hour appears in your invoice whether or not it is itemised.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Abu Dhabi families get one-to-one tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The case for that is not that it is cheaper, although it usually is. The case is that a driving radius selects tutors for proximity and against specialism. A family in Al Reef looking for someone who has supervised Biology internal assessments gets whoever can reach Al Reef by 5.30pm. Over video they get the person who has read a hundred of them.

What follows is the checkable version: how to test a provider's claims, what the travel arithmetic really costs in this emirate, what a marked script should look like when it comes back, what the evidence trail across DP1 and DP2 should contain, and where coursework support has to stop. No grade is promised anywhere on this page, and no IB session date is published, because the IB's own site could not be verified for this project.

In-home rates in this market carry the tutor's travel inside the hour, itemised or not.

A progress record that never says anything negative is not a progress record.
Assessed coursework stays the student's own work in full, and we put that in writing before the first draft session.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The evidence a parent should expect changes with the programme, because what the school produces changes. In the Middle Years the useful artefact is criterion marks over two terms; in the Diploma it is marked papers and dated draft records.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each MYP subject is marked against four criteria on an eight-point scale, with published descriptors. That makes the MYP the easiest stage at which to check whether tutoring is working: criterion marks across two reporting cycles show movement or its absence in a way a percentage never does. A tutor who cannot tell you which criterion your child is weakest on has not read the reports.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi MYP families often come to tutoring at the Year 11 decision point, choosing between continuing into the Diploma or moving to an A-Level route at one of the emirate's British schools. The evidence for that decision already exists in the criterion marks, and reading them properly is a better use of a first session than any aptitude conversation.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, each with external papers and an internal assessment, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The evidence trail here is dense and most families never collect it: mock scripts, internal examination marks, predicted grades, supervisor meeting records, and the dated sequence of coursework drafts. A tutor working properly adds to that trail rather than running alongside it.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma students sit the May session. This page publishes no IB session or results date, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a page like this is worse than no date. Take yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org, then plan the tuition block backwards from it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no external paper in the PYP, so the evidence is different in kind: reading levels, written explanation of a maths method, and the transdisciplinary reporting the school uses. Tutoring at this stage should produce short, specific notes rather than marks, and a parent should be able to see which skill was worked on in which week.
programmes.countryNote: Families arriving in Abu Dhabi mid-year from a British or American primary often find the PYP report format unfamiliar rather than the content hard. A session spent reading the report with a tutor who knows the framework is frequently worth more than extra maths practice, and it costs one hour.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines a career-related study with Diploma courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Evidence here centres on the reflective project, which is criterion-marked and routinely started too late. A tutor should be able to show you the project timeline and where your child sits against it.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Abu Dhabi schools offer the CP, so the honest position is that platform coverage for a specific career-related study is thin. We will say so rather than matching a tutor who has read the guide but never supervised the component.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the second half of the description is the evidence question: what a parent should be able to see in a marked script or a draft after a few weeks of work. That is the test of whether tuition in that subject is doing anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is non-calculator, and the evidence of progress is visible in the margins: method lines written out where there were none, and working that an examiner can follow to award method marks when the final answer is wrong. Ask to see two scripts a month apart and look at the margins rather than the totals.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is calculator-active and interpretation-heavy. Progress shows as a closing sentence on every answer that says what the number means in the context of the question, with units. If that sentence is still missing after a month, the tutoring is covering content instead of fixing the habit.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The internal assessment is the richest evidence source in Biology, because it is drafted over months and each draft is dated. Ask for the record of which draft was discussed and the criterion-referenced comments made on it. On papers, look for data-based answers that quote values from the figure rather than describing it loosely.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mechanism notation and full ionic equations are easy to audit on a returned script. So is data booklet use: a student who has been taught to find values quickly stops writing constants from memory. Energetics questions are where incomplete working is most visible and most expensive.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty arithmetic and significant figures are the clearest evidence markers in Physics, because they either appear in the working or they do not. Extended-response answers should show explanation chains with each link stated. Both are checkable by a parent who is not a physicist.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Evidence here is structural: a diagram drawn before the prose on every diagram question, and a closing judgement paragraph that references the stimulus material. Those two habits are visible on any marked script and they are the difference between the middle and the upper bands.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Look for annotation on the pre-released case study and for answers that apply a tool to the named organisation rather than to business in general. A tutor working on Business should be able to show you the annotated case and explain what was added to it week by week.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The evidence is the first paragraph. A guided analysis that opens with a thesis about how the text produces meaning, rather than with a summary of what it says, is the single clearest sign the work is landing. Individual oral progress shows in the narrowing of the global issue.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based answers should show provenance used as an argument rather than described. Essay answers should reach a judgement that follows from the evidence rather than arriving by assertion. Both are visible in marked scripts and both respond to drafting work faster than content revision does.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE carry Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside their licensed curriculum under the Ministry of Education's general regulations, so most Abu Dhabi students sit Arabic in some form. Progress evidence is in the productive skills: structure and register in the written task, and fluency in the recorded oral.

sections.heading: What the word best can actually be tested against
paragraphs: The best IB home tutor in Abu Dhabi, for practical purposes, is the one whose claims survive four questions. Where do you live and do you hold the private tuition permit? Which IB components have you taught and supervised, by name? What will I receive in writing after each session? And what is your diagnosis after one lesson with my child's marked work in front of you? A provider who answers all four plainly is already in a small minority in this market.

The questions are chosen because each one has a verifiable answer. Residency and permit status are facts. Component experience is specific enough that a bluff collapses: a tutor who has supervised Chemistry internal assessments can tell you what the evaluation criterion rewards without pausing. Written output either arrives or it does not. And a diagnosis after one real lesson is either specific - three named error classes with mark values - or it is a sales pitch about building confidence.

What cannot be tested is worth naming too, because knowing which claims to ignore saves time. Years of experience is unverifiable and weakly correlated with anything. Student numbers are unverifiable. Star ratings published by the provider itself are unverifiable and, in schema markup, a Google structured-data policy problem; two pages researched for this project publish different ratings in different places on the same page. A promised grade is not a claim at all, because no tutor controls an examiner.
The table below is the version to take into a phone call. The fourth column matters most: evasion in this market has a consistent shape, and recognising it is quicker than evaluating the claim.
bullets: Four questions: residency and permit, named components, written output, diagnosis after one lesson.

sections.heading: The travel arithmetic: what an in-home hour really costs in this emirate
paragraphs: In-home tuition in the UAE market is published at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. A Dubai rate survey from 2026 puts the common band at AED 180 to AED 350, and individual home tutors are quoted up to AED 500. Those numbers are not inflated. They are what it costs to buy a professional's time plus the journey attached to it, and the journey is the part Abu Dhabi families underestimate.

Think about an evening rather than an hour. A tutor delivering one-to-one lessons by car in this emirate can realistically do two sessions on a weekday evening, sometimes three if the households are close together. That caps their earnings for the evening, which is why the hourly rate has to carry the travel. It also explains the pattern families notice and cannot account for: that the same tutor quotes differently for Al Mushrif and for Al Reef, and that nobody good is available at 6pm in the outer communities.

The second-order effect is the one that actually matters for a Diploma student. A driving radius is a filter on who your child can work with, and it filters for the wrong variable. A family in Hydra Village wanting a Physics HL tutor who understands uncertainty treatment is not choosing between specialists; they are choosing between the two or three people who will make that drive. Subject match loses to geography every time, and the grade consequence of that is larger than the rate difference.

sections.heading: What a properly marked script looks like when it comes back
paragraphs: Most families have never seen a script marked the way an examiner marks one, which is why a grade with a tick and a well done feels like feedback. It is not. A marked script should show where each mark was awarded and where one was available and missed, in the language of the markscheme, so the student can see the gap rather than being told about it.

Four things should be visible even to a parent who does not know the subject. Marks should be allocated question by question, not as a single total. There should be annotation at the point of loss, not only at the end. The annotation should use the command term and the criterion language, saying that an explanation stopped after one link rather than saying more detail needed. And there should be one summary line that names the error class, so the same comment is not written again next month.

What should not be there is a rewritten answer in the tutor's handwriting. A model answer supplied after the student has attempted the question is a teaching tool and is fine. An answer written over the student's own is not marking; it replaces the thinking that was supposed to happen, and on coursework it crosses into territory the IB treats as misconduct.

Ask any provider for one marked script from a previous student with the identifying details removed, before you commit to a block. A provider who marks properly will send one without hesitation, because it is their strongest asset. A provider who has never marked anything will explain why they cannot.

sections.heading: The error log, and what the monthly record should say
paragraphs: Progress in tutoring is not a feeling and it is not a grade; grades move slowly and for several reasons at once. The usable unit is the error log: a written list of the specific habits costing marks, ranked by mark value, with each item marked retired when two consecutive pieces of work show it has gone. A log that shrinks is progress. A log that keeps acquiring new items every week means the diagnosis was never made properly.

The log also disciplines the tutor. It is uncomfortable to write down, four weeks in, that the second item on the list has not moved, which is exactly why it is useful. The monthly note should contain at least one sentence of that kind. A record in which everything is always going well is a marketing document, and families who have been through two providers recognise it immediately.

There is a scheduling benefit as well. When the log is explicit, the number of sessions needed becomes an estimate rather than a subscription. Two high-value habits can usually be moved inside six to eight weeks of weekly work with practice in between. A list of twelve small irritations cannot be moved at all, and the honest response to one is to re-diagnose rather than to sell a longer block.

sections.heading: The coursework paper trail, and the line nobody should cross
paragraphs: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are assessed as the student's own work, and a breach is an academic-misconduct matter that falls on the student rather than on whoever sold the help. This is the worst-behaved corner of this market: one page researched for this project advertises finished internal assessments at a fixed price. A family buying that is buying a risk attached to their child's candidature.

The boundary is clear enough to put in writing, and we do, before any coursework session. A tutor may teach the method, explain the assessment criteria, ask the questions an examiner would ask, mark a draft against the descriptors, point at reasoning that does not follow, and show a published exemplar. A tutor may not supply text, rework a passage into its final form, invent or adjust data, or decide the research question. The student makes every change.

The paper trail is what protects everybody. Each session on a draft is logged with the date and the version discussed, and the comments are criterion-referenced rather than editorial. If a question is ever raised at school, that record shows a sequence of the student's own drafts improving against published criteria, which is what honest supervision looks like. A single polished document appearing from nowhere is the opposite.

One more point on materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, markschemes and grade boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them and link to the official sites. We do not host them, supply them as files, or reproduce them here.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor is permitted to teach in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: The UAE regulates private tutoring by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page for it states a completion time of two working days and an application route through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published anywhere official, so no figure appears on this page.

Abu Dhabi adds a specific restriction that every parent in this emirate should know. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same arrangement. Treat both as press-reported rather than as the authority's exact wording, and check the current policy document if the decision turns on it. The practical advice does not depend on the wording: a paid private arrangement with your child's own classroom teacher is the one to avoid.

A business with premises and staff is regulated differently again. In Dubai that is a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute; in Abu Dhabi the equivalent approval sits with ADEK. IB Gram is an online tutor-matching platform. It holds no ADEK licence, no KHDA permit, no accreditation from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no office in the UAE. Two pages ranking for these searches imply one or more of those things, and a third routes UAE parents to an Indian mobile number while showing a Dubai address.

So the verification step for a parent is short. Ask where the tutor is resident. If they are in the UAE, ask for the permit number. If they are not, ask which qualification they hold and which syllabus they have taught, because no UAE permit applies to a non-resident teaching online. We answer both questions before a match is confirmed.

sections.heading: Month by month: what evidence should exist across DP1 and DP2
paragraphs: Across a two-year Diploma, the school generates a predictable sequence of evidence and most families only look at two points in it: the end-of-year report and the predicted grades. Reading the whole sequence is what lets you intervene while intervening is still cheap. A student whose internal assessment research question is still unsettled at the end of DP1 has a problem that costs one session in June and five in January.

The table sets out the sequence in programme terms rather than calendar dates. Specific dates vary by school, and IB session dates must come from your school's coordinator or ibo.org; this project could not verify any IB date from the IB itself, so none is stated. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own timetables, and those are worth linking for any student also carrying an IGCSE or A-Level subject: Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE series ran to 19 November 2026, and Cambridge's March 2027 series closes final entries on 27 November 2026.

Two columns are there for a reason. What the school produces is not negotiable and arrives whether you ask or not. What a tutor should produce in the same window is negotiable, and most providers produce nothing in several of these rows. The last column is what to ask for, phrased as the request rather than the principle.

Used properly this is also a budgeting tool. Tuition concentrated in the two windows where evidence is thinnest - the DP1 summer and the DP2 mock aftermath - does more per dirham than the same hours spread evenly across two years.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home tutor in Abu Dhabi, compared properly
paragraphs: A fair comparison states what each option genuinely does better. An in-home tutor is physically present, which matters for a young child, for a student who will not sit down without someone in the room, and for anything involving physical apparatus. Online one-to-one gives you a specialist chosen for the component rather than the postcode, a shared screen that beats two people leaning over one page, session recordings, and no travel inside the rate. Group classes at a centre are cheaper per hour and better for a student who needs external structure.

For a Diploma student the decisive factor is usually match quality. The components that cost the most marks - internal assessment supervision, extended response structure, uncertainty treatment, criterion-referenced drafting - need someone who has done that specific thing many times. The number of such people inside a 20-minute drive of Al Reef at 6pm on a Tuesday is small. The number reachable over video is not limited by the bridge.

Rates in the table are market figures from providers' published pages in October 2026 and from a published Dubai rate survey, with the source stated. They are not IB Gram's price list. Our own answer to the price question starts with the free trial lesson and a session count attached to the error log.

The honest summary: IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so if physical presence is the requirement, this is not the right platform and we will say so on the first call rather than after the trial.

sections.heading: When a home tutor is genuinely the right answer
paragraphs: There are cases where the honest recommendation is an in-home tutor, and we make it. A seven-year-old who needs someone sitting beside them to stay on task is one. A student with a specific access requirement that makes a screen difficult is another. A household with genuinely unreliable connectivity is a third, although that is rarer in Abu Dhabi than people expect. In each of those cases online delivery is a compromise rather than an improvement, and pretending otherwise would waste a term.

What we would still suggest in those cases is to apply the same four questions to whoever you hire locally: residency and permit, named components, written output per session, and a specific diagnosis after one lesson. The questions are not about us. They are the ones that separate a professional from an available person, and they work equally well on a tutor who arrives by car.

For most Diploma and Middle Years students in this emirate, though, the physical-presence requirement is not real and the specialist-match requirement is. That is the trade this page is arguing: the value of the right person on the right component, every week, with written evidence, against the value of someone being in the room. For a sixteen-year-old working on the evaluation criterion of a Biology internal assessment, the first one wins by a distance.

If you want to test it cheaply, the trial lesson exists for exactly that. One free 45-minute session with your child's marked work on screen, no card details, and a specific diagnosis at the end. If the diagnosis is thin, you have lost nothing and learned something about how to interview the next provider.

process.title: Send the most recent marked work
process.description: A mock script, a timed essay, or an internal assessment draft with the teacher's comments on it. One real piece of marked work tells a tutor more than a long phone call about the term. If you have a report with criterion marks across two cycles, send that as well; it is the fastest read available.

process.title: A free 45-minute diagnostic lesson
process.description: A working session rather than a sales call. The tutor marks part of the work with your child, names the error classes they can see, and tests one live. No charge and no card details. If the honest diagnosis is that your child needs teaching rather than technique work, or a different subject entirely, we say so.

process.title: The written error log and a fixed session count
process.description: You receive the error classes ranked by mark value, with a proposed number of sessions attached and an end date. The count is agreed before anything starts. A short log means a short block; we would rather run six useful sessions than sell a subscription that nobody reviews.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marking in between
process.description: The tutor marks the week's work before the session, so the hour is spent on the gap rather than on reading. The annotated script comes back within a day, the log is updated, and every session opens by checking what happened to last week's item. That is how items get retired instead of repeated.

process.title: A monthly note and an end-of-block handover
process.description: Once a month you get a written note that says what moved, what did not, and what is next. At the end of the block your child sits a full paper under exam conditions, marked to the published criteria, and the handover records what is still weak. If a second block is not needed, the handover says that.

whyPoints.title: Everything is written down
whyPoints.description: Annotated scripts, a ranked error log, dated coursework draft records and a monthly note. You can audit whether the log is shrinking without knowing the subject. Progress that exists only in a tutor's description of it is indistinguishable from no progress at all.

whyPoints.title: The match is made on the component, not the drive
whyPoints.description: Because sessions run over live video, the question is which part of the assessment your child is losing marks in. A family in Hydra Village and a family in Al Bateen get the same tutor pool, which is not true of any in-home arrangement in this emirate.

whyPoints.title: We tell you where the tutor lives
whyPoints.description: Residency and permit status are stated before a match is confirmed. UAE-based tutors are asked for their MoHRE private tuition permit number. Where a tutor is outside the UAE we say so, because no UAE permit applies to a non-resident and you should know which it is.

whyPoints.title: Marking happens before the session
whyPoints.description: The work is marked against the published criteria before the hour starts, so the lesson is spent on the gap rather than on reading the script together. Most families have never been offered this, and it is the single biggest difference in what an hour produces.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line on coursework is in writing
whyPoints.description: Before any work on an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, both the student and you receive the boundary in writing: what a tutor may question and mark, and what the student must do alone. Nobody on the platform supplies text for assessed work.

whyPoints.title: We say no to the wrong purchase
whyPoints.description: If one free lesson shows a syllabus gap rather than a technique problem, we recommend teaching instead. If no tutor on the platform covers your child's subject at the level needed, we say that rather than matching somebody approximate and hoping.

faqs.question: How do I check that a home tutor in Abu Dhabi is really qualified for the IB?
faqs.answer: Ask about components rather than credentials. A tutor who has genuinely worked on Biology HL can tell you what the evaluation criterion of the internal assessment rewards, without pausing, and can name where students lose marks on Paper 2. That question cannot be bluffed. Then ask for one marked script from a previous student with the identifying details removed. A tutor who marks properly sends one immediately, because it is their strongest asset. Years of experience, student counts and self-published star ratings cannot be checked at all, so they tell you nothing useful about the person who will teach your child.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor in Abu Dhabi charge once travel is counted?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates in the UAE market run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, and a 2026 Dubai rate survey puts the usual band at AED 180 to AED 350. Travel sits inside those figures whether or not the invoice itemises it. The reason is arithmetic: a tutor driving between households can deliver two lessons on a weekday evening, sometimes three, so the hourly rate has to cover the journeys. That is why the same tutor quotes differently for Al Mushrif and for Al Reef, and why nobody with a specialism is free at 6pm in the outer communities.

faqs.question: Will anyone actually come to our address in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Abu Dhabi families get one-to-one tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's work marked before each session and the annotated script returned afterwards. If physical presence in the room is the requirement - a young child who will not sit still, or a specific access need - we will tell you on the first call that this is not the right platform, rather than letting you discover it after a trial lesson.

faqs.question: What should a marked script actually look like when it comes back?
faqs.answer: Marks allocated question by question rather than as one total. Annotation at the point where a mark was lost, not only at the end. Comments in the language of the markscheme or the criteria, saying that an explanation stopped after one link rather than writing more detail needed. And one summary line naming the error class, so the same comment is not written again next month. What should not be there is the answer rewritten in the tutor's hand over the student's own, which replaces the thinking that was meant to happen.

faqs.question: How quickly should I expect the grade to move?
faqs.answer: Grades move slowly and for several reasons at once, so they are a poor weekly measure. The usable measure is the error log: the specific habits costing marks, ranked by value, each marked retired when two consecutive pieces of work show it has gone. Two high-value habits can usually be shifted inside six to eight weeks of weekly work with practice in between. A grade band shift often shows at the next set of internal examinations rather than immediately. A provider who promises a particular grade is describing something no tutor controls, because examiners do.

faqs.question: What progress record do parents receive each month?
faqs.answer: A short written note with three parts: what moved, what did not, and what is next. The second part is the one that matters, because it is uncomfortable to write and therefore informative. A record in which everything is always going well is a marketing document. Alongside the monthly note you receive the annotated scripts from each session, the current error log with retired items marked, and for coursework a dated record of which draft was discussed on which day. You should be able to audit the log without knowing the subject.

faqs.question: How do I verify that a tutor holds the UAE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask for the permit and the number. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years; MoHRE's service page states a two-working-day completion time and an application route through its app, website and e-services. Eligible categories include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. People tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so ignore any figure you see quoted.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell me which Internal Assessments they have supervised?
faqs.answer: A real one can, by subject and level, and will usually volunteer what goes wrong most often in that component. That specificity is the test. Supervision experience matters more than teaching experience for the internal assessment, because the work is criterion-marked and the criteria reward things that are not obvious: feasibility of the research question, the quality of the evaluation, and whether the method description is proportionate. A tutor who talks about internal assessments in general terms, without naming criteria or typical failures, has probably read the guide rather than marked the work.

faqs.question: What evidence should I ask for before paying for a block of sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things, all of which exist before any money moves. A specific diagnosis after one free lesson, with named error classes and rough mark values attached. A sample marked script from a previous student with the details removed. A statement of where the tutor is resident and whether they hold the private tuition permit. And a proposed session count with an end date, rather than an open arrangement. If any of the four produces a vague answer, that is the answer. Providers who have the evidence produce it quickly, because it is what distinguishes them.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives nearby better than one who knows the subject?
faqs.answer: For a young child, often yes. For a Diploma student, almost never. The components that cost the most marks need someone who has done that specific thing repeatedly: supervised internal assessments in the subject, marked extended responses, handled uncertainty treatment in the sciences. The number of such people within a 20-minute drive of Al Reef at 6pm is small, and the family ends up choosing from whoever makes the journey rather than from specialists. Over video the postcode stops being a filter, and a household in Hydra Village gets the same pool as one in Al Bateen.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on my child's Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary we state in writing before the first session. A tutor may question the research question, explain the assessment criteria, mark a draft against the descriptors, point at reasoning that does not follow, ask the questions an examiner would ask, and show a published exemplar. A tutor may not supply text, rework a passage into its final form, or decide the argument. The student makes every change and the school supervisor remains the authority on the task. The test we apply is whether your child could explain, in a viva, why each sentence is in the essay.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor is not the right match?
faqs.answer: Tell us after the first or second session and we move your child, with the error log and the marked scripts transferring across so nothing restarts from zero. Mismatches usually show early and usually are not about competence: a student who needs to be interrupted and questioned does badly with a patient explainer, and the reverse is equally true. The written record is what makes a change cheap rather than wasteful. A provider who treats a requested change as a complaint rather than as information is telling you something about how they operate.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi schools do the students you support attend?
faqs.answer: Students we support attend schools across the emirate, concentrated in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, on Saadiyat and Yas Island, and in the older island communities around Al Bateen and Al Mushrif. We name schools on this page only as market context. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership, client relationship or endorsement from any school, school group or education authority in the UAE, and we do not publish a list of schools as though it implied one. If a provider shows you a wall of school logos, ask what the relationship actually is.

faqs.question: Can you tutor two children in the same household at different levels?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is common in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, where one household often has a Diploma candidate and a Middle Years student on different assessment calendars. They get separate tutors matched to subject and level, separate error logs and separate monthly notes, in back-to-back evening slots. Nothing is shared except the household calendar, and either slot can be paused without affecting the other. Trying to cover two children with one tutor in one session saves money on paper and reliably produces two half-sessions.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson include, and what is the condition attached?
faqs.answer: One 45-minute one-to-one session over live video, with your child's own marked work on screen. The tutor marks part of it, names the error classes, and tests one live. The condition is simply that it is one session per student, booked in a slot we both agree, and that you send the marked work beforehand so the time is not spent reading. No card details are taken and there is no obligation to continue. If the diagnosis at the end is vague, you have lost nothing and gained a way to interview the next provider.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are comparing providers, the cheapest useful step is to ask each one the same four questions: where the tutor is resident and whether they hold the private tuition permit, which IB components they have taught and supervised by name, what arrives in writing after each session, and what their diagnosis is after one lesson with your child's marked work in front of them. Ours is a free 45-minute session with no card details. You will leave it with a ranked error log and a proposed session count. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the tutor is chosen for the component rather than for a driving radius across Abu Dhabi.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below cover IB Diploma and IGCSE subjects for Abu Dhabi families. Rates differ by programme, level and component rather than by tutor charisma, and the trial lesson is where you find out which band your child's actual need sits in.

intro.heading: Two boards, two price bands, one household budget
paragraphs: The word best does nothing to a quote on its own, but it does a great deal to the spread of quotes you receive. Ring five providers in Abu Dhabi about Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level and the numbers will land somewhere between AED 150 and AED 650 an hour. Ring the same five about Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry and the same numbers drop by roughly a third. Nobody explains the gap, because explaining the gap means explaining what the higher-priced hour is actually for.

That gap is real and it is published. A UAE agency rate card read in October 2026 lists IGCSE tuition starting at AED 150 an hour and IB tuition starting at AED 200, from the same provider, with the same tutor pool description. Other providers show the same shape at different altitudes: budget online tutoring advertised from AED 45 to AED 65, mid-market qualified subject tutors between AED 150 and AED 300, specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level work at AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, and a premium tier advertised at AED 650. Those are market figures, not ours.

What sits behind the gap is component load. An IGCSE subject is two or three written papers and, in the sciences, a practical or alternative-to-practical paper. A Diploma subject is two or three papers plus an internally assessed component marked against published criteria, inside a package that also carries Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. A tutor working on a Diploma subject has to know the criteria wording, the moderation process and the school's internal deadline calendar as well as the content. That is more knowledge for the same hour, and the market prices it.

The second thing nobody prices properly for Abu Dhabi families is the household rather than the child. A large share of the enquiries we receive from the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor involve two children in two programmes, often at two schools with two assessment calendars. One is sitting Cambridge or Edexcel papers in May and June. The other is eighteen months from a Diploma session with an Internal Assessment deadline in between. The weekly bill is not one rate times one hour; it is a shifting allocation across a year, and it peaks in predictable months.

So this page is a pricing page written honestly. It gives the market bands with their sources, prices the two-board household across a year, costs the crossover months when a child moves from Year 11 into DP1, and sets out the six local variables that move a quote in Abu Dhabi specifically. It does not publish an IB Gram rate card, because the right number depends on subject, level, component and how many weeks remain, and it is settled after a free trial lesson rather than before one.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Each programme carries a different cost profile, and the difference is structural rather than reputational. What follows is what each programme obliges a tutor to know, because that is what sets the band the market charges for it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, assessed by written papers with a practical or alternative-to-practical component in the sciences. Tiering is the cost-relevant feature: Cambridge splits Core and Extended, Edexcel splits Foundation and Higher, and the tier a school has entered a child for changes both the ceiling and the amount of work a tutor has to do.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the IGCSE load is where the household bill is widest rather than deepest. A Year 11 student carrying nine subjects cannot have a tutor for nine subjects at any sensible price, so the real decision is which two or three subjects earn the spend. Market rates for qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, so three subjects at one hour a week is a materially different commitment from one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject has an internally assessed component with its own criteria and its own school deadline, and all of it lands inside two years with one external session at the end.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma tutoring in Abu Dhabi commands the higher band for a reason that is visible on an invoice: the internal components create work in months when no exam is near. A family who budgets only for exam-season support discovers in DP1 that the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay drafts need supervision in the autumn, which is why Diploma spending is better planned across four blocks than across one.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria scored one to eight. There is no external examination in most MYP years, which makes the cost of support lower and the temptation to skip it higher.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest intervention available to an Abu Dhabi family is usually MYP support in Year 9 or 10, because it is bought at mid-market rates and it reduces the amount of expensive Diploma-rate remediation needed later. Families who leave the gap until DP1 pay the higher band to fix something that cost less to prevent.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with portfolio-based reporting and no external examinations. Support is light, short and usually about reading fluency or number sense rather than subject content.
programmes.countryNote: Primary support sits in the lowest market band and should stay there. A family in Abu Dhabi paying specialist Diploma rates for Year 4 numeracy is paying for knowledge the hour does not require, and we would say so rather than take the booking at the higher figure.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subject by subject, the cost question is the same: how many components does the tutor have to hold, and how scarce is somebody who holds them. These notes are written from that angle rather than from a syllabus summary.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: The widest IB-to-IGCSE price gap of any science, because the Diploma version adds an internally assessed investigation with its own criteria. IGCSE Chemistry sits comfortably in the mid band; Higher Level Chemistry with Internal Assessment supervision sits in the specialist band in every rate card we could source.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is among the scarcest specialisms in the emirate, and scarcity is a price driver in its own right. The non-calculator paper and the proof-style questions are what the higher band is paying for, and a generalist maths tutor at a lower rate rarely teaches either.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The most competitively supplied subject in Abu Dhabi and therefore the one where the lower bands are genuinely usable. Confirm the tier first: paying Extended rates for a Core entry is the commonest overspend we see, and it buys content the paper will never ask for.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: IGCSE Physics is mid band and plentiful. Diploma Physics is thinner on the ground locally, and the internally assessed investigation plus the uncertainty and data-analysis questions push it into the specialist band. Those two areas are also where the hour pays for itself fastest.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Content-heavy and well supplied at IGCSE, so there is little reason to pay above mid band. At Higher Level the cost driver is the volume of material plus the investigation, and a cheaper tutor who has never supervised the internal component is a false economy in DP1.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diploma Economics carries a portfolio of commentaries, which is work in months with no exam in them. That is precisely the component families forget to budget for, and it is why Economics quotes in the specialist band often look high next to the IGCSE equivalent.

subjects.name: Business Management and Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application is teachable in a small number of sessions, which makes this one of the better value subjects to buy help in. The Diploma version adds an internally assessed research project, and that is the part worth paying a specialist rate for.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0500 and 0475
subjects.description: Supply is good at both levels in Abu Dhabi, so mid band is realistic. The cost efficiency here depends on marked drafts rather than lesson count: four marked essays with written feedback usually move more marks than eight discussion sessions at the same total price.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0478 and 0417
subjects.description: Scarce emirate-wide at both levels, and scarcity is the whole reason quotes come back high. The Diploma internal solution carries most of the risk, and a tutor who has supervised one before is worth the difference between the mid and specialist bands.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies alongside the main curriculum
subjects.description: Mandatory UAE subjects run alongside the international curriculum, and their tutoring is usually bought separately and at lower rates. Note that for British-track Ministry of Education equivalency, Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the five required IGCSE subjects, which changes how a family prioritises spend.

regions.note: Established island districts where several long-standing schools create steady demand for Sixth Form and Diploma support. Demand without matching specialist supply is the condition under which quotes drift upwards.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Format changes the number more than almost anything else, and the three formats available to an Abu Dhabi family are priced differently for reasons worth seeing laid out.

modes.description: A live video session with one tutor and one student, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. sections.heading: Why a Diploma hour is priced above an IGCSE hour
paragraphs: Start with the thing being bought. An IGCSE subject asks a tutor to know two or three written papers, the tiering, the command-term conventions and where marks are routinely lost. That is a bounded body of knowledge and a competent subject teacher holds it. A Diploma subject asks for all of that plus an internally assessed component with published criteria, a moderation process, a school-set internal deadline sequence, and in several subjects a prescribed list or a data-handling convention on top.

The market has priced that difference without explaining it. One UAE agency's published rate card, read in October 2026, starts IGCSE tuition at AED 150 an hour and IB tuition at AED 200 from the same pool, a gap of about a third. Across the wider market the pattern repeats at different altitudes: budget online tutoring advertised from around AED 45 to AED 65, qualified online subject tutors between AED 150 and AED 300, specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level work between AED 200 and AED 450 or more, and a premium tier advertised at AED 650. Each of those figures is a provider's own published number rather than a price of ours.

The gap is defensible where the extra knowledge is actually required and indefensible where it is not. A Standard Level Diploma subject with the internal component already submitted is, for the remaining weeks, a written-paper job that looks a great deal like an IGCSE job. Paying the Diploma premium for those weeks buys nothing. Equally, an IGCSE science student whose practical paper technique has never been taught may need a more expensive specialist than their classmate who only needs content revision.

The practical test is to ask what the hour has to hold. If the answer includes a criterion-referenced component, a moderation deadline or a school supervisor's process, the higher band is doing work. If it does not, the quote should come down, and a provider who cannot articulate which of those applies to your child is quoting on programme name rather than on need.
