sections.heading: The two-board household, costed across one academic year
paragraphs: A single-child budget is arithmetic. A two-child, two-board budget is scheduling. The reason Abu Dhabi families in the eastern corridor so often describe tutoring as more expensive than they expected is not that the hourly rates were wrong; it is that the two children's demands peak in overlapping months and nobody mapped it in September.

Here is the shape. An IGCSE candidate's demand is flat until January and then climbs steeply towards a May or June series, with mock season in January or February acting as the first real spike. A Diploma student's demand is the opposite: heavy in the autumn when the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay drafts are live, lighter mid-year, then heavy again before the May session. Overlay the two and you get two expensive windows, autumn and the February to April run, with a cheap stretch between them that families routinely overspend in because nothing feels urgent.

The money-saving moves all come from that map rather than from negotiating the rate. Buy the Diploma internal-component supervision in the autumn when it is genuinely needed and the slot is easy to get. Keep the IGCSE child on light maintenance until mocks, then concentrate the spend from January. Do not run both children at two hours a week all year; it costs more and produces less than a concentrated allocation. And decide in advance which subjects earn the money, because nine IGCSE subjects cannot all be tutored at any sensible figure.

sections.heading: The crossover: Year 11 into DP1, when you pay for both at once
paragraphs: The most expensive months in a UAE family's tutoring life are the six that straddle the end of IGCSE and the start of the Diploma for the same child. For a short period you are paying IGCSE rates to finish one qualification and Diploma rates to start another, and most families discover it after it has started rather than before.

What makes the crossover costly is not duplication but mismatch. An IGCSE finish is about recovering marks on known papers, which is efficient work with a visible return. A DP1 start is about learning a new assessment language: criteria rather than mark schemes, an internally assessed component rather than coursework, command terms that overlap with IGCSE ones but mean something slightly different. Those are different tutors, usually, and the second one is in the higher band.

The good news is that the crossover is short and can be sequenced. The IGCSE work should be finished and stopped, not tapered into the summer. The Diploma work should start in the summer or early autumn with subject-choice and transition support rather than in October with remediation, because transition support is bought at a lower intensity than catch-up. Families who do it the other way round pay the specialist band for longer and start DP1 already behind.

Note the two months where the right answer is nothing: the gap after the series and the first weeks of DP1, where a student should be allowed to find out what they can do unaided before anybody is paid to help.

sections.heading: Six things that move a quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Hourly rates in Abu Dhabi are not a single number with noise around it. They are a base figure moved by six identifiable variables, and a parent who knows the six can tell a justified quote from an opportunistic one in a single phone call. None of the six is about how good the tutor is, which is a separate question answered in a trial lesson rather than on a price list.

Level and component come first, as the previous section set out. Urgency comes second and moves the number more than most families expect: a request for a specialist four weeks before a series is a scarcity purchase, and scarcity is priced. Format comes third, with in-home visits carrying travel inside the rate and group classes quoted per student. Frequency comes fourth, since blocks and retainers usually carry a lower effective rate than ad-hoc single sessions.

Fifth is scarcity of the specific specialism, which in Abu Dhabi is sharper than in Dubai because the Diploma cohort is smaller and more concentrated. Higher Level Computer Science, Higher Level Economics and the Analysis and Approaches non-calculator paper are all thin locally, and anything thin locally is quoted high locally. Online matching is the direct answer to that one, because it removes the local scarcity without removing the specialism.

Sixth, and least discussed, is what the quote excludes. Marking, written feedback, Internal Assessment review, report writing and rescheduling are sometimes inside the rate and sometimes extra. A lower headline figure with marking charged separately can be the more expensive arrangement, and the only way to know is to ask what the hour includes before agreeing it. That belongs in writing, which is the subject of a later section.

sections.heading: Value per recovered mark, not value per hour
paragraphs: Comparing tutors on hourly rate is comparing them on the wrong unit. The unit that matters is marks recovered per AED spent, and although nobody can publish a table of that honestly, a family can reason about it well enough to make better decisions than a price comparison allows.

Work backwards from the paper. Every component has a mark allocation, and in every subject there are categories of loss that are cheap to fix and categories that are expensive. Method not written down is cheap: a handful of sessions, mostly habit. Command-term mismatch is cheap: a drilling job with a visible before and after on marked work. A topic never taught is expensive, because it needs teaching rather than correcting. Two years of missing algebraic fluency is the most expensive thing on the list, because it underlies everything else.

That ordering is what should drive the spend, and it frequently inverts a family's instinct. The subject the child hates most is not necessarily the subject where the money works hardest. A student losing twelve marks a paper to presentation habits across three subjects will get more from four sessions on presentation than from twelve sessions on their least favourite topic. This is also why the diagnostic hour is worth paying for before the plan is set, and why a provider who sells a package before reading any marked work is selling hours rather than outcomes.

One caution. This reasoning is a method for allocating a budget, not a promise about results. No tutor can promise a grade or a mark gain, and any provider attaching a specific number of marks to a specific number of hours is making a sales claim. The honest version is that some categories of loss reliably respond faster than others, and that spending in the fast categories first is better value than spending evenly.

sections.heading: Billing structures, compared on what they actually cost
paragraphs: Four billing shapes circulate in the UAE tutoring market, and the headline rate is a poor guide to which is cheapest for your situation. Per-session billing carries the highest effective rate and the most flexibility. Blocks of eight or ten sessions reduce the effective rate and introduce expiry risk. Monthly retainers advertise well, with online packages seen around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home packages around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, and they are good value only if the sessions are genuinely used.

The fourth shape is the component or project fee, used for Internal Assessment and Extended Essay supervision and quoted as a block rather than by the hour. It is the structure most likely to be misunderstood, because the deliverable is feedback across a draft sequence over several weeks rather than a fixed number of sessions. Ask how many review rounds the fee covers, what the turnaround on written feedback is, and what happens if the school moves the internal deadline, which schools do.

Expiry and rollover are where blocks and retainers quietly cost money. A ten-session block bought in January for a May series is fine. The same block bought in September with a three-month expiry, in a household with a Ramadan period and a half-term inside it, is not. Ask for the expiry in writing, ask whether unused sessions roll over, and ask what happens to the block if you change tutor midway, which is a normal thing to do.

Our own position is deliberately plain: no rate is quoted before a free trial lesson, because the right band depends on subject, level, component and weeks remaining, and quoting first means quoting on the programme name. The trial lesson carries no charge, takes no card details and carries no obligation to continue. After it you receive the diagnostic note and a plan with the hours and the band attached, and you decide.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, entries and what else is already being paid
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the only education line in an Abu Dhabi household budget, and a figure that looks large in isolation sometimes looks different beside the rest. Private school fees across the UAE sit well above any plausible annual tutoring spend for one or two subjects, and examination entry costs land separately again, particularly for a private candidate entering outside a school.

The regulatory context differs by emirate and is worth knowing. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package the authority valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a Dubai measure rather than an Abu Dhabi one, and Abu Dhabi fee adjustments run through ADEK's own process, so do not read the Dubai freeze as applying to a school in Khalifa City.

Examination entries matter for one specific group: students sitting as private candidates, often because they are retaking a paper or taking a subject their school does not offer. Entry fees are set by the centre rather than by the board, deadlines sit months before the exam, and the Cambridge March 2027 series is the clearest worked example available: final entries were due 27 November 2026 for an examination period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. A family budgeting only for tuition can miss an entry deadline that costs far more to fix.

The honest framing for all of this is that tutoring is a discretionary line with a controllable size, sitting next to two lines that are not discretionary. That argues for concentrating the spend where it works rather than spreading it thinly across a year, which is the recommendation this whole page keeps arriving at from different directions.

sections.heading: What to agree in writing, and how to check the tutor may teach at all
paragraphs: Before a first invoice, six things belong in writing: the hourly or block figure, exactly what the rate includes, the cancellation and rescheduling terms, the expiry and rollover position on any block, the replacement process if the pairing does not work, and the academic-honesty boundary on any internally assessed work. None of those is unreasonable to ask for, and a provider who will not put them in a message is telling you how the relationship will run.

On the legal side, private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Government guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. MoHRE's own service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are described in that guidance as subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no figure appears here. For Abu Dhabi specifically, UAE press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes a prohibition on school staff providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school; treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document before relying on it. The practical consequence is that your child's own teacher is not the person to pay.

Two claims should end a pricing conversation. The first is any form of grade guarantee, including a refund tied to a result, because no tutor can guarantee an outcome and the promise is a sales device. The second is any claim of approval, accreditation or licensing by KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. IB Gram holds none of those, operates no premises in the UAE, and says so. A provider claiming otherwise should be asked for the permit number, and the number should be checkable.

Ask for the permit position of the individual who will actually teach

sections.heading: The point at which paying more stops buying more
paragraphs: There is a ceiling, and it arrives earlier than the premium tier would like you to believe. Above roughly the specialist band, the extra AED buys scarcity, reputation and convenience rather than additional component knowledge. A tutor at the top of the market and a strong specialist in the middle of it know the same criteria, the same papers and the same loss patterns. The difference is availability and a brand.

There are narrow cases where the premium is doing real work. A genuinely rare subject at Higher Level with four weeks to a session is one: you are paying for someone existing and being free, which is a legitimate thing to pay for. A student with a specific profile needing a particular kind of teacher is another. What does not justify it is a general wish for the strongest possible tutor, because strongest is not a property a price list can convey.

The other ceiling is on hours rather than rates, and it is harder for families to accept. Beyond about two subject hours a week per child, returns fall off quickly, because the limiting factor stops being teaching and becomes independent practice, sleep and school attention. A student in Al Reef who leaves home before seven does not have four productive tutoring hours a week in them, whatever the household can afford. Concentrated blocks at the right moment outperform a permanently heavy weekly load.

So the answer to the question behind the search is not a number. The strongest arrangement an Abu Dhabi family can buy is a specialist in the mid-to-specialist band, matched to the exact syllabus and level, with marking and written feedback inside the rate, bought in concentrated windows rather than spread flat across a year, and reviewed on marked evidence every few weeks. That is both cheaper and better than the premium tier bought continuously, and it is what we would recommend even where it means fewer hours billed.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, the level and the deadline
process.description: Cambridge or Edexcel with the code, or the Diploma subject with its level, plus the date of the next thing that matters: a mock, an internal deadline or the series. Those three facts determine which band the work sits in, and they are what stop a quote from being guesswork attached to a programme name.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson before any figure is agreed
process.description: A full-length working session with the matched tutor at no charge, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. We quote after it rather than before, because the right band depends on what the marked work shows rather than on which programme your child is enrolled in.

process.title: Read the plan with the hours and the band attached
process.description: After the trial you receive a diagnostic note and a plan that names the loss categories, the hours proposed, the window they sit in and the band. If the plan proposes more hours than the diagnosis supports, say so. We would rather argue about it at this stage than invoice for it.

process.title: Agree the inclusions in writing
process.description: The figure, what the rate includes, whether marking and written feedback are inside it, the rescheduling terms, and the academic-honesty boundary on any internally assessed component. One message covering those six points prevents almost every billing dispute we have ever seen in this market.

process.title: Concentrate the spend, then review on evidence
process.description: Run the hours in the window where they work rather than flat across the year, and review every three or four weeks against marked papers. If the loss categories have cleared, taper or stop. If one has not moved, change the focus or the tutor rather than adding hours at the same rate.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure is attributed
whyPoints.description: Each band on this page is a published market rate with its source and date named, not a price of ours and not an estimate dressed as data. Three of the six ranking pages we audited in October 2026 published no price at all, and the two that did quoted US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: No rate quoted before a trial lesson
whyPoints.description: The right band depends on subject, level, component and weeks remaining. Quoting before anyone has seen marked work means quoting on the programme name, which is how a Standard Level paper-only job ends up billed at Higher Level supervision rates.

whyPoints.title: Marking and written feedback inside the rate
whyPoints.description: A lower headline figure with marking charged separately is frequently the more expensive arrangement. Our sessions include the marked work and the written note, because the marking is where most of the value sits and separating it out makes the comparison dishonest.

whyPoints.title: We will argue you down on hours
whyPoints.description: Beyond roughly two subject hours a week per child the limiting factor becomes practice and attention rather than teaching. Where a plan proposes more hours than the diagnosis supports, we say so, including where that means a smaller booking than the family offered.

whyPoints.title: Coverage and format stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one and live online on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, holds no premises in the emirate, and claims no approval or licence from any regulator or examination board. Where no specialist covers a subject and level, we say so before anything is booked.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no results-linked refunds, no satisfaction percentages without a sample size and date, no self-published star ratings. Those appear across this market and each one is a reason to ask harder questions rather than a reason to pay more.

faqs.question: Why does an IB Diploma hour cost more than an IGCSE hour for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Component load. An IGCSE subject is two or three written papers plus, in the sciences, a practical or alternative-to-practical paper. A Diploma subject adds an internally assessed component with published criteria, a moderation process and a school deadline sequence the tutor has to work inside. That is more for the hour to hold, and the market prices it: one UAE agency rate card read in October 2026 starts IGCSE at AED 150 an hour and IB at AED 200 from the same pool. Where a Diploma student's internal component is already submitted, that premium stops being justified.

faqs.question: We have one child on IGCSE and one starting the Diploma. How should we budget?
faqs.answer: By month rather than by rate. The IGCSE child's demand is flat until mocks and then climbs to the series. The Diploma child's demand is heaviest in the autumn, when internal components and Extended Essay drafts are live, and again before the May session. Overlay them and you get two expensive windows, autumn and February to April, with a quiet stretch between. Buy the Diploma supervision in the autumn, keep the IGCSE child on light maintenance until January, then concentrate. Running both children at two hours a week all year costs more and delivers less.

faqs.question: Does advertising a tutor as the best justify a higher rate?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. The word carries no checkable content, and the published spread across the UAE market runs from around AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 at the premium end for work that is often described in identical language. What does justify a higher band is specific: Higher Level content, an internally assessed component, a genuinely scarce specialism, or a short deadline that makes availability valuable. Ask which of those applies to your child. If none does, the quote should sit in the mid band regardless of the adjectives attached to it.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to have one tutor cover both an IGCSE and a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on whether the pairing is real. One tutor covering IGCSE and Diploma Physics is plausible and may reduce the administrative friction, though not usually the hourly rate, since the Diploma hour still carries the component load. One tutor covering IGCSE maths and Diploma Economics is a generalist claim, and generalist claims are where quality drops fastest. Ask how many students they have taught in each specific syllabus. Two cheaper specialists are usually better value than one person saying yes to everything.

faqs.question: What does the crossover from Year 11 into DP1 actually cost a family?
faqs.answer: It is the most expensive stretch in a UAE school career, because for a few months you are finishing one qualification at one band and starting another at a higher one. The way to reduce it is sequencing rather than negotiation: finish the IGCSE work and stop it rather than tapering it into the summer, use one session in July on subject choice and Higher Level fit, buy light transition work in August, and do not buy Diploma remediation before any school assessment exists to diagnose from. Families who reverse that order pay the higher band for longer.

faqs.question: Should we spend the same amount on every subject a child is struggling in?
faqs.answer: No, and spreading evenly is the commonest budgeting mistake we see. Rank the loss categories rather than the subjects. Method not written down and command-term mismatch respond quickly to a few sessions and show up on marked work almost immediately. A topic never taught needs teaching time, which is slower. An underlying numeracy or literacy gap is the most expensive thing to close. Spending in the fast categories first produces more movement per AED than giving every subject an equal weekly hour, which usually produces a little movement everywhere and not enough anywhere.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether an hour at AED 300 was worth it?
faqs.answer: On marked work, grouped by question type, compared against the student's own earlier script rather than against a class. Within three or four weeks you should see fewer abandoned questions, method appearing without prompting, and a specific loss category shrinking. Those are the leading indicators and they arrive before any grade does. What is not evidence is an enthusiastic session note or a child who enjoyed the lesson. If nothing has moved by question type after four weeks of notes, the right move is to change the focus or the tutor, not to add hours.

faqs.question: Does a monthly retainer work out cheaper than per-session billing in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Only if the sessions are genuinely used. Monthly online packages advertised in this market sit around AED 799 for eight sessions, and in-home packages around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, which are lower effective rates than ad-hoc booking. The risk is paying a full month in a month containing a holiday, a Ramadan schedule shift or an exam week. Ask about expiry, rollover of unused sessions, and what happens to the balance if you change tutor midway. Then check the effective hourly figure rather than the headline.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi differ from rates in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published bands are UAE-wide rather than emirate-specific, so the headline figures are similar. What differs is scarcity. Abu Dhabi's Diploma cohort is smaller and more concentrated than Dubai's, so rare specialisms such as Higher Level Computer Science or Higher Level Economics have thinner local supply, and thin local supply is quoted high. In-home rates in the mainland communities also carry a larger travel element than island addresses. Online matching removes the local scarcity premium, which is the main practical reason the gap narrows for a family in Al Shamkha or Al Falah.

faqs.question: What should be in writing before we pay a first invoice?
faqs.answer: Six things: the figure, exactly what the rate includes, the cancellation and rescheduling terms, the expiry and rollover position on any block, the replacement process if the pairing does not work, and the academic-honesty boundary on any internally assessed component. A single message covering those prevents nearly every dispute in this market. A provider unwilling to put them in writing is showing you how the relationship will be run, and a grade guarantee or a results-linked refund in that message is a reason to stop rather than to proceed.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma budget should go on Internal Assessment supervision?
faqs.answer: More than most families plan for, and earlier. The internal components are live in the autumn of DP1 and again in DP2, in months with no examination to concentrate attention, and they carry a meaningful share of each subject's final mark. Supervision is usually quoted as a block fee rather than hourly, so ask how many review rounds it covers and what the written-feedback turnaround is. The boundary matters as much as the budget: feedback works on the student's own dated drafts, and no tutor supplies text or finishes any part of the work.

faqs.question: Does a higher rate buy a tutor who has marked for the examination board?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and the claim is worth probing. Examiner experience is a real thing, it is time-limited, and it is routinely asserted by people who cannot evidence current status. We do not describe tutors as examiners unless the status can be evidenced, and examiner experience does not confer access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased papers, whatever a sales page implies. What a higher band should buy is demonstrable teaching of your exact syllabus and level. Ask how many students in that syllabus, over how many sessions, and what the marked outputs look like.

faqs.question: At what point does paying more stop buying more?
faqs.answer: Above roughly the specialist band, the extra money buys scarcity, reputation and convenience rather than additional knowledge of the component. A strong mid-band specialist and a premium-tier tutor know the same criteria, papers and loss patterns. The exception is a genuinely rare Higher Level subject with a few weeks remaining, where you are paying for somebody existing and being available. The other ceiling is on hours: past about two subject hours a week per child, practice time, sleep and school attention become the limiting factors instead of teaching.

faqs.question: Can we reduce the cost by having two children share a tutor?
faqs.answer: Only where the work genuinely overlaps, which is rarer than it looks. Two siblings in the same subject, same board and same tier can share effectively, and the saving is real. Two siblings in different years or different boards cannot, and a shared session becomes two half-sessions at a full price. Group rates quoted per student look attractive and are suitable for syllabus coverage and timed practice, but not for internally assessed work or for a student who is two topics behind the rest of the room.

faqs.question: How do Abu Dhabi school fees change what is sensible to spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: They set the context rather than the figure. Fees and examination entries are largely fixed once a school is chosen, while tutoring is the discretionary line whose size you control, which argues for concentrating it where it works rather than spreading it thinly. One point of caution: the fee freeze for the 2026-27 academic year confirmed in May 2026 applied to private schools in Dubai under that emirate's incentives package, not to Abu Dhabi, where fee adjustments run through ADEK's own process. Do not plan an Abu Dhabi budget on a Dubai measure.

intro.heading: The question is which components transfer to a screen
paragraphs: Most pages arguing for online tuition argue about convenience. That is the least interesting part of it. The real question for an Abu Dhabi family is narrower and answerable: which parts of the IB Diploma can a competent tutor work on through a shared screen, which parts can they work on better than they could sitting at a dining table, and which parts cannot leave the school building at all. Once that is mapped, the decision makes itself and nobody has to argue about whether online tutoring works in the abstract.

The honest map has three bands. Things that transfer better: anything whose working surface is a document. A marked script at full size with annotation appearing live as the tutor writes it, a markscheme open beside it, a criterion descriptor pasted next to the paragraph it judges, a graph plotted and replotted in seconds, algebra worked line by line on a shared whiteboard that both people can write on. None of that is a compromise against a printed page; it is better than a printed page, and a session can be recorded so that a student in April can watch the February explanation again.

Things that transfer with care: anything involving sustained independent writing, and anything where the student's attention is fragile. A twelve-year-old who needs a presence in the room to stay on task is a genuine exception and we say so rather than pretending the format is universal. Long writing tasks need the student to work offline between sessions and send the output in, which is a discipline question rather than a technology one.

Things that do not transfer at all: the laboratory practicals and the Group 4 project, the recorded oral assessments, CAS, and the formal supervision of the Extended Essay, which belongs to the school's assigned supervisor. A tutor prepares a student for an individual oral and can rehearse it, but the assessed recording happens at school with the school's teacher. Anyone implying otherwise has not read the subject guides.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition this way. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Everything below is about what a live video lesson actually contains for an Abu Dhabi Diploma student: what to test in the free trial, how Higher Level differs from Standard Level in work terms, the component map, the minute-by-minute shape of a session, the session windows that survive the school run and Ramadan, and what the market charges.

One framing point before the detail. Private schools in Abu Dhabi are supervised by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which handles the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. ADEK sets the conditions your child's school operates under; it has nothing to do with tutoring platforms, and IB Gram holds no licence or approval from it. We mention it because the emirate's regulator is named by almost nobody else writing about tutoring here, and because knowing which body is responsible for what makes it easier to ask your school the right questions and to ignore the providers who imply official status they do not have.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Each stage of the IB continuum puts a different proportion of its assessment inside the school building, which decides how much of it an online tutor can usefully touch. The notes below are about that proportion rather than about the programme in general.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is the programme where online tuition has the most purchase, because the majority of the mark comes from written papers and written coursework. Three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each with external papers plus an internal assessment, alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Everything paper-based is workable on a shared screen; the practicals, the recorded orals and the formal Extended Essay supervision are not.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi candidates sit the May session. No IB session or results date appears on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so an unverified date here would be worse than none. Take yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org, then count the session plan backwards from it. Gulf Standard Time is a convenient zone for this: tutors working from India are ninety minutes ahead of Abu Dhabi, which makes late-evening slots routine.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP subjects are marked against four criteria on eight-point scales with published descriptors, and the descriptors are text. That makes the MYP unusually suited to screen work: the descriptor goes on screen beside the paragraph it judges, and the student can see exactly which words in the descriptor their paragraph does not yet earn. The personal project is supervised by the school and a tutor questions rather than directs it.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi MYP students often sit in a household running on two different calendars, with an older sibling in the Diploma. Staggered video slots in one evening solve that without anybody driving, which is the practical reason families in the Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City areas tend to move online first.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs a career-related study with Diploma courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Online support concentrates on the Diploma courses and on the reflective project, which is criterion-marked and routinely begun too late. The career-related study itself is usually delivered by an external provider and sits outside what a subject tutor can help with.
programmes.countryNote: Few Abu Dhabi schools run the CP, so platform coverage for a specific career-related study is genuinely thin. We will tell you that rather than matching a tutor who has read the guide and never supervised the component.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external paper, so online sessions here are short, frequent and skill-specific: reading comprehension, written explanation of a method, number fluency. Attention is the limiting factor rather than content, which is why 30-minute sessions work better than 60-minute ones at this stage, and why we say plainly when a child is too young for the format.
programmes.countryNote: For Abu Dhabi families arriving mid-year from a British or American primary, the most useful single session is often reading the PYP report format with a tutor who knows the framework. That is a screen-sharing job: the report on screen, annotated as it is explained.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject below names what the assessment actually measures, where the marks are lost, and what a shared screen adds for that specific subject. The third part is the one that decides whether an online hour is better or merely equal.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is non-calculator, and the losses are unshown method and hand-algebra collapse under time. A shared whiteboard both people can write on is the strongest tool available here: the tutor works a line, the student works the next, and the method line that earns the mark gets written rather than described. HL's extra topics need more session hours than SL by a clear margin.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is calculator-active and modelling-heavy, and the recurring loss is a correct figure with no interpretation attached. Screen sharing a spreadsheet or graphing tool lets a tutor change one parameter and show the model move, which is the fastest way to teach interpretation. The closing sentence with units is the habit a session drills.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mechanism notation, energetics and data booklet fluency. Drawing mechanisms on a shared whiteboard with the booklet open on the same screen is better than two people sharing one printed booklet. The laboratory work stays at school; the internal assessment write-up, uncertainty treatment and evaluation criterion are all workable over video.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty arithmetic, significant figures and explanation chains that break after one link. Graph work is where a screen wins outright: a plot can be redrawn with the uncertainty bars added in seconds, and the student sees why the gradient claim was unsupportable. Practical skills assessed at school remain the school's responsibility.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term drift and data-based answers that describe a figure instead of quoting values from it. Putting the figure on screen, zoomed, with the axes read aloud before the stem, fixes more marks than any amount of content revision. The internal assessment is the richest piece of screen work in Biology because it is drafted over months.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence for a claim rather than recited, and the HL extensions add research methods depth. Essay structure is the main loss, and essay structure is text, which is exactly what a shared document handles well. A tutor can rebuild a paragraph with the student in real time and leave the original visible beside it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram-first discipline and a closing judgement that cites the stimulus. Drawing the diagram on a shared whiteboard while the stimulus text sits beside it is the whole session in one frame. HL quantitative questions reward visible method, which is a screen-friendly thing to drill.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Resource interpretation, case study specificity and command-term accuracy. Maps, graphs and photographs are screen-native, and a tutor can annotate a resource live rather than describing what to notice. The fieldwork component belongs to the school and cannot be replaced by anything a tutor does.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Text-type conventions in the written assignment and register control in the productive skills. A shared document with a model text beside the student's draft is the most efficient way to teach text type. The individual oral is rehearsable over video, but the assessed recording is made at school with the school's teacher.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode traces, the HL abstract data structures section, and the solution development of the internal assessment. Screen sharing an editor and a trace table side by side is how this subject is taught properly, and it is close to impossible with one laptop between two people at a table.

sections.heading: What to test in the free trial lesson with an online IB tutor
paragraphs: A trial lesson is the only pre-purchase evidence that is worth anything, and most families use it badly: they treat it as an introduction and spend forty minutes on pleasantries and goals. Treat it instead as an audition with a brief. Send your child's most recent marked work beforehand, and judge the session on what the tutor does with it in the first ten minutes.

There are five checkpoints and they are all observable by a parent who does not know the subject. Does the tutor open the student's actual script, or do they open a generic worksheet? Do they name a specific error class, with a rough mark value, or do they talk about confidence? Do they get the student writing inside the first fifteen minutes, or do they lecture for forty? Do they use the markscheme or criterion language, or their own opinion of good work? And at the end, do they give you a number of sessions with a reason attached, or an open-ended recommendation?

The fifth one is the most revealing. A tutor who says eight sessions should move the two highest-value items, then we reassess, is thinking about your child. A tutor who recommends ongoing weekly support indefinitely is thinking about a subscription. Neither answer is proof, but the first is a far better bet, and the specificity of it is hard to fake on a first meeting.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: what changes and what it costs in session hours
paragraphs: Families routinely underestimate the step from Standard Level to Higher Level, and the usual framing - that HL covers more content - is only part of it. The additional content is the visible difference. The invisible differences are an extra paper in most subjects, a higher weighting on the components that reward synthesis rather than recall, and markschemes that expect depth of reasoning rather than more facts. That combination is why HL session needs tend to run above SL by a clear margin rather than proportionally.

The decision about which subjects to take at Higher Level is usually made in Year 11 on the basis of enjoyment and predicted grades. A more useful input is the student's own pattern of error classes. A student whose losses are mostly recall-based will find HL content volume punishing. A student whose losses are structural - evaluation without judgement, explanation chains that stop early - will find HL harder in the same way SL is already hard, which is a more tractable problem.

There is a university dimension too, and it matters in this market. Higher Level requirements are set by universities rather than by the IB, and an offer for a quantitative degree will usually specify mathematics at Higher Level, often naming Analysis and Approaches specifically. For students planning to apply to UAE universities, the Ministry's equivalency process is separate again and has its own documentary requirements, which are covered later on this page.

sections.heading: Component by component: what a shared screen handles and what stays with the school
paragraphs: This is the table the rest of this market does not publish, and it is the one that answers the real question. The IB assesses through several different kinds of component, and they divide cleanly into those whose working surface is a document, those that need a physical space or a recording made under controlled conditions, and those that are a school responsibility by design.

The practical consequence is that an honest online tutor turns work away. Nobody can run your child's Group 4 project or sit in their laboratory session. Nobody outside the school can make the assessed recording for an individual oral. The Extended Essay has an assigned supervisor at school and that supervision is part of the assessment process, so a tutor works around it rather than replacing it. A provider that implies otherwise is either misdescribing what it does or encouraging something the IB would treat as misconduct.

What is left is still most of the mark. External written papers are the largest share of nearly every subject's grade, and they are entirely document-based. The internal assessment write-up, as opposed to the laboratory work behind it, is document-based. Theory of Knowledge essay drafting is document-based. So is every piece of exam technique work, every markscheme comparison, every criterion-referenced read of a draft.

Read the last column as a boundary rather than as a limitation. Knowing exactly what belongs to the school makes it easier to use the school properly, which is the cheapest support available and the one most families under-use.

sections.heading: The anatomy of a 60-minute online session
paragraphs: A good online hour has a shape, and the shape matters more than the content of any single session. The failure mode is a pleasant conversation about a topic, which feels productive and leaves nothing behind. The structure below is the one our tutors are asked to hold to, and it exists because the alternative drifts within three weeks.

The first block is deliberately short and looks backwards: what happened to last week's error class, checked against something the student actually produced. If that check is skipped, items never retire and the error log grows forever. The middle block is the work: the marked script on screen, annotated as the conversation goes, with the student writing rather than watching. The last block is forward-looking and written down: what to practise, what will be marked next week, and one line recording what the session changed.

Timing discipline is also a teaching tool. A student who has never been made to answer a six-mark question in seven minutes with a tutor watching does not know how long seven minutes feels. Putting a visible timer on the shared screen for a single question does more for exam timing than any amount of advice about pacing, and it is one of the few things that is genuinely easier online than at a table.
The table gives the standard shape. Tutors vary it with reason, and the two blocks that are never dropped are the opening check and the written close.

sections.heading: Session windows that survive the Abu Dhabi school run, and Ramadan
paragraphs: Scheduling is where online arrangements quietly fail. A slot agreed in September against an optimistic view of homework collapses in October, the sessions start moving, and by November the rhythm has gone. Choosing a realistic window at the start is worth more than any amount of flexibility later, and the realistic window depends on where in the emirate the household sits.

Three patterns recur across Abu Dhabi. Island families with short school runs can genuinely hold a 4pm or 4.30pm slot, and they are the only ones who can. The Khalifa City, Al Raha and airport corridor loses the early evening to bus routes, so 6pm and 6.30pm are the real options. The outer mainland communities - Al Shamkha, Al Falah, Al Samha - run later still, and a 7pm start is normal rather than exceptional. Tutors working from India sit ninety minutes ahead of Gulf Standard Time, which makes late Abu Dhabi slots straightforward instead of a favour.

Ramadan reorganises everything for a month. School hours shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and the 5pm slot stops existing. The workable answer is a post-Iftar window, usually between 8.30pm and 10pm Gulf Standard Time, with shorter sessions: forty-five focused minutes beats a tired hour by a distance. Families who plan that in advance keep their rhythm through the month; families who improvise lose three or four weeks of it, which matters when the month falls close to a session.

sections.heading: The technology that matters, and the technology that is theatre
paragraphs: Very little equipment is needed and most of what providers advertise is decoration. What genuinely matters is four things: a connection stable enough to hold video for an hour, a screen large enough to read a script on, a way for the student to write that the tutor can see, and audio good enough that neither person repeats themselves. A laptop, a pair of wired earphones and a phone camera pointed at a page will cover all four.

The writing surface is the one worth spending on, and it is not expensive. A basic graphics tablet or a stylus-capable tablet changes mathematics and science sessions completely, because the student writes and the tutor sees the working as it forms rather than after it is finished. A photograph of a finished page tells you the answer was wrong; watching the line form tells you where the thinking went wrong, which is the whole point of a one-to-one session.

What does not matter: proprietary platforms, gamified dashboards, artificial-intelligence marking features, and library access that nobody opens. A provider whose pitch is largely about its software is usually compensating for something about its tutors. The platform should be invisible by the second session, and if it is not, it is taking time from the subject.

One habit is worth building regardless of equipment: the student sends their work in before the session rather than at the start of it. A tutor who reads the script in the first ten minutes of the hour has lost a sixth of the session to administration. Marking in advance is the single largest difference in what an hour produces, and it depends on nothing more technical than sending a photograph the evening before.

sections.heading: What online one-to-one IB tuition costs in this market
paragraphs: Three of the six pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency UAE families transact in. The figures below are market rates taken from providers' own published pages in October 2026 and from a published Dubai rate survey, with the source named in every row. They are not IB Gram's price list; our answer to the price question starts with the free trial and a session count attached to the diagnosis.

Online rates sit below in-home rates for a structural reason rather than a quality one: there is no travel inside the hour. An in-home tutor crossing Abu Dhabi for one lesson commits around two hours, and that appears in the rate whether or not it is itemised. Removing the journey removes the cost, and it also removes the constraint that limits the tutor pool to whoever lives nearby.

Two things change the number more than the format does. The first is whether marking between sessions is included, because a rate that covers teaching time only is not comparable with one that includes a marked script each week. The second is proximity to a session: a block agreed in October costs less per hour than the same block agreed in March, which is a market reality rather than a complaint.

For context on the wider cost picture, Dubai's KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in that emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi fee decisions sit with ADEK on their own timetable. Either way, tuition is discretionary spending on top of the largest line in most family budgets, which is an argument for buying the smallest effective block rather than the longest.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the work is on a shared screen
paragraphs: Screen sharing makes one thing easier and one thing more tempting, and both deserve stating plainly. Easier: a genuine criterion-referenced read of a draft, with the descriptors visible beside the paragraph they judge, which is honest supervision done well. More tempting: a tutor with editing access to a live document, which is where honest supervision quietly becomes something else.

Our rule removes the temptation structurally. On coursework, the tutor does not hold editing access to the student's document. The draft is shared read-only or as a file, the tutor comments against the criteria, and the student makes every change in their own copy. That also produces the record that protects the student: a dated sequence of their own drafts improving against published criteria, which is exactly what honest supervision looks like if a question is ever raised at school.

The boundary itself is the same one that applies on paper. A tutor may teach the method, explain the criteria, question the reasoning, mark against the descriptors, and show a published exemplar. A tutor may not supply text, rework a passage into its final form, invent or adjust data, or decide the research question. One page researched for this project sells finished internal assessments at a fixed price; a family buying that is buying a risk that attaches to their child's candidature and not to the seller.

The last point is about materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, markschemes and grade boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. We reference and link to the official sites. We do not host them, send them as files, or reproduce them on these pages, however convenient a download would be in a screen-sharing session.

sections.heading: Coverage, match times and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: No platform covers everything, and the ones that claim to are the ones that match approximately. Abu Dhabi families ask for a wide spread of Diploma subjects, and the honest picture is that the common ones are covered deeply, the sciences and mathematics at Higher Level are covered well, and a few components are genuinely thin. Saying which is which costs us some enquiries and saves families a term.

When a gap exists, we give three options and a date. Wait for a named tutor to free up, with the date stated rather than implied. Take a tutor who is qualified but less specialised, with the limitation written down so nobody is surprised in February. Or go elsewhere, with our suggestion of what to ask the next provider. Concealing a coverage gap is the most expensive thing a platform can do to a family, because the cost lands at the end of DP2 when nothing can be fixed.

Match times vary by how specific the request is. A Standard Level mathematics or English request is usually matched quickly. A Higher Level science with internal assessment supervision takes longer because the pool is narrower. A niche language acquisition option or an arts component may take substantially longer or may not be available at all. The table below is a description of how the platform behaves, not a service guarantee.

One structural advantage is worth restating here. Because delivery is online, a coverage gap in Abu Dhabi is not a geographic problem. The limiting factor is how many people genuinely know a given component, which is a smaller and more honest constraint than how many of them happen to live within a drive of Al Shamkha.

process.title: Send the marked work and the subject list
process.description: Before any call, send the most recent marked script or coursework draft, plus your child's six subjects with their levels. The levels matter: Higher Level and Standard Level are different jobs in the same subject, and a tutor matched without that information is matched on half the brief.

process.title: Take the free 45-minute trial as an audition
process.description: One one-to-one session over live video with your child's own work on screen, no charge and no card details. Use the five checkpoints on this page to judge it: whose document opens first, whether an error class gets named, whether the student writes, whether the markscheme is quoted, and whether the recommendation has a number attached.

process.title: Agree a window, not just a slot
process.description: Pick a session window that survives a normal week in your part of Abu Dhabi rather than an optimistic one. Island households can hold 4.30pm; the Khalifa City corridor cannot. Decide the Ramadan arrangement at the same time, because retrofitting it in the middle of the month loses sessions.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marking done first
process.description: Work is sent the evening before and marked against the published criteria before the hour starts. The session follows the standard shape: check the last error class, work the marked script on a shared screen, drill, one timed question, written close. The annotated script comes back within a day.

process.title: Review at the agreed point, not indefinitely
process.description: The block has a session count and a review point, both set before it starts. At the review you see the error log with retired items marked and a note on what has not moved. If the honest answer is that a second block is not needed, the note says so, and the arrangement stops.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a component, not to a subject
whyPoints.description: Paper 1 technique, extended response structure and internal assessment supervision are three different jobs inside one subject. We match on the one your child is losing marks in, which is only possible because delivery is online and the pool is not limited to a driving radius.

whyPoints.title: Marking happens before the hour starts
whyPoints.description: The script is read and marked against the published criteria before the session, so the lesson is spent on the gap rather than on reading. It is the largest single difference in what sixty minutes produces, and most families have never been offered it.

whyPoints.title: The screen is the right surface for most of the Diploma
whyPoints.description: Annotation visible as it is made, a markscheme open beside the script, a criterion descriptor next to the paragraph it judges, a graph redrawn in seconds, and a recording to watch again in April. These are improvements on a printed page rather than substitutes for one.

whyPoints.title: We name what stays with the school
whyPoints.description: Laboratory practicals, the Group 4 project, the assessed oral recordings, CAS and the formal Extended Essay supervision belong to your child's teachers. We work around them and say so clearly, which also helps families use the free support the school already provides.

whyPoints.title: Coverage gaps are disclosed, not disguised
whyPoints.description: Where no suitable tutor is free, you get a named wait with a date, a qualified alternative with the limitation written down, or an honest referral elsewhere. Arts components and rare language options are the usual gaps and we say so before you pay.

whyPoints.title: No editing access to coursework documents
whyPoints.description: On any assessed component the tutor comments against the criteria on a read-only draft or a file, and the student makes every change in their own copy. That removes the temptation the format creates and leaves the dated record that protects the student.

faqs.question: Is an online IB tutor as effective as one sitting in the room?
faqs.answer: For most of the Diploma, yes, and for document-based work it is better. The working surface of a serious IB session is a document: a marked script, a markscheme, a criterion descriptor, a graph. On a shared screen all of that is full size with annotation appearing live, and the session can be recorded for later. Where presence genuinely wins is with young children who will not stay on task alone, and with students who have a specific access need that makes a screen difficult. We will say when that applies rather than claiming the format suits everybody.

faqs.question: What should I look for in the first online lesson?
faqs.answer: Five things. Whether the tutor opens your child's own marked script or a generic worksheet. Whether they name specific error classes with rough mark values rather than talking about confidence. Whether the student is writing within the first fifteen minutes. Whether they quote the command term or criterion descriptor instead of their own view of good work. And whether the closing recommendation has a session count and a review point attached. The last is the most revealing: a plan with a number is about your child, an open-ended arrangement is about a subscription.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor handle the science practicals?
faqs.answer: They do not, and nobody should claim to. The laboratory work, the safety approval, the apparatus and the Group 4 project belong to your child's school. What an online tutor can work on is everything downstream of the bench: research design before the data is collected, uncertainty arithmetic, graph and gradient work, the evaluation criterion, and the write-up read against the published descriptors. That is where most of the marks in a science internal assessment sit, which is why the division is workable rather than crippling. Anyone offering to run the practical has misread the subject guide.

faqs.question: In work terms, how much heavier is a Higher Level subject than a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: More than extra content. There is usually an additional paper, longer durations, and markschemes that reward synthesis across topics and sustained reasoning rather than more facts. The internal assessment is judged against the same criteria at greater expected depth, so draft cycles tend to need one more round. School teaching hours are higher, which means a student who falls behind at Higher Level falls behind faster. In session terms, Higher Level typically needs more hours than Standard Level and a larger share of them spent on new content rather than on technique.

faqs.question: What equipment and connection does an online IB session need?
faqs.answer: Less than most providers suggest. A connection stable enough to hold video for an hour, a screen big enough to read a script on, audio good enough that neither person repeats themselves, and some way for the student to write that the tutor can see. Wired earphones solve more problems than any software feature. The one upgrade worth buying is a stylus-capable tablet or a basic graphics tablet for mathematics and science, because watching the working form tells a tutor where the thinking went wrong, which a photograph of a finished page never does.

faqs.question: Are sessions recorded, and who can watch them?
faqs.answer: Recording is available and the decision is yours. Most families take it for mathematics and the sciences, where a worked explanation is worth revisiting in April, and skip it for discussion-heavy subjects where a student speaks more freely without it. Where recording is on, the file is for your household and the tutor; it is not published, shared with other students, or used as teaching material. If you would rather not have sessions recorded at all, say so at the start and the tutor works without it, which changes nothing about the lesson.

faqs.question: What time do online IB lessons run for students in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Anything from 4pm to 9pm Gulf Standard Time on weekdays, plus weekend mornings. Which window is realistic depends on your part of the emirate: island households with a short school run can hold 4.30pm, the Khalifa City and airport corridor loses the early evening to bus routes and settles at 6pm or 6.30pm, and the outer mainland communities usually start at 7pm. Tutors working from India are ninety minutes ahead of Gulf Standard Time, so late Abu Dhabi slots are routine. Weekend mornings are the best window for a full timed paper.

faqs.question: Can online tutoring prepare my child for the individual oral?
faqs.answer: Preparation yes, the assessment itself no. A tutor can work on the choice of extract or global issue, the structure of the ten minutes, the balance between analysis and summary, timing, and the follow-up questions a teacher is likely to ask. Rehearsal over video is realistic practice because the student is speaking to a screen either way. What cannot happen outside school is the assessed recording, which is made by your child's own teacher under the school's conditions. A provider offering to produce or sit the oral assessment has misunderstood the component.

faqs.question: How much does an online IB tutor cost per hour in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates from providers' published pages in October 2026 run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to AED 450 for an IB specialist with marking and coursework supervision included. Budget online options start lower, from around AED 33 to AED 65 in published material. Those are market figures with the source named, not our price list. Online sits below in-home rates because there is no journey inside the hour, not because the teaching is thinner. Ask every provider whether marking between sessions is included before comparing numbers.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor mark a handwritten paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the part that works better than families expect. The student photographs or scans the script and sends it the evening before. The tutor marks it against the published criteria in advance, question by question, with annotation at each point of loss. In the session the marked script is on screen at full size for both people and gets annotated further live as the conversation goes. Compared with two people leaning over one printed page, the shared screen is easier to read, easier to zoom, and leaves the student with a copy they keep.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a student who is easily distracted?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, with structure, and sometimes not. Two things help: shorter sessions, forty-five minutes rather than sixty, and a session shape in which the student writes within the first fifteen minutes rather than watching a demonstration. A visible timer on a single question also sharpens attention more than instructions to concentrate. Where a student genuinely needs a person in the room to start work at all, the format is the wrong tool and we will say so after the trial rather than taking a term's fees to find out. That is usually clearer with younger students than with Diploma candidates.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to cover over video?
faqs.answer: The arts, by a distance. Process portfolios, exhibitions and performance components involve physical work and documentation that a screen handles awkwardly, and platform coverage for them is thin, which we say openly. Design Technology has the same problem at the making stage. Everything whose assessment is written transfers cleanly: mathematics, the sciences on the write-up side, individuals and societies, language A and language B on the written components. The honest dividing line is whether the marks come from a document or from a physical artefact made under supervision.

faqs.question: How is academic honesty protected when work is shared on a screen?
faqs.answer: Structurally, by removing the temptation. On any assessed component the tutor does not hold editing access to the student's document: the draft is shared read-only or as a file, the tutor comments against the criteria, and the student makes every change in their own copy. Each session is logged with the date and the version discussed. That produces a dated sequence of the student's own drafts improving against published criteria, which is what honest supervision looks like if a question is raised at school. Nobody on the platform supplies text for assessed work, at any price.

faqs.question: Can we move the weekly slot when the school timetable changes?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better to move it properly once than to shuffle it weekly. Tell us what has changed and we re-book a fixed slot, with the same tutor where the new time works for them and a named alternative where it does not. What we try to avoid is a rolling arrangement where the time differs every week, because that is the pattern that quietly ends most tutoring by November. Ramadan is worth planning in advance for the same reason: agree the post-Iftar window before the month starts rather than during it.

faqs.question: What happens if no online tutor covers my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You get told, with three options and a date. Wait for a named tutor to free up, with the date stated rather than implied. Take a tutor who is qualified in the subject but has not supervised that specific component, with the limitation written down so nothing is a surprise in February. Or go elsewhere, with our suggestion of what to ask the next provider. Arts components and rare language acquisition options are where this happens most. Concealing a gap costs a family a term, which is worse for everybody than losing an enquiry.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-tuition.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below names a subject group and a level rather than claiming the whole Diploma. That is deliberate: a tutor who teaches six subjects at Higher Level is describing a timetable, not an expertise, and the subject guide for each one runs to its own set of criteria.

intro.heading: A ranking is the wrong question; fit to a component is the right one
paragraphs: There is no league table of IB tutors in this emirate, no regulator that scores them, and no published dataset anyone could rank them from. What exists is a search results page of providers describing themselves in identical terms, several of them publishing star ratings they generated themselves. One shows two different review figures on the same page. Another shows a five-out-of-five score from twenty reviews alongside a claimed student body in the thousands. Those are not comparisons; they are decorations.

The question that can actually be answered is narrower and more useful: which tutor is the right fit for the specific component your child is losing marks on. That requires knowing what the component is, which almost no parent is told clearly by a school report. A Diploma student does not fail Physics; they lose marks on Paper 2 extended response because they describe where the command term asks them to explain. A Middle Years student is not weak at Science; their Criterion C is at three while Criterion A is at seven. Those are different problems with different solutions and different prices.

So this page is built as a diagnostic tool rather than a pitch. It explains what each of the six IB subject groups actually assesses and where marks reliably go. It sets out the command terms that decide long-answer marks and what each one instructs a marker to reward. It explains the criterion letters in Middle Years assessment, which is the single most useful thing a parent of a Year 7 to 11 student can learn. And it gives you nine questions to ask any provider, including us, whose answers are documents rather than adjectives.

Abu Dhabi matters to this in one specific way. Diploma cohorts in this emirate are small per school, spread between the island schools, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor and the newer mainland communities. A student struggling in a Higher Level subject may be one of very few doing so, with no peer to compare against and sometimes a teacher covering the subject alongside others. That isolation means the diagnosis has to come from the student's own marked work rather than from how they rank in a class of four.

The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes, which tells you about a school rather than about a subject. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, the IB or any examination board, and claims none. What we do claim is specific: one-to-one sessions over live video, a marked baseline before any hours are quoted, and feedback on coursework that arrives as questions rather than as text. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visiting is a service offered only in India.
