abu-dhabi/best-ib-tuition.programmesIntro: What good looks like differs by programme, because the assessment differs. Here is what each stage of the IB actually measures and what a tutor therefore has to know to be useful at it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external assessment, so judging a tutor here is about whether they can establish a measurable baseline at all. The useful signals are concrete: reading fluency against the same passage at intervals, number facts timed, written work marked against the same success criteria twice. A tutor who cannot describe how progress would be measured is unlikely to be able to show it later.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi PYP schools run their own inquiry cycles, and the final-year exhibition is where parents see detailed work. The right support there is visible as questions about the student's own line of inquiry, never as supplied text. Mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education run alongside the programme and are frequently the subject families actually need help with.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked from zero to eight, with the names differing by subject group. The school converts criterion totals into a reported level using its own published boundaries. A tutor who talks about the subject without referring to criterion letters is working from the content and not from the assessment, which is where the marks actually are.
programmes.countryNote: The step from the Middle Years into the Diploma is where Abu Dhabi families most often look for support, and the step is in written demand rather than in content. A student at Criterion A seven and Criterion D three will find Diploma long-answer questions brutal, and that is diagnosable two years early if anyone looks at the breakdown.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject has internally assessed work and external papers with published weightings in its own subject guide. Judging a tutor means asking which paper number and which internal assessment criteria they work on, and expecting a specific answer.
programmes.countryNote: Cohorts per school are small here, so a Higher Level subject may have very few students and limited internal comparison. The consequence is that a school report gives you a position in a group of four rather than a diagnosis, and the marked script is the only reliable evidence. It also means specialist local supply in any one Higher Level subject is thin.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: internal assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Assessed against criterion letters published in each subject guide and in the core guides, and supervised by the school. This is where judging a provider matters most, because the difference between legitimate feedback and malpractice is a difference in kind rather than degree. Ask how feedback is delivered and expect the answer to involve questions.
programmes.countryNote: One provider in the wider UAE search results sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. In a market where that is available, the single most important vetting question is how a provider describes coursework support. Any answer involving producing, completing or supplying the work should end the conversation, because the risk lands on your child.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-tuition.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects Abu Dhabi students most often need help with, each with the assessment feature that decides the grade. Naming that feature is how you tell a subject specialist from a strong graduate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry the grade, and method marks are the commonest loss: a correct answer with unwritten steps scores below a flawed attempt that shows its working. Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth. A tutor should be able to say which topics in the current guide they consider the usual failure points.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use dominate, and losses cluster on interpreting a result in context rather than on computing it. Students who can run a regression often cannot say what it means for the situation described. A tutor quoting the same approach for both maths routes has not asked which course your child takes.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Long-answer explanation is where the grade moves, and the commonest failure is describing a phenomenon when the command term asks for a causal explanation. Dropped units and unstated assumptions cost marks on every paper. Higher Level carries an additional paper and additional topics, which changes the hours substantially.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation chains, equilibrium reasoning and bonding explanations. The internally assessed work is where criterion-level judgement bites hardest, particularly on data processing and evaluation, and it is the component where feedback quality differs most between providers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than conceptual difficulty. A six-mark question wants six distinct scoring points and most students write two points three times. The fix is structural and fast, which makes Biology one of the subjects where a short, sharply aimed block genuinely changes a grade.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks and most are drawn with unlabelled axes or the wrong curve shifted. Evaluation questions want a judgement supported by a reason, not a balanced list. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that are reliable marks and frequently abandoned under time pressure.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper one analysis and the individual oral reward a thesis that answers the question asked. A fluent essay about the text that does not address the prompt sits in a middle band however well written. Ask a prospective tutor to explain the markbands rather than the texts.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the organisation in the stem separates bands. Generic answers cap low regardless of fluency, which is why marked scripts in this subject often surprise parents who have read the essays and found them good. The correction is specific and quick once it has been identified.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Carried by many Abu Dhabi students alongside the Diploma, and assessed against criteria that reward written structure as much as fluency. A confident speaker can sit in a middle band on written components, which is the gap a tutor who knows the criteria will find and a language tutor who does not will miss.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed on the exhibition and the essay, both against published criteria, and both frequently treated as unteachable. They are not: the failure mode is almost always an essay that discusses knowledge questions in general rather than answering the prescribed title. Feedback here should be questions about the argument.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-tuition.regionsIntro: Where you live changes which local options exist and therefore what a realistic comparison looks like. Online delivery widens the pool rather than narrowing it, which matters most in the communities where local specialist supply is thinnest.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense, central and well served by nearby schools, so local in-home options exist for widely taught subjects. For a thin Higher Level subject the local pool collapses quickly, and that is where the comparison stops being about price.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Small catchment with a limited local tutor population relative to the number of IB students. Families here frequently find that the available local option is a generalist and the available specialist is remote.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: Long school transport in both directions, so any in-home arrangement has to be late. The practical effect on judging options is that the pool narrows to tutors free after 17:30 and willing to travel, which is a selection on availability rather than on subject depth.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: The densest local tutor supply in the emirate and therefore the widest genuine choice for common subjects. Still thin for a specific Higher Level science, which is the pattern across the whole emirate.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer and growing, with small Diploma cohorts per school. A student can be the only one in their year taking a Higher Level subject, which removes class position as any kind of signal and makes the marked script the only evidence.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Large mainland catchment, long inbound journeys, and a mixed school profile. Judging options here almost always comes down to online against a generalist who can reach you, rather than between two specialists.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Under ADEK like the capital, but far enough out that specialist supply in a given Higher Level subject is close to absent. Comparison is between online options, which at least makes the comparison a fair one on subject depth.

regions.name: Al Dhafra and the Western Region
regions.note: Very limited Diploma-level provision locally. For most Higher Level subjects there is no local option at any price, so the question becomes which remote arrangement is strongest rather than whether remote is acceptable.

schoolClusters.city: Island IB schools: Saadiyat, Al Reem and Yas
schoolClusters.note: Where most Diploma provision in the emirate sits, with small cohorts and firm internal deadlines. Students we support in this cluster are commonly the only candidate in their year for a particular Higher Level subject, which is why a marked baseline rather than a class ranking is the starting point.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland corridor: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: A wider curriculum mix, with IB schools alongside British and American ones in the same catchment. Internal assessment deadlines cluster across several of these schools in the same weeks, which is when specialist availability is tightest and when the quality of the available option varies most.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-tuition.modesIntro: Three ways support is usually structured, judged on what each is actually good at rather than on which is best. The right one follows from the diagnosis, not the other way round.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on a named component
modes.description: A fixed slot aimed at one paper or one criterion, carried across a term. Judge this arrangement on whether the error log shrinks: errors going in and coming out is the mechanism, and a tutor who cannot produce one is working from memory. Best when the diagnosis is a technique or structure problem rather than missing content.

modes.description: A short sequence of sessions placed against your school's internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge draft dates. Judge it on the form the feedback takes: questions and criterion references, not rewritten paragraphs. Any version that offers to produce the work is the thing this market does worst and the thing to refuse.

sections.heading: What the six subject groups assess, and where marks go in each
paragraphs: A Diploma student studies one subject from each of six groups, with three taken at Higher Level. The groups are studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and the arts, with some permitted substitutions. Each group has its own assessment logic, which is why a tutor who claims the whole Diploma is describing availability rather than expertise.

The practical value of knowing the group structure is triage. A student losing marks across two sciences and mathematics has a method and precision problem that one tutor may be able to address. A student losing marks in language and literature and in individuals and societies has an argument-construction problem, which is a different specialist. Spending on both at once is often unnecessary once the pattern is visible.

The table below sets out what each group actually measures and the characteristic failure. These are not difficulty rankings; they are the places a marker most often has to withhold a mark. Every one of them is diagnosable from a single marked script, which is why the first session should produce one rather than a lesson.

One note specific to UAE schools. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandated alongside the licensed international curriculum in private schools, and in Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority calculates their instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. For an Abu Dhabi Diploma student that means genuine timetable pressure on top of six subjects and the core, which is the real reason revision time is scarce rather than any lack of effort.

sections.heading: Command terms: the five words that decide a long-answer mark
paragraphs: More marks are lost to command terms than to any single topic, and almost no school report says so. A command term is the instruction verb at the start of a question, and it tells the marker what to reward. A question asking a student to explain and receiving a description cannot be given the explanation marks however accurate the description is. Students read the noun in the question and skip the verb, and they do it consistently until someone makes them stop.

The terms worth learning are few. State and outline want brief, unelaborated answers and should be answered quickly so the time goes elsewhere. Describe wants features without causes. Explain wants causes and mechanisms. Analyse wants a breakdown into parts and their relationships. Discuss wants a balanced consideration. Evaluate wants a judgement with supporting reasoning. Justify wants a reason for a position already taken. Compare wants similarities and differences addressed together rather than two separate paragraphs.

This is the fastest-moving thing in a term of tuition, which is why it is the first thing to target when the window is short. It is a habit rather than knowledge, and a student corrected on the same term four times generally stops. Two to four weeks of marked written answers usually produces visible movement on long-answer marks, which makes it the highest-return work available before a paper.

Parents can check this at home without any subject knowledge. Take a marked script, read the command term at the start of a question where marks were lost, and read your child's answer. If the verb and the answer do not match, you have found the problem and you can say so specifically to any prospective tutor. That is the kind of question that separates a provider who will diagnose from one who will reassure.

sections.heading: Criterion letters: the most useful thing a Middle Years parent can learn
paragraphs: Middle Years subjects are assessed against four criteria, each marked from zero to eight, and the school converts the criterion totals into the level you see on the report using its own published boundaries. The criterion names differ by subject group, so the letters matter more than the words: what you want from the school is the breakdown by letter, not the summative level.

The reason is arithmetic. A reported level of five can come from four criteria at five each, or from two at seven and two at three. Those are completely different students. The first needs general consolidation; the second has one specific skill that is dragging a whole subject down, and that skill can usually be fixed in weeks. Most parents are never shown the breakdown, and most schools will provide it if asked directly.

In the sciences the criteria run broadly from knowing and understanding, through inquiring and designing, to processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In mathematics they run from knowing and understanding, through investigating patterns and communicating, to applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The names and the exact wording are in the current subject guide for each group, and a tutor should be working from that document rather than from memory of an older version.

This also predicts the Diploma. A student strong on knowing and understanding and weak on the criterion that requires extended reasoning will find Diploma long-answer questions and internal assessments hard in exactly that way, two or three years before it becomes a grade problem. Of all the things on this page, asking your school for the criterion breakdown is the one that costs nothing and changes the most.

sections.heading: Nine questions whose answers are checkable
paragraphs: Every provider in this market will say their tutors are experienced, qualified and IB-trained. None of those words is checkable, which is why they are used. The nine questions below are chosen because each has an answer that is a document, a number or a specific refusal, and a provider either produces it or does not.

Ask them in order and stop when one is dodged. The pattern is more informative than any single answer: a provider who answers seven and evades two is usually evading the two that matter. Apply them to us as well. We fail some versions of these questions on purpose, because a truthful no is worth more than a vague yes, and the answers below tell you which ones.

Two of the nine are the ones this market handles worst. The regulator question catches providers describing their tutors as approved by a body that approves no tutors. The coursework question catches providers who will produce assessed work, which is the single most dangerous purchase available to an IB family because the consequence falls on the student. If you only ask two, ask those.

A note on the free-trial question. A trial that is a consultation with a coordinator tells you nothing about the tutor who would teach. Ask whether the free session is with the actual tutor and whether it uses a real past-paper question. If it is a sales call, it is marketing with a price of zero rather than a trial.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: what the difference actually is
paragraphs: Parents often ask whether a Higher Level subject needs more tutoring than a Standard Level one, and the honest answer is that it needs different tutoring. The difference is not simply more content. It is additional assessment, greater depth in named topics, and in most subjects an extra paper, which changes both the preparation and the failure modes.

The practical consequences are three. First, the specialist pool narrows sharply: the number of tutors who have genuinely carried a Higher Level course through to the papers is much smaller than the number who can teach the subject, and in a small emirate cohort that shows up as scarcity. Second, the internal assessment carries the same weight it does at Standard Level but sits on top of more external content, so the time pressure is worse. Third, the extra paper tends to be the one where the depth is tested, which means it is where the grade is won and lost.

This should also feed a decision parents sometimes have to make in Diploma year one: whether to move a subject from Higher to Standard Level. That is a school decision with its own deadline, and it is worth making on evidence rather than on distress. A marked script that shows method and command-term losses points to a fixable problem at Higher Level; one that shows blank topics across the additional content points to a level that was the wrong fit from the start.

The table sets out what to compare across. It deliberately does not state weightings, paper durations or topic lists, because those are published per subject in the current IB subject guide and they change. A tutor should be reading your child's subject guide rather than quoting figures from memory, and that is itself a thing you can test in a trial lesson.

sections.heading: Coursework: the line, and why it decides which provider to use
paragraphs: Every IB subject has internally assessed work and the Diploma adds the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. All of it must be the student's own, submitted through a school accountable for its authenticity. That makes coursework support the place where provider quality varies most, and the place where the wrong choice carries a consequence that no refund addresses.

The legitimate version is specific. A tutor may explain the criteria in the current subject guide, model a technique on different material or a different dataset, ask questions about a draft, point to a paragraph and say that the conclusion does not follow from the evidence presented, and mark the student's own practice against the markbands. That is genuinely valuable work and it is where many students gain the most.

The illegitimate version is equally specific, and it is sold openly in this market. One provider found in the wider UAE search results prices finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. The IB's academic-honesty rules make that a malpractice matter for the candidate, and the sanction falls on the student rather than on the seller. If any part of a provider's offer involves the work arriving finished, under any label, that is the line.

There is a useful side effect of insisting on the legitimate version. A dated sequence of questions and the student's own revisions is exactly what a school's supervision process expects to see, and it is the student's own evidence that the work is theirs if authenticity is ever queried. Families sometimes treat that trail as paperwork; it is better understood as protection. Related: no provider should be sending you IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because that material belongs to the IB and redistributing it is copyright infringement.
bullets: Legitimate: criteria explained, technique modelled elsewhere, questions on a draft, practice marked

sections.heading: Claims to discount entirely
paragraphs: Four categories of claim appear throughout this market and none of them should move a decision. Knowing them makes a results page much easier to read, because once they are stripped out most providers are saying very little.

Self-generated ratings are the first. A star rating a provider publishes about itself, with no countable and attributable reviews behind it, is decoration and in structured data it also breaches Google's policies. One competitor publishes an aggregate rating of 4.9 generated by itself; another shows two different review figures on the same page; a third shows a perfect score from twenty reviews next to a claimed student body in the thousands. Treat any of these as a reason for caution.

Regulator approval is the second and the most misleading. No education regulator in the UAE approves or accredits tutoring platforms. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years to eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A tutoring business with premises needs a permit from the relevant emirate authority. Neither makes a platform accredited, and IB Gram holds no such approval and claims none.

The third is any statistic without a sample size, a date and a method: satisfaction percentages, average scores, student counts, grade-improvement figures. The fourth is a promised outcome of any kind, including a score, a specific grade movement, a university place or a refund tied to results. Nothing on this page makes any of those claims, which is why it contains fewer impressive numbers than the pages it competes with and more checkable ones.
bullets: Self-published star ratings with no attributable reviews: discount entirely
Claims of regulator or examination-board approval: no such approval exists for tutors
Any statistic without sample size, date and method: treat as absent
Promised grades, improvements or refunds tied to outcomes: a warning, not a reassurance

sections.heading: What one session can realistically change
paragraphs: Expectations about a single session are usually either too high or too low, and both cost money. A first session cannot teach a term of missing content and should not try. What it can do is produce a diagnosis that is worth more than the hour cost, which is why the first session with us is a timed paper rather than teaching.

A well-used hour does one of four things. It establishes a baseline by marking a timed paper and categorising the losses. It corrects one specific habit, such as a command term, on enough examples that the student notices the pattern. It takes one piece of the student's own draft work and asks the questions that make the weakness visible to them. Or it rehearses a procedure, such as a calculation chain or a diagram, until it is automatic. Attempting all four in one hour achieves none.

Across a term the sequence matters more than the total. Baseline first, then the largest loss category, then a review at the halfway point against the baseline, then the second category, then a comparable paper near the end so the movement is measured rather than described. A provider who cannot describe that sequence for your child specifically, after seeing marked work, is selling hours rather than a plan.

The limit is worth stating plainly. Even a well-sequenced term fixes what is in the student's work; it does not predict a grade, because boundaries move and papers vary. The claim this page makes is narrower: that you will be able to see what changed, in documents, and decide for yourself whether it was worth the money. In a market where half the providers will not print a price and several publish ratings they wrote themselves, that is a more useful promise than a better one.
bullets: A first session produces a diagnosis, not a term of teaching
One hour does one of four jobs well, or four of them badly
Baseline, largest category, midpoint review, second category, comparable paper
What a term delivers is visible change in the work, not a predicted grade

process.title: Name the component before anything else
process.description: Send the most recent marked work and, for a Diploma student, the paper the marks were lost on. For a Middle Years student, ask the school for the criterion breakdown behind the reported level and send that. Those documents turn a vague worry into a specific question that a specialist can answer in one session.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach
process.description: Not a consultation. The trial runs with the specific tutor, on a real past-paper question, and you can watch how a correction is actually made. It is also the right moment to ask about the MoHRE permit and to see whether the tutor refers to the current subject guide or works from memory.

process.title: Baseline paper marked and categorised
process.description: One full timed paper or criterion-marked task, with every lost mark tagged as recall, method, command term or timing. The counts come to you in writing. That document decides the sequence of the term and is the only thing a later paper can be honestly compared against.

process.title: A sequence, not a block of hours
process.description: Largest loss category first, a written review at the midpoint against the baseline, the second category next, and a comparable timed paper near the end. Where school coursework deadlines fall, the sequence moves to fit your school's calendar rather than ours.

process.title: A written verdict at the midpoint
process.description: The error log is compared against the baseline and you are told in writing whether it is working. If a category has not moved, the approach changes rather than the hours increasing, which sometimes means a different tutor. If the honest answer is that this was the wrong purchase, you get that answer too.

whyPoints.title: Components named, not subjects
whyPoints.description: Every plan names the paper number or criterion letter being worked on, after someone has read marked work. A tutor who can only name the subject is offering availability rather than diagnosis, and that distinction is the one thing in this market that reliably predicts whether a term achieves anything.

whyPoints.title: Nine questions we expect to be asked
whyPoints.description: The vetting questions on this page are the ones we would want a parent to ask us. Two of them we answer with a flat no, on purpose: we hold no regulator approval, and we will not produce coursework at any price. A truthful no is more useful than a vague yes.

whyPoints.title: No number we could not evidence
whyPoints.description: No satisfaction percentage, no self-published star rating, no student count, no average score. Several providers ranking for this query publish figures that contradict themselves on the same page. The test worth applying, to us included, is whether a number comes with a sample size, a date and a method.

whyPoints.title: Current subject guides, not remembered ones
whyPoints.description: Criteria, weightings and topic lists are published per subject and they change. A tutor should be reading your child's current subject guide rather than quoting figures from an older version, and that is something you can test directly in a free trial lesson by asking where a weighting comes from.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one online, which widens the pool
whyPoints.description: Sessions run live over video, one student and one tutor, at Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. In an emirate where a Higher Level specialist may not exist within a drivable radius, removing travel is what makes a genuine subject match possible rather than merely convenient.

whyPoints.title: Regulators explained, never claimed
whyPoints.description: This page explains what ADEK and the other emirate authorities actually govern and what the MoHRE permit covers, with sources. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them, from the IB, or from any examination board. The phrase describing tutors as regulator-approved is the most misleading thing in this market.

faqs.question: Is there any objective way to rank IB tutors in this emirate?
faqs.answer: No. No regulator scores tutors, no published dataset exists to rank them from, and every rating you will see in these search results was generated by the provider showing it. One competitor publishes an aggregate score it wrote itself; another shows two different review totals on the same page. What can be assessed objectively is fit: whether a tutor works on the specific paper or criterion your child is losing marks on, whether they hold the MoHRE permit, whether marking is inside the rate, and how they handle coursework. Those four have checkable answers.

faqs.question: What single question separates a real specialist from a strong graduate?
faqs.answer: Ask which paper number or criterion letter they would work on, and expect them to decline to answer until they have seen marked work. A specialist thinks in components: Paper 2 extended response, the data-processing criterion, the individual oral. A strong graduate thinks in topics and will offer to cover the syllabus. Both can teach; only one can diagnose. The follow-up that confirms it is asking where a weighting or criterion wording comes from, because the answer should be your child's current subject guide rather than memory.

faqs.question: Why does my child's school report not tell me what the problem is?
faqs.answer: Because a reported level or grade aggregates things that need different solutions. A Middle Years level of five can be four criteria at five, or two at seven and two at three, and those are different students. A Diploma grade can come from a student who knows the content and runs out of time, one who answers the wrong question, or one with blank topics. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown or the marked script rather than the summary. Most schools will provide it, and it is the single most useful thing you can obtain for free.

faqs.question: How much of an IB grade is really lost to command terms?
faqs.answer: Enough that it is the first thing to target when time is short. A command term is the instruction verb at the start of a question and it tells the marker what to reward. An answer that describes where the question says explain cannot be awarded the explanation marks however accurate it is. Students read the noun and skip the verb, consistently, until corrected. It is a habit rather than knowledge, so two to four weeks of marked written answers usually produces visible movement, which makes it the highest-return work available before a paper.

faqs.question: Can I check the command-term problem myself without knowing the subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it takes ten minutes. Take a marked script, find a question where marks were lost, read the first word of the question, then read your child's answer. If the question says explain and the answer lists features, you have found the problem. If it says evaluate and the answer gives a balanced list with no judgement, same. You do not need the subject knowledge to see the mismatch, and being able to describe it specifically to a prospective tutor is the fastest way to find out whether they diagnose or reassure.

faqs.question: Does a Higher Level subject need more hours than a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: It needs different hours as much as more of them. Higher Level adds depth in named topics and in most subjects an extra paper, and that extra paper is usually where the depth is tested and the marks are lost. The internal assessment carries its weight on top of more external content, so time pressure is the real difference rather than task difficulty. The other consequence is supply: the pool of tutors who have carried a Higher Level course to the papers is much smaller than the pool who can teach the subject, which matters in a small cohort.

faqs.question: Should we move a subject from Higher to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: That is a school decision with its own deadline, and it should be made on evidence rather than on how stressful the term feels. A marked script showing method and command-term losses points to a fixable problem at Higher Level, because those respond quickly to correction. A script showing blank topics across the additional higher-level content points to a level that was the wrong fit from the start, and no number of hours changes that cheaply. Get the script read before the conversation with the coordinator, not after.

faqs.question: How do I tell legitimate coursework help from the kind that gets a student in trouble?
faqs.answer: By the form the output takes. Legitimate support is criteria explained, technique modelled on different material, questions asked about a draft, and the student's own practice marked against the markbands. Illegitimate support is any arrangement where the work arrives finished, whatever it is called. One provider in the wider UAE results prices completed internal assessments at AED 3,750. The IB's academic-honesty rules make that a malpractice matter for the candidate, so the sanction lands on your child rather than on the seller. Ask how feedback is delivered and listen for questions.

faqs.question: Are any tutoring providers in Abu Dhabi actually approved by ADEK?
faqs.answer: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; it does not accredit tutoring platforms or individual tutors. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. A tutoring business with premises needs a permit from the relevant emirate authority. Neither of those makes a platform regulator-approved. Any provider describing its tutors as approved or accredited by an education regulator is making a claim that cannot be true, and the permit number is the thing to ask for.

faqs.question: My child is one of three in their Higher Level class. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It changes what the school report can tell you. In a group of three, class position is noise: being bottom means almost nothing and being top means almost nothing. It also means misconceptions can go unchallenged for longer, because there are fewer peers asking the questions that surface them. The practical consequence is that the marked script becomes the only reliable diagnostic. It is also the clearest case for reaching a specialist remotely, since the local pool for that subject in this emirate is unlikely to contain one.

faqs.question: What should a free trial lesson actually involve?
faqs.answer: The tutor who would teach, a real past-paper question, and a correction you can watch being made. If the free session is a consultation with a coordinator, it is marketing priced at zero and tells you nothing about the teaching. Use it to ask three things directly: which component they would work on and why, whether they hold the MoHRE permit, and where the criteria or weightings they mention come from. A tutor who reaches for the current subject guide rather than memory is showing you something real.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who covers five or six IB subjects a good sign?
faqs.answer: Usually the opposite. Each subject has its own guide, its own criterion letters and its own characteristic mark losses, and the depth required to diagnose a Higher Level component takes time in that subject specifically. A tutor offering six is describing a timetable rather than an expertise. There are reasonable pairings: two sciences, or a science with a mathematics route, often share method and work well together because the error log overlaps. A science plus an English A course plus Economics does not.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects respond fastest to tutoring?
faqs.answer: The ones where the loss is structural rather than knowledge-based. Biology long answers, Economics diagrams and evaluation, and Business Management application to the stem all tend to move quickly, because the failure is a writing pattern that can be corrected on a handful of marked examples. Mathematics method discipline takes longer. Content recall across a Higher Level science is the slowest of all and needs weeks of spaced retrieval rather than intensity. If your window is short, target the fast ones and leave the slow one to a longer arrangement.

faqs.question: Why does this page not say that your tutoring is better than other providers'?
faqs.answer: Because the claim would not be checkable and you would be right to ignore it. What this page offers instead is a set of tests you can run on any provider, us included, and the answers we give. We hold no regulator or examination-board approval. We will not produce coursework at any price. We publish market rates with their source and date rather than impressive figures about ourselves. We quote after a marked diagnostic rather than before. Those are narrower claims than the competition makes, and unlike theirs they can be verified.

faqs.question: What should I do first if I have no idea where the problem is?
faqs.answer: Two free things, in this order. Ask the school for the marked script or the criterion breakdown behind the reported level, which costs nothing and is usually provided on request. Then take a free trial lesson that uses a real past-paper question, and ask the tutor what they think the pattern is. Between those two you will usually know whether the issue is recall, method, command terms or timing, which determines what to buy and how long it will take. Buying hours before that is the commonest way families waste a term.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-tuition.closingHeading: Run the nine questions, including on us
abu-dhabi/best-ib-tuition.closingBody: Judging IB tuition is a matter of asking questions whose answers are documents. Which paper number or criterion letter will be worked on. Whether the tutor holds the MoHRE permit and will show it. Whether the free trial is with the tutor who would teach. Whether marking is inside the rate. How coursework feedback is delivered. Ask those of every provider on your list and the list usually shortens quickly. Send your child's most recent marked work, take the trial lesson, and let the baseline paper decide the plan. abu-dhabi/best-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: Read the profiles below against the rubric on this page rather than as advertising. Each names a subject, a level and the components the tutor marks, because that triple is the only part of a tutor profile that can be checked in a trial lesson.

intro.heading: The problem with the word
paragraphs: "Best" is not a property a tutor can have. It is a relation between a particular student, a particular subject at a particular level, a particular component where marks are disappearing, and a particular week in a two-year programme. The tutor who is right for a DP1 student whose Chemistry content has gaps is not the tutor who is right for a DP2 student whose Chemistry content is fine and whose Paper 2 extended response scores nothing. Both students have the same subject on their timetable and they need different people.

That is inconvenient for a tutoring market that sells on superlatives, so the market invents proxies instead. The pages competing for this search publish self-asserted star figures - two of them show different numbers for the same rating on the same page, and one shows a five-point figure from twenty reviews next to a claim about a student count in the thousands. Others lean on examiner status that is never evidenced, or on headcounts, or on satisfaction percentages with no sample size, no date and no method. None of that survives a single question.

What does survive questioning is narrow and checkable. Does this person teach the subject at the level my child sits? Have they marked the specific component where the marks are going? Can they read my child's returned script and name the failure pattern rather than describing the subject? Will they say no to something outside their specialism? Do they hold the private tutor permit, which is free and valid for two years from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation? What happens, concretely, if this match turns out to be wrong in week four?

Abu Dhabi makes the vetting both more necessary and slightly easier. More necessary because the emirate's enrolment runs from the island through the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor out to Al Reef, Al Samha and Al Shamkha, and a radius search in the outer communities returns a pool small enough that families take whoever answers. Slightly easier because the regulatory picture is clear: the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, which means it licenses schools and not tutors, so any claim of regulator approval by a tutoring provider is false on its face.

This page is written so that it can be used against us. The rubric is general. The price tiers are the market's, attributed to whoever published them. We publish no rating, no headcount and no success statistic anywhere on this site, because we could not produce the underlying data for any of them. What we do publish is the method - matched on component, documented in writing, with a free trial lesson before any payment and a replacement rather than an argument if the match is wrong - and the rubric below is how you would test whether that is true.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Vetting criteria change with the programme, because what a tutor needs to know changes. Primary work needs diagnostic fluency teaching; Middle Years work needs criteria literacy; Diploma work needs component-level assessment experience. A tutor strong in one of the three can be unsuitable in another.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each carrying an internal assessment worth a fifth to a third of the grade, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. The test of a Diploma tutor is component-level: can they name what criterion D of a sciences investigation is asking for, or where partial credit falls across the parts of a Mathematics Paper 3 question. A tutor who answers at subject level has not been assessed yet.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the vetting question with the sharpest edge is availability honesty. Specialist supply across the Gulf tightens between December and February of DP2 because every school runs mocks off the same May session. A provider who promises a Higher Level Physics specialist in January without hesitation is either very well staffed or not telling you something, and asking for a named start date separates the two.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject on an eight-point scale, converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. The test here is whether the tutor asks to see the school's own criteria descriptors before teaching anything. A Middle Years tutor who works from content alone will produce a student who knows more and scores the same, because the marks are awarded against descriptors the student has never read.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi MYP families most often arrive with a report card carrying four criteria scores and no translation. The best first session is the one that explains the report, because it tells the parent what to ask the school and tells the student what the next band actually requires. Any tutor who skips that step to get to content is answering a different question from the one you asked.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external assessment. The test of a Primary tutor is whether they measure anything: reading accuracy and rate on an unseen passage, number facts under time, the structure of a piece of writing. A tutor offering examination preparation to a Primary Years student has misread the programme and should be ruled out on that alone.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries in Abu Dhabi come disproportionately from the newer mainland communities, where a second afternoon car journey is the thing families most want to avoid. Two short online sessions a week outperform one long one at this age, and a provider who insists on an hour because it suits their billing is optimising for themselves.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: What counts as a strong tutor differs by subject, and the differences are specific enough to test. Below is what good looks like in each of the subjects Abu Dhabi families ask about most.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A strong tutor talks about where partial credit falls inside a multi-part question and reads a Paper 3 stem aloud before touching algebra. A weak one starts teaching calculus. The test question: what do you do differently on Paper 3 from Paper 1?

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A strong tutor insists on an interpretation sentence after every calculation and knows which university routes state a preference between the two Mathematics courses. A weak one treats the course as easier arithmetic.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A strong tutor asks to see an extended-response answer and rewrites the student's own sentences against the command term. A weak one offers to reteach mechanics. The test question: show me where this answer stopped earning marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A strong tutor checks mechanism conventions - charges, lone pairs, arrow origins - and sign conventions in energetics before anything else, because that is where Higher Level marks concentrate. A weak one begins with bonding theory.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A strong tutor can state what criterion A of the scientific investigation requires and the difference between describing and justifying a research design. A weak one talks about covering the syllabus.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A strong tutor separates the calculation from the evaluation and drills the evaluation, because that is the Higher Level Paper 3 ceiling. A weak one teaches diagrams the student can already draw.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A strong tutor gives an annotation protocol for an unseen text and times it, and knows the Higher Level essay carries its own criteria. A weak one discusses themes, which is the thing students already do instead of analysis.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A strong tutor hands over a mark-per-minute budget for the four parts of Paper 1 before discussing content, because overwriting part (a) is a timing fault. A weak one recommends more revision notes.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: A strong tutor goes straight to the justification of the statistical test in the internal assessment, which is marked on method rather than results. A weak one focuses on learning studies by name.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: A strong tutor understands how the Diploma course and the Ministry-mandated Arabic requirement sit in the same week, and prepares the oral components explicitly. This is the one subject where a UAE-based tutor carries a clear advantage.

sections.heading: What "best" could honestly mean, and what it usually rests on
paragraphs: Start by separating the claims that could in principle be verified from the ones that could not. "Teaches Higher Level Chemistry and has marked Paper 2 extended response" is checkable in a trial lesson. "Has a current examiner appointment with a named board" is checkable if the appointment can be shown. "Holds the private tutor permit" is checkable, because the permit exists, is free, lasts two years and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023.

Then there are the claims that cannot be verified and are presented as though they can. A satisfaction percentage with no sample size, no date and no method. A student count. A star figure asserted by the company about itself - and in this market, two competitors publish different star figures for themselves on the same page, which is both a structured-data policy problem for them and a straightforward signal for you. A "top five per cent of tutors" line in one section and a "three per cent" line in another, on the same site.

The third category is the dangerous one: claims that are not merely unverifiable but would be a liability if true. Approval, accreditation or licensing by an education authority or an examination board. A named school presented as a client or partner. A promise of a particular grade. An offer to supply a finished internal assessment, which one researched provider in this market advertises at around AED 3,750 and which would expose the student to a malpractice finding rather than the provider.

sections.heading: A ten-signal vetting rubric you can use on anybody
paragraphs: This is the rubric we would want a parent to apply to us. Each signal has one question that tests it, and each question is designed so that a weak answer is obvious without any specialist knowledge. Run it on a phone call in about fifteen minutes.

The signals divide into three groups. Four are about match: subject, level, component, and willingness to decline work outside the specialism. Three are about method: whether they start from the student's own marked work, whether anything is written down, and what the plan's end point is. Three are about trust: the permit, the honesty boundary on coursework, and the exit route if the match fails.

The one most families skip is the fourth. A tutor who says yes to every subject and every level has told you something important. Specialism is defined by what somebody refuses, and a provider that will decline a Visual Arts comparative study rather than staffing it with a generalist is giving you information about how they handle the subjects they do accept. We decline the arts regularly, which is not a selling point so much as evidence that the roster is real.

Apply the rubric before discussing price. The sequence matters, because once a number is on the table the conversation becomes a negotiation and the questions get shorter. Two of the ten are worth asking twice. The start-date question, because availability in principle and availability in January are different answers, and a provider who says immediately for every subject you name has told you they are not checking. And the written-record question, because it is the only signal on the list that keeps working after you have paid: a note you can read each week is a rubric that applies itself. Everything else on this page is a one-off test. That one runs every session.

sections.heading: What each price tier actually buys
paragraphs: Price is a signal, just not the one families assume. It does not rank tutors on quality; it ranks them on scarcity and on what is included. The published 2026 bands in this market are: budget online at AED 45-150, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500, with Bestimate showing 180-350; specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270; and premium named tutors at AED 500-650 and more, BartyED publishing AED 650.

At the bottom of the band you are often buying a university student or a school student aged between fifteen and eighteen, both of which are eligible categories for the private tutor permit. That is a legitimate product and the right one for homework supervision. It is the wrong product for Higher Level Chemistry, and the mismatch is the most common expensive mistake in this market, because the rate looks like a saving and the hours produce no marks.

In the middle, AED 150-300 buys syllabus competence and some mark-scheme awareness. At AED 200-450 you should be getting subject-and-level specialism, criterion-level feedback on coursework drafts, and marked past-paper work returned with the mark scheme beside it. If a quote at the top of that band does not include marking between sessions, it is priced as a specialist and delivered as a generalist.

Above AED 500 the premium is almost always reputational, and the most common justification offered is examiner status. We do not describe tutors as examiners for any board unless current status can be shown, and we would not use the label to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because no such access exists. If a premium rests on that claim, ask what evidences it. The table sets out what each band should contain so a quote can be checked against it.

sections.heading: The trial lesson as an audition
paragraphs: A free trial lesson is the only part of the vetting process that tests teaching rather than claims, and most families waste it by treating it as an introduction. Send the marked script in advance and then watch the first ten minutes, which contain nearly all the information.

Three things should happen. The tutor should refer to the script without being prompted, which proves they read it. They should ask the student to attempt something within the first few minutes, because a tutor who talks for twenty minutes is demonstrating knowledge rather than diagnosing. And they should watch the method rather than wait for the answer - the useful interruption comes at the second line of working, not after the result is wrong.

Two things should not happen. The lesson should not begin with the tutor's own materials, because that means the plan was written before your child was looked at. And it should not end with reassurance. The right ending is a plain statement: here is what I think is happening, here is what I would do in the next six weeks and in what order, and here is roughly how many hours that is. A tutor who cannot say that has not formed a view.

It is also worth asking the student afterwards one specific question rather than whether they liked it: what did you get wrong, and what did the tutor say to do about it? A student who can answer both has been taught. A student who enjoyed the hour and cannot answer either has been entertained, which is a real risk in a format that rewards rapport.

sections.heading: Eight claims that should end the conversation
paragraphs: Some marketing is merely overcooked and some is a reason to stop. The difference is whether the claim, if taken at face value, would put your child or your money at risk. These eight are in the second category, and several of them appear on pages currently ranking for this search.

The first is any form of regulator or board approval. Education authorities in the UAE license schools: the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees Dubai's private education quality, and the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge also approve fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. In Dubai a separate educational services permit exists for institutes with physical premises. None of this amounts to an approval a tutoring platform can hold, and IB Gram holds none.

The second is any promise of a specific grade, a point total or a percentage improvement, with or without a refund attached. The third is an offer to produce coursework. The fourth is a self-published star figure, particularly where two different numbers appear on the same page. The fifth is a statistic with no sample size, date or method. The sixth is a school presented as a client or partner. The seventh is an unevidenced examiner claim used to imply access to marking or boundaries. The eighth is a non-UAE phone number as the only contact route on a UAE page, which two ranking competitors use and one pairs with a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page.
The honest versions of all eight exist and are more persuasive, which is the point of the table below.

sections.heading: Credentials: what to ask for and what each one proves
paragraphs: Credential lists in tutor profiles are long and mostly inert. A degree in a subject proves subject knowledge and nothing about assessment. A teaching qualification proves training in pedagogy and nothing about this syllabus. An IB workshop certificate proves attendance. What matters for Diploma work is narrower: has this person taught the current subject guide, and have they marked the component in question.

The syllabus-version question is the one nobody asks and it has teeth. The IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle, and the sciences changed assessment structure in a way that moved the internal assessment to a single scientific investigation marked on four criteria of six marks each. A tutor working from an older guide will teach a coursework structure the student is not being marked against. The question to ask is simply: which subject guide is my child's school teaching, and have you taught that version?

Student-outcome credentials deserve particular care. A tutor who scored highly in their own Diploma knows what it feels like to sit the papers, which is genuinely useful for a student who is panicking, and proves nothing about their ability to diagnose somebody else's script. Treat it as rapport evidence rather than teaching evidence, and test the teaching separately.

Finally, the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two working day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so disregard any figure quoted at you.

sections.heading: The reference check almost nobody does
paragraphs: Families ask for references and then ask the wrong question. "Were you happy?" produces a yes from almost everybody, because happiness with a tutor correlates with rapport rather than with marks. Three better questions take two minutes and are hard to answer dishonestly.

The first: what did you receive in writing? A parent who can describe session notes, an error log and marked papers returned with the mark scheme is describing a real method. A parent who says the tutor was lovely has told you about the tutor's manner. The second: what did your child stop getting wrong? A specific answer - sign conventions, command-term register, running out of time on Paper 3 - is evidence of diagnosis. A general answer is evidence of a pleasant hour.

The third is the one that reveals the most: did they ever tell you to do less? A provider who has recommended reducing hours in a subject, or stopping a block because the problem was solved, is demonstrating that the plan is aimed at something. A provider who has only ever recommended more has an incentive problem that nothing in a testimonial will show.

Where references are unavailable, the trial lesson plus a six-week review substitutes for them adequately, which is why both exist. The review date should be fixed before the first payment, because families are reliably slow to act on a bad match - they wait, hoping, and in a two-year programme that patience is the real cost.

Ask what the student stopped getting wrong, and listen for a specific error
Ask whether the provider ever recommended fewer hours
Fix the six-week review date before any payment is made

sections.heading: The two tutors to rule out, whatever the rubric says
paragraphs: Two candidates can score well on every signal above and still be the wrong choice. The first is a teacher at your child's own school. Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Both are worth verifying against the current policy documents rather than taken from a tutoring page, including this one.

Even setting the rules aside, the arrangement removes the thing you are buying. A tutor's value in the Diploma is an independent reading: of a draft, of a predicted grade, of whether the school's assessment of a student is right. Pay the person who marks the work to improve it and nobody can tell afterwards whether the teaching or the marking moved, and the family has no neutral voice when a predicted grade is disputed.

The second is a provider who will sell you anything. The clearest version is the one offering to produce coursework, which one researched competitor in this market does openly at around AED 3,750 for a completed internal assessment. The IB treats authenticity as a condition of assessment, and the consequence of a finding falls on the student: a subject grade, and in serious cases the Diploma. A provider willing to take that risk with your child's registration is telling you how they weigh your interests against a sale.

The milder version of the same fault is the provider with no refusals - every subject, every level, immediate availability, in every emirate. Specialism is defined by what a roster cannot cover. A straight answer about a gap is worth more than a confident answer about everything.

process.title: Run the rubric before discussing price
process.description: Ten questions, fifteen minutes, on the phone. Subject, level, component, refusals, written record, end point, permit, coursework boundary, exit route, actual start date. Once a number is on the table the conversation becomes a negotiation and the questions get shorter.

process.title: Send the marked script
process.description: A photograph of the most recent marked paper or returned coursework draft, with the teacher's comments visible. It converts the trial lesson from an introduction into a test, because a specialist can arrive having already formed a view about which component is leaking marks.

process.title: Treat the trial as an audition
process.description: Watch the first ten minutes. Does the tutor refer to the script unprompted? Is the student asked to produce something quickly? Does the hour end with a named plan and an hour estimate rather than reassurance? No payment is taken before the trial happens.

process.title: Buy a scoped block, not a term
process.description: Four to eight sessions on one component with a stated finish. By the end there is a second attempt at the same task type to lay beside the first, which is a measurement rather than an impression, and no rolling commitment if the answer is no.

process.title: Review at six weeks, and expect a recommendation to do less
process.description: Judge against fresh marked work rather than feelings. A provider who never recommends fewer hours has an incentive problem. If the named error is still recurring, the plan changes or the tutor does, and a replacement is arranged rather than argued about.

whyPoints.title: We publish no rating, headcount or success figure
whyPoints.description: Not because they would be unflattering, but because we could not produce the sample size, date and method for any of them. Two competitors in this market publish conflicting star figures for themselves on a single page, which is a structured-data policy problem for them and a useful signal for you.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, which is testable
whyPoints.description: A tutor profile here names a subject, a level and the papers or criteria the tutor marks. That is the only part of a profile a trial lesson can check, and it is the unit in which Diploma marks are actually lost and recovered.

whyPoints.title: We decline work, and say which
whyPoints.description: The arts are thin in every market we operate in, and we would rather turn down a Visual Arts comparative study than staff it with a generalist. A roster with no refusals is not a roster. Saying no is the clearest evidence available that the yeses mean something.

whyPoints.title: Online one-to-one, stated up front
whyPoints.description: Every session for an Abu Dhabi family runs live over video with one tutor and one student. We do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India. That removes distance from the shortlist, which is the whole point in Al Reef or Al Shamkha.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims, because there are none to make
whyPoints.description: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi; it does not accredit tutoring providers. We hold no approval from it, from the IB or from any examination board, and we explain the permit regime that does apply instead.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Tutors score criteria, name the capping one and teach the skill. They do not supply prose, choose a research question or submit anything. In a market where completed internal assessments are advertised at around AED 3,750, that boundary is the difference between help and a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Can anyone honestly claim to be the best IB tutor in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No, and the claim is a signal rather than information. "Best" depends on the student, the subject, the level, the specific component losing marks and the week in the two-year programme. A tutor who is ideal for a DP1 student with content gaps in Chemistry is the wrong choice for a DP2 student whose content is sound and whose Paper 2 extended response scores nothing. What can be claimed honestly is narrow and checkable: this person teaches this subject at this level and has marked this component. Everything else is either verifiable with a document or should be treated as marketing.

faqs.question: What qualifications should an IB tutor actually have?
faqs.answer: Two that matter and several that do not. The ones that matter are current teaching of the subject guide your child's school is using, and marking experience in the specific component where marks are disappearing. A degree proves subject knowledge and nothing about IB assessment. A teaching qualification proves pedagogy training and nothing about this syllabus. A workshop certificate proves attendance. The practical question is: which subject guide version are you teaching from, and which paper or criterion have you marked? Add the private tutor permit, which is free, valid two years and issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, as the legal baseline.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor's claim to be an IB or Cambridge examiner?
faqs.answer: Ask for evidence of a current appointment, and ask what the claim is supposed to give your child. The second question is the more revealing one. No examiner has access to unreleased papers, to marking in progress or to future grade boundaries, so an examiner claim used to suggest inside knowledge is misleading regardless of whether the appointment is real. We do not describe tutors as examiners for any board unless current status can be shown, and we do not draw an inference from it. If a premium rate rests on the label, the evidence should arrive before the payment does.

faqs.question: Should I pay more for a tutor who scored very highly in their own IB?
faqs.answer: Treat it as rapport evidence rather than teaching evidence. A tutor who sat these papers recently knows what the pressure feels like and can be genuinely reassuring to a student who is panicking, which has real value. It proves nothing about their ability to read somebody else's script and name why eleven marks left Paper 2. Those are different skills, and the second is the one you are buying. Test it directly: hand over the marked script and ask them to show you where the answer stopped earning marks. A strong candidate does that in two minutes.

faqs.question: What should I be watching for during a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The first ten minutes. Does the tutor refer to the marked script you sent without being prompted, which proves they read it? Is your child asked to produce something within the first few minutes, rather than listening to twenty minutes of exposition? Does the tutor interrupt at the second line of working rather than waiting for a wrong answer? And does the hour end with a plain statement of what the next six weeks would do, in what order, and roughly how many hours that is? A trial that ends in reassurance has not told you anything.

faqs.question: Is a tutor with twenty years of experience better than one with five?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and the question that discriminates is about currency rather than duration. The IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle, and the sciences moved to a single scientific investigation marked on four criteria of six marks each. Someone teaching from an older guide will prepare a coursework structure the student is not being marked against, however long they have been teaching. Ask which subject guide version your child's school is using and whether the tutor has taught that version to a recent cohort. Five years on the current guide beats twenty years on a superseded one.

faqs.question: How do I ask a provider for references without it being awkward?
faqs.answer: Ask for something specific rather than for a testimonial, which makes the request easy to grant and hard to fake. Three questions work: what did you receive in writing; what did your child stop getting wrong; and did the provider ever recommend doing less? The third is the most informative. A provider who has advised reducing hours or stopping a block when the problem was solved has shown that the plan was aimed at something. One who has only ever advised more has an incentive problem that no testimonial will reveal.

faqs.question: Do star ratings on tutoring websites mean anything?
faqs.answer: Self-published ones mean very little, and in this market they are sometimes self-contradictory: two competitor pages we examined show different star figures for themselves on the same page, and one pairs a five-point figure from twenty reviews with a student-count claim in the thousands. Review markup that is not backed by real, countable, attributable reviews breaches Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, raises a consumer-protection question. We publish no rating anywhere on this site, because we could not produce the underlying reviews to match it. Judge the method instead.

faqs.question: What does a good IB tutor do in the first session?
faqs.answer: Start from the student's own work. A strong first session opens with the marked script or the returned coursework draft, identifies where credit was available and not taken, and tests a hypothesis by asking the student to attempt a similar task while the tutor watches the method rather than the answer. It ends with a named plan: this component, this many sessions, in this order, with this practice between. What it should not do is open with the tutor's own materials, which would mean the plan was written before your child was looked at.

faqs.question: Is the most expensive tutor the strongest choice for Higher Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Price in this market tracks scarcity and inclusions rather than quality. The band you want for Higher Level Chemistry is AED 200-450 and above, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate shows 200-450+, because that is where subject-and-level specialism and criterion-level coursework feedback sit. Above AED 500 the premium is usually reputational and should be evidenced before it is paid. Below AED 150 you are usually buying a junior tutor, which is appropriate for homework supervision and the wrong tool for organic mechanisms and energetics.

faqs.question: How many tutors should we trial before deciding?
faqs.answer: One, if the rubric was applied properly first. The phone questions are designed to rule out weak candidates before anybody's time is spent, so by the trial stage you should be testing a single plausible match rather than comparing three. Trialling several tutors with the same child has a cost nobody mentions: the student retells the same history three times and starts the real work three weeks later. Where a first match is wrong, the answer is a replacement rather than a parallel audition, and that replacement should be arranged without an argument.

faqs.question: What does good look like in an IB English tutor specifically?
faqs.answer: A protocol rather than a conversation about themes. Strong English A tutors hand a student a fixed procedure for an unseen text - what to mark, in what order, inside ten minutes - and then time it, because Paper 1 is won in the annotation rather than in the writing. They distinguish between what a text says and how the writer constructed the effect, which is the difference between a mid-band and a top-band analysis criterion. At Higher Level they treat the essay as its own assessment with its own criteria and a 1,200 to 1,500 word limit, not as a longer piece of coursework.

faqs.question: Should the tutor be a current schoolteacher?
faqs.answer: A current teacher at a different school is often an excellent choice, because they are teaching the current guide to a live cohort and they set internal deadlines themselves. A teacher at your child's own school is the one option to rule out. Reported Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the ministry permit's code of conduct is reported to bar the same arrangement. Beyond the rules, paying the person who marks the work removes the independent reading that a tutor is there to provide.

faqs.question: The tutor seems strong but my child does not like them. What now?
faqs.answer: Separate two things before deciding. A student who dislikes a tutor because the sessions are uncomfortable is sometimes describing good teaching: being interrupted at the second line of working and asked to rewrite your own sentences is not enjoyable. A student who dislikes a tutor because they cannot follow the explanations is describing a mismatch. The test is the same one used for the trial: ask what they got wrong last session and what they were told to do about it. If both answers come easily, the discomfort is probably the work. If neither does, change the tutor.

faqs.question: How do I tell a specialist from a generalist who says yes to everything?
faqs.answer: Ask what they turn down. A genuine roster has gaps, and the arts - Visual Arts, Music, Theatre, Film - are thin in every market, so a provider claiming immediate cover for a comparative study is describing their marketing rather than their staffing. Then ask for a start date rather than availability in principle: specialist supply across the Gulf tightens between December and February because every school runs mocks off the same session, so "immediately" for every subject in January is not a credible answer. A named date two weeks out is more trustworthy than an instant yes.

abu-dhabi/best-ib-tutor.closingBody: The most useful thing on this page is not a claim about our tutors; it is the ten questions. Run them on any provider in Abu Dhabi, including this one, before price comes up. Then send the most recent marked paper or returned coursework draft with the subject and level, and a specialist will read it before a free trial lesson. Watch the first ten minutes. No payment is taken before that lesson happens, every session runs one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and a wrong match is replaced rather than defended.
