abu-dhabi/best-igcse-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IGCSE subjects to Abu Dhabi households over live video, and each works from marked papers rather than from a textbook chapter order. The first thing any of them will ask for is your child's most recent mock, marked, with the mark scheme attached if the school released it.

intro.heading: A term of tutoring should leave a paper trail, not a feeling
paragraphs: Ask an Abu Dhabi parent six weeks into a tutoring arrangement how it is going and the answer is almost always about mood. He seems more confident. She does not complain about Thursdays any more. Those answers matter, but they are not evidence, and in an IGCSE year they are not enough. A grade on a Cambridge or Pearson paper is awarded by a mark scheme applied to specific question types, and the only honest way to know whether tuition is working is to watch the marks on those question types move.

That is what this page is about. Not the hourly rate, not the credentials, but the artefacts: what should arrive in your inbox after each session, what a marked past paper should look like once a tutor has been through it, what a component breakdown of a mock actually reveals, and what a timed repeat tells you that a friendly conversation cannot. If a tutor cannot produce those four things after a month, the arrangement is unmeasurable, and an unmeasurable arrangement in Year 11 is a risk dressed as reassurance. The point is not paperwork for its own sake. It is that a mark scheme is specific, so the record of what a tutor fixed has to be specific too, or you cannot tell a good term from an expensive one until the results arrive in August and nothing can be done about either.

The phrase in the search is home tutor, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a deflection. In this emirate, hiring someone to visit a household means paying for driving time, choosing from whoever can reach your community, and losing minutes to bridge and school-run traffic. Published in-home bands in the UAE run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi: in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video.

There is an evidence argument for that format, separate from the cost argument. A video lesson is naturally documented. The screen-shared paper exists afterwards. The annotated question is saved. The session note is written because the tutor has the file open anyway. A visiting tutor can of course do all of this, and the good ones do, but nothing about the format requires it, which is why so many in-home arrangements run for a year on nothing but goodwill. Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, and the school's own data is the other half of this picture; the rest of the page sets out how to read both together, document by document, in the order a parent can actually act on them.

A component breakdown names the question types where marks were lost, not the topics the student dislikes

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different at each stage. A Year 9 student has no public qualification to measure against, a Year 11 student has a mock and a statement of entry, and a resit candidate has an actual result broken down by paper. Each needs a different kind of record.

programmes.name: The year before IGCSE begins
programmes.description: No public exam, so the evidence has to be built rather than collected. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which run in March, May and October, are the one external reference available, and a Checkpoint breakdown is a far better diagnostic than a school report grade. At this stage the useful record is a short list of specific skills that are not yet secure, with a date against each one and a repeat test to close it.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor tend to set maths and science groups early, and a Year 9 set placement quietly decides the IGCSE tier a year later. A parent holding Checkpoint evidence can have that conversation with the school before the placement hardens, which is the highest-value use of tutoring in this year.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10
programmes.description: The year where evidence is cheap to gather and nobody gathers it. End-of-topic tests, the first full mock, and the school's tier recommendation are the three documents that matter. A tutor working properly in Year 10 is building a component map: which question types this student reliably gets right, which they half-get, and which they skip. That map is what makes Year 11 efficient rather than panicked.
programmes.countryNote: Tier recommendations in this emirate are usually made from Year 10 mock evidence and reviewed before entries close. That is the single window where tutoring changes what is possible rather than only what is achieved, and it is the reason a Year 10 marked paper is worth more to you than a Year 11 one.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11 and the series itself
programmes.description: Now the evidence is specific and the clock is real. The statement of entry gives the four-digit code and the tier. The mock gives a component breakdown. The official timetable gives the paper order. Progress from this point is measured in marks on named question types under timed conditions, because that is the only thing the series will test. Topic coverage is no longer the right measure.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and record it with the rest of the evidence.

programmes.name: Resits and private candidates
programmes.description: The best evidence any family ever gets is an actual result, because it arrives broken down by component. A resit plan built from that breakdown is the most efficient tutoring there is: the weak paper is named, the mark is known, and the gap to the next grade is arithmetic rather than guesswork. Most families do not request the breakdown, and then plan the resit from the overall grade.
programmes.countryNote: Published patterns show the gaps a resit plan has to live inside. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those intervals decide whether a resit block runs across a summer or across a term.

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Evidence appears at different speeds in different subjects. These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi households request most, with the component where a marked paper usually shows the leak and how quickly a repeat test can confirm a fix.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 0980, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The fastest subject to evidence, because marks are discrete and method marks are visible on the page. A marked Extended paper usually shows the same three leaks: unclaimed method marks in 'show that' questions, arithmetic slips under time pressure, and blank final questions. A timed repeat two weeks later confirms or disproves a fix with no interpretation needed.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 0972, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Evidence here splits by paper. Theory marks move within weeks once rearranging formulae and unit discipline are drilled. Practical marks, whether on the Cambridge practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, move more slowly because they test writing habits: naming a control variable, choosing a sensible graph scale, distinguishing observation from conclusion.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 0971, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: A marked chemistry paper is unusually diagnostic. Students who lose marks across moles, titration arithmetic and empirical formula have one problem, not three, and fixing the ratio work moves all of them together. Organic chemistry marks behave differently, accumulating slowly as reaction families are consolidated, so expect a flat month before movement.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 0970, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The subject where students feel most confident and marks move least, because the gap is precision rather than knowledge. A mark scheme wanting osmosis named with a gradient direction does not reward a correct general description. Evidence of progress here is the shrinking of long vague answers into short exact ones, which is visible on a marked script within three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: Hard to evidence as one subject, because a single grade hides three disciplines. Ask for the component breakdown rather than the overall mark; in this market the pattern is usually one discipline well below the other two. Tutoring aimed at the weakest third is measurable, while general science revision across all three is not.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500 / 0990, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Evidence comes from the mark grid rather than the total. The summary task and directed writing each have their own criteria, and a student can be strong on one and weak on the other inside the same grade. Progress is visible when a marked script shows selection in the summary rather than paraphrase, which is a three-session change rather than a term-long one.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0991)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with different criteria, and the one most often mis-entered in this market. Written evidence moves fast because the exercise types reward accuracy, and accuracy is drillable. Speaking is assessed separately, so ask explicitly how the tutor intends to evidence progress on that component.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Both are evaluation subjects, and marked scripts almost always show the same ceiling: two sides explained, no judgement reached, the top band unreachable. That is a structural habit and it moves quickly once a student writes three evaluations against the mark grid. Progress is measurable in band movement on the evaluation strand alone.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: 0478 evidence sits in trace tables and pseudocode accuracy, both of which are objectively markable, so progress is easy to show. 0417 is practical and the marks are lost on task compliance rather than skill, which means a checklist against the task wording is the whole fix and the evidence is a clean repeat task.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language (0508 / 0544)
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE teach Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, and the two Cambridge codes are not interchangeable. Evidence here depends entirely on being entered correctly; a student taught as a first-language speaker but entered for the foreign-language syllabus will show odd, uninterpretable marks until the code is confirmed.

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a household sits in Abu Dhabi changes the logistics of tutoring and therefore the realistic shape of a weekly commitment. These notes are about what a Thursday evening actually looks like in each community, because a plan that ignores that is a plan that lapses in week five.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Villa households with siblings in different year groups, often needing different subjects in the same evening slot. Two concurrent video lessons in separate rooms is routine here; one visiting tutor covering both children in sequence turns a two-hour evening into three.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Large school campuses close together, so the school run compresses into a narrow window and families underestimate how late a child is actually ready to work. Sessions that start at 5.30pm or 7pm survive the term; 4pm bookings quietly collapse by October.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: The clearest case in the emirate for not paying for travel. A visiting tutor prices the drive into the hour and arrives at the mercy of the road; the same specialist on video starts at the booked minute, which over a term is several hours of teaching recovered.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Abu Dhabi, and how we actually deliver it
paragraphs: A household hiring a visiting tutor in this emirate is buying three things at once: teaching, travel and a time slot that road conditions can take away. Published UAE in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with the driving inside the figure, against roughly AED 150 to AED 450 for comparable online specialists, and the difference is close to the cost of the journey. That is not a quality gap. It is a logistics gap, and in a city where households sit between the island, the Khalifa City corridor and the mainland communities, it is a large one.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and every UAE family is taught one-to-one over live video. Stating that plainly is more useful than implying otherwise, because it lets the comparison below be honest. There are households for which a visiting tutor is the right answer: a younger child who cannot yet manage a screen alone, or a parent who wants to sit in the room and watch the lesson happen.

For an IGCSE student, the evidence argument usually wins. Online delivery makes the tutor pool the whole Gulf timezone rather than whoever can reach your community, which for Extended physics or first-language Arabic is the difference between a specialist and a generalist. It keeps the booked hour intact. And it leaves artefacts by default, because the paper being marked is already a file. The table sets the two formats against each other on the terms this page cares about: what record each one leaves.

sections.heading: The four artefacts you should hold after a month
paragraphs: Four weeks is long enough to judge an arrangement and short enough that the money is recoverable. By then a parent should be holding four specific things, none of which requires a tutor to do anything unusual. First, at least one past paper marked question by question against the published mark scheme, with the marks written on it. Not a score out of eighty and a comment, but the actual allocation, because the allocation is where the diagnosis lives.

Second, a component breakdown: a short list naming the question types where the marks were lost. 'Weak on algebra' is not a breakdown. 'Loses method marks in show-that questions, no marks lost on substitution, blank on the final two questions in every paper' is. Third, a session note from each lesson saying what was covered and what to practise before the next one. Four notes in a month is not administrative overhead; it is the only continuous record that exists.

Fourth, a timed repeat. Somewhere in the month, the student should have sat a set of questions of the same type as the ones that were failing, under time pressure, and it should have been marked. That single artefact is what separates measured progress from assumed progress. A tutor who does all four of these is teaching to the assessment. A tutor who does none is teaching to the clock, and after a month you have no way to tell the difference without them.

sections.heading: Reading a marked IGCSE paper properly
paragraphs: Most parents look at a marked paper and read the total. The total is the least informative number on the page. What matters is the distribution of the lost marks, because four different problems produce four different patterns and they need completely different responses. A paper where marks are missing in ones and twos across every question is a precision problem. A paper where the last two questions are blank is a pacing problem. A paper where a whole topic is wrong is a content gap. A paper where the working is right and the final answer is wrong is an arithmetic habit.

The responses are not interchangeable, and this is where tutoring money is most often wasted. A pacing problem treated as a content gap produces a term of revision and no grade movement, because the student always knew the material and never reached the questions. A precision problem treated with more content coverage produces the same result. Only the marked script distinguishes them, which is why the first session should be spent reading one rather than teaching.

The table below is the diagnostic frame we use, with the realistic number of sessions each pattern needs. The session counts are a planning guide from how these patterns behave in this market, not a promise about any individual student; no honest tutor undertakes to deliver a particular grade, and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching. What the frame does give you is a way to ask a sharper question at the end of week four: which pattern did we have, and has that pattern changed.

sections.heading: Grade movement is lumpy, and the first month is misleading
paragraphs: Parents expect progress to look like a line. It does not. Technique marks move first and fast, because writing to a mark scheme is a skill a competent student can acquire in a handful of sessions. Content gaps move slowly and then suddenly, because a topic half-understood produces no marks until it is understood, at which point a cluster of questions becomes available at once. A tutoring plan read week by week therefore looks flat, then jumps, then flattens again.

This matters practically, because the flat stretch is when families cancel. Four weeks in, the student feels better, the marks have not moved much, and the arrangement looks like a luxury. If the evidence is being gathered properly, that is the moment it earns its keep: a component breakdown can show the precision marks already recovered even when the total has barely shifted, and a timed repeat can show pacing improving before any content has changed.

The reverse case is just as important. If six weeks of evidence shows no movement on any named component, the arrangement is not working, and the honest response is to change something rather than to add hours. Sometimes it is the match: a student who does not talk to this particular adult will not learn from them regardless of subject expertise. Sometimes it is the focus: hours spent on content when the problem was pacing. Occasionally it is the entry itself, and the tier or the syllabus code was wrong all along.

sections.heading: What a useful session note contains
paragraphs: A session note is the cheapest evidence in tutoring and the most commonly missing. It takes a tutor three minutes and it is the only thing that lets a parent follow a term they did not sit through. The useful version is short and specific: the question types covered, the errors that recurred, the single thing to practise before the next session, and anything the school should know. Four lines is plenty. A paragraph of encouragement is not a note.

The specificity is the point. 'Worked on quadratics' tells you nothing, because the student has been working on quadratics since Year 9. 'Completed the square correctly in four of six questions; still dropping the sign on the constant; practise exercise 12 before Tuesday' tells you exactly where the week stands and gives the student something to do. Over a term, twelve notes of that kind are a complete record of what tuition actually addressed.

Notes also protect the arrangement. When a mock comes back worse than expected, the notes show whether the weak component was ever covered. When a tutor changes, the notes let the next one start from the evidence rather than from scratch. And when a parent needs to talk to the school about a tier decision, a run of specific notes is the difference between an opinion and a case. Ask for the note format in the first conversation, before it becomes a complaint in the eighth week.
bullets: Question types covered, named precisely rather than by topic

sections.heading: The school's own evidence, and what it does not show
paragraphs: Before buying any evidence, use the evidence you already have. Three documents exist for every Abu Dhabi student and most families read none of them properly. The school's mock papers and mark breakdowns, which are usually available on request even when only the grade was reported. The school report, which is an opinion with a number attached. And the ADEK inspection report for the school, which is published and which describes teaching quality in named subject areas across the emirate's licensed private schools.

Each tells you something and hides something else. A mock grade hides the component distribution, which is the part that matters. A school report hides whether the grade was awarded against the real mark scheme or against the teacher's expectation of that class. An inspection report describes a whole school and will never describe your child, but it will tell you whether the department you are worried about is a known strength or a known weakness, which changes whether outside help is a supplement or a substitute.

Used together they narrow the problem before you pay anyone. If the inspection report is strong on mathematics and the mock breakdown shows pacing losses, the school can probably fix it and a short block is enough. If a department is a flagged weakness and the breakdown shows content gaps across several topics, outside teaching is doing real work rather than duplicating it. That distinction is worth an hour of reading and is the cheapest thing on this page.

sections.heading: Feedback on a draft, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework or practical components, and this is where evidence and honesty meet. A tutor may teach the skills a component assesses, explain what the criteria reward, discuss a student's own draft, give feedback on it, model a technique on a different task, and practise under timed conditions. A tutor may not write any part of the submitted work, rewrite a draft, supply an answer to be handed in, or edit a piece to the point where the words are no longer the student's.

The distinction is easy to hold in practice and easy to blur in a hurry. Feedback says: this paragraph makes a claim and never supports it, and here is what support looks like in a different example. Ghostwriting says: here is the paragraph. The first produces evidence of learning, because the next draft is better and the improvement is the student's. The second produces a mark that the student cannot repeat under exam conditions, and a malpractice exposure that falls on the candidate rather than on the person who was paid.

Pages ranking for tutoring searches in this market sell completed assessed work outright, with a price attached. Treat that as disqualifying rather than tempting. The same applies to materials: syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to the boards, and a tutor should reference and link them rather than bundle and sell them. A tutor working from the official syllabus for the exact code on your child's statement of entry is doing the job as it is meant to be done.
bullets: Feedback on the student's own draft is teaching; producing text for submission is not
Ask how a draft is handled before the first coursework session

sections.heading: If the evidence does not move, what should happen
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement that is not working should be identifiable in six weeks and changeable in one conversation. The sequence we use is deliberately unglamorous. Read the evidence together: the breakdowns, the notes, the timed repeats. Establish whether the named weak components were actually the ones taught. If they were not, the plan was wrong and the fix is free. If they were and nothing moved, the question becomes whether the match is right.

Match failure is more common than subject-knowledge failure and much less often diagnosed. A fifteen-year-old who will not say 'I do not understand' to a particular adult will spend a term nodding, and no amount of expertise survives that. The signal is usually in the session notes: the same error recurring with no change in how it is described. When that shows up, we change the tutor rather than the schedule, at the same rate, because the alternative is a parent paying for politeness.

Occasionally the evidence points somewhere else entirely: a tier that caps the grade being aimed at, a syllabus code mismatch, an entry for the practical paper when the preparation assumed the alternative, or a student carrying ten subjects where eight would have produced better grades. Those are school conversations rather than tutoring ones, and the run of notes and breakdowns is exactly what makes them productive. Evidence collected weekly is not bureaucracy; it is what turns a worry into a question somebody can answer.

A student who asks something unprompted in a trial will learn from that adult. One who answers politely and offers nothing is a match to reconsider before money changes hands.

process.description: Before the plan starts, the named weak components are written down with the current marks against them. Everything afterwards is measured against that list. Without it, the eighth-week conversation becomes a discussion about feelings, which is the conversation this page exists to avoid.

process.title: Weekly notes, fortnightly repeats
process.description: Each session produces a short note with a practice task. Every second or third session includes a timed set on the question types being fixed, marked and returned with the mark allocation visible. That cadence produces a readable record without turning the tuition into administration.

faqs.question: How soon should we see evidence that IGCSE tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Within four weeks you should hold a marked past paper, a component breakdown, a note from each session and one marked timed repeat. Whether the marks have moved depends on what the problem was. Precision and pacing losses usually improve within two to four sessions, so a timed repeat should show movement by week four. Genuine content gaps take longer and often show nothing for a month, then a cluster of recovered marks at once. What should never happen is week four arriving with nothing written down to look at.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every Abu Dhabi household is taught one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We are direct about that because the alternative is a family discovering it after booking. The upside is real: the tutor is chosen from the whole Gulf timezone on subject expertise rather than from whoever can drive to your community, and the booked hour is not shortened by traffic.

faqs.question: What does a component breakdown of a mock paper actually look like?
faqs.answer: A short list of question types with the marks lost against each, rather than topics. For an Extended maths paper it might read: four method marks unclaimed in show-that questions, six marks lost to arithmetic slips, eight marks blank in the final two questions, no marks lost on substitution. That tells you the student knows the content and is losing marks to habits and pacing, which is a two-to-four session fix. A grade and a comment cannot tell you any of that, which is why the breakdown is worth asking for.

faqs.question: Can we get our child's mock paper breakdown from an Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if you ask specifically. Many schools report a mock as a grade and keep the script, and most will release the marked paper and the mark distribution to a parent who requests them. Ask for the script and the marks per question rather than for feedback, because feedback arrives as prose and the marks arrive as data. If the school marked against the published scheme, the breakdown is directly comparable to what the real series will award, which makes it the most valuable document you can hold.

faqs.question: Our tutor says progress is good but the grades have not moved. What now?
faqs.answer: Ask for the evidence rather than the assessment. Which components were named as weak at the start, what were the marks on them then, and what are they now on a timed repeat. If those numbers do not exist, that is the finding: the arrangement is unmeasured, and six weeks have gone. If they exist and show movement on components while the total has not changed, that is normal and worth continuing. If they exist and show nothing, change the focus or the tutor rather than adding hours to the same plan.

faqs.question: How often should past papers be marked rather than just discussed?
faqs.answer: At least one full paper marked question by question in the first fortnight, then a timed section every second or third session. Discussion of a paper is useful but it tends to concentrate on the questions the student found interesting rather than the ones that cost marks. Marking forces the whole script to be read against the scheme. In the eight weeks before a series the rhythm should tighten to a marked timed section every week, matched to the paper order on the official timetable for the entered board.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring really as effective for a fifteen-year-old as someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE-age students the format rarely decides the outcome; the match and the diagnosis do. What the online format changes is the pool and the record. A household in Al Reef or Al Shamkha can work with an Extended physics specialist rather than the nearest generalist, and the marked papers and notes exist as files by default. What it demands is a quiet room, a working camera and a student willing to write while being watched on screen. Younger children who cannot yet manage that are the genuine exception.

faqs.question: What should a tutor write after each IGCSE session?
faqs.answer: Four lines is enough: the question types covered, the error that recurred in the student's own working, one practice task with a deadline, and anything the school should know. Specificity is the whole value. 'Worked on quadratics' is not a record; 'completed the square correctly in four of six, still dropping the sign on the constant, practise exercise 12 before Tuesday' is. Twelve notes of that kind across a term are a complete account of what the tuition addressed, and they are what makes a tier conversation with the school productive.

faqs.question: Does the ADEK inspection report tell us anything useful about tutoring needs?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, and it is free. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes its findings, including comment on subject areas. The report will never describe your child, but it will tell you whether the department you are worried about is a recognised strength or a flagged weakness. If it is a strength and the mock breakdown shows pacing losses, the school can probably fix it. If it is a weakness and the breakdown shows content gaps, outside teaching is doing real work rather than duplicating the classroom.

faqs.question: How do we know a tutor is marking to the real mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the marks written on the script, question by question, and ask which scheme was used. A paper marked against the board's published scheme for that series shows the allocation: method marks separately from answer marks, and the exact wording the scheme required. A paper marked to an impression shows a total and a comment. The difference is visible in thirty seconds and it decides whether the number you are being given is comparable to what the real series will award.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a coursework draft without crossing the honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor may teach the skills the component assesses, explain what the criteria reward, read the student's own draft and give feedback on it, and model a technique on a different task. A tutor may not write or rewrite any part of the submitted work, supply text to be handed in, or edit a draft until the words are no longer the student's. Ask any prospective tutor how they handle a draft before the first coursework session; the answer separates teachers from suppliers in one sentence.

faqs.question: Our child has six weeks until the papers. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only with a narrow aim. Six weeks is not enough to close several content gaps and is plenty to recover precision and pacing marks, which in most marked scripts are the larger loss anyway. Start from the most recent marked paper, pick the two question types costing the most marks, and work only on those under timed conditions. Build the sequence from the paper order on the correct zone timetable. Broad revision at this point spreads the hours thin and produces nothing you can measure.

faqs.question: Should we switch tutors if the first six weeks produced nothing?
faqs.answer: Check the plan before the person. If the components taught were not the components named as weak, the plan was wrong and a different tutor would have produced the same result. If the right components were taught and nothing moved, look at the session notes for the same error described the same way week after week; that pattern usually means the student is not telling this adult when they are lost. In that case change the tutor at the same rate rather than adding hours, which is the more expensive version of the same problem.

faqs.question: What evidence should we keep for a conversation with the school about tiers?
faqs.answer: A run of marked papers with the mark allocation visible, the component breakdowns showing which question types improved, the session notes with dates, and any timed repeats with before-and-after marks. That package turns a parental opinion into a case a head of department can act on. Tier decisions in this emirate are generally made from Year 10 mock evidence and reviewed before entries close, so the conversation is worth having while the window is open rather than after the entry has been made.

faqs.question: Who holds the evidence if we stop tutoring after one term?
faqs.answer: You should. Ask at the start for the notes and marked papers to be shared with you as they are produced rather than kept in a tutor's own records. Then if the arrangement ends, the component breakdowns and marked scripts go with your child to the next tutor, or to the school, and nothing has to be rediagnosed from scratch. The same applies to your child's personal data: ask what is collected, why it is held and how to have it deleted, and expect a straight answer in writing.

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: The fastest way to make this decision well is to find your child's most recent marked mock, note the four-digit syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry, and send both. A specialist can tell you from the script alone whether you are looking at a precision problem, a pacing problem or a content gap, and those three need different plans and different budgets. Then take the free trial lesson, one per family with no card details taken, and watch whether your child asks a question unprompted. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, for households anywhere in Abu Dhabi, with a written note after every session.

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects to Abu Dhabi families over live video. Each works from the specification code rather than a subject label, and each leaves written evidence after a session, because a tutor you cannot audit is a tutor you are taking on trust for two years.

intro.heading: An online lesson can be audited; a room usually cannot
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this market describes its tutors in adjectives. Experienced, qualified, passionate, highly rated. None of those words can be checked by a parent before money changes hands, which is why the search for the best IGCSE online tutor in Abu Dhabi usually ends in a guess dressed as a decision. There is a better test available, and it is specific to the format: an online lesson generates artefacts. Annotated papers, a shared board, a written note, a recording where one is agreed. A parent who knows what to collect can judge a tutor on what the lessons produced rather than on what the website promised.

This is a real asymmetry between formats. A visiting tutor works on paper that stays in the student's folder, explains something on a page that gets filed, and leaves. The only record is the student's memory and the tutor's verbal summary at the door. A video lesson with a shared document does the same teaching but leaves the working behind in a form you can open on a Sunday evening without asking anybody's permission. That is not a marketing advantage, it is an accountability one, and it is the honest reason to prefer the format rather than any claim about engagement.

What this page does, then, is set out the evidence an online IGCSE plan should produce and how to read it. It walks through an hour minute by minute, because what happens inside the hour determines what comes out of it. It deals with the two things parents most doubt about teaching through a screen: how mathematical working and scientific diagrams get done, and what happens to practical science when nobody is in a laboratory. Then it shows what four weeks of evidence looks like, and where the trap is in reading it.

After that come the parts that make a decision rather than describe one. Published market rates in AED with the source named beside each band, so you can place any quote you receive. A comparison of the three online models an Abu Dhabi family can buy from, which differ more than their websites suggest. And the question nobody in this market writes about: what happens to the recordings, screenshots and shared documents, given that they contain a minor's face, voice and schoolwork.

Two statements of fact before the detail. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform; it holds no approval from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and it operates no premises in the UAE. Tuition for families here is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, where ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Visiting tutors are a service available only in India. Every AED figure below is a published market rate attributed to its source rather than a price list.

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: IGCSE is not one qualification but several related ones, and which route your child is on changes what an online tutor should be doing in the hour. These are the four routes Abu Dhabi families most often need covered, described by what the evidence of progress looks like in each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The lower of the two tiers in tiered subjects, with a capped top grade and a narrower content range. Progress evidence here is unusually clean, because the papers reward completeness: most Core candidates lose grades by leaving questions unattempted rather than by answering them wrongly. A month of lessons should show the proportion of a paper attempted rising before anything else changes, and that is measurable from the scripts without any interpretation.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, Core entries are common where a child joined mid-key-stage from a different system and was placed on the evidence of unfamiliar coursework. Families in this position should ask the subject lead, in writing, what evidence the tier rests on. Online tuition suits the Core brief well, because the work is repetition of attempted questions under timing rather than new content delivery.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: The full content range with the top grades available, and the tier where most Abu Dhabi tuition demand sits. Evidence of progress is slower to appear and easier to misread, because Extended papers punish one error in a multi-step chain. A student can improve substantially in method while their raw total barely moves for three weeks, then jump. That pattern is normal and is the single biggest reason families stop tuition one month too early.
programmes.countryNote: Extended science and Additional Mathematics are the codes where local tutor supply in the emirate thins out fastest, which is the practical argument for the online format in this market. A family in Al Falah or Al Shamkha filtering by drive time will find three available tutors; filtering by who has taught the specification to candidates who sat the papers returns a different and better list.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: A separate specification family with its own codes, paper structures and grading on a 9 to 1 scale. Several Abu Dhabi schools enter candidates with Pearson in some subjects and Cambridge in others, which means one child can be preparing for two different paper conventions in the same term. Evidence of progress has to be read per board, because a mark out of 100 on a Pearson paper is not comparable to one on a Cambridge paper.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and its International GCSE exams run in May/June and November; November 2026's final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. For an Abu Dhabi family, that second series is a genuine option for a single retake subject, and the evidence to decide it on is the marked summer script rather than a general sense that the grade was disappointing.

programmes.name: IGCSE into A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The transition where IGCSE grades become entry conditions and the content gap becomes visible. A strong IGCSE grade in maths does not guarantee a comfortable start in an analysis course, because the step up is in abstraction rather than difficulty. Evidence here is about readiness rather than grades: can the student work through an unfamiliar multi-step problem without being prompted at each stage?
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi offers both routes widely, with A Level and Diploma options sometimes available inside the same school group. For families using IGCSE certificates in the UAE system afterwards, the Ministry of Education's British-track requirement is five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus Advanced Level or Advanced Subsidiary study. That count is worth confirming before any subject is dropped.

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask us to cover online, described by what the screen actually does for each one. The honest test of the format is subject by subject: in some it is plainly better than paper, in one or two it has a limitation worth stating.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 0980, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The strongest case for the format. A shared whiteboard shows the student's working line by line as it is written, so the tutor intervenes at the line where the error entered rather than after the wrong answer appears. The annotated page saves, which means a parent can compare week three's algebra with week one's without asking anybody.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 0971, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Calculation chains work well on a shared board; the limitation is apparatus handling, which no video call reproduces. Candidates sitting the alternative to practical lose little, since that paper is written reasoning about experiments. Candidates sitting the timed practical need the school's laboratory time, and the online work supports recording conventions rather than replacing bench practice.

subjects.name: Physics (0625, 0972, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Circuit diagrams and ray diagrams draw more accurately on a tablet layer than on squared paper, and both participants see the same lines. The subject's recurring losses are in graph axis choice and in significant figures carried through, both of which are visible on screen while they happen and correctable in the moment rather than a week later.

subjects.name: Biology (0610, 0970, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: A high-volume content subject where the screen helps mainly through retrieval: short written answers typed or handwritten live, marked against the criteria immediately. Data-interpretation questions suit a shared document, because the tutor can point at the figure the student should have quoted instead of describing where it is.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500, 0990)
subjects.description: Responds faster to online tuition than any other subject, because the work is drafting and the draft is already a document. Audience, register and structure are taught by editing in view, with the student making every change. The summary task improves measurably within a few sessions once compression is practised against the word limit.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Reading and note-making tasks work well on screen. The speaking component is where to ask a direct question, because 0510 and 0511 differ in how speaking is handled, and a tutor who has not checked which variant a school entered is preparing the wrong thing. Live video is a reasonable rehearsal space for the spoken task itself.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: A thin-supply code in this emirate, which is why online matching matters most here. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive without the scaffolding of the main syllabus, and the useful evidence of progress is whether the student can start an unfamiliar question unprompted, not whether they can follow a worked solution.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: The format's natural home. Pseudocode, trace tables and the programming element are all screen-native, and a shared editor means the tutor watches the logic form rather than reading a finished answer. Validation against verification and incomplete trace tables are the two marks most reliably recovered within a month.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Diagram subjects where a drawing layer earns its place: axes, a shifted curve and a labelled new equilibrium drawn by the student, corrected in view. Evaluation answers need a position held across a paragraph, which is best taught by editing the student's own paragraph rather than modelling a better one.

sections.heading: What a claim about being the best online tutor would actually require
paragraphs: The word in the search is doing a lot of work and almost none of it is checkable. Every provider competing for this phrase says some version of the same thing, and the cluster is unusually weak on substantiation: of the pages researched in this market, several publish self-asserted star ratings, one shows two different review totals on the same page, and one claims a student count that its own review count contradicts. A parent cannot distinguish between those pages by reading them harder.

The alternative is to convert each claim into the thing it would require, and then test that in a thirty-minute trial. A claim about examiner experience requires a current role that can be described specifically; a claim about specification knowledge requires the tutor to tell you, unprompted, which practical paper your child sits and what it rewards; a claim about results requires marked scripts that are not the tutor's property to show, which is why the honest version is a method rather than a statistic. None of these tests is difficult. They are simply not the questions most trials are built around.

The table below sets out five claims in the order you are likely to meet them, with what each would require and what a weak answer sounds like. Used in a trial lesson, it takes about four minutes and it is the single highest-return use of a free session. The rest of the session should be spent watching your child work, because a tutor who is impressive to a parent and inert with a fifteen-year-old is the most common expensive mistake in this market.

sections.heading: An online IGCSE hour, minute by minute
paragraphs: Families who doubt the format usually picture a lecture on a screen, and they are right to doubt that. A video lesson where the tutor talks and the student watches fails faster than the same lesson would in a room, because a screen makes passivity easy and invisible. A video lesson where the student works for most of the hour while the tutor watches the working appear is a different thing entirely, and the difference is structural rather than a matter of effort.

A useful hour has a shape. The first five minutes are a check on the week: the repeat question set from last time, marked or unmarked, and whether it was attempted. Minutes five to fifteen are a worked diagnosis on one question the student got wrong, with the student holding the pen on the shared board and the tutor interrupting at the line where the error enters rather than at the end. Minutes fifteen to forty are the student attempting similar questions, timed, with the tutor silent for stretches and intervening only on a pattern. The next ten minutes are marking against the published scheme, out loud, criterion by criterion, so the student hears what a mark is awarded for. The last five set the next repeat set and write the note.

That shape is worth asking a prospective tutor about directly, because it exposes a great deal. A tutor who intends to talk for fifty minutes will describe their explanations. A tutor who intends to make your child work will describe the question sets. In the trial, watch the clock against one measure: how many minutes of the thirty did your child spend writing? Under five is a warning, whatever else the session felt like.

sections.heading: Diagrams, graphs and working: the mechanics parents actually worry about
paragraphs: The most common objection to the format is practical rather than pedagogical: maths and science are drawn, and drawing on a screen sounds worse than drawing on paper. The honest answer is that it depends entirely on the setup, and that a tutor who has solved this will tell you about hardware in the first five minutes without being asked.

Three setups work. A graphics tablet or stylus on the tutor's side plus the student writing on paper held in view of a second camera or a phone stand is the cheapest and is perfectly adequate. A stylus on both sides, writing into the same shared document, is better, because the two sets of working sit on one page and the annotations stay attached to the question. A document camera pointed at the student's paper is the best for science, since graph plotting on squared paper is hard to replicate digitally and the plotting itself is where the marks are.

What does not work is a laptop camera pointed at a face while the student writes on a desk the tutor cannot see. That arrangement reduces the lesson to a conversation about maths, which is exactly the version of online tuition that gives the format its reputation. The question to ask before a trial is specific: how will the tutor see my child's working as it is written? A tutor who answers with a named tool and a fallback has done this before. A tutor who says the student can hold the page up afterwards has not, and the whole diagnostic value of the hour is lost, because an error found after the answer is finished is a correction rather than a repair.

sections.heading: Practical science when nobody is in the laboratory
paragraphs: This is where the format has a genuine limit, and saying so is more useful than talking around it. Cambridge science candidates sit one of two practical routes, decided by the school: Paper 5, a timed practical with real apparatus, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which is written reasoning about experiments the candidate has not performed. Which route your child sits changes what online tuition can and cannot do for them, and it is the first thing to establish.

For an alternative-to-practical candidate, the limitation is close to nil. The paper tests observation language, variable control, data processing and justified conclusions, all of which are written skills that a shared document teaches well. The marks that go missing are specific and learnable: observations described vaguely rather than in testable terms, a control variable named instead of explained, a conclusion drawn beyond what the data supports, and anomalies ignored rather than identified. A bank of tested sentences built over four sessions is worth real marks here.

For a timed-practical candidate the position is different. Bench technique needs bench time, and that comes from the school laboratory, not from a tutor of any kind. What online work can do is everything around the apparatus: the recording conventions, the table layout with units in the headers, significant figures carried consistently, graph scales chosen so the plotted range fills the grid, and reading the question's instruction about how many readings to take. Those are a large share of the available marks and they are routinely lost by students who handle the equipment competently. The honest framing is that online tuition covers the paper's written demands and the school covers the apparatus.

sections.heading: The four things you should be holding after a month
paragraphs: Tuition becomes auditable the moment it produces documents, and online delivery produces them as a by-product rather than as an extra task. After four weekly sessions a family should hold four kinds of evidence, and the absence of any one of them is a more reliable warning sign than anything a tutor says about progress.

The first is annotated work: the shared pages from each session, with the student's working and the tutor's marks on them in sequence. The second is session notes, one per lesson, each naming the component worked on, what was wrong with the attempt, and the specific task set for the week. The third is a marked repeat attempt, meaning the same question type attempted again under timed conditions and scored, because that is the only artefact that shows movement rather than activity. The fourth is a named next target, which should be narrower at week four than it was at week one.

Read the set together rather than individually. Four notes that name four different topics describe a tour of the syllabus. Four notes that name the same component and show a score rising on repeated attempts describe a repair. Four annotated pages with no repeat attempt anywhere in them describe lessons that happened. And if the notes exist but are written in general praise, ask for one to be rewritten with the criterion named; a tutor who marks against the published scheme can do that in a minute, and a tutor who marks by impression cannot do it at all.

sections.heading: Reading four weeks of marks without fooling yourself
paragraphs: Progress data over a short run is noisy, and the noise flatters whichever story you were already inclined to believe. Two scores a week apart tell you almost nothing: paper difficulty varies, a tired Thursday looks like a regression, and a question type the student happens to have revised looks like a breakthrough. Families stop paying for tuition that was working, and continue paying for tuition that was not, on the strength of exactly this kind of two-point comparison.

The readable signal is narrower and duller: the error rate on one repeated question type, attempted under the same conditions, over four or more attempts. If a student loses method marks on 'show that' questions in three attempts out of four in week one and one in four by week four, that is progress, and it will show up in a real paper eventually even if this month's mock total went down. Conversely, a total that rises while the same component keeps failing usually means the paper was easier, not that the problem moved.

The second thing to hold steady is conditions. A repeat attempt done at home, untimed, with the textbook open, is not comparable to a timed one. Ask for the attempts to be timed and for the conditions to be written on the note. The third is patience in a specific window: on the Extended tier, method improvement precedes mark improvement by two to three weeks, because the papers only reward a chain that completes. Week three is the point of maximum temptation to conclude it is not working, and it is the worst available moment to judge.

sections.heading: What online IGCSE tuition costs in this market, and who published the figures
paragraphs: Rates in this market are quoted inconsistently and often not at all, which makes any single quote hard to place. Published UAE figures run roughly as follows. Budget online tutoring, usually university students, is advertised from about AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with some platforms quoting from the low AED 30s. Qualified subject tutors online sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300; one UAE agency publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, with the travel inside the rate, is quoted between roughly AED 180 and AED 500. IGCSE, IB and A Level specialists are quoted between about AED 200 and AED 450, with one UK-based agency publishing AED 270. Named premium tutors reach AED 650.

Monthly shapes are also published: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Rate aggregators estimate monthly totals for a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. These are other organisations' published figures, dated to 2026, and they are reproduced here so a parent has a reference band rather than as our price list.

What the bands do not tell you is what is inside the hour, and that is where comparison usually goes wrong. One quote at AED 220 includes marked work between sessions and a written note; another at the same price is sixty minutes of conversation with nothing produced. Before comparing two numbers, ask each provider the same three questions: who marks the work between sessions, what the family receives in writing afterwards, and what happens if the match is wrong. The spread in answers is wider than the spread in prices.

sections.heading: Platform, agency or independent tutor: three online models compared
paragraphs: Online tutoring in this market is sold through three structures that look similar from the outside and behave very differently once something goes wrong. A platform lists tutors and handles scheduling and payment, with the relationship largely between family and tutor. An agency matches and manages, taking responsibility for the match and usually for replacing it. An independent tutor found through a community group or a classified listing is a direct arrangement with no intermediary at all.

The differences that matter are not price. They are: who is accountable when the match is wrong, who verifies the tutor's permit, what happens to continuity if the tutor takes a new full-time job in March, and whether anybody is marking work between sessions. An independent arrangement is often the cheapest hour and carries all four risks in full; the trade is real and can be worth making with the right person. A platform usually solves scheduling and payment and solves accountability least. An agency charges more for the layer that handles replacement and verification, and a parent should ask exactly what that layer does rather than assume it.

Our own position is stated in the table rather than implied around it, including where it is a limitation. IB Gram matches families to tutors, runs lessons one-to-one over live video, and swaps a tutor on request when the first match does not work. It does not operate premises in the UAE, does not hold approval from any regulator or examination board, and does not send tutors to UAE addresses. A comparison worth reading is one where the writer's own row has a weakness in it, and these are ours.

sections.heading: Recordings, shared documents and a minor's data
paragraphs: An online lesson produces a record, and a record of a fifteen-year-old's face, voice, handwriting and school performance is personal data about a child. The UAE has a federal personal data protection framework, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, and the sensible posture for a family is to treat lesson recordings as something to decide about deliberately rather than to accept as a default setting.

Three questions settle most of it. Is the session recorded at all, and does the student know? Where is the recording stored, and for how long before it is deleted? Who else can see the shared document, and can it be exported? A tutor or provider who answers those clearly has thought about it. A provider who cannot say where recordings live is telling you something useful. It is also worth asking what is collected at enquiry stage: a form that asks for a child's school, year group, grades and a photograph should say what each field is for and how to have it removed.

Recordings have genuine value, which is why this is a decision rather than a refusal. A student revising in May can rewatch the session where the moles method was explained, and a parent can see what an hour actually contained. The workable compromise most families land on is to record the worked-example portion and not the whole session, keep the shared annotated document as the permanent artefact, and agree a deletion point such as the end of the series. Written agreement beats a verbal one, and the student should be part of the conversation rather than its subject.
bullets: Ask whether sessions are recorded, where recordings are stored and when they are deleted
Keep the annotated document as the lasting artefact; it carries less personal data than video
Ask what each field on an enquiry form is for, and how to have the data removed
Include the student in the decision; it is their face and their work

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the practical route
process.description: Three facts from the statement of entry or the subject lead: the four-digit specification code, the tier where the subject is tiered, and whether the science route is the timed practical or the alternative to practical. With those, the first session diagnoses instead of interviewing, and the match is made on specification rather than on availability.

process.title: A free trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Thirty minutes at no charge with the matched tutor, no card details taken, one trial per family. Watch two things only: how many minutes your child spends writing, and whether the tutor names a criterion when marking an answer. Those two observations predict the next six months better than any conversation about method.

process.title: Agree how the working will be seen
process.description: Before the first paid session, settle the hardware question: a stylus, a phone on a stand over the page, or a document camera. The requirement is that the tutor sees the working as it is written rather than after it is finished, because an error caught at the line it entered is a repair and one caught at the end is a correction.

process.title: Four sessions, then a judgement
process.description: The first block is four sessions ending in a marked repeat attempt on the same question type that was diagnosed in week one. At that point you hold a before and an after and can decide properly. If the evidence has not moved and the tutor cannot say why, we match again rather than sell you a fifth session.

process.title: Narrow the target, review against the timetable
process.description: From week five the named target should get narrower rather than broader, and the plan is checked against the board's live timetable for the entered series. Hours move off a component once it stops losing marks. A plan that is still working across the whole syllabus in week ten is not a plan.

whyPoints.title: Judged on artefacts rather than adjectives
whyPoints.description: Every session leaves an annotated page and a written note naming the component and the week's task. After a month you hold four of each plus a marked repeat attempt, which is enough to decide whether the tuition is working without relying on anybody's description of progress, including ours.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the published scheme, out loud
whyPoints.description: Work is marked to the board's criteria with the criterion named, so the student hears what a mark is awarded for rather than whether the answer was good. This is the habit that transfers to the exam hall, and it is the clearest difference between specification teaching and general subject help.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the code, not on who is free
whyPoints.description: A 0606 or 4CH1 specialist is found among tutors who have prepared candidates for those papers, anywhere in the Gulf timezone. For families in Al Falah, Al Shamkha and the southern mainland this is the difference between a specialist and whoever could reach the villa by seven.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are other organisations' published figures with the publisher named, dated to 2026. Three of the six pages competing for searches like this publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. A reference band is more useful to a parent than another promise.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, marks against criteria and gives written feedback on the student's own draft. Nobody here will produce assessed work on a candidate's behalf, in any subject. One page competing in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments, and the malpractice consequence of that falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent platform with no approval from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, no premises in the UAE, and no self-published rating. Competing pages in this market show conflicting review totals on a single page; the honest alternative is a free trial and evidence you can read yourself.

faqs.question: How can I judge an online IGCSE tutor before paying for a single session?
faqs.answer: Use the free trial as a test rather than an introduction. Ask one specification question the tutor cannot answer generically, such as which practical paper your child sits and what that paper rewards. Ask them to mark one answer out loud and name the criterion they are awarding against. Then stop watching the tutor and watch your child: count the minutes they spend writing. Under five minutes in a thirty-minute trial is a warning, however impressive the explanations were. Finally, ask what documents you will hold after four weeks, and expect a specific list.

faqs.question: How will the tutor see my child's working if the lesson is over video?
faqs.answer: This has to be settled before the first paid session, because it determines whether the hour diagnoses anything. Three setups work: a stylus on a shared document for both sides, a phone on a stand pointed at your child's paper, or a document camera over the page. The requirement is that the tutor watches the working appear, not that they see it afterwards. A laptop camera pointed at your child's face while they write on an unseen desk turns the session into a conversation about the subject, which is the version of online tuition that deserves its poor reputation.

faqs.question: What should I actually have in my hands after four weeks of online tuition?
faqs.answer: Four annotated session pages showing your child's working with the tutor's marks on it, four written notes each naming the component worked on and the task set for the week, at least one marked repeat attempt at the same question type under timed conditions, and a named next target that is narrower than the one set in week one. Read them as a set. Four notes naming four unrelated topics describe a tour of the syllabus. Four notes naming one component with a rising score on repeated attempts describe a repair that is working.

faqs.question: My child's mock mark went down after a month of tuition. Does that mean it is not working?
faqs.answer: Possibly not, and a single comparison cannot tell you. Paper difficulty varies, question-type mix varies, and a tired afternoon reads as a regression. The signal to look at instead is the error rate on the one question type being targeted, across four or more timed attempts. If method errors on that type are falling while the overall total wobbles, the work is landing. On the Extended tier, method improvement usually shows up two to three weeks before mark improvement, because those papers only reward a chain that completes. Week three is the worst moment to judge.

faqs.question: Can science practical skills be taught properly if my child never handles apparatus with the tutor?
faqs.answer: It depends which route the school entered. An alternative-to-practical candidate loses almost nothing, because that paper is written reasoning about experiments: observation language, variable control, data processing, justified conclusions. All of that teaches well on a shared document. A timed-practical candidate needs bench time, and that comes from the school laboratory. What online work covers for them is everything around the apparatus: table layout, units in the headers, significant figures, graph scales and reading the instruction about how many readings to take. Those carry a large share of the marks students lose.

faqs.question: Is an online tutor cheaper than a visiting tutor in Abu Dhabi, and by how much?
faqs.answer: Published UAE figures put qualified subject tutors online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 500, with rate aggregators quoting AED 180 to AED 350 and home tutors AED 200 to AED 500. The gap is travel rather than teaching. The second difference is reliability of the start time: a tutor driving to Al Shamkha at six cannot hold a 6.30pm slot consistently, and the slot that slips is usually the one nearest the exam. Those are market figures from other organisations, not IB Gram's charges.

faqs.question: Should sessions be recorded, and what happens to the recording afterwards?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a decision rather than a default. A recording of a lesson contains a child's face, voice, handwriting and performance, and the UAE has a federal personal data protection framework under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021. Ask three questions: is it recorded, where is it stored, and when is it deleted. Many families settle on recording only the worked-example portion, keeping the annotated document as the lasting artefact, and agreeing deletion at the end of the series. Put it in writing, and include your child in the conversation rather than deciding over them.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a tutoring platform and a matching service for an Abu Dhabi family?
faqs.answer: A platform lists tutors and handles scheduling and payment, leaving the match and its consequences largely with you. A matching service takes responsibility for the match and usually for replacing it, and charges for that layer. The questions that separate them are not about price: who is accountable when the match is wrong, who asked to see the tutor's permit, what happens to continuity if the tutor takes a full-time job in March, and whether anyone marks work between sessions. Ask all four of any provider and compare the answers rather than the hourly rates.

faqs.question: How many minutes of a session should my child be talking or writing rather than listening?
faqs.answer: Most of it. A workable shape is five minutes checking last week's set, ten minutes diagnosing one wrong question with the student holding the pen, twenty-five minutes of timed attempts with the tutor mostly silent, ten minutes of marking aloud against the criteria, and five minutes setting the next set and writing the note. That puts the student active for roughly forty of the sixty minutes. A session where the tutor explains for fifty minutes feels productive to a parent listening from the next room and leaves almost nothing behind.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching my child online from outside the UAE still need a permit?
faqs.answer: The UAE requirement applies to private tutoring provided in the country: under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues a private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years, and those offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. For a UAE-resident tutor, online or in person, ask to see it; because it costs nothing, there is no excuse for not holding one. For a tutor based abroad, the position differs, so ask the provider directly what verification they carry out instead.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects benefit most from being taught over video?
faqs.answer: Computer Science is the natural fit, since pseudocode, trace tables and programming are screen-native and a shared editor shows logic forming rather than finished. English First Language responds fastest, because drafting is already a document and editing in view teaches audience and structure. Mathematics works very well with a shared board, where the tutor intervenes at the line the error entered. The subject needing most care is a science with the timed practical route, where bench technique has to come from the school and online work covers the written demands around it.

faqs.question: What if my child will not engage with a tutor on a screen?
faqs.answer: Some will not, and it is worth finding out in a free trial rather than three paid sessions in. The usual cause is format rather than medium: a session built around explanation gives a teenager nothing to do, and a teenager with nothing to do disengages faster on video than in a room. Before concluding the medium is wrong, try one session structured around the student working with the tutor largely silent. If engagement still fails, say so and we match again; a different adult sometimes fixes what no amount of technique will.

faqs.question: How do I compare two quotes that are the same price but describe different things?
faqs.answer: Ask both providers the same three questions and write the answers down. Who marks work between sessions, and against what. What does the family receive in writing after each lesson. What happens if the match is wrong, and who pays for the change. One quote at AED 220 may include marked papers and a written note; another at the same figure may be an hour of conversation with nothing produced. In this market the spread in what is inside the hour is considerably wider than the spread in the hourly rates themselves.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting online tuition with six weeks left before the series?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the scope is narrow. Six weeks is not enough to learn a subject and is enough to stop one specific leak: finishing papers within the time, writing method lines before answers, handling one recurring question type, or building the observation vocabulary an alternative-to-practical paper rewards. That work is worth real marks, and on a 9 to 1 scale a few marks can cross a boundary. Bring the most recent marked mock and expect an honest recommendation for a short block of two to six sessions rather than a term.

faqs.question: Can the same online tutor teach two of my children on different evenings?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is often sensible when the subjects are related, because the tutor already knows the household's rhythm and can keep notes in one place. The limit is specification depth: a tutor strong in Extended maths for a Year 11 may not be the right person for a Year 10 sitting a different board in a science. The practical approach is to match each child on their own code and tier, then check whether the same name comes up twice. Scheduling siblings consecutively on one evening tends to hold better than splitting them across the week.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school before I start paying for tuition at all?
faqs.answer: Four things, in one email to the subject lead. Which specification code and tier is my child entered for, and what would change the tier. Which practical route applies in each science. What catch-up or clinic provision does the school already run, and is my child attending it. And which component does the department think is costing the most marks. Schools answer specific questions properly, the provision is often free, and the answers make any tutoring you then buy narrower and cheaper than it would otherwise have been.

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Take the trial, then read the evidence
abu-dhabi/best-igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: Judging the best IGCSE online tutor in Abu Dhabi does not require a leap of faith, because the format leaves a trail. Start with the free trial, one per family and no card details taken, and watch two things: how long your child spends writing, and whether the tutor names a criterion when marking. Then run four sessions and read what they produced, annotated pages, written notes and a marked repeat attempt on the same question type. If the evidence has moved, continue. If it has not and nobody can say why, change tutor. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the emirate.
