intro.heading: The real question behind "best IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi" is a price question
paragraphs: Almost every Abu Dhabi parent who types this search has already had one conversation about money. A neighbour pays AED 180 an hour. A colleague at the same school pays AED 420 for what sounds like the same lesson. Nothing on the first page of Google explains the gap, because three of the six pages ranking for this query publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family here transacts in. So the search for the best IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi turns into guesswork, and guesswork in an exam year is expensive in a way that has nothing to do with hourly rates.

The honest answer is that there is no single market rate. There is a band, and your position inside that band is set by four things: how niche the subject is, whether the tutor is teaching Core or Extended, how close the June or November series is, and whether anybody has to drive. The last of those is the one nobody prices out loud. A tutor who travels to Al Reef for a 5pm session is selling you ninety minutes of their evening for a sixty-minute lesson, and that cost sits inside the rate whether or not it is itemised on the invoice.

This page prices all four factors using figures that were published by UAE providers and rate aggregators, with the source named in the table. None of them is our price list. IB Gram matches families to tutors and runs the first lesson free, so what you pay is agreed after you have seen the tutor teach your child rather than before. That sequence matters more than any number here: a cheap tutor who does not know that 0620 Paper 6 is the alternative-to-practical paper will cost you a grade, and a grade is not recoverable with money in August.

What follows is arranged for a parent making a decision this week. First the market bands, then the six things that move your quote, then the Core-versus-Extended decision that changes your total bill more than any hourly rate does. After that, the subjects where marks actually leak, a comparison of online against in-home and group tuition with the travel reality of this city built in, a two-year cost model, and the checks you can run on a tutor's right to work before you pay anybody anything. Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, and the inspection report on your child's school is public reading that will shape how much help they actually need. Read the rate table first, then the tier section, and the rest of the page will cost you less to act on.
bullets: Published bands run from roughly AED 45 an hour for university-student tutors to AED 650 for named premium tutors; IGCSE specialists cluster at AED 150-450
Extended tier costs more to tutor than Core because the content is wider and the paper set is harder, not because tutors charge a surcharge for it
In-home rates in the UAE carry the travel inside them: published in-home bands sit roughly AED 30-150 above comparable online rates
Entry deadlines for a series close months before the exam, so a late start costs availability rather than money
The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and valid for two years, which means a tutor who cannot show one has no cost excuse

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi families arrive at IGCSE from three directions: a British-curriculum primary, an Aldar or GEMS school running Cambridge Lower Secondary, or an IB MYP school where Year 11 becomes the switch point. The stage your child is at changes what tutoring is for, and what it should cost.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, ending in Checkpoint tests that Cambridge runs in March, May and October. Checkpoint is not a public qualification and no university will ever see it, but it is the cleanest early read you will get on whether your child is heading for Core or Extended in maths and science. Tutoring at this stage is cheap because the content is narrow, and it is the only point where you can fix an algebra gap without an exam deadline pressing on it.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi this is where the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor schools stream earliest, often setting maths groups in Year 8. A parent who waits for the Year 10 report to act is usually paying two years later for a gap that was visible in a Year 8 Checkpoint breakdown. Rates at this level sit at the lower end of every published band.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined in June or November. Cambridge runs two grading systems in parallel: the A*-G syllabuses such as 0580 Maths and 0620 Chemistry, and the 9-1 versions such as 0980 and 0971. The content is the same; the grade scale and the certificate are not. Your child's statement of entry carries the four-digit code, and that code is the single most useful thing you can send a tutor before a first lesson.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has British-curriculum schools entering both Cambridge and Pearson, sometimes in the same family of subjects. A tutor who assumes Cambridge when the school entered Pearson 4PH1 will teach the right physics to the wrong paper structure. Ask the school which board, not which subject, and put the answer in the first email you send any tutor in this emirate.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international GCSE runs in May/June and November each year, graded 9-1, with codes such as 4MA1 for Maths A, 4PH1 for Physics and 4EA1 for English Language A. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for future series ahead of the final version, which is why a tutoring plan should be built from the live official timetable rather than from dates copied off a blog. The question paper structure differs from Cambridge's in ways that change revision order.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools entering Pearson also offer a November resit route, and the published pattern is instructive: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. A family planning a resit needs that gap in the calendar before they plan the tutoring.

programmes.name: The step into AS and A Level
programmes.description: IGCSE grades decide which A Level subjects a school will let a student take, and the published entry bars in Abu Dhabi schools are usually a grade 7 or an A in the subject, sometimes a 6 with conditions. That makes the final six months of Year 11 a gatekeeping period rather than just an exam period. Tutoring aimed at moving a 6 to a 7 in one subject is often better value than general support across four.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count of five, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Verify your own case on the ministry's channel before assuming it.

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families ask for most, with the syllabus code and the component where the marks usually go missing. Rates vary by subject for one reason only: how many tutors in the Gulf timezone can teach it to the top of the Extended tier.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 0980, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most tutored subject in the emirate and the cheapest per hour because supply is deep. Extended marks leak in algebraic manipulation under time pressure, vectors, and the 'show that' questions where method marks are available and never claimed. Core candidates lose grade 5 by leaving the last two questions blank rather than by failing to understand them.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 0972, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Scarcer tutors, so rates sit higher. The practical paper is where plans fall apart: Cambridge candidates sit either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and the two need completely different preparation. Marks go in graph scales, significant figures, and describing a control variable rather than naming one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 0971, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and moles calculations dominate the tutoring requests. A common Abu Dhabi pattern is a student who can name every functional group and cannot carry a mole ratio through a two-step calculation. Paper 6 answers lose marks for describing an observation as a conclusion, which is a writing habit rather than a chemistry gap.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 0970, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Deceptively heavy on precise vocabulary. Extended candidates lose marks for writing 'the plant takes in water' where the mark scheme wants osmosis named with the direction of the gradient. Data-handling questions on enzyme and transpiration experiments are reliably the lowest-scoring section in mocks across this market.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: Chosen by students who need science without three separate subjects. Tutoring is awkward because one tutor rarely covers all three disciplines to Extended depth, so families often split it. Worth pricing as two half-subjects rather than one, which is usually the cheaper and more honest arrangement.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500 / 0990, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading summary are the two components where a competent writer still drops a grade. Summary marks are lost by paraphrasing in the source's order instead of selecting; directed writing marks are lost by ignoring the audience named in the task. Both are teachable in a handful of sessions, which makes this good value.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0991)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with a different mark scheme, and the one most often mis-entered. Speaking is assessed separately and the exercise types reward accuracy over range. For Abu Dhabi students arriving mid-cycle from another system, this is frequently the correct entry rather than 0500.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Both reward structure over content. Marks are lost in the evaluation strands, where candidates explain two sides and never reach a judgement supported by the case material. Tutoring here is almost entirely essay-shape work with past-paper command terms, so it tends to need fewer hours than the sciences.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: 0478 is theory plus algorithmic thinking with pseudocode; 0417 is a practical qualification with document and spreadsheet tasks. Parents regularly book the wrong one. Marks go in trace tables and in the practical papers where a single unformatted field loses the mark the task was testing.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language (0508 / 0544)
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum, and the two Cambridge syllabuses are not interchangeable. Students entered for 0544 who have been taught as first-language speakers lose marks on register; the reverse costs far more. Confirm the code before booking a tutor for this subject.

abu-dhabi/best-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi tutoring is a logistics problem before it is an academic one. The emirate's school population is spread across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and the newer mainland communities, and the distance between them is what makes in-home tuition expensive here. These notes are about time, not geography.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Dense in British and American curriculum families, with several large school campuses inside a few kilometres. The school run clears late enough that a 4pm start is rarely realistic; 5.30pm and 7pm are the slots that actually get kept, which is exactly what online scheduling makes easy.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Far enough out that an in-home tutor is pricing a forty-minute drive each way into a one-hour lesson. Families here are the clearest case for online delivery: the saving is not a discount, it is the travel that never happens.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Villa communities feeding mainly British-curriculum schools, with a strong IGCSE cohort in Years 10 and 11. Siblings often need different subjects at the same hour, which a video schedule handles and a single visiting tutor cannot.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Smaller cohort, high proportion of students at island schools offering both British and IB routes. Requests here skew towards single-subject specialists at Extended tier, which is the part of the market where tutor supply is thinnest and rates sit highest.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living with newer school capacity nearby. Evening traffic across the bridges is the deciding factor for anyone considering a visiting tutor; a 6pm in-home booking routinely becomes a 6.25pm start.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring actually costs in Abu Dhabi, with the sources
paragraphs: Published hourly rates for IGCSE tutoring in the UAE run from roughly AED 45 to above AED 650, and the spread is real rather than a negotiating position. The low end is university students and large online marketplaces working at volume. The top end is named premium tutors with a long public record. IGCSE subject specialists, which is what most Year 10 and Year 11 families are actually buying, cluster between AED 150 and AED 450 an hour depending on subject scarcity and tier.

The table below sets out the bands with the publisher beside each one, because an unattributed price is worth nothing to a parent comparing quotes. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table is the most complete public source for the in-home and specialist bands; the lower online bands come from the published starting rates of UAE online providers. These are market figures for the emirate's price level, not IB Gram's charges. We agree a rate with a family after a free trial lesson, which is deliberately the other way round from a published price list.

Two things are worth noticing in the numbers. The in-home band sits above the comparable online band at every tier, and the gap is roughly the cost of a tutor's travel time rather than a quality premium. And the monthly package figures move more than the hourly ones: published monthly packages in this market run near AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is a very different cost per teaching hour once you divide it out.

sections.heading: Six things that move your quote up or down in this emirate
paragraphs: A rate band only becomes a number once six variables are settled, and five of them are inside your control. Subject scarcity is the largest single factor: Extended physics, Extended chemistry and first-language Arabic have far fewer available tutors in the Gulf timezone than maths does, and the rate follows supply. A family booking Extended maths and a family booking 0625 Paper 5 preparation are shopping in two different markets even though the search term was the same.

Timing is the second factor and the most wasteful. Demand across Abu Dhabi concentrates in the eight weeks before a series, which is when the best-matched tutors are already full and the rate at the margin rises. The same tutor booked in January for a June series is both cheaper and more available than in April. Session length is the third: a sixty-minute slot loses five minutes at each end to settling and summarising, so ninety minutes almost always costs less per useful teaching minute.

The remaining three are tier, format and subject count. Extended is wider and harder to teach than Core and sits higher in the band. Format changes the figure by the cost of travel, which in a city this spread out is substantial. And subject count changes it through coordination rather than discount: one tutor covering maths and physics for the same student holds a single picture of that student's exam calendar, which is worth more than the small saving on a second booking fee.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that changes your total bill
paragraphs: Cambridge tiers several IGCSE subjects, and the tier your child is entered for is a harder commercial fact than any hourly rate. Core caps the grade available. Extended opens the full range but sits on wider content and a harder paper set. A student entered for Core who needs a grade 6 for an A Level place is in a problem that tutoring cannot solve, because the grade is not reachable on that paper. Finding that out in February costs a year.

In practice, the tier decision is made by the school from mock performance in Year 10, and it is reviewed before the entry deadline rather than after. That review window is the point at which tutoring has the most leverage: moving a borderline student up a tier before entries close changes what they can achieve, while the same hours spent after entries close only improve performance inside a capped scale. Parents in Abu Dhabi routinely discover the tier at the same moment they discover the entry has already been made.

The table sets out the comparison the way a parent needs it, with the tutoring implication in the final column. The numbers of papers and the weightings vary by subject, so treat the row for your child's subject as the shape of the question rather than the answer; the syllabus document on the board's own site carries the exact component structure for the code on their statement of entry.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition in Abu Dhabi, compared honestly
paragraphs: This is the comparison most parents in the emirate are actually making, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition online, over live video, to families anywhere in the UAE. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That is a limit worth stating plainly rather than burying, because it lets the rest of this section be useful instead of defensive.

In-home tuition has two genuine advantages: a young child who cannot yet self-manage a screen, and a household where a parent wants to watch the lesson happen in the room. It has three costs. The rate carries the travel. The tutor pool shrinks to whoever is within driving distance of your community, which in Al Reef or Al Shamkha can mean no Extended physics specialist at all. And the session is vulnerable to traffic in a way a video call is not, so the hour you paid for routinely becomes fifty minutes.

Online one-to-one removes the radius problem and keeps the hour intact, which is why the published online bands sit below the in-home ones. The trade is that it needs a quiet room, a working camera and a student old enough to write while being watched on screen. Group tuition is cheaper per student and works where a group genuinely shares a syllabus, a tier and a board; it stops working the moment one student needs Paper 6 technique and another needs the mole calculations they missed in Year 10.

sections.heading: The two-year IGCSE plan, costed properly
paragraphs: Hourly rates mislead because nobody buys one hour. The honest unit is the two-year plan, and once you cost it that way the decisions change. A single subject taken at one hour a week through Years 10 and 11 is roughly sixty teaching weeks of tutoring. At the middle of the specialist band that is a substantial commitment, and almost no family needs it in that shape. What most families need is uneven: light in Year 10, concentrated in the two terms before the series, intensive on one or two components.

The figures published for monthly spend in this market make the point. Aggregated UAE estimates for a weekly one-hour session run near AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are monthly numbers for one subject. A family planning three subjects at exam-year intensity should be reading the top row and multiplying, which is exactly the arithmetic nobody does before committing.

The alternative shape costs considerably less and usually works better. Diagnose from a marked mock paper. Spend on the components where the marks actually went, in short blocks. Use the school's own clinics for the content gaps they can cover. Keep continuous weekly tuition only for the subject where the grade is load-bearing for an A Level place. sections.heading: Checking a tutor's right to teach before you pay anyone
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

Because the permit is free and takes about two working days through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, there is no cost argument for not holding one. That makes it the single most useful question a parent can ask, and the answer is binary. A tutor who holds the permit can say so plainly. One who explains why it does not apply to them is telling you something.

There is a second check specific to this emirate. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, as reported in the Gulf press, bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, but the practical implication is clear: your child's own classroom teacher is the one person who should not be taking your money for private lessons.
bullets: Ask directly whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit
Treat a request for cash with no written terms as a reason to walk away
Never engage your child's own subject teacher from their own school for paid tuition
Ask what happens to your child's data and how to have it deleted

sections.heading: What a good IGCSE tutor will not do with your child's coursework
paragraphs: Several pages ranking for IGCSE and IB searches in this market sell completed assessed work. One of them prices a finished Internal Assessment openly. For a family, the risk is entirely one-sided: the examination board's malpractice process acts on the candidate, not on the person who was paid. A tutor who offers to produce coursework is offering your child a penalty with a receipt attached.

The line is not blurry, and it is worth holding a tutor to it explicitly. A tutor may teach the content, explain what a mark scheme rewards, discuss a student's own draft and give feedback on it, model a technique on a different question, and practise timed work. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of an assessed piece, supply model answers to be submitted, or edit a draft to the point where the words are no longer the student's. Ask any prospective tutor how they handle a coursework draft; the answer separates teachers from suppliers in one sentence.

The same applies to materials. Published syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to the boards and should be referenced and linked, not bundled and sold as a resource pack. A tutor working from the official syllabus document for the exact code on your child's statement of entry is doing the job properly. One working from a photocopied pack of unattributed questions is working from someone else's guess about the syllabus, and that guess is the thing you are paying for.
bullets: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback; the submitted work stays the student's own
Ask how a draft is handled before the first coursework session, not after
Expect the official syllabus document for the exact code, referenced by its publisher
Treat any offer of completed assessed work as a reason to end the conversation

sections.heading: The eight weeks before a series, counted backwards
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake in this market is not overpaying for an hour. It is starting in the wrong month. IGCSE entries close months before the papers are sat, and the whole emirate's demand for tutoring lands in the same short window afterwards. Cambridge runs its exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson's international GCSE runs in May/June and November. Both publish official timetables, and both revise them, which is why a plan should be built from the live timetable on the board's own site rather than from a date someone typed on a blog.

Cambridge's own March series shows the shape of the deadlines clearly even though UAE centres sit the June and November series: for the March 2027 series, the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results reached centres on 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper. Pearson's pattern is equally instructive: the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

There is one more Cambridge detail almost no tutoring page mentions and every Abu Dhabi parent should know. Every Cambridge exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in, then build the revision plan from that version of the timetable and nothing else.

sections.heading: What to ask before you agree a rate
paragraphs: A quote becomes comparable only once you know what is inside it. The questions below are the ones that reliably expose a difference between two tutors who have given you the same number. None of them is adversarial; a tutor who teaches this syllabus for a living will answer all nine in a single conversation and will usually be glad the questions were asked.

Start with the syllabus code rather than the subject. 'Physics' is not an answer; 0625, 0972 or 4PH1 is. Then ask which papers the entry involves, and for the sciences specifically whether the entry is for the practical test or the alternative to practical, because those need different preparation and the tutor who does not ask the question has not planned the lessons. Ask how a session ends: a written note naming what was covered and what to practise is the difference between a term of tuition and a term of company.

Finish with the commercial terms. How is a cancelled session treated. What is the notice period. Is the rate per clock hour or per booked session. Who marks the past papers and against which mark scheme. Whether the first lesson is free and what, if anything, is required to take it. In our case the trial lesson is free, one per family, with no card details taken, and the rate is agreed afterwards once you have seen the teaching. That sequence is the point: the price should be the last question, not the first.

process.title: Send the code, not the subject
process.description: Tell us the four-digit syllabus code from your child's statement of entry, the tier if it is known, and the series they are entered for. That single line removes most of the guesswork, because it fixes the board, the paper structure and the grade scale before anyone has taught a lesson.

process.title: A free trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Thirty minutes with the matched tutor at no charge and with no card details taken. The aim is not a sales call; it is to see whether your child talks to this particular adult about a maths question. If they do not, we match again rather than persuade you that they will warm up.

process.title: Diagnose from a marked paper
process.description: The first full session works from a mock or past paper that has already been marked, with the mark scheme beside it. Marks lost in method, in reading the command term, and in simply running out of paper are three different problems with three different fixes, and only the paper shows which one you have.

process.title: Agree the rate and the shape
process.description: Once the trial is done, we agree an hourly rate and the shape of the plan: weekly, a pre-series block, or a short component repair. The rate is set against the market bands published on this page rather than against what a family might be willing to pay.

process.title: Review against the exam calendar
process.description: Every few weeks the plan is checked against the official timetable for the entered series and the school's own deadlines. If a subject has stabilised, hours move to the one that has not. The plan should shrink as the year goes on, not grow.

Teaching to the code on the statement of entry is basic competence, and it is routinely missing from pages that advertise generic subject tutoring in this market.

faqs.question: How much should an IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi cost per hour in 2026-27?
faqs.answer: Published rates across the UAE run from about AED 45 an hour for university-student tutors online to AED 650 for named premium tutors. IGCSE subject specialists, which is what most Year 10 and Year 11 families need, sit between AED 150 and AED 450 depending on subject scarcity and tier. In-home rates run higher, roughly AED 180 to AED 500, because the travel is inside the rate. Those are market figures published by UAE providers and by Bestimate's 2026 rate table, not IB Gram's charges; we agree a rate after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a list.

faqs.question: Why do two Abu Dhabi tutors quote AED 150 and AED 450 for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Usually because they are selling different things. The lower quote is often a generalist working at Core tier, or a university student, or a visiting tutor who happens to live nearby. The higher one is typically a subject specialist working at Extended tier in a subject with few available tutors. Ask both for the four-digit syllabus code they teach to, which papers the entry involves, and what written record follows a session. If both answers are identical, negotiate. If one cannot name the code, the gap is not a pricing difference.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper online IGCSE tutor a false economy in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but the risk is concentrated. In Year 10 a competent generalist can carry most Core-tier content perfectly well. In the final two terms of Year 11 the work is paper technique: which command term wants what, where method marks hide, how to read a six-mark question. A tutor who has not taught that specific paper set will teach content the student already has. Judge by whether they ask for a marked mock before quoting, not by the rate. The cheapest hour that moves no marks is the expensive one.

faqs.question: Does Extended tier cost more to tutor than Core?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, by roughly the width of one band. The reason is not a surcharge. Extended covers the core content plus the supplement, sits on a harder paper set, and needs technique work that Core candidates do not require, so it takes more weeks and a narrower pool of tutors can teach it to the top of the scale. The more important point is that tier caps the grade available. Confirm from the statement of entry which tier your child is entered for before you plan any budget around a target grade.

faqs.question: What does a quoted hourly rate usually leave out?
faqs.answer: Four things. Marking time, if past papers are being marked properly against the published mark scheme rather than skimmed. The written note after each session, which some tutors treat as extra. Travel, which is inside in-home rates but shortens the lesson rather than extending it. And the difference between a clock hour and a booked session, where a sixty-minute slot can become fifty minutes of teaching. Ask which of the four are included before comparing two numbers, because the quote with the lower figure is not always the lower cost per taught hour.

faqs.question: Should we pay per session or buy a monthly IGCSE package?
faqs.answer: Do the division first. Published monthly packages in this market include figures near AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The first is eight teaching hours, the second is eight as well, so the cost per hour differs sharply even though both look like one monthly number. Packages help when the schedule is genuinely weekly and you want a fixed cost. They hurt when your child needs a short component block instead, which is often the better purchase.

faqs.question: How many hours of IGCSE tutoring does one subject actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most plans assume, if the hours are aimed. A single weak component, such as graph conventions or the English summary task, often moves within two to four sessions once a marked mock has shown exactly where the marks went. A subject where a student is two years behind on foundational algebra needs a term or more. The useful sequence is diagnose, aim, review: buy a short block, check whether marks moved on a timed repeat, then decide whether to continue. Open-ended weekly tuition without that review is how budgets drift.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi rise closer to the June series?
faqs.answer: At the margin, yes. Demand across the emirate concentrates in roughly the same eight weeks before a series, so by April the best-matched tutors in scarce subjects are full and whatever is left is priced accordingly. The fix is calendar rather than negotiation: book scarce subjects, Extended physics and chemistry in particular, in the term before the one you need them. A family booking in January gets both a better match and a steadier rate than the same family booking in April for the same series.

faqs.question: Is VAT included in the tutoring prices quoted in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider to confirm in writing, and get the answer before the first invoice rather than after. We do not publish a view on how UAE VAT applies to tuition fees, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and its own guidance rather than for a tutoring page. What a parent can reasonably require is clarity: whether the figure quoted is the figure payable, whether any tax is added on top, and whether a tax registration number appears on the invoice. A provider who cannot answer that in one line is worth a second look.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both maths and physics to keep our costs down?
faqs.answer: Often, and the benefit is bigger than the saving. Maths and physics overlap in rearranging formulae, handling units, and reading graphs, and a tutor holding both subjects sees the same error appear twice and fixes it once. It also means one person holding the whole exam calendar for that student rather than two people each assuming the other noticed the entry deadline. It does not work everywhere: coordinated sciences across three disciplines at Extended depth is usually better split between two specialists.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to get IGCSE help in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Use the school first. Subject clinics, department revision sessions and the teacher's own feedback on a marked mock cost nothing and are already paid for inside the fees. Then buy narrowly: one marked paper analysed properly, a short block on the single component where marks leaked, and a timed repeat to see whether it worked. Group tuition is genuinely cheaper where a group shares board, tier and timetable. The expensive option is not the high hourly rate; it is a term of general tuition bought without a diagnosis.

faqs.question: Does a tutor for a family in Khalifa City cost more than one on Abu Dhabi island?
faqs.answer: For in-home tuition, location changes the quote, because the travel is inside the rate and the available pool is whoever can reach you. A family in Al Reef or Al Shamkha pays for a longer drive and chooses from fewer tutors than a family on the island. For online delivery, location is irrelevant to the rate: the same Extended chemistry specialist costs the same whether your child is in Khalifa City, on Al Reem Island or on Saadiyat. That is the clearest financial argument for the format in an emirate this spread out.

faqs.question: How do I check an Abu Dhabi tutor is permitted to teach before I pay them?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the application runs through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services under Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, there is no reason not to hold one. Working without a permit exposes the tutor to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted to you with suspicion.

faqs.question: Is it acceptable to pay our child's own IGCSE teacher for private lessons?
faqs.answer: They should not. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, as reported in the Gulf press, bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the private tuition permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, but the practical position is settled: pick a tutor from outside your child's school. It also avoids the conflict of a teacher being paid to fix what they are already paid to teach.

faqs.question: What should we ask for in writing before the first invoice?
faqs.answer: Five lines. The syllabus code and tier being taught. Whether the rate is per clock hour or per booked session, and whether any tax is added. The cancellation and notice terms. What written record follows each session and who marks the past papers. And what happens if the match is wrong, including whether a different tutor is offered at the same rate. None of this is unusual to ask, and a tutor who teaches this syllabus for a living will have answered it before.

The work is practical rather than theoretical: ledger entries written out, statements built to the required format, ratios calculated and then interpreted, with scripts marked against the published criteria between lessons.

intro.heading: What Accounting tuition costs in Abu Dhabi, and why the figure varies
paragraphs: Price first. Provider rate pages reachable from Abu Dhabi, read in October 2026, put qualified online subject tuition between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, with a budget tier below that and a named-specialist tier above. Monthly shapes are the more useful comparison for Accounting, because almost nobody buys a single hour of it: published monthly packages in this market include an online entry package around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home packages at roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those are market figures from other providers, not a price list from here.

The reason a quote moves is the workload rather than the hour. Accounting is a producing subject. A student who is losing marks on the statement of financial position needs to write statements, and somebody has to read them. A session that ends with a full question set, written under timing and marked before the next lesson, costs more to supply than a session that ends with a verbal summary, and it is the only version that shifts a 0452 grade. Ask any provider in this market whether marking sits inside the quoted hour; the answer explains most of the gap between two quotes.

What IB Gram supplies in the UAE is one-to-one teaching over live video, screens shared, the student's own ledger on the screen being corrected as they write. There are no home visits in Abu Dhabi, and nothing here should be read as offering one; in-home tutoring is an India-only service. For Accounting the online format carries a specific advantage, because a tutor can type a correction into the student's own statement and show the knock-on effect through the trial balance in a way that pointing at a page cannot.

The subject itself is unusually diagnosable, which is why honest quoting is possible. Cambridge assesses 0452 with two papers: a multiple-choice paper of thirty-five marks in seventy-five minutes carrying thirty per cent, and a structured written paper of a hundred and twenty marks in one hour forty-five carrying seventy. Grade movement nearly always comes from the written paper, and within it from two places: the formats of the financial statements, and the comment that is supposed to follow a ratio calculation. Neither is a knowledge gap. Both are habits.

Abu Dhabi adds its own context. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and its calendar does not match Dubai's. Accounting is also a smaller option subject than Business Studies, so in many Abu Dhabi schools it runs as a single class with one teacher and no second set. That matters: when a student falls behind in a one-class subject, there is no parallel group to move into, and outside help becomes the only available correction.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-accounting-045.programmesIntro: 0452 sits inside a short, well-defined Cambridge pathway. Knowing where a student is on it tells a tutor whether the first month should be spent on double entry or on interpretation, and whether the target is a certificate grade or entry to an AS course.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Accounting
programmes.description: Seven syllabus areas, from the accounting equation through to principles and policies, assessed by a multiple-choice paper and a structured written paper. The written paper dominates the grade and asks students to build income statements, statements of financial position, control accounts, bank reconciliations and partnership or company accounts to a required format.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the subject is usually a Year 10 option in British-curriculum schools inspected by ADEK, often taught by one teacher to one class across both years. Several schools pair it with Business Studies in the same option block, which is why families here frequently look for a tutor who can cover both without two separate bookings.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level Principles of Accounts
programmes.description: The O Level sibling of 0452, offered by some schools instead of the IGCSE. The accounting content overlaps heavily and the ledger work is identical, but the assessment structure and question styles differ enough that revising from the wrong past papers wastes weeks. Checking which code a school enters candidates for is the first question a tutor should ask.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of Abu Dhabi schools, particularly those serving South Asian communities, enter candidates for 7110 rather than 0452. Siblings in the same household occasionally sit different codes, and a tutor who does not check will set the wrong past paper in week one.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Accounting
programmes.description: The continuation route, adding manufacturing and company accounts in depth, published accounts, budgeting, standard costing and investment appraisal. Students who reached a 0452 grade by memorising statement layouts without understanding the double entry behind them tend to collapse in the first term of AS, where the layouts stop being predictable.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools offering 9706 commonly ask for a grade B or better at 0452 before admitting a student, so the IGCSE grade functions as an entry requirement inside the same school. Families planning that route often start tutoring in Year 11 specifically to clear the threshold rather than to lift a predicted grade.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Accounting
programmes.description: The Edexcel alternative, taken by a minority of Abu Dhabi schools. The underlying accounting is the same and the terminology is close, but paper structure, mark allocation and the way adjustments are presented differ. Students who move school mid-course between boards lose time to that mismatch rather than to the accounting itself.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE series in May and June and in November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each one. Abu Dhabi families switching between a Cambridge school and an Edexcel school mid-key-stage should check which series the receiving school enters for before assuming the calendar carries over.

Depreciation on the reducing-balance method, provision for doubtful debts and ratio work all assume confident percentage and fraction handling, and students who lack it lose Accounting marks that have nothing to do with accounting.

sections.heading: Paper 2 carries seventy per cent, and that changes the revision plan
paragraphs: Cambridge splits 0452 unevenly on purpose. Paper 1 is multiple choice: thirty-five marks in seventy-five minutes, thirty per cent of the grade. Paper 2 is structured written work: a hundred and twenty marks in one hour forty-five, seventy per cent. Any revision plan that gives the two papers equal time is already misallocated, and most school-set revision does exactly that because multiple-choice practice is easier to set and quicker to mark.

The practical consequence is that a student has to write. Accounting cannot be revised by reading, and it cannot be revised by answering short recall questions. The examinable skill on Paper 2 is producing a complete, correctly headed, correctly ordered financial statement from a list of balances and adjustments, under time pressure, without arithmetic slips. That is a motor skill as much as a knowledge one, and it decays if it is not practised weekly.

It also means the marking matters more here than in most subjects. A statement can be ninety per cent right and score poorly because a figure sits under the wrong subtotal, or because the heading omits the period, or because an accrual was adjusted in the income statement and forgotten in current liabilities. Those are invisible to a student rereading their own work and obvious to somebody marking against the criteria. A tutoring arrangement without marking between sessions misses the entire mechanism by which this subject improves.

A reasonable weekly split through Year 11 is one full structured question written under timing, one marked and rewritten, and one short multiple-choice set to keep Paper 1 ticking over. Two hours of student effort a week, one hour of teaching, and the ratio of written to read material heavily in favour of written.
bullets: Paper 1: 35 marks, 75 minutes, 30 per cent of the grade
Paper 2: 120 marks, 105 minutes, 70 per cent of the grade

sections.heading: The seven syllabus areas and where each one is examined
paragraphs: Cambridge organises 0452 into seven areas, and they are not interchangeable. The first two build the machinery; the middle three apply it; the last two ask the student to step back and judge. A tutor working through them out of order ends up teaching statement formats to a student who cannot reliably decide which side of a ledger an entry belongs on, which produces a short-lived improvement and a worse mock.

Two areas carry disproportionate weight on the written paper. Preparation of financial statements is the largest single written block and the place most marks are available: sole traders, partnerships, limited companies, clubs and societies, manufacturing businesses and incomplete records each have their own expected presentation. Analysis and interpretation reliably appears as the closing part of a question, carries the judgement marks, and is where candidates stop at the number.

Verification of accounting records deserves separate mention because students systematically misunderstand what it is for. Bank reconciliation, control accounts and the correction of errors through a suspense account are not arithmetic exercises. They are proofs: each one demonstrates that two independently kept records agree, and the mark scheme rewards a student who presents it as a proof with the correct layout and narration. Treating it as a sum to get right explains most of the marks lost here.

sections.heading: Where 0452 marks disappear: presentation, not knowledge
paragraphs: Ask an Abu Dhabi teacher which students disappoint at 0452 and the answer is rarely the ones who do not understand accounting. It is the ones who understand it and present it loosely. The subject marks the form of an answer as closely as its content, and a student who has never had their form corrected does not know it is wrong, because their figures are right and their reasoning is sound.

The recurring losses are specific enough to list. Headings without the business name or the period covered. An income statement that runs straight from revenue to profit without showing gross profit as a subtotal. A statement of financial position where non-current and current assets are not separated, or where capital is not reconciled with profit and drawings. Journal entries without narrations. Control accounts that balance because a figure was forced in rather than derived. Each one costs between one and several marks, and a script can lose fifteen marks to presentation alone while containing no accounting error at all.

The second cluster sits in adjustments. A prepayment reduces an expense and creates a current asset; students reliably do the first and forget the second. Depreciation reduces profit and increases accumulated depreciation; the same split failure appears. A provision for doubtful debts changes both the income statement and the receivables figure. The pattern is identical across all of them, which means it is one habit to fix rather than six topics to relearn, and that is good news for a family counting weeks.

Fixing presentation is quick but only under marking. A student cannot see a missing subtotal in their own work; they see the number they intended. Two weeks of written questions returned with the format errors circled usually removes most of this loss permanently, which is why the first month of a 0452 booking should produce marked scripts rather than lesson notes.

sections.heading: The ratios, and the sentence that earns the second half of the marks
paragraphs: Interpretation questions are worth having a system for, because they are predictable. The syllabus expects a defined set of profitability and liquidity measures, and examiners ask for the calculation and then for what it means, usually comparing two years or two businesses. Candidates who treat the question as a calculation collect roughly half the available marks and lose the rest to silence.

The comment that scores has three parts and can be taught as a formula. State the direction of the change or the difference. Give a plausible cause tied to the information in the question. Then say what it means for a stated user: the owner deciding whether to invest further, a supplier deciding whether to extend credit, a bank deciding on a loan. A student who writes those three sentences on every interpretation part will score consistently even when their chosen cause is not the one the examiner had in mind, because the reasoning is what is rewarded.

Two further points earn marks and are regularly skipped. The limitations of ratio analysis are examinable content, not a disclaimer: historic figures, no account of quality or staff, one-year snapshots, differences in accounting policy between firms. And the distinction between profitability and liquidity needs stating explicitly, because a business can be profitable and unable to pay its suppliers, which is the scenario examiners build questions around.

sections.heading: What Abu Dhabi families actually pay, by booking shape
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for Accounting because almost nobody buys one hour. The useful comparison is monthly, and this market publishes monthly shapes more readily than it publishes hourly ones. The figures below were read from UAE provider pages and from a published Dubai tutoring cost table in October 2026. They are the market, not a quote from here, and providers revise their pages without notice, so treat any number as indicative and check the source before relying on it.

Read the in-home line carefully if you are comparing. In-home packages in this market price the travel inside the fee, which is why four two-hour visits cost more than eight online sessions despite delivering the same total contact time. That is a rational charge for a tutor crossing Abu Dhabi twice a week, not a markup. It is also the whole argument for the online format: the same budget buys either travel or a specialist, and on a one-class subject like Accounting the specialist is the scarcer item.

What changes the number from here is straightforward. Weeks remaining before the series is the largest factor, because it sets the sessions per week rather than the rate. Whether the student needs a double-entry rebuild or only format correction is the second, because the rebuild is slower. Whether marking is included is the third, and it should be. A shared slot for two students sitting the same code in the same series splits the cost without halving attention, and a tutor should decline it where the two are at different stages.

IB Gram's own position is a free trial lesson, one session, and a quoted rate afterwards. Quoting before seeing a marked script would be guesswork, and in a subject where the diagnosis determines whether four weeks or twelve are needed, guesswork costs families more than the hourly difference between providers.

sections.heading: Multiple choice is not the easy paper
paragraphs: Thirty per cent of the grade sits in thirty-five multiple-choice questions, and students treat that paper as a formality because the format looks forgiving. It is not. Multiple choice removes the partial credit that rescues a written answer: a student who understands the correction of errors but misreads which account needs debiting scores zero on that item rather than two marks out of four. Precision counts for more here, not less.

The questions cluster in predictable places. Principles and policies appear more often on Paper 1 than anywhere else, because they suit a one-sentence judgement. Classification questions, capital versus revenue expenditure, which book of prime entry a transaction belongs in, and the effect of an error on the trial balance also recur, since each has one defensible answer and three plausible distractors. Students who have only practised written questions have never been forced to make those calls at speed.

Timing is the second trap. Seventy-five minutes for thirty-five questions is slightly over two minutes each, which feels generous until a student meets three consecutive calculation items. The habit worth building is to answer, mark the uncertain ones, and move, then return with the remaining time rather than losing eight minutes to a two-mark item. That is a practised behaviour, not advice, and it needs timed sets to develop.

Short multiple-choice sets are therefore worth keeping in a weekly plan even in a Paper 2-dominated subject. Twenty minutes a week, timed, marked, with the wrong answers explained rather than just corrected, keeps thirty per cent of the grade from drifting while the written work gets the bulk of the attention.

sections.heading: Where 0452 leads, and what it counts for in the UAE
paragraphs: Accounting is a gateway subject in two directions, and families are often working towards one without knowing about the other. Inside the school, it is frequently the entry requirement for Cambridge AS and A Level Accounting 9706, with a grade B or better commonly asked for, which turns the IGCSE result into an admissions decision made by the same building the student already attends. That is worth knowing in November rather than in August.

Outside the school, 0452 counts in the Ministry of Education equivalency file like any other accredited subject. The British-track requirement is a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The exclusion families miss is that Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, so a student carrying those two plus four academic IGCSEs has four counting subjects.

No IB points figure for equivalency is published here, because none has been confirmed from the Ministry's own pages for this project. If an IB number matters to your planning, read it on moe.gov.ae or ask the attestation authority in your emirate directly. Equivalency is also not something a tutor performs, influences or accelerates, and no tutoring is required for it. Any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

For university, Accounting is useful preparation and not a prerequisite. Students arriving at a business or finance degree already able to read a set of statements, build a cash-flow position and interpret a ratio start ahead of their cohort. That advantage is real and it is not the same thing as a requirement, and it is worth being clear about the difference before a family commits a year of tutoring budget to a subject their child does not enjoy.

sections.heading: What an hour of Accounting tuition is spent on, and what it is not
paragraphs: A session that works has a shape. Ten minutes on the marked script from last week, with the format errors named rather than described. Twenty-five minutes teaching the new area, with the tutor writing the ledger or statement first and the student rebuilding it. Twenty minutes with the student working alone on screen while the tutor watches and interrupts only at the point of error, which is the most useful part and the part that cannot be replicated by watching a video. Five minutes setting the written question for the week.

The boundary on what a tutor may do matters here even though 0452 has no coursework at all. Every mark in this qualification comes from two invigilated papers, so there is nothing to submit from home and nothing a tutor could improperly author for Cambridge. School-set assignments and mocks are a different matter: they feed predicted grades, and predicted grades feed sixth-form and university applications. On that work a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on what the student has produced, and does not supply figures or sentences for submission.

Published exam material deserves the same discipline. A tutor should reference the Cambridge syllabus and past papers and point you to cambridgeinternational.org to obtain them through your child's school rather than sending them as downloads. Reproducing exam board material is a copyright matter, and with unreleased papers it becomes a malpractice exposure that lands on the student rather than on the provider.

What a tutor should promise is narrow and checkable: that the student writes and the writing is marked, that feedback names the criterion, that availability is stated honestly, and that a plan which is not moving marks after six weeks of evidence gets changed or stopped. There are no grade promises here. No tutor can offer one in a subject assessed by two papers sat in a hall, and any provider who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child.

process.title: Send a marked Paper 2 script
process.description: The most useful first message is a marked structured-paper answer, with the series the student is entered for and the syllabus code the school uses. A percentage tells a tutor almost nothing; a script shows whether the losses are double entry, format or interpretation, and those need three different plans.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one session
process.description: A 0452 specialist works a structured question with the student on a shared screen. One session, no charge. The point is to find out where the answer breaks down rather than to interview the student, so you see the teaching and the tutor sees the fault in the same hour.

process.title: A written plan with a week count
process.description: After the trial you get a short note naming the failure mode, the syllabus areas that need rebuilding, and a realistic number of weeks. The rate is quoted against that, because an hour with two marked statements in it is a different product from an hour of teaching alone.

process.title: Weekly slot, written work between
process.description: A fixed time each week in Gulf Standard Time, agreed around the school run and activities. Every session ends with a question to be written under timing and returned for marking. Where the family travels, the time difference is agreed before the trip so the slot survives it.

process.title: Review at six weeks against the scripts
process.description: Six weeks of marked work is enough to judge the plan. Frequency goes up, stays flat or the arrangement ends, and the tutor says which rather than leaving it to the parent. A programme that is not moving marks should stop instead of continuing from habit.

whyPoints.title: The hour includes marking
whyPoints.description: A 0452 grade moves when statements get written, marked against the criteria and rewritten. Teaching without marking is a cheaper product that leaves the main failure mode untouched, so written work between sessions is built into how a slot is quoted rather than sold as an extra.

whyPoints.title: Figures carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of six researched competitor pages print no price at all and two quote US dollars, a currency Abu Dhabi families do not transact in. A sourced number lets you judge a quote instead of accepting one.

whyPoints.title: Online, and said plainly
whyPoints.description: UAE lessons run one-to-one over live video with screens shared. IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring exists only in India. On a subject where a tutor needs to correct a student's statement as they write it, the shared screen is better than a page across a table.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before quoting
whyPoints.description: A rate quoted before anyone has read a marked script is a guess, and in Accounting the difference between a format fix and a double-entry rebuild is eight weeks of fees. The trial lesson exists to make the quote honest, not to sell the next one.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Accounting is a narrow subject with a small specialist pool. If nobody is free in the slot you need, you are told so rather than handed a general business tutor. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable, the fallback and its rate are stated before anything is agreed.

whyPoints.title: No promises a tutor cannot keep
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no claimed board or regulator approval, and no authoring of work a student submits. A tutor teaches, marks and advises. In a subject assessed entirely by papers sat in a hall, anything beyond that is a sales line.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Accounting 0452 tutor cost per month in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Monthly is the right unit for this subject. Published UAE provider pages read in October 2026 show an online entry package around AED 799 for eight sessions, and in-home packages at roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. A published Dubai cost table puts weekly one-hour tuition at AED 240 to 600 in the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are other providers' figures, not a price list from here. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, because the workload decides the figure.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 2 worth seventy per cent of the Accounting grade?
faqs.answer: Because it is where the subject is actually tested. Paper 2 gives a hundred and twenty marks in one hour forty-five minutes for structured written work: building income statements, statements of financial position, control accounts, bank reconciliations and partnership or company accounts from balances and adjustments. Paper 1 is thirty-five marks of multiple choice in seventy-five minutes, worth thirty per cent. The planning consequence is that revision time should follow the weighting, and most school-set revision does not, because multiple-choice practice is quicker to set and quicker to mark than a full written statement.

faqs.question: My daughter gets the right figures but loses marks on the statements. Why?
faqs.answer: That is the single most common 0452 pattern and it is a presentation problem, not a knowledge one. Marks go on headings that omit the business name or the period, income statements that never show gross profit as a subtotal, assets that are not split between non-current and current, capital that is not reconciled with profit and drawings, and journal entries without narrations. A script can lose fifteen marks to format while containing no accounting error. It is invisible to a student rereading their own work and obvious to somebody marking against the criteria, which is why marked written work matters more here than extra teaching.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE Accounting harder than IGCSE Business Studies?
faqs.answer: It is less forgiving rather than harder. Business Studies rewards judgement expressed in prose, so a well-argued answer can score even where the content is approximate. Accounting rewards precision: a figure is in the right place or it is not, and a reversed debit propagates through everything that follows. Students who like rules, order and getting an exact answer usually prefer Accounting. Students who write fluently and dislike arithmetic detail usually prefer Business Studies. Neither is a soft option, and taking both in one option block is common in Abu Dhabi schools and works well.

faqs.question: Does 0452 have any coursework or practical component?
faqs.answer: None. The whole grade comes from two papers sat under exam conditions, so nothing is written at home and sent to Cambridge. That removes the academic-honesty question that complicates coursework subjects. School-set assignments and mock papers still exist and still feed predicted grades, and the boundary on those is the same everywhere: a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has written, and never supplies figures or sentences for a submission. Any provider offering more than that is selling your child a risk rather than a service.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix double-entry confusion in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually four to six weeks of weekly sessions plus written work, and it has to come before exam technique rather than alongside it. The rebuild starts at the accounting equation, moves through the books of prime entry and the ledgers to the trial balance, and then traces each adjustment through both sides so the student sees why a prepayment changes an expense and creates an asset. Teaching statement formats on top of unstable double entry produces a short-lived improvement and a worse mock, which is why a good tutor will insist on the slower order.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor really teach ledger layout over video?
faqs.answer: This is one of the subjects where the online format is an advantage rather than a compromise. The lesson happens on a shared screen with the student's own working visible, so a tutor can correct a heading as it is typed, show the knock-on effect of a misplaced figure through the trial balance, and hand control back mid-statement. Watching a student work and interrupting at the exact moment of error is the most useful twenty minutes of any Accounting session, and a shared screen does it at least as well as sitting beside them.

faqs.question: Which ratios does 0452 expect a student to know by heart?
faqs.answer: The syllabus expects gross margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, liquid or acid test ratio, rate of inventory turnover, and the receivables and payables turnover periods in days. Knowing the formula is half the mark. The other half is a three-part comment: the direction of the change, a plausible cause tied to the information given, and what it means for a named user such as an owner, a supplier or a bank. The limitations of ratio analysis are examinable content too, not a disclaimer to add at the end.

faqs.question: Should my son take Accounting if he is weak at maths?
faqs.answer: The arithmetic demand is lower than families fear and the precision demand is higher. Accounting needs confident work with percentages, fractions and simple interest, mostly for depreciation, provisions and ratios, and almost nothing beyond that. What it genuinely requires is care: a student who habitually transposes digits or skips a line will lose marks everywhere, because errors propagate. A student who is slow at mental arithmetic but methodical on paper usually does well. If the underlying problem is percentage work, fixing that in maths lessons is cheaper than fixing it inside Accounting hours.

faqs.question: What is the suspense account and why does it confuse everyone?
faqs.answer: It is a temporary holding account used when a trial balance does not agree, and the confusion comes from treating it as a thing rather than as a symptom. Errors that affect only one side of the double entry push the trial balance out of balance, and the difference is parked in a suspense account until each error is found and corrected by journal entry. Errors affecting both sides equally, such as a complete reversal or a wrong account of the right type, never reach it. Knowing which errors do and do not affect the trial balance is what the question is actually testing.

faqs.question: Does 0452 count as one of the five IGCSEs for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Yes, like any other accredited academic subject. The British-track requirement published for UAE equivalency is a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, which catches families out when planning option blocks. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae, because equivalency is a Ministry process and not something a tutor performs or influences.

faqs.question: Is Accounting 0452 accepted for AS and A Level Accounting 9706?
faqs.answer: It is the natural entry route and many Abu Dhabi schools ask for a grade B or better before admitting a student to AS Accounting. Students who reached a good IGCSE grade by memorising statement layouts tend to struggle in the first AS term, where the layouts stop being predictable and manufacturing, published company accounts and costing arrive. The habits that carry forward are double-entry security and the discipline of commenting on a figure rather than stopping at it, which is why those are worth fixing at IGCSE rather than deferring.

faqs.question: How do we schedule Accounting sessions around Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: By agreeing the change before the month starts rather than during it. Sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing, and families who settle that in advance keep their continuity instead of losing four weeks and then trying to compress the catch-up into the spring. For a June-series candidate that month sits awkwardly close to the real revision window, so the practical approach is lighter sessions with shorter written tasks rather than a pause, and a slightly heavier schedule either side of it. Online delivery makes the timing shift straightforward since no travel has to be rearranged.

faqs.question: What does the first Accounting session with a new tutor cover?
faqs.answer: A question, not a conversation. The tutor sets a structured written part at the student's level, watches them work on a shared screen, and stops at the first point where the method breaks rather than at the end. That locates the fault precisely: debit and credit reversal, an adjustment applied on one side only, a missing subtotal, or a ratio calculated without comment. By the end of the hour there is a named failure mode and a rough week count. Sending a marked mock script beforehand makes that diagnosis faster and the first hour more useful.

Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. If nobody is free in the slot you need, you will be told rather than offered a substitute.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-additional-mat.tutorsIntro: The tutors matched to this page teach Additional Mathematics as a separate discipline from Extended 0580, because the two papers reward different habits. Each one works from your child's own scripts, marks against the published scheme, and reports the mark by topic rather than by feeling.

intro.heading: What an Abu Dhabi family is actually buying when they hire a 0606 tutor
paragraphs: Additional Mathematics 0606 is the Cambridge syllabus a school offers to the students it considers strongest in maths, usually alongside Extended 0580 in the same series. It is not a harder version of the same course. It introduces differentiation, integration, kinematics, binomial expansion, logarithmic and exponential functions, circular measure in radians, and vectors, and it asks for them in multi-step questions where a single early slip removes every mark that follows. Families in Abu Dhabi rarely search for a 0606 tutor in September. They search in January, after the first set of mock results comes home and a student who has never dropped below a high grade in maths has a mark in the fifties.

That pattern has a cause worth naming. In Extended 0580 a question usually tests one skill, and a student who is quick at arithmetic can arrive at the answer by a route of their own. In 0606 the marks are split between method and accuracy, and the method mark is awarded for a specific line of working. A student who can differentiate in their head and write only the final answer loses marks on a question they fully understood. Nothing in that student's 0580 experience taught them otherwise, so they repeat the habit for an entire year unless somebody marks their script line by line and shows them where the credit was sitting.

The second cause is vocabulary rather than mathematics. The 0606 papers use exact form, show that, hence, state, determine and in terms of as instructions with precise consequences. A correct decimal where an exact surd was requested scores nothing. A numerical verification where a proof was demanded scores nothing. Students who have been rewarded all their lives for arriving at the right number find this arbitrary, and they are not persuaded by being told it matters. They are persuaded by seeing the mark scheme next to their own paper once.

Abu Dhabi adds its own constraints. ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and enrolment is spread across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, Saadiyat and Yas, and the newer mainland communities. Few of those schools run a large 0606 set. A cohort of eight or ten students is common, which means the teacher is often covering it in a lunchtime slot or an extra period, and a student who falls behind in November has no second class to drop into. The Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies that every private school in the country teaches alongside its own curriculum occupy real hours in the same week, so the evening available for maths is narrower than it looks on paper.

What a tutor can honestly change in that situation is the quality of the feedback loop. A specialist can take a marked paper, identify whether the loss is method, accuracy, notation or topic knowledge, and work through the smallest number of questions that will fix it. That is slower than a lecture and far more useful. IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition to Abu Dhabi families; home visits are a service offered only in India, and we do not pretend otherwise. The practical effect is that your child is matched to a 0606 specialist rather than to whoever teaches maths within a twenty-minute drive of your community.
