abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-additional-mat.programmesIntro: 0606 sits inside a sequence. It is taken in the Cambridge upper secondary years, it feeds directly into AS and A Level Mathematics, and it is the closest thing an IGCSE student can sit to the first weeks of IB Diploma Analysis and Approaches. The programmes below are the ones Abu Dhabi families ask about in the same conversation.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: A separate Cambridge IGCSE assessed by two written papers of two hours each, with no coursework. The content covers functions, quadratics, indices and surds, factors of polynomials, simultaneous equations, logarithmic and exponential functions, straight-line graphs, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series, vectors in two dimensions, differentiation, integration and kinematics. Candidates are normally entered for it in the same series as Extended 0580.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the entry decision is made by the school, not the regulator. A department will look at a student's 0580 performance, the size of the set it can staff, and whether the timetable has a slot. Some schools run 0606 as an after-school option, which means a student who misses three weeks for travel has genuinely lost three weeks of teaching with no catch-up class to attend.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, Extended tier
programmes.description: The mainstream Cambridge maths IGCSE. Extended candidates sit the higher-tier papers and can reach the top grades. Content is broad rather than deep: number, algebra, mensuration, geometry, trigonometry, vectors, transformations, probability and statistics. Most questions test a single technique, which is why a strong 0580 candidate can be surprised by the multi-step structure of 0606 without any gap in their underlying knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Nearly every British-curriculum school in the emirate enters its Year 11 cohort for 0580 or for the Pearson equivalent. Where a student is taking both 0580 and 0606, the two revision programmes are not interchangeable, and a single tutor needs to be explicit about which paper a given practice question came from.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation. Pure Mathematics 1 opens with quadratics, functions, coordinate geometry, circular measure, trigonometry, series, differentiation and integration, which is close to the 0606 content list. Students who have sat 0606 usually find the first term familiar in topic and unfamiliar in rigour, because the proofs and the standards of presentation step up again.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi sixth forms ask for a strong Extended 0580 grade for A Level Mathematics and treat 0606 as helpful rather than required. If your child's school lists a specific requirement, that list is the one to work to, and the head of department is the person who can confirm it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The analytical route through IB Diploma maths, offered at Standard and Higher Level. Calculus, functions and proof carry much of the course, and the Higher Level option asks for fluency with manipulation that a student without prior calculus has to build quickly. The exploration, written over the two years, is the student's own work and must remain so.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a substantial IB sector alongside its British-curriculum schools, and families moving a child from an IGCSE school into a Diploma programme often ask whether 0606 smooths the transition. Within Analysis and Approaches it genuinely does, for differentiation and integration in particular. It is far less relevant to Applications and Interpretation.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-additional-mat.subjectsIntro: The 0606 syllabus is best read as a list of separate skills, each with its own failure mode. The grid below is the topic list as a tutor uses it: what the topic asks for, and the specific thing that costs marks when a student has not been shown it.

subjects.name: Functions, domain and range
subjects.description: Composite and inverse functions, modulus graphs, and the vocabulary of domain and range. Students lose marks by giving a range as an interval of x, by forgetting that an inverse requires a one-to-one function, and by sketching a modulus graph without reflecting the correct branch.

subjects.name: Quadratic functions and the discriminant
subjects.description: Completing the square, maximum and minimum points, and conditions on the discriminant for distinct, equal or no real roots. The common loss is answering with a value when the question asked for a range of values of k, or solving the discriminant equation and forgetting the inequality it came from.

subjects.name: Indices, surds and exact form
subjects.description: Manipulating fractional and negative indices, rationalising denominators, and leaving an answer as a surd. This is the topic behind most avoidable 0606 losses, because a student who rounds mid-question cannot recover the exact answer the mark scheme requires at the end.

subjects.name: Factors of polynomials
subjects.description: The factor and remainder theorems, division of a cubic, and solving the resulting quadratic. Marks are lost when working is correct but no conclusion is written: a show that question wants a sentence stating what the remainder proves, not only the arithmetic that produced it.

subjects.name: Logarithmic and exponential functions
subjects.description: Laws of logarithms, solving equations with the unknown in the index, and reducing a relationship to a straight-line form. Students who learn the laws as rules rather than as consequences tend to apply the subtraction law to a sum of logarithms and lose the whole question.

subjects.name: Straight-line graphs and linear law
subjects.description: Converting a non-linear relationship into Y against X form, then reading constants from a gradient and intercept. The frequent error is plotting the original variables, producing a curve, and then forcing a line of best fit through it anyway rather than transforming first.

subjects.name: Circular measure and radians
subjects.description: Arc length, sector area and problems combining triangles with sectors. Almost every mark lost here comes from a calculator left in degree mode, or from a student converting an answer back to degrees when the question was set, and is marked, in radians.

subjects.name: Trigonometry, identities and equations
subjects.description: Reciprocal ratios, Pythagorean identities, and solving equations across a stated interval. The single largest loss on the paper is giving one solution where the interval contains three or four, because the student solved the equation and stopped at the calculator's principal value.

subjects.name: Series and the binomial theorem
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric progressions, sums to infinity, and binomial expansion including a specified term. Finding the term independent of x requires setting up and solving an equation in the index, which students often skip by expanding by hand and running out of time.

subjects.name: Permutations and combinations
subjects.description: Arrangements with restrictions, selections, and problems requiring a case split. This topic is routinely postponed to the final fortnight and then met cold in the exam. It rewards careful reading more than technique, which makes it one of the cheaper topics to recover late.

subjects.name: Differentiation and its applications
subjects.description: Product, quotient and chain rules, stationary points, second derivatives, tangents and normals, connected rates of change. Students lose accuracy marks by giving an x coordinate alone where the question asked for a point, and by stating a maximum without testing the nature of the stationary value.

subjects.name: Integration and kinematics
subjects.description: Indefinite and definite integration, area under a curve, area between a curve and a line, and the displacement, velocity and acceleration chain. The classic loss is integrating correctly, then subtracting the limits in the wrong order, or forgetting the constant in a kinematics problem with a stated initial condition.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-additional-mat.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi communities differ less in what they study than in what time a session can start. The school run, the length of the commute from the mainland to the island and back, and the hours already committed to Arabic and Islamic Education all decide when a 0606 lesson is realistically possible.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Island addresses within short reach of several long-established British-curriculum schools. Students are often home by half past three, which makes an early evening slot workable before homework rather than after it.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Close to some of the oldest school campuses in the emirate. Families here frequently have two children on different exam timetables, and we schedule 0606 on a fixed weekday so the other subject keeps its slot.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A large British and American curriculum catchment on the mainland side. Bus routes through this corridor can run past four o'clock, so a sensible 0606 session starts at six and finishes before the evening meal.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island

sections.heading: Where the marks are awarded in a 0606 answer
paragraphs: A 0606 question is marked in parts. Some marks are for method, awarded when a particular line of working appears, and some are for accuracy, awarded for the final value in the form the paper asked for. A student can reach the correct answer and collect only half the available marks, and a student can make an arithmetic slip early and still collect most of them if the method is visible. Neither outcome makes sense to a family looking at a score alone, which is why the first session with a new 0606 student is spent on a script rather than on content.

The practical consequence is that presentation is part of the subject. In Extended 0580 a student who can see the answer may write one line and move on, and the paper usually rewards it. In 0606 the same habit removes marks on question after question across two papers. Once a student has watched a mark scheme being applied to their own work, the behaviour changes in a session or two. Told as a general rule, it does not change at all.

The table below sets out five question types that recur across 0606 papers, what each one is actually rewarding, and the reason the mark most often goes missing. None of these losses is a knowledge gap. Every one of them is a habit, which is why they respond quickly to being named.

This is also the honest answer to a question Abu Dhabi families ask early: what can tutoring realistically change before a series? It can change the proportion of what a student already knows that converts into marks. That is frequently the larger of the two available gains, and it is the one nobody at school has time to work on individually.
bullets: Write the line that earns the method mark even when the answer is obvious
Leave answers in exact form unless a decimal is explicitly requested
Finish a show that question with a stated conclusion
List every solution inside the interval the question gives you

sections.heading: Exact form, surds and answers that are right but score nothing
paragraphs: Exact form is the single most expensive piece of vocabulary on this syllabus. It means the answer must be left as a fraction, a surd, a logarithm or a multiple of pi, with no decimal approximation anywhere in the final line. A student who computes a square root on the calculator at step two has destroyed the exact answer before reaching the end of the question, and no amount of correct subsequent work recovers it. The mark scheme does not award the decimal, because the decimal is not the thing being tested.

This runs against everything a capable fifteen-year-old has been rewarded for. In earlier years, getting to a number quickly was the skill. In 0606 the number is often the least interesting part of the answer, and the examiner wants to see that the student can carry an irrational quantity through several steps without flinching. Rationalising a denominator, simplifying a surd, and recognising that a fraction with a root in it is a finished answer are all habits built by doing, not by being told.

The related trap is premature rounding on questions that do want a decimal. Where a paper asks for three significant figures, it wants three significant figures in the final answer, computed from unrounded intermediate values. A student who rounds at every stage arrives at a figure that disagrees with the scheme in the last digit and loses the accuracy mark while having understood the whole question. Both errors come from the same root, which is treating the calculator as the place where mathematics happens.

In a session this is fixed mechanically. The student works a question with the calculator face down, writes the exact answer, and only then evaluates it if asked to. After a dozen questions the habit holds under exam pressure, which is the only condition that matters. It is dull work and it reliably returns marks, which makes it a sensible use of paid time in the weeks before a series.
bullets: Exact form means a surd, fraction, logarithm or multiple of pi, not a decimal
Round once, at the end, from unrounded working

sections.heading: The two 0606 papers against an Abu Dhabi Year 11 week
paragraphs: Both 0606 papers run for two hours and each carries half the grade. The difference between them is the shape of the questions rather than the topics: one paper is built from a larger number of shorter items, the other from fewer, longer, multi-step problems. A student can be comfortable with one shape and poor at the other, and a mock mark that averages the two hides that completely. Asking which paper the marks were lost on is usually more informative than asking which topic.

There is no coursework on 0606 and no practical component. Every mark is earned in a timed room, which simplifies planning and raises the cost of poor exam technique. It also removes a category of worry that families carry over from other subjects: there is no portfolio to assemble, no internal deadline to miss, and no question about what a tutor may contribute to a submitted piece of work, because nothing is submitted.

What Abu Dhabi families need to watch instead is the entry calendar, which sits much earlier than parents expect. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable for each, and its own guidance is blunt about the consequences: it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam. A school handles this, but it is worth knowing that your child's timetable may not match a cousin's at a different school.

The published key dates for the Cambridge March 2027 series show how far ahead the administration runs: an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May. For the June and November series the shape is the same even where the dates differ, which means the decision about whether a student is entered for 0606 at all is usually taken months before anyone has seen a mock paper.

sections.heading: Trigonometry in 0606: identities, intervals and the degree-radian switch
paragraphs: Trigonometry is where 0606 separates students who have learned techniques from students who have understood them. The syllabus adds reciprocal ratios, the Pythagorean identities, and equations that must be solved across a stated interval. The step up from 0580 is not computational. It is that a single equation now has several valid answers, and the student has to know where to look for them rather than trusting the calculator to hand them over.

The failure is consistent enough to predict. A student rearranges correctly, applies an identity correctly, reaches a value for a ratio, presses the inverse function, writes one answer and moves on. Two or three marks are gone. The fix is a drawn quadrant diagram or a sketched graph for every equation, every time, until it is automatic. Students resist this because it feels slow, and the resistance disappears the first time they see a full mark scheme for a question they half answered.

Radians cause a separate problem that compounds the first. Circular measure questions are set in radians, so arc length and sector area formulas assume radian measure, and a calculator left in degree mode returns a plausible wrong number with no warning. Mixed questions that combine a sector with a non-right-angled triangle are common, and they require the student to hold both measures in mind without converting unnecessarily. Checking the calculator mode at the start of every question sounds trivial until you count the marks it saves across two papers.

Identities are worth separating from equations in a plan. Proving an identity is a presentation task: start from one side, work to the other, never treat it as an equation to be solved. Solving an equation is a search task: reduce to a single ratio, find the principal value, then find every other value inside the interval. Students who conflate the two attempt proofs by substituting numbers, which earns nothing, and then conclude they are bad at trigonometry when the problem was the instruction.
bullets: Sketch the quadrant diagram or the graph before writing any solution
Check calculator mode at the start of every circular measure question
Prove an identity from one side; never cross-multiply it like an equation
Read the interval first and write it at the top of the working

sections.heading: Permutations, series and the topics students leave until April
paragraphs: Every 0606 cohort postpones the same two areas. Permutations and combinations get left because they look unlike the rest of the syllabus, and series gets left because the formulas feel interchangeable until they are needed. Both then arrive cold in the final fortnight, at the point when revision time is scarcest and new content is hardest to absorb. Because both topics are self-contained, they are also among the cheapest marks available late, which makes the usual order of revision close to backwards.

Permutations and combinations reward careful reading more than technique. The decision a student has to make is whether order matters, and then whether a restriction forces a case split. Most lost marks come from reading the question once, choosing a formula, and never noticing a condition such as two particular people needing to sit together. Working through ten questions aloud, with the student stating the structure before touching a formula, generally fixes it inside two sessions.

Series splits into three jobs that get muddled. Arithmetic progressions require identifying first term and common difference from a verbal description. Geometric progressions require the same for the ratio, plus the condition for a sum to infinity to exist. The binomial theorem requires setting up an index equation to locate a particular term rather than expanding everything in sight. A student who can state which of the three a question belongs to has already done most of the work.

For an Abu Dhabi student planning revision backwards from the series, the practical advice is to schedule these two areas early and the calculus late. Calculus is the subject's backbone and benefits from spaced repetition across months. Permutations and series are short, contained, and can be lifted in a fortnight. Reversing that order is how a capable student arrives at the paper with strong calculus and two whole topics unseen.
bullets: State whether order matters before selecting a permutation or combination formula
Identify the progression type from the wording before using any formula
Check the condition for a sum to infinity before applying it
Schedule the short contained topics early and keep calculus running throughout

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through MoHRE, and the federal guidance states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anybody.

The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, available through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. That matters for a parent because it makes the permit a reasonable thing to ask about. A tutor who has been teaching in the emirate for years and has never heard of it is telling you something useful.

Abu Dhabi adds a condition that Dubai families do not face in the same form. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's own code of conduct pointing the same way. That reporting should be checked against the current ADEK policy document before anyone treats it as exact wording, but the direction is clear enough that a parent should not be arranging paid lessons with their child's own classroom teacher.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no permit, licence or endorsement from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or any other body, and it does not operate premises in the UAE. What we do is check a tutor's permit position before a match and tell you plainly what we have and have not verified. The table sets out who the permit covers so you can ask the right question of any tutor, including one you find somewhere else.

sections.heading: What 0606 support costs around Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Published tutoring rates in the UAE sit in bands that are wide enough to be confusing and specific enough to be useful once you know what each band includes. The figures below come from providers that publish their own numbers and from a 2026 Dubai cost survey, and they are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. Abu Dhabi sits broadly in line with Dubai for online specialist teaching, because the pool of people who can teach Additional Mathematics is national rather than local.

Three things move the number for this syllabus in particular. The first is scarcity: a tutor who has actually taught 0606, as opposed to 0580, prices at the specialist end because there are fewer of them. The second is marking. An hour of teaching plus a marked script between sessions is a different product from an hour of talking, and the cheaper bands generally exclude the marking. The third is timing, since the weeks before a series are when demand for every maths specialist peaks at once.

What you should not pay for is travel. An in-home visit in this market carries a rate that includes the driver's time, and in a city where crossing from the mainland to the island at five in the afternoon can absorb forty minutes each way, that time is being purchased at the teaching rate. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. The comparison is not online versus in-person as an abstract preference. It is whether the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching.

For planning purposes, a weekly hour with marking across a two-term run is the common shape for 0606, with a short intensive block before the papers. Where a family is choosing between buying more hours and buying better hours, the better hours usually win on this syllabus, because the limiting factor is almost never how much content has been covered. It is how much of the content converts into marks on a timed paper.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi schools, ADEK, and who decides whether 0606 happens at all
paragraphs: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and it publishes inspection outcomes on a banded scale running from the highest rating down to the weakest. Those reports are worth reading before a school choice and are close to useless for a question like whether a maths department runs an Additional Mathematics set. Inspection judgements are about provision across a whole school. The 0606 decision is made inside one department, by people balancing a small cohort against a timetable.

So the questions that get useful answers are departmental. How many students are entered for 0606 this year. Whether it is taught in a timetabled lesson or an after-school block. Which teacher takes it. What the department looks for in a 0580 performance before offering a place. Whether a student can be withdrawn at the mock stage without consequence for the 0580 entry. A head of maths will answer all five, and the answers tell you more about your child's prospects than any published rating.

The federal position behind all of this is that private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is why an Abu Dhabi student sitting Cambridge papers is also carrying mandated subjects in the same week, and it is a real constraint on the hours available for an extra maths qualification. A family weighing up 0606 should count those hours honestly before committing.

Where a school does not offer 0606 at all, a private entry is sometimes possible through a centre that accepts external candidates, and the school or the centre is the right place to ask about it. We can teach the syllabus; we cannot enter a candidate, and no tutoring provider can. Anyone who implies otherwise is worth a second look.
bullets: Ask the department how many candidates it enters for 0606 and in what slot
Ask whether a student can withdraw at mock stage without affecting the 0580 entry
Inspection ratings describe a school, not a single syllabus decision

sections.heading: What a 0606 tutor should not be asked to do
paragraphs: Because this syllabus has no coursework, the academic-honesty questions that dominate IB and Pearson subjects do not arise in the same way. There is no exploration, no portfolio and no submitted investigation, so there is nothing a tutor could improperly contribute to. What remains is the school's own work: weekly problem sets, assessed classwork and internal mocks, and the line there is simple. A tutor may teach the method, work a comparable question, and check the student's reasoning. A tutor should not be producing the answers that get handed in with a student's name on them.

The second boundary concerns materials. Cambridge syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the board's copyright. A tutor may reference them, cite them and point a family to the official pages on cambridgeinternational.org. Supplying them as downloads is not something a tutoring provider should be doing, and a site offering a library of them should prompt a question about what else it treats casually.

The third is credentials. Describing a tutor as an examiner is a specific factual claim about a current appointment, and it should be evidenced or dropped. It also should not be used to imply any access to marking, boundaries or unseen papers, because no such access exists. Our position is that we tell you what we have checked, which is the permit position and the tutor's own account of what they have taught, and we do not dress either up as something more.

Finally, no tutor can promise a grade. Additional Mathematics is a two-paper examination sat under timed conditions by a sixteen-year-old on a given morning, and the number of variables between a good programme of work and a specific number is large. What can be promised is a marked script after each piece of work, a named cause for each cluster of lost marks, and an honest answer when the evidence says the plan is not working.
bullets: Teaching a method is support; supplying the answers to assessed work is not

faqs.question: Is Additional Maths 0606 on the timetable at most Abu Dhabi schools?
faqs.answer: No. It is an option that British-curriculum schools in the emirate offer selectively, usually to a small group they judge strongest in maths, and often in an after-school or option block rather than a timetabled lesson. Some schools do not offer it at all. The useful questions for a head of maths are how many candidates are entered this year, when it is taught, and what a student needs to show in 0580 before being offered a place. Where a school does not run it, a private entry through a centre that accepts external candidates is sometimes possible, and the school or centre is the right place to ask.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on 0606 questions he says he answered correctly?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the marks were split between method and accuracy, and he wrote only the answer. In Extended 0580 a student who can see the result often gets away with one line of working. In 0606 the method mark is awarded for a specific line appearing on the page, so a question answered mentally and written briefly can score half of what was available. The other common cause is form: a decimal given where the paper asked for exact form earns nothing. Both are habits rather than knowledge gaps, and both change quickly once a student has seen the mark scheme applied to their own script.

faqs.question: Why is a decimal answer sometimes marked wrong in 0606?
faqs.answer: Because the question asked for exact form, which means a surd, a fraction, a logarithm or a multiple of pi, with no approximation in the final line. The paper is testing whether a student can carry an irrational quantity through several steps, so the decimal is not an acceptable alternative version of the same answer. There is a related trap in the other direction: where three significant figures are requested, they must be computed from unrounded working, and a student who rounds at every stage disagrees with the scheme in the last digit. The practical fix is to work the question with the calculator unused and evaluate only if asked.

faqs.question: How are the marks split between the two 0606 papers?
faqs.answer: Each paper runs two hours and each carries half the grade. The difference is the shape of the questions rather than the content: one paper is made up of a larger number of shorter items, the other of fewer, longer, multi-step problems. That matters for diagnosis, because a student can be solid on one shape and weak on the other while the averaged mock mark hides it. When a mock comes back, ask which paper the marks were lost on before asking which topic, and check the current syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org for the exact component details for your child's series.

faqs.question: Which calculator is my daughter allowed to take into a 0606 exam?
faqs.answer: A calculator is permitted in the written papers, and the model restrictions are set out in the information for candidates inside the current Cambridge syllabus rather than decided by the school. That document is the one to check, because the rules differ between Cambridge maths syllabuses and reading the wrong one is a genuine risk. What matters more for marks is how the calculator is used. Most exact-form losses on this syllabus come from evaluating something early, so good 0606 practice involves long stretches of working with the calculator deliberately left alone.

faqs.question: Does 0606 appear on the same certificate as her other Cambridge subjects?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics is a separate Cambridge IGCSE with its own grade, sat alongside Extended 0580 rather than in place of it, so a student who takes both receives a grade for each. That is part of the appeal and part of the risk: it is an extra qualification, and it is also an extra examination in a series that is already full. Families weighing it up should count the additional study hours against the subjects already on the timetable, including the Arabic, social studies and Islamic education that private schools in the UAE teach alongside their own curriculum.

faqs.question: My daughter solved the trigonometric equation but only got one mark. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the interval in the question contained more than one solution and she wrote down only the calculator's principal value. This is the largest single avoidable loss on the paper. Reducing the equation to one ratio earns the method mark, and the accuracy mark requires every solution inside the stated interval. The habit that fixes it is drawing a quadrant diagram or sketching the graph for every equation before writing any answer, and writing the interval at the top of the working so it cannot be forgotten. Students find this slow for about a fortnight and then stop losing the marks.

faqs.question: How many weekly hours does 0606 add on top of an Abu Dhabi Year 11 timetable?
faqs.answer: Families we work with typically find that a single focused hour a week, with a short piece of marked work between sessions, is enough across most of the year, rising to two in the weeks before the papers. What makes the difference is not volume but whether the work is written out, timed and marked against the published scheme. Count the hours already committed before you decide: an Abu Dhabi student is carrying nine or ten subjects plus the mandated Arabic, Islamic education and social studies, and a plan that ignores those collapses by the second half of term.

faqs.question: Can an Abu Dhabi school teacher tutor my child privately for 0606?
faqs.answer: Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct pointing the same way. Verify the current wording on adek.gov.ae before relying on it, but the direction is clear enough that arranging paid lessons with your child's own classroom teacher is not a sensible route. A teacher from a different school who holds the permit is a different question entirely.

faqs.question: What does a specialist 0606 tutor charge per hour around Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 or above, and premium named tutors higher again; one provider publishes AED 650. In-home rates in the UAE run from about AED 180 to 500, and that band includes the driver's time. Those are other providers' published numbers as at October 2026, not our price list. For 0606 specifically, scarcity pushes a genuine specialist towards the upper bands, and the thing worth paying for is whether marking between sessions is included.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our villa in Khalifa City for maths lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Abu Dhabi families are one to one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For a minority syllabus this is the arrangement that actually helps, because the constraint on 0606 is not distance but the number of people who have taught the course. Matching online means your child works with an Additional Mathematics specialist rather than with whoever teaches maths within a short drive of Khalifa City.

faqs.question: Which 0606 topics are worth leaving until last?
faqs.answer: Not permutations and series, which is the order most students choose. Those two areas are short, self-contained and liftable in a fortnight, which makes them cheap marks to recover late and a poor use of the final weeks if they have been left entirely unseen. Calculus is the opposite: it is the backbone of both papers, it rewards spaced repetition over months, and it does not respond well to being crammed. A sensible plan front-loads the contained topics, keeps differentiation and integration running throughout, and reserves the last fortnight for timed papers rather than new content.

faqs.question: Will a 0606 grade help with Ministry of Education equivalency in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: For the British track, reporting on the UAE equivalency requirements states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and that Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Whether a particular syllabus counts within those five is a question for the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority, not for a tutoring provider. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae before making a decision that depends on it.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson for 0606 actually cover?
faqs.answer: It is a working session rather than a sales call. The tutor sets a short piece of Additional Mathematics work, usually drawn from a released paper, watches how your child presents the working, and then reports on whether the lost marks are method, accuracy, notation or genuine topic gaps. If you have a marked mock script, send it beforehand and the trial starts from that instead. You receive the written diagnosis whether or not you continue, and there is no obligation and no card required to book it.

faqs.question: Our evenings are full with Arabic and Islamic education homework. Can 0606 fit?
faqs.answer: It usually can, but only if the plan is built around the week you actually have. Private schools in the UAE teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic education alongside their licensed curriculum, and those subjects carry homework that lands on the same evenings as everything else. We would rather schedule one protected hour at a time that survives the term than two hours that get cancelled from November onwards. Weekend mornings work well for the long multi-step 0606 questions, because those need an uninterrupted stretch rather than a tired half hour.

Send the script, tell us which other maths paper your child is sitting and which two evenings are genuinely free, and the trial lesson will start from that work. You will get a written diagnosis separating method from accuracy from topic gaps, and an honest view of what the remaining weeks can and cannot do. Lessons run one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What you are actually paying for when you hire a 0508 tutor in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Arabic as a First Language is the one subject on an Abu Dhabi timetable where families routinely assume tutoring is unnecessary and then pay for it in Year 11 anyway. The child speaks Arabic at home, speaks it in the corridor, argues in it at dinner, and comes back with a C. Nothing is wrong with the Arabic. What is wrong is the match between a confident spoken dialect and a paper that assesses Modern Standard Arabic under timed conditions, with a summary task that rewards compression and a composition task that rewards register control. That gap is a teaching problem, and teaching problems have prices.

Those prices are published almost nowhere. Three of the six tutoring sites that rank for Abu Dhabi queries show no figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family here transacts in. So this page starts with the numbers. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in the UAE run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE support from AED 150. Specialist exam-year rates reach AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350. First-language Arabic sits at the upper end of whichever band applies, for one reason, and the reason is supply.

Supply is the thing nobody prices openly. Abu Dhabi has a deep bench of Arabic speakers and a thin bench of people who have marked 0508 scripts. ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and every private school here must provide Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside whatever international curriculum it is licensed for. That federal requirement creates steady demand for Arabic teachers inside schools and leaves fewer of them free at five o'clock on a Tuesday. A first-language Arabic specialist is harder to replace than a maths tutor of the same standing, and the hourly rate reflects it.

The second price driver is what you ask the tutor to do. A session spent on vocabulary is cheap to deliver and slow to show results. A session spent marking a timed composition against the criteria, naming the three register slips that cost marks, and rewriting one paragraph together is harder to prepare and faster to show results. The same hourly rate buys either. Families who treat 0508 as a reading-comprehension problem tend to buy more hours than families who treat it as a written-accuracy problem, because the reading paper improves as a by-product of better writing far more often than the reverse.

The third is timing, and this is where Abu Dhabi families lose the most money. Entry deadlines sit months before the paper. Cambridge's own published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, a lead of more than two months. Abu Dhabi schools generally enter candidates for the June or November series, and the same arithmetic applies: once the school submits the entry, the syllabus, the components and the date are fixed, and the only variable left is how many weeks your child has to work with. Booking a scarce specialist in September costs less per hour than booking the same person in April.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-l.programmesIntro: Arabic runs through an Abu Dhabi school from the first year to the last. Cambridge 0508 is one stage on that route, and the stage before it and the stage after it both change what a tutor should be doing with the hour. These are the levels we support around the IGCSE year, and what each one is for.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Arabic
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course, where first-language Arabic either becomes a written subject or quietly stays a spoken one. Work here is about moving from confident speech to controlled Modern Standard Arabic on paper: sentence-level accuracy, paragraphing, and the habit of planning before writing. A student who leaves Year 9 able to write three hundred accurate words to a prompt starts the 0508 course with the hard part already behind them.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi this is the stage where the Arab and non-Arab Arabic streams diverge sharply, because schools teach the two groups to different expectations and in different languages of instruction. Families who arrive mid-Year 8 from a school with no Arabic provision feel it most, and that is the point at which a single term of catch-up support costs the least.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language (0508)
programmes.description: Two assessed components: a reading paper built on Arabic passages with comprehension and summary tasks, and a writing paper asking for extended composition in a set form. Marks move on precision rather than on fluency: summarising without copying, writing to a register, holding tense and agreement together under time pressure. Confirm the component structure and weightings for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org, because syllabuses are revised by series.
programmes.countryNote: Most Abu Dhabi private schools enter first-language Arabic candidates for the June series, with November used for resits and for students who joined late in the course. The entry decision belongs to the school, not to a tutor, and it is worth asking the head of Arabic which syllabus code appears on the entry sheet before you buy any tuition at all.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Arabic
programmes.description: The route after a strong 0508 grade for students who intend to keep Arabic as an examined subject. The work shifts from controlled composition to literary and discursive writing, and students who reached a high grade at IGCSE by memorising model answers tend to stall here. Tutoring at this level is mostly argument structure and use of evidence, with accuracy assumed rather than taught.
programmes.countryNote: Some Abu Dhabi schools offer A Level Arabic and many do not, which is why students in this emirate often carry Arabic forward through the IB instead. Either route keeps the language on a transcript that a UAE university or a Gulf employer will read, and both start from the same 0508 foundation.

programmes.name: IB Arabic A: Language and Literature
programmes.description: The IB alternative for a first-language speaker, taken at HL or SL. Assessment rests on prescribed texts, comparative essay work and oral commentary rather than on a single composition paper, so the skills a 0508 student built transfer unevenly. The student who learned to summarise an argument transfers well; the student who relied on fixed phrases does not.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi IB World Schools run Arabic A, and families here usually choose between it and A Level Arabic in the spring of Year 11. We teach both, and the honest answer normally depends on which one your child's school actually timetables rather than on which looks stronger in the abstract.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-arabic-first-l.subjectsIntro: A 0508 problem rarely arrives alone. The Abu Dhabi families who ask for first-language Arabic support are usually managing two or three other subjects in the same exam year, and the scheduling matters nearly as much as the teaching. These are the components we are asked for most often alongside Arabic as a First Language 0508.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508): reading and summary
subjects.description: The comprehension passage and the summary task, where marks go to students who compress an argument into their own words. The common loss is lifting phrases from the passage, which earns little even when the content selected is right.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508): directed and extended writing
subjects.description: Composition under time, judged on content, structure and accuracy. Most recoverable marks sit in agreement, verb tense and sentence-length control rather than in ideas, which is why marking drafts beats generating new essay topics.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: The learner route, with listening and reading alongside writing. It matters on this page because heritage speakers are sometimes entered for it, and because siblings in one Abu Dhabi household are often split across the two syllabus codes.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.levels: School syllabus, Arabic medium for Arab students
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools and taught in Arabic for Arab students, so a slow Arabic reading speed shows up in this grade too. Support here is reading fluency and structured written answers rather than content recall.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Also required, and for Arab students taught primarily in Arabic. Students who are strong orally but slow readers lose marks on source-based questions rather than on knowledge, which is a reading-rate problem a 0508 tutor already works on.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: The subject most often paired with 0508 on an Abu Dhabi timetable. The two papers reward opposite instincts, since ESL rewards clarity and brevity while 0508 rewards developed register, and students sometimes carry the wrong habit into the wrong paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The scheduling partner rather than the content partner. It appears here because a Year 11 student with maths on Monday and Arabic on Wednesday needs protecting from a revision plan that silently hands every spare hour to maths.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Taken by many of the same students, with a near-identical summary skill assessed in the other language. Teaching the summary technique once and applying it in both languages is one of the few genuine shortcuts available in this exam year.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Included because extended-response marks in science depend on written precision. Students who tighten their Arabic composition in a term often tighten their science explanations in the same term, without anyone teaching the science differently.

Online delivery removes that distance. Here is how the geography affects a weekday session.

sections.heading: What a 0508 tutor costs in Abu Dhabi, and who publishes what
paragraphs: Start with the number, because most of this market refuses to. Rates for private tuition in the UAE separate into clear bands. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE support from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits, which carry the tutor's travel inside the price, are put at AED 180 to AED 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, and independent home tutors advertise up to AED 500 an hour.

First-language Arabic sits high within whichever band applies, and the reason is not prestige. The pool of people who can teach Modern Standard Arabic composition against a published mark scheme is far smaller than the pool who speak Arabic fluently, and most of the qualified ones already teach full timetables in private schools licensed by ADEK. Scarcity, not difficulty, is what the premium buys. An agency that quotes AED 180 for 0580 maths and AED 260 for 0508 Arabic is not claiming Arabic is harder; it is telling you how many people it can call.

What the figures below are not: our price list. These are market rates read off competitor pages and a published rate table, with the source named so you can check them yourself. Our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many hours the gap actually needs, because the honest answer for a Year 10 student who already writes accurately is often fewer hours than a family expects, and for a Year 11 student two months out it is often more than they want to hear.

Treat any quote that arrives without a named format, a session length and a stated number of weeks as incomplete. Three figures decide what you spend: the hourly rate, the length of the session and the number of weeks. Families negotiate hard on the first, accept the second without thinking, and underestimate the third, which is the one that decides the total.

sections.heading: Five things that move an Abu Dhabi 0508 quote
paragraphs: Two families on the same street in Khalifa City can be quoted rates that differ threefold for what looks like the same lesson, and the difference is almost never the quality of the tutor's Arabic. Five variables set the number. Four of them are yours to set, which makes a quote a negotiation about scope rather than a fixed price you either accept or refuse.

Scarcity is the variable you do not control. Fewer first-language Arabic specialists are free on an Abu Dhabi weekday evening than chemistry tutors, and the gap widens in the ten weeks before a series, when every Year 11 cohort in the emirate starts looking at once. Booking in September for a June paper costs less per hour than booking in April for the same person, for the same reason a flight does. The second variable is session length: a ninety-minute slot usually carries a lower effective hourly rate than a sixty-minute one, and for a writing subject it is also more useful, because a timed composition plus marking does not fit inside an hour.

The third is what the tutor is asked to do with the time. Vocabulary coaching is cheap to prepare and slow to show results. Criteria-based marking of a timed composition takes longer to prepare and shows results faster, and it is the thing a Year 11 grade actually responds to. The fourth is format: in-home rates carry travel across Abu Dhabi inside the hour, which is why the market charges AED 180 to AED 350 for a visit against AED 150 to AED 300 for the same teaching delivered online.

The fifth is who is being taught. Two children in one household on separate syllabus codes is two bookings with two specialists, not one shared hour at a discount. Agencies that offer the shared hour are usually putting a generalist in front of both, and on a language syllabus that is the single worst place to economise, because 0508 and 0544 reward opposite instincts.

sections.heading: Where an Arabic grade is counted, and where it is not
paragraphs: Before you decide how much to spend, it helps to know what the grade is for. The UAE Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements for the British track ask for passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That is sourced, and it is the opposite of what one ranking competitor publishes, which tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects.

What follows from that is narrow but useful. Money spent on 0508 is not money spent on equivalency, so no agency should sell you Arabic tuition on the grounds that your child's certificate will not be recognised without it. Equivalency is a Ministry process with its own channel, and no tutoring company performs it, speeds it up or guarantees its outcome. Describe it, check it on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation channel, and treat any urgency added by a sales conversation as a reason for scepticism.

The 0508 grade still matters, just elsewhere. It decides sixth-form progression at most Abu Dhabi schools, it is what an Arabic department reads before admitting a student to A Level Arabic or IB Arabic A, and it appears on a transcript that a UAE university or a Gulf employer may well read in Arabic. Those are real reasons to spend on it. The recognition of a British-track certificate is not one of them.

sections.heading: The two 0508 components, and which hours pay back fastest
paragraphs: 0508 is assessed by a reading paper and a writing paper. That sounds like two equal problems and is not. The reading paper contains a comprehension sequence and a summary task, and the summary task is the most teachable thing on the whole syllabus: it has a method, the method can be learned in a handful of sessions, and students who have never been taught it lose marks consistently rather than randomly. The usual error is reproducing the passage in the passage's own order and running out of space before the last point, which looks like a language problem and is actually a planning problem.

The writing paper is slower to move. Content and structure respond to teaching within a few drafts, because they are decisions a student makes before writing. Accuracy under time does not: agreement, tense and sentence control hold up in a relaxed homework and collapse in the exam room, which means the only treatment that works is weekly timed writing with the same criteria applied every time. A tutor who explains the rule again is not treating the problem. A tutor who makes your child write to the clock, then shows them their own three recurring errors in their own handwriting, is.

Register is the third issue and the one specific to heritage speakers in Abu Dhabi. A student who reads and speaks Arabic daily writes down spoken forms without noticing, because nothing in their environment flags them. Marks for standard written forms are lost silently. This is visible within a term of marked work and takes about that long to fix, which is why the autumn term of Year 11 is worth more than the spring term at the same price.
The ranking below is about rate of return, not importance. Spend the first block of hours where the marks come back quickest, then move to the slow work with whatever time is left.

paragraphs: An hourly rate is almost useless on its own. What a family needs is the total, set against the other numbers already in the household budget, and that total depends on arithmetic nobody in this market shows. The table below runs it at the middle of the published band, AED 200 an hour, so you can scale it to whatever quote you are holding. Nothing in it is our price list; it is the market band multiplied by a plan.

Two patterns come out of it. The first is that a term of weekly ninety-minute sessions costs roughly what two weeks of twice-weekly exam-term sessions cost, and buys considerably more change, because written accuracy responds to repetition over months rather than intensity over weeks. The family that starts in September spends less and gets more than the family that starts in April and panics. The second is that the in-home premium, across a full term, is large enough to notice: at the published visit rate, the travel built into the hour costs about the same as three extra sessions.

The one figure we will not estimate is the exam entry. Entry fees for a private candidate are set by the exam centre rather than by Cambridge, and they vary between centres in the same emirate, so ask the centre your child is entered through. If your child sits as a school candidate, the entry is normally inside the school fee and there is nothing extra to budget for, but the school's internal deadline for confirming it is often earlier than parents expect.

sections.heading: Permits, ethics, and why the cheapest 0508 quote in Abu Dhabi can be the riskiest
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through MoHRE, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

The enforcement position is equally plain and equally worth knowing: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting you an amount is guessing, and we will not repeat the figure circulating online. What matters for a parent is simpler. Ask the question. A tutor who holds the permit will answer it in a sentence, and the permit costs them nothing to hold.

Abu Dhabi adds a condition the rest of the country does not emphasise as sharply. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct has been reported as barring the same thing. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical rule holds either way: do not ask your child's own Arabic teacher to tutor your child for a fee, however convenient it looks, and be wary of any agency that offers to arrange it.

This is the real risk inside a very cheap quote. A rate well below the budget band usually means an unpermitted tutor, an unqualified one, or someone tutoring students they are not allowed to take. None of those three is a saving.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or a tuition centre: the Abu Dhabi arithmetic
paragraphs: Families here compare three things, so this page compares them honestly. Say the plain part first: IB Gram does not send a tutor to your address anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every 0508 lesson for an Abu Dhabi family is one-to-one and delivered over live video. That is a limit, and it is also the reason we can put a first-language Arabic specialist in front of a child in Al Reef on a Tuesday evening.

The in-home market in this emirate is real and it is priced accordingly. Bestimate's 2026 table puts a visit at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 for comparable qualified teaching online, and the gap is travel. Travel is not only money. A tutor who drives from the island to Khalifa City in the evening arrives inside a window rather than at a time, and a lesson that starts twelve minutes late ends twelve minutes early, because the next family is waiting. Across a term that is a session and a half of teaching lost to the Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Street at six o'clock.

The deeper difference is the pool. An in-home tutor must live within a reasonable drive of your community, which in practice means your child is taught by whichever Arabic specialist happens to live nearby and happens to be free. Online, the constraint is only the overlap with Gulf Standard Time, and the question becomes who has actually marked 0508 compositions. For a scarce language syllabus that is the whole argument, and it is why we took the decision this way round rather than defending it after the fact.

A tuition centre is the third option, cheaper per student and worse suited to this particular subject. Group teaching cannot mark twelve different compositions against the criteria in an hour, and 0508 marks move through individual marking. Use a centre for subjects where a worked example on a board helps everyone at once.

sections.heading: How many sessions a 0508 student needs, by starting point
paragraphs: Three starting points cover most of what we see in Abu Dhabi, and the honest hour counts differ by a factor of four. The first is the fluent speaker in Year 10 whose reports say the Arabic is strong and the marks say otherwise. This student usually needs the summary method and a term of marked composition: around twelve to sixteen sessions across two terms, mostly ninety minutes, with the heavier work in the autumn. Started early, this is the cheapest version of the problem and the one with the most predictable outcome.

The second is the student who arrived in the emirate during the course, often from a school with lighter Arabic provision or none. Here the gap is content as well as technique, and the work has to establish written forms before it can polish them. Expect twenty to thirty sessions, expect the first six to feel slow, and expect the school's entry decision between 0508 and 0544 to be live rather than settled. That decision is worth more than any six sessions, which is why we raise it in the trial lesson rather than after a month of teaching.

The third is the Year 11 student eight weeks from the paper. This is the version families ask about most and the version where honesty costs us money. Eight weeks of twice-weekly timed writing will reliably move the summary task and the structure marks on the composition. It will not reliably move deep accuracy, because accuracy under pressure is a habit built over months. We say so before the block is booked, and we aim the hours at what can actually move rather than selling the full course at a sprint.

If no first-language Arabic specialist is free in the slot an Abu Dhabi family needs, we say that too, with the next realistic slot and the option to wait. The alternative, putting a general Arabic speaker in front of a 0508 composition, is how families end up paying twice.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with your child's Arabic writing
paragraphs: This matters more on a language syllabus than on any other, because the deliverable looks like something a tutor could simply supply. A tutor may teach the form, model a paragraph on a different prompt, mark your child's own work against the published criteria, explain why a sentence lost a mark, and set the next timed task. A tutor may not supply sentences that go into something your child submits, rewrite a piece into a finished state, or hand over material to be copied. The line is not subtle, and it is the student who carries the consequence when it is crossed.

One site ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. We will not name it and we will not imitate it. Boards treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the penalty lands on the child, not on the person who sold it. Any tutoring page that offers to produce assessed work for you is telling you something useful about how it treats the rest of its promises.

In practice the boundary makes the teaching better rather than worse. A marked composition that still contains your child's own three recurring errors is diagnostic. A composition improved by someone else is a clean sheet of paper with no information in it. Parents who ask us to tidy a draft before it goes to school are usually asking for reassurance, and the useful answer is a marking record that shows the same error disappearing over four weeks.

You should expect to see that record. Every session produces something marked, the criteria used are the published ones, and the note that follows names what changed and what is next. If a tutor cannot show you which criterion a mark came off, there is nothing to audit and no way to tell whether the hours worked.

process.title: Send the syllabus code and the series
process.description: Send the code on your child's entry sheet, 0508 or 0544, the series the school has entered them for, and the most recent Arabic report or marked composition. That is enough to tell whether the problem is reading technique, written accuracy or register, which is what decides the number of hours and therefore the price.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson, with marking in it
process.description: The trial is a real lesson rather than a sales call. The tutor sets a short timed task, marks it against the published criteria while your child watches, and names the two things that would move the grade first. You hear the same summary afterwards, in the same words, with no plan attached yet.

process.title: Get a written plan with the price attached
process.description: The plan names the component to attack first, the number of sessions, the session length and what each week produces. The market rate context from this page sits beside it, so you can measure the quote against an Abu Dhabi agency rather than taking our word for what is reasonable.

process.title: Weekly sessions that end in marked work
process.description: Same tutor, same slot in Gulf Standard Time, over live video. Every session produces something marked, whether a summary, a paragraph or a full composition, plus a short note naming the next target. Nothing is marked that your child did not write, and nothing is written for them.

process.title: Review before the school's entry deadline
process.description: Before the final entry date we check whether the plan still fits: whether the component priority was right, whether the hours were enough, and whether the syllabus code on the entry sheet is still the right one to be sitting. Changing that code later costs far more than changing it now.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the competitor or rate table that published it, with the year attached. You can check them before you speak to us. Three of the six sites ranking for this query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.description: 0508 and 0544 are different syllabuses that reward different instincts, and we staff them separately rather than sending one Arabic speaker to both. Siblings in one household get two tutors and two trial lessons, scheduled back-to-back on the same evening so the household only loses one evening.

whyPoints.description: Sessions are built around your child's own writing, marked against the published criteria, with the criterion named for every mark lost. A plan measured in topics covered is easy to sell and hard to audit. A plan measured in marked compositions shows you whether the hours did anything.

whyPoints.title: Plain about what we do not do
whyPoints.description: We do not visit homes in the UAE, we hold no regulator or exam-board accreditation, and we do not supply sentences for work your child submits. Stating the limits is cheaper for everyone than discovering them in week three, and it is how the rest of our pages are written too.

whyPoints.description: Slots are booked in Gulf Standard Time, after the school run rather than during it, with later starts in Ramadan when families move study to after Iftar. School holidays and travel between the emirate and abroad are handled by moving the slot rather than losing the week.
