sections.heading: Academic honesty when the assessment is a portfolio
paragraphs: A written exam is hard to cheat at and a sketchbook is not, which is why Cambridge treats authenticity in coursework-based subjects seriously and why the school signs a declaration about the work it submits. The line is simple to state. The work must be the candidate's own. A tutor may teach, question, demonstrate, review and be blunt about quality. A tutor may not supply an image, a composition, a resolved outcome or a page of annotation for the candidate to copy, and no reputable tutor will offer to.

In practice the grey area is annotation, because a candidate who cannot articulate their reasoning will happily accept words put in their mouth. Our method is to ask the question and wait: what were you testing on this page, and what changed because of it. The candidate speaks, the tutor reflects it back, and the candidate writes it in their own words. It is slower than dictating a sentence and it is the only version that survives a conversation with a teacher who asks the same question.

Parents should also know what to look for in a provider. One operator ranking for UAE IB and IGCSE queries openly sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger that falls on the student rather than the seller, and a family who buys it is risking the entire qualification. Any service offering to supply finished assessed work, for any subject, should be treated as a red flag rather than a shortcut, however reassuring the website looks.

sections.heading: ADEK, the private tuition permit, and checking who is teaching your child
paragraphs: In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, private schools are supervised by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which the UAE government's own portal describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai has KHDA, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this cluster, which tells you how little localisation this part of the market has.

Private tutoring itself is permitted and regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you read with suspicion.

There is one condition Abu Dhabi families should know about. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical reading for a parent: your child's own art teacher is the wrong person to hire privately, and a tutor who offers that arrangement is telling you something about their judgement.

sections.heading: Does Art and Design count towards MoE equivalency?
paragraphs: This is the question that quietly worries Abu Dhabi parents into talking their child out of the subject, and the answer is better than the rumour. For the British track, the UAE Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements as reported in July 2026 ask students to pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

Nothing in that framework excludes Art and Design from the count of five. What it does mean is that the five have to be chosen with the eventual destination in mind, because a university course has its own subject prerequisites on top of equivalency. A candidate taking Art and Design plus four academic subjects is in a different position from one taking Art and Design plus three, and the conversation to have is with the school's university guidance office in Year 10, not in Year 13.

Two cautions. One ranking competitor publishes that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which contradicts the five-subject rule in the sourced reporting above, so do not take a tutoring website's word for a regulatory requirement, including this one. And no IB points threshold for equivalency should be believed unless you have read it on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's own attestation channel, because the published reporting on the American and British tracks states no IB figure at all. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs; no tutoring service performs it or can promise its outcome.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The honest version of the process is short. You tell us the school, the year group, the area of study and the supervised session window if the school has given one. The candidate photographs four or five sketchbook spreads, including the worst ones, because a curated upload wastes the diagnostic. A trial lesson is booked at a Gulf Standard Time slot that survives the school run. The tutor reads the upload before the hour starts, and the hour is spent on the weakest assessment objective rather than on introductions.

After the trial you get a written page plan and a straight answer about whether weekly review, a rehearsal block or nothing at all is the right call. Sometimes the answer is nothing at all: a candidate eight weeks from a supervised session with a strong sketchbook and a competent department does not need us, and saying so costs one trial lesson and buys a family's trust. The free trial is one lesson per family, booked without card details, and the condition is simply that it is a first session rather than a recurring entitlement.

Cambridge 0400 is a narrow specialism and availability is finite, so here is the fallback stated openly rather than buried. If no Art and Design specialist has a slot in the window you need, we say so at the point of enquiry instead of matching you with a general art teacher and hoping. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the match may be a specialist elsewhere teaching into Gulf Standard Time, and we tell you that before you book rather than after. No competitor in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

process.title: Tell us the school, the year and the window
process.description: The school sets the internal deadlines and the centre's zone sets the series, so those two facts shape everything. We also ask which area of study the candidate has committed to, because printmaking and lens-based media need different specialists and different planning horizons.

process.title: Upload the sketchbook, including the bad pages
process.description: Four or five spreads photographed in daylight, plus any work in progress. A curated upload produces a flattering diagnostic and a useless one. The tutor reads the pages before the session starts, so the hour itself is spent on judgement rather than on looking.

process.title: Take the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: One hour, one assessment objective, the weakest one. The candidate leaves with three named pages to make. One free trial lesson per family, booked without card details, and the honest outcome is sometimes that no tutoring is needed at all.

process.title: Agree a mode and a slot that survives the school run
process.description: Weekly review, a rehearsal block, or a transfer sprint. Slots run from late afternoon into the evening in Gulf Standard Time, and during Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing. The slot is held for the term rather than rebooked each week.

process.title: Rehearse the supervised session twice
process.description: Four weeks out and two weeks out, under the clock the school will actually impose and with the materials the candidate will actually have. The debrief after each one is written down, so the second rehearsal starts from the first one's failures.

process.title: Close the sketchbook a week early
process.description: Nothing new is started in the final week. The pages are ordered, numbered, annotated and photographed properly. This is the least glamorous session of the year and routinely the one that recovers the most marks across the organisation objective.

whyPoints.title: The feedback is objective by objective
whyPoints.description: A session names which of the four Cambridge assessment objectives is weakest and works on that one. Generic encouragement about a sketchbook is what the candidate already gets. A reading that separates research from development from organisation from materials is what changes the mark.

whyPoints.title: Timed rehearsal is built in, not optional
whyPoints.description: The supervised session is the component most candidates meet unrehearsed. Two full timed runs before the window, in the conditions the school will impose, is standard in our plans because it is the intervention with the clearest effect on a resolved outcome.

whyPoints.title: Local source material is part of the plan
whyPoints.description: Louvre Abu Dhabi, Manarat Al Saadiyat, Warehouse421 and Qasr Al Hosn are within reach of most of the emirate and are first-hand sources a candidate can legitimately record. Using them properly is a planning question, and we plan it rather than mention it.

whyPoints.title: The authorship line is held, in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, demonstrates and reviews. The candidate makes the work and writes their own annotation, in their own words, in every session. Any provider offering finished assessed work is a risk to the qualification rather than a shortcut to it.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: 0400 is a narrow specialism. If no specialist is free in the window you need, you hear that at enquiry, and if the match is a specialist teaching into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE you hear that too. No competitor page in this cluster states a coverage limit.

whyPoints.title: Everything is on the record for a parent
whyPoints.description: Marked-up uploads, page plans and rehearsal debriefs are dated and kept. A parent who wants to know whether a term of sessions moved anything can read the sequence rather than ask for a reassuring summary at the end of it.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge IGCSE Art and Design 0400 count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Nothing in the reported equivalency framework excludes it. For the British track, reporting from July 2026 describes a requirement to pass five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Art and Design can sit inside that five. University course prerequisites are a separate matter from equivalency, so check both. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae rather than on any tutoring website, including this one.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor review a sketchbook they cannot physically hold?
faqs.answer: The candidate photographs spreads in daylight and uploads them before the session. The tutor reads them in advance, then marks them on a shared screen with the candidate watching, zooming into a single study at a size no one achieves holding a book across a table. Demonstrations happen on the tutor's own paper under a second camera. The output is a saved, dated, annotated copy of every page discussed, which a parent can re-read. The one thing that cannot be done remotely is physical correction of a hand, and we say so when that is genuinely the problem.

faqs.question: What are the four assessment objectives in Cambridge 0400?
faqs.answer: They cover gathering, recording and research from first-hand sources; exploring and developing ideas; organising visual and other forms; and selecting and controlling materials, media and processes. In the current syllabus they carry an equal share of the marks, which means three quarters of the credit lives in the preparatory work rather than in the final outcome. That single fact reorders most candidates' priorities. Confirm the exact weightings against the syllabus edition your child's cohort is entered for, published on cambridgeinternational.org, because Cambridge revises syllabuses on a cycle.

faqs.question: My child's school has entered them for 0400 but we do not know which components they sit?
faqs.answer: Ask the art department, because the component combination is a decision the centre makes at entry and it is not something a parent can look up. The department also holds the internal deadlines and the supervised session window, both of which follow the Cambridge administrative zone the centre is allocated to. Cambridge places every centre in one of six timetable zones and states that using the wrong zone version of a timetable is the centre's risk. One email in the first term answers it; the same question in the second term answers it too late to change anything.

faqs.question: Can a 0400 tutor help with the externally set supervised assignment?
faqs.answer: With the preparation, yes, and that is where the work belongs. Before the window a tutor audits the preparatory studies for gaps, runs timed rehearsals under the clock the school will impose, and debriefs what ran out of time. During the supervised session itself the candidate is alone under the centre's conditions, which is the point of the component. Anyone offering help inside that window is describing malpractice rather than tutoring. Rehearsal beforehand is both legitimate and, in our experience of this subject, the single change with the clearest effect.

faqs.question: What does Art and Design tutoring cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates in the UAE run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE specialist, with in-home visits from about AED 180 to 500 once travel is inside the rate. Those are other providers' published figures as of October 2026, not ours. Creative coursework is often priced above a written subject because the tutor reads a long upload before the session, so ask any provider whether portfolio reading time sits inside the hour. We quote after a free trial and a diagnostic.

faqs.question: Is Art and Design a soft option for a Year 11 candidate in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It is not, and the workload shape is what catches families out. There is no single revision push that fixes an Art and Design grade, because the marks accumulate across months of preparatory study that cannot be recreated in April. A candidate who treats it as the easy subject in the block typically arrives at the supervised session with a thin sketchbook and loses marks in three objectives at once. Treated seriously it is one of the more predictable grades on a timetable, precisely because most of the credit is earned before any exam condition applies.

faqs.question: Where can an Abu Dhabi candidate gather genuine first-hand source material?
faqs.answer: Louvre Abu Dhabi and Manarat Al Saadiyat on Saadiyat Island, with Abu Dhabi Art at Manarat each November; Warehouse421 in the Mina Zayed district for contemporary regional practice; and Qasr Al Hosn and the Cultural Foundation for historic architecture and coral-stone surface. The recording matters more than the venue: drawings made on site, photographs taken by the candidate rather than lifted from a website, dates, and a written note on what was being looked for. Check each venue's current photography policy first, and plan on drawing where cameras are restricted.

faqs.question: Can a tutor suggest what my child should actually make for their 0400 outcome?
faqs.answer: A tutor can ask the questions that help a candidate find their own subject, show how other artists have handled a comparable problem, and say honestly when an idea is too thin to sustain a term of development. What a tutor must not do is hand over the idea, the composition or the image. The work is assessed as the candidate's own and the school signs a declaration to that effect. In practice the useful session is the one where the tutor asks what the candidate keeps photographing without noticing, and then waits.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the supervised session should 0400 support start?
faqs.answer: Twelve weeks out is comfortable, eight is workable, four is a rescue. At twelve weeks the area of study and the enquiry can still change and the preparatory studies can be built properly. At eight weeks the plan becomes fixing the weakest objective and getting two timed rehearsals in. At four weeks the honest offer is a rehearsal block and an audit of what already exists, not a new direction. A family who starts in the first term of Year 11 rather than the second pays for fewer hours in total.

faqs.question: Does my child need expensive materials to score well in 0400?
faqs.answer: No, and the assumption costs marks in a different way. The materials objective rewards informed choice and technical control, not cost. A candidate who tests three cheap media on the page, labels what each test was for, and then commits to one with reasons will out-score a candidate using expensive materials with no evidence of selection. Constraints are legitimate content: a candidate in an apartment who cannot use solvent-based media should write that down as a stated reason for a media decision rather than leave it looking like a gap.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge exam series do Abu Dhabi schools enter for Art and Design?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE series in June and November, and most Abu Dhabi centres on a September-to-June year enter the June series. Your centre is allocated to one of six administrative timetable zones and Cambridge is explicit that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used, stating it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. The administrative dates sit far earlier than families expect: for the March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 against an exam period starting 3 February 2027.

faqs.question: Our studio time collapses during Ramadan - can 0400 sessions move later in the evening?
faqs.answer: Yes. Session times move to post-Iftar slots through Ramadan, which in practice means a later start and often a shorter, sharper hour. For Art and Design the bigger issue is that school timetables compress and studio access shrinks at exactly the point preparatory studies need building, so we usually front-load material tests before Ramadan and use the month for annotation, selection and sequencing work that needs a screen rather than a sink. Reduced-hours weeks are planned around rather than lost, and the slot returns to its normal time afterwards.

faqs.question: What happens if no Cambridge 0400 specialist is free when we enquire?
faqs.answer: You hear that at the point of enquiry rather than after a payment. Art and Design is a narrow specialism and the pool of tutors who have genuinely taught or marked 0400 is small, so the first option we offer is a different weekday slot with the right specialist rather than the right slot with the wrong one. Where no UAE-based specialist is available, the match may be a specialist teaching into Gulf Standard Time from elsewhere, and that is disclosed before you book. No competitor page researched for this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with Abu Dhabi families need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published you should distrust any specific amount quoted to you. Verify on mohre.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Should my child switch from an MYP arts cohort into Cambridge 0400 mid-course?
faqs.answer: That is a school decision rather than a tutoring one, and it happens often in this emirate because some Abu Dhabi schools run MYP through Year 11 while others move to IGCSE at Year 10. If it happens, the first sessions should be spent translating the existing body of work into Cambridge assessment language rather than making anything new. An MYP process journal usually contains strong reflective writing and thinner sustained observational drawing, so the recoverable marks sit in re-reading and re-presenting work the candidate already owns.

intro.heading: Price first, because almost every page in this search refuses
paragraphs: Three of the six highest-ranking pages for Abu Dhabi science tutoring publish no price at all. Two quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. One asks the price in its own frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. That silence is a choice, and it costs parents weeks: you cannot compare a tuition centre, an agency and an independent tutor if only one of the three will say a number. So this page starts with the market rates in AED, states where each figure came from, and only then explains what a Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 tutor actually does with the money.

The honest framing is that there is no single rate for 0610. The band published across UAE providers for qualified science tuition runs from roughly AED 150 an hour at the lower end of the qualified-tutor tier to AED 450 and above for specialist exam-year work, and the gap is not arbitrary. It tracks six things: the tutor's subject depth, whether the entry is Core or Extended, which practical component the school has entered, how close the series is, how long each session runs, and whether anyone is being paid to sit in traffic. Abu Dhabi adds a seventh, which is scarcity. The emirate has a smaller independent tutoring market than Dubai, and a Biology specialist who knows the 0610 mark scheme is harder to find inside a twenty-minute drive of Khalifa City than inside the same radius of Jumeirah.

That scarcity is the single clearest argument for delivering lessons over live video rather than in person, and it is worth being direct about it. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE lesson runs one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The result for an Al Shamkha or Al Reef family is not a compromise. It is access to a Biology specialist who has worked through hundreds of 0610 scripts, instead of whichever generalist happens to live nearby and is free at six in the evening.

Abu Dhabi has its own regulator, and it matters for cost in a way parents rarely hear about. The Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical effect is that the obvious cheap option, your child's own Biology teacher after hours, is not an option in Abu Dhabi, and the supply of permitted local specialists is correspondingly thinner.

What follows is costed, not estimated. There is a rate table by provider model with sources. There is a component table showing which 0610 papers your child sits and what each one needs, because an Extended candidate sitting Paper 4 and Paper 5 is buying different hours from a Core candidate sitting Paper 3 and Paper 6. There is a section on everything that is not on the tutor's invoice, from private-candidate entry fees to re-mark charges. And there is a plain statement of the permit position, with the official application route, so you can check who you are hiring rather than taking anyone's word for it.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-t.programmesIntro: Biology 0610 sits inside a longer route, and the cost of support changes at each stage. A Year 10 student buying consolidation hours is not in the same market as a Year 11 candidate eight weeks from a series, and an AS Level student carrying a weak 0610 foundation is buying remediation on top of new content. These are the stages Abu Dhabi families most often ask us to cost.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE (Core and Extended)
programmes.description: The two-year course that ends in the 0610 certificate. Candidates follow either the Core route, which is assessed by Paper 1 and Paper 3, or the Extended route, assessed by Paper 2 and Paper 4, and both add a practical component. Core caps the available grade; Extended opens the full range. Confirm which route your child's school has entered them for on the statement of entry rather than assuming, because set placement and entry code are decided separately and families are often surprised.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools licensed by ADEK run both routes, and the mix is school-specific rather than emirate-wide. Schools in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor with large Year 11 cohorts often stream by attainment early, while some island schools delay the decision until the end of Year 10. If the entry is still open, a term of targeted support is cheaper than a late tier change and far cheaper than a resit.

programmes.name: The combined and coordinated science alternatives
programmes.description: Not every Abu Dhabi student takes separate Biology. Combined Science 0653 awards one grade across biology, chemistry and physics; Coordinated Sciences 0654 awards two. A family weighing separate 0610 against one of these is weighing three sets of tutoring hours against one or two, and the arithmetic usually decides the question faster than the prospectus does. Work out what the certificate needs to open before you cost the hours.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the choice is often made by timetable capacity rather than by preference, particularly in schools where the science department runs limited separate-science sets. Where a student has been placed on a combined route but wants A Level Biology at a school such as Cranleigh Abu Dhabi or The British School Al Khubairat, the gap to close is specific and can be costed as a block of hours rather than an open-ended commitment.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology
programmes.description: The 9700 syllabus assumes the Extended 0610 content as a floor and then moves quickly into biochemistry, transport mechanisms and statistical treatment of data. Students who passed 0610 on recall rather than reasoning find the first AS term expensive, because they are paying someone to reteach foundations while new material arrives weekly. Spending on 0610 reasoning in Year 11 is almost always cheaper than spending on AS remediation in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi sixth forms feed Khalifa University, UAE University and the international applications that run through school counsellors. Universities publish their own subject requirements and these change, so check the current published entry criteria for each programme directly rather than relying on a tutoring page. What a tutor can do is make the AS prerequisite genuinely secure before the course starts.

programmes.name: IB MYP sciences, for students crossing over
programmes.description: Some Abu Dhabi students move from an IB Middle Years Programme science course into a Cambridge IGCSE entry, usually at a school change. MYP assesses against criteria and rewards investigation design and reflection; 0610 rewards precise recall and tight command-term answers. The transition is not a knowledge gap so much as an answer-style gap, and it is one of the cheapest things to fix because it responds to marked practice rather than reteaching.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has both IB and Cambridge schools within a few kilometres of each other, so mid-course moves happen more often here than the curriculum literature suggests. A student arriving from an MYP cohort in Al Reem Island into a Cambridge Year 11 set in Khalifa City typically needs a short diagnostic block, not a two-year programme, and should be quoted on that basis.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-t.subjectsIntro: Families rarely buy one subject. The common Abu Dhabi pattern is Biology plus one other science, or Biology plus Mathematics, and the cost of the second subject is usually lower than the first because the diagnostic work is already done. These are the codes most often requested alongside 0610.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Twenty-one topic areas with a heavy recall load and a reasoning layer on top. The expensive weaknesses are enzyme and transport explanations, genetics crosses written without working, and data questions where the student describes a graph instead of explaining it. All three respond to marked practice rather than reteaching.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Pairs with Biology for medicine and life-science routes. The costly gaps are mole calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables, and they compound: a student who cannot balance an equation loses marks across half the paper, so hours bought early go further than hours bought in April.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: The third separate science. Marks concentrate in formula selection, unit handling and graph gradient work. For a family already paying for Biology, Physics is often the better second purchase because its failure modes are narrower and therefore quicker to close.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Two grades covering all three sciences. Students on this route who want A Level Biology need the 0610 reasoning depth that the coordinated syllabus treats more lightly, and that specific gap can be quoted as a defined block of hours.

subjects.name: Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: One grade for three sciences. The commonest cost question is whether one tutor can cover all three, and the answer depends on which of the three is actually failing. Diagnose before you buy a triple-subject package.

subjects.name: Physical Science (0652)
subjects.description: Chemistry and physics without biology, offered by a small number of schools. Families who find themselves on this route usually need help identifying which half of the paper is losing marks before any hours are committed.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The most frequent second purchase alongside Biology, because the data-handling and ratio work in 0610 depends on it. A student who cannot reliably calculate a percentage change will lose 0610 data marks that look like biology marks on a report.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Year 11 sets heading for A Level sciences. Worth costing only once the core subjects are secure; it is an enrichment purchase, not a remedial one.

subjects.name: Environmental Management (0680)
subjects.description: Overlaps 0610 ecology and human-impact content, so a student taking both can often be supported in shared sessions. That overlap is one of the few genuine ways to reduce total tutoring spend without reducing hours on biology.

subjects.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology (9700)
subjects.description: The continuation route. Early AS support is frequently bought to repair 0610 foundations rather than to teach new AS content, which is why spending in Year 11 is the cheaper option.

subjects.name: IB DP Biology
subjects.description: Requested by Abu Dhabi families whose children move from a Cambridge Year 11 into an IB Diploma. The content overlap is real but the assessment style differs sharply, and the internal assessment is where the hours go.

regions.note: Dense central housing with short school runs, so an in-home tutor loses less time here than almost anywhere else in the emirate. That is also why local in-home rates hold at the upper end: demand is high and the travel cost is low enough that tutors can fill an evening.

regions.note: Long-established family villas within reach of several British-curriculum schools. Families here often start with one subject and add a second mid-year, and the second subject should be quoted lower because the diagnostic work is already done.

regions.note: A large Year 10 and 11 population and a long drive from the island. An in-home tutor crossing from central Abu Dhabi charges for that drive whether the quote names it or not, which is where the gap between an AED 200 and an AED 350 hour often sits.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Villa and apartment communities with a heavy school-run pattern. A 4pm session is unrealistic for most households here; evenings from 6pm onwards work, and a video lesson is the only format that reliably holds that slot without a surcharge.

regions.name: Yas Island and Al Zeina
regions.note: Access is straightforward but the distances are real. Families here are among the quickest to switch to video delivery once they have costed the travel component of an in-home quote across a full term rather than a single lesson.

regions.name: Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Zayed City
regions.note: Fast-growing mainland communities where the local pool of permitted Biology specialists is thinnest. This is where the scarcity premium on an in-home rate bites hardest, and where online delivery changes the available choice most.

regions.name: Al Reef, Al Samha and Al Ghadeer

regions.note: Mixed housing with several large-cohort schools nearby. Group classes are common and cheap, and they suit consolidation; they do not suit a student whose problem is that nobody has read their written answers closely.

sections.heading: What an hour of 0610 support actually costs in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Qualified one-to-one science tuition in the UAE is published between roughly AED 150 and AED 300 an hour online, and between roughly AED 200 and AED 450 an hour for specialist exam-year work. Those are market figures taken from providers' own published pages, not an IB Gram price list. The table below sets them out by provider model with the source attached, because a number without a source is worth very little when you are comparing four quotes.

Read the table as a map of what you are buying rather than a ranking. The budget tier exists and it is legitimate for some purposes: a university student who sat 0610 four years ago can drill recall effectively and cheaply. What that tier generally does not include is marking written answers against the current Cambridge command terms, which is the work that moves an Extended candidate from a 5 to a 7. The specialist tier charges for exactly that, and if a quote in the specialist band does not include marked written work between sessions, the premium is not buying you anything.

The in-home column deserves separate attention in this emirate. Published in-home rates sit above the online equivalent for the same tutor quality, and the difference is travel. A tutor driving from the island to Al Shamkha and back loses most of an hour in each direction, and that hour is priced into the lesson whether the quote names it or not. Across a thirty-week year the travel component alone can exceed the cost of a full exam-term intensive block. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and families who cost the travel line honestly rarely ask for them twice.

One more thing the table cannot show: availability. A rate is only real if someone is free at the time you need. In February and March, evening slots in the 6pm to 9pm Gulf Standard Time window are the scarce resource in Abu Dhabi, not the tutors themselves. Families who book a block in November pay the quiet-season rate and get the slot they want; families who start in March pay more for less convenient timing.

sections.heading: The seven variables that move a 0610 quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Two Abu Dhabi tutors can quote AED 180 and AED 400 for what sounds like the same lesson, and both can be quoting fairly. The difference is usually not quality in the abstract but a combination of seven measurable things, and a parent who asks about each one directly gets a comparable set of quotes instead of a set of numbers.

The first is subject depth: a general science tutor and a Biology specialist who works through 0610 scripts weekly are different purchases. The second is the entry route, because a Core candidate and an Extended candidate are preparing different papers. The third is the practical component, since Paper 5 and Paper 6 demand different preparation and the school decides which one your child sits. The fourth is proximity to the series, and rates across the UAE market do rise as a session approaches because evening demand rises. The fifth is session length, because a 90-minute slot allows a full paper section sat to time and a 45-minute slot does not.

The sixth is travel, which exists in every in-home quote in Abu Dhabi whether or not it appears as a line item. The seventh is scarcity, and this is the one specific to the emirate. Abu Dhabi's independent tutoring market is smaller than Dubai's, and the ADEK professional-ethics position reported in the press removes the most convenient local supply, because school staff may not take paid private work with students enrolled at their own school. Fewer permitted local specialists chasing the same February evening slots means a higher local rate for the same work.

There is an eighth variable that nobody prices, and it is the one that actually determines value: how much of your child's written work comes back marked. Ask every provider that question before you compare anything else. A cheaper tutor who marks three written answers a week is better value than an expensive one who marks none, and the difference will show on a mock script long before it shows on a bank statement.

sections.heading: Which papers your child sits, and what each one costs in hours
paragraphs: You cannot cost 0610 support sensibly without knowing which three components your child is entered for. Cambridge assesses the syllabus through a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component, with separate versions for Core and Extended candidates. The statement of entry from the school carries the answer. Ask for it before you book anything, and confirm the current component structure and weightings for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org, because syllabus versions change.

The reason this matters financially is that the three components absorb very different amounts of tutoring. The multiple-choice paper responds to recall drilling, which is the cheapest hour on the table and the one a budget-tier tutor can deliver competently. The theory paper is where the specialist rate earns its money, because the marks there are won by writing precise answers to command terms and lost by writing vaguely correct ones. The practical component is narrow, technical and highly coachable, and it is the one families most often ignore until February despite it carrying a fifth of the grade.

A worked example makes the arithmetic visible. Take an Extended candidate sitting Paper 2, Paper 4 and Paper 6, currently at a grade 5 with a theory-paper problem. Hours on multiple-choice recall will move very little, because that is not where the marks are leaking. Hours on written command-term work and marked practice answers will. A plan that spends two thirds of its hours on Paper 4 technique and the remainder on Paper 6 question types is a smaller plan than a general revision programme and will usually cost less while doing more.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the ceiling you are paying to raise
paragraphs: The Core and Extended decision is the largest single cost variable in 0610 support, and it is often treated as an administrative detail. Core assessment covers the core syllabus content and caps the grade available; Extended covers the supplementary content as well and opens the full range. A family paying for tutoring without knowing which route the school has entered is buying hours against an unknown target.

Three situations recur in Abu Dhabi. The first is a student in a Core set who needs Extended for an A Level science route, where the question is whether the school will move them and what evidence it wants. That is the cheapest problem to solve early and the most expensive to solve in March, because a late tier change means covering supplementary content at speed on top of normal revision. The second is a student in an Extended set who is not coping, where the honest answer may be that a secure Core grade serves them better than a struggling Extended entry. The third is a student correctly placed on Extended whose grade has stalled, which is a technique problem rather than a tier problem.

Each situation carries a different price. Moving tiers upward is a content purchase measured in terms, not weeks. Stabilising a struggling Extended candidate is a technique purchase measured in marked scripts. Deciding between the two is a diagnostic purchase of three or four sessions. Knowing which conversation you are in before you ask for a quote is worth more than any discount you will negotiate.

One caution applies throughout. No tutor can promise a tier change, a grade or a specific improvement, and any provider that does is selling something they cannot deliver. What a tutor can do is produce the marked evidence a head of science actually responds to when deciding a set or an entry, and set out honestly how many weeks of work that evidence typically takes to assemble.

sections.heading: What is not on the tutor's invoice
paragraphs: Parents budget for the hourly rate and are then surprised by everything else. Some of these costs are unavoidable, some are optional, and a few only appear if something goes wrong, but all of them belong in the plan before you commit to a term of lessons.

The first is examination entry itself. For a candidate entered by their school the entry sits inside the school's fee structure, and in Abu Dhabi private school fees operate under ADEK's framework, with schools applying to the regulator rather than setting increases freely. Confirm the current position with the school's finance office rather than with a tutoring page. For a private candidate sitting outside a school, entry is arranged and paid through a registered examination centre, and the centre sets its own administration charge on top of the Cambridge fee. That route is more common in Abu Dhabi than people expect, usually for a resit or a retake in a different series.

The second is the material. A tutor may reference and link the official Cambridge syllabus and specimen material, and should direct you to cambridgeinternational.org to obtain it, but reproducing or supplying syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads is a copyright matter and we do not do it. Your child's school has legitimate access to practice material through its Cambridge centre, and asking the science department for it costs nothing.

The third is what happens after results. A review of marking has a published cost and a short deadline, and the request goes through the school as the centre rather than directly from a parent. A resit in a later series means another entry fee and, usually, another block of tutoring hours. Both are a reason to spend earlier rather than later: the cheapest version of a 0610 plan is the one that does not need a second attempt. Figures for entry, review and resit charges vary by centre and by series, so get them in writing from the school or centre rather than from any provider.

sections.heading: Why Abu Dhabi pays a scarcity premium, and how a family avoids it
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's independent tutoring market is smaller than Dubai's, and the effect on price is straightforward. Fewer permitted Biology specialists are available in the emirate, demand concentrates into the same early-evening window, and the rate for a specialist hour in February reflects that. This is a supply problem, and families keep trying to solve it by paying more rather than by widening the pool.

Two structural facts narrow the local pool further. The private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 defines who may legally provide private lessons, and that is a boundary rather than an inconvenience: a tutor without a permit is not a cheaper option, they are an unpermitted one. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics position as reported in the press bars private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify both against the current source documents. Between them, the two rules remove the most obvious local supply from the market.

Online delivery is the answer that costs less rather than more, and it is worth stating plainly why. A video lesson removes the travel component from the rate, removes the geographic limit on who can teach your child, and removes the scheduling fragility that comes from a tutor crossing the emirate in evening traffic. A family in Al Falah or Al Ghadeer gets the same access to a 0610 specialist as a family in Al Bateen, at the same rate, in the slot they actually wanted.

To be unambiguous about what is being sold: IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Abu Dhabi, and we do not arrange home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service offered only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We say so before you book rather than after, because the commonest complaint about tutoring agencies in this market is discovering the delivery model late.

sections.heading: Permits, invoices and what a free trial has to tell you
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is one of the few places where a parent can check something concrete rather than taking a claim on trust. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow for cost. First, nobody should be charging you for the permit, because the permit itself carries no fee. Second, a tutor who tells you no permit is needed is wrong: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you either, and a provider quoting one is guessing.

On invoicing, ask for the rate, the session length, the number of sessions, and whether the figure is per hour or per lesson, in writing, before the first paid session. Ask specifically whether marking of written work between sessions is included at that rate or billed separately. On VAT, the correct answer from any provider is whether their own quoted price includes it; the general tax treatment of tuition in the UAE is a question for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance rather than for a tutoring page, and we do not state it as fact here.

A trial lesson is genuinely free only if the conditions are on the same screen as the word. Ours is one session, with no card details required to book it, no automatic conversion into a paid block, and a written summary afterwards of what the session found. If a competing offer uses the word free, ask what the condition is, because there usually is one.

sections.heading: The line a 0610 tutor does not cross, and why it protects your spend
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Biology does not carry an internal assessment in the way an IB Diploma subject does, but 0610 students still produce practical write-ups, coursework-style tasks set by the school, and prepared work for the practical component. The boundary around that work is not a formality. A tutor teaches method, explains why a particular control variable matters, reviews a student's own draft and gives feedback on it. A tutor does not write it, complete it, or produce a version for the student to submit. We will not do that, and no amount of exam pressure changes the answer.

This matters commercially as well as ethically. There are providers in this market selling completed assessed work, and one published rate card for finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. A family who buys that has bought an academic-malpractice exposure for their child and a document that teaches them nothing. The marks on a practical paper come from understanding method well enough to write about an unfamiliar experiment under time, which is precisely the skill that cannot be bought ready-made.

What a tutor can legitimately do with practical work is substantial and is where some of the best value in a 0610 plan sits. Reading a student's own method and asking where the error would come from. Working through how to record results so that the recording convention itself does not lose marks. Practising the written questions about variables, reliability and improvement that the alternative-to-practical paper is built from. All of that is teaching, all of it is attributable to the student's own work, and all of it shows up in marks.

The same boundary applies to materials. We reference the official Cambridge syllabus and specimen papers and point you to the source; we do not reproduce or distribute them. If a provider offers you a bundle of past papers and mark schemes as a selling point, note that they are distributing material they do not own, and ask yourself what else they are relaxed about.

sections.heading: A Cambridge series counted backwards, and why early hours cost less
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and the entry deadline for any series sits months before the first paper. The published key dates for the March 2027 series make the shape unmistakable: the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades were due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Always use the official dates for your child's own series and zone from cambridgeinternational.org rather than a restatement.

Read that sequence as a budget, not a calendar. The decisions that cost the most to change, the entry code and the tier, are locked by the entry deadline, which falls roughly two months before the papers. A family that starts tutoring after the mock in January has already passed the point where the cheap decisions were available and is now paying for the expensive ones. The same hours bought in September would have been spent on content and tier evidence; bought in February they are spent on triage.

There is also a timetable trap worth knowing about. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your child's school which zone the centre sits in, and work from the school's own copy of the timetable. A revision plan built on the wrong zone's dates is a plan built on sand.

For planning purposes, the practical sequence for an Abu Dhabi family is simple. Confirm the series and the component entries in the autumn term. Buy a diagnostic block early enough that tier evidence is still useful. Keep the exam-term intensive to a fixed hour count agreed in advance. And build in the Ramadan shift, because revision rhythm in the UAE changes for several weeks and a plan that ignores it will quietly lose a fortnight of work.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates for qualified one-to-one science tuition run from roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online, rising to roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above for specialist exam-year work. Those are providers' own published figures as at October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. In-home rates sit higher, between roughly AED 180 and AED 500, because travel is priced into the lesson whether or not the quote says so. For an accurate figure, send the statement of entry showing which 0610 components your child sits, a recent marked script and the school report, then ask for the rate and hour count in writing.

faqs.question: Why do two Abu Dhabi tutors quote AED 180 and AED 400 for the same 0610 lesson?
faqs.answer: Seven things usually explain the gap, and both quotes can be fair. Subject depth, whether the entry is Core or Extended, which practical component the school entered, how close the series is, session length, travel, and the local scarcity of permitted Biology specialists in this emirate. Ask about each one and the quotes become comparable. Then ask the question nobody prices: how many of your child's written answers come back marked each week. A cheaper tutor who marks three answers weekly is usually better value than an expensive one who marks none, and the difference shows on a mock script.

faqs.question: Which 0610 papers will my child actually sit, and does that change the price?
faqs.answer: It changes it significantly. Core candidates sit a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper; Extended candidates sit the extended versions of both. All candidates add a practical component, either the practical test or the alternative to practical, decided by the centre. The multiple-choice paper responds to recall drilling, the cheapest effective hour available. The theory paper is where specialist rates earn their money, because marks there turn on precise command-term writing. Confirm the components on the statement of entry and check the current structure and weightings for your series on cambridgeinternational.org before planning hours.

faqs.question: Is the Paper 6 alternative to practical cheaper to prepare for than the practical test?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, and it is often the best value block of hours in a 0610 plan. The alternative to practical asks written questions about method, variables, sources of error and improvements, and those question types are narrow, repeatable and highly coachable. The practical test needs apparatus technique, recording conventions and observational drawing, which takes more sessions to build. Either way the component carries about a fifth of the grade, so a plan that ignores it until February is leaving accessible marks on the table. The school decides which one your child sits, not you.

faqs.question: Does moving my child from Core to Extended 0610 cost more in tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the cost rises sharply with delay. An upward tier move means covering the supplementary content as well as the core, which is a purchase measured in terms rather than weeks. Done at the end of Year 10, before entries close, it is a manageable block. Attempted in February it means learning new content on top of full revision, which is both expensive and risky. No tutor can promise a school will move a set. What a tutor can do is produce the marked evidence a head of science responds to, and say honestly how many weeks that typically takes.

faqs.question: Does ADEK stop a school teacher from becoming our paid 0610 tutor?
faqs.answer: Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi are barred from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document. The practical consequence for a parent budgeting is that the convenient cheap option is not available in this emirate, which is part of why local specialist rates hold firm in the exam term.

faqs.question: Do 0610 tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi go up closer to the June series?
faqs.answer: Rates across the UAE market do move with demand, and demand concentrates in the weeks before a series. The scarcer resource is not tutors in general but evening slots in the 6pm to 9pm Gulf Standard Time window, which is when most Abu Dhabi families can actually sit down. Booking a block in the autumn term secures the quiet-season rate and the slot you want. Starting in February means paying more for less convenient timing, and spending those hours on triage rather than on the content and tier decisions that were available earlier.

faqs.question: Is a group science class at an Abu Dhabi centre better value for 0610?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong. A group class is good at coverage: getting through topics, keeping pace, maintaining revision rhythm, and it is cheaper per student. It is poor at precision, because nobody is reading your child's written answers closely. If a mock shows gaps in topic knowledge, a group may be enough. If it shows technically correct answers scoring two marks out of four, the problem is written expression against command terms, and that only improves when someone marks the work. Ask any group provider how much individual written work is marked per student per week.

faqs.question: What costs should I budget for beyond the 0610 tutor's hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Examination entry, which sits inside the school's fee structure for a school candidate or runs through a registered examination centre with its own administration charge for a private candidate. Review of marking after results, which has a published cost, a short deadline, and must be requested through the school as the centre. A resit in a later series, which means another entry fee and usually more hours. Practice material, which your child's school can access legitimately through its Cambridge centre. Get entry, review and resit figures in writing from the school or centre, because they vary by centre and series.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with Abu Dhabi families need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure quoted to you as unverified. The application route is on mohre.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Are lessons for 0610 delivered at our villa in Khalifa City or Al Raha?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. Every UAE lesson runs one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. For a Khalifa City or Al Raha family that is usually the better outcome rather than a compromise, because it removes the travel premium from the rate, removes the geographic limit on which Biology specialist can teach your child, and holds the early-evening slot reliably instead of depending on a tutor crossing the emirate in traffic.

faqs.question: How many hours of 0610 support does a stuck grade usually take to move?
faqs.answer: Nobody can answer that honestly without seeing a marked script, and any provider who quotes a number before looking is selling rather than diagnosing. What is predictable is the shape. A recall problem responds to drilling and shows movement within a few weeks. A written-precision problem on the theory paper needs marked practice answers over a longer run, because the student has to learn what each command term is paying for. A tier gap is a content purchase measured in terms. Buy a short diagnostic block first and get the hours estimate in writing.

faqs.question: Can we pause 0610 sessions during Ramadan and resume afterwards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning for it beats discovering it. Revision rhythm across the UAE changes for several weeks, school days shorten and energy in the late afternoon drops, so sessions commonly move to a later evening slot after Iftar rather than stopping altogether. Where a family does prefer to pause, the block should be rescheduled rather than written off, and the hour count agreed in writing makes that straightforward. A revision plan that ignores these weeks will quietly lose a fortnight of work in the run-up to a June series.

faqs.question: Will a 0610 tutor send us Cambridge past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering them as a selling point is distributing material they do not own. We reference the official Cambridge syllabus and specimen material and point you to cambridgeinternational.org to obtain it. Your child's school has legitimate access to practice material through its Cambridge centre, and the science department will usually share it on request at no cost. What a tutor adds is not access to papers but marking against the command terms, which is the part that actually moves a theory-paper grade.

faqs.question: Can a 0610 tutor help write up my child's practical work?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches method, explains why a control variable matters, reviews your child's own draft and gives feedback on it. A tutor does not write it, complete it or produce a version to submit, and we will not do that at any price. There are providers in this market selling finished assessed work, one at a published AED 3,750, and a family buying that has bought an academic-malpractice exposure rather than a grade. The marks come from understanding method well enough to write about an unfamiliar experiment under time, which cannot be bought ready-made.

faqs.question: What happens if no Cambridge 0610 Biology specialist is free when we enquire?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of substituting quietly. Demand for Biology specialists in the Gulf Standard Time evening window peaks between January and April, and in those weeks the honest answer is sometimes a wait of a few days or a different slot. Where that happens you are told the wait, offered the nearest available alternative and told plainly what that alternative does and does not cover, before anything is paid. Being told about a coverage limit before booking is the point; no competitor page found in this market discloses one at all.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-t.closingBody: You came here for a price, so take the price with you: roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for qualified online science tuition in this market, rising towards AED 450 and above for specialist exam-year work, with in-home rates higher because travel is in them. What turns that band into your number is which 0610 components your child sits, whether the entry is Core or Extended, and how many weeks remain before the series. Send the statement of entry, a marked script and the school report, take the trial session, read the written summary, and agree the hours in writing. If the answer is that you do not need a tutor yet, we will tell you that too.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-business-studi.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies to Year 10 and Year 11 students in Abu Dhabi schools. Each one works from the 0450 syllabus and the published mark schemes, marks timed answers between lessons, and reports back on which assessment objective is costing marks.

intro.heading: What a 0450 tutor costs in Abu Dhabi, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Start with the figure, because that is what the search was about. Across published UAE provider rate pages read in October 2026, hourly tuition for a Cambridge IGCSE subject in Abu Dhabi runs from roughly AED 45 at the student-tutor end to AED 650 at the named-specialist end. For Business Studies specifically, most Abu Dhabi families end up transacting somewhere between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, because 0450 is taught by subject specialists rather than general maths-and-science tutors, and because the marking workload between lessons is real rather than decorative.

The spread is wide for reasons you can control. A Year 10 student starting in September, two terms clear of any exam, needs fewer hours and less urgency than a Year 11 student eight weeks out from the June series. A tutor who only teaches is cheaper per hour than one who also marks two timed Paper 2 answers each week and writes back on them. A single weekly hour costs less than a block bought for the final stretch. Two siblings sharing one slot splits the rate without halving the attention, provided they sit the same paper in the same series.

What IB Gram sells in the UAE is one-to-one teaching delivered live over video, screen shared, with the student's own script on the screen. IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; that service exists only in India. For 0450 this is less of a compromise than parents expect and often an improvement, because the thing a Business Studies candidate needs is somebody who can mark a case-study answer line by line in front of them, and a shared screen does that better than a notebook passed across a table.

The teaching itself is narrower than the subject title suggests. Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450 is assessed by two written papers of ninety minutes each, four twenty-mark questions in each, with no coursework to submit at any point. Almost all the grade movement a tutor can produce sits in the later parts of those questions, where the command word turns from define to analyse and then to recommend. A student who knows every definition in the glossary and still scores in the fives is losing marks on structure, not on knowledge, and that is a diagnosable, teachable problem.

Abu Dhabi adds its own variables. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools and publishes its own inspection outcomes. School weeks, holiday dates and internal mock calendars therefore differ from Dubai's in ways that matter when you book a slot. The practical effect is that a session that works for a family in Khalifa City at 5pm may be impossible for one on Al Reem Island, and both are solved by scheduling rather than by paying more.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-business-studi.programmesIntro: 0450 sits in the middle of a Cambridge pathway that most Abu Dhabi schools run from Year 7 through Year 13. Knowing what comes before and after it changes how a tutor spends the first month, because a Year 10 student who has never met a balance sheet needs different groundwork from one arriving from a Lower Secondary business course.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies
programmes.description: Six syllabus areas: understanding business activity, people in business, marketing, operations management, financial information and decisions, and external influences. Assessed by Paper 1, a short-answer and data-response paper, and Paper 2, a case study built on an insert supplied in the exam. Both papers are ninety minutes and worth half the grade each. Grades run A* to G.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, 0450 is most often a Year 10 option choice in British-curriculum schools licensed by ADEK, taught over two years with a mock in the January or February before the June series. Some schools compress it into a single year for students arriving mid-key-stage from another curriculum, which is the single most common reason an Abu Dhabi family looks for outside help in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics
programmes.description: Frequently taken alongside 0450 and frequently confused with it. Economics works at the level of markets, governments and whole economies; Business Studies works inside one firm. The overlap is real in the external-influences topic, where exchange rates, inflation and interest rates appear in both syllabuses, but the command words and the expected depth of diagram work differ sharply.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools timetable 0450 and 0455 as alternatives rather than a pair, so the option-block conversation in Year 9 decides which one a student sits. Where a school offers both, students who pick both tend to need help separating the two answer styles rather than help with content, and a tutor can fix that confusion in two or three sessions.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Business
programmes.description: The direct continuation of 0450 for students staying in a Cambridge school. It adds strategic management, deeper finance including investment appraisal, and a far heavier evaluation demand at A2. Students who reached 0450 by memorising definitions tend to stall in the first term of AS, which is why the analysis habits built at IGCSE matter beyond the grade on the certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families planning a Cambridge sixth form locally, or a transfer to a UK or Canadian university, usually treat 0450 as the entry test for 9609. Schools in the emirate commonly ask for a grade B or above at IGCSE before admitting a student to AS Business, so the IGCSE grade has a gatekeeping function inside the same building.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Business Management
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, taken by students moving from a British-curriculum IGCSE into an IB Diploma school. It replaces Cambridge's case-study insert with a pre-released case study at HL and an internal assessment written on a real organisation. The transferable part of 0450 is the toolkit of business terms; the transferable habit is justifying a recommendation.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a well-established set of IB Diploma schools alongside its Cambridge ones, and movement between the two sectors at sixteen is routine here in a way it is not in most markets. A student finishing 0450 and starting DP Business Management benefits from a bridging block over the summer, mostly on the research and referencing skills the IB assessment requires and Cambridge never asks for.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-business-studi.subjectsIntro: A Business Studies tutor rarely arrives alone. The subjects below are the ones Abu Dhabi families most often add to a 0450 booking, usually because the same option block produced two weak grades at the January mock rather than one.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: The subject of this page. Teaching concentrates on the later parts of each twenty-mark question, where analysis and evaluation sit, and on the discipline of applying every point to the specific business named in the Paper 2 insert rather than to businesses in general.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Four units from the basic economic problem through to international trade and development. The common failure is diagram work: students draw a correct supply-and-demand diagram and then write a paragraph that never refers to it. Marks live in the link between the two.

subjects.name: Accounting (0452)
subjects.description: Taken by students who liked the financial-information topic in 0450 and wanted more of it. Paper 2 carries seventy per cent of the grade and is punishing about presentation: a correct figure in the wrong statement, or a missing narration, scores nothing.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The subject behind most of the arithmetic trouble in 0450's finance topic. Students who cannot work confidently with percentages, ratio and simple interest lose Business Studies marks on cash-flow forecasts and break-even calculations that have nothing to do with business knowledge.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: 0450 is a written-answer subject and the twelve-mark judgement questions reward controlled, sequenced prose. Students whose English is strong in conversation but loose on paper tend to lose evaluation marks for structure, and work on paragraph discipline transfers directly into Business Studies scores.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Many Abu Dhabi candidates sit 0510 alongside 0450. The useful overlap is the writing paper's register work: both subjects reward a clear claim followed by support, and both punish long sentences that lose their subject halfway through.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Shares 0450's demand for evidence and perspective but assesses it through coursework as well as an exam. Students who handle the Business Studies evaluation questions well usually find the Individual Report's argument structure familiar, and the reverse also holds.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: A common pairing in Abu Dhabi option blocks. The relevance to 0450 is the operations-management topic, where automation, stock-control systems and e-commerce appear as exam contexts, and a student with programming background can usually give sharper examples than the textbook supplies.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Overlaps 0450 in the location-of-industry and external-influences material, and shares the case-study habit: a named place, specific figures, and a conclusion that commits. Students carrying both subjects can reuse the same revision method across them.

subjects.name: Travel and Tourism (0471)
subjects.description: An applied business subject that several Abu Dhabi schools offer alongside 0450, with obvious local context in aviation, hospitality and cultural attractions. Marketing and customer service content overlaps directly, so a tutor can often cover shared ground in one pass.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-business-studi.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi is spread out, and that geography is the practical argument for online delivery rather than a marketing line. Below is what a weekday session realistically looks like from the communities where most 0450 candidates live.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense apartment living with a long causeway commute to the island's schools. Families here often finish the school run after 4pm, which makes a 5.30pm or 6pm slot the first workable one on a weekday.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities feeding several British-curriculum schools, with internal mock timetables that cluster in late January. A 4pm start is usually possible here, and that extra ninety minutes matters when a Paper 2 drill needs a full timed answer.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Short school commutes but heavy after-school activity schedules. Business Studies sessions here are most often booked as a single weekly hour with marking in between, rather than as two shorter slots.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A newer residential catchment where many families moved mid-key-stage. That produces more Year 11 starters who met 0450 only one year ago, and a correspondingly heavier first month of groundwork on the finance topic.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Older established neighbourhoods close to the city's longest-running British schools. Students here are more likely to have followed the full two-year 0450 course, so help tends to be technique-focused rather than content-focused.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Longer drives to the island schools and the latest realistic session starts in the emirate. Evening slots after 7pm Gulf Standard Time are the norm, which online delivery can hold and a travelling tutor generally cannot.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Growing mainland communities with a wide mix of curricula in one street. Siblings here frequently sit different boards, so a household may need a 0450 specialist and an Edexcel tutor on separate evenings.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Al Mushrif corridor
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's longest-established British-curriculum schools sit here, and most run 0450 as a two-year Year 10 to Year 11 course with a formal mock in the spring term. Students from these schools usually arrive with good notes and weak timed-answer technique.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and Al Raha
schoolClusters.note: A dense cluster of newer schools with large year groups and a high proportion of students who joined mid-course from another country. Business Studies classes here are often taught in sets, and the lower set moves through the finance topic quickly.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Yas and Al Reem
schoolClusters.note: Newer premium campuses with mixed curriculum offerings, including schools that run both Cambridge and IB routes in the same building. Option-block advice here is the most common reason a parent contacts a tutor before any grade problem appears.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-business-studi.modesIntro: 0450 support comes in a small number of useful shapes. The one that fits depends on how far the student is from an exam and whether the problem is knowledge or technique.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one over live video
modes.description: The default for a Year 10 or early Year 11 student. One hour a week, screen shared, working through a syllabus area and finishing with a timed question the tutor marks before the next session. Progress is visible because the marked scripts accumulate and a parent can read them.
