modes.title: Paper 2 case-study clinic
modes.description: A short block aimed at one failure mode: answers that are correct in general and unmarked in particular. Sessions use real past-paper inserts, and the student rewrites the same answer twice, once cold and once after marking, so the difference in score is attributable to one change in method.
bullets: Four to six sessions, usually booked after a disappointing mock

modes.title: Pre-series intensive
modes.description: Booked for the eight weeks before a June or November series. Two sessions a week, each covering one syllabus area and one full twenty-mark question, with a running list of definitions the student keeps failing to state precisely. Intensive blocks are sold as blocks because the marking load is front-loaded.

modes.title: Sibling or study-pair slot
modes.description: Two students in the same household sitting the same paper in the same series can share a slot. The rate splits, the attention does not halve, and peer pressure on timed answers is useful. It does not work where the two students sit different boards or different series, and a tutor will say so rather than take the booking.

sections.heading: What the Abu Dhabi market charges for IGCSE Business Studies support
paragraphs: Published hourly rates for IGCSE tuition reachable from Abu Dhabi span roughly AED 45 to AED 650, and the reason nobody prints that range is that it makes the middle look expensive. The range is real, though, and it maps onto genuinely different products rather than onto negotiating skill. At the bottom sit university students teaching from a textbook. At the top sit individually named tutors sold as a scarce resource. A 0450 candidate needs neither extreme in most cases.

The figures below were read from providers' own published rate pages in October 2026 and are presented as the market, not as IB Gram's price list. Rates in this market move, providers revise their pages without notice, and a figure read today may be stale in a term. Check each provider's own rate page before you treat any number here as a quote. IB Gram's own position is a free trial lesson first and a quoted rate after the subject, year group and marking load are known, because quoting before that is guessing.

Two line items are worth reading carefully. In-home visits in this market price travel into the hourly rate, which is why the in-home band starts above the qualified-online band and tops out higher: you are paying for a car as well as a teacher. And the premium band is almost never sold by the single hour, so an advertised AED 650 is usually the unit price inside a block of ten or twenty, which changes the real commitment considerably.

sections.heading: The six syllabus areas, and which two actually cost marks
paragraphs: Cambridge divides 0450 into six areas: understanding business activity, people in business, marketing, operations management, financial information and decisions, and external influences on business activity. They are not equally difficult and they do not fail students equally. In practice two of them account for most of the lost marks in Abu Dhabi mock results, and neither is the one students complain about.

Financial information and decisions is the first. It asks students to build and interpret cash-flow forecasts, calculate break-even, read a simple income statement and statement of financial position, and then say what the numbers mean for a decision. Candidates lose marks here twice over: once on the arithmetic, and again because they stop at the figure instead of explaining what it implies for the business in the question. A correct break-even output with no comment on whether the target is realistic scores a fraction of the available marks.

External influences is the second. Exchange rates, inflation, interest rates, legal controls, ethics and environmental pressure all appear, and they appear as contexts rather than as topics. A question will describe a firm importing components and then ask what a weaker local currency does to it. Students who learned the definitions can state that imports become more expensive; students who were taught the chain explain the effect on unit cost, on pricing, on demand and then on cash flow, and that chain is where the analysis marks are. Teaching it is a matter of drilling three-step consequences until they become automatic.

The other four areas reward preparation more than insight. Business activity and people in business are definition-heavy and respond well to a maintained glossary. Marketing and operations are context-heavy and respond to worked examples, which Abu Dhabi supplies generously: a student can illustrate segmentation, channel choice and quality management with firms they pass every day.

sections.heading: Paper 1 and Paper 2 are two different exams in the same subject
paragraphs: Both 0450 papers last ninety minutes, carry eighty marks, contain four twenty-mark questions and count for half the grade. That symmetry hides a real difference in what they test. Paper 1 presents short pieces of stimulus material, one per question, and moves across the syllabus. Paper 2 supplies a single case study in an insert, and every question draws on it. The same student can score a solid grade on one and a weak grade on the other, and most do.

Paper 1 rewards coverage. Any of the six areas can appear, the stimulus is brief, and a student who has revised unevenly will find the gap. The marks lost here are usually knowledge marks: a definition that is nearly right, a calculation method half-remembered, a two-mark question answered in a paragraph when two words would have scored. The fix is systematic and unglamorous, built on a definitions log and short recall drills rather than on essays.

Paper 2 rewards application, and it is where Abu Dhabi tutors spend most of their time. The insert describes a business with a name, a size, a market, a problem and some figures. Every mark above the basic knowledge tier depends on the answer referring to that specific business. Students who write a textbook-perfect paragraph about motivation theory without once mentioning the firm in the insert collect the AO1 marks and lose the AO2, AO3 and AO4 marks stacked above them. That is the single largest recoverable loss in the whole qualification.

Assessment-objective weightings are approximate and Cambridge publishes the authoritative split in the syllabus document for each exam series, so work from the version that matches your child's series.

sections.heading: Command terms: reading the question for what it pays for
paragraphs: 0450 command terms are a pricing system. Each one names a skill and carries a predictable mark band, and a student who answers the wrong skill correctly still scores badly. This is the fastest improvement available in the subject, because it requires no new content at all. A Year 11 student in Abu Dhabi who has already covered the syllabus can usually add marks inside three or four sessions purely by learning to read the verb.

The pattern runs in one direction. Define and identify pay for recall and nothing else, so a long answer wastes time that the twelve-mark question will need. Explain pays for a point plus its consequence, which means two sentences, not two points. Analyse pays for a chain, and a chain means the second and third consequence, not a restatement of the first. Discuss and evaluate pay for a decision supported by the rejected alternative, which is the part students skip.

Recommend and justify questions deserve separate attention because they close most Paper 2 questions and carry the heaviest marks. The structure that scores is mechanical: state the choice, give the strongest reason drawn from the insert, state what is wrong with the option you rejected, and close with a condition under which your answer would change. Students resist the last step because it feels like weakness. In the mark scheme it is the difference between a judgement and an opinion.
The table lists the terms with typical mark bands and the error that costs marks on each. Mark allocations vary between papers and series, so treat the bands as typical rather than fixed.

sections.heading: What changes the quote for an Abu Dhabi family
paragraphs: Two families in the same building can be quoted different hourly figures for the same subject without either being overcharged. The variables are predictable, and knowing them lets you shape the brief rather than haggle over the rate. The first is distance from the exam. A Year 10 student in October has four terms of runway, and one hour a week with homework between sessions is usually enough. A Year 11 student in March has eight weeks, needs two sessions a week and a far heavier marking load, and the weekly cost roughly doubles for the same hourly rate.

The second variable is what the hour contains. An hour of teaching is cheaper to supply than an hour of teaching plus two marked timed answers and written feedback, and the second is what moves a 0450 grade. Ask any provider directly whether marking is inside or outside the quoted rate, because the answer explains most of the difference between two quotes that look alike. A rate that excludes marking is not cheaper; it is a smaller product.

The third is specificity. A tutor who teaches 0450 specifically, works from the current syllabus and knows the case-study insert format commands more than a general business graduate, and for Paper 2 work the difference shows up in the first session. The fourth is format: a shared sibling slot splits the rate, a group class lowers it further and lowers the attention with it, and a pre-exam block prices differently from an open-ended weekly booking. None of these is a discount to be negotiated. They are different products, and matching the product to the problem is where families actually save money.

One more Abu Dhabi-specific factor: scheduling. Slots in the 4pm to 6pm window are the most contested in the emirate because that is when the school run clears and before evening activities start. Families who can take a 7pm or 8pm Gulf Standard Time slot have more choice of specialist, which matters more than any rate difference when the subject is narrow.
bullets: Weeks remaining before the series, not the hourly rate, drives total cost

sections.heading: Where 0450 fits in the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency count
paragraphs: Parents ask whether Business Studies counts, and the honest answer is that it counts like any other accredited subject. For the British track, the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements ask students to pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and to show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Business Studies sits inside that five perfectly well.

The detail worth knowing is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. That surprises families who assumed the mandatory UAE subjects their school teaches would carry equivalency weight, and it changes option-block planning: a student taking Arabic, Islamic education and four academic IGCSEs has four counting subjects, not six. At least one competing tutoring site publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong, and acting on it leads to unnecessary extra entries.

IB numbers are a different matter. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been confirmed from the Ministry's own pages for this project, so nothing here states one. If your planning depends on an IB figure, read it on moe.gov.ae or ask the emirate attestation authority directly rather than relying on a tutoring site, including this one. Equivalency is also not something a tutor performs or influences. It is a process you complete with the Ministry, and no tutoring booking is required for it.

For the American track, the same source sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. Those figures matter to Abu Dhabi families whose children switch curricula mid-school, which happens here often.

sections.heading: ADEK, your child's school and what a 0450 mock result is telling you
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi answer to ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is a different authority from Dubai's KHDA and from Sharjah's private education authority, and it matters practically rather than abstractly: inspection cycles, calendar dates and reporting formats differ, so advice written for a Dubai parent does not transfer cleanly to Abu Dhabi.

What a school report gives you about 0450 is usually a predicted grade and a mock percentage, and neither is as informative as the mock script. Ask for the marked paper. A mock mark of fifty-two per cent can mean two entirely different things: a student who scored well on knowledge parts and nothing on the twelve-mark questions, or one who was thin everywhere. The first is eight weeks of technique work. The second is a content rebuild. No tutor can tell which without reading the script, and a parent who brings the script to a first session saves an hour of diagnosis.

The second thing to ask the school is which series the student is entered for and when the final entry deadline falls. Cambridge entry deadlines sit months before the exam itself, and the school handles entries, not the family, so the deadline is only visible if you ask. A late discovery that a student is entered for a series they are not ready for is a scheduling problem, not a teaching one, and it is far easier to solve in October than in March.

One caution worth stating plainly, because it affects who you can legally hire in this emirate: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours are required to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against current ADEK guidance before relying on it. The practical consequence is simple: your child's own class teacher is not an option.
bullets: ADEK licenses and inspects Abu Dhabi private schools; KHDA does not
Ask for the marked mock script, not just the percentage
Entry deadlines sit months before the exam and are held by the school
A child's own school teacher may not take them as a paid private student

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with a student's work
paragraphs: 0450 has no coursework, which removes the academic-honesty question that dominates IB subjects and some other IGCSEs. Nothing a student submits for Business Studies is written at home and sent to Cambridge. Every mark comes from two invigilated papers. That makes the tutoring boundary unusually clean, and it is worth stating because the surrounding market is not clean at all.

The boundary still matters for school-assessed work. Abu Dhabi schools set internal assignments, projects and mock papers that feed predicted grades, and predicted grades feed sixth-form and university applications. A tutor's job on that work is to teach, question and give feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission, does not edit a piece until the authorship is unclear, and does not sit alongside a student during a timed school assessment. Any provider willing to cross that line is selling your child a risk, not a service.

What a tutor can legitimately do is more useful than what they cannot. They can mark a past-paper answer against the published criteria and show which assessment objective failed. They can model a twelve-mark structure on a different question and then make the student build their own on the one that matters. They can audit a definitions log, run recall drills, and set timed conditions the student will not impose on themselves. They can read a mock script and name the three changes worth making. None of that involves authoring anything.

Published syllabus material deserves the same discipline. A tutor should reference the Cambridge syllabus and past papers and point you to cambridgeinternational.org to obtain them through your child's school, not supply them as downloads. Reproducing exam board material is a copyright matter, and with unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure for the student.

sections.heading: Booking a 0450 slot around the Abu Dhabi school week
paragraphs: Scheduling decides whether tuition works more often than teaching quality does, because a session a student is too tired to use is wasted at any rate. The Abu Dhabi weekday sorts itself into three windows. The first, from roughly 3.30pm to 5pm, suits students in Khalifa City, Al Raha and the island communities with short commutes. The second, 5.30pm to 7pm, is the widest window and the most contested. The third, after 7pm, is the one mainland families and those with long drives actually use, and it is the window where specialist availability is best.

The academic year has its own shape here. Internal mocks cluster in January and February for June-series candidates, and that is the moment most Abu Dhabi 0450 bookings begin, which is also why specialists are hardest to find then. Starting in October or November costs the same per hour and buys a far better choice of tutor. The weeks around Ramadan need deliberate planning: sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing, and families who agree that shift in advance keep their continuity instead of losing a month.

Travel is the other recurring factor. Abu Dhabi families move during school holidays and often across time zones, and a weekly slot that only exists in Gulf Standard Time breaks when the family is away. Online delivery holds through that, provided the time difference is agreed before the trip rather than after it. A student revising in another country can keep the same tutor and the same marking cycle, which is the practical difference between a continuous programme and a stop-start one.

Getting started is deliberately short. Send the marked mock script, the school's 0450 scheme of work if you have it, and the series the student is entered for. A trial lesson follows, free and limited to one session, in which the tutor works a past-paper question with the student rather than interviewing them. After it you get a written note on what is actually wrong and how many weeks it should take. If no 0450 specialist is free in the slot you need, you will be told that rather than offered a general business tutor in their place.
bullets: Three usable weekday windows, with the widest specialist choice after 7pm
January and February are peak demand; October bookings get better choice
Ramadan sessions commonly shift to post-Iftar timing by agreement
Bring the marked mock script to the trial lesson

process.title: Send the script, not the symptoms
process.description: The useful first message is the marked mock paper, the entered series and the year group. A description of the problem is less informative than the paper, because the paper shows whether marks were lost on knowledge, application, analysis or evaluation. That distinction decides the whole plan.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one session
process.description: A 0450 specialist works a past-paper question with the student rather than asking them how they feel about business. One session, no charge, no card needed to book it. You see the teaching before any money is discussed, and the tutor sees the gap before any plan is written.

process.title: A written diagnosis and a quoted rate
process.description: After the trial you get a short note naming the assessment objective that is failing, the syllabus areas that need rebuilding, and a realistic number of weeks. The quoted hourly rate follows that, because it depends on the marking load, and quoting before the diagnosis would be a guess.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: One slot, same time each week, agreed around the school run and activities rather than around the tutor's convenience. Sessions run live over video with screens shared. Where a family travels, the time difference is agreed in advance so the slot survives the trip.

process.title: Marked work between every session
process.description: A timed question is set, written and marked before the next lesson, with feedback that names the criterion rather than the mood. The marked scripts accumulate into the only honest progress record there is, and a parent can read them without asking anybody how it is going.

process.title: Reassess at six weeks
process.description: Six weeks produces enough marked work to tell whether the plan is working. At that point the session frequency goes up, stays flat or stops, and the tutor says which. A programme that is not moving marks should end rather than continue out of habit.

whyPoints.title: The rate is published, with its date
whyPoints.description: Market AED bands on this page carry the provider that published them and the month they were read. Three of six researched competitor pages print no price at all and two quote US dollars. Showing the number and its source lets you judge a quote instead of accepting one.

whyPoints.title: Online is the method, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons in the UAE run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi, and nothing on this page suggests otherwise. Home tutoring is a service offered only in India, and pretending otherwise on a UAE page would be a promise nobody could keep.

whyPoints.title: Marking is part of the hour
whyPoints.description: A 0450 grade moves when timed answers are written, marked against the criteria and rewritten. Teaching without marking is a cheaper product that leaves the main failure mode untouched, so marked work between sessions is built into how a slot is quoted.

whyPoints.title: Subject-specific, not subject-adjacent
whyPoints.description: A 0450 session is taught by somebody who works from the current syllabus and knows the case-study insert format, not by a business graduate improvising from a textbook. On Paper 2 technique the difference is visible inside one lesson.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, not hidden
whyPoints.description: If no Business Studies specialist is free in the slot you need, you are told so. faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450 tutor charge per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published rates for IGCSE tuition reachable from Abu Dhabi ran from about AED 45 to AED 650 an hour when provider pages were read in October 2026. Most 0450 bookings settle between AED 150 and AED 300, because the subject needs a specialist and because marking timed answers between lessons takes real time. The number moves with how many weeks remain before the series, how many sessions a week you need, and whether marking sits inside the quoted hour. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson rather than before, since a quote given without seeing the student's marked work is a guess.

faqs.question: Why does my son score well on Paper 1 but badly on the 0450 case study?
faqs.answer: Because they test different things. Paper 1 pays mostly for knowledge across the six syllabus areas, and a student with good notes does well on it. Paper 2 supplies a named business in an insert, and almost every mark above the basic tier depends on the answer referring to that business specifically. A textbook-perfect paragraph about motivation that never mentions the firm collects the knowledge marks and loses the application, analysis and evaluation marks stacked above them. It is the largest recoverable loss in the qualification and it responds to four to six sessions of rewrite-and-remark work on real inserts.

faqs.question: Is Business Studies 0450 an easier IGCSE than Economics 0455?
faqs.answer: They are difficult in different places, and neither is a soft option. Business Studies works inside one firm and asks for applied judgement about decisions, so the marks sit in evaluation and in tying every point to a named business. Economics works at market and national level and asks for diagram work that must be referred to in the prose, not just drawn. Students who write fluently but dislike graphs usually find 0450 more comfortable; students who think in models often prefer 0455. The overlap is the external-influences material, where exchange rates, inflation and interest rates appear in both.

faqs.question: How many 0450 sessions a week does a Year 11 student in Abu Dhabi usually need?
faqs.answer: One a week is enough through most of Year 11 if the student does the marked work between sessions. Two a week becomes sensible in the eight to ten weeks before a June series, or immediately after a mock result that showed losses across several syllabus areas rather than in technique alone. More than two a week rarely helps, because the limiting factor is how much timed writing a student can produce and absorb feedback on, not how many hours a tutor is available. Frequency should be reviewed at six weeks against the marked scripts rather than set once and left.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies have any coursework to submit?
faqs.answer: No. 0450 is assessed entirely by two written papers taken under exam conditions, each ninety minutes, each worth eighty marks and half the grade. Nothing is written at home and sent to Cambridge. That removes the academic-honesty question that complicates IB subjects and coursework-based IGCSEs. School-set assignments and projects still exist and still feed predicted grades, and the boundary there is the same as everywhere: a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has written, and never supplies sentences for a submission or edits a piece until the authorship is unclear.

faqs.question: Can a 0450 tutor mark my daughter's past papers between lessons?
faqs.answer: That is the part of the service that moves the grade, so yes, and you should check it is included before comparing two quotes. The cycle that works is simple: a timed question is set at the end of a session, written under exam conditions, marked against the published criteria, and returned with feedback naming the assessment objective that failed rather than a general comment. The marked scripts then accumulate into a record a parent can read directly. An hourly rate that excludes marking is not cheaper than one that includes it; it is a smaller product that leaves the main problem untouched.

faqs.question: Does Business Studies count towards the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency subjects?
faqs.answer: It counts like any other accredited academic subject. The British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The detail families miss is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. So a student taking those two plus four academic IGCSEs has four counting subjects, not six. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae, because equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutor performs.

faqs.question: My child's Abu Dhabi school teaches 0450 in Year 10 only. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a known pattern in this emirate and it is manageable, but it changes the plan. A one-year 0450 course means the finance topic and the external-influences chain arrive quickly, with less time to consolidate before mocks. Students who joined mid-key-stage from another curriculum feel it most, because they meet cash-flow forecasts and break-even analysis for the first time under time pressure. The first month of tutoring in that situation is groundwork on the financial-information area rather than exam technique, and technique work starts once the arithmetic and the statement formats are secure.

faqs.question: Should my child sit 0450 in the June series or the November series?
faqs.answer: The school decides the entry, not the family, so the first step is to ask which series your child is entered for and when the final entry deadline falls. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, and most Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools enter candidates for June at the end of Year 11. November is used for resits and for students who joined late. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers themselves, which is why a late discovery that a student is unready becomes a scheduling problem rather than a teaching one.

faqs.question: What is the difference between analyse and evaluate in 0450 mark schemes?
faqs.answer: Analyse pays for a chain of consequence. A weaker currency raises the cost of imported components, which raises unit cost, which forces a price rise or squeezes margin, which affects cash flow. Three links score where one does not. Evaluate pays for a judgement that weighs both options and commits. The structure the mark scheme rewards is: state the choice, give the strongest reason drawn from the case, say what is wrong with the option you rejected, and name a condition that would change your answer. Students skip the last two steps because they feel like weakness, and that is where the marks are.

faqs.question: Will an online 0450 tutor work for a student who is weak at writing in English?
faqs.answer: Often better than an in-person session, because the whole lesson happens on a shared screen where the student's own sentences can be rebuilt in front of them. 0450 is a written-answer subject and the twelve-mark questions reward controlled, sequenced prose, so paragraph discipline is part of the subject teaching rather than a separate problem. Sessions in that situation spend time on sentence structure inside business answers, not on general English work. Where the underlying English level is the main barrier, a tutor will say so and recommend parallel support rather than charging for 0450 hours that cannot land.

faqs.question: Do you have a 0450 tutor free after 7pm Gulf Standard Time?
faqs.answer: The window after 7pm is usually the easiest to fill, which is useful to know if your family lives in Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Mussafah or another mainland community with a long school commute. The contested window in Abu Dhabi is 5.30pm to 7pm, when the school run has cleared and evening activities have not started. Families who can take a later slot get a wider choice of subject specialist, and on a narrow subject like Business Studies that matters more than a small difference in rate. If nothing is free in the slot you need, you will be told rather than offered a substitute.

faqs.question: Is 0450 useful if my child wants to study business at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: It is useful preparation and it is not a requirement, and nobody should tell you otherwise. For admission, what counts is the full IGCSE profile, the post-16 qualification and the Ministry equivalency the university asks for, not any single subject. Where 0450 earns its place is in the transition: students who arrive at a business degree already able to read a statement of financial position, build a cash-flow forecast and justify a decision in writing start ahead. It also feeds directly into Cambridge AS and A Level Business 9609 and into IB Diploma Business Management for students staying in Abu Dhabi for sixth form.

faqs.question: What should I send a tutor before the first 0450 lesson?
faqs.answer: Three things, and the first matters most. Send the marked mock script, not the percentage, because a fifty-two per cent can mean a student who scored on knowledge and nothing on the twelve-mark questions or one who was thin everywhere, and those need different plans. Send the school's 0450 scheme of work or topic order if you have it, so sessions run alongside the class rather than against it. And send the series your child is entered for. With those three, a first session can start teaching instead of spending an hour working out what is wrong.

Find the marked script and send it with the series they are entered for. A 0450 specialist will work a past-paper question with them in a free trial lesson, one session, and write back on which assessment objective is actually costing marks and roughly how many weeks it should take to fix. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. If no specialist is free when you need one, you will hear that instead of being handed a substitute.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched through this page teach separate chemistry rather than general science. The first session divides your child's lost marks into two piles: the ones that need understanding built, and the ones that need a specific form of words learned. The second pile is almost always larger than anybody expects.

intro.heading: Two kinds of lost mark in Cambridge chemistry, and only one needs teaching
paragraphs: Families in Abu Dhabi arrive at a chemistry tutor with a diagnosis already in hand, and it is nearly always organic chemistry or moles. Both are reasonable guesses and both are usually incomplete. When a marked 0620 script is divided up properly, a large share of the missing marks turns out to sit in material that requires no reasoning at all: the test for a particular ion and the observation it produces, the steps for preparing a soluble salt, the trend down Group VII and the reason attached to it, the conditions for an industrial process. None of that is difficult. All of it is exact.

That matters because the two piles need completely different hours. Building understanding of a reaction mechanism or of mole ratios takes weeks and benefits from spacing. Learning that the test for a halide ion is silver nitrate solution in the presence of dilute nitric acid, and that the precipitate is white, cream or yellow depending on which halide is present, takes a session and then needs testing twice. A family paying for weeks of conceptual teaching while the recall pile sits untouched is buying the wrong hours, and the script will say so if anybody reads it.

The current 0620 syllabus covers states of matter, atoms and bonding, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, energetics, rates and reversible reactions, redox, acids, bases and salts, the Periodic Table, metals, the chemistry of the environment, organic chemistry, and experimental techniques and analysis. Candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper at Core or Extended tier, and a practical component. The exact components and weightings for a given series are in the current syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org, which is the document to work from rather than a revision guide of uncertain vintage.

There is a second reason this page emphasises precision. Chemistry answers are marked against specific wording, and a student who writes a sentence that is chemically true but not the sentence being rewarded collects nothing. It turned cloudy is not limewater turning milky. A gas was produced is not carbon dioxide identified by a named test. The acid was added is not the acid was added in excess and the remaining solid filtered off. These are not style preferences; each clause is attached to a mark.

IB Gram matches Abu Dhabi families to a 0620 specialist and teaches one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, around the school week. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For separate chemistry that arrangement is an advantage rather than a compromise, because the person who can mark an analysis question properly may be nowhere near Al Reem, Khalifa City or Al Rahba, and nothing about this work needs a bench.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620.programmesIntro: Separate chemistry is a decision with consequences that run past Year 11, and Abu Dhabi families usually ask about the alternatives in the same conversation. The programmes below are the ones that come up.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry
programmes.description: Separate chemistry as a single IGCSE, examined by a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper at Core or Extended tier, and a practical component. Content runs from particle theory and bonding through stoichiometry, electrochemistry and energetics to the Periodic Table, metals, environmental chemistry, organic chemistry and chemical analysis. Extended candidates meet additional depth in most of those areas.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, separate sciences tend to be offered by the larger British-curriculum departments, while other schools place most of a year group on a combined or coordinated route. Which route applies to your child is a departmental decision, and the head of science can explain the reasoning behind a particular set placement.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science
programmes.description: A single award covering biology, chemistry and physics, producing one grade. The chemistry inside it is narrower than 0620, with less stoichiometry and a reduced organic section, but the command vocabulary and the practical conventions are identical. A student who loses marks on exact wording in one course will lose them in the other.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student is carrying a heavy option block or arrived mid-course, the combined route is a sensible placement rather than a demotion. If chemistry is intended to continue beyond Year 11, that is a question for the sixth form, because a single science grade covers all three subjects at once.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Chemistry
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation, with formal treatment of equilibria, kinetics, energetics and organic mechanisms, and practical papers of its own. Students arriving from Extended 0620 find the topics familiar and the expected level of explanation entirely new, because mechanisms now have to be justified rather than recalled.
programmes.countryNote: Entry requirements are set by each Abu Dhabi school rather than centrally, and they usually specify a grade in chemistry and often one in mathematics as well. The published requirement at your child's school is the only reliable version; figures quoted on tutoring sites are not.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Available at Standard and Higher Level, with experimental work running across both years and an internal assessment that is the student's own work from the first draft to the last. The conceptual overlap with 0620 is substantial, and the shift is in how much of each answer has to be argued rather than stated.
programmes.countryNote: The emirate has a large IB sector, and students regularly move from a Cambridge Year 11 into a Diploma Year 12 at a different school. The most useful preparation in that gap is explanation practice rather than new content, which happens to be the same work that raises a 0620 grade.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620.subjectsIntro: The grid below lists the 0620 content as a tutor plans it, with the specific thing that costs marks in each area. The pattern across them is worth noticing: in most areas the loss is precision, not comprehension.

subjects.name: States of matter and particle theory
subjects.description: Changes of state, diffusion and the kinetic particle model. Answers need particle arrangement, spacing and motion stated explicitly. Saying the particles move faster when heated collects a mark; saying the substance gets hotter collects nothing.

subjects.name: Atoms, elements and bonding
subjects.description: Atomic structure, isotopes, ionic and covalent bonding, metallic bonding and giant structures. The frequent loss is explaining a property without referring to the structure: high melting point answers need strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, not just strong bonds.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: Formulae, equations, relative masses, moles, concentration and limiting reactants. Where students have been drilled on single-step conversions, the losses appear on multi-step problems that require a ratio from a balanced equation before any arithmetic begins.

subjects.name: Electrochemistry and electrolysis
subjects.description: Electrolysis of molten and aqueous compounds, products at each electrode, and half equations for Extended candidates. Marks go missing on the aqueous cases, where the rule about which ion is discharged has to be applied rather than remembered as a list.

subjects.name: Chemical energetics
subjects.description: Exothermic and endothermic changes, energy level diagrams and bond energy calculations. A diagram needs labelled axes, the activation energy marked from the reactants, and the enthalpy change shown with the correct sign. Each of those is separately creditable.

subjects.name: Rates of reaction
subjects.description: Effect of concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts, with collision theory as the explanation. The required sentence pairs frequency of collisions with the energy of those collisions, and students who give only one half of it lose half the marks.

subjects.name: Reversible reactions and equilibrium
subjects.description: Dynamic equilibrium and the effect of changing conditions, usually examined through an industrial context. Answers must state the direction of the shift and the reason, and a student who names the shift without the reason has written half an answer.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and salts
subjects.description: Properties of acids and bases, neutralisation, indicators, pH, and the preparation of soluble and insoluble salts. Preparation questions are examined as sequences of steps, and the marks sit on the steps students regard as obvious: excess, filtration, evaporation and crystallisation.

subjects.name: The Periodic Table and group trends
subjects.description: Group I, Group VII, the transition elements and the noble gases, with trends in reactivity and physical properties. Each trend has a required explanation attached to it, and reproducing the direction of the trend without that explanation collects part marks at best.

subjects.name: Metals, reactivity and extraction
subjects.description: The reactivity series, displacement, rusting and its prevention, and the extraction of iron and aluminium. Extraction questions are marked on conditions and named equations, which makes this one of the most exactly recalled areas on the whole syllabus.

subjects.name: Chemistry of the environment
subjects.description: Water treatment, fertilisers, air pollutants, their sources and their effects, and the role of catalytic converters. Short, highly predictable question types, and one of the fastest areas to recover marks in a final fortnight.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.description: Homologous series, fuels, alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids, polymers and the reactions linking them. The reliable losses are conditions rather than products: the reagent, temperature and catalyst for each conversion are exactly what the mark scheme asks for.

subjects.name: Experimental techniques and analysis
subjects.description: Separation methods, chromatography, measurement, and the identification of ions and gases. This area overlaps the practical component and is the clearest example of marks that are available to any student willing to learn a list precisely.

sections.heading: Qualitative analysis: the marks that are pure recall
paragraphs: Chemical analysis is examined in the theory papers as well as the practical component, and it is the clearest example of marks that any student can collect by learning a list properly. A question gives an unknown and asks for a test, or gives a test and asks what the result shows. The full answer has four parts: the reagent, the condition under which it is used, the observation in precise terms, and the conclusion drawn from it. Students routinely supply two of the four.

Observation language is where most of the loss happens. A precipitate is white, not cloudy. Limewater turns milky, not white. A gas relights a glowing splint, which is not the same as the splint burning brightly. Litmus is bleached by chlorine rather than simply changing colour. Each of these distinctions is attached to a mark, and a student who has only ever discussed the tests verbally in class has never had to write them in the form that earns credit.

The practical half matters too. Where a student sits a written alternative to the laboratory test, the analysis questions are exactly this content with apparatus added, so the recall work pays twice. Where a student sits the laboratory test instead, handling the apparatus belongs to the school and the written reasoning can still be taught remotely. We are explicit about that division rather than suggesting that a video call substitutes for a bench.

In a session this is drilled rather than discussed. The student writes a test in full, the scheme wording goes beside it, the gap is named, and the same test is asked for again a week later without warning. It is the least sophisticated thing in a tutor's repertoire and it reliably returns marks on this syllabus, which makes it a sensible use of paid time in the run-up to a series.

sections.heading: Acids, bases, salts and the preparation question
paragraphs: Salt preparation is one of the most predictable questions on the paper and one of the most commonly half answered. The method for a soluble salt from an insoluble base runs through a fixed sequence: warm the acid, add the solid base in excess, filter off the unreacted excess, evaporate the filtrate to the point of crystallisation, and leave the remainder to crystallise. Each of those steps is separately creditable, and the two that students skip are excess and filtration, because both feel like housekeeping rather than chemistry.

The reason for using excess is a mark in itself. Adding the base until no more dissolves guarantees that all the acid has reacted, which is why the resulting solution is neutral and why the excess can simply be filtered out. A student who states the steps without that reason loses the explanation marks in any question that asks why the method works. The same logic appears again in titration questions, where the purpose of each step is examined as much as the procedure.

Insoluble salts take a different route by precipitation, mixing two soluble solutions and then filtering, washing and drying the product. Washing and drying are marks. Students who stop at filtering have produced a contaminated damp solid and have written an incomplete method, and the solubility rules that decide which route applies are themselves a short list worth learning precisely rather than reasoning about under time pressure.

Alongside this sit the standard acid and base properties, neutralisation, the pH scale and indicators. These are generous marks if the language is right. An acid reacts with a metal carbonate to produce a salt, water and carbon dioxide, and the equation generalises; a student who has learned the three general reactions can answer a wide range of questions from them without memorising individual cases.
bullets: Excess, filtration, evaporation and crystallisation are each separate marks
Using excess is also the explanation for why the product is neutral

sections.heading: Group trends, and the explanations already written for you
paragraphs: Periodic Table questions follow a tight pattern: state the trend, then explain it. Students almost always manage the first half. Group I becomes more reactive down the group, Group VII becomes less reactive down the group, melting points fall in Group I and rise in Group VII. Those are facts worth a mark each and they are rarely the problem. The explanation is where the marks are, and it is where students write something plausible instead of the thing being rewarded.

For Group I, the required reasoning concerns the outer electron being further from the nucleus and more easily lost down the group. For Group VII, it concerns the atom's decreasing tendency to gain an electron as the shells increase. Displacement questions follow directly from that: a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from solution, and the answer should name both species and the observation. Transition elements are examined on the characteristic properties as a set, and the noble gases on their full outer shells and consequent lack of reactivity.

There is a useful efficiency here for a student short of time. Because the explanation structures repeat, learning two sentence shapes covers most of the group chemistry on the paper. A tutor can hand those shapes over in a single session, and the following week test whether they survived. That is a far better use of an hour than reading around the topic, which is what revision guides invite and what produces plausible non-scoring answers.

The same precision applies to the physical properties of metals and non-metals, and to explaining a property from a structure. High melting point in an ionic compound requires strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions. Electrical conductivity in a metal requires delocalised electrons free to move. Each of those is a sentence, not a concept to be paraphrased, and each is worth learning in the form the scheme uses.

sections.heading: Rates and energetics: the graph plus the sentence
paragraphs: Rate questions are a pairing. One half is a graph, drawn or interpreted, and the other is an explanation in terms of collisions. The graph half is mechanical: a steeper initial gradient means a faster reaction, the curve levels off when a reactant is used up, and two reactions producing the same amount of product must finish at the same height even if one gets there sooner. Students who have been shown this once rarely get it wrong again.

The explanation half is where the marks go. The full answer needs both frequency and energy: raising the temperature increases the frequency of collisions and increases the proportion of collisions with sufficient energy to react. A student who gives only the frequency half has written half an answer, and this is the single most repeated partial answer in the whole syllabus. Concentration and surface area affect frequency alone, and a catalyst provides an alternative pathway of lower activation energy, which is its own specific sentence.

Energetics is examined through diagrams and bond energies. An energy level diagram needs labelled axes, reactants and products at the correct relative heights, the activation energy marked from the reactants to the peak, and the enthalpy change marked with the right sign. Those are four separate marks on a single drawing, which makes it one of the more generous questions available to a student who has practised the conventions.

Bond energy calculations trip students on signs rather than arithmetic. Breaking bonds requires energy and making bonds releases it, so the overall change is the difference between the two totals, and a negative result means exothermic. Setting the calculation out in two labelled columns before subtracting removes almost all of the error, and it is a two-minute habit to install.

sections.heading: Metals, extraction and the conditions that must be exact
paragraphs: Extraction is the most exactly examined content on the syllabus. The blast furnace question asks for the raw materials, what happens at each stage, the named equations, and the role of each substance added, and every one of those is a mark with a specific form of words. Coke burns to produce carbon dioxide, which is reduced to carbon monoxide, which reduces iron oxide to iron; limestone decomposes and the resulting calcium oxide removes acidic impurities as slag. A student who knows the story loosely scores loosely.

Aluminium extraction is examined on why electrolysis is required rather than reduction with carbon, on the role of cryolite in lowering the operating temperature, and on the products at each electrode. The reactivity series question that sits behind both is the useful organising idea: metals above carbon are extracted by electrolysis, metals below it can be reduced by carbon, and the position of a metal predicts the displacement reactions it can perform.

Rusting and its prevention is a short, reliable topic. Iron rusts in the presence of both oxygen and water, which is why experiments isolating each one appear so often, and prevention methods divide into barriers and sacrificial protection. Galvanising is examined as both at once, which makes it a favourite question. Each prevention method should be named with the mechanism, because the method alone collects less than the method with its reason.

For an Abu Dhabi student this area has an additional advantage: it is almost entirely recall, so it can be learned in a fortnight at any point in the year, including during a month when the school day is shortened and longer concentrated work is harder to schedule. We often move extraction and environmental chemistry into exactly those weeks for that reason.

sections.heading: The Cambridge calendar, counted backwards from the chemistry papers
paragraphs: Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The administration around those series sits much earlier than families expect, and the published key dates for the March 2027 series make the shape of it visible: entries close on 27 November 2026 for an examination period that runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due on 27 February 2027, results released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates issued in late June.

The practical consequence is that the decision about which tier a chemistry candidate is entered for happens months before anyone has seen the final mock. That is worth knowing before a conversation with a head of science, because asking in April about a change that had to be made in November is a different conversation from asking in October. If your child is in a Core set and the family is hoping for an Extended entry, the time to raise it is early.

There is a second administrative point that catches families out. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, and its own guidance is unambiguous: it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination as a result of using the wrong one. Your child's dates may therefore differ from a cousin's at another school, and the school's exams officer holds the correct version.

Where a student sits Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers instead, the pattern is similar with different dates. Pearson offers May and June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is always the document to work from rather than a date restated on a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Core and Extended 0620: what the tier decides
paragraphs: The tier your child sits is a real constraint and not a judgement of ability. Core and Extended candidates sit different papers, cover different depths of content, and face different grade ceilings. The practical effect on tutoring is immediate: teaching Extended stoichiometry to a Core candidate wastes the hour, and revising only Core content with an Extended candidate leaves whole sections of the theory paper unprepared. The first thing to establish is therefore which tier applies, and the statement of entry is the document that says so.

Movement between tiers is possible in principle and constrained in practice by the entry calendar described above. A school that has entered a candidate for Core papers in November is working to a decision already made, and a change in March is an administrative matter rather than simply a conversation about progress. Where a family believes the tier is wrong, the time to act is the autumn term, with mock evidence in hand.

There is an honest point to make about ceilings. A Core entry limits the range of grades available, so a student who is capable of more and is entered at Core has a cap applied before they begin. That is worth raising with a department calmly and with evidence, which usually means a marked paper rather than a general sense that the student is doing well. Departments respond better to a script than to an opinion.

For tutoring purposes the tier also changes what good value looks like. A Core candidate gains most from the recall half of the syllabus, because the exact-wording marks are available at both tiers and the conceptual depth is reduced. An Extended candidate needs the recall work too, and in addition needs the stoichiometry, equilibrium and half-equation content that the Core papers do not reach. The plan should look different in each case, and anyone selling the same plan for both is not reading the entry.

sections.heading: Equivalency, and what an IGCSE science grade is for in the UAE
paragraphs: Families in Abu Dhabi often ask what a chemistry IGCSE is actually for in this country, and the answer involves the Ministry of Education's equivalency process rather than anything a tutor controls. Reporting on the published requirements for the British track states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and that Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.

For the American track the same reporting sets out different requirements: English proficiency demonstrated by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT mathematics test. No International Baccalaureate points threshold appears in that reporting, so no IB figure should be published anywhere without a source on the Ministry's own site, and this page publishes none.

Two cautions follow from that. The first is that whether a particular syllabus counts within the five is a question for the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority, not for a tutoring provider, and it should be verified on moe.gov.ae for your own case rather than assumed from a general rule. The second is that at least one ranking competitor publishes a different subject count for UAE candidates, which is a useful reminder that a number on a tutoring site is not a source.

Equivalency is also not something any tutoring platform performs, guarantees or accelerates, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. We describe the process, name the authority, and point you to the official channel. What a chemistry grade does for your child beyond that is decided by the sixth form or the university they apply to, and those requirements should be read directly from the institution rather than inferred.

sections.heading: What a chemistry session fixes in one hour, and what it cannot
paragraphs: It is worth being specific about the size of the units involved. One hour can teach the full set of gas tests and secure them, or the salt preparation sequence with its reasoning, or the blast furnace in the detail the scheme wants, or the two group trend sentence shapes. Those are real, measurable gains and they are available to any student who turns up and writes. A family with four sessions to spend should spend them on units of this size rather than on a survey of the syllabus.

One hour cannot build mole fluency, and nobody should claim otherwise. Stoichiometry is a skill with several prerequisites, and a student who cannot take a ratio from a balanced equation needs weeks of spaced practice rather than an intensive afternoon. The same is true of organic mechanisms at the Extended level and of aqueous electrolysis, where the rules only become reliable after a good deal of application. Where the diagnosis is conceptual, the honest estimate is longer and we give it.

There is also a category we cannot help with at all, and it is worth naming. Apparatus handling for the laboratory practical test belongs to the school. Submitted assessed work, where a course requires any, stays the student's own from the first line to the last, and a tutor's role with it is to teach method and to comment on reasoning the student has already written. Official syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are the board's copyright: we reference them, cite them and link to them rather than redistributing them.

Finally, no grade can be promised. A chemistry result depends on papers sat under timed conditions on particular mornings and on thresholds set after the series by the board. What can be committed to is the process: a diagnosis from a real script, recall lists taught and then tested cold, written work marked against the scheme wording, and an honest view when the evidence says the plan is not working.

faqs.question: Which ion and gas tests does my child have to know for 0620?
faqs.answer: The core set is short and examined repeatedly: carbon dioxide with limewater, oxygen with a glowing splint, hydrogen with a lighted splint, ammonia with damp red litmus, chlorine bleaching damp litmus, halide ions with acidified silver nitrate, sulfate ions with acidified barium salt solution, and carbonate ions by adding dilute acid and then testing the gas. A full answer gives the reagent, the condition, the observation in precise terms and the conclusion. That list can be taught in one session and secured by testing it cold a week later.

faqs.question: Why does writing that the solution turned cloudy score nothing?
faqs.answer: Because the mark is attached to a specific observation and cloudy is not it. Limewater turns milky, a precipitate is white, cream or yellow, litmus is bleached by chlorine rather than merely changing colour, and a glowing splint relights rather than burning more brightly. Students who have only discussed these tests aloud in class have never had to write them in the form that earns credit, so the answer sounds right and collects part marks at best. Writing them out and comparing against the scheme wording fixes it inside a session or two.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my daughter is entered for Core or Extended 0620?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry, which the school issues before the series, names the exact components and tier. Ask the science department or the exams officer rather than inferring it from a set name, because set names vary between schools and do not always map onto the entry. The distinction matters immediately for tutoring: Core and Extended candidates sit different papers at different depths and different grade ceilings, so the same revision plan cannot be right for both. We check this before writing any plan.

faqs.question: Can a student move from Core to Extended chemistry during Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the constraint is the entry calendar rather than the student's progress. Cambridge entries close months before the papers, with 27 November 2026 published as the final entry date for the March 2027 series, so a change raised in the spring is an administrative question rather than simply a conversation about readiness. If you believe the tier is wrong, raise it in the autumn term with a marked script in hand. Departments respond to evidence of what a student can actually produce, not to a general impression.

faqs.question: Which group trends come up most often in 0620?
faqs.answer: Reactivity down Group I, reactivity down Group VII with the displacement reactions that follow from it, melting points in both groups, the characteristic properties of the transition elements as a set, and the lack of reactivity of the noble gases. In each case the question asks for the trend and then the explanation, and the explanation is where the marks sit. Because the explanation structures repeat, learning two sentence shapes covers most of the group chemistry examined, which makes this one of the quickest areas to improve.

faqs.question: How much of 0620 is about industrial processes?
faqs.answer: Enough to be worth learning exactly. Iron extraction in the blast furnace, aluminium extraction by electrolysis with the role of cryolite, and the equilibrium contexts used to examine reversible reactions all recur. These questions are marked on conditions, named substances and balanced equations rather than on reasoning, which means a student can collect the marks by learning the detail precisely. It also makes the area a good fit for weeks when the school day is shortened and longer concentrated work is harder to schedule.

faqs.question: How far before the chemistry exam does the Cambridge entry deadline fall?
faqs.answer: Months. The published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due on 27 November 2026 for an examination period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due on 27 February 2027 and results released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May. The June and November series follow the same shape with different dates. The practical consequence for families is that the tier decision is settled well before the final mock, so questions about changing it belong to the autumn rather than the spring.

faqs.question: Why might my child's exam timetable differ from a friend's at another school?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each. Its own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Two Abu Dhabi schools can therefore sit the same paper on different days. The school's exams officer holds the correct version for your centre, and that is the document a revision plan should be built around.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE equivalency rule count, and is Arabic one of them?
faqs.answer: Reporting on the published British-track requirements states five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and that Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Whether a particular syllabus falls within those five is a question for the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority rather than for a tutoring provider, and it should be verified on moe.gov.ae for your own case.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on the salt preparation question?
faqs.answer: Almost always on the two steps that feel like housekeeping. The method runs: warm the acid, add the base in excess, filter off the unreacted excess, evaporate to the point of crystallisation and leave the rest to crystallise. Students who skip excess and filtration have removed two creditable steps and also lost the explanation mark, because using excess is the reason the resulting solution is neutral. For insoluble salts the equivalent omissions are washing and drying the precipitate after filtering.

faqs.question: What can one chemistry session realistically fix?
faqs.answer: A unit of exact content. One hour can secure the full set of gas tests, or the salt preparation sequence with its reasoning, or the blast furnace in the detail the scheme requires, or the two group trend sentence shapes. Those are measurable gains available to any student who turns up and writes. What an hour cannot do is build mole fluency or Extended organic mechanisms, both of which need spaced practice over weeks. Where the diagnosis is conceptual we give an honest estimate in weeks rather than sessions.

faqs.question: Does the periodic table come with the 0620 examination paper?
faqs.answer: Cambridge provides a periodic table with its chemistry papers, and the current syllabus and the front matter of any released paper confirm what candidates are given and what they are expected to recall. That distinction matters for revision planning, because time spent memorising something the paper supplies is time taken from the ion tests and extraction conditions that it does not. Check the current documents on cambridgeinternational.org for your child's series rather than relying on a revision guide, since the provided materials can be revised between syllabuses.

faqs.question: Will a chemistry tutor come to our house in Al Reef?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Abu Dhabi families run one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For chemistry this costs the student nothing, because none of the written work requires a bench, and it gains them access to a separate-science specialist rather than whoever teaches science within a short drive of the airport road communities. Apparatus handling for a laboratory practical test remains the school's part of the work.

faqs.question: What is a realistic number of chemistry sessions before a June series?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which pile the losses sit in, which is why the first session sorts them. A student whose losses are mostly exact recall can clear most of that pile in four to six sessions, because each one teaches a list and then tests the previous list cold. A student with genuine stoichiometry gaps needs spaced work across a term, and compressing it does not work. We would rather give an honest estimate at the start, with a recount after a few weeks, than quote a package that assumes an answer nobody has yet.

faqs.question: Does 0620 prepare a student for A Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: It is the normal route, and the step up is in the level of justification expected rather than in the topic list. Equilibria, kinetics, energetics and organic chemistry all reappear with mechanisms that have to be argued rather than recalled, and the practical papers are assessed in their own right. Students who struggle in the first term are frequently those whose mathematics is weak, because the calculations become heavier. Each Abu Dhabi sixth form sets its own entry requirements, so ask the school for the grades it actually expects.

intro.heading: What the single award certifies, and what it quietly leaves out
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653 is one course covering biology, chemistry and physics, producing a single grade. That sentence is the whole of the confusion. Families see three sciences on the syllabus and assume three qualifications, or see one grade and assume a reduced subject. Neither is right. It is one IGCSE whose content is drawn from all three disciplines at a reduced depth, and it occupies one subject slot on a timetable where separate sciences would occupy three.

The reduction is real and worth being specific about. Compared with separate biology, chemistry and physics, the single award carries less stoichiometry, a lighter organic chemistry section, fewer of the quantitative physics relationships, and less of the detailed physiology. It keeps the whole structure of each discipline: the particle model, the reactivity series, the energy stores, cells and transport, electricity and circuits. A student on 0653 is not studying different science. They are studying the same science with less of it.

That makes 0653 a sensible placement in several situations and a problem in one. It suits a student carrying a heavy option block, a student who arrived mid-course and has ground to make up, and a student whose interests sit elsewhere. It becomes a problem only where somebody intends to continue a science past Year 11 and nobody has checked what the sixth form expects, because a single grade covers all three subjects at once and cannot demonstrate strength in one of them.

Where the marks go is a separate question, and here the answers are predictable enough to plan around. Across marked 0653 papers the chemistry arithmetic and the physics relationships take more than their share, while biology losses are usually about diagrams, named structures and the precision of a definition rather than about understanding. That split matters because it means a session spent on biology revision generally returns less than a session spent on the chemistry calculations, whatever the student believes about which strand is hardest.

There is a scheduling point behind all of this that applies specifically to this emirate. Private schools in the UAE teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their own curriculum as part of the federal baseline, and those subjects carry homework that lands on the same evenings as everything else. A student on the single award is carrying one science subject rather than three, which is often exactly why the school placed them there. A tutoring plan that then tries to run three strands in parallel across one weekly hour recreates the load the placement was meant to remove, and it is the most common way a year of science support achieves very little.

IB Gram matches Abu Dhabi families to a tutor who teaches this syllabus and delivers it one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, around the school week. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a course spanning three disciplines that is a practical advantage, because the constraint is finding somebody who can carry all three strands properly, and that person does not have to live in your community.
