sections.heading: The five questions that explain a price difference
paragraphs: When two Abu Dhabi quotes differ sharply, the gap is almost always explained by five things, and none of them is quality in the abstract. The first is strand coverage: is this one tutor across biology, chemistry and physics, or one discipline with the other two uncovered. The second is marking: does written work come back marked against the published scheme between sessions, or is the hour the entire product. Those two account for most of the spread on their own.

The third is the tier. An Extended candidate has more content to cover than a Core candidate and will need more hours for the same grade movement, so a quote that does not ask which tier your child is entered for has not been costed against anything. The fourth is the practical component, which carries a meaningful share of the grade and is often left out of a plan entirely because it is assumed to require a laboratory. The conventions do not.

The fifth is scarcity, and it is the one that moves the top of the band. A tutor who can carry all three strands of the double award at Extended depth and mark them properly is not common, and in the weeks before a series the demand for that person peaks at once across the whole country. Booking earlier costs less than booking in April, not because of a surcharge but because the available choices narrow.

What should not be in the price is travel, which is why the arithmetic in the next section matters. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The practical consequence for a family in Al Rahba or on Yas Island is that the hour is an hour, and the rate is being paid for teaching rather than for a journey across the city.
bullets: Ask whether one tutor covers all three strands or only one
Ask whether marked work between sessions is inside the rate

Ask whether the practical component is in the plan

sections.heading: The travel arithmetic across Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: This section exists because the in-home published band of AED 180 to 500 does not tell a family what proportion of the booking is teaching. The emirate's geography makes the question sharper than it is in a dense city: journeys run between the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, Saadiyat, Yas, and mainland communities to the north and south, and the slowest hour of the day is exactly the hour when a session would start.

The table works the figure out for a typical ninety-minute in-home booking arriving around five in the afternoon. The journey estimates are deliberately described as typical rather than precise, because traffic varies, but the structure of the result does not change with the exact minutes. Where a tutor spends a substantial part of the trip travelling, the effective rate per teaching hour is well above the headline rate, and the family is paying it without ever being shown the sum.

There is a second cost that nobody prices, which is the student's own state. A session that starts after a long bus journey and a rushed meal is not worth the same as a session on a weekend morning, whatever the clock says. For Abu Dhabi families on long commutes the arrangement that produces the most value per dirham is usually a short midweek review and the longer timed work moved to the weekend, which is a scheduling decision rather than a pricing one.

None of this is an argument that in-home tutoring is bad. It is an argument that the published in-home band should be read as including a journey, and that a family comparing two quotes should ask how long the tutor expects to travel. Where the answer is twenty minutes each way from the next community, the arithmetic is mild. Where it is forty minutes each way across the city, it is not.

sections.heading: How many hours the tier commits you to
paragraphs: The tier your child is entered for is a budgeting fact before it is anything else. Core and Extended candidates sit different papers with different content depths and different grade ceilings, and an Extended candidate therefore has more ground to cover for the same amount of grade movement. A plan priced without reference to the tier is not a plan, and the statement of entry is the document that settles it rather than a set name.

For a Core candidate the money goes furthest on the exact-recall and presentational areas, because the conceptual depth is reduced and the cheap marks are available at both tiers. For an Extended candidate those areas are still the first purchase, and there is additional quantitative content behind them that the Core papers never reach. The sequence is the same; the length of the programme is not.

Movement between tiers is bounded by the entry calendar rather than by progress. Cambridge entries close months before the papers are sat, with final entries for the March 2027 series published as 27 November 2026, so a conversation about changing tier in the spring is administrative while the same conversation in the autumn is real. If a family is budgeting partly in the hope of an Extended entry, that hope needs testing with the department early.

This also affects what a quote should look like. We would rather state a number of sessions for a defined block, against a counted set of losses and a known tier, than quote an open-ended weekly arrangement. A block that ends has to justify itself; an arrangement that continues by default does not, and a family paying monthly for an indefinite period is the most common way money is wasted in this market.
bullets: Check the statement of entry for the tier before accepting any quote

sections.heading: Budgeting across two years, with the school bill in view
paragraphs: Tutoring is a small line next to school fees, and it is worth putting the two together before deciding what to spend. The table below is a planning frame rather than a quotation, and the AED figures in it come from the published market ranges set out earlier on this page. Filling it in for your own household usually clarifies the decision faster than any amount of comparison between providers.

One piece of relevant context has to be labelled carefully, because it applies to a different emirate. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under a second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. That is Dubai. Abu Dhabi families should check adek.gov.ae for the position in this emirate rather than assuming the same decision applies here.

The useful discipline is to decide the total first and the shape afterwards. A family that knows it can spend a fixed amount across Year 11 can choose between a short targeted block now and a weekly arrangement later, and can tell a provider which it wants rather than being sold the larger option by default. A family that starts with a monthly commitment and no total in mind usually spends more and reviews less.

Two further costs belong in the frame and are usually forgotten. Preparation for the practical component is cheap and is often omitted from plans entirely. And any private-candidate entry fee, where a student is sitting a paper outside their school's entry, is a separate matter arranged through a centre and nothing to do with a tutoring provider.

sections.heading: Group classes, and why three strands resist grouping
paragraphs: Group classes are genuinely cheaper per student, and in the mainland districts of Abu Dhabi they are readily available. For a single-subject syllabus with a shared timetable they can work well. For the double award they are harder to make work, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of teaching quality: four students in a 0654 group are usually losing marks in different strands, and the hour can only be pointed at one of them.

That produces a predictable pattern. The student whose losses match the session's focus gains; the others sit through content they already hold. Over a term each student receives perhaps a third of the hours they paid for in terms of relevance, which makes the lower per-student rate considerably less of a saving than it appears. Where a group has been formed around a shared diagnosis rather than a shared timetable, this objection falls away.

The second limitation is marking. Individual script marking against the published scheme is the first thing that disappears from a group arrangement, because it does not scale. Since marking is the mechanism that moves presentational and definitional marks, and since those are the cheapest marks in the course, a group class often removes exactly the component that would have given the best return.

Where a budget is genuinely tight, our view is that a short one-to-one block aimed at counted losses beats a term of group classes, and it costs less in total. That is an unusual thing for a provider to say, and it follows from the arithmetic rather than from generosity. A family that can afford only four hours should spend them on the four hours that return the most marks.
bullets: Groups formed around a timetable rather than a diagnosis dilute every hour

sections.heading: What to send so the quote does not change later
paragraphs: Most of the complaints families have about tutoring pricing come from quotes given without information. A provider asked how much do you charge will give a band; a provider sent a marked paper, a tier and two available evenings can give a number of sessions and a total. The second is a quote. The first is a brochure, and it will change once anybody looks at the work.

Four things are enough. The most recent marked science paper, so the losses can be counted by strand. The statement of entry or a confirmation of the tier, since Core and Extended plans differ in length. The two or three evenings and weekend slots that are genuinely free, because a plan built on an evening that is already taken will be rescheduled out of existence. And the date of the series your child is sitting, so the plan can be counted backwards from it.

With those in hand, the first session is free and produces a counted set of losses, a written diagnosis and a recommendation with a number of sessions attached. The free lesson is one per student, needs no card, and nothing has to be cancelled afterwards. We mention the condition here because a provider advertising something free without saying what the condition is should be asked, and we would rather be held to the same standard.

On invoices and tax, our position is narrow and deliberate. Ask any provider whether a quoted AED figure includes value added tax and ask for a proper invoice. We do not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE as a general fact, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring page, and a family that needs certainty on it should take the question to an accountant or to the authority itself.
bullets: Send a marked paper, the tier, your free slots and the series date
Expect a number of sessions and a total, not a band
The free lesson is one per student, with no card required
Ask whether a quoted figure includes VAT, and ask for an invoice

sections.heading: When we would tell an Abu Dhabi family not to spend the money
paragraphs: There are several situations where buying sessions is not the right decision, and saying so costs us a sale and keeps the page honest. The first is where the school is already providing targeted support that the family has not used. A science department running a clinic for its coordinated sets is offering free teaching from somebody who knows the cohort and the scheme of work, and paying for a parallel arrangement before trying it is poor value.

The second is where the mark count shows large content gaps across all three strands with only a few weeks left. More hours cannot cover a syllabus in that window. The honest advice is to spend a small amount on the recall-heavy and presentational areas for the best marks per hour and let the rest go, rather than buy a package that cannot do what the family is hoping for.

The third is where the problem is not academic. A student who is not sleeping, who has lost confidence after a poor mock, or who is carrying more subjects than they can manage is not helped by a seventh hour of science a week. That is a conversation with the school, and occasionally with somebody else entirely. A tutoring provider that cannot recognise it is selling the wrong thing.

And the fourth is simply that the counted losses are small. Where a comparable paper shows a student a few marks below their target with the losses spread thinly, the realistic gain from a term of paid sessions may be smaller than the cost, and the better purchase is a single diagnostic session with a written plan the student can execute alone. We offer that, and a number of families take it and stop there.
bullets: Try the school's own support before paying for a parallel arrangement
With weeks left and gaps across all three strands, buy only the cheap marks

process.title: Send four things
process.description: The most recent marked science paper, the statement of entry or the tier, the evenings and weekend slots that are genuinely free, and the series your child is sitting. With those, a provider can quote a number of sessions and a total rather than an hourly band.

process.title: A free first lesson that counts the losses
process.description: One free session per student, with no card required and nothing to cancel. It attributes every lost mark to biology, chemistry or physics and to a type of error, and produces a written diagnosis you keep whether or not you buy anything.

process.title: Price the plan, not the hour
process.description: The recommendation names the areas to work on in order of marks returned per hour, the number of sessions, and the total. A short targeted block is often what the count supports, and it is often cheaper than the weekly arrangement families expect to be sold.

process.title: Marked work inside the figure
process.description: Written work is set each session and comes back marked against the published scheme, with a record of which strands have been tested. That is inside the quoted figure rather than billed on top, because it is the part that moves the cheapest marks.

process.title: Recount, then decide whether to spend more
process.description: After the block, the losses are counted again on a comparable paper. You then decide whether further hours are worth buying, with a number in front of you. Where the honest answer is that they are not, we say so rather than roll the arrangement forward.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The bands on this page are other providers' published rates and figures from a 2026 Dubai cost survey, stated as at October 2026 and attributed. A page that publishes a range without saying who charges it is publishing an opinion dressed as data.

whyPoints.title: Costed per mark, not per hour
whyPoints.description: Marks come back at very different prices depending on where they are being lost. Counting the losses first and ranking the areas by marks returned per hour is what turns a budget into a plan, and it usually makes the plan smaller.

whyPoints.title: The travel arithmetic shown, not implied
whyPoints.description: The published in-home band includes a journey across Abu Dhabi, and this page works out what that does to the effective teaching rate. Lessons are delivered over live video, so the hour you pay for is the hour your child is taught.

whyPoints.title: One tutor across three strands
whyPoints.description: The double award needs biology, chemistry and physics covered at a consistent depth. Three separate specialists at mid-band rates is a much larger monthly figure, and for most families on this page it buys coverage the student does not need.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: We would rather quote a defined number of sessions against counted losses than an open-ended monthly arrangement. A block has to justify itself at the end; a rolling arrangement does not, which is how money quietly disappears in this market.

whyPoints.title: Advice against spending, where it applies
whyPoints.description: Where the school's own support has not been tried, where the gaps are too wide for the time remaining, or where the counted losses are small and thin, the honest recommendation is to spend less or nothing. That recommendation is part of the free first session.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654 tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published figures across the UAE run from about AED 33 to 65 at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, AED 200 to 450 or above for an IGCSE specialist, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits including travel, and AED 650 at the premium end where one provider publishes that figure. Those are other providers' own rates as at October 2026 rather than our price list. For the double award the number that matters more is the total, because the plan has to cover three disciplines.

faqs.question: Which part of 0654 gives back the most marks per dirham spent?
faqs.answer: Physics unit handling first, then biology definitions and named structures, then thermal physics mechanisms, then group trends with their explanations, then the practical conventions. All of those are forms of words or habits rather than concepts, so one session each can secure them and they are often being lost by students who understand the science perfectly well. Quantitative chemistry is the opposite: a large block of marks that moves slowly and needs spaced work across weeks. Counting the losses on a real paper tells you which applies to your child.

faqs.question: Why do two Abu Dhabi tutors quote such different rates for the same course?
faqs.answer: Five things explain nearly all of it: whether one tutor covers all three strands or only one; whether written work comes back marked against the published scheme between sessions; whether the plan was costed against Core or Extended; whether the practical component is included; and scarcity, which moves the top of the band in the weeks before a series. A quote that does not ask which tier your child is entered for has not been costed against anything, and is a band rather than a price.

faqs.question: Does the tier my daughter is entered for change what I should budget?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially. Extended candidates have more content to cover for the same grade movement, so a plan runs longer at the same hourly rate. The cheapest areas are identical at both tiers, which means the first block of work looks the same; what differs is the additional quantitative content behind it that Core papers never reach. Check the statement of entry rather than a set name, because set names vary between schools and do not always match the entry that was actually made.

faqs.question: How much should I budget for 0654 across Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: Published monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run from about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to over 2,000 for specialist examination-year support. A short targeted block of four to six sessions aimed at the cheapest marks is a much smaller total and is frequently enough. The discipline that helps most is deciding your total first and then choosing the shape, rather than starting a monthly arrangement with no ceiling in mind.

faqs.question: How much of an in-home hour in Abu Dhabi is actually teaching?
faqs.answer: It depends on the journey, and the published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 includes it. Within the central island a trip is short and the headline rate is close to the real one. From the island out to Khalifa City, or from the mainland to Al Rahba, Al Shahama or Al Shamkha at five in the afternoon, a meaningful part of the booking is the approach, and the effective teaching rate rises accordingly. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India.

faqs.question: Is a small group class a sensible way to cover three sciences?
faqs.answer: Only where the group was formed around a shared diagnosis rather than a shared timetable. Four students on the double award are usually losing marks in different strands, and an hour can be pointed at one of them, so each student receives a fraction of the relevance they paid for. Individual script marking is also the first thing a group arrangement drops, and that is the mechanism that moves the cheapest marks. On a tight budget, a short one-to-one block aimed at counted losses usually costs less in total.

faqs.question: Does the quote include marking between sessions?
faqs.answer: Ask, every time, of anybody. It is the single largest hidden variable in this market. An hour of live teaching is one hour of work; an hour plus a script marked against the published scheme and a record of which strands have been tested is closer to ninety minutes, which is why the specialist bands sit where they do. In our arrangement the marking is inside the quoted figure rather than billed on top, because it is the part that moves definitional and presentational marks.

faqs.question: Do science tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi change as the exam series approaches?
faqs.answer: The published bands do not move, but the available choices narrow sharply, which has the same practical effect. A tutor who can carry all three strands of the double award at Extended depth and mark them properly is not common, and demand for that person peaks across the whole country at once in the weeks before a series. Booking earlier does not buy a discount; it buys a choice. Families who wait until April are generally choosing from whoever is left rather than from whoever fits.

faqs.question: Should we take a monthly 0654 package or pay for a defined block?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the questions that decide it are what happens to unused sessions, how much notice is needed to pause, and whether marking sits inside the figure. Published packages in this market appear at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and between AED 1,599 and 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours. A package is good value when the student will genuinely use every session and poor value across a term containing travel, assessment weeks and a shortened school day.

faqs.question: What should I ask about VAT on a tutoring invoice?
faqs.answer: Ask whether the AED figure you have been quoted is inclusive or exclusive of value added tax, and ask for a proper invoice showing it. We deliberately do not state the general VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE on this page, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring provider, and a page that asserts it without citing the authority is guessing on your behalf. Where certainty matters for your household, put the question to an accountant or to the authority directly.

faqs.question: What does the free first lesson include, and is there a condition?
faqs.answer: It is one free session per student, with no card required and nothing to cancel afterwards. In it, the lost marks on a paper you send are counted by strand and by error type, your child writes one description answer which is marked against the published scheme wording in front of them, and you receive a written diagnosis with a recommended number of sessions. You keep that diagnosis whether or not you buy anything, and several families take it to their school instead.

faqs.question: How much does preparing for the 0654 practical component add?
faqs.answer: One or two sessions, which is cheap relative to the share of the grade it carries. The skills examined are conventions rather than content: reading instruments, recording to consistent precision, tabulating with units in the heading, plotting, drawing a line of best fit that is not obliged to pass through the origin, identifying anomalies, naming a specific source of error and suggesting an improvement that addresses it. Those can be taught over video. Apparatus handling for a laboratory test remains the school's part of the work.

faqs.question: Does Abu Dhabi school fee policy affect what we should budget for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It affects the total household figure, and the position here should be checked locally. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That decision is Dubai's. For Abu Dhabi, check adek.gov.ae rather than assuming the same applies, and put the school bill and the tutoring plan in the same frame before deciding what to spend.

faqs.question: When would you tell us not to buy any sessions?
faqs.answer: Four situations. Where the school already runs targeted support the family has not tried, since that is free teaching from somebody who knows the scheme of work. Where the mark count shows wide gaps across all three strands with only weeks left, when the honest plan is a small amount of work on the cheapest marks. Where the real problem is sleep, confidence or subject load rather than science. And where the counted losses are small and thinly spread, when a single diagnostic session with a written plan may be all that is worth buying.

intro.heading: Price this subject by the marking, because that is what you are buying
paragraphs: Economics is unusual among IGCSE subjects in that the content is not the hard part. A reasonably attentive student can learn what a subsidy does and how a central bank raises interest rates in a term. What takes two years is writing about it in the form the mark scheme pays for: define, explain the mechanism, use a diagram, then evaluate with a judgement that follows from the argument rather than from an opinion. That writing has to be produced and marked, repeatedly, and that is what a family is actually purchasing.

This matters for the money question because most tutoring is sold as teaching time, and for 0455 the limiting input is marking turnaround. An hour spent explaining price elasticity has some value. An hour spent reading the student's own twenty-mark answer against the criteria, naming where the evaluation marks were available and were not taken, and then watching them rewrite one paragraph, has much more. A family who understands that will buy a different package, and usually a cheaper one.

Here are the market figures first, since almost nobody in this search result publishes any. UAE providers' own published rates in October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget and university-student end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IGCSE or A-Level specialist, and AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in. Premium named tutors are advertised up to around AED 650. Those are other providers' numbers from their own pages, not IB Gram's price list, which is discussed on the consultation after a free trial.

There are no in-home visits in the UAE — that part of the service exists only in India — so every Abu Dhabi session is delivered online over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For a writing subject this removes the travel premium entirely, and it also means a student's answers can be submitted, annotated and returned as files that a family keeps rather than as a page handed back and lost in a school bag.

The rest of this page is organised around cost: what the papers demand and therefore what has to be bought, what the different kinds of work are worth, what moves the number in this emirate specifically, and what tutoring sits alongside in a household already paying private school fees. The aim is that you can price any provider's offer, including this one, before making a single enquiry, and that you know which two questions separate quotes that look identical on paper.

One framing note before the detail. Nothing here is a statement about what your child will achieve. No tutor can see the paper, the boundaries or the day, and any provider attaching a grade to a price is selling something other than teaching. What a price can honestly buy is a number of marked extended answers, returned quickly, with the available marks named. Whether that moves a grade depends on what the student does with them between sessions.

sections.heading: The two papers, and why one of them decides the grade
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Economics is assessed by two papers. The first is a multiple-choice paper of forty-five minutes carrying thirty marks and thirty per cent of the grade. The second is a structured paper of two hours fifteen minutes carrying ninety marks and seventy per cent. Section A of that paper is a compulsory data-response question worth thirty marks; Section B offers four structured questions of which the candidate answers three, each worth twenty marks.

That distribution tells you where the money goes. A candidate who performs well on multiple choice and poorly on structured answers is losing from the large pool, and no amount of content revision changes that, because the content was already known. A candidate who is weak on multiple choice is usually weak on definitions, which is cheap and quick to fix. Diagnosing which of the two you are dealing with takes one past paper and an hour of marking.

Inside a twenty-mark structured question the marks are distributed across parts, with the earlier parts asking for definitions and explanations and the later parts asking for discussion or analysis. The upper-band marks sit almost entirely in those later parts. Students reach them with ten minutes left, write two sentences of opinion, and lose a quarter of the available marks on the paper while believing the answer went reasonably well.

Confirm the paper structure, timings and weightings for your child's exam year on the Cambridge International website. Syllabuses are revised on a cycle and a second-hand revision guide may describe a different arrangement, which is a real and avoidable source of wasted preparation.

sections.heading: Evaluation: the marks that separate a middling grade from a strong one
paragraphs: Ask a 0455 candidate in the middle of the range what they find hard and they will usually say the long questions. Ask what they do in them and the answer is revealing: they explain, thoroughly and correctly, and then stop. The explanation earns the lower and middle band marks. The upper band asks for something structurally different, and it can be taught as a structure rather than coaxed out as a style.

The move has three parts. First, identify two effects that pull in opposite directions — the policy helps producers and hurts consumers, the tariff protects employment and raises prices. Second, say what the net outcome depends on: elasticity, the time period, the size of the change, the state of the economy. Third, reach a judgement that follows from the second part rather than from a preference. A student who writes those three things in that order earns the discussion marks almost regardless of how elegant the prose is.

The second reliable gain is time. Candidates reach the discussion part with ten minutes remaining because the earlier parts were over-written. A definition worth two marks does not need a paragraph. Rationing time by the mark allocation, rehearsed on full papers rather than discussed in principle, recovers upper-band marks that the student was fully capable of earning and never reached.

This is also where marking turnaround earns its money. A discussion paragraph read against the criteria, with the available marks pointed out and the structure named, teaches more in fifteen minutes than an hour of general advice about writing. Which is why the honest unit of cost for this subject is the marked piece rather than the lesson.

sections.heading: Diagrams: drawn wrong, or drawn right and never used
paragraphs: Economics diagrams are among the cheapest marks in the Cambridge suite and among the most reliably lost. There are perhaps eight or nine a 0455 candidate needs to be able to draw without hesitating: demand and supply with a shift, a price ceiling and a floor, elasticity cases, external costs and benefits, and the basic macroeconomic picture. That is a finite list, which makes it a drill rather than a topic.

Two failure modes account for nearly all the losses. The first is mechanical: axes unlabelled or labelled with the wrong variable, no original equilibrium marked, a shift drawn without an arrow or a new label, a new equilibrium left unidentified. Each of those is a lost mark on a diagram the student essentially understood. Ten minutes a week of drawing against a checklist clears it in a month.

The second is subtler and costs more. A candidate draws a correct diagram and then writes a paragraph that never refers to it. The diagram sits on the page as decoration. Marks for diagrams are earned when the prose points at them: name the shift, name the movement from one equilibrium to the other, say what happened to price and quantity. The habit to install is a sentence that begins by referring to the figure, every time.

On a screen this work is straightforward. The student draws on paper and holds it up, or draws on a shared whiteboard, and the tutor annotates the labels that are missing while both watch. The annotated version is saved with the marked answer, so the checklist becomes a record rather than a piece of advice.

paragraphs: A single hourly rate is a poor way to price this subject, because the five things a family might ask for have very different value and very different turnaround. The pattern worth noticing is that the cheapest tasks and the most valuable tasks are not the same tasks. Content teaching is the easiest thing to buy and the least likely to move a near-miss candidate, because the content was usually not the problem. Marking extended answers is harder to buy, because it requires somebody who knows the criteria, and it is what moves a grade from the middle band upwards.

Two questions separate comparable-looking quotes. Does the figure include marking of work done between sessions, or only time in the lesson? And what is the turnaround — an answer marked within two days while the question is still fresh is worth considerably more than the same marking returned in a fortnight. Providers rarely volunteer either answer, and both change the real price per unit of value.

On tax, ask the provider directly whether their quoted AED figure is inclusive, and get it in writing. The UAE treatment of tuition fees is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for any tutoring site, including this one, and two quotes are only comparable once you know what each includes and how long a session actually runs.

sections.heading: Using the UAE economy in answers, and why it earns marks
paragraphs: Structured questions ask candidates to apply ideas, and an answer anchored in a real economy the student knows is almost always sharper than one built on an invented country. Students in Abu Dhabi have a particularly rich set of examples available, and almost none of them use it, because nobody has pointed out that they may.

The obvious material is economic diversification: an economy with substantial hydrocarbon revenues deliberately building tourism, logistics, financial services and manufacturing is a live illustration of structural change, opportunity cost and the problem of relying on a single export. Development questions about the structure of an economy, and trade questions about export concentration, both land naturally here.

There is more. An expatriate-majority labour market is a usable example in questions about labour supply, migration and wage determination. Free-zone arrangements illustrate incentives, foreign direct investment and the trade-off between revenue and attracting activity. The introduction of value added tax is a concrete instance of an indirect tax and its incidence. Private school fees themselves are a workable example of a market with inelastic demand, which students find memorable for obvious reasons.

Two rules keep this safe. Use the mechanism, not a statistic: an unsourced number is worth nothing and risks being wrong, while a correctly explained mechanism earns the mark regardless. And keep the example subordinate to the economics — examiners reward the analysis the example supports, not the local knowledge itself. A paragraph that explains incidence correctly and mentions an indirect tax in passing beats a paragraph of local colour with no theory in it.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context for an Abu Dhabi household
paragraphs: Families rarely ask whether tutoring is expensive in the abstract. They ask whether it is a sensible addition to what they already pay for school. The table below puts the published tutoring bands beside the other costs attached to a Cambridge course, so the comparison is explicit rather than implied.

Some context on the market those fees sit in. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum schools taking 37 per cent of students, Indian 26, US 14 and the International Baccalaureate 7. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in that emirate for 2026-27, under an economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi regulates its own fees through its own authority, so neither figure is a statement about this emirate — they are the nearest published anchors available, and they are Dubai's.

Against that backdrop the arithmetic is usually straightforward. Published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in the UAE market run around AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised include roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, the gap between those two being largely travel.

The expense that catches families out is not the hourly rate; it is duration. An open-ended weekly arrangement running from September to June at a specialist rate is a significant annual commitment, and much of it is often spent on content the student already knew. A block with a stated number of marked pieces and an end point costs less, is easier to judge, and can always be renewed.

sections.heading: After 0455: the Diploma, A-Level and the equivalency question
paragraphs: A 0455 grade leads in three directions, and knowing which one a student is heading for changes what is worth paying for now. Diploma Programme Economics and A-Level Economics both demand substantially more evaluation and a much larger volume of writing, so a student continuing with the subject gets more value from marking hours in Year 11 than from content coverage. A student stopping at IGCSE needs the grade and nothing more, which argues for a shorter, sharper block.

The transition itself is specific enough to plan. The content overlap between 0455 and either post-16 course is considerable: the basic economic problem, allocation of resources, microeconomic decision makers, government and the macroeconomy, development, trade and globalisation all reappear with more depth. What is new is the quantity of judgement expected and, in the Diploma, the internal assessment, which is the student's own work and must remain so.

On university equivalency, the published British-track rule from the Ministry of Education asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. An Economics grade can be one of them. One competitor ranking in this market publishes a different subject count; the published rule is five.

Private schools in Abu Dhabi are supervised by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which handles licensing and accreditation in the emirate, while Dubai, Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah and the remaining emirates have their own arrangements. Alongside the Cambridge options, schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, with prescribed content supplied by the school. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education or Cambridge International, takes no part in the equivalency process, and nobody should suggest tutoring is required for it.

process.title: Send one structured answer and its mark
process.description: A photograph of a marked twenty-mark answer tells a specialist more than any description of how your child finds Economics. The mark distribution across the parts usually shows immediately whether definitions, mechanism, diagrams or evaluation is the costly one.

process.title: Take the free trial, one per student
process.description: A full session at no charge, no card details taken, no obligation afterwards. Use it to have one extended answer marked against the criteria rather than to discuss approach, so that a dated script exists before anything is paid for.

process.title: Ask what the figure includes
process.description: Specifically: does it cover marking of work written between sessions, what is the turnaround, is the figure per hour or per session, and how long is a session. In this subject the marking is most of the value, so a quote without those answers is not comparable to another quote.

process.title: Buy a block with an end point
process.description: A stated number of marked pieces and a scope taken from a marked paper. Open-ended weekly arrangements from September to June are where the budget disappears, usually into content the student already knew. A block can always be renewed; an endless arrangement is hard to shorten.

process.title: Write between sessions, not during them
process.description: The student produces the extended answer alone, under time, and brings it. Session time goes on marking it, naming the available marks that were not taken, and rebuilding one paragraph. An hour watching a tutor model an answer teaches far less than an hour on the student's own.

process.title: Read the marks by part, halfway through
process.description: Halfway through a block, look at how marks are distributed across the parts of each answer rather than at the totals. If the discussion parts are still empty, change the target or the tutor rather than renewing at the same rate.

whyPoints.title: Priced by the work, not by the hour
whyPoints.description: Content teaching, definition drilling, data-response practice, extended-answer marking and full papers have different values and different turnarounds. Separating them lets a family buy what their child actually needs instead of a single undifferentiated hourly rate.

whyPoints.title: A published AED band
whyPoints.description: Three of the six top-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all and two of the rest quote in dollars. The bands here come from providers' own rate pages with the collection month stated, so a parent can compare before making an enquiry.

whyPoints.title: Evaluation taught as a structure
whyPoints.description: Two opposing effects, what the outcome depends on, then a judgement that follows. Written in that order, the upper-band discussion marks are reachable by an ordinary writer, which is a different proposition from being told to be more analytical.

whyPoints.title: Diagrams marked twice
whyPoints.description: Once for accuracy — axes, original equilibrium, shift, new equilibrium — and once for whether the prose actually refers to them. A correct diagram nobody mentions is decoration, and this is among the cheapest sets of marks in the syllabus to recover.

whyPoints.title: Travel priced out
whyPoints.description: In-home visits in this emirate are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour and a real share of that is the drive. There are no in-home visits in the UAE from IB Gram, so the saving either buys a scarcer specialist or stays with the family.

whyPoints.title: No claims you cannot check
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no examiner status asserted without evidence, no regulator approval implied, and no statistic without its source and date. IB Gram holds no accreditation from ADEK, the Ministry of Education or Cambridge International, and the page says so.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 tutor cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates collected in October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget or university-student online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IGCSE or A-Level specialist, and AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in. For this subject the figure matters less than what it covers: ask whether marking of extended answers written between sessions is included, and what the turnaround is. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours.

faqs.question: Why is seventy per cent of the grade on one paper, and what does that mean for spending?
faqs.answer: The structured paper carries ninety of the available marks and runs two hours fifteen minutes, with a compulsory thirty-mark data-response question and three structured questions of twenty marks each chosen from four. The multiple-choice paper carries thirty marks in forty-five minutes. So most of the grade is produced by extended writing, which means most of the budget should buy marking of extended writing. Content revision addresses the smaller pool and is usually not where a middling candidate is losing marks.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but sits in the middle of the range. What is missing?
faqs.answer: Almost always the discussion marks at the end of each structured question. Candidates explain thoroughly and then stop, which earns the lower and middle bands. The upper band wants a different structure: name two effects pulling in opposite directions, say what the net outcome depends on — elasticity, time period, scale, the state of the economy — and then give a judgement that follows from that. Written in that order it is reachable by an ordinary writer, and six to eight marked pieces usually install it.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest intervention that actually moves a 0455 grade?
faqs.answer: For a near-miss candidate, an evaluation-only block of six to eight sessions scoped from a marked paper, with a re-test on comparable questions at the end. It is cheap because it is narrow and because it targets the marks the student was already capable of earning. For a Year 10 student, fortnightly marking of one extended answer is cheaper still and usually removes the need for an intensive Year 11 block altogether, which is the real saving.

faqs.question: Are diagram marks worth paying attention to?
faqs.answer: They are among the cheapest marks in the syllabus and among the most reliably lost. There are only eight or nine diagrams a 0455 candidate needs to draw without hesitating, which makes it a drill rather than a topic. Marks go missing in two ways: mechanically, through unlabelled axes, no original equilibrium or an unmarked new one; and through a correct diagram that the written answer never refers to. Ten minutes a week against a checklist clears the first within a month.

faqs.question: Is an in-home Economics tutor worth the extra cost?
faqs.answer: For a marking-led subject the case is weak. Extended answers are documents, so they can be submitted, annotated against the criteria and returned as files a family keeps, which is more useful than a page handed back in a school bag. In-home visits in this emirate are quoted between AED 180 and 500 an hour, with the drive forming part of that. There are no in-home visits in the UAE from IB Gram; that service runs only in India, and Abu Dhabi lessons are delivered online.

faqs.question: How many marked pieces should we budget for across Year 11?
faqs.answer: Around thirty for a weekly arrangement from September, with full structured papers added after the January mock. Starting after that mock compresses the same work into five months at the point when specialist availability in Abu Dhabi is tightest, which costs more in both hours and rate. A Year 10 fortnightly arrangement is about twenty marked pieces, bought at the quieter end of the market, and it is the better value by a wide margin.

faqs.question: Can my child use UAE examples in their answers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually sharpens an answer. Economic diversification away from hydrocarbon revenue illustrates structural change and export concentration. An expatriate-majority labour market is usable in questions on labour supply and wages. Free zones illustrate investment incentives, and value added tax is a concrete indirect tax for incidence questions. Two rules: use the mechanism rather than a statistic, since an unsourced number earns nothing, and keep the example subordinate to the economics, because the analysis is what is marked.

faqs.question: Should we choose Economics or Business Studies?
faqs.answer: They are marked for different things, and schools often present them as interchangeable. Business rewards applied judgement on a case study with a recommendation. Economics rewards abstract mechanism, diagrams and evaluation of policy. A student who likes concrete decisions tends to prefer Business; one who likes explaining why a market behaves as it does tends to prefer Economics. One or two sessions on a real structured question in Year 9 answers it far better than an option-evening description.

faqs.question: Does the quoted price include marking work written between sessions?
faqs.answer: Ask, because for this subject it is most of the value. A twenty-mark answer read against the criteria, with the available marks pointed out and the structure named, teaches more in fifteen minutes than an hour of general advice about analytical writing. Some providers include that in the session rate, some bill it separately, and some do not mark between sessions at all. Two quotes with the same hourly number are not the same offer if one of them includes this and the other does not.

faqs.question: How quickly should marked work come back?
faqs.answer: Within two days, while the student still remembers the decisions they made writing it. Marking returned a fortnight later is read as a verdict rather than as feedback, and the student has usually written another answer in the meantime with the same fault in it. Turnaround is a question worth asking any provider and one almost none volunteer. It changes the real value of the same hourly rate considerably, which is why it belongs in a price comparison.

faqs.question: Is value added tax included in the rates quoted by UAE tutors?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing before committing to a block. The tax treatment of tuition in the UAE is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority, not for a tutoring website, including this one. What matters practically is comparability: two quotes mean nothing side by side until you know whether each is inclusive, whether the figure is per hour or per session, and how long a session actually runs in minutes.

faqs.question: How does tutoring spend compare with what we already pay for school?
faqs.answer: Published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in the UAE market run around AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, against private school fees that run into the tens of thousands per year. The expense that catches families out is duration rather than rate: an open-ended arrangement from September to June at a specialist rate adds up, and much of it is often spent on content the student already knew.

faqs.question: Does a 0455 grade count towards UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five. An Economics grade can be one of them. One ranking competitor publishes a different subject count; verify the current rule with the Ministry rather than with any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Is 0455 good preparation for Diploma or A-Level Economics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the overlap is larger than most students expect: the basic economic problem, allocation of resources, microeconomic decision makers, government and the macroeconomy, development, and trade all reappear with more depth. What changes is the volume of writing and the weight of judgement expected, plus the internal assessment in the Diploma, which is the student's own work and must remain so. A student continuing with the subject gets more value from marking hours now than from extra content coverage.

faqs.question: What if no 0455 specialist is free at the hours we want?
faqs.answer: You will be told rather than quietly matched with a general tutor. Economics specialists who mark extended answers against the criteria are a narrower group than tutors who can teach the content, and the evening slots in the two months before a June series fill first. The workable options are a waiting slot, a different time, or a weekend session long enough to mark a full structured paper, which several families end up preferring. A non-specialist match would cost a term and change little.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-economics-0455.closingBody: You now have the AED bands, the task-by-task breakdown, the session totals and the two questions — what the figure includes and how fast work comes back — that separate quotes which look identical. Use them on any provider, this one included. If you want a starting point, send one marked twenty-mark answer with its mark distribution, take the free trial, and ask inside that hour for a second answer to be marked against the criteria. Sessions run one-to-one over live video to Abu Dhabi in Gulf Standard Time, the block has a stated end point, and the marked scripts are yours.

intro.heading: An English grade moves when the marking gets specific, and not before
paragraphs: English as a First Language is the subject where Abu Dhabi parents most often feel they are paying for something they cannot inspect. A maths script has right answers on it. A 0500 composition comes back with a mark, perhaps a comment about expression, and no visible mechanism connecting the two. Families then do the only thing available to them, which is to buy more reading and more practice, and six months later the grade has moved by a mark or two. The money was not wasted exactly, but almost none of it was aimed at anything in particular, and nobody in the house can say what the next six months should be spent on either.

The mechanism exists, and it is public. Each of the two written papers carries eighty marks and half the qualification. The composition tasks are marked on two separate scales: twenty-four marks for content and structure, sixteen marks for style and accuracy. Directed writing is marked for reading as well as for writing, which is why a candidate who writes beautifully but ignores half the source material cannot reach the top band. Once a student knows which of those scales is costing them, the work becomes concrete.

That is the whole argument for this page. A Cambridge IGCSE English First Language 0500 tutor in Abu Dhabi should hand you a dated script every week with the mark split written on it, and a second script eight weeks later on a comparable task. You read the two. If content and structure has moved from the middle band to the upper band while style and accuracy has not, you know precisely what the next month is for. Nothing about that process requires trusting anybody's judgement, including the tutor's.

Sessions are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. For written English the online format is genuinely better rather than merely acceptable, because the work is a document. A tutor and a student can look at the same paragraph on a shared screen, highlight the four sentences that all open the same way, and rewrite one of them together while both watch the sentence change. That is harder to do sitting side by side over a single sheet of paper.

It also widens the pool, which matters more in English than in most subjects. The useful 0500 tutor is somebody who has marked a great many scripts and can tell you, within a paragraph, whether a candidate's problem is range of vocabulary, control of sentence structure, paragraph shape or simply not answering the question. The number of people in Abu Dhabi who can do that and who are free at 17:00 on a Tuesday is small. Over video it is a roster rather than a radius.

Reading marks tracked separately from writing marks

Redrafting is coached; the words on the page stay the student's

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-english-first-.programmesIntro: 0500 sits at the end of a long run-up and the start of another. These are the stages where English support changes something, and what the hour is actually spent on at each one.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the English route is set
programmes.description: The year a school decides whether a student will sit First Language or Second Language English. The deciding evidence should be a piece of extended writing marked against the 0500 criteria rather than a general impression of fluency. Work at this stage is paragraph architecture, sentence variety and the habit of planning before writing, all of which are cheaper to install now than to retrofit in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi cohorts are highly multilingual, and a confident English speaker is not automatically a First Language candidate. The distinction Cambridge draws is about written range and control, not about conversation, and a school that decides on fluency alone sometimes places a student on a route that caps them.

programmes.name: Year 10, building the two papers separately
programmes.description: The best year for skill isolation. A Year 10 student can spend four weeks on summary alone, then four on writer's effects, then a block on descriptive writing, and finish each block with a marked task on that one skill. Treating the papers as a single blur called 'English' is why Year 10 often produces no measurable movement despite a full year of lessons.
programmes.countryNote: Term structure in the emirate puts a long break in the middle of the year and a Ramadan term with compressed days near the end. A single short weekly session held through those weeks keeps the writing habit alive, which matters far more in English than in a content subject.

programmes.name: Year 11, the June series and the mark split
programmes.description: Work becomes production under time. Full papers, strictly timed, with each composition marked on both scales and the lost marks attributed to a cause: ran out of time, drifted off the task, narrow sentence range, punctuation errors repeating. Those four causes need four different responses, and a term spent on general practice addresses none of them in particular.
programmes.countryNote: Candidates in Abu Dhabi sit the June series with final entries submitted months earlier. The speaking and listening component is separately endorsed and reported apart from the grade, so a family worried about an oral test should confirm with the school what is actually being entered.

programmes.name: After 0500: A-Level English and other literate subjects
programmes.description: A 0500 grade is a gateway to AS and A-Level English Language or Literature, and a prerequisite in effect for subjects that are assessed through extended writing. The transition work is argument structure and evidence handling rather than more description, and students who learned to plan in Year 10 find it a short step.
programmes.countryNote: For university admission in the UAE and abroad, English attainment is usually examined twice: once through the school certificate and once through a separate language test. Treat the 0500 grade and an IELTS or TOEFL score as two different pieces of work with different preparation.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-english-first-.subjectsIntro: The Cambridge IGCSE subjects most often taken alongside 0500 in Abu Dhabi schools, with the part of each that draws on the same writing skill.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English Literature (0475)
subjects.description: The closest neighbour. Literature rewards close reading of language, which is the same muscle as the writer's effects question in 0500. Students taking both should be shown explicitly that the two papers want different outputs from the same observation.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: The alternative English route. 0510 is assessed through structured exercises and a listening paper rather than extended composition. The choice between the two is one of the more consequential decisions in a bilingual Abu Dhabi household.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE History (0470)
subjects.description: Source-based essays with a strict demand for evidence. History students often bring strong paragraph discipline to 0500 and lose marks instead on descriptive range, which is a useful thing for a tutor to know in week one.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Rewards precise description of data and process. Geography candidates tend to handle the summary question well because they are used to compressing information, and need more work on the imaginative writing tasks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Built on defined terms used exactly. Economics students write tightly and often too tightly for a 0500 composition, where variety of sentence structure carries real marks on the style and accuracy scale.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: No shared content, but a shared scheduling problem. Maths and English both reward daily short practice, and a Year 11 timetable that gives all its evening hours to maths is the most common reason an English grade stalls.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study answers with a clear structure and a recommendation. Business candidates are often good at directed writing because they already write to an audience and a purpose, which is exactly what that task is marked on.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Research, argument and reflective writing. It builds the planning habit that 0500 rewards, and the written components are a useful place to practise the same paragraph discipline under lower stakes.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Taken by many Abu Dhabi students alongside 0500. Carrying two first-language literacies at once is demanding and real, and a revision plan that ignores the Arabic paper is a plan the student will quietly abandon.

sections.heading: What a 0500 tutor actually changes
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE English First Language 0500 tutor changes the specificity of the feedback a student receives. That is the product. Lessons run one-to-one over live video to Abu Dhabi families, each session produces a marked piece of writing with the mark split written on it, and the trial lesson is free.

The reason specificity is the product rather than a feature of it is that English teachers in school are marking thirty scripts a week against a deadline. A class teacher can tell a student their expression needs work and be entirely correct. What they usually cannot do, with thirty scripts and a lesson to plan, is sit with one candidate for forty minutes and rebuild two paragraphs with them while they watch the sentence shapes change. That is the gap a tutor fills, and it is a narrow gap rather than a replacement for the class.

In practice the first session produces a baseline. The student writes one composition under time, on camera, to a task drawn from past Cambridge material. It is marked on both scales with the band written on the script and a short reason for each. The commonest outcome is a student sitting in the middle band for content and structure and the lower middle for style and accuracy, with the whole gap explained by three habits: every sentence the same length, dialogue punctuated inconsistently, and a plan that was never written so the piece has no shape.

Those three habits are fixable in weeks. What is not fixable in weeks is a candidate who does not read the task carefully, because that is a reading failure wearing a writing costume, and it will cost marks on the reading paper too. A tutor who starts with a marked baseline finds out which of those two situations you are in during the first fortnight rather than in March.

sections.heading: Two papers, eighty marks each, and what each one is really testing
paragraphs: 0500 is assessed by two written papers of two hours each, carrying eighty marks apiece and half the qualification each. The reading paper asks a candidate to work with unseen texts: short comprehension responses, an analysis of how the writer uses language to achieve effects, an extended response that requires reading the material closely and writing in a specified form, and a summary question that is marked for reading and for writing separately.

The writing paper has two halves. Directed writing asks the candidate to transform source material into a specified form for a specified audience, and it is marked for reading as well as writing, which is why a stylish piece that ignores half the material cannot reach the top band. The composition section asks for one piece, descriptive or narrative, marked out of forty: twenty-four marks for content and structure, sixteen for style and accuracy. That split is the single most useful number in the whole syllabus for a parent to know.

There is also a speaking and listening component, and in most Abu Dhabi schools it is separately endorsed, meaning it is reported alongside the grade rather than inside it. Some centres offer a coursework portfolio route in place of one examined component. Which arrangement your child is entered for changes what the final term should contain, and it is a question for the school's exams officer rather than for a tutor.

Confirm the component structure against the syllabus for your child's exam year on the Cambridge International site. Syllabuses are revised on a cycle, and a revision guide bought two years ago may describe a paper that no longer exists in that form.

sections.heading: The reading paper: three different jobs that look like one
paragraphs: Candidates treat the reading paper as a single activity called reading, and the mark scheme treats it as three distinct jobs. Retrieval questions want the text's own specifics, and an answer that paraphrases loosely loses marks that were sitting in plain sight. The writer's effects question wants the effect, not the label: naming a metaphor earns nothing on its own, while explaining what the comparison makes the reader picture or feel earns the mark. The summary wants ruthless selection, in the candidate's own words, inside a focus the question has defined.

Summary is the most teachable of the three and the most commonly neglected. The reliable method is mechanical: underline the focus in the question, go through the text marking only points that answer that focus, number them, then write in continuous prose without borrowing the text's phrasing. Students who do this score consistently. Students who read the passage once and then write a general account of it score in the middle of the range no matter how well they write.

Writer's effects improves fastest when a student is made to finish the sentence 'which makes the reader...' every single time. It feels mechanical for a fortnight and then becomes the way they read. The common failure is a candidate with a wide vocabulary who identifies five devices in a paragraph and explains none of them; the mark scheme pays for the explanation, and a quieter answer that unpacks two images properly beats a confident list of six.

All three jobs are measurable separately, which is why a marked script should report them separately. A student whose summary marks are strong and whose effects marks are weak does not have a reading problem in general. They have one question type to fix, and four weeks is usually enough.
bullets: Retrieval: use the text's own detail, not a loose paraphrase
Effects: finish 'which makes the reader...' on every point
Summary: underline the focus, number the points, then write
Never borrow the passage's phrasing in a summary
Report the three question types as three separate scores

sections.heading: Sixteen marks for style and accuracy, and how they leak
paragraphs: The composition is marked out of forty on two scales, and the smaller scale is where most Abu Dhabi candidates lose a grade. Twenty-four marks cover content and structure: whether the piece has a shape, whether the description builds, whether the narrative has a controlled arc rather than a list of events. Sixteen marks cover style and accuracy: range and precision of vocabulary, variety of sentence structure, control of punctuation, and consistency of tense and person.

Style and accuracy leaks quietly. A candidate writes a piece with genuine atmosphere, then undercuts it with twenty consecutive sentences of similar length, dialogue punctuated three different ways in two pages, and a drift from past tense into present halfway down the second side. None of that is a vocabulary problem, and none of it is fixed by reading more books. It is fixed by rewriting four paragraphs under supervision, four weeks running, until the habits change.

Content and structure leaks differently. The commonest cause is no plan. A planned descriptive piece moves deliberately through a small number of focal points; an unplanned one wanders and repeats. Five minutes of planning is worth more marks than five minutes of extra writing, and students resist this until they see two marked scripts side by side, one planned and one not, with the band difference written on them.

Directed writing has a third failure mode that belongs only to it: the candidate writes well and uses half the source material. Because that task is marked for reading as well as writing, ignoring material caps the mark regardless of quality. The fix is a two-minute source audit before writing, ticking each point as it is used.

sections.heading: The redraft cycle, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Redrafting is how writing improves, and it is also where tutoring in this subject can go badly wrong. The useful version is this: the student writes, the tutor marks against the criteria, the two of them rebuild one or two paragraphs together on screen with the student typing, and then the student rewrites the rest alone. The student's hands stay on the keyboard. What they learn is a repeatable move, not a better paragraph.

The version to refuse is a tutor who improves the piece for the candidate. It produces a better script and a student who has learned nothing, and for any component that is assessed and submitted it is an integrity breach that puts the qualification itself at risk. Everything submitted has to be the candidate's own work. Where a school runs the coursework portfolio route, that rule is not advisory.

Parents can audit this easily. Ask to see the marked script and ask the student to explain, without help, why one sentence was changed. A student who has been coached can answer. A student whose work was rewritten for them cannot, and the gap shows up within a sentence or two. This market contains sites that sell completed assessed work outright, and a family who knows the boundary is in a much better position to spot one.

The same boundary makes feedback more useful rather than less. A tutor who cannot hand over improved sentences has to explain the principle instead, and the explanation is the transferable part. Eight weeks of that produces a student who marks their own first draft before anybody else sees it, which is the actual goal.

sections.heading: 0500 or 0510: the decision a bilingual Abu Dhabi household should make on evidence
paragraphs: A large share of Abu Dhabi students speak English confidently and write it at a level that would be marked differently on the two syllabuses. First Language English assesses extended composition and close analysis of unseen text. Second Language English assesses structured reading and writing exercises plus a listening paper, and reports speaking separately. They are different qualifications with different demands, and the choice is sometimes made on how a child sounds in conversation.

The evidence that should decide it is a piece of extended writing, marked against the 0500 criteria, with the band written on it. A student who sits comfortably in the middle band for content and structure on an unseen descriptive task is a First Language candidate. A student whose ideas are strong but whose sentence control is still developing may be better served, and better rewarded, by the Second Language route, where the writing tasks are shorter and more defined.

Two practical considerations matter beyond the marks. Universities and employers read the two qualifications differently, and some sixth-form English courses prefer the First Language route as preparation. Against that, a grade ceiling reached on the wrong syllabus is a real cost, and a student grinding through two years of a paper they cannot access loses confidence in the subject as well as marks.

Whichever way it goes, the decision belongs to the school and the family together, and the useful contribution a tutor makes is the marked evidence rather than a view. Ask for it before the option block is signed off, not after the first mock.

sections.heading: What the marked-script record looks like over a term
paragraphs: The point of keeping every script is that English progress is invisible week to week and obvious across a term. A single composition is noisy: a student can write their best piece of the year on a task that happened to suit them. Six scripts on comparable tasks, marked on the same two scales, are not noisy. They show a trend, and the trend is the thing you are paying for.

The table below is the shape of that record for a Year 11 candidate who arrived in the middle of the range. It is organised by skill rather than by week, because that is how the marks are reported and how a parent can read it. Each row carries a starting point, what the marking targets, and what a term of it typically changes. These are patterns from marking, not a promise about any individual student, and no tutor can commit to a grade.

Two things in that record surprise families. The first is that style and accuracy usually moves before content and structure, because punctuation and sentence variety are habits while structure is a way of thinking. The second is that reading marks often move fastest of all, because summary technique is mechanical and a student who adopts the method picks the marks up almost immediately.

If after six scripts nothing has moved on any row, that is information worth acting on. It may mean the tutor is wrong for this student, or that the real problem is how much independent writing is happening between sessions, which no tutor can do for them. Either way a family holding six dated scripts can make that call themselves.
