sections.heading: The two writing tasks, and the register problem that costs most
paragraphs: The writing half of Paper 1 is where fluent English speakers in Abu Dhabi most often lose marks they did not expect to lose. The informal task and the formal task are marked for content and for language separately, and the two scores behave independently. A student can cover every prompt point and still score modestly on language, or write with impressive control and lose content marks for ignoring a third of the prompt.

Content marks go first. The informal task usually supplies prompt points, and every one has to be addressed. Candidates read three bullets, respond warmly to two of them, and lose a chunk of the available content marks while feeling the piece went well. A thirty-second audit — tick each bullet in the margin, tick it again after writing — recovers those marks permanently. It is the cheapest single habit in the whole syllabus.

Language marks are a register problem more often than a grammar problem. The formal task has a defined readership: a school magazine, a head teacher, a local newspaper. A candidate who writes it in the voice they would use to a friend has produced good English in the wrong place, and the mark reflects the mismatch. The drill is to decide the readership and the two or three structural features that follow from it before the first sentence rather than after the piece is finished.

Where grammar is genuinely the limiting factor, the errors are usually a small repeating set: articles, prepositions, tense consistency across a paragraph, subject-verb agreement in longer sentences. Four or five recurring slips account for most of the lost language marks in most scripts, and a running error list drilled weekly removes them in a term. A general grammar course does not, because it spends most of its time on things the student already does correctly.

Paragraphed with an opening and a close that match the form
Two or three structural features chosen before writing starts
Language range
Everyday precision rather than showy vocabulary
Range used accurately, not range attempted
Precise verbs replacing weak verb plus adverb pairs
Accuracy

Short enough to leave the long task its full time
The task that suffers when the informal one overruns

sections.heading: Where marks go missing for students who speak English all day
paragraphs: A significant share of 0510 candidates in Abu Dhabi speak English at school, with friends and sometimes at home, and arrive at the paper expecting fluency to carry them. It does not, and the gap between how confident they feel and what they score is the most common reason a family looks for a tutor. The cause is nearly always precision rather than ability.

Three patterns recur. The first is approximate answers: a response that shows the student understood the text but does not contain the specific words the mark scheme requires. The second is borrowed phrasing, particularly in the summary, where lifting the text's own words earns nothing however well selected the points are. The third is instruction drift, where a candidate answers the question they expected from the layout rather than the one printed, which costs marks across the whole reading half.

None of these show up in conversation, which is why schools and parents can both be surprised by a mock result. They show up immediately on a marked paper with per-exercise scores. A student who is strong in conversation and losing a third of their reading marks to approximation is a student whose next eight weeks should be spent on precision drills, not on more reading or more speaking practice.

The reassuring part is that precision responds quickly. Habits like underlining the instruction, counting the words allowed, and checking whether a question wants a phrase or a sentence can be installed in a few weeks. Marked scripts from week two and week eight usually show the reading half moving before the writing half, because precision is faster to fix than range.
bullets: Approximate answers: right idea, wrong words, no mark
Borrowed phrasing in the summary earns nothing
Instruction drift: answering the expected question, not the printed one
Word limits ignored, which caps otherwise correct answers
Precision usually improves faster than range of language

sections.heading: 0510, 0511 and 0500: three codes and one decision
paragraphs: Three Cambridge English codes come up in Abu Dhabi option conversations and families are rarely told how they differ. 0510 is English as a Second Language with speaking reported separately from the grade. 0511 is the same syllabus content with the speaking component counted inside the grade. 0500 is English as a First Language, assessed through extended composition and close analysis of unseen text rather than structured exercises.

The decision between the Second Language and First Language routes should rest on a marked piece of written work, not on how a child sounds. A student who writes with control and range on an unseen descriptive task is a First Language candidate. A student whose ideas are strong but whose sentence control is still settling will usually score better, and learn more, on the structured route where tasks are shorter and more defined.

The choice between 0510 and 0511 is narrower and belongs to the school, since it determines how speaking is reported. For a confident speaker whose writing lags, having speaking counted can help the overall grade. For a student with the reverse profile it can hurt. Either way the family should know which code is being entered, because it changes what the final term should contain.

What should not drive the decision is a belief that one code is viewed as lesser. Universities and employers read these qualifications as evidence of English attainment, and most institutions in the UAE and abroad also ask for a separate language test regardless of which code appears on the certificate. The real cost of the wrong route is two years on a paper a student cannot access, or a capable writer held below their level.

sections.heading: What one 0510 session actually fixes
paragraphs: It is worth being concrete about what an hour buys, because tutoring is sold in hours and almost never described in them. A 0510 session has a single target, taken from the last marked paper. The target is an exercise type, not a skill area. 'Note-making' is a target. 'Reading' is not.

A typical note-making session runs like this. Five minutes reading the last marked attempt and naming what went wrong — in most cases points placed under the wrong heading, or full sentences written where notes were wanted. Fifteen minutes on a worked example with the tutor thinking out loud while the student watches the heading-first method. Twenty minutes of the student doing the same task under time while the tutor stays quiet. Fifteen minutes marking it together against the mark scheme, with the student finding their own errors first. Five minutes setting the task they will do alone before next week.

The part that matters most is the twenty quiet minutes. A session where a tutor talks for fifty minutes produces a student who understood the lesson and cannot perform the exercise. The marks come from performance under time, so time under performance has to be part of the hour. Families who sit in on a trial lesson should be looking for that silence as much as for the explanation.

At the end of the session the exercise score goes on its own line in the record. Over a term those lines form a picture: note-making climbing, summary flat, formal writing climbing slowly, listening steady. That picture is what tells you whether to keep going, change the target, or change the tutor.

sections.heading: ADEK, the Arabic parallel, and what an English grade is accepted for
paragraphs: Universities in the UAE and abroad read a Cambridge English qualification as evidence of attainment, and most of them still ask for a separate language test on top. That is the first thing worth saying to a family who assume the 0510 grade settles the admissions question. It contributes; it rarely concludes. The published Ministry of Education guidance for the American track, for example, requires English proficiency evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT.

For the British track the published equivalency rule is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. An English qualification is in practice one of the five for nearly every candidate, which makes this grade load-bearing however it is coded. Verify the current rules through the Ministry rather than through a tutoring site, including this one.

In the emirate itself, private schools are supervised by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which handles licensing and accreditation for Abu Dhabi. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education covers Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Abu Dhabi families reading Dubai inspection guidance are reading about a different regulator.

Running alongside the Cambridge options are the mandatory UAE subjects. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations, and the content of those subjects is prescribed. So a 0510 candidate is frequently building literacy in two languages at once on the same timetable. IB Gram holds no accreditation or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education or Cambridge International, takes no part in the equivalency process, and nobody should suggest tutoring is required for it.

process.title: Send a past paper attempt if you have one
process.description: A photograph of a marked Paper 1, or even an unmarked attempt, is the most useful thing a family can send. Per-exercise scores tell a specialist in two minutes what a phone call takes half an hour to approximate, and the first session can then start on the right exercise.

process.title: Trial lesson at no charge, one per student
process.description: A full session free, with no card details taken and no obligation afterwards. Use it as a working lesson rather than a conversation: ask for one exercise to be taught and one timed attempt to be marked, so a script with per-exercise marks exists before anything is paid for.

process.title: Name the target exercise
process.description: The plan says which exercise type is being attacked and for how many weeks. 'Improve reading' is not a target. 'Note-making, three weeks, timed attempt in week three' is. Everything outside the target is deliberately left for later.

process.title: Listening starts in week one
process.description: A listening set every week from the beginning, not from March. Twenty minutes is enough. This single scheduling decision is the difference between a listening mark that climbs steadily and one that is still where it was in September.

process.title: Per-exercise marks recorded on their own line
process.description: Scores are logged exercise by exercise so movement is attributable. When a total rises you can say which exercise lifted it, and when it stalls you can say which one is stuck. A single overall grade cannot support either conclusion.

process.title: Review the lines after six papers
process.description: Six marked attempts make a readable pattern. If every line is flat, the conversation is about the match or about how much independent work is happening between sessions, rather than about booking more hours at the same rate.

whyPoints.title: Exercise-level diagnosis
whyPoints.description: The 0510 paper is a fixed sequence of exercises, so marks can be attributed to a specific one rather than to English in general. That is the difference between a plan and a wish, and most families have never been shown their child's scores broken down this way.

whyPoints.title: Listening is not left until April
whyPoints.description: A real share of the grade sits in the listening component and it is the first thing most preparation drops. Twenty minutes a week from the start, with the mark scheme shown beside the student's own wording, is what stops that mark being stuck.

whyPoints.title: Register taught before vocabulary
whyPoints.description: Fluent speakers lose formal-task marks because the voice is wrong, not because the words are. Deciding the readership before writing the first sentence recovers more marks in this syllabus than any amount of vocabulary building.

whyPoints.title: Twenty quiet minutes every session
whyPoints.description: Marks come from performance under time, so a session includes the student working alone while the tutor stays silent. An hour of explanation produces a student who understood the lesson and still cannot do the exercise.

whyPoints.title: Specialists chosen for mark-scheme knowledge
whyPoints.description: The useful tutor here can explain why an answer that reads correctly earned nothing. Online delivery means an Abu Dhabi family picks from a roster of people who know these mark schemes rather than from whoever is a short drive away.

whyPoints.title: Clear about the route decision
whyPoints.description: If a marked piece of writing suggests the First Language syllabus suits a student better, you will be told, and the reverse too. Two years spent on a paper a candidate cannot access is a worse outcome than a difficult option conversation in Year 9.

faqs.question: What is in the Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510 exam?
faqs.answer: Two examined papers plus a separate speaking component. The reading and writing paper runs two hours and carries the larger share of the grade; it moves through short reading responses, a scanning or matching task, note-making, a summary, a shorter informal piece of writing and a longer formal one. The listening paper is shorter and carries the remainder. Speaking is assessed separately and in most UAE centres is reported alongside the grade rather than inside it. Confirm the exact structure for your child's exam year on the Cambridge International website.

faqs.question: My child speaks English fluently but keeps scoring in the middle of the range. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always precision rather than ability. Fluency does not produce the exact words a mark scheme requires, and three patterns recur: approximate answers that show understanding without containing the required detail, summaries that borrow the text's own phrasing and so earn nothing, and answers to the question the candidate expected rather than the one printed. None of this is visible in conversation, which is why a mock result can surprise everybody. All three respond to a few weeks of precision drills on marked papers.

faqs.question: How important is the listening paper and when should we start practising it?
faqs.answer: It carries a real share of the grade and it should start in the first month, not in the spring. Listening is a perishable skill: a student who has not worked with unfamiliar accented English under time since last year will lose marks for reasons unconnected to their English. Twenty minutes a week is enough. The highest-value drills are capturing exact details without trying to transcribe everything, recognising when a speaker self-corrects, and comparing their own wording with the mark scheme's accepted answer.

faqs.question: Our school mentioned 0511 rather than 0510 — does the code change what my child sits?
faqs.answer: The syllabus content and the written papers are the same. The difference is how the speaking component is treated: in 0510 speaking is reported separately from the grade, and in 0511 it is counted inside it. The school decides which code it enters, so ask the exams officer directly. For a confident speaker whose writing lags, having speaking counted can lift the overall grade; for a student with the opposite profile it can pull it down. Either way it changes what the final term of preparation should prioritise.

faqs.question: Can the note-making and summary exercises really be trained, or is it general reading ability?
faqs.answer: They are the two most trainable exercises in the paper. Note-making is a method: read the headings first, work through the text placing each point under the right heading, and write notes rather than sentences. Summary is also a method: underline the focus in the question, mark only the points that answer it, number them, then write in your own words without borrowing the text's phrasing. Students who adopt those sequences usually move within two or three timed attempts, regardless of how much reading they do outside lessons.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable for a listening and speaking subject?
faqs.answer: For listening it is better than the alternative, because the tutor controls the audio, can replay a four-second window and can put the mark scheme on screen next to the student's own answer. Writing tasks are documents, so register can be rewritten in place with the student typing. There are no home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India, so every Abu Dhabi session happens over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run.

faqs.question: What do tutors charge for IGCSE English support in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Rates published by UAE providers in October 2026 sit in bands rather than at a single figure. Specialist IGCSE and A-Level tutors are advertised from around AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, qualified subject tutors working online from roughly AED 150 to 300, and budget or university-student online tutoring from about AED 45 to 150. An in-home visit typically costs more once travel is priced in, commonly quoted between AED 180 and 500. Those are other providers' own figures; ask about our model during the trial.

faqs.question: How many prompt points does the informal writing task need me to cover?
faqs.answer: All of them. The task supplies prompt points and the content marks are distributed across them, so a warm, well-written response that addresses two of three loses a meaningful share of the available content score while feeling successful. The fix takes thirty seconds: tick each prompt point in the margin before writing, then tick each one again after finishing. It is the cheapest recoverable mark in the whole syllabus and the one most commonly left on the table by strong candidates.

faqs.question: My child's formal writing gets marked down even though the English is good. What is wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually register. The formal task has a stated readership — a school magazine, a head teacher, a local newspaper — and a piece written in the voice a student would use with a friend is good English in the wrong place. The mark reflects the mismatch rather than the quality. The drill is to decide the readership first, then choose two or three structural features that follow from it, before writing a sentence. Students who do that consistently see the language marks move without their grammar changing at all.

faqs.question: Which grammar should we actually work on?
faqs.answer: Only the errors that appear in your child's own scripts, which is usually a small repeating set: articles, prepositions, tense consistency across a paragraph, and subject-verb agreement in longer sentences. Four or five recurring slips account for most lost language marks in most papers. A running error list drilled weekly clears them within a term. A general grammar course spends most of its time on structures the student already handles correctly, which is why it produces so little movement for the hours involved.

faqs.question: Who is legally allowed to give private English lessons in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Private tuition in the UAE operates under a permit regime. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years and is open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service for private tutor licensing, via its app, website or e-services. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Will a 0510 grade be enough for university admission in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It contributes and it rarely concludes. For the British equivalency track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. The American track separately requires English proficiency evidenced by IELTS 5, TOEFL internet-based 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing. Check the current requirements with the Ministry and with each university.

faqs.question: My child is also sitting Arabic as a first language. How do we fit both in?
faqs.answer: By accepting the workload rather than planning around it. Private schools in the UAE must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the international curriculum they are licensed to teach, and the content of those subjects is prescribed, so the material has to come from the school. A student building literacy in two languages in the same year needs a revision timetable that names both. Plans that quietly assume Arabic will look after itself are the ones students abandon in February.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start if the exams are in June?
faqs.answer: Eight to twelve weeks is a workable run-in; four weeks is triage. The reason is sequencing: each exercise type needs a couple of weeks and a timed attempt, and the paper has six of them, so a short runway forces choices. With a month left the sensible plan is listening every week plus the two exercises with the largest recoverable losses, usually the prompt-point audit on the informal task and summary method. Starting late still helps. Starting in October costs a fraction of the effort for the same movement.

faqs.question: Can we change tutor if it is not working?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the per-exercise record is what makes that call possible. Six marked papers with every exercise scored on its own line either show lines moving or they do not. If nothing has moved, the honest options are a different specialist or an honest conversation about how much independent work is happening between sessions, which no tutor can do on a student's behalf. When the tutor changes, the record and the marked scripts go with the student so the work does not restart from week one.

faqs.question: What happens if no 0510 specialist is free at the time we need?
faqs.answer: You will be told rather than matched quietly with whoever is available. English as a Second Language has a reasonable roster, but the evening slots either side of a Cambridge series fill up, and the tutors who know these mark schemes in detail are a smaller group than the tutors who can teach English. The options are a waiting slot, a different session time, or a specialist whose strength is the reading half when the diagnosis already points there. Guessing at a match helps nobody.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-english-second.closingHeading: Start from a marked paper, not a description
abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-english-second.closingBody: If you can send one completed Paper 1 attempt, marked or unmarked, a specialist can usually name the exercise costing the most marks before the first lesson begins. That is a better starting point than any description of how your child finds English. Take the free trial, ask for one exercise to be taught and one timed attempt to be marked, and keep the script with its per-exercise scores. Sessions run one-to-one over live video to Abu Dhabi in Gulf Standard Time, listening included from the first week, and the record of which lines are moving belongs to you.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-environmental-.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management to Abu Dhabi students in Years 10 and 11. The teaching is applied: named causes separated from named strategies, data and map questions worked under timing, and local case material used where it is genuinely stronger than the textbook's.

intro.heading: What 0680 support costs here, and what it buys that reading cannot
paragraphs: The money question first, because that is the search. Published UAE provider rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tuition between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, with a budget tier beneath and a named-specialist tier above. A published Dubai tutoring cost table puts weekly one-hour tuition at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month in the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist support in an exam year. Those are other providers' numbers and a market reference, not a price list from here.

What makes 0680 slightly cheaper to support than a laboratory science is that there is nothing to equip and nothing to supervise. The subject has no assessed practical component. What makes it more expensive to support badly is that it looks easy from outside: the content is readable, the themes are familiar, and a student can finish the textbook and still write answers that score in the middle. The gap between understanding the material and answering the question is wider in this subject than in almost any other IGCSE.

The specific failure is worth naming before anything else, because it determines whether tutoring is worth buying. Cambridge gives candidates a problem and asks for management. Students answer by explaining the problem. Asked how a country could reduce water stress, they describe water stress. The marks are in named strategies, their costs, their limitations and who pays for them, and a student who has never been taught to separate cause from strategy will keep producing confident, well-written, mid-band answers no matter how much reading they do.

Abu Dhabi students have a real advantage here that most 0680 candidates worldwide do not. Several of the nine themes are visible from a car window in this emirate. Water management, energy choices, fisheries pressure, desert agriculture and habitat protection are not abstractions here; they are local policy with documented numbers attached. A student who can write about a named desalination plant, a named protected wetland or a named solar project answers with the specificity the mark scheme rewards, and that specificity is free.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video with screens shared. IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is an India-only service. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and 0680 is a smaller option subject than the mainstream sciences, so in many schools it runs as a single class. When a student slips in a one-class subject there is no second set to move into, which is the usual reason a family looks outside.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-environmental-.programmesIntro: 0680 sits slightly apart from the main Cambridge science pathway, and understanding where it does and does not lead saves families from two expensive assumptions. It is a cross-curricular subject, and its onward routes are not the ones people expect.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management
programmes.description: Nine themes drawing on geography, biology and economics: rocks and minerals, energy, agriculture, water, oceans and fisheries, natural hazards, the atmosphere, human population, and natural ecosystems. Assessed by two written papers of equal weight, one structured across the themes and one built on supplied source and data material. There is no coursework and no assessed practical.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi 0680 is usually a Year 10 option, often chosen by students who want a science-adjacent subject without a laboratory load, and sometimes timetabled as an alternative to a third separate science. Where a school runs it as one class across both years, the teacher is frequently a geographer or a biologist rather than a specialist in the whole syllabus, which shows up as uneven coverage between the themes.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography
programmes.description: The closest companion subject, overlapping 0680 on water, population, hazards and resource management. Geography brings the skills that transfer most usefully: reading a graph properly, interpreting a map, handling a data table and writing a case study with named places and real figures rather than a general description.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi students taking both find roughly a third of their revision doing double duty, provided they keep the two answer styles apart. Geography asks for physical process; Environmental Management asks for management decisions and their costs. Blending the two is a common and avoidable way to lose marks in both.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology
programmes.description: Supplies the ecological grounding behind the natural-ecosystems and oceans themes: food webs, energy transfer, nutrient cycling, population dynamics and the effects of pollution on living systems. Students carrying Biology write more credible 0680 ecosystem answers because they can explain a mechanism rather than assert an outcome.
programmes.countryNote: Many Abu Dhabi schools timetable 0680 so that it can be taken alongside Biology rather than instead of it, and that combination is the strongest preparation for environmental study after school. It also matters for sixth-form entry, since 0680 is not always accepted as a science prerequisite on its own.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS Level Environmental Management
programmes.description: The direct continuation at AS Level, extending the resource, population and ecosystem material and adding considerably more data analysis and policy evaluation. Students who reached a strong 0680 grade by learning case studies tend to need help with the step up in quantitative work rather than with the content.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school offers 8291, so students planning that route should check availability in Year 10 rather than Year 11. Where it is unavailable locally, the common alternatives are IB Diploma Environmental Systems and Societies in an IB school or a geography and biology combination at A Level.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-environmental-.subjectsIntro: 0680 is rarely booked alone. The subjects below are the usual companions in an Abu Dhabi option block, and most of them share either the data-handling skill or the case-study habit.

subjects.name: Environmental Management (0680)
subjects.description: The subject of this page. Sessions separate named causes from named management strategies, build local case material that can be written with real figures, and drill the data, map and graph questions that carry a large share of the available marks.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: The strongest overlap. Shares water, population, hazards and resource themes, and contributes the skills of reading a proportional symbol map, interpreting a climate graph and writing a case study with named places and figures.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Supplies the mechanisms behind 0680's ecosystem and pollution content: energy transfer through food webs, nutrient cycling, eutrophication and the effect of a contaminant on a population rather than on a landscape.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Relevant to the atmosphere and energy themes, where combustion products, acid deposition and the chemistry of fuels appear. Students with Chemistry can explain why a pollutant behaves as it does instead of naming it and moving on.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: A frequent alternative to separate sciences in Abu Dhabi schools, and often timetabled alongside 0680. The ecology and chemistry content inside it covers most of what the environmental themes assume as background knowledge.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: More useful here than families expect. 0680 management answers need costs, trade-offs and who bears them, and a student who has met opportunity cost and externalities formally writes far stronger evaluation than one who has not.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Shares the sustainability topics and asks for evidence-based argument on them. A student doing both can use the same reading twice, as long as nothing written is reused, and the perspective work sharpens 0680 evaluation.

subjects.name: Travel and Tourism (0471)
subjects.description: Overlaps on the environmental impact of tourism, carrying capacity and the management of visitor pressure at sensitive sites, which is directly examinable in both subjects and has obvious local examples.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Behind the quantitative questions that catch students out: percentage change, rates, reading values off a graph accurately and comparing proportions. These lose 0680 marks for reasons unconnected to environmental knowledge.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-environmental-.regionsIntro: This emirate gives 0680 students usable local material, and it also shapes what time a session can start. The notes below cover both.

regions.name: Masdar City and Khalifa City
regions.note: Sustainable urban design and large-scale energy projects are local rather than theoretical here, which gives students a specific case for the energy theme instead of a general paragraph about renewables.

regions.name: Al Zeina, Al Raha Beach and the Eastern Mangroves
regions.note: Coastal communities beside mangrove systems, so habitat protection and coastal management can be written from observation. Sessions here are usually single weekly hours with case-study reading set in between.

regions.name: Al Wathba and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Inland communities near protected wetland habitat and the edge of the desert agriculture belt. Students here can build credible answers on groundwater use and reclamation rather than borrowing a textbook example from elsewhere.

regions.name: Yas Island and Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Newer catchments with many mid-course arrivals, so more Year 11 students who met 0680 only one year ago. First sessions go on coverage gaps between themes rather than on exam technique.

regions.name: Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Industrial and residential mix with the longest drives to island schools, so the first realistic weekday slot is usually after 7pm Gulf Standard Time. Online delivery is what makes that window usable.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif

sections.heading: The nine themes, and the two that carry the hardest questions
paragraphs: Cambridge builds 0680 from nine themes that draw on geography, biology and economics in roughly equal measure. That cross-curricular design is the subject's strength and the source of its uneven teaching: a school with one 0680 class usually staffs it from whichever department has capacity, and the themes nearest that teacher's specialism get covered properly while the others get covered quickly. The first job in any tutoring plan is therefore mapping what has actually been taught rather than assuming the scheme of work was followed.

Two themes reliably produce the hardest questions. Water and its management is the first, because it combines a physical process, a set of competing users, a list of engineering and policy responses and a cost argument, and a good answer has to hold all four. Oceans and fisheries is the second, for a similar reason: the biology of a fish stock, the economics of a fleet and the politics of a shared sea all appear in one question, and students who have learned only the biology cannot reach the management marks.

The themes that look hardest usually are not. Rocks and minerals and their exploitation reads like geology and is in fact largely about extraction methods, their impacts and restoration, which is a learnable list. Natural hazards is similarly structured: cause, hazard, risk, prediction, preparation, response. Students who are taught that structure answer well because the structure is the answer. The atmosphere and human activities is the theme most often thinly covered, and it is worth checking specifically, since acid deposition, ozone depletion and the enhanced greenhouse effect are each distinct and students conflate them routinely.

The table below sets out the nine themes with a local case worth knowing for each and the characteristic error. Local cases are offered because specificity scores: an answer naming a real plant, a real reserve or a real fishery with real figures is worth more than one describing the general phenomenon, and an Abu Dhabi student has several within reach.

sections.heading: Two papers, and the one skill they both reward
paragraphs: 0680 is assessed by two written papers of equal weight, with no coursework and no assessed practical. One works across the nine themes in structured questions; the other is built on supplied source and data material and asks the candidate to apply management thinking to a described situation. Durations and mark totals are set in the syllabus for each exam series, so work from the version that matches your child's series rather than from an older copy circulating in a revision folder.

Both papers reward the same underlying skill, which is why the subject improves faster than its content volume suggests. The skill is reading supplied information accurately and then saying what should be done about it. Reading accurately is the half students assume they can already do: values taken off a graph without checking the axis units, a trend described as a rise when the data shows a slowing rise, a table compared in absolute terms when the question asked about proportion. Each of those costs a mark that no amount of theme knowledge recovers.

Saying what should be done is the half that needs teaching. The structure that works is consistent across every theme. Name the strategy. Say how it works in one sentence. Give its cost or its limitation. Say who pays and who benefits. Four moves, applied whether the question is about fisheries quotas or about solar installation, and a student who has them automated writes to the top of the band without having to improvise an approach under time pressure.

The practical consequence for a weekly plan is that one timed data question a week matters more than an extra hour of reading. Data questions are quick to set, quick to mark and diagnostic: the marked script shows immediately whether the loss was in reading the source, in naming a strategy, or in evaluating it. That is three different fixes, and guessing between them wastes weeks.

sections.heading: Where 0680 answers lose marks: cause written in place of management
paragraphs: The dominant failure in this subject is a single confusion repeated across every theme. The question asks how something could be managed and the student explains why it is a problem. This is not laziness; it is what the textbook taught, because the textbook has to explain the problem before it can discuss the response, and students absorb the first half more thoroughly than the second. The result is an articulate answer that sits in the middle of the band and leaves the candidate baffled.

The fix is mechanical and teachable within a few weeks. For every theme, the student builds two separate lists: named causes and named management strategies. They never appear on the same page. When a question arrives, the student decides which list it is asking from before writing a word. That sounds trivially simple and it removes most of the loss, because the error is one of retrieval rather than of understanding.

A second cluster of marks goes to unevaluated strategies. A student names three responses to a problem and stops, as though naming were the task. The mark scheme wants the cost, the limitation and the distribution: who pays, who benefits, what fails. Desalination manages water scarcity and is energy intensive and expensive. A fishing quota protects a stock and is hard to enforce across a shared sea and costs fishing crews their income this season. Those second halves are where the higher-band marks live.

The third cluster is specificity. A named plant, reserve, fishery or project with a real figure attached scores above a general description of the same phenomenon, and Abu Dhabi students can be specific more cheaply than most candidates because the examples are local. sections.heading: What 0680 tuition costs set against the rest of the school bill
paragraphs: Tutoring is usually judged in isolation, which makes it look either cheap or expensive depending on the family's reference point. Put beside the other education costs a UAE household carries, the figure becomes easier to decide about. The table below sets published tutoring bands alongside the fee context, with the month each figure was read. These are market and published figures, not quotations from here, and providers revise their pages without notice.

One fee point is worth stating carefully because it is widely mentioned and often misattributed. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. That is a Dubai measure announced by the Dubai regulator. Abu Dhabi fee changes are handled through ADEK, and no comparable emirate-wide freeze for 2026-27 is cited on this page, because none has been read from an ADEK source. If your planning depends on it, ask the school or check ADEK directly.

The exam entry line matters for private candidates and for families adding a subject their school does not offer. Entry fees are set and charged by the Cambridge centre administering the exam, not by a tutor, and they vary between centres. A tutor can explain how private entry works and when the deadline falls; the figure and the booking come from the centre. Cambridge's own entry deadlines sit months before the papers, which is the single most common scheduling surprise in private-candidate plans.

Against that backdrop, the practical question is not whether tutoring is expensive but what shape of it is worth buying. For 0680 the honest answer in most cases is one weekly hour with a marked data question between sessions, started early, rather than a dense block in the final weeks. The block costs more and achieves less, because the subject's core fix is a habit that needs several weeks of repetition to stick.

sections.heading: What actually changes an Abu Dhabi quote for this subject
paragraphs: Two families asking for the same subject get different numbers for reasons that are predictable and worth knowing, because the right response is usually to change the brief rather than to argue about the rate. The largest factor is how many themes have genuinely been taught. A student who has covered all nine unevenly needs a mapping session and then targeted work; a student who has covered five needs teaching, which is more sessions at the same hourly figure. The hourly rate is rarely where the money goes.

The second factor is whether marking is inside the hour. In 0680 the marked data question is the diagnostic instrument, so an arrangement without marking removes the mechanism that tells anybody whether the plan is working. An hour of teaching plus a marked timed question is a different product from an hour of teaching, and comparing the two on price alone produces the wrong decision. Ask directly, and get the answer in writing.

The third is timing within the year. Demand in Abu Dhabi spikes after the January and February mocks, which is when specialist availability is tightest for a minority subject like this one. Booking in October costs the same per hour and gives a genuine choice of tutor. The fourth is format: a shared slot for two students sitting the same syllabus in the same series splits the cost sensibly, while a group class lowers the rate and lowers the attention, which matters more in a subject where individual answer habits are the problem.

What IB Gram does rather than publishing a rate card is a free trial lesson, one session, followed by a quoted figure once the theme coverage and the failure mode are known. In a subject where the gap between a technique fix and a content rebuild is six weeks of fees, quoting before the diagnosis would mislead one side or the other.
bullets: Theme coverage, not the hourly rate, drives the total

sections.heading: Where 0680 leads, and what it counts for
paragraphs: Two assumptions cost families more than any rate difference, and both concern what the subject is accepted as. The first is that 0680 counts as a science for sixth-form entry. Sometimes it does and often it does not, and the decision belongs to the receiving school rather than to Cambridge. A school asking for two sciences at IGCSE before admitting a student to AS Biology may or may not count Environmental Management among them. That is a question to ask in Year 10, in writing, from the school the student intends to stay at.

The second is that 0680 is a soft option. Its content is readable and its marking is not generous: the management and evaluation demand is closer to a humanities subject's than to a recall-based science's, and students who chose it expecting an easy grade are the ones who find themselves in the middle band with no obvious explanation. A tutor's first useful act is often telling a family that honestly rather than selling extra hours against the wrong diagnosis.

For Ministry of Education equivalency, 0680 counts as an accredited subject like any other. The British-track requirement is a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, which is the detail that catches option-block planning out. No IB equivalency figure appears on this page, because none has been confirmed from the Ministry's own pages. Verify anything you rely on at moe.gov.ae.

Onward routes are real but narrower than for the mainstream sciences. Cambridge offers AS Level Environmental Management, which not every Abu Dhabi school teaches; IB schools offer Environmental Systems and Societies; and a geography plus biology combination at A Level reaches most environmental degree courses. None of these requires tutoring, and no provider should imply that a regulatory or admissions process depends on buying hours.

sections.heading: What a session covers, and how to start
paragraphs: A working 0680 session has a predictable shape. Ten minutes on last week's marked data question, with the lost marks named specifically rather than described. Twenty-five minutes on one theme, taught through a named case with figures attached so the student leaves with usable material rather than a summary. Fifteen minutes with the student answering a question on screen while the tutor watches and interrupts at the point of error. Ten minutes setting the timed question for the week and adding anything new to the strategies list.

The honesty boundary is simple on this subject because there is nothing to submit. All marks come from invigilated papers, so no tutor could improperly author anything for Cambridge even in principle. School-set assignments and mocks still feed predicted grades, and there the rule is the usual one: a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on what the student has written, and does not supply sentences or figures for a submission. Syllabus documents and past papers are referenced and obtained through the school from cambridgeinternational.org rather than circulated as downloads.

Starting is short. Send the school's 0680 scheme of work or a list of themes covered so far, a marked mock or class test, and the series the student is entered for. A free trial lesson follows, one session and no charge, spent on a real data question rather than on an interview. What comes back is a written note saying which themes are missing, whether the problem is reading data or naming management, and roughly how many weeks it should take.

Two caveats stated plainly. Nobody can promise a grade in a subject assessed by two papers sat in a hall, and no claim of approval or accreditation by Cambridge, ADEK or any other authority is made anywhere on this page, because none is held. And 0680 is a minority subject with a small specialist pool, so if nothing is free in the slot you need you will be told that rather than offered a general science tutor who has never read the syllabus.

process.title: Map what has actually been taught
process.description: The first useful document is a list of which of the nine themes the class has covered, because 0680 is often taught by one teacher whose specialism shapes the coverage. A plan built on the published scheme of work rather than on reality wastes the first three sessions.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a real data question
process.description: One session, no charge, spent working a supplied-source question with the student on a shared screen. That locates the fault precisely: reading the data, naming a strategy, or evaluating it. Three different problems, three different plans, and guessing between them costs weeks.

process.title: A written diagnosis and a week count
process.description: After the trial you get a short note naming the missing themes and the failure mode, in plain language. The rate follows from that, because filling five themes of content is a different job from fixing one answer habit, and quoting before the diagnosis would mislead somebody.

process.title: Weekly slot with a marked question between
process.description: A fixed time each week in Gulf Standard Time, agreed around the school run. Each session ends with a timed data or source question to be written and returned for marking, which is the instrument that shows whether the plan is working rather than whether it feels like it is.

process.title: Build the two lists, theme by theme
process.description: Named causes on one page, named management strategies with costs and limitations on another, built up across the term and audited by the tutor. Most of the recoverable marks in this subject come from a student knowing which list the question is asking from.

process.title: Review at six weeks on the evidence
process.description: Six weeks of marked questions is enough to judge. Frequency rises, holds or the arrangement ends, and the tutor says which rather than leaving the parent to decide from feel. A plan that is not moving marks should stop rather than continue out of habit.

whyPoints.title: The core fix is named, not implied
whyPoints.description: Most 0680 marks are lost to one confusion: describing the problem when the question asked for management. Sessions treat that as the primary target from the first week, with causes and strategies kept as separate lists, rather than working through the textbook again more slowly.

whyPoints.title: Local cases instead of borrowed ones
whyPoints.description: An answer naming a real plant, reserve or fishery with a figure attached outscores a general description of the same phenomenon. Abu Dhabi students have several within reach, and using them costs nothing extra while making the specificity the mark scheme rewards available.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source and date
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here name the provider or published table they came from and the month they were read, and the Dubai fee announcement is labelled as Dubai rather than presented as a UAE-wide fact. A sourced number can be checked; an unsourced one cannot.

whyPoints.title: Online, and said without hedging
whyPoints.description: UAE lessons run one-to-one over live video with screens shared, which suits a subject built on maps, graphs and data extracts. IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is offered only in India.

whyPoints.title: Marked work as the measuring instrument
whyPoints.description: A timed data question written, marked against the criteria and rewritten tells a parent more than any progress report. The marked scripts accumulate into a record you can read yourself, which is why marking is inside the quoted hour rather than sold alongside it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about ceilings and coverage
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no claimed regulator or board approval, and no pretence that 0680 is a soft option when a student chose it expecting one. If no specialist is free in the slot you need, you are told so rather than handed a substitute.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE Environmental Management 0680 tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE provider rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tuition at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with a budget tier below and named-specialist rates above. Monthly, a published Dubai cost table gives AED 240 to 600 for a weekly budget-tier hour, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are other providers' figures offered as market context, not a price list from here. What moves the total most is how many of the nine themes still need teaching, not the hourly figure itself.

faqs.question: Is Environmental Management 0680 a science or a geography subject?
faqs.answer: Both, which is the point and also the complication. The nine themes draw on geography, biology and economics, so the content feels like physical geography while the assessment rewards management decisions and their costs, closer to a humanities subject. Practically, a student needs ecological mechanisms from biology, data and map skills from geography, and trade-off thinking from economics. Schools usually staff it from whichever department has capacity, which is why theme coverage is often uneven and why mapping what has actually been taught is the first thing a tutor should do.

faqs.question: Does 0680 count as a science for sixth-form entry?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision belongs to the receiving school rather than to Cambridge. A school asking for two sciences at IGCSE before admitting a student to AS Biology may or may not count Environmental Management among them, and practice differs between Abu Dhabi schools. Ask the school your child intends to stay at, in writing, during Year 10 rather than Year 11. Where it will not be counted, the usual fix is taking 0680 alongside Biology rather than instead of it, which is also the stronger preparation for environmental study after school.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter describe the problem and lose the marks?
faqs.answer: Because that is what the textbook models. A textbook explains a problem before discussing responses, and students absorb the first half more thoroughly. The question then asks how something could be managed and they explain why it is a problem, producing a well-written mid-band answer. The fix takes a few weeks and is mechanical: for every theme, keep named causes and named management strategies on separate pages, and decide which list a question is asking from before writing. The error is one of retrieval rather than understanding, which is why it responds quickly.

faqs.question: Are there practical experiments in IGCSE Environmental Management?
faqs.answer: There is no assessed practical component and no coursework. The whole grade comes from written papers, so nothing has to be equipped, supervised or submitted. That has two consequences worth knowing. It makes the subject accessible to private candidates and to students whose school does not offer a laboratory science, and it means revision has to be writing rather than activity. Data, map and graph questions are the examinable skill that most resembles practical work, and they need to be practised under timing with the answers marked, not read through.

faqs.question: Can my son take 0680 alongside Biology and Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the combination that works best if the timetable allows it. Biology supplies the ecological mechanisms behind the ecosystem and oceans themes, Chemistry supports the atmosphere and energy content, and 0680 adds the management and evaluation layer neither of them teaches. The overlap saves revision time rather than duplicating it. The one caution is answer style: a Biology answer explains a mechanism, while a 0680 answer names a strategy and costs it, and students carrying both occasionally write the wrong kind of answer in the wrong paper.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi case studies are worth learning for 0680?
faqs.answer: The ones with documented numbers attached. Desalination capacity and treated wastewater reuse serve the water theme. Large-scale solar projects and the Barakah nuclear plant in Al Dhafra serve energy. Date farming and the Liwa agriculture belt serve agriculture and salinisation. Gulf fisheries pressure on grouper stocks and the marine protected areas serve oceans and fisheries. Mangrove systems and protected wetland habitat serve natural ecosystems. A named case with a real figure outscores a general description, and these are local enough for a student to check rather than memorise blindly.

faqs.question: How many 0680 sessions does a Year 11 student need before the June series?
faqs.answer: It depends on theme coverage rather than on the calendar. A student who has been taught all nine themes and is losing marks on answer habits usually needs six to eight weekly sessions, because the fix is a habit that has to be repeated rather than a body of content. A student with three or four themes effectively untaught needs those taught first, which is closer to twelve to sixteen sessions. The distinction is visible from a marked mock script in one session, which is why the diagnosis should come before any quote or package.

faqs.question: Is 0680 counted among the five IGCSEs for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: It counts as an accredited subject like any other. The British-track requirement published for UAE equivalency is a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education sit outside that count of five, which catches families out when planning option blocks. Confirm current rules at moe.gov.ae, because equivalency is a Ministry process that no tutor performs or influences.

faqs.question: Does 0680 lead anywhere at A Level?
faqs.answer: Cambridge offers AS Level Environmental Management as the direct continuation, extending the resource, population and ecosystem material with considerably more data analysis and policy evaluation. Not every Abu Dhabi school teaches it, so check availability in Year 10 rather than assuming. Where it is unavailable, the common routes are IB Diploma Environmental Systems and Societies in an IB school, or a geography and biology combination at A Level, which reaches most environmental degree courses. None of those routes requires tutoring, and any provider suggesting otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

faqs.question: How do you teach map and graph questions over video?
faqs.answer: On a shared screen, which works better than paper for this specific task. The source sits on screen and the tutor can annotate it live, point at the axis the student misread, and overlay the calculation. The most useful part is handing control back: the student reads values and describes trends while the tutor watches silently and interrupts only at the point of error. Catching a misread axis at the moment it happens is worth more than correcting the finished answer, and it is difficult to do while sitting beside somebody looking at the same sheet.

faqs.question: What does the tutoring cost compared with school fees in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Tutoring at one weekly hour sits well below a term of fees at any Abu Dhabi private school, which is the comparison most families find useful. The fee context needs care, though. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, and that is a Dubai measure from the Dubai regulator. Abu Dhabi fee changes go through ADEK, and no equivalent emirate-wide freeze is cited here because none has been read from an ADEK source. Ask your school or check ADEK before planning on it.

faqs.question: Can 0680 be taught to a private candidate not in a school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the absence of coursework and practical assessment is what makes it practical. The teaching covers the whole syllabus planned backwards from the chosen series, usually across about twelve months of weekly sessions from a standing start. The entry itself is arranged by the family with a Cambridge centre, which sets the fee and the deadline; a tutor can explain how the process works but does not make the entry. Cambridge entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and that gap is the most common surprise in private-candidate planning.

faqs.question: What should we bring to the first 0680 session?
faqs.answer: Three things. A list of which of the nine themes the class has actually covered, which is more reliable than the published scheme of work. A marked mock or class test, because the script shows whether marks were lost reading data, naming strategies or evaluating them, and those need different plans. And the series the student is entered for. With those, a first session can spend the hour on a real question and produce a written diagnosis, rather than spending it working out what the problem is.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-environmental-.closingHeading: Send the theme list and a marked test
abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-environmental-.closingBody: If your child is sitting Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management 0680 at an Abu Dhabi school and the marks are not matching the effort, the likely cause is one answer habit rather than missing knowledge. Send a list of the themes covered so far and a marked mock or class test. A 0680 specialist will work a real data question with them in a free trial lesson, one session and no charge, then write back naming whether the loss is in reading the source, naming a strategy or evaluating it, with a week count attached. abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-french-0520-tu.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach French to an exam specification rather than to a conversation class. Each starts by establishing which of the three Abu Dhabi profiles your child fits, because the first eight hours of teaching differ completely between them. Each session ends with something marked that goes into a record you can read.

intro.heading: Why two Abu Dhabi students with the same French get different 0520 marks
paragraphs: French in Abu Dhabi is not one subject taught to one kind of child. The emirate has long-established French-curriculum schools, large British and IB schools where French is the main foreign language option, and a sizeable francophone population from Lebanon, North and West Africa, France and Belgium. A single Year 11 IGCSE French class in Khalifa City can contain a student who has written dissertations in French, a student who has had two lessons a week since Year 7, and a student who argues with their mother in French every evening and cannot spell any of it. Their 0520 marks are often within a grade of each other, and they arrive there by completely different routes.

That is why a general diagnosis is useless here. The transfer student from a lycée usually has fluency and accuracy well beyond the syllabus and loses marks on format: a reading paper that wants a specific short answer rather than a developed one, a writing task with a word range and a register to hit, a speaking test with a structure that rewards preparation of a kind French schools do not drill. The learner from a British school has the opposite problem. The format is familiar, the language is thin, and marks go on attempted complexity that collapses mid-sentence. The home-language speaker is a third thing again: strong listening, confident speech, written accuracy that nobody has ever corrected because no exam has ever asked.

Cambridge samples four skill areas in a modern foreign language, and the components and weightings for your child's series are published per syllabus and revised from time to time, so confirm them on cambridgeinternational.org rather than taking them from a tutoring page. There is a second question to settle first, and families often get it wrong: which board. Cambridge IGCSE French carries the code 0520, and the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in French is a different qualification with a different code, usually 4FR1. The papers, the structure and the timetables differ. Read the code off your child's entry sheet before you buy a single revision guide.

What this page does, then, is show the evidence each profile produces and what a plan built on that evidence looks like. Not a grade promise, because nobody can offer one honestly, and not a generic course. A marked script, a recorded oral, a word-range check on a written task, and a comparison against the same student six weeks earlier. For a subject where parents frequently cannot assess the work themselves, that record is the whole product.

The practical arrangements are the same for all three profiles. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time so they sit after the Abu Dhabi school day rather than inside it. We do not visit homes in the UAE, and the reason is visible in the subject itself: a 0520 specialist who has marked both boards' papers is rare in any one neighbourhood, and online delivery is what puts that person in front of a student in Al Reef or Al Ain on a Tuesday evening.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-french-0520-tu.programmesIntro: French runs from primary through to the Diploma in Abu Dhabi schools, and the step between each stage is where students are misplaced. These are the levels we teach around 0520, with a note on what each one assumes your child already has.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary French
programmes.description: Two or three lessons a week, usually alongside Spanish or Arabic as the other option, with the aim of arriving in Year 10 able to handle present, past and future reliably. Students who leave Year 9 without secure past tenses enter the IGCSE course with a deficit that shows up in every written task for two years, and it is cheap to close now and expensive to close later.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the Year 9 option choice is often made on which subject looks easier rather than on which the student can sustain for two years. Families transferring in from a French-curriculum school mid-Year 9 face the opposite issue: a child placed in a beginners' set because nobody checked what they could already do.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE French (0520)
programmes.description: The two-year course sampling listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed on accuracy and task fulfilment within a defined range rather than on range itself. Most recoverable marks sit in tense control, agreement and answering the question actually asked. Confirm the component structure and weightings for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org, because the specification is revised between series.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter candidates mainly in the June series, with November available. A number of schools in the emirate run the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE instead, so the first job on any new student is to establish the board and the code and not assume Cambridge because the family said IGCSE.

programmes.name: IB French B
programmes.description: The main continuation route at SL or HL for students with a solid IGCSE grade. The step up is in text handling and in producing a position rather than a description: longer authentic material, unfamiliar registers, and written tasks judged on argument as well as language. Students who reached a strong 0520 grade on memorised phrases usually find the first term of HL uncomfortable.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi IB World Schools run French B at both levels, and departments vary in how readily a 0520 student is admitted to HL. A recorded oral and two marked written tasks are more persuasive in that conversation than a grade on its own.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level French
programmes.description: The A Level route, with literature or topic-based study and substantially more independent writing. It suits the student who enjoyed the reading paper rather than the one who enjoyed the oral. Accuracy is assumed at this level, which means a 0520 student who was still losing agreement marks at sixteen needs that fixed before Year 12 rather than during it.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer Abu Dhabi schools offer A Level French than IB French B, so the choice is often made by what the school timetables rather than by preference. Either way the gap to close over the summer after Year 11 is accuracy, not vocabulary.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-french-0520-tu.subjectsIntro: 0520 marks are lost in identifiable places, and the places differ by profile. These are the components we track separately, plus the subjects Abu Dhabi students most often carry alongside French in the same exam year.

subjects.name: 0520 listening at exam speed
subjects.description: Where learners lose marks to speed rather than to vocabulary, and where transfer students lose them to over-reading a question. We record what is captured on the permitted number of plays and nothing beyond it, because practice with unlimited replays builds a habit the paper does not allow.

subjects.name: 0520 reading and the paraphrase trap
subjects.description: The paper rarely uses the word the text uses. Students who scan for a matching word find the wrong line confidently. The fix is recognising synonym and negation patterns, which is teachable in a handful of sessions and is the fastest available gain on this paper.

subjects.name: 0520 writing within a word range
subjects.description: Tasks with a stated length and register. Lycée transfers routinely overrun and lose task marks while writing beautiful French; learners underwrite and lose content marks. Both are solved by drafting to the range before polishing the language.

subjects.name: 0520 speaking: role play and presentation
subjects.description: The component most often prepared wrongly, by memorising a script that collapses on the first unexpected question. We rehearse recovery rather than content and record each attempt so progress is audible rather than remembered.

subjects.name: Tense and agreement accuracy
subjects.description: Not a component, but the single largest source of avoidable loss across the writing and speaking marks. Perfect and imperfect confusion, adjective agreement and the past participle of reflexives account for most of what we mark week after week.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE French
subjects.description: The other board several Abu Dhabi schools use. Different paper structure, different timetable and different past material, which is why confirming the code on the entry sheet comes before any revision planning.

subjects.name: Spanish (0530)
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside French by the same student, which produces predictable cross-contamination in verb endings and gendered agreement. Scheduling the two on different evenings is a small change with a measurable effect on written accuracy.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Often the third language on an Abu Dhabi timetable, since Arabic provision is required in UAE private schools. Carrying two examined languages plus Arabic in one year is a workload question we will give you an honest answer about before taking the booking.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: The subjects whose essay technique transfers best into French writing tasks. A student who plans in English before writing in French usually produces better-structured French than one who writes straight through.

sections.heading: Three kinds of French student in Abu Dhabi, and what each one's script shows
paragraphs: The first useful thing a 0520 tutor does is work out which student they have. It takes one marked past paper and about twenty minutes, and getting it wrong wastes a term in a direction that feels productive.

The transfer student from a French-curriculum school writes well and scores moderately. Their reading answers are developed where a short answer was wanted, their written tasks overrun the stated range, and their oral is articulate and unstructured. Nothing about their French needs teaching. What needs teaching is a set of conventions, and because the gap is narrow, the honest plan is four to eight sessions rather than a course. Agencies that sell them a two-year package are selling them language they already have.

The long-term learner from a British or IB school in the emirate has the mirror-image profile. Format is second nature, because they have been sitting school assessments in this shape since Year 7. The language is the constraint: tenses that hold in homework and slip under time, adjective agreement applied inconsistently, and a habit of attempting a complex structure where two correct simple sentences would score higher. This student needs the slow weekly build, and the marked work shows movement in error counts long before it shows in grades.

The home-language speaker is the profile most often misread, including by their own school. Listening is excellent, speech is fast and idiomatic, and written accuracy has never been examined because nobody at home corrects spelling. Their reports are glowing and their written marks are mediocre, which parents find baffling. The treatment is written accuracy and register, plus the uncomfortable discovery that the register they speak at home is not the register the writing task wants.

sections.heading: The lycée transfer problem nobody plans for
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi has an established French-curriculum presence, and families move out of it for all the usual reasons: a sibling's school, a change of plan about university, a move to an IB or British school closer to home. The student arrives in a Year 10 or Year 11 IGCSE French class and everybody relaxes, because obviously French will be the easy subject. Then the first assessment comes back in the middle of the class and nobody can explain it.

The explanation is almost always mechanical. A reading paper in this format rewards the shortest answer that contains the required information; a student trained to develop an answer writes three sentences where one was asked for and loses nothing for the extra but gains nothing either, while running the clock down. Written tasks carry a stated length and a register. A student who writes four hundred elegant words for a task with a much smaller range has not met the task, and task marks are not recoverable by quality of language. The speaking test has a structure that rewards preparation of a specific kind, and fluent candidates frequently under-prepare precisely because they are fluent.

The second part of the problem is placement. Some schools put a transfer student into a set by their year group and others by a quick conversation, and a conversation flatters this profile enormously. We have seen strong francophone writers placed in a middle set because the school checked speech rather than script, and learners placed in a top set for the same reason. Ask the department what the placement was based on. If the answer is a conversation, ask for a marked written task.

The honest commercial consequence for us is that this student usually needs a short block. We say so in the trial session and we say when to stop, because continuing to teach French to a child who already has it is the most comfortable money in this market and the least defensible.

sections.heading: What the mark sheet records, and how a tutor should mirror it
paragraphs: Marks on 0520 come off specific criteria within specific components, and feedback that does not name the criterion cannot be acted on. Sounds a bit off is not teaching. Lost two marks for the tense in the second paragraph, and the same tense in last week's task, is.

So the record we keep mirrors the mark sheet rather than summarising it. Each marked written task carries an error category count rather than a score out of ten, because counts are comparable across weeks and scores are not. Each recorded oral carries response length and a note on recovery behaviour. Each timed paper gets every lost mark attributed to a component and a category, and a two-line comparison against the previous paper: what improved, what repeated, what is now the biggest single loss.

This matters particularly in Abu Dhabi because many parents here cannot read the work. A family that speaks Arabic and English at home has no way to judge a page of French, and the usual substitute is trusting the tutor's manner. A record of error categories is independent of manner. If the count for perfect-versus-imperfect confusion has gone from nine to two across six weeks, something happened, regardless of how the lessons felt.

What the record deliberately does not contain is a predicted grade. Grade boundaries are set after a series on the actual paper, they move between series, and converting a mock mark into a confident prediction is guesswork dressed as reassurance. We will tell you what the error list says and what six weeks of the same work would plausibly change. We will not tell you your child is a grade 7.
