sections.heading: Accent, register and the marks that are not there
paragraphs: Two beliefs cost Abu Dhabi families real money on this subject. The first is that sounding French earns marks. The second is that a tutor from France is therefore better than a tutor who has marked the papers. Neither survives contact with a mark scheme.

Pronunciation matters in the speaking component to the extent that it affects communication. Beyond that threshold, a beautiful accent earns nothing additional, and a student with a strong accent and poor structure will score below a student with an audible English accent and controlled, relevant answers. This is not an argument against good pronunciation; it is an argument about where the next hour of teaching should go. For most candidates the next hour should go to tense control, because tense errors cost marks in two components at once.

Register is the related trap for home-language speakers. The French spoken in a Lebanese or Ivorian household in Abu Dhabi is real French and often richer than the syllabus requires, and some of it is wrong for a written task that specifies a formal letter or a report. A student who writes to their teacher the way they speak to their cousin loses register marks without ever making a grammatical error. That is invisible to a parent reading the work and obvious to anyone who has marked it.

The practical test for any tutor you are considering is to ask what a particular written task rewards and where its marks sit. A specialist answers in a sentence or two, naming components. A native speaker without exam experience usually answers with something about fluency, which tells you what the next term would be spent on.

sections.heading: The oral: rehearsing a conversation you cannot script
paragraphs: The speaking component is where preparation most often goes in the wrong direction. Students memorise answers, parents hear them delivered perfectly at the kitchen table, and the first unexpected question in the actual test takes the whole structure down. A memorised answer is brittle by design, and the examiner's job includes asking something slightly off the expected path.

What is worth rehearsing is recovery, not content. In the four seconds after a student meets a word they do not have, they do one of three things: freeze, switch to English, or paraphrase around the gap. Only the third keeps the marks coming, and it is a trainable behaviour rather than a vocabulary problem. We practise it deliberately, by asking questions slightly outside the prepared topics on purpose and rewarding the recovery rather than the answer.

The second thing worth rehearsing is response length. Candidates who answer in four words lose developable marks even when the four words are correct, and candidates who talk for ninety seconds lose the thread. We record length and keep the recordings, because this is the clearest example in the subject of progress a student cannot hear in themselves week to week but can hear across a month.

Recording also handles the part of oral preparation that families in this emirate find hardest to arrange: a second person to speak French with. A parent who does not speak the language cannot rehearse it, and a sibling will not keep doing it. A fixed twice-weekly slot with the same tutor and a recording to compare against is a plainer solution than a conversation group that meets once.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0520 or Pearson Edexcel: settle the board before the revision
paragraphs: A surprising amount of wasted work in this emirate comes from a family revising for the wrong qualification. Cambridge IGCSE French is 0520. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in French is a separate qualification, usually carrying the code 4FR1, with its own paper structure, its own past material and its own timetable. Abu Dhabi schools use both. The code is on the entry sheet and takes one email to confirm.

The timetables differ in ways that matter for planning. Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones; Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson's International GCSEs are available in May and June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a session plan should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that may be revised.

Results timing differs too, which matters for anyone considering a resit. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge publishes its own results dates per series on Direct, and for the March 2027 series its key dates show results on 13 May with certificates in late June. Work out the resit arithmetic from the official dates for your board rather than from a general calendar.

None of that is exotic information and none of it appears on the competing pages for this query. It is also the cheapest thing a parent can check, which is why we put it before any discussion of teaching.

sections.heading: What a French IGCSE is worth in the UAE, and what it is not
paragraphs: French has an advantage in this market that Arabic does not, and it is worth understanding before you decide how much the grade is worth to you. For the British track, the UAE Ministry of Education's published equivalency requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. French, as an accredited subject, can be.

That is a genuine practical point for an Abu Dhabi family counting subjects. A student with five strong non-excluded IGCSEs including French is in a different position from a student relying on Arabic to make up the number. It is also worth noting what the sourced guidance does not say: it states no IB points threshold, and the American-track requirements are expressed through test scores, with English proficiency via a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math. Any page quoting you an IB equivalency figure should be asked for its source on moe.gov.ae.

What a French grade is not is a requirement for anything. No university admission, no school progression and no equivalency process demands tutoring, and nobody should sell you French lessons on the basis that a process will fail without them. Equivalency is a Ministry procedure with its own channel; we do not perform it, speed it up or guarantee its outcome, and neither does anybody else in this market.

The reasons to spend on French are narrower and more honest. Sixth-form entry to French B or A Level French, a continuation route for a child who may study or work in a francophone country, and the simple fact that a language grade earned at sixteen is difficult to go back for later.

sections.heading: Six weeks of marked French work, and what it should show
paragraphs: Grade movement is slow and error movement is fast, and knowing the difference keeps families from quitting in week five of something that is working. Within six weeks of weekly sessions, the record should show change in the error counts even where no grade has moved at all.

A realistic six-week picture for the long-term learner: perfect-versus-imperfect confusion down from most tasks to occasional, adjective agreement applied consistently in prepared writing and still slipping under time, word counts inside the stated range in every task rather than in half of them, and reading questions lost to synonym patterns reduced noticeably once the pattern is taught explicitly. None of that is a grade yet. All of it is evidence that the next six weeks are worth buying.

For the transfer student the six-week picture is different and shorter. Format errors either disappear or they do not. If written tasks are landing inside the range, reading answers are the right length, and the oral has a structure, the block is finished and we will say so. Continuing past that point is how a short job becomes an annuity, and it is the most common quiet overcharge in language tutoring.

For the home-language speaker the first six weeks are usually the least satisfying, because the work is spelling, accents and register on material they find childishly easy to understand. Marked drafts show the change clearly in counts. Students in this group frequently resist the work, and telling a parent that in advance is more useful than discovering it in week three.

sections.heading: How sessions run, and the line on school homework
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one and delivered over live video, booked in Gulf Standard Time so they sit after the Abu Dhabi school day. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and for this subject the online format carries a specific advantage. A tutor who has marked both Cambridge 0520 and the Edexcel paper is not reliably available within driving distance of Al Reef or Al Ain, and format expertise is precisely what two of the three profiles on this page need.

The boundary on homework is firm and it comes up constantly with languages. A tutor may teach a structure, model a task on a different prompt, mark what your child has already submitted, name the criterion a mark came off, and set a parallel task. A tutor may not supply sentences for a piece going to school, polish a draft into a finished state, or provide material to be copied. Boards treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever helped.

In French this boundary is easy to cross by accident, because correcting a sentence feels like teaching. The test we use is whether the student could reproduce the correction unaided tomorrow. Explaining why the auxiliary is wrong passes that test. Writing the corrected sentence for them does not, which is why marking names the error category and hands the revision back.

What you can expect to see is the record: marked tasks with error counts, recorded orals, attributed timed papers, and a short note after each session naming the next target. Ask for it at any point, including the weeks where nothing moved, which are the weeks that tell you most about whether a plan needs changing.

process.title: Confirm the board and the code first
process.description: Send the syllabus code from the entry sheet, Cambridge 0520 or the Pearson Edexcel equivalent, with the series and the centre. Confirming this before teaching starts prevents the single most wasteful error in this subject, which is revising from the wrong board's past papers for a term.

process.title: Diagnose the profile from a marked paper
process.description: In the free trial the tutor marks a past paper section or a recent piece of school work and identifies which of the three profiles your child fits. The first eight hours differ completely between them, so this twenty minutes decides more than any amount of discussion about goals.

process.title: Agree a plan sized to the profile
process.description: A transfer student usually gets a four to eight session format block. A long-term learner gets a weekly build with a termly timed paper. A home-language speaker gets accuracy and register work. We size the plan to the diagnosis and state when it should end rather than leaving it open.

process.title: Weekly marked work and a recorded oral
process.description: Each session produces a marked written task with error counts, or a recorded spoken attempt, and a note naming the next target. Recordings are kept with your consent so a month of oral progress can be heard rather than described. Nothing is written for your child at any stage.

process.title: Review against the error counts, not the mood
process.description: At six weeks we compare the error counts and the timed paper attributions against where they started. The options are continue, change the focus, change the tutor, or finish because the problem the block was bought for has gone. The last of those is a real outcome and we do say it.

whyPoints.title: The profile is diagnosed before anything is sold
whyPoints.description: A lycée transfer and a Year 7 learner need opposite first blocks, and selling both the same package is how a term disappears. We mark a paper first and size the plan to what it shows, including the version where the honest answer is a handful of sessions.

whyPoints.title: Board and code confirmed up front
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0520 and the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in French are different qualifications with different papers and timetables. Several Abu Dhabi schools use each. We settle which one your child is sitting before a revision plan is built on the wrong past papers.

whyPoints.title: Error counts rather than scores
whyPoints.description: Marked work carries counted error categories and word counts against the range, which are comparable week to week. A mark out of ten moves for reasons nobody can name. A count that falls from nine to two is something you can see without reading French.

whyPoints.title: Oral work recorded and compared
whyPoints.description: Response length and recovery behaviour are tracked, with recordings kept so a month of change is audible. For families in this emirate who do not speak French, a recording is the only honest way to judge whether the speaking component is improving.

whyPoints.title: No predicted grades
whyPoints.description: Grade boundaries are set after a series on the real paper. We attribute every lost mark to a component and a category and say what six more weeks of the same work would plausibly change. A confident prediction offered as reassurance is worth less than an error list.

whyPoints.title: Online, and plain about why
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with later starts during Ramadan. We hold no accreditation from any regulator or exam board, do not claim any, and do not write any part of what your child submits.

faqs.question: What does marked French work look like after six weeks of tutoring?
faqs.answer: It looks like falling error counts rather than a new grade. For a typical learner, six weeks of weekly sessions should show perfect-versus-imperfect confusion dropping from most tasks to occasional, agreement applied consistently in prepared writing, word counts landing inside the stated range on every task rather than half of them, and fewer reading questions lost to synonym patterns once that pattern has been taught explicitly. Grades move later and more slowly. The point of counting errors is that you can see the change at week six and make an informed decision about week seven.

faqs.question: My son moved from a French-curriculum school into an IGCSE French class. What does he need?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly exam conventions rather than French. This profile writes beautifully and scores moderately, because reading answers get developed where a short answer was wanted, written tasks overrun the stated range, and the oral is articulate without a structure. Task marks are not recoverable by quality of language. The realistic plan is four to eight sessions of format work, and we will tell you when it is finished. Also ask the school what his set placement was based on: if it was a conversation rather than a marked written task, the placement may be wrong in either direction.

faqs.question: Does a French IGCSE count towards the five subjects the Ministry of Education requires?
faqs.answer: Yes, as an accredited subject it can. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are explicitly not included among the five, which is why French is the more useful of the two for the subject count. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation channel rather than on a tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: My daughter sounds French but gets a 5 in 0520. What is she losing marks on?
faqs.answer: Usually written accuracy and register, in that order. Pronunciation counts in the speaking component only to the extent it affects communication; beyond that threshold a strong accent earns nothing extra. Meanwhile spelling, accents and agreement have never been corrected, because no exam at home ever asked. Register is the other half: the French spoken to a cousin is not the register a formal written task wants, and a student can lose register marks without making a single grammatical error. Marked drafts expose both within three weeks, which is why we start there rather than with vocabulary.

faqs.question: Cambridge 0520 or the Edexcel International GCSE in French: which is my child sitting?
faqs.answer: Read the code on the entry sheet, because Abu Dhabi schools use both and the two are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE French is 0520; the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in French usually carries the code 4FR1. Paper structures, past material and timetables all differ. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, while Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series before finalising them. One email to the school settles it, and it should happen before any revision plan exists.

faqs.question: How do we rehearse the 0520 speaking test without scripting it?
faqs.answer: By practising recovery instead of content. A memorised answer is brittle, and the first slightly unexpected question takes the whole structure down. What we train is the four seconds after a student meets a word they do not have: freezing, switching to English and paraphrasing around the gap are three different behaviours, and only the last keeps marks coming. We ask questions deliberately outside the prepared topics and reward the recovery. Response length is tracked too, since very short correct answers leave developable marks unclaimed and very long ones lose the thread.

faqs.question: Which 0520 component should we fix first if there are only eight weeks left?
faqs.answer: Reading, then writing structure, then listening technique, and deep accuracy last because it will not move in eight weeks. The reading paper gives the fastest return: most losses come from scanning for a word that matches the text when the question has paraphrased it, and teaching synonym and negation patterns explicitly changes that within a few sessions. Writing to the stated range and register is next, since task marks are lost structurally rather than through weakness. We will tell you plainly what eight weeks cannot reach rather than selling an intensive that implies it can.

faqs.question: How is French homework set by the school handled in a tutoring session?
faqs.answer: We mark it after it has been submitted, or set a parallel task on a different prompt before it is due. What we will not do is sit with your child while they write the piece that goes to the teacher. Boards treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice and the consequence falls on the student. The working test is whether your child could reproduce a correction unaided tomorrow: explaining why an auxiliary is wrong passes, writing the corrected sentence for them does not, so marking names the error category and hands the revision back.

faqs.question: Can my child sit French in November instead of June?
faqs.answer: Both Cambridge and Pearson run a November series as well as a summer one, so it is usually possible, but the decision belongs to the school and the entry deadline sits months ahead. Check the dates for your board: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while Cambridge publishes results per series on Direct. The practical question is whether the extra months will be used. A November entry with no plan attached is simply a later disappointment.

faqs.question: We speak French at home. Does my child still need a 0520 tutor?
faqs.answer: Possibly not for the language, and possibly yes for the paper. Home-language speakers typically score well on listening and speaking and lose marks on written accuracy and register, because spelling and accents have never been examined and the household register is not the one a formal task wants. If the written marks are already strong, there is nothing for us to do and we will say so in the trial. If there is a gap between glowing reports and mediocre written marks, that gap is specific, visible in a marked draft, and usually a short block of work.

faqs.question: How do you record speaking progress over a video lesson?
faqs.answer: Each attempt is recorded with your consent, and the same task is repeated a month later so the two can be compared directly. We log response length and recovery behaviour rather than an impression of fluency, because impressions are unreliable after four weeks. For Abu Dhabi families who do not speak French, this is the only honest way to judge the speaking component: you can hear two recordings a month apart without being able to assess the grammar. It also solves the practical problem that a parent who does not speak the language cannot rehearse it.

faqs.question: What does a French IGCSE tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: qualified subject tutors working online in the UAE are advertised between roughly AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE support from AED 150, while in-home visits are put at AED 180 to AED 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table. Specialist exam-year rates run higher. What changes the total more than the hourly rate is the plan length, and the three profiles on this page need very different lengths, which is why we diagnose before quoting rather than selling a standard package.

faqs.question: Should my child take French and Arabic IGCSEs in the same exam year?
faqs.answer: Many Abu Dhabi students do, because Arabic provision is part of the deal in UAE private schools and French is the chosen option. It is manageable and it is not free. Two languages with different scripts and different grammars in one year means two sets of written accuracy work, and the usual failure is that one quietly gets all the practice. If you add a third language, be deliberate about which evenings each one gets. We will give you an honest view of the workload before taking a booking rather than after.

faqs.question: Do you teach students at the French-curriculum schools in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: We teach students from across the emirate's schools, including children at the French-curriculum lycées who are preparing for an IGCSE entry or planning a move into a British or IB school. Those students usually need format work rather than language work, which makes for a short block. We have no affiliation with any school in Abu Dhabi, name them only as context for where French is taught here, and would be inventing a relationship we do not have if we suggested otherwise.

faqs.question: What evidence should I ask the school for before paying for French tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four things, all of which someone in the building knows. The syllabus code and board your child is entered for. The component or criterion breakdown behind the last assessment, in order of marks lost. Which set or group they sit in and what moving up requires. And what the current set placement was based on, since a conversation flatters a fluent speaker and underrates a careful learner. With those four answers a tutor can size the work accurately, and sometimes they show that no tutoring is needed at all.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-french-0520-tu.closingHeading: Send the entry code and one piece of marked work
abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-french-0520-tu.closingBody: Useful Cambridge IGCSE French 0520 support in Abu Dhabi starts with two documents rather than a conversation: the syllabus code from your child's entry sheet, and one recent piece of marked French. From those the trial session will tell you which of the three profiles your child fits and roughly how long the work should take, which for a transfer student from a French-curriculum school is often a handful of sessions rather than a course. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, spoken work is recorded so progress is audible, and nothing is written for your child at any point.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 for Abu Dhabi families: Paper 1 theme questions, Paper 2 skills, and feedback on a school-set fieldwork assignment. Each has marked humanities answers against a mark scheme rather than only taught from a course book.

intro.heading: The 0460 grade is decided by three different skills, and only one of them is knowledge
paragraphs: Geography is the subject where a hard-working student can read every page of the syllabus and still come out with a 5. Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 does not pay for recall on its own. Paper 1 pays for case-study detail attached to a named place, written in a causal chain. Paper 2 pays for technique on a resource the student has never seen before: a map extract, a climate graph, a table of raw figures, a photograph. The coursework component, or the written paper that replaces it, pays for method and honest limitations. A student can be strong at one of these and weak at the other two, and the report will simply say "inconsistent".

That is why the first useful thing a tutor does is separate the three. We ask for the most recent marked geography paper your child has sat at school, in whatever state it came back, and read it question by question before teaching anything. Within one session it is usually clear which of the three skills is costing the grade. A student losing marks on describe questions has a resource-reading problem. A student losing marks on the eight-mark evaluation has a judgement problem. A student whose Paper 1 answers are full of real content but score in the middle band is almost always writing lists instead of chains.

The second thing a tutor does is stop guessing about the components. Which papers your child sits is a decision their school made, often two years ago, and many parents in Abu Dhabi have never been told. A school that runs fieldwork enters Paper 3, the internally assessed coursework. A school that does not enters Paper 4, the Alternative to Coursework, where the student answers questions about fieldwork someone else carried out. The revision for those two is not the same work. Getting this wrong wastes an entire term, and it is a two-line email to the head of humanities to confirm.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. For a 0460 candidate that is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise. Geography specialists who can mark a Paper 2 map extract properly are thin on the ground in any one district, and a screen share is the format in which a map, a graph and a student's own answer can all be annotated at once while the student watches the pen move.

What this page sets out, in order: what each 0460 component actually assesses, where Abu Dhabi candidates lose marks question type by question type, how the coursework decision is made, what fieldwork data a student here can genuinely collect, what the Abu Dhabi tutoring market charges in AED and who publishes those figures, and the honesty line a tutor must not cross on a school-set assignment. Nothing on this page is a promise about a grade. Geography grades move when a student changes how they write, and that takes marked work and weeks.
bullets: Paper 1 rewards named places and causal chains, not general knowledge
Paper 2 is a technique exam and technique responds quickly to drilling
Paper 3 coursework and Paper 4 are alternatives, never both
Session times follow Gulf Standard Time and the ADEK school week

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460.programmesIntro: Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 sits inside a longer route. Abu Dhabi families usually arrive here from Cambridge Lower Secondary and leave towards AS and A Level or an IB Diploma. The four stages below are the ones that affect how a 0460 year is planned.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Geography
programmes.description: The three years before 0460 build map reading, graph drawing and the habit of naming a place. Schools vary enormously in how much of this they do. A Year 9 student who has never measured a distance on a scale bar or drawn a cross-section arrives in Year 10 with a skills gap that Paper 2 will find in the first ten minutes of the exam.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools teach a thematic humanities course up to Year 9 rather than separate geography, so the first weeks of Year 10 are often the first time a student meets the subject as its own discipline. Asking the head of humanities which skills were covered in Checkpoint teaching tells you whether to start 0460 support with content or with technique.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography (0460)
programmes.description: Two years, three themes, two written exams and one coursework component or its written alternative. Theme 1 covers population and settlement, Theme 2 the natural environment, Theme 3 economic development and its environmental risks. Paper 1 asks one structured question on each theme. The content is wide rather than deep, which is why students underestimate the volume of case-study detail required.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi 0460 is commonly taken alongside Environmental Management 0680 or History 0470, and the overlap with 0680 on water, energy and environmental risk is large enough that one tutor can usefully cover both. Which combination a school offers depends on timetable blocking, so the subject choice conversation in Year 9 is worth having early.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Geography (9696)
programmes.description: The step up is in the expectation of theory and in the length of written answers. Students who scored well at 0460 by memorising case studies tend to struggle in the first term of AS, where arguments have to be built rather than recalled. The students who cope are the ones who learned to write evaluation at 0460 rather than avoid it.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families planning a UK or UAE university route in geography, urban planning or environmental science should check which post-16 geography their child's school actually runs, since several British-curriculum schools in the emirate offer A Level geography in alternate years depending on cohort numbers.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Geography
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, taken at the IB schools in the emirate. DP Geography keeps the physical and human split but adds a compulsory fieldwork investigation and a global-change core. A 0460 student moving into DP Geography finds the skills transfer well and the essay demand rises sharply.
programmes.countryNote: Because Abu Dhabi has both British-curriculum and IB schools within a short drive of each other, families here change curriculum more often than they would in most cities. A 0460 candidate who may move to an IB school for Year 12 benefits from spending some 0460 time on structured evaluation, which is the part that carries over.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460.subjectsIntro: The 0460 syllabus is organised as three themes plus a skills component. The grid below is the version a tutor plans from: each entry names the theme, the paper it is examined in, and the specific thing that costs marks in it.

subjects.name: Population dynamics and population structure
subjects.description: Birth rates, death rates, the demographic transition model and population pyramids. Marks go missing when a student describes a pyramid shape without reading the axis values, or explains a falling birth rate with one factor and stops. Examiners want a named country for each stage and a reason tied to that country.

subjects.name: Migration
subjects.description: Push and pull factors, voluntary and forced movement, and the effects on both origin and destination. The common error is a push-pull list with no actual migration stream named. A student living in the UAE has a usable example in front of them, but it only scores if the flow, the reason and the consequence are all stated.

subjects.name: Settlement, service provision and urbanisation
subjects.description: Settlement hierarchy, land-use zones, the problems of rapid urban growth and attempts to manage them. Candidates lose marks by describing a generic city. The fix is two contrasting named cities, one in a higher-income country and one in a lower-income country, each with three specific details.

subjects.name: Earthquakes and volcanoes
subjects.description: Plate boundaries, hazard causes, and why people live in hazardous places. The weak answer explains the science and forgets the human geography. The strong answer attaches a named event to a named boundary type and separates primary from secondary effects without being asked.

subjects.name: Rivers and river landforms
subjects.description: Processes of erosion, transport and deposition, the features they create, and flood causes and management. This topic appears in Paper 2 as cross-sections and hydrographs, so it has to be learned twice: once as process and once as a graph to read. Hydrograph lag time is a reliable mark-loser.

subjects.name: Coasts and coastal management
subjects.description: Wave processes, erosional and depositional landforms, coral and mangrove environments, and hard versus soft engineering. Students in Abu Dhabi have mangroves and engineered shoreline on their doorstep, which makes the management section easier to remember and the landform sequence harder, because there is little classic cliff retreat to see.

subjects.name: Weather, climate and natural vegetation
subjects.description: Instruments and their siting, climate graph interpretation, and the characteristics of tropical rainforest and hot desert ecosystems. The desert ecosystem is the one Abu Dhabi students answer well and the rainforest the one they answer from memory. Both need named adaptations, not adjectives.

subjects.name: Development and food production
subjects.description: Development indicators, inequality within and between countries, and farming systems with their inputs, processes and outputs. The system diagram is worth learning as a diagram. Answers that treat development as a single number score poorly; the mark scheme rewards a student who knows why one indicator can mislead.

subjects.name: Industry, tourism and energy
subjects.description: Industrial location factors, the growth and management of tourism, and energy supply including renewable and non-renewable sources. Abu Dhabi offers usable material on energy transition and on tourism development, and both score well when the candidate gives the location, the reason and one measurable consequence.

subjects.name: Water supply and environmental risks of economic development
subjects.description: Water sources and demand, pollution, soil degradation, and the management of resources. This is the theme with the heaviest overlap with Environmental Management 0680, and the one where a Gulf student has the most direct experience to draw on if they are taught to convert it into exam language.

subjects.name: Map and photograph interpretation
subjects.description: Grid references, scale and distance, direction, relief description, cross-sections, and describing settlement or land-use patterns from a map extract and a photograph together. This is pure technique. Most students gain marks here faster than anywhere else in the syllabus, because almost nobody has practised it deliberately.

subjects.name: Graphs, tables and simple statistics
subjects.description: Completing and reading bar, line, pie, scatter and triangular graphs, choosing an appropriate graph type, and calculating or interpreting means, medians and ranges. The commands are narrow and the marks are predictable, which makes this the most coachable part of 0460.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Abu Dhabi changes two practical things for geography: which fieldwork sites are within reach for a coursework assignment, and what time an evening session can realistically start. The notes below are about geography specifically, not general area description.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Central, close to several island schools, and within reach of the city's older land-use zones, which makes an urban land-use transect a realistic coursework option. Sessions here can usually start at 16:00 on a normal school day.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Shoreline and marina frontage give a workable coastal-management study: engineered defences, groynes and reclaimed land are all visible within a short walk. Useful for the Theme 2 coasts content as well as for fieldwork.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: A high-rise, recently built district where population density and service provision can be observed as they are being created. Apartment living also means quieter, earlier sessions are easier to schedule than in villa communities with later sport.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities with long school runs to the island. Evening sessions here commonly start at 17:30 or later. The low-density residential pattern is itself a usable contrast for a settlement-density investigation against Al Reem or Al Zahiyah.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Purpose-built leisure and tourism development, which gives Theme 3 tourism material a candidate can describe at first hand: visitor management, seasonality, traffic generation and the pressure on a small land area.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Coastal residential development on reclaimed frontage, within sight of mangrove channels. Good for the coral and mangrove section of the coasts topic, where most candidates have only textbook knowledge.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Rapidly expanding mainland communities where urban growth is visible year on year. For a candidate who needs a named example of settlement expansion and service provision lagging behind housing, this is on their own street.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Inland, with oases, wadis and a genuinely different climate record from the coast. An Al Ain student has access to irrigation, groundwater and hot-desert ecosystem material that coastal candidates can only read about, and a different evening timetable because of the commute patterns there.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island schools
schoolClusters.note: Island schools tend to run the longest-established British-curriculum humanities departments in the emirate, and most enter Cambridge or Pearson IGCSEs. Which geography syllabus and which coursework route a school uses is the school's own decision and changes between cohorts, so confirm it with the head of humanities before planning a revision year.

schoolClusters.city: The Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas corridor
schoolClusters.note: The mainland corridor holds a large share of the emirate's newer British-curriculum and international schools, and the families there face the longest school runs. Students we support in this corridor most often ask for Paper 2 skills work, because it is the component their own revision plan tends to leave until last.

sections.heading: What a Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 tutor in Abu Dhabi actually changes in the first month
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 tutor in Abu Dhabi earns the fee in the first month by diagnosing rather than teaching. The opening session is spent on work that already exists: the last school assessment, a mock answer booklet, or a single past-paper question done at the table while the tutor watches. Reading a student's own writing against the mark scheme tells you more in twenty minutes than a term of general revision. Most 0460 candidates are not short of knowledge. They are short of a method for turning what they know into the specific thing each command word asks for.

The second thing that changes is the vocabulary of feedback. Instead of "be more detailed", a student hears "that is a level-one answer because it names no place; add Dubai and a figure and it becomes level two". Mark-scheme language is unglamorous and it is also the whole trick. Students who learn the level descriptors for the eight-mark question stop writing until they run out of ideas and start writing until the descriptor is satisfied. That single change is usually worth more than any amount of re-reading.

The third is a confirmed component plan. By the end of the first month a family should know which papers their child sits, when the school's internal deadlines fall for any fieldwork write-up, and which of the three themes is weakest on the evidence of marked work rather than on the student's own sense of it. Students are consistently wrong about which theme they are worst at, because they confuse the topics they dislike with the topics that lose them marks. The marked papers settle it.

sections.heading: The three themes, the two written papers and the coursework decision
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 is assessed across three components, and the third one has two possible forms. Paper 1 is the Geographical Themes paper: structured questions drawing on population and settlement, the natural environment, and economic development, with case-study detail expected throughout. Paper 2 is the Geographical Skills paper, built entirely on resources provided in the booklet. The third component is either Paper 3, a coursework assignment set and marked by the school and moderated by Cambridge, or Paper 4, the Alternative to Coursework, a written exam about fieldwork the candidate did not carry out themselves.

The decision between Paper 3 and Paper 4 is made by the school, not the family, and it is usually made on logistics: whether the department can run a fieldwork programme, whether sites are accessible, and whether staff have capacity for internal marking and moderation. Neither route is easier in any general sense. Paper 3 rewards students who are organised across months. Paper 4 rewards students who can read somebody else's method and criticise it under timed conditions. The revision for the two has almost nothing in common, which is why confirming the route is the single highest-value email a parent can send.

Weightings and durations in the table below are given in relative terms on purpose. Cambridge republishes the syllabus on a cycle, and the exact percentage split and paper length for the series your child sits must be read from the current syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org or confirmed by the school's exams officer. What does not change year to year is the shape: one content paper carrying the largest share, one skills paper, and one fieldwork component in two alternative forms.

sections.heading: Paper 2 is a technique exam, and technique is the fastest thing to fix
paragraphs: The Geographical Skills paper is the part of 0460 that behaves least like a school subject and most like a driving test. There is a finite list of things it can ask. Give a grid reference. Measure a distance using the scale. State a direction. Describe the relief of an area. Complete a cross-section. Describe the pattern of settlement or land use. Read a value off a graph. Complete a bar, line or triangular graph. Calculate or interpret a mean, median or range. Suggest what a photograph shows about land use. Each of these has a correct procedure and a predictable way of being got wrong.

Because the list is finite, this component responds to drilling in a way that content revision does not. A student who practises six-figure grid references for fifteen minutes stops losing those marks permanently. A student who learns to describe relief using height values and slope direction, rather than saying "it is hilly", gains two or three marks every time the question appears. Over a full paper those small, repeatable gains add up to more than most students pick up from another month of reading Theme 1.

What a tutor adds here is the discipline of marking. Skills answers feel right to the student and are often wrong by a technicality: the easting given before the northing, the units dropped, the scale misread by a factor of ten, the cross-section plotted without checking the vertical axis. Those errors are invisible without a mark scheme and obvious with one. Screen sharing suits this work: the resource, the student's answer and the mark scheme sit side by side, and the annotation happens where the student can watch it rather than arriving a week later in red pen.

sections.heading: Where 0460 candidates lose marks, command word by command word
paragraphs: Almost all avoidable mark loss in 0460 comes from answering a different question from the one asked. The command word sets the task, and students who have not been taught the commands explicitly default to whichever mode they find most comfortable, which is usually explaining. An explain answer to a describe question scores nothing extra for the explanation, and loses the marks the description would have earned. This is not a knowledge failure, and it cannot be fixed by revising harder.

The second avoidable loss is the ignored resource. When a question says "using Fig. 2", the marks are for material lifted from Fig. 2. A student who writes a perfectly sound general answer without quoting a single figure from the insert is marked down for exactly that. Examiner reports return to this point every series. In practice it is a habit problem, fixed by a rule the student applies without thinking: if the question names a figure, the first sentence quotes a number from it, with its unit.

The third is the extended evaluation question at the end of each theme question, where the command is some version of "to what extent do you agree". It carries more marks than anything else on the paper and it is the one most often answered as a one-sided description. The mark scheme wants two sides, named examples, and a stated judgement. A student who writes a short paragraph for each side and then one sentence beginning "overall, the evidence suggests" reliably moves up a level, even before the content improves.

sections.heading: Coursework or the Alternative to Coursework: how the choice is really made in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: In this emirate the coursework decision is driven by access and staffing more than by pedagogy. Running a fieldwork programme for a full Year 10 cohort means transport, supervision, permissions, a site that is safe in the heat, and a department with the capacity to mark and internally standardise the write-ups. Schools with a long-established humanities team and a workable nearby site often do it. Newer departments, smaller cohorts and timetables already stretched by mandatory subject requirements frequently choose the written alternative instead.

If your child is on the coursework route, the tutoring job is mostly about structure and honesty. The student chooses a question that can actually be answered with data they can collect, writes a hypothesis narrow enough to test, decides on a sampling method and can justify it, presents data in a form that suits the data rather than the prettiest chart available, and writes a conclusion that answers the hypothesis including where it was not supported. A tutor can teach all of that, ask hard questions about a draft, and point out where a graph type is doing the student no favours. A tutor cannot and does not write any part of the submission, and we say that to the student in the first session.

If your child is on the Paper 4 route, the work looks different. The paper hands over somebody else's investigation and asks the candidate to evaluate it: was the sample large enough, was the method biased, does the data support the conclusion, what would you change. Students find this harder than coursework in one specific way - they have never been taught to criticise a method, only to follow one. Practice is the whole remedy, and it is practice on the specific insert style the paper uses rather than on general fieldwork theory.

sections.heading: Fieldwork and case-study material an Abu Dhabi student can genuinely use
paragraphs: One of the quiet advantages of studying 0460 in Abu Dhabi is that several syllabus topics are observable from a car window. Coastal engineering, land reclamation, mangrove environments, desert ecosystem adaptation, groundwater and desalinated water supply, energy transition, rapid urban expansion and tourism development are all part of the syllabus and all visible in this emirate. Examiners reward specificity, and a student who can name a local site and describe what is happening there has a better answer than one reciting a textbook example they have never seen.

The practical version of this is a short list of usable sites rather than a general encouragement to look around. A land-use transect from the older central districts out towards the newer mainland communities gives a settlement pattern with real variation. The shoreline at Al Bateen and along Al Raha Beach gives engineered coastal defence and reclaimed frontage. Mangrove channels give a coral-and-mangrove environment and a conservation management angle. Al Ain gives oasis irrigation, groundwater and a genuinely inland climate record. Yas Island gives tourism pressure on a small, purpose-built land area.

Two cautions. First, a local example is only worth marks if it is converted into exam language: process, cause, effect, named place, measurable detail. A student who writes about the mangroves as scenery scores nothing. Second, case studies for Paper 1 still need a contrasting example from a different income context, because the mark scheme repeatedly asks for comparison between a higher-income and a lower-income country. Local material is a supplement to that requirement, not a replacement for it.

sections.heading: What 0460 geography tutoring costs in the Abu Dhabi market, in AED
paragraphs: Published hourly rates for IGCSE humanities tutoring in the UAE are spread across a wide band, and the figures below are other providers' own published numbers, read in October 2026, with the provider named. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list. Our own position on a 0460 request is settled in a consultation after a free thirty-minute trial lesson, because the right number depends on whether a student needs weekly content support across two years or a six-week Paper 2 clinic before a series.

Three things move a quote in this emirate specifically. The first is format: an in-home visit prices travel time into the hour, which is why market in-home rates sit above online rates for the same tutor quality. The second is scarcity: geography is a smaller subject than maths or the sciences, and a tutor who has actually marked 0460 answers is harder to find within one district than within a national pool. The third is timing: demand concentrates in the eight weeks before each series, and a family booking in the April before a June series has fewer slots to choose from than one booking in October.

A useful sanity check for any quote is the question of what is included. Ask whether the hourly figure covers marking done between sessions, whether progress notes are written up, whether a cancelled slot is recoverable, and whether the rate changes closer to the exam. Several providers quote an attractive headline rate and charge separately for marked work, which for a subject assessed on written answers is the part that matters most.

sections.heading: ADEK, the tutoring permit, equivalency, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That matters to a geography family in two ways: the school's inspection report is a public document worth reading before you blame a teacher for a grade, and the emirate's rules on staff conduct affect who may tutor your child. Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy before relying on it, and do not ask a classroom teacher to tutor their own student privately.

Individual private tutors in the UAE need a work permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee shown and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and claims none.

On equivalency, the British-track rule as reported in July 2026 is that students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Whether a particular geography certificate counts within those five is a question for the Ministry of Education or the emirate attestation authority, and only they can answer it. IB Gram does not carry out or guarantee equivalency, and nothing about tutoring is required for it. Finally, the honesty line: a tutor teaches, questions, and gives written feedback on work the student has produced. Assessed submissions must be the student's own from first word to last, and no part of a 0460 fieldwork assignment is drafted on their behalf.

process.description: Whatever came back from school most recently, in whatever state. A mock booklet is ideal, a single marked question is enough. process.title: Confirm the component route with the school
process.description: A short email to the head of humanities asking which Cambridge series the cohort is entered for, and whether the third component is Paper 3 coursework or Paper 4. If coursework, ask for the internal submission deadline. Everything about the revision plan depends on these two answers.

process.title: Take the free thirty-minute trial lesson
process.description: One trial per family, no card details taken to book it. The tutor works through a single 0460 question with the student, marks it live, and names the specific habit costing marks. You get a written note afterwards saying what they would do in the first six weeks and roughly how many sessions it needs.

process.description: Sessions are scheduled around the ADEK school week and your own commute, not around a tutor in another time zone. Families in Khalifa City and Al Shamkha usually take a later slot than island families. The slot stays the same each week so that it becomes part of the routine rather than a negotiation.

process.title: Review at each half-term against marked work
process.description: Every six to eight weeks the marked answers are reviewed together: what has moved, what has not, and whether the plan should change. If the next milestone is a mock or a coursework deadline, the plan is rebuilt backwards from that date rather than continuing forward from the last session.

whyPoints.title: The tutor has marked 0460 answers, not just read the syllabus
whyPoints.description: The difference shows in the first session. Someone who has marked humanities papers knows why a sound-sounding answer sits in level one, and can quote the descriptor that explains it. Someone who has only taught the content explains the content again, which is rarely what the grade needed.

whyPoints.title: Paper 2 is treated as its own subject
whyPoints.description: Skills work is booked as a block and taught as technique, not folded into content lessons where it always gets squeezed. This is deliberate: the skills list is short, it responds to drilling, and it is the component most school revision programmes reach last.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support stops where the mark scheme says it stops
whyPoints.description: Feedback, questions, structure, choice of data presentation, and hard interrogation of a draft the student has written. Not drafting, not supplying text, not improving sentences into something that is no longer the student's own. The boundary is stated to the student directly in the first session.

whyPoints.title: Abu Dhabi timings and Abu Dhabi deadlines
whyPoints.description: Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time around the local school week, move later during Ramadan when families ask, and are planned against the school's own internal deadlines rather than a generic revision calendar. A plan built around the wrong exam series is worse than no plan.

whyPoints.title: A national tutor pool instead of a district one
whyPoints.description: Geography is a smaller subject than maths or physics, and a specialist who can mark 0460 skills answers may not live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Reem or Al Shamkha. Online delivery removes the geography of hiring from the problem entirely, which for this subject is the point.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed before you commit
whyPoints.description: If no 0460 specialist has a slot that suits your week, you are told that at the enquiry stage along with the realistic alternative, rather than being matched with a generalist and left to discover the gap in week three. A plain no is more useful than a slow disappointment.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 tutor in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates for IGCSE humanities tutoring run roughly AED 33-65 at the budget online end, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit with travel included, and AED 200-450 or more for a subject specialist. Those are other providers' own figures, read in October 2026. Monthly packages advertised in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. IB Gram sets its own figure in a consultation after a free thirty-minute trial, because a two-year weekly plan and a six-week Paper 2 clinic are different pieces of work.

faqs.question: Which 0460 papers does my child sit if their school never runs fieldwork?
faqs.answer: A school that cannot run a fieldwork programme enters candidates for Paper 4, the Alternative to Coursework, instead of Paper 3. Paper 4 is a written exam built on an investigation someone else carried out, and it asks the candidate to evaluate the method, the sampling and the conclusions. It is not a soft option, because criticising a method is a skill most students have never been taught. Confirm the route in writing with the head of humanities, since the preparation for Paper 3 and Paper 4 has almost nothing in common and planning for the wrong one wastes a term.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between 0460 coursework and the Alternative to Coursework?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 coursework is one school-based fieldwork assignment, written over weeks, marked by the school and moderated by Cambridge. It rewards organisation, a testable hypothesis, sensible data presentation and an honest conclusion. Paper 4 is a timed written paper about fieldwork the candidate did not do, and it rewards method criticism: sample size, bias, reliability, what you would change. Coursework spreads the pressure across months; Paper 4 concentrates it into one exam. The school decides which applies, usually on staffing and site access rather than on which suits your child.

faqs.question: Why does my son score well on Paper 1 but badly on Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Because they test different things and only one of them rewards knowing the content. Paper 1 pays for case-study detail and causal explanation. Paper 2 pays for technique on resources he has never seen: grid references, measuring with the scale, describing relief with height values, completing a cross-section, reading a graph, choosing an appropriate graph type, and handling a mean or a range. Strong content students often lose Paper 2 marks on technicalities such as giving the northing before the easting or dropping a unit. Those errors are invisible without a mark scheme and disappear quickly with deliberate drilling.

faqs.question: What skills does 0460 Paper 2 test that the textbook does not really cover?
faqs.answer: The skills paper works from a provided insert, so the examinable list is procedural rather than factual: grid references, distance and scale, direction, relief description, cross-section completion, describing settlement and land-use patterns, photograph interpretation, completing and reading bar, line, pie, scatter and triangular graphs, choosing a suitable graph type, and simple statistics such as mean, median and range. Textbooks explain the topics but rarely drill the procedures. That is why a short block of technique sessions usually moves this component faster than any additional content revision does.

faqs.question: Is 0460 the same geography my daughter studied in Year 9?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Several Abu Dhabi schools teach a combined humanities course up to Year 9 rather than separate geography, so Year 10 can be the first time a student meets the subject as its own discipline with its own command words. The content widens considerably and the assessment expects named places, figures and a stated judgement in the extended questions. If her Year 9 course did little map work or graph drawing, start 0460 support with Paper 2 technique rather than with Theme 1 content.

faqs.question: What does the extended evaluation question at the end of a 0460 theme question want?
faqs.answer: Two sides, named places, and a verdict. The command is some version of to what extent do you agree, and it carries more marks than anything else in that question. Most students answer it as a one-sided description and sit in the middle band however good the content is. The reliable structure is one paragraph supporting the statement with a named example, one paragraph challenging it with a different named example, then a short closing judgement that actually commits. That structural change often moves a level before the content improves at all.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's 0460 fieldwork write-up before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read a draft the student has written, ask hard questions about it, point out where the hypothesis is untestable or the data presentation is unhelpful, and explain what the assessment criteria reward. What a tutor must not do is supply text, redraft sentences, or take the piece over, because the submission has to be the student's own work from first word to last. We state that boundary to the student in the first session. Your child's school will also have its own rules on outside help, and those should be checked and followed.

faqs.question: Where can a student in Abu Dhabi collect real fieldwork or case-study data?
faqs.answer: Several syllabus topics are observable in this emirate. A land-use transect from the older central districts out towards newer mainland communities gives genuine variation in settlement pattern and service provision. The shoreline at Al Bateen and along Al Raha Beach shows engineered coastal defence and reclaimed frontage. Mangrove channels give a conservation management angle. Al Ain offers oasis irrigation, groundwater and an inland climate record. Yas Island shows tourism pressure on a small land area. Local material only scores when it is written as process, cause and effect with measurable detail.

faqs.question: Is 0460 geography accepted as one of the five subjects for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: The British-track rule reported in July 2026 requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Whether a specific geography certificate sits inside those five is a decision for the Ministry of Education or the emirate attestation authority, and only they can confirm it for your child's certificate set. IB Gram does not perform equivalency and tutoring is not required for it. Check the current rule on moe.gov.ae before relying on anything written here.

faqs.question: How late in Year 11 can 0460 tutoring still move a geography grade?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, because two of the three components respond quickly. Paper 2 is technique and improves within weeks of deliberate practice. The extended evaluation question is a structural fix rather than a content one. What does not compress well is case-study depth across three themes, which needs months. A student starting eight weeks before a series should expect the plan to prioritise skills, command words and the evaluation question, and to accept that Theme 3 content may stay thin. That is a reasonable trade, not a failure.

faqs.question: Does a private geography tutor working with Abu Dhabi families need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published you should treat any specific amount quoted to you as unverified.

faqs.question: Can 0460 sessions move to a later slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. School hours shorten, afternoons become unworkable for concentrated study, and evening slots after Iftar suit both the student and the household. We move the weekly slot for the month rather than suspending it, because geography benefits from continuity in written practice more than from a pause. If a series falls shortly after Ramadan, the pre-exam plan is rebuilt around the shortened days instead of pretending they are normal ones, with shorter and more frequent sessions where that works better.

faqs.question: Is online geography tutoring really as good as having someone at the table?
faqs.answer: For this subject the honest answer is that it is better in one specific way and neutral in the rest. Geography teaching revolves around annotating a resource: a map extract, a graph, a photograph, a student's own paragraph. Screen sharing puts the resource, the answer and the mark scheme side by side and lets the student watch the annotation happen live, which is hard to do over a single printed page. It also widens the tutor pool from one district to a national one, which matters for a smaller subject. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What happens if no Cambridge 0460 specialist is free when we enquire?
faqs.answer: You are told at the enquiry stage, before any payment, along with what the realistic alternative is. Demand concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before each series, so a request in April for a June exam has fewer options than one made in October. The alternatives we would name are a humanities tutor with strong skills-paper experience, a start date a fortnight later with the specialist you actually wanted, or a shorter technique block instead of a weekly plan. What we will not do is quietly match a generalist and leave you to discover it in week three.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge series do Abu Dhabi schools usually enter for 0460?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and the school chooses which one its cohort sits as the exam centre. Most British-curriculum schools in Abu Dhabi enter the June series for Year 11, with November used for re-sits or for candidates who joined late. Entry deadlines sit months before the exam itself, which is why the series date has to be confirmed with the exams officer before building a revision plan. Timetables are published by zone on cambridgeinternational.org, and using the wrong zone version is a real and avoidable risk.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-geography-0460.closingBody: If you want to know whether tutoring would change your child's geography grade, the fastest test is not a conversation about the syllabus. Send the most recent marked geography paper, confirm with the school whether the third component is Paper 3 coursework or Paper 4, and book the free thirty-minute trial lesson. In that half hour a tutor marks one question with your child, names the habit costing the marks, and tells you honestly whether the gap is technique, content or structure. You get a written note afterwards. If the answer is that your child does not need regular sessions, we will say so.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-global-perspec.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives to Abu Dhabi students across all three components. The work is research coaching as much as subject teaching: questions sharpened, sources evaluated, arguments tested, and drafts read back with questions rather than corrections.

intro.heading: A subject that marks thinking, and why that is harder to teach
paragraphs: Global Perspectives does not have a body of content to learn, and that is why students who revise well can still score badly on it. There is no syllabus of facts to memorise. Cambridge assesses a set of skills instead: research, analysis, evaluation, reflection, collaboration and communication. A student is asked to take a global issue, turn it into a question that can actually be argued, find evidence from different perspectives, weigh that evidence rather than collect it, and then say what they now think and why they changed their mind. Nothing about that is revisable in the usual sense.

The assessment comes in three parts. There is a written examination built on source material supplied in the paper. There is an Individual Report of 1,500 to 2,000 words, researched and written by the student on a global topic. And there is a Team Project, which produces a collaborative outcome plus an individual Reflective Paper of 750 to 1,000 words. Two of those three are coursework, which makes 0457 unusual among the IGCSEs Abu Dhabi students take and makes the academic-honesty boundary a live question rather than a theoretical one.

Most families contact a tutor at one of two moments. The first is when a research question has been chosen and is clearly unworkable, usually because it has only one answer or because the evidence for it does not exist in English at a Year 10 reading level. The second is after a draft comes back with a comment like needs more analysis, which tells the student nothing they can act on. Both are fixable, and both are fixed by questions rather than by rewriting.

What a tutor can legitimately do on a coursework subject is narrower than on an exam subject, and it should be stated before any money changes hands. A tutor may teach research method, show what evaluation looks like on a different topic, read a draft and ask the questions a reader would ask, and point out where a claim has no support. A tutor does not contribute sentences to an assessed submission, does not edit a draft until the authorship is unclear, and does not supply sources the student has not read. That is not caution for its own sake; coursework malpractice is an expulsion risk for the student, not a service-level problem for the provider.

Delivery in the UAE is online, one-to-one, over live video with screens shared, and IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi. For this subject the format suits the work: a draft on a shared screen with a cursor moving through it, the tutor asking what the evidence for a given sentence is, is exactly the right shape for teaching 0457. Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, and because internal coursework deadlines are set by the school rather than by Cambridge, the first thing a tutor should ask for is the school's own 0457 calendar.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-global-perspec.programmesIntro: 0457 sits inside a Cambridge skills pathway that starts earlier and continues well beyond IGCSE. Knowing where a student entered it explains a lot about how comfortable they are with the research demand.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Global Perspectives
programmes.description: Three components: a written examination based on supplied sources, an Individual Report of 1,500 to 2,000 words on a global topic built around a research question, and a Team Project producing a collaborative outcome plus a Reflective Paper of 750 to 1,000 words. Assessment is of skills rather than recalled content.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, 0457 is sometimes a free-standing option and sometimes a subject the whole year group takes, which changes the teaching entirely. Where a full cohort sits it, one teacher may be supervising well over a hundred Individual Reports, and the per-student feedback a draft receives is correspondingly thin. That is the usual reason an Abu Dhabi family looks outside the school for help with this subject rather than with any other.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Global Perspectives
programmes.description: The preparatory course, built around challenges rather than assessed components. Students who followed it arrive at 0457 already used to framing questions, reading for perspective and reflecting in writing. Students who did not meet research as a taught skill until Year 10 are at a real disadvantage and need that groundwork laid rather than assumed.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school runs the Lower Secondary version, and students who moved into the emirate at the start of Year 10 frequently have no prior exposure to it at all. A tutor should establish that in the first session, because a student with three years of practice and a student with none need completely different first months.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme, Individuals and Societies
programmes.description: The nearest equivalent in the IB sector, with interdisciplinary units and an independent project in the final year. Students transferring from an MYP school into a Cambridge school part-way through Year 10 usually have the research habits and lack familiarity with the specific 0457 criteria, which is a far easier gap to close than the reverse.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a substantial IB sector alongside its Cambridge schools, and movement between the two at fourteen or fifteen is common here. A student arriving from MYP tends to over-write: their previous assessment rewarded breadth, and 0457 rewards a tight question answered with evidence.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay
programmes.description: Where 0457 pays off for students who move into an IB Diploma sixth form. The Extended Essay is a longer version of the same discipline, a research question answered with evidence and a defended conclusion, and Theory of Knowledge extends the perspective work. Students who did 0457 properly at sixteen find both less alarming at seventeen.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run a Cambridge lower school and an IB Diploma sixth form in the same building, so this transition happens inside one campus. Families planning it should treat 0457 as the rehearsal rather than as a filler subject, because the skills are the ones the Diploma will assess twice.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-global-perspec.subjectsIntro: 0457 bookings often sit alongside a second subject, usually one that shares the writing demand. The list below is what Abu Dhabi families most commonly combine with it.

subjects.description: The most useful pairing. 0457 is assessed through extended writing, and students who cannot control a paragraph lose marks on arguments they have actually understood. Directed writing work transfers straight into the Individual Report.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Many Abu Dhabi candidates sit 0510 alongside 0457, and the overlap is the reading paper's skill of identifying attitude and implication in a text. That is the same move the 0457 written paper asks for when it says identify the perspective.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Shares several 0457 topic areas, including water, population and sustainable development, and brings the case-study habit with it. A student carrying both can often reuse research for one in the other, provided nothing written is reused verbatim.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: The strongest source-handling overlap. 0470 teaches students to ask who produced a source and why, which is precisely the skill the 0457 written paper rewards and the one weaker candidates never develop.

subjects.description: Overlaps 0457 on energy, water, fisheries and natural hazards, and supplies the technical grounding that makes a sustainability-themed Individual Report credible rather than general. Useful where a student's chosen topic is environmental.

subjects.name: Sociology (0495)
subjects.description: Shares the demand for evidence-based evaluation of social issues, and its research-methods unit teaches sampling, bias and reliability explicitly. Students who have met those terms formally handle 0457 source evaluation with far more confidence.
