abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-history-0470-t.programmesIntro: History at Cambridge IGCSE is one stage in a route that usually starts in Year 7 and ends with an AS, A Level or IB Diploma choice. Each stage below carries a different cost profile for a family planning support, which is why they are set out together.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary History
programmes.description: The years where source handling and paragraph structure are either built or skipped. Schools differ widely: some teach historical enquiry from Year 7, others cover history inside a combined humanities course. A student who has never been asked to judge the reliability of a source arrives in Year 10 needing a skill the 0470 source paper assumes they already have.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the cheapest intervention a family can make is a short block of support in Year 9 rather than a panic in Year 11. Support at that stage is usually fortnightly rather than weekly, which halves the annual cost, and it buys the writing habits that the ten-mark questions pay for two years later.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE History (0470)
programmes.description: Two years covering a core content option, a depth study and a prescribed source topic. Paper 1 asks three structured questions built from four, six and ten-mark parts. Paper 2 is source analysis. The third component is either internally assessed coursework or the written Alternative to Coursework, chosen by the school. Content volume is the thing families underestimate.
programmes.countryNote: The twentieth-century core content option used by most Abu Dhabi schools includes a key question on events in the Gulf between roughly 1970 and 2000, which is the one piece of 0470 content a student living in this region often knows something about before the lesson starts. It is also the one most likely to be taught quickly at the end of the course.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level History (9489)
programmes.description: Post-16 history drops the short-answer scaffolding entirely. Answers become extended essays judged on argument, and source work becomes evaluation in depth rather than comprehension. Students who reached a 7 at 0470 by learning content and avoiding the ten-mark questions find the first AS term unpleasant. The ones who practised judgement at 0470 arrive ready.
programmes.countryNote: Not every British-curriculum school in Abu Dhabi runs A Level history every year, because cohort size decides whether the set is viable. Families who expect to continue the subject should ask in Year 10, since the answer affects both the school choice for Year 12 and whether paying for 0470 support is an investment or a one-off.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme History
programmes.description: The route at the emirate's IB schools. DP History adds a prescribed subject with source work, two world history topics, a regional option and a research assignment. The written demand is higher than at 0470 and the historiography expectation is new. Skills built on the ten-mark questions transfer directly into DP paragraph structure.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families move between British-curriculum and IB schools more often than families in most cities, because both sit within a short drive. A 0470 student who may switch for Year 12 should spend some of their support time on judgement and argument, which carry across, rather than on memorising extra content that may not.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-history-0470-t.subjectsIntro: 0470 is taught as a set of key questions plus a depth study. The grid below names the parts a tutor plans around, with the paper each is examined in and the specific thing that costs marks in it.

subjects.name: Were the peace treaties of 1919 to 1923 fair?
subjects.description: Versailles and the other settlements, the aims of the leaders, and the reaction in Germany. The ten-mark question here almost always asks how far something was fair or justified. Candidates lose marks by narrating the terms rather than judging them against a stated criterion, and by forgetting that fairness is a question about perspective.

subjects.name: To what extent was the League of Nations a success?
subjects.description: Structure, aims, the 1920s disputes, humanitarian work, and the failures of the 1930s. The reliable mark-loser is a one-sided answer: successes listed or failures listed, with no weighing. Six-mark parts want explained reasons, not a list of bodies and their functions.

subjects.name: Why had international peace collapsed by 1939?
subjects.description: Appeasement, Hitler's foreign policy, the Nazi-Soviet Pact and the road to war. Strong candidates separate long-term causes from the immediate trigger and say which mattered more. Weak ones produce a chronology. The difference is worth several marks in the ten-mark part every time.

subjects.name: Who was to blame for the Cold War?
subjects.levels: Core content and common prescribed topic · Papers 1 and 2
subjects.description: The breakdown of the wartime alliance, the conferences, Soviet expansion and American responses. This key question appears frequently as the source-paper prescribed topic as well, which doubles the value of learning it properly. Attribution of sources, not content recall, is where candidates fall short.

subjects.name: How effectively did the United States contain the spread of communism?
subjects.description: Korea, Cuba and Vietnam as case studies in containment. Marks go missing when a candidate tells the story of each conflict without ever answering how effective the policy was. The question is an assessment, and an assessment needs a yardstick stated in the first line.

subjects.name: How secure was Soviet control over Eastern Europe?
subjects.description: Hungary 1956, Czechoslovakia 1968, Solidarity in Poland and the collapse of 1989. Candidates handle the events and miss the pattern: control was maintained by force until the moment force was withdrawn. A ten-mark answer that notices that scores above one that lists uprisings.

subjects.name: Why did events in the Gulf matter, c.1970 to 2000?
subjects.description: The regional key question: oil, the Iranian revolution, the Iran-Iraq war and the 1990-91 Gulf conflict. Students in Abu Dhabi often have family memory and local context here, which helps once it is converted into dated, evidenced argument. It is also commonly taught last and therefore revised least.

subjects.name: Germany, 1918 to 1945
subjects.description: Weimar's crises and recovery, the Nazi rise to power, control and consolidation, and life under the dictatorship. The most widely chosen depth study. The ten-mark part frequently asks whether a factor was the main reason for Nazi success, which demands weighing several factors rather than describing one.

subjects.name: Russia, 1905 to 1941
subjects.description: Tsarist collapse, 1917, the civil war, Lenin's measures and Stalin's transformation. Dense with policy names that students confuse under pressure. A terminology drill is cheap and effective here, because precision on War Communism, the New Economic Policy and collectivisation is directly examinable.

subjects.name: The United States, 1919 to 1941
subjects.description: The boom, the Crash, the Depression and the New Deal. Candidates tend to be strong on the 1920s and thin on the evaluation of the New Deal, which is where the ten-mark questions concentrate. Statistics are not required; dated, specific examples are.

subjects.name: Source analysis for the prescribed topic
subjects.description: Comprehension, comparison, reliability, usefulness, purpose and the final judgement question across a set of sources on a topic that changes between series. The single biggest error is answering what the source says when the question asks why it was published. Technique here is independent of content knowledge.

subjects.name: Coursework or the Alternative to Coursework
subjects.description: The school chooses one. Coursework is a single internally assessed assignment on a depth study; the alternative is a timed written paper on the same material. Coursework spreads pressure across months and needs planning support; the written paper needs essay timing under exam conditions.

sections.heading: What an Abu Dhabi family is actually buying when they pay for a 0470 tutor
paragraphs: An hour of history tutoring is a container, and providers fill it differently. At one end, the hour is a conversation about the period with no written work produced or marked. At the other, the hour is the visible part of a cycle: the student writes a timed answer, the tutor marks it against the published level descriptors, the session is spent moving that answer up a level, and a note is written saying what to do next. Both can be sold as sixty minutes of 0470 tutoring at any price between AED 100 and AED 500.

For history the marking is not an extra, it is the product. A 0470 grade is a judgement about written answers, so the only reliable evidence that support is working is a sequence of marked answers getting better. Parents who ask for that sequence and are told it will be discussed verbally are being quoted for a cheaper service without being told. Parents who ask for it and receive it have something they can read themselves in ten minutes at half term, without needing to understand the Weimar constitution.

Five questions, each with what a straight answer sounds like and what a deflection sounds like. Used before a quote is accepted, it turns two incomparable hourly rates into a comparison of what is in the hour. It also makes the follow-up easier: a provider who promised written notes in week one can be asked for them in week four.

sections.heading: The shape of 0470: core content, a depth study, and a source paper on a prescribed topic
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE History is built from three pieces that are examined separately. The first is a core content option, in practice the twentieth-century one in most Abu Dhabi schools, taught as a series of key questions about the peace treaties, the League of Nations, the collapse of peace by 1939, the Cold War, containment, Soviet control of Eastern Europe and events in the Gulf. The second is a depth study chosen by the department, commonly Germany 1918 to 1945, Russia 1905 to 1941 or the United States 1919 to 1941. The third is source analysis on a prescribed topic.

Paper 1 draws on the core content and the depth study, with each question built from parts worth four, six and ten marks. Paper 2 is the source paper, set on a prescribed topic that Cambridge changes between series, which is why last year's revision guide can be the wrong book. The remaining component is either internally assessed coursework or the written Alternative to Coursework, and the school decides which. Weightings in the table are given in relative terms because Cambridge revises the syllabus on a cycle; read the current document on cambridgeinternational.org or ask the exams officer for the series your child sits.

Two practical consequences follow. First, a tutor needs to be teaching the same core option and the same depth study as the school, and that has to be confirmed in writing rather than assumed. Second, the prescribed topic for Paper 2 must be checked for the specific series, because source technique transfers but the content does not. Both checks are free, take one email each, and prevent the most expensive mistake available in this subject, which is paying for a term of accurate teaching about the wrong period.

sections.heading: The four, six and ten-mark pattern, and where each part leaks marks
paragraphs: The most useful thing a 0470 candidate can learn is that the three parts of a Paper 1 question want three different kinds of writing, and that writing the wrong kind is the commonest way to lose marks while knowing the material. The four-mark part asks what happened: it wants a set of separate, accurate, specific points, and it rewards nothing for explanation. Students who write a paragraph here spend five minutes earning two marks, then run short of time in the part that carries ten.

The six-mark part asks why. It wants explained reasons, each one developed into a consequence rather than named and abandoned. The distinction between a reason and an explained reason is where most of the mark difference sits, and it is teachable in a single session: a reason becomes an explanation the moment the sentence continues with because, which meant that, or with the result that. Students who learn to write two or three developed reasons rather than six undeveloped ones reliably gain marks on this part.

The ten-mark part asks how far the candidate agrees, and it is marked in levels. A one-sided answer, however accurate, sits in the lower levels. The structure that works is a paragraph supporting the statement with precise evidence, a paragraph challenging it with different precise evidence, and a short final judgement that commits to a position and says why. The judgement is not a summary. Candidates who write three sentences beginning with on balance, and then explain which factor mattered more and on what criterion, move up a level before their content knowledge changes at all.

sections.heading: The source paper: why strong students with good knowledge still lose marks
paragraphs: Paper 2 hands a candidate a set of sources on the prescribed topic and asks a sequence of questions that get progressively harder. Early questions test comprehension and comparison. Later ones test reliability, usefulness and purpose. The final question asks the candidate to use the sources to reach a judgement. The content knowledge required is real but limited; the skill required is specific and is rarely taught as its own thing in a crowded scheme of work.

The dominant error is answering what a source says when the question asks why it was produced. A cartoon published in a British newspaper in 1946 is evidence about British opinion in 1946, whoever it depicts. A speech is evidence of what a politician wanted an audience to believe. Students who have been taught to look at the attribution line before reading the source itself, and to ask who produced this, when, and for whom, start scoring on the purpose questions almost immediately.

The second error is treating reliability as a verdict rather than a question. Sources are not reliable or unreliable in the abstract; they are reliable for particular purposes. A propaganda poster is unreliable evidence of conditions and excellent evidence of what a government wanted believed. Teaching that distinction is a short piece of work with a large return, and it is the part of Paper 2 technique that transfers directly into AS and A Level or IB Diploma source work later.

sections.heading: The Gulf key question, and the content a student in Abu Dhabi should not dread
paragraphs: The twentieth-century core content includes a key question about why events in the Gulf mattered between roughly 1970 and 2000: oil and its politics, the Iranian revolution, the Iran-Iraq war, and the conflict of 1990 to 1991. For a candidate living in Abu Dhabi this is the one section of 0470 where the place names are familiar before the lesson begins, and where family memory sometimes supplies detail the textbook skips. Used properly that is an advantage on a paper where specific evidence earns the marks.

Used carelessly it is a trap. Examiners reward dated, evidenced argument, not opinion about the region, and a candidate who writes from family conviction rather than from the material can produce a confident answer that scores in the lowest level. The work in a session is to convert what the student already knows into the form the mark scheme pays for: a dated event, a named actor, a stated consequence, and a judgement about significance that could be challenged with evidence.

There is a scheduling point too. This key question commonly sits at the end of the course, which means it is taught in the weeks when the department is also running mocks and chasing coursework. In practice it is the content most often covered quickly and revised least, and a tutor working backwards from the series should check whether it has been taught at all before assuming it is secure. It appears on papers like any other key question, and a candidate who has met it for twenty minutes in April is exposed.

sections.heading: What 0470 tutoring costs in Abu Dhabi, in AED, and what moves the number
paragraphs: The figures below are published rates from other providers in the UAE market, each attributed to the provider that published it and dated October 2026, together with the rate bands in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. They describe the market, not IB Gram's charges. We do not publish a single headline rate for 0470 because the honest answer depends on format, frequency and how close the series is, and a number without those three things attached would mislead you.

Four variables move a quote in this emirate. Format comes first: an in-home visit prices travel into the hour, which is why market in-home bands sit above online bands for comparable tutors. Frequency comes second: fortnightly essay feedback across a school year costs roughly half what a weekly slot costs, and for a Year 10 student who is coping it is often the better buy. Scarcity is third, and history is a smaller subject than maths or the sciences, so a tutor who has marked 0470 answers is easier to find in a national pool than in one district. Timing is fourth, because demand concentrates in the two months before each series.

One further cost belongs in any realistic plan: exam entry itself, if your child is sitting as a private candidate rather than through their school. That is paid to the centre, not to a tutor, and it is the item families discover last. If the school is the exam centre, entry is handled inside school fees and the question does not arise. If it is not, ask early, because private-candidate entry deadlines fall months before the exam and some centres limit which components they will accept.

sections.heading: Planning 0470 support across two years without overspending
paragraphs: Most families buy history support in the wrong term. The instinct is to wait until a Year 11 report looks poor and then book weekly sessions for the final eight months, which is the most expensive version of the plan and the one with the least time to work. A cheaper sequence exists. Fortnightly essay feedback through Year 10 builds the writing habits the ten-mark questions pay for, at roughly half the weekly cost, and it surfaces the depth-study gaps while there is still a year to fill them.

The second half of the plan is a short intensive before the series rather than a long weekly commitment through it. Six to ten weeks of twice-weekly sessions, built backwards from the date the exams officer confirms, covers Paper 1 timing and Paper 2 technique while the school handles content revision. For many Abu Dhabi families this two-stage shape costs less across two years than weekly sessions from January of Year 11, and it puts the intensive work where it converts into marks.

Three further savings are worth naming. Siblings in the same household can sometimes share a slot if they sit the same depth study, though for a judgement-heavy subject one-to-one usually wins. A student who needs only source technique can buy a four-session block rather than a term. And a family that confirms the core option and depth study before the first session never pays for a term of teaching about the wrong period, which is the single largest avoidable cost in this subject.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in Abu Dhabi, and what a tutor must not do
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which the federal portal u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. One consequence matters directly to families looking for a history tutor. Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules prevent private and charter school staff from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Confirm the current wording against ADEK's own policy before relying on it; in practice, do not ask your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately.

The permit itself is a federal matter. Private tuition work permits were introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, are granted free of charge for two years, and are open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The route is MoHRE's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which shows no fee and a two working day completion time. Working without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no schedule of fines is published, any specific figure quoted to you should be treated as unverified. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and does not claim any.

Then there is the academic boundary, which matters more in history than in most subjects because so much of the assessment is written prose. A tutor may teach the period, question an argument, mark an answer against the level descriptors, and explain in detail why a paragraph sits in level two. A tutor may not supply text for a submission, rewrite a student's paragraphs, or take over a coursework assignment, because the work handed in must be the student's own throughout. We say that to the student in the first session, and your child's school will have its own rules on outside help that should be read and followed.

Four answers, and they determine everything that follows. Buying support before you have them is how families pay for the wrong period.

process.title: Send one marked history answer
process.description: A mock essay, a class assessment, or a single ten-mark answer with the teacher's comments on it. The tutor reads it against the published level descriptors before the trial lesson, so the first thirty minutes diagnose a specific writing habit instead of covering introductions.

process.description: One trial per family, no card details taken to book it. The tutor works through a single part-question with your child, marks it live, and names the level it reached and the one change that would move it up. A written note follows with a view on format, frequency and the number of sessions likely to be needed.

process.description: Fortnightly essay feedback, a weekly slot, or a pre-series intensive. For a Year 10 student who is coping, fortnightly usually buys more improvement per dirham. For a Year 11 candidate eight weeks out, the intensive is the only shape that fits. We will say which we think applies and why.

process.description: Every six to eight weeks, read the marked answers in sequence and decide whether the plan still fits. If a mock or a coursework deadline is next, the plan is rebuilt backwards from that date. If the levels have stopped moving, the format changes rather than the hours increasing.

whyPoints.description: History improves through marked written work, so a timed answer is read and annotated against the level descriptors between sessions and the session is spent on the rewrite. A quote that treats marking as optional is a cheaper service, and we would rather you knew that before comparing numbers.

whyPoints.title: The tutor teaches the option your child's school teaches
whyPoints.description: Core content option, depth study and prescribed topic are confirmed before the first paid session. Accurate teaching about the wrong period is the most expensive mistake available in this subject, and it is entirely preventable with one email to the department.

whyPoints.description: History is a smaller subject than maths or the sciences, and a tutor who has marked 0470 answers may not live near Al Reef or in Al Ain. Online delivery removes distance from the hiring problem and avoids paying the travel premium published in the in-home market bands.

whyPoints.title: Progress is written down
whyPoints.description: After each session there is a short written note in a shared folder: what was marked, what level it reached, what changes next. A parent can read a term of them in ten minutes without knowing anything about the Weimar Republic, which is the point.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for a Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 tutor in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates run roughly AED 33-65 at the budget online end, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the fee, and AED 200-450 or more for an exam-year specialist. Those are other providers' own figures, read in October 2026. The number that matters more is what the hour contains: for history, essay marking between sessions is the product. IB Gram sets its own figure in a consultation after a free thirty-minute trial, with the likely session count written down.

faqs.question: Why do two 0470 quotes in Abu Dhabi differ by three hundred dirhams an hour?
faqs.answer: Usually because they are selling different things under the same name. The cheaper hour is often a conversation about the period with no written work marked. The dearer hour normally includes a timed answer marked against the level descriptors, a written progress note, and a tutor who knows the specific depth study the school teaches. Format matters too, since in-home rates price travel into the fee. Ask five questions before comparing: marking, written notes, which option the tutor covers, cancelled slots, and whether the rate rises near the series.

faqs.question: Which depth study has my child's Abu Dhabi school chosen for 0470?
faqs.answer: Only the school can tell you, and it varies by department and sometimes by cohort. Germany 1918 to 1945, Russia 1905 to 1941 and the United States 1919 to 1941 are the most commonly taught. Send one email to the head of humanities asking for the core content option, the depth study, whether the third component is coursework or the written alternative, and which series the cohort sits. Those four answers decide what any tutor should be teaching, and buying support before you have them risks paying for a term about the wrong period.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a four-mark and a six-mark part in Paper 1?
faqs.answer: They want different writing. The four-mark part asks what happened and pays for separate, accurate, specific points with no explanation attached; a paragraph here wastes time that the ten-mark part needs. The six-mark part asks why and pays for developed reasons, where each reason continues into its consequence. Two or three explained reasons score better than six named ones. Learning to tell the two formats apart is a single session's work and it is the cheapest mark gain available in the whole syllabus.

faqs.question: How does the ten-mark how far do you agree question get marked?
faqs.answer: In levels, which is why accurate one-sided answers stall. The structure that works is a paragraph supporting the statement with precise dated evidence, a paragraph challenging it with different precise evidence, then a short judgement that commits to a position and states the criterion it is judged on. The judgement is not a summary of the two paragraphs. Candidates who adopt that shape usually move up a level before their content knowledge changes, which is why it is the first thing a session addresses in an exam year.

faqs.question: Can a 0470 tutor help if they have not taught our exact prescribed source topic?
faqs.answer: Partly, and you should know which part. Source technique is largely independent of content: reading the attribution line first, distinguishing what a source says from why it was produced, treating reliability as reliability for a stated purpose. All of that transfers to any prescribed topic. What does not transfer is the contextual knowledge needed for the final judgement question. We would rather match a tutor who covers both, and if that means a fortnight's wait for the right person we will say so at the enquiry stage.

faqs.question: Is fortnightly history tutoring enough, or does my child need weekly sessions?
faqs.answer: For a Year 10 student who is coping but not scoring, fortnightly essay feedback is often the better purchase: one timed answer written between sessions, marked against the descriptors, with the session spent on the rewrite. It costs roughly half what a weekly slot costs across a year and it starts a year earlier, which matters more. Weekly makes sense in an exam year, or where content gaps are wide enough that marking alone cannot close them. We will say which we think fits after the trial lesson.

faqs.question: When should an Abu Dhabi family start paying for 0470 support?
faqs.answer: Earlier and lighter beats later and heavier. Fortnightly support from the middle of Year 10 builds the writing habits the ten-mark questions reward and exposes depth-study gaps while there is a year left to fill them. The common pattern, waiting for a poor Year 11 report and then booking weekly sessions for eight months, is the most expensive version and the one with least time to work. The cheapest effective shape is light in Year 10 and intensive in the final two months.

faqs.question: Does the Gulf key question actually come up in 0470 exams?
faqs.answer: It is one of the key questions in the twentieth-century core content, so it can appear like any other. The practical problem for Abu Dhabi candidates is that it commonly sits at the end of the scheme of work and is therefore taught quickly and revised least. Local familiarity with the region helps only once it is converted into dated, evidenced argument: a named actor, a dated event, a stated consequence, and a judgement that could be challenged. Opinion about the region, however strongly held, scores nothing on its own.

faqs.question: Can my child's own history teacher tutor them privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also prevents serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical answer is to look outside the school for paid support, and to use the class teacher for the free help they are already paid to give.

faqs.question: Do we also have to pay exam entry fees for 0470?
faqs.answer: Only if your child is sitting as a private candidate rather than through their school. Where the school is the Cambridge exam centre, entry is handled within school fees and the question does not arise. Private candidates pay the centre directly, and the amount depends on the centre, so ask for it in writing. Entry deadlines fall months before the exam itself, and some centres limit which components they accept, so this is a question for October rather than April if a private entry is likely.

faqs.question: How do history sessions fit around an Abu Dhabi school run and after-school sport?
faqs.answer: Slots are set in Gulf Standard Time around your week rather than a tutor's time zone. Families in Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Al Reef and Shakhbout City usually take 17:30 or later because of the commute to island schools, while central districts such as Al Khalidiyah and Al Zahiyah can often start at 16:00. Weekend slots suit villa communities with long drives and work well for history, because one uninterrupted hour of writing is worth more than two interrupted half hours.

faqs.question: Will sessions move during Ramadan, and does that change the cost?
faqs.answer: The slot moves and the price does not. School hours shorten, afternoons stop being usable for sustained writing, and most families ask for a later evening slot after Iftar. We move the weekly or fortnightly slot for the month rather than suspending it, because history needs continuity in written practice more than it needs a pause. If a series falls shortly afterwards, the pre-exam plan is rebuilt around the shortened days, often as shorter and more frequent sessions rather than long ones.

faqs.question: Does paying for a tutor mean my child will get a higher history grade?
faqs.answer: No one can promise that, and anybody who does should be treated with suspicion. What tutoring can reliably provide is marked written work, feedback in the language of the level descriptors, and a plan built backwards from a confirmed exam date. Grades move when a student changes how they write, which takes weeks of practice they have to do themselves. The honest measure of whether the money is working is the sequence of marked answers: if the levels are not moving by half term, the plan should change.

faqs.question: What happens if no Cambridge 0470 specialist is available when we enquire?
faqs.answer: You are told before any payment, with the realistic options named. Demand concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before each series, so an April enquiry for a June exam has fewer choices than one made in October. The alternatives we would offer are a humanities tutor with strong source and essay-marking experience, a start date a fortnight later with the specialist who covers your exact depth study, or a short technique block instead of a weekly plan. Substituting a generalist without saying so is not one of them.

If fortnightly is enough, we will tell you that rather than sell you weekly.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each tutor profile below names the Cambridge syllabuses they teach and the components they mark. Marking matters here: a tutor who marks the work between sessions is the one who can show you why a score moved, rather than telling you that it felt better this week.

intro.heading: The difference between tuition that works and tuition that feels fine
paragraphs: Most tuition that fails does not fail noisily. The sessions happen, the student is polite about them, the tutor is encouraging, and in April the grade is where it was in October. Nobody behaved badly. What was missing was evidence: nothing was measured at the start, nothing was marked in a way anyone kept, and so nobody could tell in November that the arrangement was not working, when there was still time to change it.

That is a solvable problem, and solving it is mostly a matter of insisting on four records. The first is a baseline: a full paper or a substantial section of one, sat under timed conditions in the first week, marked, and kept. Without it there is no before, and every later claim about improvement is an opinion. The second is a run of marked answers in the student's own handwriting or typing, annotated against the mark allocation, so a parent can see what was wrong rather than being told. The third is a topic log: a one-line record per session of what was diagnosed and what was practised, which over six weeks becomes a map of the gap. The fourth is a score series from timed attempts, written down as numbers, which is the only one of the four that shows direction.

Those four records do something a weekly phone call cannot. They let a parent who does not teach Cambridge Chemistry make a judgement about whether Cambridge Chemistry tuition is working. The score series answers the question of direction. The marked answers answer the question of why. The topic log answers the question of whether the work is targeted or drifting. And the baseline makes all three comparable to something. Six weeks of that is enough to decide whether to continue, change tutor, change subject, or reduce.

Abu Dhabi families have a specific reason to care about this. The emirate's British-curriculum schools draw students from several systems, so a Year 10 cohort in Khalifa City or on the island can contain children who have had three different mathematics curricula in five years. Gaps in that situation are individual rather than typical, and a generic revision programme will miss them. The only way to find an individual gap is to mark individual work, which means the record is not administrative overhead. It is the actual mechanism.

One thing to be clear about before any of it. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. We have kept the phrase home tutor on this page because it is what parents search for, and because the honest answer to the question is about what a family actually wants from a tutor in the house, which is attention, continuity and a record. The format that produces the best record is the one where every annotated script is saved automatically rather than carried out of the door.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The evidence a parent should expect changes with the stage, because what is being measured changes. These are the four stages behind most Cambridge enquiries in Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: Lower secondary and Checkpoint years
programmes.description: Nothing is certificated at this stage, which makes the evidence question simpler: the measure is whether the student can now do, unaided, a type of question they could not do six weeks ago. Checkpoint results broken down by strand are the best baseline available and most families never ask for them.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools differ in how much Checkpoint detail they release. Requesting the strand-level breakdown before Year 10 starts gives a tutor something real to work from, and it tends to predict which IGCSE subjects will need attention two years later.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Year 10
programmes.description: The year where evidence is cheapest to act on, because entries and tiers are not yet fixed and there is time for a content gap to close. The measure here is topic coverage against the syllabus rather than paper scores, since the student has not met most of the paper yet.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 is when a tier decision is still genuinely open in Abu Dhabi schools, and a baseline paper in the autumn is the piece of evidence that makes that conversation factual rather than hopeful. By Year 11 the entry has usually been submitted.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Year 11
programmes.description: The year of timed scores. From the first mock onwards there are real numbers to track, and the useful record is a series of attempts at full components under exam timing with the marks written down. Content teaching gives way to diagnosis, and the gap between knowing and scoring becomes the whole job.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi mock seasons cluster in the autumn and again after the winter break, which gives two natural measurement points. A tuition plan that does not use them is throwing away the only independent evidence the family gets before results.

programmes.name: The step into AS, A Level or the Diploma
programmes.description: Included because the IGCSE record has a second life. A student who arrives in Year 12 with a documented history of which question types defeated them, and what fixed it, starts the harder course knowing how they fail. That is worth more than a certificate grade on its own.
programmes.countryNote: Sixth forms and Diploma programmes in the emirate commonly set subject-specific IGCSE entry grades, so the Year 11 score series is also the evidence a family needs when discussing whether a particular post-16 option is realistic.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: What counts as evidence differs by subject. These are the Cambridge syllabuses we are asked for most in Abu Dhabi, with the specific measurement that tells you whether the work is landing.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The evidence is method marks recovered. Score the same question set twice, weeks apart, and count the marks earned from working rather than from final answers. A student who gains three method marks on identical questions has changed a habit, which is the thing that transfers.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: The measure is tool selection on unseen questions, not execution. Keep a log of unfamiliar problems and record whether the student chose the right approach before any algebra. Execution improves with practice; selection improves only with teaching, so the log tells you which you are getting.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: Count distinct creditable points per answer against the mark allocation. Students with strong knowledge and weak scores are almost always making two points where four were available, and that count is a cleaner measure of progress than any percentage.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Two separate measures are needed: accuracy on quantitative work, which is arithmetic discipline, and the ability to answer unfamiliar organic questions from functional-group reasoning rather than recall. A student can improve on one and not the other, so track them apart.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Track units and full-chain calculation separately from conceptual explanation. Marked scripts here typically show a student who understands the physics and loses marks on presentation of the arithmetic, which is visible in the record long before it is visible in a grade.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Keep three score lines, one per discipline, not one average. The commonest failure in this entry is a tutor strong in two disciplines and thin in the third, and an averaged score hides it until the paper arrives. Separate lines expose it in the first month.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: The measure is task fulfilment against the prompt, point by point, rather than impressions of fluency. A rubric-based score on each writing attempt, kept in sequence, shows movement that general comments about better writing never will.

subjects.name: English First Language 0500
subjects.description: Track the ratio of analysis to narration in each response, which can be counted sentence by sentence on a marked script. Students who narrate drop into the middle bands regardless of vocabulary, and the ratio changes measurably once it is pointed out.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450 and Economics 0455
subjects.description: The evidence is whether an answer reaches a judgement. Mark each practice response for application to the stimulus and for evaluation separately; definition marks are rarely the problem, and an average score conceals which half of the paper is costing the grade.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Keep theory and problem-solving scores apart, because they move independently. For algorithm questions the measurable thing is whether another person could execute the pseudocode as written, which is a pass or fail judgement rather than an impression.

subjects.name: Accounting 0452
subjects.description: Presentation and consistency marks can be counted on every attempt, and they are the marks most often lost by students who understand double entry perfectly well. A score series split into substance and presentation shows the fix landing within a few weeks.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language 0508
subjects.description: Continuity is itself the evidence here, because tutors able to teach first-language Arabic to IGCSE standard are scarce relative to demand in the emirate. Keep the same tutor and the same marking rubric across the year so that the comparison between September and March means something.

sections.heading: The record set: what should exist after six weeks
paragraphs: Six weeks is the right horizon for a first judgement. It is long enough for a competent arrangement to produce visible change and short enough that a bad one has not cost a term. At the end of it a parent should be able to assemble four documents without asking anyone to prepare anything special, because they were produced as a by-product of the work rather than for the review.

The baseline comes first and is the one most often missing. It is a full component or a substantial section, sat under timed conditions in week one, marked and filed. Its purpose is comparison, so the paper must be kept and the marks recorded per question. The second record is the marked work itself: the student's own answers with annotations against the mark allocation, showing which points were creditable and which were not. The third is the topic log, a single line per session naming what was diagnosed, what was practised and what was set. Six lines tell you whether the work is targeted or wandering. The fourth is the score series from timed attempts, as numbers in order.

What makes this practical rather than bureaucratic is that all four are automatic in an online arrangement. The annotated script is a file that saves itself. The topic log is three sentences a tutor writes at the end of a session. The score series is a column of numbers. Nobody is producing a report; the record is the residue of doing the job properly. The table below sets out each record, who produces it, and what its absence usually means, because absence is informative. A tutor who cannot produce a baseline after six weeks did not take one, and a tutor who cannot produce marked work did not mark any.

sections.heading: Three numbers the school gives you, and what each can honestly be compared to
paragraphs: Parents in Abu Dhabi are handed several different numbers across a school year and are rarely told which ones are comparable. Treating them as interchangeable is the most common source of unnecessary alarm and of unwarranted comfort, and getting it straight costs nothing. There are three kinds, and they answer three different questions.

The first is a working-at or current grade on a school report. It is a teacher's judgement about the standard a student is operating at now, formed from classwork, and it is not the output of a marked paper. It is useful as a direction indicator and it cannot be compared to a mock percentage. The second is a mock score, which is a real mark on a real paper and is therefore comparable to other mock scores on the same paper under the same conditions. It is not comparable across schools, because the paper chosen and the timing allowed differ. The third is a predicted or forecast grade, which Cambridge requires centres to submit, and which is a professional estimate rather than a measurement.

The practical rule is to compare like with like and to insist on knowing which kind of number you are looking at. A mock percentage that has moved from 48 to 61 on comparable papers is evidence. A working-at grade that moved from a 5 to a 6 is a judgement, and a reasonable one, but it is not evidence of the same type. Where the two disagree, as they frequently do in this emirate because students arrive from different systems and classwork can flatter or understate paper performance, the marked paper is the thing to trust and the discrepancy itself is worth a conversation with the subject teacher.

sections.heading: Turning one marked paper into a plan: the error taxonomy
paragraphs: A single marked component is enough to build a term's work from, provided somebody sorts the losses into kinds rather than counting them. Six kinds cover almost everything an Abu Dhabi Cambridge student loses marks to, and they have wildly different costs to fix. Sorting the losses is the whole value of the first session, and it is the step that gets skipped when a tutor starts by asking what topic the student finds difficult.

Recall gaps are genuinely missing content and are the slowest to close, running to weeks per topic. Method omission is not writing the working, and it is close to free to fix once pointed out. Command-word mismatch is answering the wrong instruction, which takes a handful of supervised attempts. Arithmetic and precision slips respond to a mechanical discipline about rounding and units. Time allocation failures, where a student spends twelve minutes on a three-mark question and leaves a six-mark one blank, are fixed by practice against a clock rather than by teaching. And question abandonment, where the last part of every multi-step question is empty, is usually a confidence pattern rather than a knowledge one.

Sorted this way, the plan writes itself and so does the budget. A student whose losses are mostly method, timing and command words can expect visible movement in four to six weeks, because none of those require new learning. A student whose losses are mostly recall needs a term and should not be promised anything faster. A parent who knows which mix they are looking at can tell whether a quoted plan is realistic, and can ask for the mix explicitly after the first marked paper rather than accepting a general statement that the student needs to work on exam technique.

sections.heading: Six weeks, session by session, and what each one leaves behind
paragraphs: A plan that cannot say what will exist at the end of each week is not a plan. The shape below is what we run for a Cambridge IGCSE student in Abu Dhabi starting in the autumn, and it is deliberately front-loaded with measurement, because the cheapest time to discover that an arrangement is wrong is in week two.

Week one is the baseline and nothing else: a component sat under timing, marked per question, and a conversation with the student about what they thought was happening. Week two is the diagnosis session, where the losses are sorted into the six kinds and the student is told plainly which of them is costing the most. Weeks three and four take the two cheapest fixes and drill them, with narrow work set in between that can be marked properly rather than a chapter of revision. Week five takes the most expensive gap and starts the slow work on it. Week six is a second timed attempt at a comparable component, marked the same way, and then the review.

What the review compares is specific: baseline score against week-six score, and the per-question pattern rather than the total. Two attempts are not a trend, so the honest reading at week six is directional rather than conclusive, and the review says so. What it can conclude is whether the diagnosis was right, which is visible even when the total has not moved much: if the method marks are up and the recall gaps are still open, the plan is working on the right things and needs more time. If nothing has changed anywhere, the diagnosis was wrong or the arrangement is not functioning, and six weeks is the point to say so rather than the point to ask for patience.

sections.heading: What families actually want from a tutor in the house, and how live video supplies it
paragraphs: It is worth taking the home-tutor question seriously rather than deflecting it, because the instinct behind it is sound. A parent asking for a Cambridge IGCSE home tutor in Abu Dhabi usually wants four things: undivided attention for their child, a person who knows the child well enough to notice a bad week, a predictable routine in the house, and some visibility over what is happening. Those are reasonable requirements and none of them is really about geography.

What a visiting arrangement supplies well is presence and routine. What it supplies poorly, in this emirate specifically, is choice of tutor and durability of record. The choice problem is geographical: a family in Al Reef or Al Samha can realistically hire from whoever will drive out there in the evening, which may be nobody who teaches Additional Mathematics 0606 or first-language Arabic. The record problem is physical: feedback given verbally across a kitchen table and written on a paper copy that goes into a school bag is not a record anyone can audit in March.

Live video changes both without changing the attention or the routine. The tutor pool stops being the set of people within a forty-minute drive and becomes the set of people who teach that syllabus. The annotated script is a file that persists, so the six-week review has something to review. The fixed slot is easier to hold, because no session is lost to traffic on the bridge or to a tutor stuck on the island. To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address, home visits are a service we run only in India, and what we sell for the UAE is one-to-one teaching over live video with the record attached.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what is plausible over a term, and what is not
paragraphs: No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be treated with real scepticism, because the final mark depends on a paper nobody has seen and on a student's performance on one morning. What can be discussed honestly is the pattern of what tends to move and how fast, based on which kinds of loss were diagnosed. That conversation is more useful than a target, and a provider who will have it is telling you something about how they work.

The quickest movement comes from technique losses. A student who has never written method in mathematics, or who answers every explain question with a description, can show a materially different score within four to six weeks because nothing new has to be learned. Timing failures move in three or four timed attempts. These are real changes and they are also finite: once method is written, writing it twice does not help again.

Content gaps are slower and compound differently. A student missing two topic blocks in Chemistry 0620 needs those blocks taught and then retrieved over weeks, and the score often does not move at all for a month and then moves in a step. That flat month is where families cancel, which is precisely the wrong moment, and it is also why the topic log matters: it shows work happening when the score does not. The honest summary is that a term of properly diagnosed weekly work with marked practice in between, starting from a specific diagnosis rather than a general one, produces visible change in most cases and no guarantee in any of them. Anyone promising a specific grade is selling something other than teaching.

sections.heading: Mocks: what a mock grade is evidence of, and what it is not
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi schools run mocks on their own calendars, usually once in the autumn and again after the winter break, and those weeks produce the only independent measurement a family gets before results. They are extremely useful and they are routinely over-read. A mock is evidence about performance on that paper, under those conditions, on that day, marked by that teacher against whatever boundaries the school chose to apply.

Three things limit what a mock grade means. The paper is usually a past component, so a student who has already seen it is being measured on recall of the paper rather than on the syllabus. The boundaries applied are a school decision and schools differ, sometimes deliberately setting them harshly to motivate a cohort. And conditions vary: a mock sat in a classroom with the full time allowance is not the same measurement as one sat in a hall with a reduced one. None of that makes mocks unreliable. It makes them comparable to other mocks at the same school and nothing else.

What a mock is excellent for is the per-question pattern, which survives all three limitations. A script showing blanks in the last part of every multi-step question tells you something true regardless of boundaries. So does a script where the method is absent, or where the longer-response questions were answered in two lines. That is why we ask families for the mock script rather than the mock grade, and why a session in the week after mocks is worth more than three sessions in the week before them. The grade starts an argument; the script starts a plan.

sections.heading: Sharing the record with the school without starting a second argument
paragraphs: Families who hold a good tuition record often do not know what to do with it, and a few use it badly. Walking into a parent evening with a folder of a private tutor's marking and a view about the teacher's grading is a reliable way to make the next two terms harder. The record is valuable in that meeting, but as a question rather than as a challenge.

The version that works is specific and deferential about judgement. My child's timed attempts at this component have moved from this score to that one; the losses are now concentrated in the longer-response questions; does that match what you see in class? That invites the teacher's own evidence and usually produces something a parent cannot get any other way, including which topics the class has genuinely finished and which were covered quickly. It also tells the teacher that the family is engaged rather than adversarial, which affects everything from how a tier conversation goes to how quickly a concern gets raised next time.

There is one piece of the record that should always be shared, and that is a disagreement about entry or tier. If the baseline and six weeks of marked work suggest a student is entered at the wrong tier, that is a factual matter with a deadline attached and the school is the only party who can act on it. Raise it early, in writing, with the evidence attached, and ask what the school's deadline for a change is. By the spring of Year 11 that conversation is usually closed, which is the single strongest argument for having started the record in the autumn of Year 10.
bullets: Bring the record as a question about agreement, never as a challenge to grading
Ask which topics the class has finished rather than which it covered

sections.heading: When the evidence says change tutor, and when it says stop
paragraphs: A record is only worth keeping if a family is willing to act on it, and acting on it sometimes means ending an arrangement that everyone has been polite about. Three patterns in the evidence point to changing tutor. There is no marked work after four weeks, which means no diagnosis is happening and the sessions are being improvised. The topic log reads like a textbook contents page rather than like a response to a student, which means the work is not targeted. Or the student can repeat what the tutor said and cannot do the question unaided, which means the sessions are explanation without practice.

A different set of signals points to stopping rather than switching. The student is now doing the set work before the session rather than during it. Timed scores have sat at or above target across three consecutive comparable attempts. The questions in the session have changed from what does this mean to is this the best way to answer it. At that point the bottleneck is practice, and practice is something the student can do alone, far more cheaply than with a tutor present.

Tapering is usually better than stopping outright, for a practical reason specific to this market. Availability tightens sharply as a series approaches, so a family that cancels in February and tries to rebook in April will be choosing from whoever is left. Moving to fortnightly sessions while keeping a standing slot through the exam period holds the arrangement and the rate, and gives the student a place to bring a problem. We write both the stop condition and the taper into the plan at the start, which is an odd thing for a provider to do and the right thing for a parent to insist on.

process.title: Send the last marked paper, not a description of the problem
process.description: The most useful first message carries a photograph or scan of a recent marked component, the Cambridge syllabus number, the tier and the year group. A marked script tells us in ten minutes what a conversation about how your child finds the subject takes three sessions to establish, and it makes the first session a working one.

process.title: A free 45-minute trial that produces a diagnosis
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor, 45 minutes, no charge, no card details collected. It runs on your child's own work, and it ends with a written note naming the dominant kind of mark loss, whether it is technique or content, and roughly how long that takes to shift. If the honest answer is that tuition is not the purchase you need, you will be told.

process.title: A baseline component in week one, kept for comparison
process.description: Before teaching starts, the student sits a full component or a substantial section under timed conditions and it is marked per question. That paper is filed and becomes the thing every later score is read against. An arrangement without a baseline has no way of proving anything later, which is why this comes before any content.

process.title: Weekly sessions with narrow work marked in between
process.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. Work set between sessions is small enough to mark properly and is returned annotated before the next session. Nobody travels to an Abu Dhabi address; UAE delivery is online and home visits are a service we run only in India.

process.title: A written review at session six, against the baseline
process.description: At six sessions you receive the baseline score, the latest score, the per-question comparison, the topic log and a direct recommendation. Continue, change tutor, change the component being worked on, or reduce the hours. The review is written so that you can disagree with it, which is the point of writing it down.

process.title: The records stay with you
process.description: Every annotated script, the topic log and the score series belong to the family and remain available if the arrangement ends. A record that only exists inside a provider's system is not evidence a parent can use with a school, and the whole argument of this page is that the evidence is what you are buying.

whyPoints.title: A baseline before any teaching
whyPoints.description: A timed component in week one, marked per question and kept. It is the least glamorous part of the arrangement and the part that makes every later claim checkable. Most tuition that quietly fails never took one, which is exactly why nobody noticed in November that it was failing.

whyPoints.title: Marking is the product, not an extra
whyPoints.description: A tutor who marks the work between sessions arrives knowing what went wrong; a tutor who does not spends the first twenty minutes finding out, at your expense. Narrow set work that is properly marked beats a chapter of revision that is glanced at, and the annotated script is the artefact that proves either happened.

whyPoints.title: Losses sorted into kinds, with honest timescales
whyPoints.description: Method omission, command-word mismatch and timing failures move in weeks. Recall gaps take a term and go flat before they step. Saying which mix a student has, and therefore which timescale applies, is more useful than a target grade and considerably more honest.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, in writing or in conversation
whyPoints.description: The final mark depends on an unseen paper and one morning's performance. We will tell you what tends to move and how quickly for the diagnosis in front of us, and we will not attach a number to it. A provider who attaches a promised number to a term of work is making a claim about something they do not control.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: On any syllabus with a coursework or portfolio element, a tutor teaches the skill, reads a draft the student wrote and asks questions against the criteria. No text is supplied in either direction and no finished work changes hands. Academic honesty rules place the consequence on the student, which is why the boundary is published rather than implied.

whyPoints.title: A stop condition written at the start
whyPoints.description: The plan states the evidence that would make us recommend fewer hours: three stable comparable attempts at target, work started before the session, and questions that have changed character. A provider whose interest runs one way should put the other case in writing on day one.

faqs.question: What should I have to look at after six weeks of Cambridge tuition?
faqs.answer: Four things, and none of them should need preparing specially. A baseline component sat under timed conditions in week one, marked per question and kept. The student's own marked answers from each week, annotated against the mark allocation. A topic log with one line per session recording what was diagnosed, what was practised and what was set. And a score series from timed attempts, written as numbers in order. Plus a short written review at session six comparing the latest attempt to the baseline. If a provider cannot produce those after six weeks, the work that generates them did not happen.

faqs.question: Is a mock grade a reliable prediction of a final Cambridge grade?
faqs.answer: It is reliable evidence about that paper, on that day, under those conditions, marked against boundaries the school chose. It is not a prediction. Mock papers are often past components the student may have seen, boundaries are set at the school's discretion and sometimes deliberately harshly, and conditions differ between a classroom sitting and a hall sitting. What survives all of that is the per-question pattern, which is why we ask for the mock script rather than the mock grade. Blanks at the end of every multi-step question tell you something true no matter how the paper was graded.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether tuition is actually working?
faqs.answer: Compare comparable things and look at the per-question pattern rather than the total. Two timed attempts at similar components, marked the same way, six weeks apart, will show whether the diagnosed losses have reduced even when the overall score has barely moved. If method marks are up and recall gaps are still open, the plan is working on the right things and needs more time. If nothing has changed anywhere in the pattern, either the diagnosis was wrong or the sessions are not functioning, and six weeks is the point to say so.

faqs.question: Why does my child's school report say one grade and the mock say another?
faqs.answer: Because they measure different things. A working-at or current grade is a teacher's judgement formed from classwork; a mock percentage is a mark on a timed paper. A student who contributes well in class and performs poorly under timing will show exactly this gap, and so will a quiet student who is better on paper than in discussion. In Abu Dhabi the mismatch is common because students arrive from several different systems. Where the two disagree, trust the marked paper for paper performance, and treat the discrepancy itself as a question worth asking the subject teacher.

faqs.question: Should I show the tutor's notes to my child's teacher?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a question rather than as a challenge. Saying that timed attempts have moved from one score to another, that the remaining losses sit in the longer-response questions, and asking whether that matches what the teacher sees in class, usually produces information a parent cannot get any other way, including which topics the class has genuinely finished. Arriving with a private tutor's marking and a view about the school's grading tends to make the next two terms harder. The one exception is a suspected wrong tier, which is factual, has a deadline and should be raised formally and early.

faqs.question: How much grade movement is realistic in one term?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what kind of losses were diagnosed, and no honest answer attaches a number. Technique losses move fastest: a student who never writes method, or who answers explain questions with descriptions, often shows a materially different score within four to six weeks because nothing new has to be learned. Timing failures move in three or four timed attempts. Content gaps are slower, frequently showing no movement for a month and then moving in a step. Anyone promising a specific grade for a specific term is making a claim about an unseen paper and one morning's performance.

faqs.question: Can I see the marked work rather than a summary?
faqs.answer: You should insist on it. A summary is somebody's account of evidence; the annotated script is the evidence. On an online arrangement the annotated file saves itself, so there is no administrative reason for a parent not to have it, and a provider who offers summaries instead is usually not marking in enough detail to show you. Ask for the scripts with the marks recorded per question, since a single percentage tells you the size of the problem and nothing about its shape, and shape is what a plan is built from.

faqs.question: My child says the sessions go well but the marks have not moved. What now?
faqs.answer: Check one specific thing: can the student do the question unaided, cold, a week later? Sessions that feel good and produce nothing are usually explanation without practice. The student follows the tutor's reasoning in real time, which is genuinely pleasant, and has no independent route to the answer afterwards. The fix is narrow set work that is marked properly and a re-test of the same question type two weeks later. If a tutor has set nothing markable in four weeks, that is a change-tutor signal rather than a reason to wait another month.

faqs.question: Do you record the lessons?
faqs.answer: The artefact we keep as standard is the annotated script and the written session note, not a video of the hour. Where a family wants a session recorded, we agree it in advance, in writing, with a stated purpose and a stated retention period, because recordings of a minor are personal data and the UAE's personal data protection law makes that a question of consent and purpose rather than of convenience. What is more useful in practice is the marked work: a student revising in April gets more from twenty annotated scripts than from twenty hours of video they will never rewatch.

faqs.question: How many timed papers should a Year 11 student sit before the exams?
faqs.answer: Enough that the number is a series rather than an anecdote, and spaced so that each one can be acted on. A fortnightly full component from the start of the spring term, marked per question and returned before the next one, gives six or seven data points and six or seven chances to change something. Sitting a paper a week sounds more serious and usually means none of them is marked properly or acted upon. The exit condition we use is three consecutive comparable attempts holding at or above target, which is the point to reduce the hours.

faqs.question: What does it mean if a tutor never sets written work?
faqs.answer: It means there is no diagnosis, and without diagnosis the session has to begin by guessing what went wrong. Marking is where a tutor finds out that a student understands the chemistry and loses the marks on arithmetic, or knows the content and answers the wrong command word. A tutor who teaches for an hour and sets nothing is producing an experience, which a student may enjoy, rather than evidence anybody can audit. Four weeks with no markable work set is the clearest signal in this list that the arrangement needs changing.

faqs.question: Is it worth changing tutor in the middle of the year?
faqs.answer: Yes, where the evidence says so, and the cost of changing is lower than families fear if a record exists. A new tutor handed a baseline, a run of marked scripts and a topic log starts from the diagnosis rather than from scratch, which is most of the reason to keep those records in the first place. The signals that justify a change are no marked work after four weeks, a topic log that reads like a textbook contents page, and a student who can repeat the explanation but cannot answer the question unaided.

faqs.question: Does a Cambridge IGCSE home tutor in Abu Dhabi come to the house?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We do not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address, because home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. The visiting market in this emirate does exist and published rates for it run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, depending on distance. What that market cannot reliably supply to an outer community such as Al Reef or Al Samha is a specialist in a scarce syllabus, or a record you can still read in March.

faqs.question: Can a tutor correct my child's coursework draft for them?
faqs.answer: No, and you should not want one who will. On any syllabus with a coursework or portfolio element the folder must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain what each criterion rewards, read a draft the student has written and ask questions about where an argument does not follow. A tutor may not supply wording or hand back a rewritten version. Academic honesty rules place the consequence of submitted work that is not the candidate's own on the student, so good feedback arrives as questions the student answers themselves.

faqs.question: What evidence should a trial lesson produce?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis, not a sales impression. Our trial runs 45 minutes, free, with no card details collected, on your child's own marked work rather than a generic test, and it ends with a note naming the dominant kind of mark loss, whether that loss is technique or content, and roughly how long it takes to shift. Ask any provider for the same thing. A trial that produces nothing in writing has told you only that your child can sit through an hour, which was not in doubt.

intro.heading: Sixty per cent of this grade is produced at a keyboard, under time
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE ICT is assessed by one theory paper and two practical papers, and the practical papers together carry more of the grade than the theory does. That single fact ought to shape every hour of preparation, and in most households it shapes none of it. Students revise the theory because revision is what revision guides are for, then sit two and a half hours at a computer on each practical paper and lose marks for things no amount of reading addresses: a missing candidate detail, a file saved under the wrong name, a spreadsheet function that works but was not the function asked for.

So the work on this page is deliberately unglamorous. A session is mostly the student at the keyboard, sharing their screen, producing an actual file against an actual task, under time, while a tutor watches and says very little. Then the file is marked against the published criteria, the lost marks are named, and the task is repeated the following week with the same fault watched for. That is how a practical mark moves. It does not move by being explained.

Families looking for a Cambridge IGCSE ICT 0417 tutor in Abu Dhabi often describe the problem as speed. The student knew how to do everything and ran out of time. That is usually accurate and usually incomplete. Running out of time in these papers is a symptom of hesitation, and hesitation comes from not having done the same operation enough times to do it without thinking. The cure is repetition with a stopwatch, which is why the record of marked tasks matters more here than almost anywhere else in the IGCSE curriculum.

The second thing a family should know is that the evidence requirements are themselves examined. Candidates produce an evidence document alongside their files, and marks depend on that document containing what it should, with the candidate's own details present where they are required. Students lose real, recoverable marks to this every series. It feels like administration and it is worth as much as a topic.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; in-home work is an India-only service. For 0417 this is the format the subject was waiting for. The examination is performed on a computer, so the natural classroom is two screens showing the same thing, one of them being driven by the student while the other watches the cursor hesitate.

Read the sections below alongside your child's own marked practical work rather than on their own. Each one takes a part of the examination, says what it rewards, names how the marks are lost, and says what a session does about it. If you have the component split from a mock, the two sections that matter will be obvious within a minute, and the rest can wait until they become relevant.

programmes.description: The year to build fluency while there is time to repeat things.
