sections.heading: What a 0417 tutor actually does with the hour
paragraphs: The job is to make common operations automatic and to make evidence requirements habitual. Those two things account for most of the recoverable marks in Cambridge IGCSE ICT. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, the student shares their screen and does the work while the tutor watches, and the files produced are marked against the published criteria. The first session is free.

It is worth describing what that looks like minute by minute, because it is unlike a conventional lesson. Five minutes reading the last marked task and naming the faults. Ten minutes on a worked demonstration if a new operation is needed. Then thirty minutes with the student driving, under time, while the tutor stays quiet and notes every hesitation and every wrong turn. The last fifteen minutes are spent marking it together, with the student finding their own errors first against the criteria.

The quiet thirty minutes are the part that works and the part families sometimes find uncomfortable in a trial lesson. A tutor who talks for most of an ICT session produces a student who understands the operation and still cannot perform it at speed in an examination room. Marks here come from performance, so performance has to occupy the hour. If you sit in on a trial, that silence is a good sign rather than a bad one.

What a tutor cannot do is promise a grade, and in this subject there is a second boundary worth stating: the files submitted for assessment must be the candidate's own work, produced by them. A tutor demonstrates, explains and marks. Anything a candidate submits has to have been typed by the candidate, and a provider who offers otherwise is offering something that puts the qualification at risk.

sections.heading: Three components, and where the grade really sits
paragraphs: The current 0417 syllabus has one theory paper and two practical papers. The theory paper runs an hour and a half and carries the smaller share of the grade. The two practical papers run two and a half hours each and between them carry the larger share. One covers document production, databases and presentations; the other covers spreadsheets and website authoring.

The arithmetic of that distribution is the most useful thing a parent can take from this page. A student who spends four evenings a week with a revision guide and none at a keyboard is preparing for the smaller part of the grade. A student who can produce a mail-merged document, build a database query and report, construct a nested spreadsheet formula and author a styled web page, all without hesitating, is preparing for the larger part. Both matter; only one of them is usually being practised.

The practical papers are taken on a computer, with source files supplied by the examination and an evidence document produced alongside the work. That changes what preparation means. It is not enough to know how to apply a conditional format; the candidate has to find the file, name it as instructed, apply the format, evidence that they did so, and have their own details present where the task requires. Each of those steps is markable and each is losable.

Confirm the component structure, timings and weightings for your child's exam year on the Cambridge International website. This syllabus has been revised and older guides describe a different arrangement, which is a real source of confusion in households revising from second-hand material.

sections.heading: The evidence document, and the marks that are lost before any work is judged
paragraphs: Every series, candidates lose marks on the practical papers for reasons that have nothing to do with their competence with the software. A printout or screenshot without the candidate's own details on it cannot be credited to them. A file saved with a different name from the one the task specified may not be found. Evidence of a step that was genuinely performed, but never captured, is evidence that does not exist as far as the marking is concerned.

This is the cheapest cluster of marks in the whole syllabus to recover, and the one most preparation ignores because it feels like administration rather than learning. It is not administration; it is a stated requirement of the task, and it is marked. Treating it as part of the content is the single change that most reliably moves a borderline candidate up.

The way to install it is mechanical and slightly boring. Every practical task in every session is submitted the way it would be in a centre: correct filename, candidate details present where required, evidence captured as the task asks, nothing omitted because it is obvious. A tutor who marks the task and ignores those requirements is training the student to lose those marks in June. A tutor who refuses to credit a task missing them is doing the student a favour.

Within a term this becomes habit and stops costing anything. The marked-task record makes the progress visible in a satisfying way: a column that starts with several evidence faults per task and reaches zero, and then stays at zero through a full timed paper, which is the moment it can be trusted under pressure.

sections.heading: Where practical marks vanish, and what fixes each one
paragraphs: The failure modes in these papers are specific enough to be listed, which makes them trainable. The largest is hesitation: a student who knows how to build a query but has to think about where the option lives loses thirty seconds, forty times, and runs out of paper rather than out of knowledge. The fix is repetition of the same operation until the hand moves before the mind does.

The second is the plausible wrong answer. A spreadsheet formula that returns a number is not necessarily the formula the task asked for, and relative referencing copied down a column where absolute referencing was required produces output that looks fine and is wrong from row two onwards. These are caught by checking against the task wording rather than by looking at the result, and that checking habit has to be taught explicitly.

The third is instruction drift. The practical tasks are issued as precise written requirements, often with several conditions in one sentence, and a candidate who delivers four of the five conditions has produced an impressive piece of work that scores poorly. A thirty-second re-read of the task after finishing recovers these marks reliably, and almost nobody does it unless they have been trained to.

The fourth is environment: a student who has practised on one application version all year and sits the paper on another in the school's practical room. Menus move. Functions are named differently. It is worth asking the school which versions its examination machines run, and rehearsing the last few weeks on those rather than on whatever is convenient at home.

sections.heading: Why a shared screen is the right classroom for this subject
paragraphs: Most subjects make the case for online tutoring on convenience. ICT makes it on fit. The examination is performed at a computer, so a lesson in which both people watch the same screen while one of them drives is a closer rehearsal of the real thing than sitting side by side at a kitchen table with a textbook ever was.

There are four specific advantages. The tutor sees the cursor, which means they see hesitation — the pause before the right menu, the second attempt at the same option — and hesitation is the signal that an operation is not yet automatic. The tutor can take control briefly to demonstrate and then hand it straight back, which keeps the student's hands on the keyboard. The files produced exist as files, so they can be marked properly rather than glanced at. And the whole session can be run on the student's own machine with the applications they will be rehearsing on.

The format also removes a genuine obstacle in this emirate. The specialist you want for 0417 is someone who has marked practical work against the criteria and knows how the evidence requirements are applied, and that is a narrow group. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address, since in-home work is an India-only service, so the question becomes which specialist is free rather than which one is willing to drive to Al Shamkha on a Tuesday.

One practical requirement: the student needs a computer with the right applications, not a tablet, and a connection stable enough for screen sharing. Families planning a shared household machine around session times is a small logistical conversation that is much better had in week one than in week six.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of marked tasks: what you see and when
paragraphs: Because practical marks move through repetition, the record of what was produced each week is the most informative thing a family can hold. Below is the shape of a twelve-week block for a Year 11 candidate whose theory marks were acceptable and whose practical papers were incomplete at the mock.

The sequence is deliberate. Component drilling first, because speed has to exist before a full paper is worth attempting. A full paper in the middle, to find out what breaks under the real time limit. Then alternating repair and full papers, with the evidence-fault count tracked separately from the content marks, because those two improve at different rates and a family should be able to see both.

What usually surprises parents is the order of improvement. Evidence faults disappear first, often within three weeks, because they are rules rather than skills. Spreadsheet and database accuracy improves next. Completion — actually finishing the paper in the time available — comes last, because it depends on everything else already being automatic. A block that looks stalled in week six is frequently a block where the first two have moved and the third has not yet.

Every marked task carries a date, a mark against the criteria, a one-line cause for each lost mark and the evidence-fault count. If after six tasks none of those three measures has moved, that is a reason to change tutor or change approach, and the record is there so the decision belongs to you rather than to anybody's reassurance.

sections.heading: ADEK, the mandatory subjects, and what an ICT grade is worth
paragraphs: Parents sometimes ask whether ICT is taken seriously by universities. The honest answer is that it depends entirely on the course, and that the question is better asked of the admissions pages of the three or four institutions a family actually has in mind than of a tutoring site. For applied, business and information-systems routes it is directly relevant. For a degree that wants mathematics and physics, it is a supporting subject rather than a qualifying one, and no tutor should pretend otherwise.

What is published and specific is the equivalency rule. For the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. An ICT grade can be one of the five; whether a particular university counts it towards a particular course is a separate question, and one ranking competitor in this market publishes the wrong subject count altogether.

In the emirate itself, private schools are supervised by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which handles licensing and accreditation for Abu Dhabi. Dubai's authority is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education covers Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a reminder of how much sits at emirate level rather than federal.

Alongside the Cambridge options, private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and the content of those subjects is prescribed, so the material has to come from the school. That is real timetable space and belongs in any revision plan that expects to be followed. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education or Cambridge International, performs no part of the equivalency process, and tutoring is not a requirement for any of it.

faqs.question: How is Cambridge IGCSE ICT 0417 assessed?
faqs.answer: One theory paper and two practical papers. The theory paper runs an hour and a half and carries the smaller share of the grade. The practical papers run two and a half hours each: one covers document production, databases and presentations, the other spreadsheets and website authoring, and between them they carry more of the grade than the theory does. Practical papers are taken at a computer with supplied source files and an evidence document produced alongside. Confirm the current weightings for your child's exam year on the Cambridge International website.

faqs.question: My child revises hard but the practical papers come back unfinished. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost always hesitation rather than ignorance. A student who knows how to build a database query but has to think about where the option lives loses thirty seconds, repeatedly, and runs out of paper rather than out of knowledge. Revision does not fix this because reading about an operation is not performing it. The fix is repetition of the same operation against a stopwatch until the hand moves before the mind does, which usually takes three or four weeks per practical area.

faqs.question: What is the evidence document and why do candidates lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: It is the record a candidate produces alongside their files to show the steps they performed. Marks depend on it containing what the task asked for, with the candidate's own details present where required. Every series, students lose marks for work they genuinely did but never captured, for files saved under the wrong name, and for printouts that cannot be attributed to them. It feels like administration and it is examined content, which makes it the cheapest cluster of marks in the syllabus to recover.

faqs.question: Can practical ICT skills really be taught over video?
faqs.answer: This is the subject where online delivery fits best rather than worst. The examination is performed at a computer, so a session where both people watch the same screen while the student drives is a direct rehearsal. The tutor sees the cursor hesitate, can demonstrate briefly and hand control straight back, and the files produced can be marked properly. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; in-home work is an India-only service, so every Abu Dhabi session runs on screen.

faqs.question: Does it matter which version of the software we practise on?
faqs.answer: It matters in the final weeks. Practical papers are sat on the centre's own machines with the centre's own installed applications, and menus and function names differ between versions. A student who has spent a year on one version and meets another in the examination room loses time finding things. Ask the school which versions its practical rooms run, and rehearse the last month on those. Earlier in the course, practising on whatever is available at home is perfectly reasonable.

faqs.question: Should my child take ICT or Computer Science?
faqs.answer: ICT is examined mostly through practical work with applications; Computer Science is examined entirely in writing, on algorithms, programming logic and systems theory. Students who enjoy building things with software often dislike debugging, and the reverse. The reliable way to choose is two sessions, one task of each kind, in Year 9 before the option block closes. That costs a fraction of a Year 11 rescue and informs the decision with the most money attached to it.

faqs.question: How much does ICT tutoring cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates collected in October 2026 put budget and university-student online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to 300, specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in. Monthly packages advertised in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' own published figures, not IB Gram's price list; ours is discussed after the trial.

faqs.question: My child's spreadsheet answers look right but still lose marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually referencing. A formula using relative references, copied down a column where absolute references were needed, returns a number in every row and the wrong number from the second row onwards. It looks finished and it is not. The same applies to a function that works but was not the function the task specified. The habit that catches both is checking the formula against the task wording rather than against the output, and it has to be taught explicitly because it is counter-intuitive.

faqs.question: How many marked tasks before we can tell whether this is working?
faqs.answer: Six, and read three measures rather than one. Evidence faults per task usually fall to zero within three weeks because they are rules. Component accuracy moves next. Completion under time moves last, because it depends on everything else already being automatic. A block that looks flat in week six is often one where the first two measures have moved and the third has not yet. If none of the three has moved after six tasks, change something.

faqs.question: Is ICT taken seriously by universities?
faqs.answer: It depends on the course, and the question belongs to the admissions pages of the specific institutions your family has in mind. For applied, business and information-systems routes it is directly relevant. For degrees built on mathematics and physics it is a supporting subject rather than a qualifying one. For UAE equivalency, the published British-track rule asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 plus an Advanced Level qualification, and an ICT grade can be one of the five.

faqs.question: Who is permitted to teach private lessons in the UAE, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Private tuition operates under a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service for private tutor licensing. Ask any tutor whether they hold it. Working without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Could my child's own ICT teacher tutor them privately instead?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi that is a problem rather than a convenience. Professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the private tuition permit also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours need the permit. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document before relying on any summary, including this one.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with files that will be submitted?
faqs.answer: Demonstrate an operation, explain why the task wants it a particular way, mark the finished work against the criteria, and set the next task. What a tutor must not do is produce any part of what the candidate submits. Everything assessed has to have been typed by the student. A straightforward audit for a parent is to ask your child to repeat one operation from the session unaided; a coached student can, and a student whose work was done for them cannot.

faqs.question: We only have one family computer. Does that cause problems?
faqs.answer: It is manageable with a little planning and it causes real friction if ignored. Your child needs a computer rather than a tablet, with the relevant applications installed and a connection stable enough for screen sharing, for the whole session. Practical fluency is built by repetition between sessions too, so twenty minutes of keyboard practice on three evenings a week needs a slot on the household machine. Agreeing that in week one saves a frustrating conversation in week six.

faqs.question: My child joined an Abu Dhabi school mid-course. What should we check first?
faqs.answer: Which practical areas the previous school had already covered, and which application versions they used. Mid-course arrivals commonly have a solid half of the practical syllabus and a complete gap in the other half, and no school timetable has room to revisit it. The first two sessions should be a timed task from each practical area to find the gap rather than teaching anything. That diagnostic is also the cheapest hour a late-joining family will spend.

faqs.question: What if no 0417 specialist is free at the time we want?
faqs.answer: You will be told rather than quietly matched with a general tutor. ICT practical marking is a narrower specialism than it looks, because it needs somebody who applies the evidence requirements the way a centre does. The realistic options are a waiting slot, a different time of day, or a weekend session long enough for a full practical paper, which many families end up preferring anyway. A non-specialist match would cost you the term and gain your child very little.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-ict-0417-tutor.closingHeading: Send the files, not a description
abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-ict-0417-tutor.closingBody: If your child has files from a recent practical attempt, send those. A specialist can usually see from the work itself whether the problem is speed, referencing, instruction reading or missing evidence, and those four need four different months. Take the free trial, ask for a timed practical task produced by your child with their screen shared and marked inside the hour, and keep what comes back. Sessions run one-to-one over live video to Abu Dhabi in Gulf Standard Time, and the record of evidence faults, accuracy and completion is yours to read every week.

intro.heading: Why a 0607 plan should produce paper, not reassurance
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 is the syllabus chosen by a particular kind of school: one that wants its students to use a graphics display calculator as a mathematical tool, to meet an investigation as a formal assessment, and to move into an International Baccalaureate Diploma or an international sixth form without a jolt. In Abu Dhabi it is most often found in schools running the IB continuum alongside, or instead of, a British curriculum. That context matters, because it changes what a parent can check.

The problem families run into is that the usual signals are unreliable on this syllabus. A school report gives a predicted grade, which is a judgement made from several pieces of evidence that you have never seen. A mock mark gives one number from one sitting, which may have been Paper 2 on a bad morning. Neither tells you whether your child is losing marks because of the mathematics, because of the calculator, because of how the answer was written down, or because the investigation paper asked for something unfamiliar. Those four causes have completely different fixes and completely different timescales.

So the arrangement on this page is built around producing evidence rather than producing confidence. The first week is a baseline: your child sits work drawn from each of the three component types, and it is marked against the published scheme, question by question. The output is a short written diagnosis that assigns every lost mark to a category. Nothing is taught in that week beyond what the marking reveals, because teaching before diagnosis is how a term disappears into topics the student already knew.

After that the pattern is fortnightly. Work is set, written out under time, marked, and added to a running record. Every two weeks you get a note that says which topics moved, which did not, and what the next fortnight will do about it. The note is deliberately short and deliberately specific. A parent should be able to read it in two minutes and know whether to carry on paying. Where the record says a plan is not working, we say so rather than wait for the series to say it for us.

One practical point about delivery. Lessons for Abu Dhabi families are taught one to one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, around the school week. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service offered only in India. For 0607 that arrangement is the useful one: this is a minority syllabus in the emirate, the number of teachers who have actually taught the investigation component is small, and matching by subject rather than by driving distance is what puts one of them in front of your child.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-international-.programmesIntro: 0607 is usually chosen because of where it leads. Schools that run it tend to be planning for an international sixth form rather than a British one, and the programmes below are the ones that appear in the same conversation when an Abu Dhabi family asks what the grade is for.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
programmes.description: A Cambridge IGCSE assessed by a short-answer paper taken without a calculator, a structured paper taken with one, and an investigation component. A graphics display calculator is treated as part of the mathematics rather than as an aid, and candidates are entered at Core or Extended. The exact components for a given series are set out in the current syllabus, which is the document to check before buying revision material.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi this syllabus clusters in schools with an international outlook, several of which also offer the IB Diploma. That makes the department small, and it makes a transferring student's prior experience the first thing to audit: a child arriving from a 0580 class has met most of the content and none of the calculator expectations.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The more widely entered Cambridge maths IGCSE, with Core and Extended tiers and no investigation component. The content overlaps substantially with 0607, which is why families assume the two are interchangeable for revision purposes. They are not: a 0580 past paper trains none of the calculator work and none of the investigative writing that 0607 assesses.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools in the emirate enter 0580 or the Pearson equivalent, so a student moving between Abu Dhabi schools mid-course can change syllabus without changing subject. The marked baseline exists partly to find out which of the two sets of habits a new student actually has.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: The programme that precedes 0607 in many international schools, assessed against criteria including knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students arriving in 0607 from the Middle Years Programme are often strong at investigation and less practised at the timed, non-calculator precision the short-answer paper demands.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a substantial Middle Years Programme population, and the transition into an examined syllabus in Year 10 is a recognisable pressure point. The baseline marking usually shows it clearly: good investigative writing, thin accuracy under time.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The Diploma route that most closely matches the habits 0607 builds, with technology used throughout and statistics carrying real weight. The exploration written across the two years is the student's own work from first draft to final submission, and the course rewards the modelling instincts an investigation component has already started to develop.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi family is choosing between the two Diploma maths routes, 0607 experience is relevant evidence but not a decision. The school's own guidance on Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation should lead, and university subject requirements should be checked directly rather than assumed.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-international-.subjectsIntro: The grid below is the 0607 content as it appears in a marked record. For each area, the entry says what the script usually shows when marks are going missing there, because that is the form in which a parent meets the syllabus.

subjects.name: Number and accuracy
subjects.description: Standard form, upper and lower bounds, ratio and percentage change. On a marked script this area shows up as answers correct to the wrong degree of accuracy, or bounds calculated in the right way and then combined the wrong way round in a division.

subjects.name: Algebra and manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving, including work without a calculator. The record almost always shows the same thing: method secure, sign errors frequent, and a noticeable drop in accuracy on the paper where the calculator is not available.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Function notation, domain and range, asymptotes, and reading features from a displayed graph. Losses cluster around describing a feature rather than stating it, and around giving a value read from the calculator screen without the accuracy the question asked for.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradients, midpoints, parallel and perpendicular lines, and equations of straight lines. This area is usually solid in the record. Where marks go, they go on questions that require the equation in a specified form rather than any correct equivalent.

subjects.name: Geometry and reasoning
subjects.description: Angle properties, congruence, similarity and circle theorems. The script shows the answer reached and the reason omitted. Marks here are attached to naming the property used, and students who were never required to write reasons simply do not write them.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Area, surface area, volume, arcs, sectors and compound shapes. Errors are rarely conceptual. They are substitution slips, a radius used where a diameter was given, and units left off a final answer in a question that specified them.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled work, the sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems. The record usually separates into two causes: a diagram never drawn, and a calculator in the wrong angle mode producing a plausible number that attracts no suspicion.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, combining transformations and describing them fully. A full description needs every parameter, so a rotation stated without a centre and a direction loses marks even where the image drawn on the grid is perfectly correct.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree diagrams and conditional cases. On the script this shows as a tree drawn correctly and then read along the wrong branch, or as probabilities multiplied where the question described events that were not independent.

subjects.name: Statistics and data
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, scatter diagrams and correlation. Marks are available for interpretation as well as calculation, and the record shows students who compute a statistic accurately and then write nothing about what it means.

subjects.name: Sets and logic
subjects.description: Set notation, Venn diagrams and problems requiring regions to be identified from a description. Losses come from notation rather than reasoning: the right region shaded and the wrong symbol written, or an intersection and a union confused under time pressure.

subjects.name: Investigation and modelling
subjects.description: Working from a pattern or a situation towards a generalisation, with the reasoning written out. This is the area where a marked script is most revealing, because students who can see the pattern often lose most of the marks available for explaining how they saw it.

sections.heading: What a marked 0607 script shows that a report grade cannot
paragraphs: A predicted grade is a conclusion. A marked script is the data behind one. The difference matters because the actions available to a family are all specific: practise bounds, stop reading the calculator screen to two figures, write the reason next to the angle, draw the diagram before starting the trigonometry. None of those actions can be deduced from a letter on a report, and no amount of discussion with a tutor substitutes for seeing where the pen stopped.

This is also the only honest way to answer the question every Abu Dhabi parent asks in the first message, which is whether tutoring will make a difference. The truthful answer depends on which of four things is happening, and nobody can know which without reading a script. A student losing marks on content needs teaching. A student losing marks on calculator handling needs a fortnight of drills. A student losing marks on presentation needs the mark scheme shown to them once. A student losing marks on reading the question needs a slower start, not more mathematics.

The table sets out what each kind of evidence can and cannot settle. It is worth reading before the first session, because it also tells you what to send: the scripts, not the report. Where a school does not return marked papers, the next best thing is your child working a released paper at home under time, which produces the same evidence a fortnight earlier than waiting for the next internal assessment.

One caution about this approach. A record only has value if it is read, and the discipline of reading it is the parent's rather than the tutor's. Families who look at the fortnightly note and ask about the trend get a much better return on the same hours than families who file it. The note is kept short for exactly that reason.

sections.heading: The baseline: one week, three component types, one diagnosis
paragraphs: The first week does not teach. It measures. Your child sits short-answer work without a calculator, structured work with one, and a piece of investigative work, each under time and each drawn from released material. The tutor marks all of it against the published scheme wording rather than against a general sense of what a good answer looks like, and then writes two pages: what was lost, where, and which of four causes was responsible.

Splitting the baseline across component types is the point of it. A student can be strong with a calculator and weak without one, which the structured paper will never reveal on its own. A student can handle both written papers and have no idea what an investigation is asking for, which no amount of algebra practice addresses. Averaging these into a single mark, which is what a mock does, destroys exactly the information a family needs.

Parents sometimes ask whether this is a wasted week when the series is approaching. In February, with a June entry, it is the opposite: the week spent measuring is what stops the following eight being spent on topics the student already knew. The one situation where we would shorten it is a student four weeks from a paper, where we would mark a single existing script instead and start work the same day.

What you receive at the end of the baseline is specific enough to act on without us. Several families have taken the diagnosis to the school's head of maths and arranged support internally, which is a perfectly good result. The evidence belongs to you, and it is more useful than anything we could say about our own teaching.

sections.heading: The four categories every 0607 loss falls into
paragraphs: Over enough marked scripts, lost marks on this syllabus sort into four families. Content means the student does not know or cannot do the mathematics. Technology means the mathematics is understood but the calculator has been used, read or trusted incorrectly. Presentation means the answer is right and does not earn the marks, because a reason, a unit, a form or an accuracy requirement was missing. Reading means the student answered a question that was not asked.

The reason for insisting on this taxonomy is that the four have different costs. Presentation errors are the cheapest to fix and often the largest single block of marks on a first baseline. Reading errors respond to a procedural change, usually underlining the instruction and the accuracy requirement before starting. Technology errors take a concentrated fortnight. Content gaps take as long as they take, and they are the only category where the honest answer to how long is sometimes longer than the time available.

A family that knows the split can also judge the plan. If a baseline shows the majority of losses in presentation and reading, a programme of new topic teaching is the wrong purchase, and anyone selling you one should be asked why. If the losses are genuinely content, then hours matter and the realistic gain over eight weeks is smaller than parents hope. Either way the conversation is about the record rather than about anybody's confidence.

The table gives the four categories with what each looks like on a page, so you can run the first pass yourself on any marked paper your child brings home. It is not difficult. The mark scheme wording tells you what was being rewarded, and the gap between that and what your child wrote is the category.

sections.heading: Why a higher mark does not always move the grade
paragraphs: Families are often disappointed by the first set of evidence for a reason that is arithmetic rather than educational. Marks move continuously and grades move in steps. A student who gains several marks across a paper has genuinely improved and may still be inside the same grade band, because the gain landed in the middle of a band rather than at its edge. The record shows the progress; the report does not yet.

This cuts the other way too. A student sitting just below a boundary can cross it with a very small gain, which makes the cheap categories disproportionately valuable late in the year. Where a baseline shows a block of presentation losses on a student whose predicted grade is one step below their target, fixing presentation is the highest-value work available, and it can be done in a fortnight. That is a specific, checkable claim, and it is the one piece of good news the evidence often contains.

What nobody can do is tell you where the boundary will fall. Grade thresholds are set after the series by the board, on the papers actually sat, and they vary. Any tutor who tells your child they need a specific mark for a specific grade is guessing, and the guess is usually taken from a previous series. The useful framing is directional: more marks is better, and the cheapest marks first.

This is why the fortnightly note records marks by topic rather than predicting a grade. A prediction would be more comforting and less honest. What we can show is movement, its direction, and which categories are still carrying losses, and from that you can judge whether to continue, change the plan, or stop.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of evidence, week by week
paragraphs: The table below is the shape of a standard twelve-week run for a student entered for 0607, starting from a baseline. It is not a revision timetable, because the topics depend entirely on what the baseline found. It is a record of what should exist on paper at each point, so that a family can tell whether they are being given a programme or a sequence of pleasant hours.

Two features of it are worth drawing out. The first is that comparable papers are sat at week one, week six and week eleven. Comparability matters: a student who sits an easier paper in week six appears to have improved and has not, which is why the papers are chosen to match rather than taken in sequence from whatever is nearest. The second is that week six is a decision point with a real alternative. If the record shows no movement in the dominant category, the plan changes or the sessions stop.

Abu Dhabi families should adjust this for the school calendar rather than against it. Internal assessment weeks, residential trips and travel all take their slots, and Ramadan timings shift the practical window for an hour of concentrated work. A plan that ignores those collapses by the halfway point, which is why the schedule is agreed in writing at the start and moved deliberately rather than abandoned quietly.

By week twelve there should be three marked comparable papers, a topic record covering every area that has been tested, and a short written view of what the remaining weeks can realistically do. That final judgement is the part families value most, and it is the part that only exists if the evidence was collected from the beginning.

sections.heading: The graphics display calculator as a category of its own
paragraphs: 0607 treats the graphics display calculator as part of the mathematics, which means it is also part of the error record. On a marked script, calculator errors look different from mathematical ones. The working is short, the number is wrong but reasonable, and there is nothing on the page to diagnose, because the mistake happened on a screen nobody else saw. Over a term these losses are substantial and they are entirely fixable, which makes them worth isolating.

The recurring causes are few. An angle mode left in the wrong setting produces trigonometric answers that are wrong by a believable margin. A value read from a graph to two significant figures is then used in a calculation that needed more. A window set badly hides the intersection the question was about, and the student reports the one they can see. A statistical function is used with the frequencies in the wrong list. None of these is a conceptual failure, and none of them appears in a mark scheme as a topic.

In a session these are drilled against questions where the answer is already known, so the student discovers the discrepancy themselves rather than being told about it. Working over live video helps here rather than hurting: the student narrates what they are pressing and what the screen shows, which is more informative than a tutor watching a device over a shoulder. Two weeks of this generally closes the category.

Model rules are set in the syllabus and in the information for candidates, not by the tutor, and they do change between syllabuses and series. The current Cambridge documents on cambridgeinternational.org are the only reliable source for what your child may take into the room, and a school's exams officer will confirm it for your centre. We teach on whatever model your child actually owns, because a fortnight spent fluent on a different device is a fortnight wasted.

sections.heading: Reading a school mock and an ADEK report against each other
paragraphs: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes on a banded scale. Those reports are genuinely useful for a school choice and close to useless for the question a 0607 family is actually asking, which is about one set taught by one teacher. An inspection judges provision across a whole school, including areas that have nothing to do with upper secondary mathematics.

A mock mark has the opposite problem. It is precisely about your child and almost impossible to interpret, because you do not know how the paper compared with a real one, how it was marked, or how the department converted the mark into a predicted grade. Two schools in the same emirate can run mocks of quite different difficulty and both call the result a prediction.

Used together, with the actual script in hand, they answer more. The report tells you how the school is judged overall. The script tells you what your child did. The department can tell you how the mock was set and marked, and whether the paper was a past series or an internally written one. That third question is worth asking, because an internally written paper tells you much less about likely performance in a real series.

The practical request to make of the school is simple and rarely refused: the marked script back, and confirmation of which components and tier your child is entered for on the statement of entry. With those two documents and a published mark scheme, a family can see almost everything a tutor can see. Anything we add after that is teaching, not information.

sections.heading: What the record costs, and what each band includes
paragraphs: Marking is the expensive part of this arrangement and the reason the rate sits where it does. An hour of live teaching is one hour. An hour of teaching plus a full script marked against the published scheme plus a maintained topic record is closer to ninety minutes of work, and providers at the lower end of the published market bands are generally not doing the second part. That is the distinction worth interrogating in any quote you receive, in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else.

The figures in the table are other providers' published rates and the bands from a 2026 Dubai cost survey, stated as at October 2026. They are market context rather than our price list, and Abu Dhabi tracks Dubai closely for online specialist teaching because the pool of tutors is national. What varies locally is in-home pricing, where the published range includes travel, and where crossing the city at five in the afternoon is bought at the teaching rate.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. We are not therefore comparing an in-home option against an online one as a matter of preference. The comparison in the table exists because families are quoted both, and the relevant question is how much of the hour is teaching and how much of it is a journey. For a syllabus as thinly taught as 0607 in this emirate, the tutor pool argument is stronger than the price argument anyway.

What to ask before paying: is the script marked between sessions, against what, and do I receive it. Is there a written record, and how often. What happens if the record shows no movement. A provider who answers all four plainly is offering something different from an hourly rate, and the difference is the thing you are actually buying here.

sections.heading: What this page will not claim
paragraphs: No IB examination or results date appears anywhere on this page. The International Baccalaureate's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing in this project has been confirmed from the source, and publishing a date that turns out to be wrong would be worse than publishing none. Where an Abu Dhabi family needs an IB date, the Diploma coordinator at the school holds the authoritative version. Cambridge and Pearson dates are a different matter: both publish timetables, and the published figures are quoted on this site with their source.

No grade is promised. A 0607 result depends on three components sat under timed conditions by a teenager on particular mornings, and on thresholds set after the series. What can be committed to is the process: work set, work marked against the published scheme, causes recorded, movement reported fortnightly, and an honest view when the record says the plan is not working.

No approval is implied. IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the International Baccalaureate, and it operates no premises in the UAE. Private tutoring in the country is regulated by permit through MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and we check a tutor's permit position before a match. We do not describe that check as anything more than it is.

No assessed work is produced for a student. The investigation component of this syllabus is the candidate's own, and a tutor's role with it is to teach the skills of investigating, to discuss method, and to give feedback on reasoning the student has written themselves. Official syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are the boards' copyright: we reference them, cite them and link to them, and we do not redistribute them as downloads.

faqs.question: What will I actually receive after a fortnight of 0607 sessions?
faqs.answer: Two marked scripts with the mark scheme wording noted beside each loss, a topic record showing which areas have been tested and what was scored, and a short written note saying what moved, what did not, and what the next fortnight will do. The note is deliberately brief enough to read in two minutes. All of it belongs to you and can be shown to your child's school. If you have received nothing written after a fortnight from any tutor, that is worth asking about, because the record is the part that makes the hours accountable.

faqs.question: Why would a higher 0607 mark leave the predicted grade unchanged?
faqs.answer: Because marks move continuously and grades move in steps. A gain of several marks is real improvement, and if it landed in the middle of a band rather than at its edge the grade stays where it was. The reverse is also true: a student sitting just under a boundary can cross it on a very small gain, which is why cheap categories such as presentation and reading are disproportionately valuable late in the year. Nobody can tell you where the threshold will fall, because the board sets it after the series on the papers actually sat.

faqs.question: Which 0607 component should the first marked paper be?
faqs.answer: Ideally not one component but work sampled from each type, because that is where the information is. A student can be fluent with a calculator and weak without one, which a structured paper alone will never reveal, and can handle both written papers while having no idea what an investigation is asking for. Averaging those into a single mark, which is what a mock does, removes exactly the detail a family needs. Where a series is only weeks away we compress this and mark whatever existing script you already have, then start teaching the same week.

faqs.question: How do you tell a calculator error from a maths error on a script?
faqs.answer: By the shape of the working. A calculator error usually leaves short working, a wrong but believable number, and nothing diagnosable on the page, because the mistake happened on a screen. The four recurring causes are an angle mode left in the wrong setting, a value read from a graph to too few figures, a badly set window hiding the intersection the question was about, and statistical data entered in the wrong list. In a session these are drilled against questions whose answers are already known, so the student finds the discrepancy instead of being told about it.

faqs.question: Can I use my child's school mock and the ADEK report together?
faqs.answer: Up to a point, and only with the script in hand. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes on a banded scale, which tells you how a whole school was judged and nothing about one maths set. A mock mark is precisely about your child and hard to interpret without knowing how the paper was set and marked. Ask the department whether the mock was a past series paper or written internally, and ask for the marked script back. Those two answers are worth more than either document alone.

faqs.question: How is a 0607 error record built, and who keeps it?
faqs.answer: It is built from marked work, one line per cluster of lost marks, with each entry assigned to content, technology, presentation or reading. The tutor maintains it and sends it to you, so both of you are looking at the same document. It grows only as work is tested, which means it never claims anything about topics your child has not met yet. After eight weeks a typical record carries a dozen or so entries, several of them closed, and the pattern across them is what the fortnightly note describes.

faqs.question: Can my child's school see the marked 0607 scripts?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we encourage it. The scripts and the written diagnosis are yours. Some families take them to the head of maths and arrange additional support inside the school, which is a perfectly good outcome and occasionally the right one. A department that can see which category the losses fall into can usually act on it faster than a parent can. We ask only that the marking is presented as an external tutor's marking against the published scheme rather than as a formal assessment, because the school's own judgements are the ones that feed a prediction.

faqs.question: How many marked papers before we know whether this is working?
faqs.answer: Three comparable papers, spread across roughly twelve weeks, gives a trend you can trust. Two gives a direction. One gives a starting point and nothing more. Comparability is the part people skip: a student who sits an easier paper at the halfway point appears to have improved and has not, so the papers are chosen to match rather than taken in order from whatever is nearest. The formal decision point is week six, when the record is read as a whole and the plan either continues, changes, or stops.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter lose accuracy marks on the paper without a calculator?
faqs.answer: Because the non-calculator paper tests manipulation that most students have quietly stopped practising. Sign errors in expansion, fractions handled by converting to decimals, surds left unsimplified and arithmetic done hurriedly in the margin all cost marks there and nowhere else. The record usually shows method secure and accuracy dropping sharply on that component alone, which is a reassuring finding: it is a drill problem rather than a comprehension problem, and a fortnight of short daily sets addresses most of it.

faqs.question: Is the 0607 investigation component something a tutor can mark honestly?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills of investigating, work comparable problems, and give feedback on reasoning the student has already written. Where a piece of work is being submitted as assessed, it stays entirely the candidate's own from first line to last, and the honest service is teaching the method rather than improving the artefact. For practice work drawn from released material there is no such constraint, and marking it against the published criteria is one of the most useful things a session can do, because investigative marks are where strong students most often underperform.

faqs.question: What happens if the evidence says the sessions are not helping?
faqs.answer: You hear it from us at the week-six review rather than discovering it after the series. If the dominant category has not moved across two comparable papers, there are three honest options: change the category being worked on, change the tutor, or stop. We will say which one the record supports. Occasionally the right advice is to stop paying and put the time into the school's own support, and that advice is part of what the fortnightly record exists to make possible. A plan nobody is willing to abandon is not a plan.

faqs.question: Do you provide 0607 past papers and mark schemes to download?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade threshold tables are the board's copyright. We reference them, cite them and point you to the official pages on cambridgeinternational.org, and your child's school can supply released material through the proper channel. A provider offering a library of board material as free downloads is treating somebody else's copyright casually, which is worth noticing before you hand over anything about your child. Within a session we work from material the student legitimately has.

faqs.question: How much does weekly 0607 support with marking cost around Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialist IGCSE or Diploma tutors at AED 200 to 450 or above, with one provider publishing AED 650 at the premium end. Those are other providers' own rates as at October 2026, not our price list. The band matters less than what sits inside it: an hour of teaching with a script marked against the published scheme between sessions is a different product from an hour of talking, and the lower bands generally exclude the marking entirely.

faqs.question: We may move to another emirate mid-year. Does the record follow us?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the reasons for keeping it. Lessons are delivered over live video, so a move from Abu Dhabi to Dubai, Sharjah or outside the country changes the time zone calculation and nothing else. The marked scripts, the topic record and the written diagnosis travel with you, which also helps the receiving school: a new head of maths can see what has been tested and what the causes were rather than starting from a transcript. Where the new school uses a different syllabus, the first job is a fresh baseline against that one.

faqs.question: Can 0607 sessions run during Ramadan and a shortened school day?
faqs.answer: They can, with the timing agreed in advance rather than improvised. School hours shorten, family routines change, and the useful hour moves for most households, often to later in the evening or to a weekend morning. We would rather set one protected slot that survives the month than keep a weekday evening that gets cancelled three times. The practical compromise most families settle on is shorter sessions, more focused work, and the timed papers moved out of the month entirely so that nothing measured happens under unrepresentative conditions.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-tut.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge 0580 specifically rather than general maths. Each works from the current syllabus, knows which tier a topic belongs to, and marks past paper questions the way a Cambridge examiner does - method marks and accuracy marks counted separately.

intro.heading: The two questions that decide a 0580 grade before revision starts
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the most widely taken maths qualification in Abu Dhabi's British-curriculum schools, and most of the difficulty families have with it is structural rather than mathematical. Two facts about a student's entry determine more than any amount of revision, and a surprising number of parents do not know either of them. The first is whether the child is entered for Core or Extended. The second is which papers that entry means they will sit, and how the marks on those papers are split.

The tier decision sets a ceiling. Core and Extended are different syllabus content and different papers, and they lead to different grade ranges - Core cannot reach the top grades at all. A student entered for Core who is capable of Extended has had their ceiling lowered by an administrative decision, and a student pushed onto Extended who is not secure on Core content will lose marks across both papers rather than gaining access to higher ones. Schools make this call in Year 10 and sometimes revisit it; families should know where their child sits and on what evidence.

The paper structure is the second fact, and it changed. The 0580 syllabus was revised for examination from 2025, which introduced a non-calculator paper and moved the weightings so that the two papers a student sits carry equal value. That is a substantial change to how revision has to work, because a generation of past papers and revision guides were built around an unequal split and a calculator being available throughout. Check the current syllabus for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org rather than relying on an older summary, and ask the school's exams officer to confirm the entry.

What a tutor adds to 0580 is narrower and more measurable than in most subjects. Maths past papers are marked against published mark schemes, which means a tutor can say exactly where a student is losing marks and whether the loss is method - not showing the route, so the method marks are unavailable - or accuracy, where the method was right and the final figure was not. Those two require different work. Method loss is a habit problem fixed by requiring working on every question. Accuracy loss is usually rounding, units or premature approximation, and it is fixed in a fortnight.

Abu Dhabi contributes two practical matters that almost no competing page mentions. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version per zone, warning that it is essential to use the correct one and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. And 0580 counts towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency for British-curriculum students, under a sourced rule that one ranking page in this market states incorrectly. Both are covered below. Lessons are one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we offer only in India.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-tut.programmesIntro: 0580 sits in the middle of a Cambridge pathway and feeds several different post-16 routes, each with its own expectation of what a student arrives knowing. The map below is written around those transitions, because the tier choice at 0580 affects all of them.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The qualification in the URL. Mathematics 0580 is examined in two tiers, Core and Extended, with students sitting two written papers in whichever tier they are entered for. The syllabus covers nine topic areas from Number through to Statistics, and Extended adds content as well as depth. Cambridge examines IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with results and certificates on a published schedule.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi's British-curriculum schools are the main 0580 centres in the emirate and sit the June series in the overwhelming majority of cases. November entries exist and are used mainly for resits and for students whose school year is offset. The school's exams officer, not the maths department, is the person who can confirm the entry code, the tier and the centre's timetable zone.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The direct continuation. AS and A Level Mathematics assumes Extended content as a starting point, particularly algebra, trigonometry and coordinate geometry, and a student arriving from Core has a real gap to close before the first term is out. This is the strongest practical argument for getting the tier decision right in Year 10 rather than accepting it as fixed.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run A Level Mathematics with an internal entry requirement at IGCSE, and those requirements are published or available on request. A family weighing the Core and Extended decision should read that requirement first, because it converts an abstract tier choice into a concrete consequence two years later.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Many Abu Dhabi students move from IGCSE into the IB Diploma, where mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at SL and HL. Extended 0580 is the realistic preparation for Analysis and Approaches at HL; Core is not, and the gap in algebraic fluency shows up within weeks. Students choosing between the two Diploma routes should know which their 0580 tier actually supports.
programmes.countryNote: Because Abu Dhabi has substantial British and IB sectors side by side, cross-sector transfer at 16 is common in the emirate. A student moving from a Cambridge school into an IB school for the Diploma arrives with 0580 rather than MYP mathematics, and the algebra expectations of Analysis and Approaches HL are the usual friction point.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The stage before IGCSE, with Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. The content that most determines later 0580 performance is laid here: fluency with fractions, negative numbers, indices and basic algebraic manipulation. Students who reach Year 10 shaky on those four lose marks across every topic area rather than in one.
programmes.countryNote: Lower Secondary provision varies across Abu Dhabi schools, and students transferring into the emirate in Year 9 frequently arrive from curricula that sequence algebra differently. That mismatch, rather than ability, is behind a good share of the Core and Extended placement difficulties that surface in Year 10.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-tut.subjectsIntro: 0580 is rarely the only booking, and the subjects alongside it share the same marking logic - working shown, method rewarded, accuracy separate. The grid lists the Cambridge codes most often studied with 0580 in Abu Dhabi and what each one costs students marks on.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Two papers, nine topic areas, equal weighting under the syllabus examined from 2025. Marks are lost roughly equally to method - no working, so no method marks - and to accuracy, mostly premature rounding and missing units.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: Cambridge's alternative maths syllabus, assessed with a graphics calculator and an investigation paper. Schools choose between 0580 and 0607, and the two are not interchangeable in revision terms, so confirm which code your child is entered for before buying any resources.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside or after Extended 0580 by stronger students as a bridge to A Level. It assumes Extended fluency and punishes gaps in algebra immediately, so it is a poor choice for a student whose 0580 method marks are still unreliable.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: The subject most dependent on 0580 algebra. Rearranging formulae, standard form and unit conversion are maths skills examined in a physics paper, and a student losing marks there is usually losing them to the same habit in maths.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and percentage yield calculations are proportional reasoning with chemical labels. Students who find those impossible generally have a ratio problem rather than a chemistry problem.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Lighter on calculation but heavy on data handling, graphs and percentage change - the same statistics and number skills as topic areas 8 and 9 of the maths syllabus, assessed in a different register.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: A single award covering all three sciences, common in Abu Dhabi schools for students not taking separate sciences. The maths content is spread thin across the three, which hides a numeracy weakness until the papers are marked.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Data response questions require graph reading, percentage change and index numbers. Students strong in essay work and weak in 0580 statistics lose marks on exactly the questions that look easiest.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Break-even, ratio analysis and cash flow are arithmetic in a commercial setting. A student secure on 0580 Number finds this straightforward; one who is not finds it opaque for reasons that have nothing to do with business.

sections.heading: What 0580 assesses: the papers, the tiers and the weightings
paragraphs: Every 0580 candidate sits two written papers, and which two depends entirely on the tier they are entered for. Core candidates sit the Core pair; Extended candidates sit the Extended pair. The syllabus was revised for examination from 2025, introducing a non-calculator paper and setting the two papers at equal weight, which is a change from the older structure that many revision resources still reflect.

The practical consequence is that half of a student's grade now rests on a paper where no calculator is available. Under the previous structure the larger paper allowed a calculator throughout, so a student with weak number fluency could carry a grade on method and technology. That route has closed. Fractions, indices, surds, standard form, exact trigonometric values and estimation have gone from useful to load-bearing.

The table below sets out the structure as examined from 2025. Treat it as a planning summary and confirm the detail for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org, because Cambridge publishes the syllabus per examination year and the figures are revised between versions. The school's exams officer can confirm the paper codes on the actual entry, which is the only version that matters.

One more structural fact worth knowing: the tier is an entry decision, not a prediction. A school enters a candidate for Core or Extended, and that entry determines the papers sat and therefore the grades available. It can be changed up to the final entry deadline, which is months before the exam - so a student whose performance has shifted since Year 10 has a window, and it closes quietly.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: This is the most consequential conversation a parent can have with an Abu Dhabi maths department, and it happens too rarely. Core and Extended are not easy and hard versions of one paper. They are different content with different papers and different grade ranges, and Core cannot deliver the top grades at all. A student entered for Core has a ceiling, and whether that ceiling is right for them is a judgement based on evidence that parents are entitled to see.

The honest case for Core is real and should not be dismissed. A student who is insecure on number, fractions and basic algebraic manipulation will score better on Core papers than on Extended ones, and a solid Core grade is worth more than a poor Extended one for Ministry of Education equivalency purposes, where the requirement is a minimum grade rather than a high one. Pushing such a student onto Extended produces a paper full of half-attempted questions and a lower grade.

The case against Core is the two-year consequence. A Level Mathematics assumes Extended content, particularly algebra, trigonometry and coordinate geometry, and schools publish internal entry requirements that a Core grade generally cannot meet. IB Diploma Analysis and Approaches at HL assumes the same fluency. A student intending either route needs Extended, and the time to establish that is Year 10, not the week of the final entry deadline.

What settles it is marked evidence rather than opinion. Give the student a recent Extended paper and a recent Core paper under timed conditions, mark both against the published schemes, and look at where the marks fall. A student scoring respectably on Extended method marks and losing accuracy is an Extended candidate with a fixable habit. A student scoring in the lowest band on Extended across both method and accuracy is being asked to run before they can walk. That diagnosis takes two papers and an afternoon.

sections.heading: The nine topic areas and where the marks actually go
paragraphs: The 0580 syllabus is organised into nine topic areas: Number, Algebra and graphs, Coordinate geometry, Geometry, Mensuration, Trigonometry, Transformations and vectors, Probability, and Statistics. Students and parents talk about being bad at maths; mark schemes talk about specific topic areas, and the difference matters because one of those is actionable.

In Abu Dhabi cohorts the losses concentrate predictably. Algebra and graphs is the largest single source across both tiers, and within it the recurring failures are rearranging formulae with the unknown on both sides, factorising quadratics where the coefficient is not one, and solving simultaneous equations when one is non-linear. Trigonometry is second, with the sine and cosine rules applied to the wrong triangle and bearings misread. Mensuration produces losses that are almost entirely unit errors rather than method errors - surface area in the wrong power, volume mixed between centimetres and metres.

Probability and Statistics are the quiet ones. Students assume they are easy because the arithmetic is light, and lose marks on tree diagrams without replacement, on cumulative frequency read-offs, and on interpreting a histogram with unequal class widths. These are high-yield topics to fix precisely because students do not think they need to.

The useful method is to stop revising topics and start auditing a paper. Mark a full past paper against the published scheme, write every lost mark against its topic area, and the pattern appears within one paper and is unmistakable across three. Most students discover that two topic areas account for the majority of their losses, which turns an unbounded revision task into a specific one that can be finished.

sections.heading: Method marks: why a right answer can still score badly
paragraphs: Cambridge mark schemes award method marks and accuracy marks separately, and this single fact explains more unexpected 0580 results than any other. A question worth four marks may award three for the route and one for the final figure. A student who writes only the answer, correct, collects the accuracy mark and forfeits the method marks they would have been given for working they did in their head. A student who shows the route and makes an arithmetic slip at the end keeps the method marks and loses one.

Across a full paper the difference is large, and it falls hardest on confident students. The pattern is familiar to any maths teacher in the emirate: a bright child who finds the work easy, works mentally, writes little, and scores well below what their understanding predicts. They are not being punished for cleverness. They are leaving marks on the table that the mark scheme was ready to give them.

The second category is accuracy loss, and it has three recurring causes. Premature rounding, where a student rounds an intermediate value and the final answer falls outside the accepted range. Units, particularly in mensuration where area and volume scale differently from length. And final-answer form, where the question asks for an exact value, a specific number of significant figures, or a particular unit, and the student gives something else that is numerically reasonable and formally wrong.

Both categories are habits rather than knowledge, which is why they are the fastest marks to recover. The working rule is absolute: every question gets a visible route, including the ones the student finds trivial, because the mark scheme cannot read intentions. The accuracy rule is to carry exact or full values through the calculation and round once, at the end, to what the question asked for. A fortnight of enforcement on a student's own marked papers typically recovers several marks per paper.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper changed what revision has to be
paragraphs: The 2025 revision of 0580 introduced a non-calculator paper and set the two papers at equal weight. For a student who learned maths with a calculator permanently available, that is a genuine change in what preparation means, and it is not yet reflected in every revision resource on the shelf.

What becomes load-bearing is a short, specific list. Fractions - all four operations, including mixed numbers, done reliably rather than approximately. Indices and standard form, manipulated rather than evaluated. Surds, simplified and rationalised at Extended. Exact trigonometric values for the standard angles. Percentage and ratio arithmetic without a device. And estimation, which is both a question type and a checking strategy for the rest of the paper.

The way to build it is the opposite of a long session. Ten minutes of timed short questions, daily, beats ninety minutes weekly, because this is recall and fluency rather than understanding. A student who can do fractions slowly does not have the skill the paper tests; the paper tests doing them quickly enough to leave time for the questions that require thought. Treating this as a drill rather than a topic is the single most useful reframing available for the non-calculator paper.

There is a knock-on benefit on the calculator paper. Students with weak number fluency over-rely on the device, type values in mid-problem, and lose track of exactness - which is precisely the premature-rounding error that costs accuracy marks. Fixing non-calculator fluency improves the calculator paper as a side effect, which is not true in the other direction.
